items.title: Prevalence of Multidrug-Resistant Escherichia coli from Poultry Farms in Nairobi and Kiambu Counties, Kenya
items.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a critical global one-health issue affecting human, animal, and environmental health. Factors driving AMR include antibiotic misuse, poor disease prevention, agricultural antimicrobial waste, pollution, and the spread of drug-resistant bacteria via travel and trade. In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), antibiotics are frequently added to animal feed in small, non-therapeutic doses to promote growth and prevent disease, with about 70% of antibiotics used annually for non-therapeutic purposes. Escherichia coli (E. coli) , a common bacterium in the lower digestive tracts of warm-blooded animals, is part of the coliform bacteria group. It is a rod-shaped, facultatively anaerobic, Gram-negative bacterium and serves as an indicator for monitoring antibiotic-resistant bacteria in the environment. A significant number of antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) bacteria, including E. coli , have been isolated from chickens in Kenya, especially against antibiotics such as ampicillin, tetracycline, sulphamethoxazole, and co-trimoxazole. This study investigated the prevalence and antimicrobial resistance profiles of Escherichia coli isolated from poultry farms in Nairobi and Kiambu counties, Kenya. A total of 429 fecal samples were collected from which 92 E. coli isolates were confirmed through microbiological methods and MALDI-TOF. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing revealed widespread resistance to individual agents, with 30.4% of isolates meeting multidrug-resistance (MDR) criteria and a high rate of tetracycline resistance (55%). PCR analysis identified blaTEM, tetA , strB , and sul2 as the most common resistance genes. Resistance and MDR were statistically comparable between Kiambu and Nairobi counties, indicating a shared regional AMR burden rather than a county-specific pattern, with resistance observed across multiple antibiotic classes. This highlights the urgent need for improved veterinary practices, stricter antibiotic regulations, and alternative treatment approaches to curb the spread of AMR in poultry, which threatens both animal and public health.

items.title: Direct comparison of the effects of functionally equivalent dosing regimens of methamphetamine, methcathinone, and α-pyrrolidinopropiophenone on behavioral and neurochemical markers of stimulant-induced neurotoxicity.
items.abstract: Given that previous studies have provided mixed results on cathinone neurotoxicity, we compared the effects of 'functionally equivalent' dosing regimens of methamphetamine (METH), methcathinone, and α-pyrrolidinopropiophenone (α-PPP) on behavioral and neurochemical markers associated with dopaminergic alterations and cognitive function. Male Swiss Webster mice received METH (5 mg/kg), methcathinone (80 mg/kg), or α-PPP (80 mg/kg), using a 'binge'-like dosing regimen (q2h × 4, intraperitoneal). Body weight and temperature were recorded during dosing. Behavior was assessed 2-4 days later, followed by brain extraction. Motor function was evaluated by open-field testing and stride length analysis. Cognitive function was assessed with the passive avoidance test. Striatal levels of dopamine and its major metabolites were measured using ultra-HPLC. All three drug treatments induced weight loss. METH treatment produced a small, transient increase in rectal temperature (~1 °C); methcathinone and α-PPP did not. All three drug treatments impaired passive avoidance performance ( P < 0.05 to P < 0.01), but none produced persistent motor deficits. METH and methcathinone treatment significantly reduced striatal dopamine levels ( P < 0.001), whereas α-PPP did not, and only METH treatment increased homovanillic acid/dopamine turnover ( P < 0.01). Only METH exposure triggered measurable changes in dopamine metabolism and a small, transient increase in temperature, highlighting its distinct neurochemical profile compared with methcathinone and α-PPP under these conditions. All three drug treatments impaired passive avoidance performance, but none caused lasting motor deficits, demonstrating that behavioral deficits can occur without persistent motor changes.

items.title: Flavonoids in the Prevention and Treatment of Liver Diseases: Research Progress and Future Perspectives.
items.abstract: The liver is a central metabolic organ essential for maintaining physiological homeostasis, and its dysfunction is closely associated with the development and progression of various chronic diseases. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and alcohol-related liver disease (ALD) have become major causes of chronic liver injury worldwide, posing a substantial public health burden. Flavonoids are naturally occurring polyphenolic compounds widely distributed in plants. Representative flavonoids, including quercetin, epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), luteolin, naringenin, and puerarin, exhibit diverse biological activities, such as anti-oxidant, anti-inflammatory, and metabolic regulatory effects, highlighting their therapeutic potential in liver diseases. This review systematically summarizes the preventive and therapeutic roles of flavonoids in MASLD and ALD, with particular emphasis on their underlying molecular mechanisms. Current evidence indicates that flavonoids protect against liver injury by regulating glucose and lipid metabolism, alleviating oxidative stress and inflammation, modulating the gut microbiota and maintaining gut-liver axis homeostasis, thereby reducing hepatic lipid accumulation and hepatocellular injury and ultimately attenuating disease progression. We also discuss the major challenges limiting their clinical application, including low bioavailability, interindividual variability, insufficient long-term safety data, limited large-scale clinical evidence, and potential drug interactions. Future research should focus on structural optimization, advanced drug delivery systems, combination therapies, and microbiota-based personalized interventions. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive mechanistic framework for the hepatoprotective effects of flavonoids and offers a theoretical basis for their development as promising therapeutic agents and nutritional interventions for liver diseases.

items.title: Rapid polarization position angle variations in FRB 20240114A point to a magnetospheric origin
items.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs), thought to originate from magnetars, exhibit diverse polarization properties that provide key constraints on their emission physics and local magneto-ionic environments. Among these, the polarization position angle (PPA) is particularly sensitive to magnetic-field geometry in the emitting region and propagation effects in the magnetosphere and beyond. In hyperactive repeating FRBs, the PPAs are typically stable across the duration of a burst and, in two well-studied cases, remain stable on timescales of hours to days. In contrast, here we present observations of the repeating source ̊onefourseven that show significant burst-to-burst jumps in the PPA. Using full-Stokes, high–time-resolution observations from the Nançay Radio Telescope (1.1--1.8 GHz) and the Effelsberg 100-m telescope (1.3--1.5 GHz) spanning ∼1 year, we measure burst rotation measures (RMs), as well as time-resolved polarization fractions and PPAs at 12 epochs. The burst RMs remain stable across all epochs, and the emission is predominantly highly linearly polarized, with sim81% of bursts showing L/I > 0.8, while circular polarization is weaker (sim16% with $|V/I| > 0.1$). We find no evidence for Faraday conversion. The PPA exhibits rapid, stochastic variations on timescales from milliseconds to hours, spanning the full range of pm90 degrees during two periods of high activity and ±50 degrees in a third active period. We also investigate the statistics of PPA jumps, defined as the difference in PPA between two consecutive bursts. We find that: (1) there is no difference in the distribution of jumps on timescales shorter or longer than 1 s; (2) positive and negative jumps are equally likely; and 3) a jump of ±90 degrees, as expected from, for example, orthogonal mode jumps, is not more common than any other value. No other hyperactive repeaters show this combination of relatively stable RM, consistently high linear polarization, and extreme burst-to-burst PPA variability. The observations disfavor emission from a single fixed region in a rotating magnetosphere and instead point toward multiple emission regions, or strong magnetospheric propagation effects, and/or propagation effects in the foreground medium, such as plasma lensing.

items.title: Probing a New Subclass of Low-Luminosity Gamma-Ray Burst–Supernovae: Insights from EP250304a and SN,2025fhm
items.abstract: With the advent of the ( ) mission, we are entering a new era in the study of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), enabling the detection of faint, low-luminosity transients that would previously have gone undetected. EP250304a was an event discovered by associated with the broad-lined type Ic supernova (SN) SN,2025fhm located at Einstein Probe EP EP z = 0.2. Despite no gamma-ray emission being detected at the time of the trigger, we identified evidence of a relativistic outflow consistent with a GRB-like jet across multiple wavelengths. We present a detailed spectral and photometric analysis of EP250304a/SN,2025fhm, including multi-band light curve modelling performed with the EP Redback Python package. we found that this event closely resembles low-luminosity GRB-SNe (llGRB-SNe) such as GRB,060218/SN,2006aj, GRB,100316D/SN,2010bh, and GRB,171205A/SN,2017iuk, all of which exhibit early-time emission consistent with a thermal shocked cocoon. These similarities suggest that EP250304A/SN,2025fhm may belong to an emerging subclass of shocked cocoon-dominated llGRB-SNe, representing the low-luminosity end of a broader continuum of engine-driven GRB-SN explosions.

items.title: Improving constraints on the Yukawa correction at the Galactic center with multiple stellar orbits
items.abstract: We investigate the presence of a Yukawa-like correction (∝ , α - r/łambda ) to Newtonian gravity at the Galactic center, using a multi-star fitting code, including the newly discovered star S301, to improve the constraints obtained using S2 orbit alone. We performed a Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis using the astrometric and spectroscopic data of stars S2, S55, S29, S38, and S301 collected by GRAVITY, GRAVITY+$, NACO, and SINFONI instruments, covering the period from 1992 to $2025. Compared to our previous paper, in which only S2 was fitted, the tightest bound on the Yukawa coupling is again reached at łambda = 3̧dot10^ 13 ,̊m m (∼ 200,AU), where we find $|α| < 6 -4 $, an improvement of roughly a factor of 5. The addition of S301 extends the constraint to short ranges that were inaccessible to S2, yielding $|α| < 0.004$ at łambda =10^ 12 ,̊m m and $|α| < 0.006$ at łambda =5⋅ 10^ 11 ,̊m m. By contrast, S29, with its larger apoapsis, yields $|α| < 0.1$ at łambda ∼ 2̧dot10^ 15 ,̊m m. The latter two represent the tightest limits at these scale lengths on a Yukawa correction obtained to date around a supermassive black hole.

items.title: The nearby Type II supernova 2024ggi beyond 600 days: Circumstellar interaction and dust formation
items.abstract: The Type II supernova (SN) 2024ggi is one of the nearest core-collapse supernovae (SNe) to have exploded in recent decades. Its proximity has enabled extensive multiwavelength monitoring from early times through the nebular phase. Signatures of late-time interaction between the SN ejecta and hydrogen-rich circumstellar material (CSM) have recently been reported. Here we extend its study using late-time optical photometry and spectroscopy from 570 to 820 d after explosion. We investigate the emergence and evolution of late-time ejecta--CSM interaction and constrain the geometry of the interaction region and the properties of newly formed dust. We present optical light curves and a series of low-resolution optical spectra of SN 2024ggi covering phases between 570 and 820 d after explosion. Comparisons with other interacting SNe II and with synthetic spectra are presented. We model the Hα profile with the Monte Carlo radiative-transfer code , including both gas and dust components. Damocles Spectroscopic signatures of interaction precede photometric flattening. The spectra evolve from ejecta-dominated to interaction-dominated as Hα develops a broad, boxy profile. The optical light curves subsequently flatten relative to the 56 Co decay rate at approximately 650--670 d. The emission lines show a systematic blue-to-red asymmetry that requires a newly formed dust component within the ejecta. The inferred dust mass formed in the ejecta is 10^ -6 -10^ -5 M_⊙ if the grains are amorphous carbon or a carbon--silicate mixture, but can reach up to 10^ -3 M_⊙ for pure silicates. By ≳ 600 d, the optical evolution of SN 2024ggi is dominated by ejecta--CSM interaction, while the asymmetric line profiles provide evidence of recent dust formation. Our observations and findings regarding SN 2024ggi add to the growing number of SNe II observed several hundred days after explosion, demonstrating the diversity in late-time interaction and constraining the mass-loss histories of these massive star explosions.

items.abstract: Gas-rich ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs) provide powerful and novel tests of galaxy formation models at low stellar surface densities. However, the structure of their neutral atomic hydrogen ( (R)). We present the Finding Rotation In ultra-Diffuse gAlaxies (FRIDA) survey, a 250-hour MeerKAT programme complemented by existing Very Large Array data, providing high-resolution imaging of 12 gas-rich UDGs. By expanding the number of UDGs with high-resolution observations from two to 12, FRIDA provides a foundation for detailed studies of the gas structure, evolution, and dark-matter content of diffuse, gas-rich dwarfs. In this paper, we introduce our sample and delve into the associated interferometric observations and data reduction. Moreover, we place our UDGs in the M_ ̊m HI - ̊m HI and M_ ̊m HI - R_ ̊m 50,HI mass--size relations defined by reference literature samples, where R_̊m HI is the isophotal radius at which Σ_ ̊m HI = ,1,M_⊙, , and R_̊m 50,HI is the radius enclosing 50% of M_̊m HI. items.title: Prioritizing submarine canyons as climate refugia for global deep-sea biodiversity conservation
items.abstract: Abstract The deep sea covers approximately 65% of the Earth’s surface, yet it remains poorly protected. Here, we show that submarine canyons, covering ~1.2% of the ocean floor, could strengthen deep-sea conservation and provide climate refugia. By integrating global databases, we find that canyons harbour 56% of deep-sea habitats and ~13,613 species, representing up to 50% of deep-sea biodiversity. Prioritizing canyon protection could safeguard deep-sea biodiversity and support climate-resilient marine conservation.

items.title: Kinetic oscillation stimulation by the Chordate System S101 in the treatment of non-allergic rhinitis (KOSNAR): a randomised controlled trial.
items.abstract: Objectives To determine whether kinetic oscillation stimulation is superior to sham treatment for non-allergic rhinitis. Methods In this multi-centre, double-blinded, sham-controlled trial, patients with non-allergic rhinitis received intranasal kinetic oscillation stimulation or placebo on two treatment occasions. The primary outcome was improvement in nasal congestion score at three months. Secondary outcomes included total nasal symptom score, nasal obstruction and septoplasty effectiveness score, EQ-5D-5L and peak nasal inspiratory flow. Results Of 279 recruited patients, 224 were analysed (112 patients received kinetic oscillation stimulation, 112 placebo). Response rates did not differ (40 per cent vs 46 per cent; p = 0.30). Both groups improved over time in total nasal symptom score (median change -2 vs -2; p = 0.81), nasal congestion score (-0.35 vs -1; p = 0.18) and nasal obstruction and septoplasty effectiveness score (-15 vs -15; p = 0.80), without significant between-group differences. Peak nasal inspiratory flow did not improve in the treatment group. Conclusion This confirmatory trial found no superiority of kinetic oscillation stimulation over sham and does not support kinetic oscillation stimulation for non-allergic rhinitis.

items.title: The association of childhood maltreatment, depression, and their combination with adiposity and dyslipidemia: an individual participant data meta-analysis.
items.abstract: While childhood maltreatment and depression are recognized risk factors for poor metabolic health, the extent to which these individually or in combination with each other contribute to metabolic risk remains unknown. Therefore, we investigated adiposity and dyslipidemia across four groups: adults with neither a history of childhood maltreatment nor depression (controls), with childhood maltreatment, with depression, or with both. We conducted an individual participant data meta-analysis using 11 cohort studies. Childhood maltreatment was assessed with reports of physical, emotional, and/or sexual abuse. Depression was established with clinical interviews or validated symptom scales. Adiposity was assessed with body mass index (BMI) and waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) and dyslipidemia with circulating triglycerides and low-density/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (LDL-c/HDL-c). In the pooled sample (N = 167,332), 6% had childhood maltreatment, 21% depression, and 6% both. Compared to controls, participants with maltreatment had slightly higher adiposity (dBMI=0.06 [95%CI, 0.01-0.10], p=.012; dWHR=0.06 [95%CI, 0.01-0.12], p=.030) but similar lipid levels (dtriglycerides=0.01 [95%CI, ‒0.03-0.04], p=.751; dLDL-c/HDL-c=0.01 [95%CI, ‒0.03-0.06], p=.560). Those with depression had higher adiposity (dBMI=0.06 [95%CI, 0.01-0.12], p=.030; dWHR=0.12 [95%CI, 0.08-0.16], p<.001) and dyslipidemia (dtriglycerides=0.08 [95%CI, 0.04-0.12], p<.001; dLDL-c/HDL-c=0.13 [95%CI, 0.07-0.18], p<.001). Participants with both maltreatment and depression had the highest adiposity (dBMI=0.17 [95%CI, 0.04-0.30], p=.010; dWHR=0.16 [95%CI, 0.07-0.24], p<.001) and dyslipidemia (dtriglycerides=0.14 [95%CI, 0.11-0.16], p<.001; dLDL-c/HDL-c=0.18 [95%CI, 0.12-0.23], p<.001). Childhood maltreatment and depression are associated with unfavorable metabolic health, with the largest dysregulations found when maltreatment and depression co-occur. Mechanisms of metabolic dysregulation in maltreatment and/or depression should be better understood to prevent progression to metabolic disorders.

items.title: Cannabis use and mental health symptoms in adolescents and adults: a 4-year longitudinal study.
items.abstract: Background Adolescence may be characterised by increased sensitivity to the psychological harms of chronic cannabis use. However, few studies have directly compared the consequences of cannabis use on adolescent and adult mental health over time. Methods We ran a 4-year longitudinal study of 274 participants, who were recruited as mid-adolescents (16-17 years) and young adults (26-29 years). At baseline, participants either used cannabis (≥1 day/week) or did not. We measured drug use, mental health, and cognitive function every 3 months for 1 year and ~4 years post-baseline. We ran linear mixed models to estimate associations between time-varying cannabis use frequency and our outcomes. We covaried for sociodemographic, environmental, and polygenic risk variables. Results Adolescents were more likely to have problematic cannabis use symptoms than adults ( p = .001). Cannabis use frequency was associated with: severity of problematic cannabis use ( p p = .003), and worse spatial working memory performance ( p = .038). Cannabis use cessation was associated with reductions in psychotic-like ( p = .005) and depressive symptoms ( p = .016). Most cannabis use by age-group interactions were null. Conclusions Adolescents have a persistently enhanced risk of problematic cannabis use. Using cannabis more frequently is associated with greater psychotic-like symptoms and worse spatial working memory. Apart from problematic cannabis use, we found no significant evidence that mid-to-late adolescents are especially vulnerable to the associations between cannabis use and poorer mental health. However, cessation of cannabis use was linked to improvements in mental health.

items.title: Childhood trauma and side-effects of antipsychotic medication after first-episode psychosis: A HAMLETT study.
items.abstract: Background Childhood trauma is a well-established risk factor for psychosis and is linked to worse outcomes and higher doses of antipsychotic medication needed. Trauma-exposed individuals also exhibit endocrinological, immunological, and metabolic alterations that may influence medication metabolism and sensitivity to side effects. This study examined whether childhood trauma severity predicts side-effect burden in individuals with first episode psychosis (FEP). Methods This analysis utilized baseline data from the HAMLETT study. Participants in symptomatic remission following an FEP and receiving antipsychotics were included if they had completed the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire - Short Form (CTQ-SF), Subjective Reaction to Antipsychotics (SRA), Subjective Well-Being under Neuroleptics (SWN), and medication data ( N = 235). Generalized linear regressions were conducted to examine associations between childhood trauma severity and side-effect outcomes. Models were adjusted for age, sex at birth, medication dose, and receptor profile. Moderation analysis was performed to assess whether sex influenced these associations. Results Childhood trauma severity was associated with more antipsychotic side effects, as assessed by both SWN ( p p = .001), independent of antipsychotic dose. The effect was also significant across all five SWN subscales and four out of seven SRA side-effect domains, namely, sedation, affective flattening, extrapyramidal symptoms, and diminished sociability. Moderation analyses showed no sex differences in SRA or SWN side-effect scores. Conclusions Childhood trauma may be related to more side effects of antipsychotics experienced in individuals with FEP, independent of sex. Clinicians could expect a greater burden of side effects in individuals with childhood trauma and be extra alert for these effects.

items.title: Gsx1 modulates endogenous progenitors to promote excitatory circuit remodeling following spinal cord injury.
items.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) activates endogenous neural stem and progenitor cells (NSPCs), yet their response is largely restricted to gliogenesis and insufficient for effective circuit repair. The homeobox transcription factor Gsx1 regulates excitatory interneuron specification during development, but its ability to reengage endogenous repair programs in the adult injured spinal cord remains unclear. Here, we show that AAV6-mediated Gsx1 expression promotes functional recovery after contusion SCI by linking acute progenitor state remodeling with chronic excitatory circuit reorganization. Gsx1 treatment significantly improved locomotor coordination and mechanical sensory recovery. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis during the acute phase revealed that Gsx1 shifts ependymal cells toward naïve and stem-like states and biases oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) away from proliferative programs toward myelinating and synaptogenic phenotypes. During the chronic phase, single-nucleus transcriptomics and histological analyses demonstrated a shift in neuronal composition toward excitatory interneuron identities, with pronounced enrichment of Chx10/Vsx2 + glutamatergic interneurons, enhanced synaptogenesis-related signaling, and increased neuronal activity. Mechanistically, Ascl1 knockdown in OPC-lineage cells attenuated early OPC responses, reduced chronic excitatory interneuron enrichment, and diminished Gsx1-mediated locomotor recovery. Together, these findings identify Gsx1 as a regulator of endogenous NSPC plasticity that redeploys developmental excitatory patterning programs to promote circuit remodeling and functional recovery after SCI.

items.title: Patients', family members' and healthcare professionals' attitudes towards medical assistance in dying on psychiatric grounds: systematic review of qualitative literature.
items.abstract: Background Medical assistance in dying on psychiatric grounds (MAiD-PS) is a complex issue of emerging international importance. Beyond existing research on the moral and legal aspects of MAiD-PS, more studies are now examining the attitudes of those directly involved. However, systematic comparison between the perspectives of patients, family members and healthcare professionals is still lacking. Aims This paper provides an overview of attitudes towards MAiD-PS across different countries, with specific attention paid to contrasting perspectives between respondent groups. Method This preregistered systematic review and metasynthesis of qualitative studies followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses and Enhancing Transparency in Reporting the Synthesis of Qualitative Research guidelines. Six databases were searched for 'attitudes', 'medical assistance in dying' and 'psychiatry'. Qualitative studies on attitudes towards MAiD-PS were included. Conceptual and normative papers were excluded. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Thematic analysis was employed to conduct the metasynthesis. Results Twelve qualitative studies (2018-2024) were included. Studies were categorised by population: patients, family members and healthcare professionals. Metasynthesis resulted in 15 themes. Despite substantial thematic overlap between groups, results show conceptual differences in their interpretations. Patients and family members primarily prioritise individual self-determination and dignity, whereas healthcare professionals focus on relational autonomy and the clinical challenges of establishing irremediability. Conclusions This is the first review to systematically compare perspectives across stakeholder groups, showing that attitudes towards MAiD-PS are intertwined with the respondent's role. The identified contrasts underscore the need for open discussions in which all stakeholder perspectives are recognised and heard, eventually leading to clinical guidelines that take into account stakeholder perspectives.

items.title: Global and National Perspectives on the Role of the WHO Model Lists of Essential Medicines.
items.abstract: Since 1977, the World Health Organization (WHO) Model Lists of Essential Medicines (EML) have guided countries in selecting medicines that address priority health needs. This study explores how global and national stakeholders interpret the role of the WHO EML and why its impact on access varies across therapeutic areas. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 52 participants across 17 countries. Data were analyzed thematically and mapped onto a two-axis framework reflecting trust in EML as a selection reference and control over access policies. Findings reveal that the influence of the EML was greatest where inclusion aligned with financing and procurement mechanisms, as seen in HIV and hepatitis C, where pooled procurement and voluntary licensing (and compulsory licensing as in the case of hepatitis C medicines) translated listing into tangible access gains. In contrast, in high-priced therapeutic areas, EML inclusion was often described as aspirational, reflecting clinical priority without resolving affordability or implementation barriers. In many national settings, the EML substitutes for formal health technology assessment but remains weakly connected to reimbursement and procurement decisions. Overall, the study indicates that the influence of the WHO EML depends on whether its normative authority is linked to concrete mechanisms that enable affordability and access.

items.title: Free-flying moths respond to bat-like ultrasound with a rapid powered dive directed away from the sound source.
items.abstract: Many nocturnal moths have evolved tympanal hearing to detect echolocating bats, and evade them by turning away, diving and flying erratically. These responses are well studied separately, but how free-flying moths combine them in a single escape, and which aerodynamic forces drive them, remains poorly understood. We analysed escape responses of tomato looper moths (Chrysodeixis chalcites) exposed to a bat-like ultrasound buzz (40 kHz) in a greenhouse. We reconstructed 447 flight trajectories from 11 ultrasound nights and 22 no-sound control nights. Before the stimulus, moths flew about 0.3 m s-1 faster on ultrasound nights, suggesting a sustained response to predation risk. Within 0.1-0.2 s of sound onset, moths dived at about 13° below the horizontal, irrespective of sound direction. They increased flight speed by 0.6 m s-1 and aerodynamic force by 0.7 times their body weight. A passive drop would have reduced the aerodynamic force, so the escape dives were powered. Escape directions were highly variable (circular standard deviation 74°), but on average pointed almost directly away from the sound (average offset 2°). This required a directional response to the sound. Moths with the source in front turned about 60° more than controls, and those with the source behind them about 25° more. Consequently, 80% ended with the source behind them (controls: 58%). Threatened moths thus fly faster before and during the escape, and steer powered dives away from the threat, yet unpredictably. Combining directional bias with variability may be a general escape strategy against fast, manoeuvrable predators.

items.title: GenErlangFit: a tool for estimating empirical waiting-time distributions to inform compartmental epidemic models.
items.abstract: In standard compartmental models of infectious diseases, assumptions about the duration of time spent in each state (e.g., latent period, infectious period) significantly influence model outcomes and interpretation. When represented deterministically as systems of ordinary differential equations or stochastically as Markov chains, these models often assume constant transition rates between states, which implies an exponential distribution of "waiting times" in each state. However, this assumption is not consistent with available data for many diseases. An alternative that remains analytically or computationally tractable is to model each state as a series of multiple identical substates, which results in a gamma (Erlang) distributed overall duration of time spent in each disease state (known as the "linear chain trick"). While well-known, few studies have presented formal methods for determining the optimal number of substates or extended this approach to encode a wider variety of distributions by including non-identical substates. Here we introduce GenErlangFit, an open-source R package and Shiny web application for fitting Erlang and related distributions to empirical waiting-time data. It combines maximum likelihood parameter estimation with parametric bootstrap hypothesis testing to prioritize the simplest model structures that produce waiting times consistent with observed data. To improve flexibility, we incorporate the Erlang-Exponential model, an extension of the standard Erlang distribution that adds a final exponentially-distributed stage with a unique transition rate, allowing better approximation of empirical distributions with varying skewness and tail behavior. The web application provides an accessible interface for modelers to fit empirical data and build parsimonious, data-driven compartmental models.

items.title: The Attraction of Anastrepha ludens to Myrcene, a Volatile Compound Derived from Host Fruits, is Enhanced by its Pheromone Constituents.
items.abstract: Chemical compounds play a crucial role in the communication of tephritid fruit flies. Anastrepha ludens males emit a pheromone and produce sounds to attract both conspecific females and males. Moreover, both sexes are attracted to host fruit volatile compounds. Nonetheless, it remains unclear whether the pheromone components influence A. ludens attraction to host fruit volatiles. Here, we asked whether the attraction of both sexes of A. ludens to myrcene, a volatile compound released by host fruits, is enhanced by male live volatiles, trans-tetrahydroactinidiolide (THA, a pheromone analogue), and two synthetic pheromone constituents [(Z)-3-nonenol and racemic 3,6-nonadienol]. We conducted bioassays in semi-natural settings using cylindrical field cages and Multilure traps. Overall, more females and males were captured in traps containing males + myrcene than in traps with myrcene alone. THA, however, was not attractive on its own, and did not enhance the attraction of females or males to myrcene. The attraction of females, but not males, to myrcene was enhanced by (Z)-3-nonenol. Furthermore, the attraction of both sexes to myrcene was augmented by 3,6-nonadienol and the other way around. Both sexes of A. ludens showed a stronger attraction to the combinations of myrcene, (Z)-3-nonenol, and 3,6-nonadienol, as well as myrcene and 3,6-nonadienol, compared to the combination of myrcene and (Z)-3-nonenol. The integration of fruit volatiles and pheromone constituents may be an effective approach to developing species-specific lures for monitoring A. ludens.

items.title: The predictive value of resilience for participation restrictions in people with spinal cord injury or acquired brain injury.
items.abstract: Participation and quality of life are often affected in people with spinal cord injury (SCI) or acquired brain injury (ABI). While most research has focused on physical disabilities and unmodifiable risk factors, the role of resilience and other psychological factors in predicting participation outcomes remains underexplored. To investigate the association between resilience at admission and participation restrictions in people with SCI or ABI six months after discharge. Prospective longitudinal cohort study. Twelve Dutch rehabilitation centers. Overall, 195 participants (100 with SCI, 95 with ABI; mean age 56 years, 56% male, mean time since injury five weeks). The Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC-10) and the Restrictions subscale of the Utrecht Scale for Evaluation of Rehabilitation Participation (USER-P-R) were the main predictive and outcome measures. Correlational and hierarchical regression analyses were performed. Baseline resilience was not significantly correlated with participation restrictions at six months after discharge (r=0.03). Regression analysis showed no significant association between resilience and participation restrictions after adjusting for other variables. The model explained 25% of the variance in participation restrictions (F (15, 169) =3.67, P<0.01). Physical independence showed the strongest association (r=0.36). No significant differences were found between diagnostic groups. Resilience early in rehabilitation was not associated with participation restrictions six months after discharge, after adjusting for relevant factors. As the six-month follow-up reflects an early phase of recovery and participation outcomes can continue to evolve over time, longer-term participation outcomes may not yet have been fully captured. Physical independence appears central to reducing objective participation restrictions, while psychological factors such as resilience may be more relevant to subjective aspects like satisfaction with participation. More research in this regard is needed.

items.title: Implementing a Mental Imagery Micro-Intervention to Improve Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Sessions: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Objective On the background of the broaden-and-build theory, this study tested whether the implementation of a mental imagery instruction aimed at enhancing positive affect at the beginning of therapy sessions improves the efficacy of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT). Methods Treatment data from 12 sessions were analyzed for n = 87 patients with emotional disorders and n = 25 therapists. The positive affect-focused instruction, as the experimental condition, was compared with CBT + neutral mental imagery instruction and treatment as usual as active control conditions. Both imagery instructions consisted of standardized 6-min interventions, in which patients were instructed to imagine a personal event from the last week. Primary outcomes were positive and negative affect, self-perceived strengths, resilience, and self-esteem. Secondary outcomes were psychological distress and working alliance. Data were analyzed using multilevel modeling. Results On average, the positive affect-focused instruction led to increased mood ratings at the beginning of therapy sessions. No significant differences favoring the positive mental imagery condition in comparison to the control conditions were found across outcome variables. Conclusion This study provides initial evidence supporting mental imagery as an ecological strategy to induce positive affect in individuals with emotional disorders, although no added benefits for treatment efficacy were found. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, Identifier: NCT03767101 (registered 2018).

items.title: Registered Report: Does the Relationship Between Intellectual Humility and Argument Quality Sensitivity Depend on Motivation and Cognitive Capacity?
items.abstract: Intellectual humility (IH) has been linked to analytical thinking and the ability to distinguish strong from weak arguments, known as argument quality sensitivity. However, it remains unclear whether this association reflects motivational factors, cognitive capacity, or both. Using an argument evaluation paradigm adapted from the persuasion literature, we experimentally manipulated participants' motivation and cognitive capacity to examine when IH predicts argument quality sensitivity. Consistent with previous research, IH was associated with greater sensitivity to argument quality, such that individuals higher in IH more effectively differentiated strong from weak arguments. Contrary to expectations, the experimental manipulations did not reliably influence argument quality sensitivity, limiting conclusions about the processes underlying this relationship. Furthermore, the association between IH and argument quality sensitivity did not vary across motivation or cognitive capacity conditions. These findings replicate prior work while highlighting the need for stronger tests of the mechanisms linking IH to argument evaluation.

items.title: Less Human in Herds: Social Crowding Contributes to Dehumanization.
items.abstract: As urbanization accelerates, social crowding has become a common daily experience. However, its impact on social interactions remains insufficiently understood. Prior work has emphasized social avoidance, but crowding may also shape how people perceive others. Across five studies ( N = 773), we applied dehumanization theory to the novel context of social crowding, showing that crowding fosters dehumanization with consequences beyond avoidance. Study 1 used natural language processing to analyze over 80,000 social media posts ( N = 71,093 users), revealing a link between crowding and dehumanizing language. Study 2 confirmed this through a field study, whereas Study 3 identified social avoidance as a pathway. Study 4 showed that suppressing social avoidance weakens crowding's impact on dehumanization. Finally, Study 5 demonstrated that dehumanization mediated the effect of crowding on aggression. These findings advance dehumanization theory and provide insights for promoting healthier social interactions in increasingly dense urban environments.

items.title: Worry as a mechanism of change in internet-delivered cognitive-behavioral therapy for generalized anxiety disorder.
items.abstract: Background Understanding how evidence-based treatments drive recovery remains a key challenge in psychotherapy research. Progress has been slowed by the lack of frameworks integrating theory of change with adequate design and dynamic modeling of longitudinal within-treatment data. We investigated worry as a candidate mechanism in therapist-guided internet-delivered cognitive-behavioral therapy (iCBT) for generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). We formulated a multimethod framework to examine dynamics between worry and (1) anxiety-related impairment and (2) somatic GAD symptoms. Methods Our sample comprised 8,870 patients (78.2% women) receiving a 12-session iCBT for GAD. In sessions 1, 6, and 12, worry and anxiety-related impairment were assessed with the Penn State Worry Questionnaire (PSWQ) and the Overall Anxiety Severity and Impairment Scale (OASIS), respectively. Across sessions 1-12, the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) was used to assess worry and somatic GAD symptoms. Non-Gaussian direction of dependence analysis modeled global dynamics between PSWQ and OASIS, while continuous-time structural equation modeling (CT-SEM) modeled local dynamics between GAD-7 scores. Results Non-Gaussian analyses indicated directional dependence from worry to anxiety-related impairment throughout treatment. CT-SEM revealed bidirectional cross-effects consistent with a feedback mechanism whereby worry may increase somatic symptoms, which then reduce subsequent worry. Moreover, CT-SEM suggested that unobserved common-cause mechanisms may contribute substantially to worry-somatic symptom dynamics. Conclusions Our findings support worry as a plausible mechanism of change in iCBT for GAD, particularly aligning with the contrast avoidance CBT model. The study illustrates a multimethod framework combining theory-guided design and dynamic modeling to evaluate mechanisms of change in routine care.

items.title: The fertility crisis and post-labor social architecture: Why Elon Musk should build FamilyLand.
items.abstract: Low fertility partly reflects a weakening of the pathway through which attraction leads to pair-bonding and childbearing. Modern mating ecologies allow mating to remain active while making family-forming partnerships harder to achieve, producing a Post-Pair-Bonding Fertility Trap. This article uses that evolutionary diagnosis to develop FamilyLand, an institutional prototype for post-labor life, in which residents would be freed from economically necessary work. Private family life would be embedded within communities designed to strengthen social connections, make childrearing less isolating, and make family formation more attractive and fulfilling. FamilyLand would simulate a future of AI-enabled material abundance before it exists society-wide, testing whether such conditions can strengthen pair-bonding and fertility realization rather than deepen social isolation. Elon Musk is identified as the clearest candidate to build FamilyLand because he combines the technological resources and capacity to realize such an ambitious project with a deep concern about declining fertility.

items.title: Neurocognitive deficits in controlling aversive memory in insomnia disorder.
items.abstract: Background Insomnia disorder is a common sleep disturbance characterized by cognitive hyperarousal, such as intrusive and uncontrollable thoughts (e.g. thoughts about sleeplessness, worries). Memory control, a key self-regulatory ability to control or inhibit unwanted thoughts and memories, plays an essential role in supporting cognitive functions and emotional well-being. Here, we delineate the neurocognitive mechanisms underlying memory control among individuals with insomnia. Methods Forty-one participants meeting DSM-5 criteria for insomnia disorder and 40 healthy sleepers completed an emotional Think/No-Think task, during which they were instructed to either retrieve (Think), suppress the retrieval (No-Think) of aversive memories, or visually process cues without retrieval or suppress retrieval (Perceptual Baseline). At the same time, electroencephalographic (EEG) activity was recorded. Results Linear mixed model analyses with age and depression scores as covariates showed that the insomnia group exhibited impaired memory control abilities, as evidenced by reduced suppression-induced forgetting during memory recall compared with the healthy group. Electrophysiologically, the insomnia group showed enhanced P300, a well-established neural marker of conscious episodic retrieval, in the No-Think condition compared to the Perceptual Baseline condition, indicating residual episodic retrieval during memory suppression. In contrast, this difference was absent among the healthy group, suggesting successful inhibition or abolishment of the memory traces. Conclusions Individuals with insomnia showed impaired memory control of aversive memories and aberrant electrophysiological activities during retrieval suppression. Future research shall investigate the neural mechanisms underlying memory control deficits in insomnia disorder and the causal relationship between memory control abilities and insomnia symptoms.

items.title: Data-driven classification for avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder.
items.abstract: Background ARFID is a heterogeneous illness characterized by restrictive eating secondary to sensory sensitivity, lack of interest in eating or food, and/or a fear of aversive consequences. Research utilizing data-driven approaches to examine the nosology of ARFID is scant, but needed to inform etiological inquiry and treatment planning. We aimed to examine whether a hybrid categorical-dimensional model of ARFID could explain within-ARFID heterogeneity. Methods We used Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview (PARDI) data from 188 children, adolescents, and adults to fit a Gaussian finite mixture model (GFMM) to inform the nosology of ARFID. The data were collected from three separate National Institute of Mental Health-funded studies. Results The best-fitting GFMM identified four classes, indicating that ARFID symptom distribution varied across the groups. We labeled the groups: Mild Interest-Sensory Phenotype ( n = 115, 61%), Mild Three Phenotype ( n = 30, 16%), Moderate-to-High Three Phenotype ( n = 27, 14%), and High Fear-Interest/Mild Sensory Phenotype ( n = 16, 9%). Validation analyses supported significant differences among the GFMM-identified groups, such that the Moderate-to-High Three Phenotype and High Fear-Interest/Mild Sensory Phenotype groups were more severe compared to the Mild Interest-Sensory Phenotype and the Mild Three Phenotype groups. Finally, results supported the dimensionality of sensory sensitivity and lack of interest and found that fear of aversive consequences may be more categorical. Conclusions Our results found support for a hybrid categorical-dimensional model of ARFID and provided a new exploratory framework that could guide future etiological and treatment research efforts.

items.title: Does autism still mean something?
items.abstract: Autism has expanded from a narrowly defined childhood condition to a heterogeneous spectrum diagnosed across the lifespan. Rather than asking whether this expansion has made autism meaningless, we suggest a different test: does the category continue to predict systematic differences in how people think, decide, and behave?

items.title: Association between remitted major depressive disorder and subsequent risk of cognitive deficit and neurocognitive disorders - A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: In late life, a major depressive episode (MDE) is often a prodrome for dementia. Several studies have also shown that even an MDE in full remission is a risk factor for dementia, including when the MDE occurred years earlier. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the extent to which a diagnosis of remitted major depressive disorder (rMDD) is associated with cognitive deficits or a diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or dementia in late life. We searched PubMed, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, EMBASE, and Web of Science from inception through May 2, 2026 for peer-reviewed publications that examined cognitive performance or a diagnosis of MCI or dementia in older adults with rMDD. We narratively synthesized and meta-analyzed findings; 50 publications were included reporting on 28 separate studies with nonoverlapping participant groups (6,512 participants with rMDD and 60,493 healthy controls [HCs]). Of 24 studies assessing cognitive performance, 19 (79.2%) supported that rMDD is associated with cognitive deficits in late life. Of six studies assessing diagnoses with rates reported in both groups, three (50.0%) supported that rMDD increases the risk of MCI or dementia. All 24 studies assessing cognitive performance were meta-analyzed; while there was significant heterogeneity among the studies, individuals with rMDD demonstrated significantly worse performance than HCs for global cognition and each of the seven cognitive domains analyzed. Overall, our results strongly support that rMDD is associated with cognitive deficits in late life. Older adults with a history of rMDD require individualized risk assessment for cognitive decline.

items.title: Examining mindfulness-based exercises, relaxation practices and Strategies for Safety and Well-being in English primary and secondary schools (INSPIRE): multi-school, cluster-randomised controlled trial.
items.abstract: Background Schools may be a suitable place to deliver mental health interventions to children and young people, yet the evidence base is insufficient. Aims The INSPIRE trial aimed to evaluate three interventions in schools across the UK: a mindfulness-based intervention (MBI), relaxation-based practice intervention (RBPI) and Strategies for Safety and Well-being (SSW), compared with usual practice. Method INSPIRE was a parallel, cluster-randomised controlled trial. Eligible participants were pupils in primary and secondary schools across England who were in Years 4 and 5 (aged 8-10 years, primary schools) or Years 7 and 8 (aged 11-13 years, secondary schools) at baseline. Primary outcomes were emotional difficulties for MBI and RBPI, and intended help-seeking for SSW (both at 3-6 months). Results A total of 213 schools were randomised, including 20 489 pupils (primary: 145 schools, 9731 pupils; secondary: 68 schools, 10 758 pupils). In primary schools, intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis for MBI versus control ( n = 3732) found no improvement in emotional difficulties (standardised mean difference (SMD) 0.002, 95% CI -0.08 to 0.08). For RBPI versus control ( n = 3731), there was no improvement in emotional difficulties (SMD = -0.01, 95% CI -0.10 to 0.07). For SSW versus control ( n = 3453), there was an improvement in intended help-seeking (SMD = 0.09, 95% CI 0.01-0.18). In secondary schools, ITT analysis for MBI versus control ( n = 3791) found no improvement in emotional difficulties (SMD = -0.07, 95% CI -0.18 to 0.05). For RBPI versus control ( n = 3531), there was no improvement in emotional difficulties (SMD = -0.10, 95% CI -0.24 to 0.02). For SSW ( n = 3762), there was no improvement in intended help-seeking (SMD = 0.07, 95% CI -0.03 to 0.18). Conclusions SSW led to improvements in help-seeking in primary school children. There was no evidence that MBI or RBPI were effective at reducing emotional difficulties in either primary or secondary schools.

items.title: A fentanyl vaccine adjuvanted with a TLR7/8 agonist does not precipitate withdrawal in fentanyl-dependent rats but does block fentanyl's acute reinforcement-enhancing effects.
items.abstract: Rationale Opioid use disorder (OUD) and overdose involving synthetic opioids such as fentanyl are major public health problems. Vaccines against opioids have several advantages over current OUD pharmacotherapies (e.g., longer duration of action), can reduce several OUD- and overdose-related effects of fentanyl and other opioids in animals, and are being evaluated in clinical trials. A potential concern regarding this approach is that the resulting reduction in brain opioid levels could precipitate withdrawal symptoms (e.g., anhedonia), which could motivate relapse. Objective This study assessed the potential for the anti-fentanyl vaccine F 1 -CRM + INI-4001 to precipitate withdrawal in fentanyl-dependent rats as measured by elevations in intracranial self-stimulation (ICSS) thresholds (anhedonia-like behavior), weight loss, and somatic (physical) withdrawal signs. We also evaluated the ability of F 1 -CRM + INI-4001 to attenuate the acute ICSS threshold-lowering (i.e., reinforcement-enhancing) effects of fentanyl in fentanyl-naïve rats. Methods and results Despite eliciting a strong anti-fentanyl antibody response and increasing serum fentanyl levels, vaccination with F 1 -CRM + INI-4001 did not precipitate withdrawal in fentanyl (0.3 mg/kg/day)-dependent rats as measured by elevation of ICSS thresholds, weight loss, or somatic signs. However, F 1 -CRM + INI-4001 did attenuate the amount and duration of weight loss during spontaneous fentanyl withdrawal. F 1 -CRM + INI-4001 also reduced the acute ICSS threshold-lowering effects of fentanyl (0.0032-0.01 mg/kg, s.c.), indicating reduced fentanyl abuse liability. Conclusions These findings support the safety and efficacy of F 1 -CRM + INI-4001 in preclinical models of OUD and support its evaluation for the treatment of OUD and prevention of overdose in clinical trials.

items.title: Vaginal Birth in Women After One Previous Caesarean Delivery at Term: A Population-Based Study.
items.abstract: Background Guidelines quote a vaginal birth rate after caesarean delivery of 74%. This, however, is based on studies that include women who have also had a previous vaginal birth. Women with one caesarean delivery who are now in their second pregnancy may not have the same rate. Objective To determine the vaginal birth rate among these women who laboured, its associated factors and maternal and neonatal morbidity. Methods Routinely collected Queensland Perinatal Data were obtained for women with a singleton pregnancy, cephalic presentation at ≥ 37 weeks' gestation and who birthed in a public maternity facility in Queensland, Australia, during the period 2011-2021. Results In 6787 women who laboured, the vaginal birth rate was 49.3%. Factors associated with vaginal birth were midwifery-led care (adjusted risk ratio [aRR] 1.13, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05, 1.22) and private accommodation in a public hospital (aRR 1.10, 95% CI 1.01, 1.19). Maternal age > 30 years [30-34 years (aRR 0.93, 95% CI 0.87, 0.98), 35-39 years (aRR 0.87, 95% CI 0.80, 0.95) and 40+ years (aRR 0.79, 95% CI 0.64, 0.98)], smoking (aRR 0.86, 95% CI 0.79, 0.95), overweight (aRR 0.92, 95% CI 0.87, 0.98) and obesity [30-39 kg/m 2 (aRR 0.87, 95% CI 0.81, 0.93), 40+ kg/m 2 (aRR 0.84, 95% CI 0.72, 0.98)] and having any form of diabetes (aRR 0.87, 95% CI 0.80, 0.95) were associated with a decreased likelihood of vaginal birth. Uterine rupture rate was lower in women who birthed vaginally (0.2% vs. 1.5%; aRR 0.18, 95% CI 0.08, 0.41); their newborns had lower rates of resuscitation (16.9% vs. 24.4%; aRR 0.79, 95% CI 0.74, 0.85) and admission to a special care or intensive care unit. Conclusions In this select group of women who laboured, the vaginal birth rate was lower than what is currently quoted. This finding may assist clinicians and such women in making an informed choice on mode of birth.

items.title: Biosecurity discourse among horse owners and veterinarians in the United Kingdom.
items.abstract: Despite its importance for disease prevention, biosecurity implementation across the equine industry remains inconsistent. Horse owners and veterinarians may describe biosecurity differently, which may shape how biosecurity advice is communicated and interpreted. Examining how biosecurity is talked about can provide insight into how it is described and understood within each group. To identify and compare patterns in how horse owners and veterinarians talk about biosecurity. Qualitative study situated within a post-structuralist framework. Individual semi-structured interviews were conducted with 23 horse owners and 14 veterinarians across the United Kingdom between December 2018 and November 2019. Transcripts were analysed using Foucauldian discourse analysis. Three patterns were identified: contrasting ways of framing biosecurity, differing accounts of responsibility for biosecurity, and expressions of distrust between veterinarians and horse owners. Both participant groups described biosecurity as difficult to implement but did so in contrasting ways, with veterinarians emphasising procedural complexity and population-level responsibility, and horse owners emphasising practical challenges and individualised care. Responsibilities were described using metaphors, hedging, and blame-shifting, with differing accounts of who was responsible for which tasks. Distrust between groups was evident in how participants talked about the other group, with frustration, scepticism, and dismissiveness appearing in both sets of accounts. Findings are based on accounts from a self-selected sample, do not represent direct observations of behaviour, and may not capture the range of ways in which biosecurity is talked about across the wider equine industry. Horse owners and veterinarians described biosecurity and responsibility in different ways, and distrust was evident in how each group talked about the other. These differences may be relevant to understanding challenges in communication between groups. Reflecting on how clients, responsibility, and expertise are talked about in everyday interactions may support more constructive and collaborative veterinary communications.

items.title: Adopting legal frameworks for public health: a toolkit for physical activity and nutrition policy, implementation, and evaluation.
items.abstract: Public health challenges such as physical inactivity and unhealthy diets demand policy responses that operate upstream of individual choice. Our perspective connects exposure-response evidence for physical activity (PA) and lifestyle factors with legal levers shaping environments. We argue that coherent legal frameworks are indispensable tools for shaping healthier environments at population scale while protecting autonomy through least-restrictive and equity-oriented design. Drawing on international evidence and illustrative examples, we synthesise legal strategies that shift price signals, availability, marketing exposure, procurement standards, and built environment in ways that make routine PA and healthy diets easier defaults. We then frame these elements as strategic considerations for public-health proponents and policymakers: equity and proportionality, transparency and safeguards against undue influence, enforceability, intersectoral coordination through Health in All Policies, and built-in monitoring and evaluation to improve legitimacy, adaptation, and durability. Finally, we outline an evaluation pathway grounded in legal epidemiology and policy surveillance: systematic approaches for specifying, coding, comparing, and monitoring laws and their implementation over time, enabling jurisdictions to identify gaps, learn from others, and link legal change to health and equity outcomes. These elements form a practical 'legal toolkit' for jurisdictions seeking measurable reductions in exposure to inactivity and unhealthy food environments.

items.title: Associations of fat mass and fat-free mass accretion in early childhood with body composition and cardiometabolic markers at age 10 years: the Ethiopian iABC birth cohort.
items.abstract: There is limited evidence on how fat mass (FM) and fat-free mass (FFM) accretion in childhood influence adiposity and cardiometabolic health later in life. We aimed to examine associations of FM and FFM accretion in periods from 0-60 months with body composition, abdominal subcutaneous and visceral fat, and cardiometabolic markers at a mean age of ∼10 years (range: 7-12 years). In the Ethiopian iABC birth cohort, FM and FFM was measured using air-displacement plethysmography. We applied linear spline mixed-effects modeling to estimate FM and FFM accretion during infancy (0-3, 3-6 months) and early childhood (6-48, 48-60 months) in 403 children. The analytical sample ranged from 312 to 307 participants across the outcomes. Multiple linear regression analysis was used to examine associations of FM and FFM accretion in each period with outcomes at age 10 years. FM accretion between 0-3 and 6-48 months was associated with a higher body mass- and FM index, while FFM accretion in all periods was associated with greater height and FFM index at 10 years. FM and FFM accretion from 6-48 months were associated with higher and lower abdominal subcutaneous fat, respectively. Furthermore, FM accretion from 3-6 months was associated with higher systolic blood pressure and glucose levels. FM accretion from 6-48 months was associated with higher fasting insulin, C-peptide, and HOMA-IR, whereas FFM accretion from 6-48 months was associated with lower total and LDL cholesterol. Overall, FM accretion in early infancy and from 6-48 months was linked to adiposity and higher glucose metabolism markers, while FFM accretion from 6-48 months was associated with lower unfavorable lipids, suggesting potential cardiometabolic benefits.

items.title: Hospital Disaster Resilience Under Climate Test: Learnings From a Flooding Event Due to Heavy Rains in Metropolitan City of Delhi.
items.abstract: Extreme weather events expose hospitals to risks of disruption in the delivery of essential health care services. Insights into mitigation or response measures offer valuable learnings for resilience planning. This study is a retrospective case report that reconstructs the sequence of events in a level 1 trauma center during the June 28, 2024 Delhi floods, based on incident and inquiry reports. The qualitative narrative examines the cause, administrative decisions, and mitigation measures. Heavy rains led to flooding that disrupted patient care, laboratory, and support services. A multidisciplinary team of doctors and engineers, under the leadership of the Additional Medical Superintendent, supported by the Hospital Administrators and guided by the Chief of Hospital as Incident Commander, coordinated the response through the hospital administration control room. Admissions were restricted and elective surgeries suspended, and patients were transitioned to manual ventilation or horizontally evacuated to safer zones with an alternate power supply. Drainage was initiated and later augmented with additional pumps and flood barriers. Central sterile supply services and laundry services were arranged from nearby blocks, and mortuary bodies were shifted out to a nearby hospital. The case emphasizes the importance of preventive and dynamic maintenance engineering and architectural safeguards into hospital systems for making health care facilities disaster resilient.

items.title: Cancer-Risk Numeracy Among U.S. Adults: Observations from HINTS 2024.
items.abstract: Understanding numerical risk information is important for informed decisions about cancer prevention, screening, and treatment. This study estimated national respon​ses to a cancer-risk numeracy item, distinguishing incorrect answers from uncertainty, and examined their correlates. This study analyzed data from the Health Information National Trends Survey 7 (HINTS 7, 2024). Respondents were asked which probability of developing cancer was greater: 1in 100 or 1 i​n 1,000. Survey-weighted multinomial logistic regression modeled responses (correct [reference], incorrect, "don't know"), adjusting for age, sex assigned at birth, race/ethnicity, education, income, and cancer history. An exploratory model added questionnaire language, self-rated health, and act​ivity limitations, using imputed income. Among 6,697 respondents, 69.8% answered correctly (95% CI, 68.1-71.5), 4.7% incorrectly (95% CI, 3.9-5.8), and 25.4% "don't know" (95% CI, 23.8-27.1). In adjusted analyses (n = 6,006), the probability of answering "d​on't know" was higher with less than high school versus college education (17.3 percentage points; 95% CI, 7.9-26.7), income <$20,000 versus ≥$75,000 (13.5 percentage points; 95% CI, 6.9-20.2), and among non-Hispanic Black (23.5 percentage poin​ts; 95% CI, 17.9-29.1), Hispanic (17.2 percentage points; 95% CI, 12.1-22.3), and non-Hispanic Asian (18.2 percentage points; 95% CI, 6.6-29.8) versus non-Hispanic White adults. Older age was associated with "don't know" relative to correct responses (relative risk ratio​ per decade, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.12-1.32). In an exploratory model (n = 6,178), activity limitations were associated with a 6.1-percentage-point higher probability of incorrect responses (95% CI, 2.5-9.6). One in four U.S. adults were unsure which of two cancer probabilities was greater, with marked sociodemographic disparities. Cancer educator​s should pr​esent risks with consistent denominators and confirm patients' understanding rather than assume it.

items.title: A Systematic Review of Data to Care: Practical Considerations for Health Departments.
items.abstract: Data to care is a public health strategy to improve care engagement among people with HIV (PWH). Health departments face common barriers to the success of data to care programs, particularly the relatively low accuracy of surveillance data for identifying and contacting out-of-care PWH. We conducted a systematic review focused on practical approaches for health departments to more effectively reach out-of-care PWH. Across 31 publications describing data to care programs using public health surveillance data, a median of 20.2% (IQR 10.7-36.3%) of investigated cases led to a PWH who was confirmed to be out of care. Programs that incorporated other data sources, such as HIV clinic records, more efficiently identified out-of-care PWH. Supplementing surveillance-based data to care efforts with additional data sources like clinical records or real-time alerts at points of clinical contact can improve the efficiency of finding PWH who are truly out of care.

items.title: Sustainable Removal of Ciprofloxacin from Aqueous Media Using Pine Needle Biosorbent.
items.abstract: The increasing use of antibiotics and the inadequacy of conventional treatment systems contribute to their accumulation and the spread of antibiotic resistance in aquatic environments, posing significant environmental and public health concerns. In this study, the removal of ciprofloxacin from aqueous solutions by adsorption was investigated using a low-cost and environmentally friendly biosorbent derived from pine needles. The biosorbent was prepared using a water-based modification method and characterized in terms of surface morphology, specific surface area, and pore properties. The effects of operational parameters, including solution pH, adsorbent dose, initial ciprofloxacin concentration, and contact time, on biosorption performance were investigated. Despite its low specific surface area (1.13 m²/g) and macroporous structure, the biosorbent exhibited high removal efficiency. The pH at the point of zero charge (pHpzc) was determined to be 4.77. Considering the amphoteric nature of ciprofloxacin and the surface charge of the adsorbent, electrostatic interactions, as well as hydrogen bonding and π-π interactions, are considered to contribute to adsorption under neutral and slightly acidic conditions. High removal efficiency (> 90%) was achieved under the optimum conditions of pH 7, an initial ciprofloxacin concentration of 30 mg/L, a contact time of 90 min, and an adsorbent dosage of 100 mg/50 mL. Kinetic analyses indicated that the adsorption process followed a pseudo-second-order model, while equilibrium data were best described by the Langmuir isotherm, yielding a maximum adsorption capacity of approximately 47.6 mg/g. Thermodynamic analysis indicated that the adsorption process was spontaneous and exothermic and was predominantly governed by physical interactions. These findings demonstrate that pine needle-derived biosorbents represent a sustainable and economical alternative for antibiotic removal from aqueous media.

items.title: Fabrication of a novel electrochemical aptasensor for accurate detection of benzylpenicillin in food: egg, milk, and meat.
items.abstract: The presence of antibiotic residues in food poses an important public health concern, since they may lead to the emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacterial strains. Creating an accurate, simple, and quick analytical instrument is essential for food safety analysis. This work presents a novel label-free electrochemical aptasensor for the precise detection of benzylpenicillin, a widely used antibiotic, in animal-derived foods. The carbon paste electrode (CPE) is modified by the use of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and MnFe2O4 nanoparticles (NPs) as conductive and high-surface area nanomaterials. The electrode surface morphology was analyzed using a field emission scanning electron microscope (FESEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX). The electrode surface provided an ideal scaffold for the covalent immobilization of the benzylpenicillin-specific aptamer. Each phase of aptasensor fabrication is defined by cyclic voltammetry (CV), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and square wave voltammetry (SWV). The aptasensor performance was optimized by adjusting factors such as aptamer concentration, aptamer immobilization time, aptamer-analyte interaction time, and aptamer-analyte interaction temperature using SWV. The developed aptasensor, designated Apt/CNT/MnFe2O4/CPE, can reliably detect benzylpenicillin within two linear ranges: 1 fM to 10 pM and 10 pM to 1 μM, with a detection limit of 0.21 fM. The developed aptasensor is an effective electrochemical instrument for the measurement of benzylpenicillin in food products, including milk, meat, and egg.

items.title: Predicting pediatric stroke outcomes using adult lesion-symptom models
items.abstract: Lesion location is a key predictor of post-stroke outcomes in adults, but its relevance for predicting childhood stroke outcomes is unclear. Recent developmental neuroscience work suggests that the gross spatial organization of large-scale brain systems may be generally conserved across development, raising the possibility that damage to common anatomical substrates might underlie chronic domain-level impairments after both adult-onset and childhood stroke. If so, then it should be possible to leverage adult lesion-symptom relationships to predict chronic childhood stroke outcomes. We tested the hypothesis that lesion-symptom models trained to predict sensorimotor and language impairments in patients with adult-onset brain lesions can be translated to predict chronic sensorimotor and language outcomes after childhood stroke. We trained multivariate lesion-symptom models to predict sensorimotor (Grooved Peg-Board Test: N=463; median age=53.6, IQR=17.9 years) and language (Token Test: N=379; median age=53.2, IQR=19.4 years) impairments in patients with adult-onset brain lesions. We applied the trained models to lesion segmentations from childhood stroke survivors enrolled in the SCOUTS Study (N=469; median age=9.3, IQR=11.0 years), resulting in outcome predictions that we compared against chronic (6+ month) measures of sensorimotor and language impairment derived from the Pediatric Stroke Outcome Measure and the Recurrence and Recovery Questionnaire. The adult lesion-symptom models generated outcome predictions that robustly correlated with pediatric impairment scores (sensorimotor: rho=0.43; language: rho=0.42; PFWE <0.001), enabled classification of pediatric impairment status (both AUC=0.76; PFWE=0.004), and afforded unique predictive power in multivariable pediatric outcome models (sensorimotor: adjusted OR=3.6, 95% CI=2.4-5.2; language: adjusted OR=3.0, 95% CI=1.67-5.30). Lesion-symptom models trained using pediatric lesion and outcome data captured robust lesion-symptom relationships (both rhocv=0.40, P<0.001), but yielded no advantage over the adult model predictions when compared directly via cross-validation in the pediatric cohort. Further, the adult and pediatric models made similar predictions when applied to the same lesion data even after adjusting for common effects of lesion size and laterality, suggesting a general convergence towards common anatomical signals present in both children and adults. Lesion-symptom models trained in patients with adult-onset brain lesions can be translated across outcome measures and developmental stages to predict chronic sensorimotor and language impairments after childhood stroke. These results establish lesion location as an important predictor of childhood stroke outcomes, demonstrate the feasibility of translating adult lesion-symptom models for chronic outcome prediction in children, and support the broader conclusion that the critical anatomy underlying post-stroke sensorimotor and language impairments may be generally conserved across development.

items.title: The Coherence Problem: Integrating Computational, Phenomenological, and Network Accounts of Psychopathological Transformation
items.abstract: Psychotic and affective states alter not only what a person thinks and perceives, but how coherently their experience hangs together. Phenomenological, computational, network-neuroscience, and dynamical-systems traditions have each characterized aspects of this alteration, but largely in isolation from one another. This paper argues that these traditions converge on a shared control problem. If inference on the brain's recurrent architecture tends toward self-reinforcing certainty, as the paper proposes, then the system must continuously counteract that drift or experience reorganizes. Bipolar disorder provides the clinical lens because it resists the compartmentalization the field has imposed: the condition can produce manic, psychotic, depressive, and mixed configurations, and no account designed for one configuration readily extends to the others. A minimal decomposition, targeting the entry, propagation, and temporal depth of coherence, maps these psychopathological presentations as neighboring regions in a shared space and reframes the explanatory question: which control policies sustain proportionate coherence in ordinary cognition, and how they destabilize.

items.title: Cumulative Adversity Moderates Associations Between Brain Microstructure and Body Mass Index in Early Adolescence: Sex-Specific Patterns in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study.
items.abstract: Purpose Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are stressful, traumatic events associated with higher pediatric obesity risk and variation in neurodevelopment; optimal neurodevelopment is needed to make healthy decisions. It remains unclear whether cumulative adversity modifies associations between the brain and body mass index (BMI) during early adolescence, a developmental window with rapid neurobiological remodeling and increasing autonomy over health behaviors. Methods Using data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study℠ (release 5.1, n = 4,627; ages 11-12), we tested whether ACEs moderated associations between neurobehavioral outcomes and BMI. Neurobehavioral measures included macrostructural (e.g., cortical thickness, subcortical volume) and microstructural (e.g., Restricted Normalized Isotropic; Restricted Normalized Directional) metrics from 22 cortical and 16 subcortical regions, and behavioral measures (e.g., Behavioral Inhibition System/Behavioral Approach System, Positive Urgency, Impulsive Behavior Scale, NIH Toolbox). Sex-stratified linear mixed-effects models tested ACE × neurobehavioral interactions on BMI, adjusting for age, puberty, and education (random effects: scanner/site, where appropriate); Benjamini-Hochberg corrected. Results In males, ACE exposure significantly moderated associations between BMI and microstructure. Significant ACE × Restricted Normalized Isotropic interactions were observed cortically (e.g., left caudal anterior cingulate, posterior cingulate, right insula), and subcortically (e.g., bilateral accumbens, pallidum, putamen, left caudate, right hippocampus). ACE × Restricted Normalized Directional interactions were observed in the bilateral putamen, and right caudate and pallidum. No moderation effects were observed for macrostructure or behavioral neurobehavioral measures, or in females. Discussion Cumulative adversity may strengthen sex-specific associations between microstructure and BMI during early adolescence. Microstructural markers may capture stress-sensitive neurodevelopment variation not reflected in macrostructure or behavioral assessments, highlighting potential early neurobiological markers of vulnerability during a critical developmental window.

items.title: Enduring increases in attachment security following psychedelic retreats: prospective pre-, post-, and follow-up findings.
items.abstract: Attachment theory offers a promising framework for understanding psychedelic experiences and outcomes, yet evidence remains limited. In this preregistered prospective longitudinal study (N=173), psilocybin retreat participants were assessed at seven timepoints, from baseline through 12 months post-retreat, on dispositional (ECR) and state (SAAM) attachment and acute psychedelic experiences. In covariate-adjusted linear mixed-effects models, baseline avoidance modestly predicted more challenging experiences and less favorable perceptions of the retreat environment. Contrary to expectations, attachment anxiety did not predict mystical experiences. As predicted, dispositional avoidance ( d s = 0.41-0.50) and anxiety ( d s = 0.20-0.26) decreased, and state security increased ( d s = 0.22-0.59) across follow-up, with the largest changes among participants higher in baseline insecurity. Mystical experiences predicted greater changes in state attachment and, more modestly, reductions in dispositional anxiety. Psychedelic retreat experiences were thus followed by enduring increases in attachment security, particularly among insecure individuals, with mystical experiences predicting change.
