items.title: Cumulative Sedentary Behavior is Associated with Increased Default Mode Network-Sensory Coupling in Young Adults.
items.abstract: BackgroundSedentary behavior is increasingly recognized as a lifestyle exposure with implications for cardiometabolic and cognitive health, yet its neural correlates in young adulthood remain poorly characterized. Young adulthood represents a developmental period marked by continued refinement of large-scale brain networks, making it a potentially sensitive window for lifestyle-related neural adaptations. The default mode network (DMN), a core intrinsic network supporting self-referential processing, memory, and executive functioning, is metabolically demanding and highly sensitive to both vascular and behavioral influences, positioning it as a plausible neural substrate through which sedentary behavior may impact brain health. This longitudinal study examined whether cumulative sedentary behavior is associated with intrinsic functional connectivity of the DMN in young adults and whether these relationships differ across resting-state conditions.MethodsParticipants were healthy young adults (n = 32) enrolled in the Healthy Student Brain study. Using Fitbit monitoring, sedentary behavior was quantified as total sedentary minutes across an eight-week period (Study Days 1-56). Resting-state fMRI data were acquired under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions and processed using the NeuroMark pipeline to derive reproducible intrinsic connectivity networks. Post-intervention network-level functional connectivity was computed between the DMN and major large-scale networks and regressed onto baseline connectivity metrics. Pearson correlations assessed associations between total sedentary minutes and DMN coupling for each resting condition.ResultsGreater total sedentary time was associated with stronger DMN coupling with sensory networks. Specifically, sedentary minutes were positively correlated with DMN-visual connectivity during both eyes-open ( r = .38, p = .05) and eyes-closed rest ( r = .40, p = .05). Sedentary behavior was also associated with increased DMN-sensorimotor connectivity during eyes-closed rest ( r = .38, p = .034), but not during eyes-open rest. No significant associations were observed between sedentary time and DMN connectivity with cognitive control, subcortical, cerebellar, or auditory networks.ConclusionsIn this preliminary study of healthy young adults, cumulative sedentary exposure was associated with greater DMN coupling with sensory systems, particularly visual and sensorimotor networks. Given the modest sample size, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. Larger studies would enable us to determine whether sedentary behavior is robustly associated with state-dependent alterations in intrinsic brain network organization.

items.title: Automated Interictal Epileptiform Discharge Detector Scores in Serial EEG: Record-Level Concordance Did Not Extend to Within-Participant Change.
items.abstract: ObjectiveAutomated deep learning-based interictal epileptiform discharge detectors have been validated for cross-sectional recognition, but longitudinal concordance is uncertain. We tested whether three distinct pretrained detectors agreed on direction and rank ordering of within-participant change in serial EEG.MethodsThis secondary analysis included 45 routine EEG recordings from 15 adults with drug-resistant focal epilepsy at baseline, week 1, and month 3 in the active arm of a parent tDCS trial; treatment efficacy was not evaluated. SpikeNet1, SpikeNet2, and Cyclops used pretrained weights and detector-specific pipelines on identically staged 25-min intervals. The record-level endpoint was the unthresholded mean window score. Concordance was characterized using record-level and change-score Spearman correlations, directional agreement, and a standardized detector × time repeated-measures ANOVA.ResultsDescriptive record-level correlations ranged from ρ = 0.341 to 0.696. Change-score correlations ranged from -0.011 to 0.379 (week 1) and from -0.089 to 0.536 (month 3). All six were smaller in absolute magnitude than their record-level counterparts and nonsignificant after Holm adjustment. Three-detector directional agreement was 7/15 (week 1) and 6/15 (month 3). The detector × time interaction was nonsignificant (Greenhouse-Geisser-corrected p = .142). Post hoc tolerance zones did not increase three-detector agreement. Thresholded SpikeNet2 and Cyclops outputs were sparse, and high-threshold agreement reflected shared zero change.ConclusionsRecord-level concordance did not extend to within-participant change or establish longitudinal interchangeability of mean window scores. Even for validated detectors, a longitudinal finding from one detector should not be assumed to generalize across detectors without independent corroboration. Parent trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05951244), NCT05951244.

items.title: Predicting Seizure Recurrence After Withdrawal of Antiseizure Medications Through Electroencephalogram Connectivity Analysis: A Proof-of-Concept Study.
items.abstract: BackgroundDetermining antiseizure medication (ASM) withdrawal in patients with prolonged seizure freedom is crucial, yet no reliable biomarker exists. Pediatric neurologists often rely on clinical risk factors and electroencephalogram (EEG) inspection to predict recurrence.MethodsWe applied EEG connectivity analysis using directed transfer function (DTF) to predict recurrence after ASM withdrawal in 63 patients (29 recurrence, 34 nonrecurrence). All patients were seizure-free for at least 2 years before their ASMs were withdrawn. Before ASM withdrawal, an EEG was obtained for each patient, and indicated the absence of epileptiform discharges. Classification was conducted with feature selection and five classifiers.ResultsThe statistical results revealed that the DTF connectivity in the motor regions, including the right primary motor cortex (Brodmann area 4, BA4) and the left and right medial premotor regions (Brodmann area 6, BA6), was significantly higher in the recurrence group. The highest average performance across the five evaluated classifiers (sensitivity, 87.50%; specificity, 87.35%; accuracy, 87.28%; and AUC, 87.43%) was achieved when 16 DTF features were selected. Compared with the majority-class baseline of 53.97% (representing the proportion of the majority non-recurrence class, 34/63), all trained classifiers demonstrated vastly superior performance. Among these classifiers, SVM had the best individual performance index, achieving a sensitivity of 96.67%, specificity of 90.58%, accuracy of 93.36%, and AUC of 93.63% while 16 selected features were used.ConclusionsThe method effectively identified Brodmann areas with significant differences and built models distinguishing recurrence from nonrecurrence at the patient level.

items.title: When the Part B of the Trail-Making Test is not applicable: Clinical meaning in cognitive disorders due to neurodegenerative etiologies.
items.abstract: BackgroundIn clinical settings, it is not an infrequent occurrence that patients with cognitive disorders successfully complete the Part A of the Trail-Making Test (TMT-A) while being unable to complete the Part B (TMT-B).ObjectiveThis study investigated the correlates and determinants of the non-applicability of the TMT-B, despite the TMT-A being applicable, in a cohort of patients with cognitive disorders due to neurodegenerative etiologies.MethodsThis retrospective cohort included 461 patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI, N = 161) or dementia ( N = 300) due to Alzheimer's disease (AD), frontotemporal lobar degeneration, Lewy body disease, mixed (i.e., AD and chronic cerebrovascular load) and unspecified neurodegenerative etiologies. Linear/generalized linear models examined whether TMT-B non-applicability predicted performance across both first- and second-level cognitive measures, years of education, and disease status (MCI versus dementia), adjusting for relevant demographic and clinical confounders. A logistic model aimed to determine whether global cognitive efficiency, education, and disease severity independently predicted TMT-B non-applicability net of relevant demographic and clinical covariates.ResultsThe TMT-B was not applicable in the 42.3% of patients. Across all cognitive measures considered, TMT-B non-applicability was consistently associated with poorer cognitive performance. Non-executers/-completers had significantly lower educational attainment and were more likely to present with dementia (versus MCI). Finally, lower MMSE scores, lower educational attainment and dementia status independently predicted TMT-B non-applicability.ConclusionsThe TMT-B non-applicability in patients with neurodegenerative cognitive disorders reflects more widespread cognitive involvement and is possibly indicative of dementia status, being also associated with lower educational attainment.

items.title: ENAH binding to the huntingtin proline-rich domain modulates HTT1a assembly.
items.abstract: The proline-rich domain (PRD) of huntingtin (HTT), located C-terminal to the polyglutamine tract within the exon-1 region, plays a critical role in modulating the aggregation and toxicity of mutant Huntingtin exon-1 fragment (HTT1a). To identify PRD-interacting proteins, we performed mass spectrometry analysis of PRD peptide pulldowns from human neurons. ENAH, a member of the Ena/VASP family of actin regulatory proteins, emerged as the top enriched interactor from neuronal membrane fractions. In neurons, ENAH colocalized with HTT1a species, suggesting a biologically relevant interaction. Because the Enabled/VASP homology 1 (EVH1) domain of ENAH binds polyproline motifs with high affinity, we examined its interaction with HTT1a using recombinant proteins. EVH1 directly bound HTT1a and unexpectedly formed condensate-like assemblies capable of recruiting HTT1a monomers. Remarkably, EVH1 robustly suppressed HTT1a oligomerization and promoted remodeling of preformed HTT1a fibrils in vitro. These findings demonstrate that ENAH-PRD interactions modulate HTT1a aggregation dynamics and identify EVH1 assembly as a potential proteostatic mechanism regulating mutant HTT1a states. More broadly, this work establishes a framework for investigating how EVH1-containing proteins may influence HTT1a proteostasis and neurotoxicity in Huntington's disease.

items.title: rTMS attenuates microglial phagocytosis and promotes neurorepair in a photothrombotic stroke mouse model.
items.abstract: Objective This study investigated the effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) on functional recovery in photothrombotic (PT) stroke mice and whether rTMS promotes neurorepair by modulating microglial phagocytosis. Methods Eight-week-old male C57BL/6J mice were used to establish a focal stroke model via photothrombosis (PT group). The Sham group and PT + rTMS group were included. rTMS was initiated 24 h after modeling. Neurological deficits were assessed. Microglial activation, synaptic phagocytosis, neuronal injury and the levels of tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and interleukin-1β (IL-1β) were evaluated. Differentially expressed proteins and core regulatory pathways were analyzed. Results rTMS treatment significantly increased body weight, prolonged the latency to fall and shortened the balance beam crossing time, reduced foot faults, and improved the discrimination index in PT mice. rTMS reduced the number of Iba1-positive microglia and CD68-positive cells, attenuated microglial synaptic phagocytosis and alleviated neuronal loss and apoptosis. rTMS significantly decreased the levels of TNF-α, IL-6 and IL-1β in the brain. A total of 416 differentially expressed proteins were identified between the PT and PT + rTMS groups. The differentially expressed proteins were significantly enriched in microglial phagocytosis pathways and related signaling pathways. Conclusions rTMS significantly ameliorates neurological deficits and cognitive impairment in PT stroke mice. The underlying mechanism may involve the inhibition of excessive microglial activation, attenuation of microglia-mediated synaptic phagocytosis and alleviation of neuroinflammation. Proteomic analysis reveals that rTMS modulates the expression of proteins associated with microglial phagocytosis-related signaling pathways, which may contribute to the observed post-stroke neurorepair effects.

items.title: Birth position and tissue context influence bipolar cell translocation mode in the developing retina.
items.abstract: Neuronal translocation is essential for establishing functional tissue architecture in the developing central nervous system. While many of the cell-intrinsic mechanisms driving translocation have been identified, how these strategies adapt to dynamic developmental tissue changes remains less understood. Here, we address this question using zebrafish retinal bipolar cells as a model, as they are generated across unlaminated and laminated stages, which enables direct comparison of neuronal translocation modes and dynamics across development. We show that the mode of movement of bipolar cells changes depending on tissue lamination state. Bipolar cells born before photoreceptor layer formation undergo directed, microtubule-dependent somal translocation, as seen for other early born neurons. In contrast, later-born bipolar cells exhibit more passive and less directed displacement that seems to be mostly driven by collective tissue movements. Interference with tissue-wide movements reduces this displacement, while disrupting photoreceptor layer formation also leads to directed translocation at later developmental stages. Independent of strategy, cells achieve accurate laminar positioning. Together, this shows that tissue context can influence cell movement modes, a principle likely relevant across developing neural and other tissues.

items.title: Disentangling homogeneous and heterogeneous representation of human functional connectome via graph learning.
items.abstract: Objective. Functional connectivity analysis of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data provides critical insight into large-scale brain organization; however, conventional approaches often ignore the specific information mixed with population-level structure and individual- or condition-specific variability. We aimed to develop an interpretable framework that separates these shared and heterogeneous components of the human functional connectome. Approach. We developed Joint Individual Graph Learning (JIGL), a multi-view graph learning framework that jointly estimates a low-rank common graph and sparse view-specific graphs across subjects or experimental conditions. We evaluated JIGL using resting-state and task-based fMRI data from 422 individuals across eight conditions and compared it with Pearson correlation, SIMLR (CIMLR), and Simplex. Performance was assessed using alignment with established resting-state network (RSN) organization, associations with age and cognitive phenotypes, task identifiability, and low-dimensional representations of task-specific connectivity. Main results. The common graph learned by JIGL captured a biologically meaningful functional backbone and showed stronger alignment with established RSN organization than the comparison methods. JIGL-derived individual graphs preserved biologically relevant inter-individual variability, yielding stronger associations with age and cognitive phenotypes. The task-specific graphs also showed improved identifiability, as quantified by the intraclass correlation coefficient. Furthermore, low-dimensional embeddings of the connectivity matrices revealed structured, network-dependent task signatures that were consistently distinct from both the common graph and the resting-state condition. Significance. JIGL provides a principled framework for disentangling shared functional architecture from individual- and condition-specific connectivity patterns. This decomposition improves sensitivity to biologically meaningful variability and supports more interpretable analyses of functional brain organization across individuals and cognitive states.

items.title: Monte Carlo simulation of a neuroimaging acquisition with MAPSSIC, aβ+sensitive intracerebral microprobe for awake and freely moving rats.
items.abstract: Objective. Establishing robust correlations between molecular neuroimaging and behavioral studies is essential in preclinical research to advance our understanding of brain function and to critically assess the translational relevance of animal models in drug development. Achieving this goal, however, requires imaging animals while they are awake and freely moving-an ongoing challenge, as most preclinical imaging techniques rely on anesthesia. Approach. To overcome the limitations imposed by anesthesia, the MAPSSIC project aims to develop a novel implantable pixelated probe based on monolithic active pixel sensors (MAPS), designed for use in awake, freely moving rats. By virtue of its direct implantation within the targeted brain regions, the MAPSSIC probe enables the local detection of short-rangeparticles emitted by radiotracers, in contrast to conventional micro-PET systems that rely on detecting coincident annihilation-rays. In this study, we present Monte Carlo simulations of a typical in vivo brain imaging experiment using [C]Raclopride, a commonly employed-emitting radiotracer, to evaluate the probe's performance. Main results. Results show that over 93% of detected events originate from particles emitted within the first 2 mm surrounding the probe while also allowing to quantify variations of 5%-30% of the non-displaceable binding potential (BP) with discrepancy of less than 4% compared to micro-PET. Significance. This Monte Carlo study demonstrates the device's ability to capture small variations of BPbased on spatially localized information, validating its suitability for quantitative kinetic analysis in brain structures such as the striatum.

items.title: Bipolar intracortical microstimulation expands the repertoire of neuronal activation patterns.
items.abstract: Objective . Intracortical microstimulation is a promising approach for sensory restoration, but its spatial selectivity is limited, and the variability of evoked percepts is influenced by current spread and electrode configuration. We investigated how varying the return-electrode position during intracortical bipolar stimulation influences the spatial distribution and composition of activated neuronal populations. Approach . We combined two-photon calcium imaging in acute mouse cortical slices with biophysically grounded computational modeling to characterize neuronal activation at the cellular and population level. We applied bipolar stimulation across a range of electrode configurations, systematically varying current direction, electrode spacing, and stimulation parameters. Main results . Bipolar stimulation activated distinct neuronal populations depending on electrode configuration, with activation patterns showing less overlap as the angular difference between stimulation directions increased. Population-level analyses revealed a small number of dominant activation patterns across stimulation configurations. Electrode spacing influenced both the number of activated neurons and the spatial extent of activation, whereas polarity and waveform asymmetry had comparatively modest effects. Computational modeling indicated that bipolar activation predominantly reflected the combined effect of the two corresponding monopolar stimulations, with an additional bipolar-specific component. Neurons activated exclusively by bipolar stimulation were relatively sparse and spatially dispersed. Significance . Our findings demonstrate that varying bipolar electrode configurations produces distinct patterns of neuronal activation, providing an additional mode for recruiting different neural populations. Computational modeling suggests that these patterns largely reflect the combined contributions of the individual electrodes, with additional differences that may reflect nonlinear neuronal or network interactions. Together, these findings provide insight into how the electrode configuration shapes cortical activation patterns and how intracortical bipolar stimulation provides additional ways to activate neuronal populations without increasing electrode density.

items.title: A small set of morphological metrics describes wing-planform plasticity: a correlational analysis in a population of the European grapevine moth Lobesia botrana (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae)
items.abstract: The insect wing is a complex morpho-functional organ, and it remains unclear whether a set of well-defined metrics can fully capture wing-planform variation. To address this question, we digitised 339 male forewings of the European grapevine moth, Lobesia botrana (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae), an economically important grapevine pest. Specimens came from two non-overlapping seasonal flight generations. We applied two complementary shape-analysis methods - Generalised Procrustes Analysis (GPA) and Elliptic Fourier Analysis (EFA) - and correlated their principal components with four flight-related morphological metrics: aspect ratio (AR), a proxy for the second moment of wing area (MA), sweep angle (SA), and apex taper (Taper). For both methods, each of the first four principal components was most strongly correlated with its corresponding metric; together, these components represented 92.3% (GPA) and 95.7% (EFA) of the total variation of the shape. Both methods yielded concordant results, indicating that a small set of interpretable metrics captures the major axes of wing-planform variation. Generations differed significantly in mean MA, AR, and SA, and in Taper variance, consistent with seasonal phenotypic plasticity. These characters can be calculated from a small number of landmarks and therefore can serve as wing-shape markers. The analysis pipeline is implemented in the open-source MorphoGet software. This protocol provides an interpretable summary of wing-planform variation, applicable to flight-related morphology, ecology and evolution, pest monitoring, and other fields.

items.title: Rodent Plant Diets Show Dimension-Specific Variation Across Contrasting Forest Habitats.
items.abstract: Habitat heterogeneity can alter consumer resource use, but different components of diet may not respond in parallel. Using plant metabarcoding of stomach contents from 319 rodents across five contrasting forest habitats in Xinglong Mountain, China, we reconstructed the plant diets of rodents using both relative read abundance (RRA) and occurrence-based data and compared five dietary dimensions: composition, breadth and overlap, phylogenetic structure of consumed plants, and rodent-plant network topology. Dietary composition varied with habitat in a species-dependent manner. Within the broadly distributed Apodemus peninsulae, transect-level habitat differences were detected in occurrence-based but not RRA-based diets. Phylogenetic structure also differed among habitats, with primary coniferous forest showing weaker average phylogenetic clustering than several other habitats. By contrast, dietary breadth and overlap showed no significant habitat differences under either data representation. Network responses were metric-dependent: Most metrics showed no clear habitat signal, with only RRA-based standardized modularity showing an isolated habitat effect. Overall, habitat-associated variation was dimension-specific, expressed more clearly in dietary composition and phylogenetic structure than in aggregate breadth, overlap, or network properties. These findings indicate that aggregate dietary metrics alone may miss ecologically relevant variation in resource use and argue for integrating compositional, phylogenetic, and network perspectives when assessing consumer responses to habitat heterogeneity.

items.title: Ocular findings in northern gannets (Morus bassanus) following an outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1).
items.abstract: Background Between 2021 and 2022, high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) caused mass mortality in wild birds, with northern gannets (Morus bassanus) among the most affected. Following the outbreak, unusual alterations in the characteristic pale iris of this species were observed in some individuals. Methods Gannets opportunistically captured on Bass Rock (n = 51) were examined using slit-lamp biomicroscopy, rebound tonometry and photography. Eleven birds underwent avian influenza virus (AIV) serology. Paired eyes from two birds underwent histopathology and were compared with an archival sample. Results Iris hyperpigmentation affected 73% of adult and immature gannets, with 60% affected bilaterally. Additional signs consistent with uveitis were present in 77% of affected birds. Iris pigmentation abnormalities were positively associated with AIV H5 seropositivity (Fisher's exact test, p = 0.018). Histopathology of affected eyes showed increased melanin deposition, loss of a distinct anterior melanocytic layer and hypertrophy of iris stromal melanin-laden cells. Limitations Field conditions limited uniform lighting and concurrent serology. Few eyes were available for histopathology. Conclusions Iris pigmentation changes were associated with HPAI exposure and frequently accompanied by signs of uveitis, suggesting such alterations may indicate past infection and chronic sequelae.

items.title: Native amphibians in modern European zoos.
items.abstract: Historically, zoos and aquariums have focused on displaying exotic animals. However, the biodiversity crisis has driven a paradigm shift, with modern zoos evolving into integrated conservation hubs at the nexus of species safeguarding, species recovery, and societal engagement. Despite this shift, native amphibians remain underrepresented in European zoos, largely overshadowed by non-native exotic species. The extent to which this pattern reflects institutional priorities or visitor preferences is unclear. This study assessed the value placed on native amphibian fauna by both zoological institutions and their visitors. A survey of zoos accredited by the European Association of Zoos and Aquaria (EAZA) revealed that although nearly a third of institutions house native species, these often comprise only a small fraction of their overall amphibian holdings. Additionally, zoos with a stronger focus on threatened species tend to have a greater representation of native species, irrespective of the country's native diversity or their conservation status. Native amphibians are primarily used for education and research (both ex situ and in situ), with their presence in the surveyed zoos mainly influenced by their threatened status rather than their nativeness. Our case study of visitor preferences showed a clear preference for the display and conservation of local fauna over non-native species when perceptual biases were controlled. Although most zoos will likely continue to focus on exotic species, our findings suggest that increasing the representation of native species offers an underexplored opportunity to bolster public support for local conservation efforts.

items.title: Heart rate, metabolic rate and developmental time: local adaptations in thermal plasticity decrease developmental costs in prairie lizards.
items.abstract: Embryonic development in ectotherms is strongly shaped by temperature, yet the multivariate nature of metabolism complicates attempts to link local thermal environments to developmental physiology and energetic costs. In this study, we examined embryonic heart rate, metabolic rate (V̇CO2) and developmental time in two populations of the prairie lizard, Sceloporus consobrinus, from a cool, northern versus a warm, southern environment. Eggs from each population were incubated at 25 and 31°C to test for countergradient variation in developmental physiology and assess how populations differentially use these physiological pathways in relation to developmental cost and time. To that end, we evaluated predictions of developmental cost theory, which posits that the energetic cost of development is a product of metabolism and developmental time, with natural selection acting on each to minimize developmental costs, although the two phenotypes respond to temperature differently. Developmental time decreased with increasing temperature in both populations, but embryos from the cool environment developed faster overall, consistent with countergradient variation. Across populations and temperatures, heart rate and metabolic rate were dissociated: at the warmer incubation temperature, cool-population embryos exhibited higher heart rate but lower metabolic rate relative to the warm population, achieving faster development at lower estimated energetic cost, whereas reliance on increased metabolic rate in the warm population produced slower development and higher costs. These results show that populations can evolve distinct combinations of physiological traits to meet similar developmental challenges and underscore the complex nature of metabolism as a multivariate trait when predicting ectotherm responses to thermal variation.

items.title: The Quantitative Psychologist Is Dead, Long Live the Quantitative Psychologist
items.abstract: Much of what quantitative psychologists publish consists of developing statistical methods, implementing them in software, and evaluating them in simulation studies. I argue that artificial intelligence (AI) can already do much of this work, and that its share will only grow. The quantitative psychologist has always been a jack of all trades, combining programming, statistics, and psychological knowledge without being a master of any one of them. AI is now the better jack of all trades. When methods become cheap, value moves to what AI cannot supply and to what it newly makes possible. I describe three directions: collecting trustworthy data from real people, formalizing psychological theory now that computational modeling is within reach of any researcher, and rethinking methodological educationso that students learn to judge the analyses that AI will run for them. Thespecialist role built around producing methods for others will fade, whilequantitative thinking spreads through all of psychology.

items.title: The Quantitative Psychologist Is Dead, Long Live the Quantitative Psychologist
items.abstract: Much of what quantitative psychologists publish consists of developing statistical methods, implementing them in software, and evaluating them in simulation studies. I argue that artificial intelligence (AI) can already do much of this work, and that its share will only grow. The quantitative psychologist has always been a jack of all trades, combining programming, statistics, and psychological knowledge without being a master of any one of them. AI is now the better jack of all trades. When methods become cheap, value moves to what AI cannot supply and to what it newly makes possible. I describe three directions: collecting trustworthy data from real people, formalizing psychological theory now that computational modeling is within reach of any researcher, and rethinking methodological educationso that students learn to judge the analyses that AI will run for them. Thespecialist role built around producing methods for others will fade, whilequantitative thinking spreads through all of psychology.

items.title: Automating Personality Research with LLMs
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have been shown to reproduce central aspects of human personality. This correspondence creates opportunities to automate research, but its theoretical value will depend on what LLMs recover and what accounts for their discrepancies with human data. We propose a heuristic distinction between model-derived variance--the regularities in human personality data recoverable from LLM predictions—and residual variance--the structure that remains unexplained by those predictions. LLM-human correspondence may reflect several factors, such as general semantic structure, culturally shared beliefs, scientific findings in LLM training corpora, or psychometric fine-tuning. Residual variance, in turn, may reflect model limitations, population-specific variation, or psychological information not captured in language. Using this distinction, we examine three applications in personality psychology with substantial potential for automation: enhancing assessment, improving conceptual clarity, and simulating human respondents. Current evidence suggests that linguistic representations account for a substantial share of LLM–human correspondence, with psychometric fine-tuning providing additional gains; however, the relative contribution of other factors remains unresolved. We argue that automation can contribute to conceptual progress to the extent that the sources and limits of LLM–human correspondence are identified. Doing so can establish what similarities and divergences reveal about personality itself and where automation is justified.

items.title: Do Scales Semantically Resemble the Sources They Cite? Embedding Analysis of Construct Proliferation in Five Anomy Instruments
items.abstract: Construct proliferation in psychology is associated with jingle and jangle fallacies that psychometric methods are not designed to detect. Semantic embeddings offer a complementary approach, but existing applications have compared scales within a single level without bringing in the theoretical texts a construct's tradition rests on. This study extends the embedding framework of Wulff and Mata (2025a) to across-level comparison paired with a documentary audit of citation acts. We embedded 43 items from five anomy scales alongside 3,762 propositions extracted from nine source texts at three analytical levels (foundational texts, scale articles, and items), using six embedding models from three architectural families, and we coded every passage in which a scale article cites a theoretical source. Items formed thematic clusters that crossed scale boundaries, beyond the expression of a single homogeneous theme per instrument, while retaining within-scale cohesion, and were rarely nearest to the article that introduced them (14%). All five scale articles were semantically nearest to Merton's (1938) text, a pattern identical across models, stable under bootstrap resampling, and not reproduced by two genre-matched control texts. The documentary audit showed that no article adopts Merton's formulation; the two articles that adopt a foundational text both adopt Durkheim's Suicide, which was the nearest foundation for neither of them. This proximity coexists with the absence of any direct adoption of Merton. This extension, combining semantic proximity with documented citation acts, offers an approach for examining whether the sources an instrument cites are also the ones its content most resembles.

items.title: Jargon as a Psychological Construct? A Multidecade Analysis of Communication Failure in Evaluation Reports
items.abstract: For seven decades, studies have asked whether the people who receive psychological evaluation reports understand what they say. Existing research has largely measured reader satisfaction rather than what readers comprehend, recall, or interpret. This narrative synthesis identified six studies, conducted between 1984 and 2025 in school psychology and, most recently, child neuropsychology, in which 253 readers were assigned to a standard-format report and had their comprehension scored directly. Comprehension ranged from 46.6% to 61.1% (weighted mean = 55.2%) and showed no detectable change across four decades. In every study that also scored an accessible version of the same report, readers understood it better, with scores from 60% to 82%. Recent evidence from pediatric neuropsychology shows the same gap: parents rated their understanding of their child's report highly, yet almost half could not state the child's diagnoses without error. Effective formats combined plain-language wording with one or more of domain-based organization, concrete behavioral examples, and elaborated recommendations. These findings suggest that jargon-related comprehension failure is a persistent, measurable, and modifiable problem spanning specialties within psychology. Implications for training, supervision, and evidence-based communication practice across school and clinical psychology are discussed.

items.title: The Psychology of Algorithmic Bias
items.abstract: Algorithmic bias—the systematic discrimination of disadvantaged social groups by AI systems—is widely documented, yet its psychological foundations remain poorly understood. We argue that algorithmic bias originates primarily from human prejudice and social cognition, which shape AI training data and use of AI systems. We introduce the psychology-centered Human–AI Loop model that explains how biases can enter an AI system during its creation and consumption, specifying the psychological mechanisms operating at each entry point. These mechanisms and their interactions create feedback loops through which AI systems amplify, perpetuate, and obscure existing prejudices and social inequalities. We then outline psychology-informed strategies for disrupting these cycles and discuss implications for theories of prejudice and discrimination in the age of AI.

items.title: Worlding the Self: The Ecological Constitution of the Pattern Theory of Selflessness
items.abstract: This paper develops the ecological dimension of the pattern theory of selflessness (PTSL), reconceptualizing its six transformations (T1–T6) as organism-environment enactments. Drawing on ecological psychology and enactivism, it argues that ecological processes are constitutive rather than merely causal contributors to self-pattern transformation: affordances, affective scaffoldings, and social ecologies are not contextual backdrops but co-creators of each transformation. Integrating a relational account of affordances and the distinction between the landscape and the field of relevant affordances with the PTSL's six-transformation model—and drawing on canonical Buddhist sources and ethnographic research on Thai, Burmese, and secular practice contexts—each transformation is shown to involve a distinct mode of ecological participation, from ethical consolidation (T1) and engineered ecologies of attention (T2) to cross-contextual mindful awareness (T3), withdrawal of ordinary self-scaffolding (T4), flexible organism-environment coupling (T5), and irreversible ecological reorientation in self-liberation (T6). Taking the organism-environment system as the unit of analysis specifies testable empirical signatures that distinguish the constitutive hypothesis from causal alternatives.Note: Preprint (Author's Original Manuscript) of an article accepted for publication in Mindfulness (Springer Nature, 2026). Version of Record: https://doi.org/10.1007/s12671-026-02980-x

items.title: From Preprocessing to Interpretation: Current Practices of Machine Learning in Psychological Research
items.abstract: The application of machine learning methods is becoming increasingly widespread across psychology and related disciplines. However, there is limited knowledge of how and for what purposes researchers employ machine learning to analyze psychological data. To investigate the extent and form in which machine learning is applied in psychological research, we developed a structured description framework that consists of five major steps: (1) data assessment and preprocessing, (2) model fitting, (3) identifying informative variables, (4) interpreting their relationship with the outcome variable, and (5) reporting. Using this framework, we systematically examined current practices employed in psychological and psychiatric research articles published in 2022 and between June 2024 and May 2025 that used one or more of three widely applied supervised machine learning models (specifically, random forests, support vector machines, and neural networks) for data analysis. We observed that the majority of researchers (1) used low-dimensional data typical for the psychological field, despite the fact that a particular advantage of machine learning methods is their ability to deal with high-dimensional data, (2) performed a variety of model fit evaluation approaches using cross-validation and train-test splits, which are important strategies for avoiding overfitting, (3) used machine learning approaches to identify informative variables, but (4) did not use the full potential of interpretable machine learning techniques for interpreting the relationship between these variables and the model’s outcome. Furthermore, we observed incoherent reporting practices of machine learning analyses (5). Although first reporting recommendations for machine learning in psychology exist, they have yet to be consolidated into field-wide standards that researchers routinely follow.

items.title: Fifty Shades of Well-Being: Addressing an Overlooked Source of Confusion in the Science of Well-Being.
items.abstract: Despite constant progress, the science of well-being remains marked by confusion, with a proliferation of competing conceptual frameworks, theoretical approaches, and measurement tools undermining both scientific progress and real-world applications in areas such as counseling, therapy, and public policy. This paper identifies an overlooked contributor to this confusion: the adoption of Philosophically Dense Concepts (PDC) into empirical science, facilitated by academic practices that favor theoretical novelty and discourage interdisciplinary collaboration. Using a conceptual genealogy of the hedonic-eudaimonic well-being distinction as a paradigmatic example, I show how such PDC, when translated from philosophy into psychology and social and health sciences, became semantically fuzzy and led to inconsistent theoretical frameworks and measurement tools. The paper concludes with recommendations on how to better deal with PDC in well-being research and the emerging science of flourishing.

items.title: An Autobiographical Narrative Reveals How Implementation Mechanisms Shaped the Collapse of the 1994 South Korean University Admissions Reform
items.abstract: Abstract Educational reforms can fail not because their goals are misguided but because implementation mechanisms are misaligned with institutional conditions. This Perspective examines South Korea’s 1994 university admission reform proposed by the Presidential Commission on Education Reform (PCER). The proposal sought to reduce dependence on university-specific written examinations and strengthen comprehensive high school records in university selection. Although the direction received broad support within the commission, members disagreed over timing: the author argued for three to five years of preparation, whereas the majority supported implementation only five months before the admission cycle. President Kim Young-Sam rejected the proposal approximately seven hours after its public announcement. Drawing on autobiographical narrative, contemporaneous policy materials and media coverage, Jerome Bruner’s cultural psychology, and Cho Dong-Sung’s SER-M framework, the article interprets the episode through the interaction of Subject, Environment, Resource, and Mechanism. Clandinin and Connelly’s concepts of temporality, sociality, and place situate the lived experience; Bruner’s concepts of folk pedagogy, cultural scripts, intersubjectivity, and subjunctivity explain competing meanings; and SER-M illuminates how political urgency consumed preparation time and weakened consultation and feedback. The discussion considers possible longer-term institutional effects, including continued reliance on high-stakes external assessment and private tutoring, without claiming that the 1994 episode directly or solely caused these developments. It concludes with four principles for resilient reform: protected preparation time, stakeholder intersubjectivity, iterative feedback, and institutional continuity.

items.title: Psycho-Social Factors of Non-Suicidal Self Injury Among Adolescents Admitted to Tertiary Psychiatric Centre.
items.abstract: BackgroundNon-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is a significant concern among adolescents, particularly in inpatient mental health settings. This study explores common psychosocial factors of NSSI.MethodsThe study was conducted at a tertiary psychiatric centre and involved a retrospective chart review of 80 adolescents aged 12 to 18 years who were admitted between August 2023 and January 2024. Adolescents with severe mental illness, neurodevelopmental disorders, and severe medical conditions were excluded. Data were extracted from case records using a semi-structured proforma developed by the researcher.ResultsThe mean age of the adolescents was 15.13 (SD = 1.57) years, with a gender distribution of 62.5% female. Analysis of psychosocial factors revealed that poor parenting practices (76.3%), attachment ruptures (71.3%), caregiver burden (66.3%), family conflicts (62.5%), negative expressed emotions (65%) and financial constraints (37.5%) were prevalent. A majority (71.3%) of documents noted four or more psychosocial risk factors. Gender-wise comparison showed that females more frequently reported multiple adversities. A significant association was found between a higher cumulative number of risk factors and repeated psychiatric hospitalisations (χ 2 = 9.814, p = 0.007), indicating the impact of cumulative adversity on clinical severity.ConclusionThe study highlights the multifactorial influences on phenomena such as NSSI among adolescents. Poor parenting practices and family conflicts were among the most commonly reported psychosocial adversities among adolescents with NSSI, emphasising the need for targeted interventions focusing on family dynamics and support systems.

items.title: Three decades since Daubert I: Performance and symptom validity tests in forensic contexts.
items.abstract: The year 2023 witnessed an important anniversary in forensic psychological practice. In 1993, the United States Supreme Court issued the classic decision in Daubert v Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals, Inc. , providing guidance on criteria for admissible scientific evidence in legal proceedings. Daubert was followed by two other decisions, and collectively they comprise the Daubert trilogy. The article examines psychological validity tests used in forensic and related disability assessments: they are widely used psychometric tests designed to assess neuropsychological test performance and psychological symptom/problem reporting - performance validity tests (PVTs) and symptom validity tests (SVTs), respectively. The article especially examines research design in the field, key statistics, especially error rate and classification accuracy, the efficacy of PVTs and SVTs compared to clinical opinion, frameworks for determining invalid response set, the fail rate for invalid response set, malingering and related attributions, PVT and SVT test interpretation, and conundrums in PVT battery and combined PVT-SVT battery interpretation. In sum, the current state of the literature clearly demonstrates that performance and symptom validity testing has robust empirical support and meets Daubert standards such that PVTs and SVTs are appropriate for routine use in forensic settings. Finally, the article identifies future research avenues for validity testing.

items.title: Evaluating Health Professional Burnout and Job Satisfaction Using the US Surgeon General's Framework for Workplace Mental Health and Well-Being.
items.abstract: Objectives Burnout among US physicians, nurses, and other health professionals is a major issue. We assessed associations between health professional burnout and job satisfaction with workplace factors represented in the US Surgeon General's Framework for Workplace Mental Health and Well-Being. Methods Health professionals (N = 588) from across the United States participated in a survey conducted from 2022 through 2024. We used the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health Worker Well-Being Questionnaire to measure health professionals' perceptions of their workplace environment. We used the US Surgeon General's Framework for Workplace Mental Health and Well-Being as an analytical framework for examining relationships between burnout and job satisfaction and framework domains. Data analysis included descriptive statistics, bivariate analysis, factor analysis, and logistic regression. Results Higher levels of protection from harm (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 0.71; 95% CI, 0.65-0.78; P P = .003) significantly reduced the likelihood of burnout. Health professionals who were not satisfied with their opportunities for growth had higher odds of burnout (AOR = 2.10; 95% CI, 1.30-3.50; P = .003) and lower odds of job satisfaction (AOR = 0.26; 95% CI, 0.17-0.41; P P = .01). Conclusions Future research should evaluate the effectiveness of interventions designed to improve physical and psychological safety, workplace value and recognition, and opportunities for employee growth.

items.title: Altered cerebellar-cerebral connectivity in the imbalance between goal-directed and habitual systems in obsessive-compulsive disorder.
items.abstract: Background Compulsive behaviors in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) are thought to stem from an imbalance between the goal-directed and habitual systems. This hypothesis has been further supported by connectome-level neural evidence. Although the cerebellum has increasingly been implicated in OCD, its specific involvement in goal-directed and habitual systems, as well as alterations in OCD, remains unclear. Methods This study examined cerebellar-cerebral connectivity by analyzing multimodal networks underlying the goal-directed and habitual systems in 51 patients with OCD (39 male) and 59 healthy controls (HC, 37 male). Simulated lesion approaches and modularity analysis were used to assess the involvement of distinct cerebellar regions in the goal-directed and habitual systems. Further modular interaction analysis was performed to examine differences in cerebellar-cerebral connectivity between patients and controls. Results Simulated lesion analyses demonstrated that removing cerebellar Crus I/II disrupted network integration in both groups, whereas lobules V/VI had a similar effect in HC but not in OCD. We identified a distinct modular organization, with Crus I/II clustering in the goal-directed module and lobules V/VI in the habitual module. Both functional and structural measures indicated that patients with OCD exhibited enhanced intra-module connectivity within the habitual module, which correlated with compulsive symptom severity in the OCD group. Conclusions This study provides evidence that cerebellar-cerebral connectivity patterns are associated with goal-directed and habitual systems, with distinct regions showing differential involvement in these processes. It may provide further insight into the neural correlates underlying the imbalance between goal-directed and habitual systems in patients with OCD.

items.title: Development and Validation of the Spanish-Language Risk Prevention and Harm Reduction Strategies Scale for People who Snort Cocaine.
items.abstract: Cocaine use carries substantial health, social, and legal risks, yet validated instruments to assess risk prevention and harm reduction strategies in this population are lacking. This study developed and psychometrically evaluated the Risk Prevention and Harm Reduction Strategies Scale (RPHRS) for Spanish-speaking people who snort cocaine. Method: Overall, 550 people who snort cocaine, from 16 Spanish-speaking countries, completed an online survey on harm reduction strategies, cocaine use, and related consequences. The sample was randomly split for exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n = 279) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n = 271). Results: EFA yielded a five-factor, 22-item structure explaining 43.7% of the variance, and CFA showed adequate fit (CFI = .916, RMSEA = .046, SRMR = .067). McDonald's omega ranged from .65 to .83 and composite reliability from .62 to .82, whereas average variance extracted exceeded .50 for only one factor. Discriminant validity was supported (HTMT r = -.13) and consequences ( r = -.33). Conclusions: The RPHRS shows preliminary validity for five harm reduction domains. Two subscales need refinement and replication before clinical use.

items.title: Cultural adaptation and pilot validation of the Menopause-specific Cognitive Scale (Meno-Cog) among Chinese women: Mixed-methods study.
items.abstract: Lay summary Many women notice changes in memory, concentration, and mental clarity during the menopause transition. These symptoms can affect quality of life, but there is currently no validated tool designed to assess menopause-related cognitive complaints among Chinese women. In this study, we adapted a questionnaire developed in the United Kingdom, called the Menopause-specific Cognitive Scale (Meno-Cog), for use in China. We worked with women aged 40-60 years and healthcare professionals to ensure that the questionnaire was clear, relevant, and culturally appropriate. We then tested it in a pilot study involving 50 women. Findings showed that the Chinese version of the Meno-Cog is a feasible tool for exploring women's cognitive experiences during the menopause transition. It was easy to understand and consistently measured cognitive symptoms. Women reporting greater cognitive difficulties in the Meno-Cog also reported more menopausal symptoms, anxiety and depressive symptoms, and poorer quality of life as expected.

items.title: Efficacy of psychological treatments for premenstrual dysphoric disorder: A preliminary meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Objectives Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) is a chronic mood disorder. While pharmacological interventions to treat PMDD are well researched and established as efficacious treatment options, little research has investigated the efficacy of psychological interventions. The aim of the current study was to synthesize the current literature on the efficacy of psychological interventions for PMDD using a meta-analytic approach. Methods Relevant articles were identified through an electronic database search, and seven studies (8 comparisons) were included in the meta-analysis (n = 629 participants; mean age 16.3 to 35.5 years). Random-effects models were used to compute within-group effect sizes (Hedges's g) for PMDD, depression and anxiety outcomes. Planned moderator analyses examined potential sources of variability. Results Psychological interventions produced large within-group reductions in PMDD symptoms from pretreatment to post-treatment (g = .87, 95% CI [.65, 1.08] and pretreatment to follow-up (g = 1.01, 95% CI [.59, 1.42]). Medium sized improvements were also observed for depression from pretreatment to post-treatment (g = .64, 95% CI [.37, .91]) and pretreatment to follow-up (g = .57, 95% CI [.39, .76]). Small improvements were found for anxiety symptoms from pretreatment to post-treatment (g = .49, 95% CI [.05, .93]) and pretreatment to follow-up (g = .44, 95% CI [.07, .82]). Moderator analyses were non-significant. Conclusions Psychological interventions may yield large and durable improvements in PMDD symptoms. However, only a small number of studies were available, and some were of lower methodological quality; thus, results should be considered alongside these limitations.

items.title: One-year reliable change for middle school, high school, and collegiate athletes on the Sway Medical System Sports+ Test Battery: implications for assessing sport-related concussion.
items.abstract: Sports neuropsychologists use test batteries designed to be repeatable, and the reliable change methodology is encouraged for interpreting scores. We documented test-retest reliability and reliable change estimates on the Sway Sports+ Test Battery, which yields a balance score and four discrete cognitive measures, across one year, within independent samples of athletes ages 12 through 22 ( N = 23,281). All completed pre-season assessments prior to Fall sport participation in 2023 and 2024. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) were used to calculate reliable change estimates (RCEs) using 70%, 80%, and 90% confidence intervals (CIs). ICCs ranged from .45 to .53 for Balance and from .35 to .51 for Reaction Time, Impulse Control, and Inspection Time. ICCs for Memory ranged from .19 to .33. Developmental changes show better/faster test scores by age. RCEs reflected some developmental differences, with a greater magnitude of change required for younger versus older athletes. It was uncommon for both balance and cognition to decline; the base rates for one or more cognitive scores declining with the balance score also declining ranged from 2.5-7.8%. It was common for one or more cognitive scores to decline (28.6-40.8%), but not for two or more cognitive scores to decline (5.3-11.0%). These results support the value of age-stratified normative data and RCEs for early adolescent through young adult athletes.

items.title: Reproductive costs of anhydrobiosis: female tardigrades protect stored sperm better than males.
items.abstract: Anhydrobiosis is a reversible process that allows organisms to survive prolonged periods in a desiccated state. Very little is known about the costs of anhydrobiosis on reproduction beyond a hiatus in activity. Tardigrades are suited to investigate such effects on male gamete function, as the latter can be tracked non-invasively. We compared the effects of three anhydrobiotic state durations (from 1 day to 1 month) on male- and female-stored sperm function in Macrobiotus dolosus. Our study shows that in-testis sperm motility upon rehydration is considerably impaired after long anhydrobiosis periods, and that its recovery is significantly slowed (up to several days). In contrast, we found no evidence for a negative impact of anhydrobiotic state on the fertilisation ability of spermatheca-stored sperm. Therefore, tardigrade female sperm storage structure can protect stored sperm even during long-term desiccation. Ultimately, our results highlight the need for further study of tissue-specific physiological adaptations to anhydrobiosis.

items.title: Jargon as a Psychological Construct? A Multidecade Analysis of Communication Failure in Evaluation Reports
items.abstract: For seven decades, studies have asked whether the people who receive psychological evaluation reports understand what they say. Existing research has largely measured reader satisfaction rather than what readers comprehend, recall, or interpret. This narrative synthesis identified six studies, conducted between 1984 and 2025 in school psychology and, most recently, child neuropsychology, in which 253 readers were assigned to a standard-format report and had their comprehension scored directly. Comprehension ranged from 46.6% to 61.1% (weighted mean = 55.2%) and showed no detectable change across four decades. In every study that also scored an accessible version of the same report, readers understood it better, with scores from 60% to 82%. Recent evidence from pediatric neuropsychology shows the same gap: parents rated their understanding of their child's report highly, yet almost half could not state the child's diagnoses without error. Effective formats combined plain-language wording with one or more of domain-based organization, concrete behavioral examples, and elaborated recommendations. These findings suggest that jargon-related comprehension failure is a persistent, measurable, and modifiable problem spanning specialties within psychology. Implications for training, supervision, and evidence-based communication practice across school and clinical psychology are discussed.

items.title: Potential public health and economic impact of influenza and COVID-19 multicomponent vaccination (mRNA-1083) for adults aged 65 years and older in France
items.abstract: Seasonal influenza and SARS-CoV-2 continue to cause substantial disease burden, particularly among older adults. The potential public health and economic impact of introducing combined enhanced influenza/COVID-19 vaccine, mRNA-1083, was assessed, for adults ≥65 years, versus separate high-dose inactivated influenza vaccine (HD-IIV) and BNT162b2 COVID-19 vaccination. A static decision-tree health economic model for France evaluated five value dimensions with mRNA-1083, in a stepwise approach, during an average post-pandemic season. Health system efficiencies, potential improved protection versus current comparators, avoidance of influenza egg-adaptation effects, and increased vaccine coverage rates (VCR) were assessed in the base case, and a future-looking scenario assessed potential reduced strain mismatch from antigenic drift, due to later influenza strain selection enabled by the mRNA platform. During an average season, mRNA-1083 was estimated to potentially prevent 25,830 medically-attended cases and 4,286 hospitalisations, saving EUR69.4 million in healthcare costs. Replacing separate influenza and COVID-19 vaccinations with mRNA-1083 may generate health system efficiencies, including 439,285 healthcare-provider hours saved. Potential improved clinical protection with mRNA-1083 prevented 2,194 hospitalisations saving EUR11.8 million in treatment costs. Avoiding egg-adaptation effects prevented a further 75 influenza hospitalisations, saving EUR0.3 million. Increased VCR with mRNA-1083 prevented an additional 2,017 hospitalisations, saving EUR10.4 million. Later strain selection could reduce antigenic drift and prevent a further 148 influenza hospitalisations and EUR0.6 million treatment cost on average per season. Results support that mRNA-1083 may improve seasonal respiratory vaccination by combining convenience, health system efficiency and potential for improved protection, higher coverage, and better influenza strain matching in a single injection.

items.title: ViDAS: Timely and Granular Estimation of Respiratory Virus Distributions in SARI Surveillance in Brazil
items.abstract: Effective monitoring of Severe Acute Respiratory Infections (SARI) is critical for public health but faces challenges such as reporting delays, incomplete information on negative test results, and data sparsity in specific regions and age groups. This study proposes a novel statistical framework to estimate the granular distribution of respiratory viruses among hospitalized SARI patients in Brazil. We employ Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT) to model viral proportions as conditional probabilities based on patient age, location, and time. A key methodological contribution is the development of SViDAS, a semi-parametric estimator that integrates viral probabilities over continuous lognormal age distributions, enabling estimation for arbitrary age intervals. Additionally, to address the black box limitations of machine learning, we introduce an interpretability strategy based on the estimator's internal embedding space, which identifies relevant training instances to explain individual predictions. Using data from the Brazilian SIVEP-Gripe system (2022-2024), results demonstrate that our models reduce the Brier Score estimation error by approximately 40% for SARS-CoV-2 and 36% for RSV compared with the empirical aggregation benchmark. Furthermore, the reporting-delay analysis indicates that estimation error decreases sharply during the first few weeks and tends to stabilize after approximately 3 to 5 weeks for the main viruses, although the stabilization point varies by virus and geographical region. This approach provides a computationally efficient, high-resolution framework for timely surveillance of respiratory-virus distributions, including in municipalities with limited immediate data availability.

items.title: Effects of Internet Adoption on Depressive Scores and Self-Rated Health in China: Multi-Period Difference-in-Differences Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Internet use has grown rapidly worldwide over the past decades. Extensive research has explored the health implications of internet use across diverse demographic groups, but most existing studies rely on associational designs. Evidence on the population-level causal effects of internet adoption on both psychological well-being and overall health status remains limited, particularly in settings where individuals adopt the internet across different time points. Objective: This study aimed to investigate the dynamic causal effects of internet adoption on both depressive scores and self-rated health among baseline internet nonusers in China. Methods: This study used longitudinal data from 4 waves of the China Family Panel Studies spanning 2016-2022. Participants who were internet nonusers at the 2016 baseline and provided complete responses across all 4 waves were included, whereas those who ever discontinued internet use after initial adoption were excluded. Internet use was assessed via self-reported questionnaires, depressive scores were evaluated using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale Short Form (CES-D 8), and overall health status was measured using self-rated health on a 5-point scale. A Difference-in-Differences framework with multiple time periods was applied to estimate the causal effects of internet adoption on both outcomes under the conditional parallel trends assumption. Robustness checks and mechanism analyses were further conducted to verify result validity and explore underlying pathways. Results: A total of 4026 participants were included in the analysis. Internet adoption reduced depressive scores on the CES-D 8 scale under a simple weighted average of all group-time average treatment effects (overall ATT = -0.302, SE = 0.156, P < .10), whereas event-study aggregation across post-adoption periods revealed a statistically significant cumulative reduction that intensified with longer exposure durations (overall dynamic ATT = -0.354, SE = 0.179, P < .05). In contrast, the average treatment effect on self-rated health was not statistically different from 0 (overall ATT = 0.039, SE = 0.046). Mechanism analyses suggested that internet adoption may have lowered depressive scores through expanded engagement in media entertainment, more frequent physical exercise, and higher total family expenditure, whereas the physiological gains of physical exercise may have been offset by prolonged sedentary behavior and health-compromising habits such as smoking. Robustness checks confirmed that these findings were not driven by random chance or sample selection bias. Conclusions: This study demonstrated that among baseline internet nonusers in China, internet adoption generated a cumulative reduction in depressive scores relative to what would have happened in the absence of internet adoption, yet had no statistically significant effect on self-rated health. Future public health initiatives should prioritize inclusive digital infrastructure expansion and age-friendly adaptations alongside fostering digital health literacy, curating health-oriented online content, and implementing targeted measures to mitigate the physiological risks of sedentary behavior and health-compromising habits.

items.title: Advancing Cyanobacterial Toxin Monitoring Capacity: A Large-Scale Multi-Year Comparison of ELISA, LC-MS/MS, and qPCR in Temperate Waters
items.abstract: Cyanobacterial toxins are an increasing environmental and public health concern, driven by rising temperatures and anthropogenic pressures such as eutrophication. Due to the colder climate, Northern Europe is generally believed to be less vulnerable, however, cyanobacterial blooms have increased in recent years in many areas including Arctic lakes and Northern Baltic Sea. Yet, monitoring remains challenging due to toxin diversity, variable bloom dynamics, and the differences in analytical targets among methods. We compared the complementarity, agreement, and practical utility of enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) for detecting cyanobacterial toxins and toxin-producing genotypes. This large-scale, multi-season study leveraged a sampling effort encompassing over 816 samples from freshwater, brackish, and marine ecosystems across Sweden over three consecutive summers. Toxins detected included microcystins, nodularin, cylindrospermopsins, anatoxins, and saxitoxins; where the fraction found in the cyanobacteria or as dissolved toxins varied with toxin type. Overall, concentrations measured using the three methods were proportional, but ELISA yielded, on average, approximately three times higher values than LC-MS/MS. ELISA provided high-throughput with lower selectivity compared to LC-MS/MS that ensured congener specific confirmation while qPCR complementarily revealed widespread presence of toxin-gene-carrying cyanobacteria. Across the 173 triple-analyzed samples, the combined use of ELISA, LC-MS/MS, and qPCR improved interpretation of cyanotoxin occurrence, bloom stage and potential risk compared to any single method alone. This multi-season field study represents one of the most extensive evaluations of these methods applied for cyanobacteria and their toxins in temperate waters.

items.title: Eco-anxiety and eco-depression: Two faces of the same coin? Examining roots, perceptions and mental health outcomes
items.abstract: Eco-anxiety and eco-depression are related but not interchangeable psychological responses to climate change and broader ecological degradation. Eco-anxiety is usually described as an anticipatory, threat-oriented response marked by worry, fear and cognitive-emotional preoccupation, whereas eco-depression is more closely aligned with sadness, helplessness, hopelessness, grief and diminished future orientation. Although both constructs overlap with general anxiety and depressive symptoms, their ecological anchoring raises important theoretical, clinical and public health questions: when should these responses be understood as proportionate forms of concern and mourning, and when do they become impairing forms of distress requiring support? This chapter synthesises definitions, theoretical foundations, determinants and mental health outcomes associated with eco-anxiety and eco-depression, and integrates an empirical illustration from a French population sample. The findings support the view that eco-depression and severe climate anxiety are strongly related, but partly distinct, phenomena. General self-efficacy appears more closely associated with depressive dimensions than with anxious dimensions, whereas environment-related self-efficacy, perceived inaction by others and collective action show more complex relationships. The chapter concludes that eco-depression should not be treated merely as a variant of eco-anxiety, nor should either construct be prematurely pathologised. A public health approach is needed that validates ecological distress, strengthens individual and collective agency, integrates mental health into climate policy and addresses the environmental and social conditions that generate these forms of suffering.

items.title: Recruitment and retention in randomised controlled trials involving autistic adults: a systematic review
items.abstract: A significant body of research highlights physical and mental health inequities faced by autistic adults. However, randomised controlled trials (RCTs) with autistic people are often underpowered, with this population considered ‘difficult to recruit’. This systematic review aimed to examine recruitment and retention to RCTs with autistic adults, as well as synthesising strategies used to facilitate recruitment and retention. MEDLINE, PsycINFO, EMBASE, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science databases were systematically searched for RCTs recruiting autistic adults published to June 2023, with a second search conducted in December 2025. ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry were also searched. We report details for N=47 trials, including type of intervention and control, planned and achieved recruitment and retention rates, and strategies to maximise these. Included studies focused on improving e.g., social skills, cognition, mental health, quality of life, employment, and driving skills. Findings are reported in a narrative synthesis, showing a proliferation of trials recruiting small samples, wide ranging recruitment and retention rates, and a paucity of information regarding target sample sizes and/or power calculations. Facilitators of recruitment and retention included integrating Patient and Public Involvement and co-production, involving family/carers, public advertising and accepting self-referrals, remote participation, and reasonable adjustments.

items.title: The Endogenous Aspects of Addiction: Diathesis-Stress Interactions between PID-5 Personality Traits and Socio-Ecological Triggers in Substance Use Disorder Patients from North East India
items.abstract: Substance use disorder (SUD) is a global public health crisis, with Northeast India exhibiting disproportionately high prevalence rates. Traditional socio-ecological models often emphasize familial and environmental factors in SUD etiology. This cross-sectional study investigated the interplay between self-reported triggers, family history, and pathological personality traits among N=62 male residents across three rehabilitation facilities in Jorhat, Assam. Utilizing the Personality Inventory for DSM-5 Brief Form (PID-5-BF), findings revealed that Disinhibition and Antagonism are the primary neuro-behavioral drivers of early onset, severe polysubstance use, and opioid endorsement. Contrary to socio-ecological assumptions, familial indicators (parental education and substance use) did not independently predict severity. However, a significant diathesis-stress interaction emerged: parental substance use exacerbated polysubstance severity exclusively among highly disinhibited individuals. Furthermore, comorbid gambling strongly aligned with intrapsychic triggers and a psychopathy-spectrum profile (high Detachment/Antagonism, low Negative Affect), indicating under-stimulation rather than distress. These results highlight the necessity of personality-targeted interventions, demonstrating that systemic family vulnerabilities catalyze severe SUD primarily in the presence of underlying personality pathology

items.title: Psychedelics use, trust in authority and institutions
items.abstract: Trust in institutional authority is central to social cohesion and public health engagement, yet declining trust has been increasingly linked to conspiratorial thinking. Despite rapid recreational and clinical interest in psychedelics, little research has examined their interactions with attitudes towards trust and authority. This manuscript addresses several questions: What is known about the associations between recreational psychedelic use and trust in governmental and medical institutions? How have historical and contemporary cultural narratives shaped the relationship between psychedelics and institutional authority? How might mistrust of medical and governmental institutions among psychedelic users affect the integration of psychedelic-assisted therapies into mainstream healthcare? How might conspiratorial thinking affect linking psychedelic use to institutional mistrust? We synthesise interdisciplinary literature across empirical studies, theoretical models, and historical analyses, with evidence integrated across three domains: historical and sociocultural context, psychological and mechanistic models of belief change, and contemporary institutional dynamics. Findings indicate that while psychedelic experiences may alter belief processes, there is insufficient empirical evidence to determine how the alteration of these processes, in turn, alters trust in institutions or conspiratorial thinking. These relationships appear context-dependent and influenced by pre-existing social, cultural, and political influences, as well as competing narratives surrounding psychedelics. We suggest that current mechanistic accounts may be insufficient in isolation, and the effects of psychedelics on belief systems cannot be understood without situating them within broader contexts. Future research is therefore necessary to explore and clarify these relationships in a multidisciplinary manner that merges empirical data collection with historic context. Such knowledge would be essential for the responsible integration of psychedelics into clinical and societal settings.

items.title: The Worldwide Wellbeing Twin Project: Estimating Genetic and Environmental Influences Across Populations Around the Globe
items.abstract: Wellbeing is central to public health and policy. Yet, it remains unclear whether sources of wellbeing differences are similar across populations worldwide. We investigated genetic and environmental influences on wellbeing using standardized classical twin models across 20 cohorts from 18 countries (N = 122,418 twins; 19,848 complete monozygotic and 29,037 complete dizygotic pairs). Estimates across cohorts were combined in meta-analyses. The pooled heritability estimate was 36% (95% CI: 35-37%), indicating moderate and broadly consistent genetic influences across diverse populations. However, estimates varied substantially between cohorts (18-77%). Exploratory analyses suggested that heterogeneity was partly related to mean cohort age (b = -0.004, p = .047). The estimate was higher (41%; 95% CI: 40–43%) and less heterogeneous among cohorts using the Satisfaction with Life Scale. Heritability did not differ between W.E.I.R.D. and non-W.E.I.R.D. countries (36% and 33% respectively). These findings highlight both cross-population similarity and context-dependence among sources of individual differences in wellbeing. items.title: The Worldwide Wellbeing Twin Project: Estimating Genetic and Environmental Influences Across Populations Around the Globe
items.abstract: Wellbeing is central to public health and policy. Yet, it remains unclear whether sources of wellbeing differences are similar across populations worldwide. We investigated genetic and environmental influences on wellbeing using standardized classical twin models across 20 cohorts from 18 countries (N = 122,418 twins; 19,848 complete monozygotic and 29,037 complete dizygotic pairs). Estimates across cohorts were combined in meta-analyses. The pooled heritability estimate was 36% (95% CI: 35-37%), indicating moderate and broadly consistent genetic influences across diverse populations. However, estimates varied substantially between cohorts (18-77%). Exploratory analyses suggested that heterogeneity was partly related to mean cohort age (b = -0.004, p = .047). The estimate was higher (41%; 95% CI: 40–43%) and less heterogeneous among cohorts using the Satisfaction with Life Scale. Heritability did not differ between W.E.I.R.D. and non-W.E.I.R.D. countries (36% and 33% respectively). These findings highlight both cross-population similarity and context-dependence among sources of individual differences in wellbeing. Keywords: wellbeing, twin design, global approach, behavioral genetics
