items.title: Neighbourhood-Level Alcohol-Related Social Disorder and Subjective Well-Being: A Multilevel Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Alcohol-related neighbourhood disorder has been increasingly recognised as a social and public health concern, yet its relationship with subjective well-being remains underexplored particularly in India. This study examines the association between perceived neighbourhood alcohol-related disorder and subjective well-being and assesses whether neighbourhood trust moderates this relationship. Multilevel linear mixed-effects models are estimated to account for clustering at the neighbourhood level while controlling for demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. The findings indicate that perceived alcohol-related neighbourhood disorder is associated with lower levels of subjective well-being (β = -0.07, 95% CI: -0.14 to -0.00). Similarly neighbourhood trust is positively associated with subjective well-being only in neighbourhoods without alcohol-related disorder, suggesting that the benefits of trust may be diminished in disorderly environments. These findings highlight the importance of local social environments and the need to consider both structural and social dimensions of local neighbourhoods when evaluating policies aimed at improving community well-being.

items.title: Environmental Sustainability and Climate Change: Growing Concerns for the Banking Sector
items.abstract: Abstract This study examines how the banking sector can contribute to climate action and environmental sustainability. As climate change poses growing risks to economies, ecosystems, and public health, banks have an important opportunity to support the transition towards a low-carbon economy. Green banking incorporates environmental, social, and economic considerations into conventional financial services, enabling banks to support sustainable development while pursuing financial returns. The study considers how sustainable banking practices and environmentally responsible programmes may improve operational efficiency and profitability. It also examines barriers to implementing environmental sustainability, including the relative roles of mandatory regulation and voluntary action. The findings highlight the need for effective regulatory measures and incentives to encourage banks to adopt sustainable practices and contribute to a more resilient, low-carbon economy. Overall, the analysis underscores the banking sector’s influential role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable future. Clinical Trial Registration Not applicable. The investigation concerns educational practices, reflective learning experiences and selfreported digital pedagogical measures and does not involve clinical trials, medical interventions or clinical research procedures.

items.title: Preventive interventions to improve visual and emotional health in young university students: A public health approach
items.abstract: Abstract This descriptive study analyzes research on visual and emotional health in academic environments. It seeks to objectively survey students at the Cooperative University of Colombia (UCC) and the Autonomous University of the West (UAO) across multiple campuses in order to propose and develop intervention tools using a mobile application. This descriptive, exploratory study includes a phase of understanding the phenomenon through documentary research and an empirical-analytical phase. Four digital survey instruments were administered. The results of three separate questionnaires show that 83% of 312 students report visual fatigue associated with prolonged screen use. 37.4% of 222 students report weekly recurring stress or anxiety, 37.4% few times per month and 8.6% daily. 91.3% report insufficient sleep (between 5 and 6 hours or less), and 91.4% believe the university does not provide information on visual health or they are uninformed or insufficient. The study concludes that visual and emotional health are directly related. Stress exacerbates visual discomfort, hindering adequate concentration and efficient performance, due to exposure to risk factors, long workdays, and a lack of preventive practices. While self-care strategies are positive, they don't have the desired impact. It is suggested that prevention programs and visual health campaigns focused on healthy habits be designed.

items.title: Household water sources, drinking-water treatment and two-week diarrhoeal illness in Karangura Sub-County, Kabarole District, Uganda: a cross-sectional study with implications for safe water governance and public health
items.abstract: Abstract Background Unsafe drinking water, inadequate sanitation and poor hygiene remain major drivers of preventable enteric disease. Rural households often use several water sources, so classification based on the presence of an improved source alone may conceal concurrent reliance on higher-risk sources and household-level water-safety gaps. We assessed household water-source portfolios, drinking-water treatment, sanitation and handwashing practices in Karangura Sub-County, western Uganda, and examined their association with recent household diarrhoeal illness. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the 2025 Karangura Child Focused Community Transformation household baseline survey. Of 620 surveyed households, 618 had a valid response for the primary outcome, self-reported diarrhoea in any household member during the previous two weeks. Water-source categories were derived from the survey response options using WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme source classifications. We distinguished households reporting any higher-risk source from those reporting improved-source categories only. Regular drinking-water treatment and regular handwashing were defined as “always” or “often”. Sanitation was conservatively classified as private/personal sanitation when households reported a flush toilet or personal pit latrine because the survey did not capture all Joint Monitoring Programme criteria for safely managed or improved sanitation. We estimated prevalence ratios using modified Poisson regression with village-clustered robust standard errors, adjusting for household size, presence of a child younger than five years, asset ownership and hill of residence. Results Among 618 households, 385 (62.3%) reported at least one improved-source category, but 450 (72.8%) also reported at least one higher-risk source; only 168 (27.2%) reported improved-source categories without a concurrent higher-risk source. Any drinking-water treatment was reported by 165 (26.7%) households and regular treatment by 147 (23.8%). Private/personal sanitation was reported by 533 (86.2%) households and regular handwashing with soap by 305 (49.4%). Eighty-six households (13.9%) reported diarrhoea in at least one member during the previous two weeks. Diarrhoea prevalence was 6.1% among households reporting regular water treatment compared with 16.3% among those without regular treatment. In the adjusted model, regular water treatment was associated with lower diarrhoea prevalence (adjusted prevalence ratio [aPR] 0.48, 95% CI 0.30–0.77; p = 0.002). The presence of a child younger than five years was associated with higher household diarrhoea prevalence (aPR 2.09, 95% CI 1.30–3.38; p = 0.003). Higher-risk source use, private/personal sanitation and regular handwashing were not independently associated with the outcome after adjustment. Conclusions Karangura households frequently combined improved-source categories with higher-risk water sources, while regular household water treatment and handwashing remained limited. Regular water treatment was associated with substantially lower two-week household diarrhoea prevalence. Local water governance should therefore move beyond infrastructure counts toward water-safety management across all sources households use, reliable access, household treatment, safe handling, hygiene promotion and routine water-quality surveillance. Longitudinal studies with microbial water testing are needed to assess causality and identify the highest-risk points in the household water chain.

items.title: Engineered Neisseria meningitidis Outer Membrane Vesicle Nanoplatform for Tetravalent Dengue Virus Antigen Delivery Induces Balanced Humoral and Cellular Immune Responses
items.abstract: Abstract Background Dengue virus (DENV) represents an escalating global public health emergency, placing approximately 3.9 billion people at risk of infection annually across its four distinct serotypes (DENV-1–4) [1, 2]. Developing an effective vaccine remains challenging due to the necessity of eliciting balanced, tetravalent protective immunity without inducing antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) [1–3]. Methods Here, we report an engineered nanovaccine candidate utilizing bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) derived from Neisseria meningitidis as a self-adjuvanted nanoscale delivery carrier conjugated with formaldehyde-inactivated virions of all four DENV serotypes [1, 2, 9]. OMVs isolated by tangential-flow ultrafiltration were physically conjugated with DENV-1–4, and particle assembly was evaluated using Nanoparticle Tracking Analysis (NTA), Zeta potential profiling, and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) [33, 38]. Subcutaneous prime-booster immunization in outbred Swiss albino mice elicited robust total IgG and IgG1 titers uniformly distributed against DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, and DENV-4 [34, 39]. Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) of splenocytes demonstrated transcriptional modulation of key cellular and humoral cytokines (IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, TNF-α, TGF-β, IFN-γ, and PAF) [40–50]. Results Hydrodynamic diameter analysis revealed size expansion from native OMVs (D90 = 209.6 nm) to tetravalent nanoconjugates (D90 = 413.8 nm), with a net surface charge of − 11.47 mV [38]. Subcutaneous prime-booster immunization in outbred Swiss albino mice elicited robust total IgG and IgG1 titers uniformly distributed against DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, and DENV-4 [34, 39]. Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) of splenocytes demonstrated balanced transcriptional modulation of key cellular and humoral cytokines (IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, TNF-α, TGF-β, IFN-γ, and PAF) [40–50]. Conclusions These results establish N. meningitidis OMVs as a versatile self-adjuvanted nanoplatform capable of overcoming serotype immunodominance in tetravalent flavivirus vaccine design [21, 26, 32].

items.title: Prevalence of Hepatitis B virus genotypes among Hepatic jaundice patients in Ibb city Yemen
items.abstract: Abstract Background and Aims: Hepatitis, an inflammation of the liver, can lead to serious health complications and mortality, causing approximately 1.34 million fatalities annually—a burden comparable to that of HIV/AIDS. This study aims to assess the prevalence and genotype distribution of the hepatitis B virus (HBV) among patients presenting with jaundice in Ibb City, Yemen, and evaluating host associated risk factors. Methods This multi-center, cross-sectional study was carried out between January 2024 and December 2025 across major clinics and hospitals in Ibb City. The study enrolled 256 patients presenting with jaundice. Serum samples from all participants were evaluated for liver transaminases, HBV DNA viral load, and HBV serological markers (specifically HBsAg, total anti-HBc, HBeAg, and anti-HBe). To determine the HBV genotypes, a nested PCR-based assay was employed using type-specific primers that targeted highly conserved sequences within the P and S genes, successfully identifying six distinct genotypes. Results Of the 256 jaundice patients evaluated, 82.4% (211) were male and 17.6% (45) were female. The leading presentation was undiagnosed jaundice (37.5%), followed by confirmed hepatitis B (25.4%). Other identified etiologies included non-B viral hepatitis (10.5%), autoimmune liver diseases (7.4%), drug-induced liver injury (5.9%), schistosomiasis (4.7%), malaria (4.3%), and dengue fever (0.8%). Overall, 85 patients (33.2%) tested positive for HBV infection via serological or molecular markers, with men exhibiting a significantly higher infection rate (37.0%) than women (15.6%). Specifically, HBsAg positivity was detected in 51 patients (19.9% overall prevalence; 21.3% in males vs. 13.3% in females). Among the 65 genotyped patients, genotype D was the most prevalent (32.3%), followed by genotype B (20.0%) and genotype C (13.8%), while mixed genotypes were identified in 33.8% of cases. Conclusions The vast majority of jaundice patients in Ibb City are male, which may indicate either higher biological susceptibility or gender-based disparities in healthcare-seeking behaviours. The high prevalence of HBV particularly genotype D and mixed genotypes highlights an urgent need for targeted public health interventions, routine screening, and robust vaccination strategies in the region.

items.title: Policy Capacities & Policy Normatives: Analyzing Artificial Intelligence Adoption in the Health and Justice Sectors in Latin America
items.abstract: Abstract Building on the Policy Capacity Framework (PCF) we propose a normative dimension to evaluate the public value toward which those capacities are directed. This article examines the relationship between AI adoption and policy capacities in the health and justice sectors across five major Latin American countries. Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly entering into public administration, and while increasing efforts are made to adopt the technology over the promises of efficiency gains, little attention has been devoted to the capacities required to govern it, ergo, implementing it effectively, ethically, and sustainably. Using a comparative, theory-informed research design, we formulate nine ideal guiding PCF propositions to assess the two portfolios of capacities -technical and governance- that should accompany the public sector’s AI adoption efforts. We then analyze 40 national-level AI applications in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, and Mexico to understand what is happening on the ground. Thanks to our augmented version of the PCF analytical tool, we found that current efforts primarily concentrate on developing the technical portfolio of capacities required to deploy AI systems, while the governance portfolio remains underdeveloped. The results suggest that technical capacities can surge at individual and organizational levels autonomously, but governance-related normative capacities are only observed in the cases where systemic political capacities have enabled them. We also attest the power of political systemic capacities to influence both sets of portfolios -technical and normative- in improving analytical and operative capacities in the other two levels. The article contributes by integrating normative considerations into policy capacity theory and by identifying institutional conditions necessary for responsible AI governance in public organizations.

items.abstract: Abstract Background: In 2019, the World Health Organization estimated that approximately 21 million girls aged 15-19 years in low- and middle-income countries became pregnant annually, with nearly half of these pregnancies being unintended. Despite interventions to improve adolescent sexual and reproductive health, teenage pregnancy and low contraceptive uptake remain important public health challenges in Cameroon, including the Buea Health District. Data on socio-demographic characteristics, knowledge of teenage pregnancy prevention, contraceptive uptake, sexual and reproductive history, and other potential risk factors were collected using a structured questionnaire. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize participants’ characteristics, while bivariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify determinants of teenage pregnancy. items.title: Animal Aggressions with Rabies-Transmission Potential in Risaralda, Colombia, 2016–2026: Rising Severe Exposures and a Shifting Aggressor Profile
items.abstract: Background: Animal aggressions with rabies-transmission potential remain an important public health concern, requiring effective surveillance and timely post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). This study aimed to characterize temporal trends, epidemiological patterns, aggressor species, exposure severity, and clinical management of animal aggressions in Risaralda, Colombia, between 2016 and 2026. Methods: A retrospective, descriptive, ecological time-series study was conducted using records notified to Colombia’s National Public Health Surveillance System (SIVIGILA, event 300) from 2016 through epidemiological week 46 of 2026. Demographic characteristics, aggressor species, injury characteristics, animal observability, exposure classification, and PEP administration were analyzed. Temporal trends were estimated using quasi-Poisson regression, while categorical variables were compared using chi-square tests. Concordance between initial and final exposure classifications was assessed using weighted kappa statistics. Results: Overall, 41,419 notifications were analyzed. Annual notifications increased by 59%, from 3,041 in 2016 to 4,829 in 2025, with an annual percentage change of 4.5% (95% CI: 1.9–7.1). Median age was 28 years, and 51.8% were male. Dogs accounted for 80.4% of aggressions, followed by cats (18.3%), whose contribution increased from 15.6% to 22.2%. Severe exposures increased from 7.1% in 2016 to 16.5% in 2025, reaching 18.0% in 2026. Unobservable aggressor animals increased from 20.2% to 33.8% between 2016 and 2025. Rabies vaccination was administered in 99.4% of severe exposures and antirabies serum in 94.9%. Initial and final exposure classifications agreed in 85.9% of comparable records (weighted κ = 0.83). Conclusions: Animal aggression notifications increased substantially in Risaralda, accompanied by a disproportionate rise in severe exposure classifications, increasing feline involvement, and reduced animal observability. These findings highlight the need to strengthen integrated One Health surveillance, domestic animal vaccination, standardized exposure assessment, and timely PEP management.

items.title: Rainfall Deficits, Financial Protection, and Where Households Seek Care: Evidence from Four Rounds of the Nigeria General Household Survey Panel
items.abstract: Background: Climate variability is widely expected to raise the burden of illness in sub-Saharan Africa, but far less is known about what it does to the financing of care. A rainfall deficit arrives as an income shock in agrarian households at the same time as it may arrive as a health shock, and in a system financed overwhelmingly out of pocket those two events interact. Methods. We assembled an individual-level panel of 107,668 person-rounds drawn from 53,575 individuals in 8,518 households across all four rounds of the Nigeria General Household Survey Panel, covering 2010/11 to 2018/19 and 899 enumeration areas in 37 states. Rainfall at each household’s true coordinates, extracted before public displacement, was expressed as a proportional deviation from that location’s own long-run mean; a deficit is the bottom quintile of that deviation. Two-way fixed-effects models with household or individual effects and round effects, and standard errors clustered on the enumeration area, were estimated for reported morbidity, care-seeking, the source of care and out-of-pocket outlay measured against the SDG 3.8.2 thresholds. Information access was measured by household broadcast ownership and tested against a matched non-informational durable. Results. A rainfall deficit raised the probability that a household spent more than a tenth of its consumption out of pocket on health by 3.74 percentage points (95% CI 0.61 to 6.87) against a base of 14.3 percent, and the out-of-pocket budget share by 4.24 percentage points (95% CI 0.43 to 8.05). The effect was positive at every threshold between 1 and 40 percent of consumption and was concentrated in rural households (5.08 points, 95% CI 1.46 to 8.70). It survived correction for multiple testing within the financial-protection family (q = 0.039). Conditional on consulting, deficits moved care away from retail drug sellers and toward traditional and spiritual providers; the latter shift was confined to households without broadcast access, where it reached 3.51 points on a base of 6.8 percent and was fully offset among households with access (interaction −4.64 points, p = 0.028). Reported illness rose modestly and the decision to consult at all was unchanged. Conclusions. The dominant health consequence of a rainfall deficit in this setting is financial rather than clinical: households do not stop seeking care, they pay a larger share of a smaller budget for it and some of them change who they pay. Financial protection instruments that are responsive to agro-climatic conditions, and broadcast health communication in deficit-prone areas, address two distinct margins of the same shock.

items.title: Prevalence of the HbS Allele and Malaria in Congolese Children Admitted to Hospital with Fever in Mbujimayi, a Semi-Rural Area, Democratic Republic of Congo
items.abstract: Background: Sickle Cell Disease and malaria represent major public health burdens in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The long-standing malaria hypothesis posits that the sickle cell allele confers an evolutionary advantage against Plasmodium falciparum infection. Population, Material and Method. To evaluate this relationship in a hyperendemic region, a cross-sectional study was conducted at Bonzola Hospital in Mbujimayi, DRC, enrolling 309 febrile children under 18 years of age between July and December 2018. Malaria was diagnosed using rapid diagnostic tests combined with blood smears, while hemoglobin phenotypes were identified using point-of-care immunoassays and confirmed via capillary electrophoresis. Results: Among the 309 participants, 58.6% exhibited the normal AA phenotype, 29.4% carried the AS trait, and 12.0% had the homozygous SS phenotype. The presence of the HbS allele significantly decreased both overall malaria susceptibility and clinical severity. Children with the normal AA phenotype demonstrated an estimated 38.12% probability of developing uncomplicated malaria compared to 25.78% among HbS carriers. This potential protective effect was most pronounced in cases of severe disease: the estimated probability of severe malaria was 17.68% in the AA group versus just 1.56% in HbS carriers, representing a nearly thirteenfold reduction in odds. Severe malaria occurred predominantly in AA children and minimally in AS children, with zero cases observed in SS patients. Conclusions: These results significantly strengthen the "advantage" hypothesis, particularly in children with sickle cell trait (heterozygous carriers), thereby confirming that the HbS allele does not confer total immunity against malaria infection, but rather provides proven protection.

items.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Antimicrobial Resistance in Infectious Diseases: Advances in Therapeutic Strategies and Public Health Interventions
items.abstract: Drug resistance in infectious diseases present a major global health concern, reducing treatment efficacy and increasing morbidity and mortality. Resistance arises from different molecular mechanisms including genetic mutations, enzymatic degradation of drugs, alterations in target sites, efflux pump overexpression, and reduced membrane permeability. These mechanisms contribute to the development of multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant pathogens across bacterial, viral, and mycobacterial species. Scientist have developed therapeutic strategies to control these mechanisms of multidrug-resistant. These include the development of novel antimicrobials such as teixobactin and pretomanid, the application of β-lactamase inhibitors, rational drug combinations, host-directed therapies, and antimicrobial peptides. Advances in biotechnology have enabled precise-targeted approaches, including phage therapy, CRISPR-based antimicrobials, and nanocarrier-mediated drug delivery. Public health interventions are important in reducing the burden of AMR. These include global surveillance systems, antimicrobial stewardship programs, vaccination, infection control protocols, and regulatory policies governing antimicrobial use in humans and animals. Future directions emphasize the integration of precision medicine, artificial intelligence, environmental monitoring, and international governance to strengthen AMR control. A sustained and coordinated global response is essential to preserve the efficacy of current therapies and promote the development of new interventions. By linking each resistance route to its therapeutic vulnerability and control requirement, this review provides a mechanism-to-intervention framework for prioritizing diagnostics, stewardship, and public-health action.

items.title: Emergency Department Visits and Hospitalizations for Controlled Substance Use Among Youth With Chronic Medical Conditions.
items.abstract: Purpose The risk of controlled substance misuse among adolescents with chronic medical conditions (CMCs) is poorly understood. This study examines variation in controlled substance-related emergency department (ED) use within a clinically defined population of adolescents with CMCs. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of substance use-related ED visits and hospitalizations among adolescents aged 12-21 years with CMCs from 2021 to 2024. Youth were classified as having noncomplex chronic conditions or complex chronic conditions (CCCs) using a validated system. ED encounters were identified using International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision (ICD-10 codes) and categorized by ingestion type: use/abuse/dependence (UAD), intentional self-harm, or unintentional ingestion. Encounters were further classified as involving controlled versus other substances. Multivariable generalized linear mixed models estimated odds of (1) controlled-substance ED visits and (2) hospitalization following a substance use-related ED visit, adjusting for sociodemographic, clinical, and contextual factors. Results Among 70,621 substance use-related ED visits, 16.0% occurred among adolescents with CCCs. CCCs were associated with higher odds of ED presentation for controlled-substance UAD compared with noncomplex chronic conditions (adjusted odds ratio 1.87, 95% CI 1.74-2.00). Non-Hispanic Black adolescents and older youth had lower odds of controlled-substance UAD visits compared with non-Hispanic White and younger adolescents. Among youth with UAD-related ED visits, CCCs were strongly associated with subsequent hospitalization (adjusted odds ratio 5.76, 95% CI 5.45-6.08). Discussion Medically complex adolescents experience disproportionately high ED use and hospitalization for controlled-substance UAD. These findings support targeted, equity-focused screening, prescribing vigilance, and adapted Screening, Brief Intervention, and Referral to Treatment (SBIRT) models in ED and inpatient settings.

items.title: Trends in Prescribed and Nonprescribed Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder Medication Use Among Students in Grades 7 to 12 in Ontario, Canada (2013-2023).
items.abstract: Purpose To characterize contemporary trends in prescribed and nonprescribed use of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) medications among adolescents. Methods Population-based survey data from 34,137 students in grades 7-12 in Ontario, Canada, were analyzed (2013-2023). Past-year ADHD medication use was self-reported as prescribed and/or nonprescribed. Trends in use were estimated using average annual prevalence changes (AAPCs) in the overall sample and stratified by subgroups, both aggregated and disaggregated by prescription status. Results Any ADHD medication use increased from 4.4% in 2013 to 6.2% in 2023 (AAPC = .21%; 95% confidence interval: .08-.34). Increases were significant among females (AAPC = .27%), grades 7-9 (AAPC = .33%), low socioeconomic status households (AAPC = .34%), and adolescents who did not use or infrequently used alcohol, cigarettes, cannabis, and social media. Prescription use was stable from 2013 to 2017 but then rose sharply from 2.9% in 2017 to 5.4% in 2023. Nonprescribed use increased from 1.4% in 2013 to 2.7% in 2019 but returned to 1.4% in 2023. In 2023, 11.7% self-identified as having ADHD. Notably, 7.9% of nonusers self-identified as having ADHD, while 25.4% of those using with a prescription and 43.1% of those using without a prescription did not self-identify as having ADHD. Discussion ADHD medication use among Ontario adolescents increased substantially over the past decade, driven largely by prescriptions, particularly among females and younger adolescents. Whether the increasing trend reflects increased ADHD prevalence, improved diagnosis, or overdiagnosis remains unclear. Discordance between medication use and ADHD self-identification raises questions about current prescribing practices and underscores the need for ongoing surveillance.

items.title: Effects of Snoezelen Multisensory Therapy on Behavioral and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia: A 12-Week Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Objectives To examine the effects of Snoezelen multisensory therapy (SMT) on agitation, depressive symptoms, and anxiety in older adults with mild-to-moderate dementia living in long-term care. Methods In this 12-week stratified randomized controlled trial, 63 older adults with mild-to-moderate dementia were randomized to SMT plus standard care ( n = 33) or standard care alone ( n = 30). Outcomes were assessed at baseline and every two weeks thereafter; 59 participants completed all assessments. Repeated-measures ANOVA and ANCOVA were used. No assessments followed the intervention. Results Significant time × group interactions were found for agitation (CMAI, p 2 p = .26), depressive symptoms (CSDD, p = .002; HADS-D, p p Conclusions Participants randomized to SMT showed greater reductions in agitation, depressive symptoms and anxiety than controls, emerging gradually and largest for agitation. Because assessments occurred during active treatment and were not independent of delivery, these differences should not be read as evidence of efficacy. Clinical implications Reductions emerged progressively across repeated assessments during the 12-week intervention. Whether these between-group differences persist once sessions stop was not tested.

items.title: Beyond the national average: Demographically stratified estimates of resource utilization for trauma systems planning.
items.abstract: Background Trauma systems are planned for populations, but resources are consumed by individual patients whose needs vary by age, sex, and injury pattern. To estimate the resources a population will need, existing tools often apply simple national averages of what admissions consume, creating a potential mismatch between the resources needed and those available. We compared simple population size-based estimates against estimates stratified by patient demographics. Methods Using the American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Programs Participant Use Files (2022-2024), we conducted a retrospective analysis of adult admissions to 502 Level I/II trauma centers. Per-admission estimates for seven resources were derived from pooled 2022-2023 admissions using three approaches: simple estimates based on population size, singularly stratified estimates by age, sex, or payer alone, and jointly stratified estimates combining all three. Estimates were applied to held-out 2024 admissions and percent error calculated, with a 2017-2019 sensitivity analysis. Results Among 1,803,746 derivation and 947,281 validation admissions, the simple estimate fell outside 10% of observed utilization in 40 of 63 subgroup and metric combinations, 21 higher than observed and 19 lower. Blood product estimates were 236% higher than observed among Medicare-covered patients. Stratifying on one characteristic corrected error chiefly within its own subgroups (59 of 63 within 10%). Applied jointly, age, sex, and payer brought 62 of 63 combinations within 10%, reducing median absolute error from 13.8% to 3.0%. Conclusions Simple estimates differed from observed resource use by 10% or more for nearly every patient group examined, failing in both directions in a manner no single adjustment can correct. Stratification by age, sex, and payer, characteristics knowable before injury, substantially reduced this error. Level of evidence Prognostic/Epidemiological; Level III.

items.title: Real-world remote multidisciplinary educational intervention combined with intermittently scanned continuous glucose monitoring in youth with type 1 diabetes mellitus at a public referral center.
items.abstract: Objective To evaluate the impact of a remote multidisciplinary educational intervention combined with intermittently scanned continuous glucose monitoring (isCGM) on glycemic control in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus followed at a public referral center in an upper-middle-income country that serves a socioeconomically vulnerable population. Subjects and methods This prospective interventional study included 49 youth randomized to either a study group (SG), which received a six-month structured, telehealth-based multidisciplinary educational intervention delivered through a digital platform, or a control group (CG), which received conventional in-person follow-up. All participants initiated isCGM use from the third month onward. Socioeconomic, clinical, anthropometric, and laboratory data were collected on days 0, 90, and 180. Results Most participants belonged to low-income households (CG: 79.2%; SG: 80.0%). Mean HbA1c values remained above recommended targets in both groups throughout follow-up (CG: 9.2% on day 0 and 9.4% on day 180; SG: 9.1% on day 0 and 9.4% on day 180), with no significant between-group differences. After isCGM initiation on day 90, the SG showed a higher frequency of daily glucose scans and better time in range than the CG. Difficulties adhering to remote appointments were reported by 72% of SG participants and were associated with higher HbA1c levels. Conclusion In youth with type 1 diabetes mellitus receiving care in a public health setting, telemedicine-based education combined with isCGM use was associated with improvements in selected glycemic metrics but not with reductions in HbA1c. Barriers related to adherence and digital access were frequent and may limit the effectiveness of remote interventions. Further studies with longer follow-up are warranted.

items.title: Pathology and diseases of free-ranging New World primates from the Brazilian Atlantic Forest.
items.abstract: Neotropical primates (New World primates, NWP) are natural and accidental hosts of many infectious agents, yet there is scarce literature on the pathology and diseases affecting free-ranging NWP, with the majority of reports involving serological diagnoses. This study aimed to characterize the pathological findings and infectious agents identified in free-ranging NWP from the Atlantic Forest biome in the State of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, using histochemical, ultrastructural, immunohistochemical, and molecular methods during the period of January 2017 to July 2019. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded samples from brain, heart, lungs, liver, spleen, and kidneys were evaluated from more than 1000 animals, including the genera Callithrix , Alouatta , Sapajus , Leontopithecus , and Callicebus . The analysis demonstrated that free-ranging NWP are hosts of several infectious diseases, including important zoonoses such as rabies, toxoplasmosis, and yellow fever, and warrant consideration in the development of strategies for disease control and prevention, both with a focus on public health and conservation of these species. Some infectious agents, including known human pathogens and commensals, were observed for the first time in free-ranging NWP, such as human parainfluenza viruses 1 and 3, Staphylococcus capitis , Streptococcus sanguinis , and Moraxella spp. Additionally, evaluation of this large number of animals provided information about changes interpreted as background lesions in these species.

items.title: Challenges in leprosy diagnostics.
items.abstract: Introduction Leprosy remains a public health challenge, with persistent diagnostic delays particularly affecting patients with paucibacillary, oligosymptomatic forms, and pure neural disease, in whom clinical manifestations may be subtle and conventional tests have limited sensitivity. Areas covered This narrative review examines the current diagnostic landscape of leprosy, focusing on clinical and dermato-neurological assessment, bacteriological examination, histopathology, serological assays, and molecular methods. It also discusses emerging diagnostic approaches, including multimarker strategies, point-of-care testing, digital health, and artificial intelligence. The literature was reviewed in conjunction with international diagnostic recommendations, with emphasis on evidence relevant to early diagnosis, decentralized testing, active case finding, and the identification of individuals at risk of disability. Expert opinion Clinical and dermato-neurological assessment remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, while laboratory methods provide complementary information but have important limitations, particularly in paucibacillary disease. No single diagnostic method can reliably detect all clinical forms of leprosy. Improving early diagnosis will therefore require integrated, context-adapted strategies that combine clinical assessment with complementary technologies, strengthen diagnostic capacity at decentralized levels, promote active case finding, and improve healthcare networks to reduce diagnostic delays and prevent disability.

items.title: How does digital monitoring affect teachers? Parent sousveillance and teacher stress.
items.abstract: Online work blurs work-life boundaries, raising new occupational health concerns. Teachers, one of North America's largest professions, transitioned to online teaching during the pandemic and faced real-time parental surveillance in their virtual classrooms. Using the lens of "sousveillance," or surveillance of authority figures "from below," we examine teachers' experiences of parental presence and accountability requests in their online classrooms and the implications this had for their work and mental health. We conducted semi-structured focus groups and interviews with 47 educators and nine key informants across Canada. We identified three themes: parental sousveillance role and the pressure of visibility; boundary issues in the online classroom; and sousveillant accountability for teachers. The real-time visibility of online classrooms undermined teacher-student connections, adding a new type of occupational stressor to teachers' work. Parental sousveillance reshaped work practices and strained classroom relationships; parents contacting teachers during classes and by email also created strain. Teachers' occupational health in digital classrooms was shaped by parent monitoring, and these conditions changed their job demands. We recommend school board policies to reduce these stressors.

items.title: Quality of life in andrology: a scoping review of original human studies.
items.abstract: Background Andrological and male urologic conditions can reshape daily life in ways that are not captured by laboratory, anatomical or technical endpoints. Fertility plans, sexual confidence, body image, continence, intimate relationships and the burden of treatment may all matter as much as symptom relief. Objective To map original human studies reporting quality of life (QoL) or closely related patient-reported outcomes across eight clinical topics: male infertility, erectile dysfunction, ejaculatory dysfunction, Peyronie disease, hypogonadism, varicocele, penile cancer and ejaculation-sparing surgery for benign prostatic obstruction (BPO). Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Embase were searched from inception to 11 September 2026 for the original six andrology topics. A targeted PubMed and backward-citation update through 18 October 2026 added penile cancer and ejaculation- sparing BPO surgery. Eligible reports were randomized studies, observational cohorts, registries, cross-sectional or casecontrol studies, qualitative studies and instrument-development work in adult men. For penile cancer, QoL had to be analyzed directly, including explicit QoL-focused multidomain assessments or life satisfaction; sexual, urinary, aesthetic or reconstructive outcomes alone were deemed insufficient. In the BPO domain, surgery had to be explicitly ejaculation-sparing and QoL had to be measured directly. Reviews, meta-analyses, guidelines, editorials, case reports and non-human studies were excluded from the evidence map. Two reviewers independently screened and charted eligible reports. Results Sixty-five original reports were included: seven instrument- development or validation studies and 58 condition-focused reports. Infertility and sexual dysfunction affected distress, confidence, intimacy and couple dynamics; Peyronie disease added a prominent burden from body image and deformity; and testosterone trials showed more consistent effects on sexual activity than on global vitality. Varicocele remained poorly studied from the patient's perspective. Twenty penile-cancer reports directly analyzed global QoL, QoL-focused domains or life satisfaction; they showed a multidimensional burden but provided little comparative or longitudinal evidence. Five studies of explicitly ejaculation- sparing BPO surgery measured QoL directly; urinary bother generally improved, whereas preservation of ejaculation varied by technique and study design. Conclusions QoL should be treated as a core outcome, not inferred from technical success. A practical framework pairs a brief generic measure with a validated condition-specific instrument and targeted questions that reflect the intervention. Prospective studies should prespecify patient-reported endpoints, use clinically meaningful time points and report improvement, stability and deterioration separately.

items.title: Educational quality of youtube videos on hypospadias repair: a comparison of institutional vs. individual sources.
items.abstract: Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the educational quality of hypospadias surgery videos on YouTube using structured tools, and to investigate the relationship between digital popularity metrics and educational value by comparing institutional and individual sources. Methods A YouTube search using the terms "hypospadias surgery" and "hypospadias repair" yielded 96 eligible videos, categorized as institutional (n = 43) or individual (n = 53). Educational quality was independently assessed by three reviewers using the LAP-VEGaS, JAMA, Modified DISCERN, and Global Quality Score (GQS) criteria. Digital popularity metrics, including the Video Power Index (VPI), were calculated, and a multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of educational quality. Results Institutional videos achieved significantly higher educational quality scores across all structured assessment tools (LAPVEGaS, JAMA, Modified DISCERN, and GQS) compared to individual videos. Furthermore, institutional videos demonstrated significantly higher views, VPI, and longer durations. Although significant correlations existed between popularity metrics and quality scores, multivariable regression analysis revealed that video duration was the sole independent predictor of the LAP-VEGaS score; channel type and VPI were not independent determinants. Conclusions Institutional videos provide superior structured educational quality for hypospadias repair. Digital engagement metrics do not independently predict actual educational value; instead, video duration is the key determinant of quality. Surgical trainees should preferentially utilize detailed, adequately long institutional content over popular, short videos.

items.title: Racial Misclassification of American Indian and Alaska Native People by Cause of Death and Indian Health Service Region, PRCDA Counties, 2020.
items.abstract: Objectives Racial misclassification in vital statistics data is common among American Indian and Alaska Native (AI/AN) populations and varies by geographic region. A previous study showed racial misclassification varies by cause of death (COD) among the non-Hispanic AI/AN (NH-AI/AN) population nationally. We examined how racial misclassification by COD varied geographically in data from 2020. Methods We used the 2020 US Cancer Statistics American Indian and Alaska Native Mortality Database, which links the Indian Health Service patient registration database to death records to correctly classify AI/AN individuals misclassified as another race. We calculated death rates per 100 000 population for 10 common CODs in 2020 among NH-AI/AN people. Pre-linkage and post-linkage death rates and percentage misclassification were calculated by race, sex, COD, and region. Analyses of death rates and percentage misclassification were restricted to NH-AI/AN people living in purchased/referred care delivery area counties. We calculated death rates for non-Hispanic White people for comparison. Results Overall, percentage misclassification of NH-AI/AN race by COD ranged from 6.3% for COVID-19 to 20.3% for Alzheimer disease. Percentage misclassification varied by geographic region, COD, and sex. Infectious diseases, such as influenza/pneumonia and COVID-19, had a lower percentage misclassification than several chronic diseases including heart disease, chronic lower respiratory disease, Alzheimer disease, and cancer. Conclusions Racial misclassification among NH-AI/AN people varied by COD, sex, and region. Future work could explore causes for the differential misclassification by geographic region and COD among NH-AI/AN populations.

items.title: An algorithm to predict new magnetic resonance imaging lesions to support improved disease surveillance in multiple sclerosis.
items.abstract: Background People with multiple sclerosis undergo magnetic resonance imaging to monitor disease activity and treatment response. Current recommendations are non-individualized, increasing unnecessary imaging and cost. Risk-based tools could enable more personalized surveillance strategies. Objective To develop an algorithm that predicts new lesions in subsequent brain magnetic resonance imaging. Methods Using longitudinal data from adults with MS at the Johns Hopkins MS Center (2017-2025) with ⩾2 visits and ⩾1 magnetic resonance imaging scan, a logistic regression model with fivefold stratified cross-validation predicted new lesions, using a sensitivity-prioritized threshold. Features included disease activity history, therapy class, and patient-reported outcomes. Results Among 1131 participants, 8.8% developed new magnetic resonance imaging lesions. At a 0.08 threshold, sensitivity was 0.71 and specificity 0.75, with area under the curve 0.804 (95% confidence interval = 0.755-0.851). Negative predictive value was 0.96 (95% CI = 0.95-0.98), and residual risk among the 71% classified as low risk was 3.6%. Prior magnetic resonance imaging activity and higher disability predicted new lesions, while older age and high-efficacy disease-modifying therapy use were associated with lower risk. Conclusion The algorithm accurately stratified patients by risk of magnetic resonance imaging lesion activity and identified who could undergo longer surveillance intervals with low risk of missed inflammation. With validation and integration, it may enable personalized monitoring in multiple sclerosis care.

items.title: Phenotypic Frailty Assessed Using Different Instruments and Incident Falls in Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
items.abstract: Background Systematic reviews of prospective studies have consistently reported associations between phenotypic frailty and a higher risk of falls. However, the phenotype has been defined across studies using an assortment of frailty assessment instruments that vary in complexity. We determined associations of phenotypic frailty assessed by the more complicated Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS) phenotype and simpler Study of Osteoporotic Fractures (SOF) and FRAIL scale phenotypes with risk of falls in community-dwelling older adults. Methods Prospective study of 14,596 participants (7593 women, 7003 men) enrolled in 4 cohort studies of older adults. CHS (5 components), SOF (3 components), and FRAIL (5 components) frailty phenotypes assessed at an index examination in each cohort. Participants were classified as robust, pre-frail, or frail using each phenotype. Primary outcome was self-reported recurrent (≥ 2 vs. 1 or none) falls in the subsequent year after the index examination. Results During the year after the index examination, 1220 (16.1%) women and 1025 men (14.6%) reported recurrent falls. Increasing evidence of frailty defined by each phenotype in women and men was similarly associated with higher odds of recurrent falls. After accounting for traditional fall risk factors, odds ratios of recurrent falls for prefrailty versus robust ranged from 1.6 to 1.7 in women and 1.5 to 1.8 in men. Odds ratios of recurrent falls for frail versus robust ranged from 2.2 to 2.8 in women and from 2.6 to 3.5 in men. Associations in both sexes were present in individuals with and without a past fall history. Conclusions Pre-frailty and frailty defined by CHS, SOF, or FRAIL phenotypes are similarly associated with a higher risk of recurrent falls. These findings suggest the potential utility of using SOF or FRAIL phenotypes in time-limited and space-constrained practice settings to identify community-dwelling older adults at increased risk of falls.

items.title: Pain and Sedative Prescribing and Diagnostic Delay in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A National Population-Based Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Introduction Symptoms of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) often evolve over 5 years before diagnosis, yet little is known about pain and sedative medication use during this period. We aimed to characterise prescribing trajectories before and after IBD diagnosis and examine associations of prescribing with diagnostic delays. Methods Using UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink-GOLD, we identified adults with IBD diagnosed between 2010 and 2021. Among those with 5 years' follow-up before and after diagnosis, we assessed prescribing prevalences of opioids, gabapentinoids, tricyclic antidepressants, benzodiazepines, and Z-drugs. Among those with 5 years' follow-up before diagnosis, Cox regression examined associations between prescribing and time from first gastrointestinal symptom to diagnosis. Time-to-discontinuation of long-term prescriptions after diagnosis was examined in those with follow-up 1 year before diagnosis and 5 years after. Results Among 4433 adults with IBD, the proportion prescribed pain or sedative medications doubled from 8% to 16% during the 5 years before diagnosis and remained high (19% to 21%) throughout the subsequent 5 years. In a second cohort of 8848 individuals, median time from first gastrointestinal symptom to diagnosis was 13 months longer for UC and 14 months longer for CD among those prescribed pain or sedative medications than those who were not. Median time to discontinuation of long-term prescriptions after diagnosis was 4-8 months. Conclusions Pain and sedative prescribing is common before and after IBD diagnosis and is associated with a longer time to diagnosis. Timely investigation for IBD should be considered in patients receiving these medications who present with suggestive symptoms.

items.title: Hyperimmune immunoglobulin for people with COVID-19.
items.abstract: Rationale Hyperimmune intravenous immunoglobulin (hIVIG) is a preparation of polyclonal antibodies obtained from pooled convalescent plasma or immunised animals. It is a potential therapy for coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). This review update focusses on hIVIG. It emanates from a 2021 parent review investigating convalescent plasma and hIVIG for people with COVID-19. Objectives To assess the benefits and harms of hIVIG therapy for people with COVID-19, and to maintain evidence currency using a living systematic review approach. Search methods We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, the Epistemonikos COVID-19 L*OVE Platform, and clinical trial registries from 1 January 2019 onwards. We conducted searches on 15 December 2024. Eligibility criteria We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that evaluated hIVIG for COVID-19, irrespective of participants' disease severity, age, gender, or ethnicity. We excluded other coronavirus disease studies, and those evaluating standard immunoglobulin. Outcomes We used the GRADE approach to rate the certainty of evidence for all-cause mortality, clinical status or symptom resolution, quality of life, adverse events, grade 3-4 adverse events, and serious adverse events. Risk of bias We used the RoB 2 tool to assess bias in the RCTs. Synthesis methods We followed standard Cochrane methodology. Included studies We included eight new RCTs in this update, for a total of 13 included studies with 3374 participants. Of these, 1511 participants received hIVIG from humans, 547 received swine glyco-humanised polyclonal antibody, 1075 received a bovine-derived polyclonal preparation, and 241 received equine-derived polyclonal antibody (EpAb). Three RCTs included participants with asymptomatic or mild disease, one included participants with mild to moderate disease, and nine included participants with moderate to severe disease. We identified eight ongoing studies and nine studies awaiting assessment. Synthesis of results We summarise key results for three prioritised comparisons below. The main review presents five comparisons (including these three) in summary of findings tables, and all analysed comparisons (including additional dose ranges of hIVIG and animal-derived polyclonal antibodies), with some results presented in supplementary tables. Participants with moderate to severe disease Benefits of human-derived hIVIG hIVIG may have little to no impact on all-cause mortality at 28 days (risk ratio (RR) 0.75, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.45 to 1.24; low-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain about the effect on worsening of clinical status by day 7 (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.58 to 1.23; very low-certainty evidence). It may have little to no impact on improvement of clinical status by day 28 (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.97 to 1.08; low-certainty evidence). No studies reported on quality of life. Harms of human-derived hIVIG hIVIG may have little to no impact on adverse events (any grade) by day 28 (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.19; 449 per 1000; 2 studies, 599 participants; low-certainty evidence). Participants receiving hIVIG probably experience more grade 3-4 adverse events than those given placebo (RR 4.09, 95% CI 1.39 to 12.01; moderate-certainty evidence). hIVIG therapy may have little to no effect on serious adverse events or death by day 28 (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.45 to 1.14; 96 per 1000; 1 study, 572 participants; low-certainty evidence). Benefits of equine-derived polyclonal antibody (EpAb) EpAb may reduce all-cause mortality at 28 days (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.26 to 1.37; low-certainty evidence). EpAb may reduce worsening of clinical status by day 28 (RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.38 to 1.18; low-certainty evidence). It may improve clinical status by day 28 (RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.17; low-certainty evidence). No studies reported on quality of life. Harms of EpAb EpAb may have little to no impact on the number of adverse events (any grade) by day 28 (RR 0.99, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.31; low-certainty evidence). Grade 3-4 adverse events were not reported. EpAb may reduce serious adverse events (RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.38 to 1.19; low-certainty evidence). Participants with asymptomatic or mild disease Benefits of human-derived hIVIG We do not know whether hIVIG has any impact on all-cause mortality at 28 days (RR not estimable as no events; very low-certainty evidence). hIVIG may have little to no effect on admission to hospital or death by day 28 (RR 2.38, 95% CI 0.63 to 9.03; low-certainty evidence). It may have little to no impact on symptom resolution by day 14 (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.87 to 1.21; low-certainty evidence). Quality of life was not reported. Harms of human-derived hIVIG hIVIG may have little to no impact on adverse events (any grade) by day 28 (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.72 to 1.18; low-certainty evidence). Grade 3-4 adverse events were not reported. hIVIG may have little to no effect on serious adverse events by day 28 (RR 2.38, 95% CI 0.63 to 9.03; low-certainty evidence). Authors' conclusions We included data from 13 RCTs that compared hIVIG to standard therapy or placebo. Clinical heterogeneity (e.g. human- and animal-derived preparations, varying doses and comparators) precluded pooling most of the studies. In moderate to severe disease, human-derived hIVIG may have little to no impact on mortality or clinical improvement. hIVIG may have little to no effect on adverse events of any grade and serious adverse events, and probably increases grade 3-4 adverse events. In moderate to severe disease, equine-derived polyclonal antibody may reduce mortality and clinical worsening, and may increase the number of people discharged at 28 days. EpAb may have little to no impact on adverse events at 28 days and may reduce serious adverse events. In asymptomatic to mild disease, the effect of human-derived hIVIG on mortality is very uncertain. It may have little to no impact on symptom resolution, adverse events (any grade), and serious adverse events. This is the second and final update of this living systematic review. We regularly searched for new evidence and updated the review as relevant studies became available. With funding expired and the need for a living approach no longer urgent, the review will be retired after this update. items.title: Stream Nitrate and Land Cover Correlations in a Baseflow Dominated Sandplain in the North-Central United States.
items.abstract: High nitrate concentrations in groundwater and surface water are a significant regulatory and public health concern in central Wisconsin and across the Midwest United States. High-quality regional scale nitrate data are key to understanding and implementing policy that might reduce nitrate in groundwater. To meet this need, nitrate was measured at 502 stream/road crossings across the Central Sands region of Wisconsin. Since the streams in this region are baseflow dominated, surface water nitrate measurements provide insights into nitrate concentrations in groundwater. Additionally, because both the streams and the road are public, the stream/road crossings provide long-term site access. Groundwater flow paths were derived from a regional model to test correlations between the stream nitrate measurements and land cover in the upstream groundwater catchment area. Agriculture, specifically potato/vegetable land cover, had a moderate correlation, R 2 = 0.47, with stream nitrate. When the smaller groundwater contributing zones ( 2 = 0.86. This result suggests nitrate measurements from features with small contributing zones, such as headwaters, springs, and wells, have greater uncertainty than larger contributing zones. It is an example of having greater certainty in a relationship over a larger, more integrated measurement area and less certainty but more spatial resolution from a smaller measurement area. This study shows groundwater models can effectively be used with limitations to assess nitrate sources to baseflow dominated streams, providing a tool for effective and informed management.

items.title: Changes in Insulin Resistance During a Personalized Lifestyle Intervention in Children With Overweight and Obesity: The Role of BMI Z-Score and Puberty.
items.abstract: Aim To examine changes in insulin resistance (IR) during a personalized lifestyle intervention in children with overweight or obesity, while considering influencing factors such as BMI Z-score and pubertal development. Materials and methods This retrospective cohort study included 662 children (aged 4-17 years), enrolled in the Centre for Overweight Adolescent and Children's Healthcare (COACH) program at Maastricht University Medical Centre (MUMC+), for cross-sectional analyses. A subset of 136 children had follow-up data. IR was assessed using the Homeostatic Model Assessment for Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR), calculated from fasting insulin and glucose levels. Pubertal stage was determined according to Tanner staging. Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) was included as a marker for Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD). Results At baseline, HOMA-IR was significantly positively associated with age, BMI Z-score, pubertal stage (Tanner 2-3), and ALT levels, but not with sex. During intervention, BMI Z-score significantly decreased, whereas mean HOMA-IR did not change significantly. Furthermore, change in HOMA-IR was positively associated with change in BMI Z-score and baseline ALT. Conclusion During a personalized lifestyle intervention, improvements in BMI Z-score were linked to favourable changes in IR. Reductions in BMI Z-score were associated with improved insulin sensitivity, after adjustment for pubertal stage and the other variables included in the model. These findings highlight the importance of considering developmental and clinical context when interpreting HOMA-IR during interventions, as such variables substantially influence metabolic patterns over time.

items.title: Pandemic Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 and SARS-CoV-2 Transmission During Commercial Air Travel: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis, 2009-2023.
items.abstract: Objective We conducted a systematic review to understand the transmission risk of novel influenza A viruses and novel coronaviruses during commercial air travel. Methods Eight databases were searched for studies describing communicable disease transmission risk on commercial flights published from 2004 through 2025. We focused on influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Title and abstract screening, full-text review, and data extraction were performed using Covidence software. Proximate passengers were defined as people seated within 2 or 3 rows of the index case. Attack rates, which represented the number of laboratory-confirmed infections divided by the number of passengers, were computed for proximate passengers, non-proximate passengers, and the whole plane. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed to compute pooled attack rates and pooled risk differences between proximate passengers and non-proximate passengers. Results Twenty-nine studies met inclusion criteria. Among influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 studies, the pooled attack rate for the whole plane was 1.3% (95% CI, 0.7%-2.4%) and the pooled risk difference was 1.8% (95% CI, -2.1% to 5.6%). Among SARS-CoV-2 studies, the pooled attack rate for the whole plane was 2.2% (95% CI, 0.7%-6.5%) and the pooled risk difference was 14.8% (95% CI, 6.5%-23.1%). Subgroup analysis showed that the SARS-CoV-2 pooled risk difference for people with intensive follow-up was 28.1% (95% CI, 17.2%-39.1%) in contrast with 3.9% (95% CI, -5.7% to 13.6%) for people with non-intensive follow-up. Conclusion Transmission occurred with both influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 and SARS-CoV-2, with greater transmission risk observed for SARS-CoV-2. Evidence-based, pathogen-specific preventive measures may be considered to help reduce the risk of in-flight transmission.

items.title: Associations Between Particle Radioactivity and Mean Arterial Pressure Among a Cohort of Older Men.
items.abstract: Background Although particulate matter and the radiometric components of ambient particulate matter, namely, particle radioactivity (PR) (measured as particle gross β activity), have been associated with cardiovascular health effects including increased blood pressure, there is a lack of epidemiological literature demonstrating associations between PR exposures on mean arterial pressure (MAP) differed by measured positions. As such, in this study, we examined the impact of PR exposures on MAP in a cohort of older men. Methods We investigated the associations between PR and MAP in sitting, supine, and standing positions using repeated measurements of 1749 participants including a total of 10 111 visits from 1980 to 2017. We analyzed the data using generalized linear mixed-effects regression models with random intercepts for each individual. Results We found increases in sitting MAP, supine MAP, and standing MAP associated with PR across all exposure windows (1-28 days) after adjusting for covariates, with supine MAP showing the strongest estimated associations. Specifically, an interquartile range change in the 28-day moving average PR exposure (Bq/m 3 ) was associated with 1.66 (95% CI, 1.13-2.18) mm Hg ( P P P Conclusions As an extension of our previous study in 2018, we observe a positive association between PR exposures and MAP in different positions. MAP can be an important biomarker when assessing air pollution health effects on cardiovascular diseases.

items.title: Plasma Alpha-Defensin 1 and Prognosis of Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Prospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Background To evaluate the association between DEFA1 (alpha-defensin 1) levels and prognosis of acute ischemic stroke. Methods We measured plasma DEFA1 levels in 3424 participants from 26 hospitals across China. Study outcome data on death, major disability, and vascular events were collected at 3 months after stroke onset. The primary outcome was defined as a combination of death and major disability (modified Rankin Scale score ≥3) at 3 months after stroke onset. Results During the 3-month follow-up period, 861 participants (25.15%) experienced major disability or death. After multivariate adjustment, participants in the highest quartile of plasma DEFA1 had significantly higher odds of the primary outcome, major disability, and mortality than those in the lowest quartile, with adjusted odds ratios of 2.17 (95% CI: 1.69-2.79; P for trend P for trend P for trend P for linearity ≤0.05). Integration of DEFA1 into the conventional model improved discrimination and stratification performance for these adverse outcomes, while enhancing model fit and calibration. Conclusions Elevated DEFA1 levels in the acute phase of ischemic stroke were associated with higher odds of 3-month mortality and major disability, suggesting that DEFA1 may serve as a valuable prognostic biomarker in ischemic stroke.

items.title: Building Readiness for Group-Based Fibroid Care: Implementation Insights From the Centering Patients With Fibroids Intervention.
items.abstract: In the United States, fibroids affect an estimated 26 million people and are associated with $5.9 to $34.4 billion in annual health care costs. To address gaps in education and care, we developed a low-cost solution: Centering Patients With Fibroids (CPWF), a patient-centered group-based intervention grounded in the Centering Healthcare Institute's evidence-based model. This qualitative study identifies organizational factors that influenced the implementation of the CPWF in hospital settings and specifies how these factors can be addressed to support sustainability and scalability. We conducted semi-structured interviews with 17 health care providers and administrators who facilitated CPWF or other women's health education interventions. We collected data from April 2023 through April 2024 and used rapid qualitative thematic analysis guided by the practical, robust implementation and sustainability model (PRISM). Five themes emerged from the data: (a) Ensure Organizational Readiness and Build Infrastructure for Program Delivery, (b) Design an Adaptable Intervention for Hospital Context, (c) Secure Adequate Staffing to Support Implementation, (d) Strengthen Internal Communication to Enhance Program Uptake, and (e) Preemptively Address Financial Barriers. Successful implementation of CPWF and similar women's health interventions requires clear infrastructure, defined staff roles, and consistent communication. In addition, incorporating sustainable funding strategies, such as adapting existing billing codes, leveraging value-based care models, and building community or institutional partnerships, has potential to increase program viability and long-term impact. Findings can help practitioners address implementation barriers in group-based care programs before they arise and may contribute to cost savings over time.

items.title: Photoallergic Reactions to Coumarin: A Case Series.
items.abstract: Background Skin exposure to coumarin and its derivatives is common, from both natural sources and cosmetics, where it is valued for its fragrant properties. Despite this widespread exposure, coumarin is not included in recommended photopatch test series, even though it can cause photoallergy. Objectives To describe a case series of coumarin photoallergy identified through photopatch testing and to characterize its clinical presentations and diagnostic pathway. Patients/materials/methods Seven patients (five from Montpellier, two from Lille University Hospitals) presenting with recurrent, photodistributed or seasonal cutaneous eruptions suggestive of photoallergic contact dermatitis underwent photopatch testing with the European baseline photopatch test allergens plus additional allergens selected according to clinical history, including coumarin 5% in petrolatum. Reactions were graded using the ICDRG classification. Results All seven patients showed a positive photopatch reaction to coumarin, confirming allergic photosensitization. Two also had positive photopatch tests to ketoprofen, and one had a positive patch test to colophonium. The cohort included five men and two women, with a mean age of 41.6 years (range 8-69) and a mean diagnostic delay of nearly 7 years (range 3-11). Clinical presentation varied by exposure source. Conclusions Coumarin photoallergy appears under-recognized, affecting both children and adults, with substantial diagnostic delay. Coumarin should be more systematically included in photopatch test series.

items.title: Epidemiology of unhealthy dietary patterns in Nigeria: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Background Unhealthy dietary patterns are major drivers of non-communicable diseases, but population-level evidence from Nigeria remains fragmented, limiting targeted policy and public health response. To address this gap, we synthesised study-defined dietary indicators in Nigerian populations. Methods We searched MEDLINE, Embase, CABI Global Health, African Journals Online, Google Scholar, and reference lists for Nigerian community/population-based studies published between 1 January 2000 and 1 October 2025. We grouped unhealthy diets into five domains: fruit and vegetable inadequacy, high salt intake, high fat/unhealthy fats, high sugar/ultra-processed foods (UPFs), and unhealthy meal patterns/food environment. We generated pooled prevalence by age (5-17 years; 18-79 years) through a random-effects meta-analysis and estimated illustrative population extrapolations using the United Nations' mid-2025 population projections for Nigeria. Results Twenty-four studies contributed 74 dietary-indicator estimates. Fruit and vegetable inadequacy had the highest pooled prevalence (72.0%; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 63.6-79.1), followed by high salt intake (63.8%; 95% CI = 48.2-77.0), high sugar/UPFs (57.1%; 95% CI = 40.6-72.2), high fat/unhealthy fats (48.8%; 95% CI = 38.3-59.4), and unhealthy meal patterns (40.5%; 95% CI = 27.0-55.7). Illustrative extrapolations to Nigeria's 2025 population suggested about 95 million adults with inadequate fruit and vegetable intake and over 83 million exposed to high salt intake. Pooled prevalence for sugar/UPF was the highest in the younger study group (82.5%; 95% CI = 76.9-87.0), corresponding to about 60 million 5-17-year-olds. Conclusions Unhealthy dietary concerns were frequently reported in the studied populations. However, better dietary surveillance and action to improve diet quality are needed to draw inferences to the national level, as we observed substantial variation in definitions, sampling, and geographical coverage of the included studies. Registration PROSPERO: CRD420251252492.

items.title: Parallel long-term changes in body roundness index and fasting plasma glucose and their association with incident heart failure: evidence from the Kailuan study.
items.abstract: Background Body roundness index (BRI), which better captures central adiposity than the body mass index, and fasting plasma glucose (FPG) are both associated with heart failure (HF) risk, but their joint longitudinal patterns remain unclear. We aimed to identify the joint trajectories of BRI and FPG and evaluate their associations with incident HF. Methods In this prospective cohort study, we enrolled 41,767 participants from the Kailuan Study with repeated measurements of BRI and FPG between 2006 and 2010. We identified joint BRI and FPG trajectories using group-based multi-trajectory modelling. We then ascertained incident HF from the 2010-2011 survey through to 31 December 2022 using medical records, administrative databases, questionnaires, and adjudication by cardiologists, and formed Cox proportional hazards models to assess the associations between joint BRI and FPG trajectories and HF risk, while adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, and clinical covariates. Results We identified four distinct dual trajectory groups: low BRI/low FPG (39.5%), moderate BRI/moderate FPG (47.3%), highest BRI/high FPG (7.8%), and high BRI/highest FPG (5.4%). A total of 747 HF cases occurred during a median follow-up of 12.1 years. Compared with the low BRI/low FPG group, multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios were 1.47 (95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.21-1.79) for the moderate BRI/moderate FPG, 2.31 (95% CI = 1.79-2.97) for the highest BRI/high FPG, and 2.90 (95% CI = 2.18-3.85) for the high BRI/highest FPG groups. Joint longitudinal trajectories of BRI and FPG group showed significant interactions with age and hypertension status in relation to incident HF. The associations were stronger associations among younger individuals and those without hypertension. Multiple sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these findings. Conclusions Joint longitudinal trajectories of BRI and FPG were independently and progressively associated with incident HF risk. Repeated assessment of BRI and FPG may enhance long-term HF risk stratification and support earlier targeted prevention.

items.title: Mathematical foundations of boundary-enhanced decoupled networks for endoscopic polyp segmentation.
items.abstract: Background and ObjectiveAccurate segmentation of colorectal polyps in endoscopic images is critical for early diagnosis of colorectal cancer. Although deep learning has achieved promising results, the entanglement of body and edge features remains a fundamental challenge, particularly at ambiguous boundaries where gradient information is weak. This paper presents a mathematical treatment of boundary-enhanced decoupled segmentation networks.MethodsWe establish the mathematical foundations of a boundary-enhanced decoupled framework. The SBE (body-edge flow decoupling), BEM (boundary enhancement), and GAB (group aggregation bridge) building blocks are adopted from existing literature; our contribution lies in their principled mathematical analysis and systematic combination. The analysis includes: (1) a formal comparison of Roberts and Sobel gradient operators, proving Sobel's superior noise robustness for endoscopic boundary detection; (2) complete formulation of flow-field decoupling via differentiable bilinear sampling; (3) a dual-stream loss with boundary relaxation and online hard example mining to address class imbalance; and (4) rigorous definitions of evaluation metrics including Hausdorff distance.ResultsThe framework achieves mIoU of 91.21% and 91.41% on two private polyp datasets, outperforming nine state-of-the-art methods. On public benchmarks Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB, it attains mIoU of 89.12% and 91.14%, respectively. The Cohen's kappa coefficient reaches 0.94. Ablation studies confirm each component contributes positively, with boundary enhancement yielding the largest improvement.ConclusionsThe mathematical analysis provides a principled understanding of why boundary enhancement and body-edge decoupling improve polyp segmentation. Explicit gradient priors and differentiable decoupling are effective for medical image segmentation with ambiguous boundaries.

items.title: ROS-Programmed Ruthenium Nanotheranostic for Spatiotemporally Controlled Chemo-Photodynamic-Immunometabolic Therapy of Breast Cancer.
items.abstract: Metal-based photodynamic therapy holds promise for cancer treatment, yet its clinical translation is hindered by poor tissue penetration, off-target phototoxicity, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Herein, a ROS-programmed ruthenium nanotheranostic, NRuIR NPs, is developed to integrate imaging-guided chemo-photodynamic therapy with metabolic immune remodeling for amplified antitumor efficacy. NRuIR NPs are engineered by coloading a newly synthesized near-infrared-absorbing ruthenium(II) photosensitizer (RuIR) and the IDO1 inhibitor NLG919 into a folate-targeted amphiphilic polymer containing ROS-cleavable thioketal (TK) linkers. Upon 808 nm laser irradiation, RuIR generates ROS that (i) mediates cytotoxic chemo-PDT effects and (ii) cleaves TK linkers to trigger on-demand payload release while enhancing intratumoral penetration. This cascade provokes immunogenic cell death (ICD) to promote dendritic cell maturation and T-cell priming. Simultaneously, laser-triggered NLG919 release blocks the IDO1-mediated tryptophan-to-kynurenine metabolic axis, which diminishes regulatory T-cell populations and restores cytotoxic T-lymphocyte function, thereby transforming immunologically "cold" tumors into "hot" phenotypes. Integrated proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses revealed disrupted redox homeostasis, activation of TNF-α/IFN-γ-associated inflammatory signaling, and suppression of proliferation- and metastasis-related pathways. Collectively, this work presents a spatiotemporally controlled supramolecular platform for ruthenium-based photoimmunometabolic therapy.
