items.title: Theory of mind and social problem solving in patients with gambling disorder.
items.abstract: Introduction This study aimed to investigate the profile of Theory of Mind (ToM) and social problem solving impairments in patients diagnosed with gambling disorder (GD), using a scenario-based measure that requires both freely generating and identifying the best explanations and solutions. Methods The sample comprised 25 patients diagnosed with GD along with two comparison groups: 25 patients diagnosed with alcohol use disorder (AUD), and 25 healthy controls (HCs). A performance-based ToM and social problem solving measure, as well as clinical and cognitive measures, were administered. Results The GD group showed impairments in generating quality solutions on the Social Problem Resolution Task and in the number of optimal solutions generated on the Social Problem Fluency Task. However, the mere recognition of optimal solutions and ToM were intact. The two clinical groups did not differ from each other. Based on exploratory correlational analyses, state anxiety might have confounded some of the impairments observed in the GD group. Conclusions These results highlight the importance of assessing sociocognitive functions in behavioural addictions, such as GD, using performance-based measures that can reveal specific sociocognitive impairment patterns. This can guide intervention planning, potentially enhancing the effectiveness of interventions and leading to better outcomes.

items.title: Identification of Insomnia Disorder Using Machine Learning and Wearable Technology.
items.abstract: Insomnia is a prevalent sleep disorder. Wearable electroencephalography (EEG) combined with machine learning (ML) offers a promising, low-burden approach for home-based sleep monitoring and objective assessment of insomnia. The study included 112 patients with insomnia disorder (ID) and 98 healthy controls (HC), who underwent overnight forehead EEG recording. For each subject, macro-sleep metrics, as well as EEG-derived features including aperiodic and periodic features, were extracted. To classify ID and HC, we constructed predictive models based on three feature categories and their combinations. Specifically, we trained five ML models, namely Elastic Net, SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost and CatBoost. All models performed significantly better than chance. Performance was highest for feature sets including periodic features, with the CatBoost periodic and macro + periodic models achieving the highest AUC (0.765). SHAP analysis of the full-feature CatBoost model showed that delta-band power and sleep timing ranked at the top, whereas aperiodic features contributed less but remained informative. This study explored the value of objective metrics derived from wearable sleep devices in insomnia assessment and the role of aperiodic and periodic sleep features. These findings support the hyperarousal model of insomnia and the feasibility of wearable sleep monitoring as a low-burden adjunct for insomnia assessment.

items.title: Implicit Age Identity and Psychological Distress in Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
items.abstract: This study examined associations between implicit age identity and explicit self-perceptions of aging with depressive and anxiety symptoms and guilt related to self-perceived burden (GSPB) in 109 community-dwelling older adults. Implicit age identity was assessed using an Implicit Association Test, and a path model was estimated to evaluate their contribution to psychological distress. The model showed excellent fit, explaining 44% of depression, 20% of anxiety, and 15% of GSPB. Implicit age identity and negative self-perceptions of aging were significantly related to depression, anxiety, and GSPB. These findings underscore the relevance of implicit and explicit aging cognitions for late-life mental health.

items.title: From Virus to Sexual Violence: The Dark Spillovers of Pandemic Uncertainty.
items.abstract: Pandemic uncertainty has magnified underlying societal issues, bringing the hidden crisis of sexual violence into sharper focus. As fear, isolation, and breakdowns in institutional support systems collide, the threat of exploitation surges, often unnoticed and unaddressed. This study investigates how pandemic-induced uncertainty asymmetrically affects sexual violence in 10 nations that record historically high prevalence and substantial uncertainty levels: India, South Africa, the USA, Brazil, Mexico, Bangladesh, the Philippines, Colombia, Nigeria, and France. Unlike prior research limited to COVID-19 alone, this investigation applies an expanded Pandemic Uncertainty Index built on several outbreak episodes, namely SARS, MERS, avian influenza, Ebola, and COVID-19, thereby capturing the full spectrum of health-related uncertainty. Utilizing the Quantile-on-Quantile approach, the study examines the distributional link across multiple quantiles of both variables, providing country-specific insights. The results reveal that pandemic uncertainty is strongly and positively linked with sexual violence in most of the economies examined, whereas France and Colombia display mixed patterns. These findings underscore the urgent need for adaptive, context-sensitive policies that not only respond to public health crises but also safeguard vulnerable populations from escalating sexual violence.

items.title: Does suppressing pupil reactivity weaken the peripheral drift illusion?
items.abstract: A recent computational account of the peripheral drift illusion proposes that reflexive changes in pupil size contribute to illusory motion. We examined this proposal in observers tested before and after tropicamide administration to suppress the pupillary light reflex. The illusion was reduced in most observers but was not abolished. These findings are consistent with a contribution of pupil dynamics.

items.title: Romantic Attachment and Sexual Dissatisfaction Among Spanish-Speaking Couples: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Emotionally Focused Couple Therapy.
items.abstract: This study examined whether emotionally focused couple therapy (EFCT) reduces sexual dissatisfaction and whether romantic attachment insecurity is associated with sexual dissatisfaction among Spanish-speaking couples experiencing relationship distress. Seventy heterosexual couples from Argentina, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Mexico, and Spain were randomly assigned to EFCT (8-20 sessions) or to a wait-list control condition. Participants completed repeated assessments of sexual dissatisfaction (MSI-R SEX subscale) and romantic attachment insecurity (ECR-36). Longitudinal mixed-effects models and an actor-partner interdependence model were used to evaluate trajectories of change and dyadic interdependence. EFCT was associated with a small but statistically significant overall reduction in sexual dissatisfaction. The treatment effect did not differ significantly by sex, and exploratory sex-stratified results should be interpreted with caution. Greater romantic attachment anxiety and avoidance were associated with higher sexual dissatisfaction, both as stable between-person differences and as session-to-session within-person fluctuations. Concurrent actor-partner interdependence models (APIM) analyses indicated that both actor attachment anxiety and avoidance were associated with greater sexual dissatisfaction, whereas partner attachment anxiety and avoidance were not significantly associated with actor sexual dissatisfaction. Findings highlight the relevance of attachment-related processes for understanding sexual dissatisfaction and suggest that integrating EFCT with interventions more directly targeting sexual functioning and communication may further enhance treatment outcomes.

items.title: Neurocognitive Performance in Middle-Aged Adults With and Without HIV Infection in Côte d'Ivoire (VIRAGE).
items.abstract: Introduction A decline in neurocognitive and physical functioning is common among people living with HIV (PLWH) as they age. In many resource-limited countries, screening for neurocognitive impairment (NCI) remains challenging and available data are scarce. This study aimed to assess the cognitive performance of PLWH followed in Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire, and to examine the association between NCI and HIV factors, functional abilities and physical capacities. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 298 PLWH and 199 HIV-uninfected individuals (median age 51 years, female: 69%) participated in neurocognitive tests assessing verbal fluency, memory, processing speed, attention, executive functioning and motor speed. Tests for physical performance included the 6-min walk test, the five-times sit-to-stand test and grip strength. HIV factors included nadir CD4, antiretroviral duration, treatment failure and toxicity. Functional ability was assessed through the Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL) and the WHODAS-2 questionnaires. The global neurocognitive score (GNS) and global deficit score (GDS), summarizing participants' overall functioning, were computed after transformation of the neurocognitive raw scores into regression-based z-scores relative to the performance of the HIV-negative group. These global scores were used to assess the associations between NCI and the HIV factors, physical capacities and functional abilities. Results In adjusted analysis, PLWH achieved poorer scores than controls on the forward digit span test (p adj = 0.0008), colour trail tests 1 (p adj = 0.04) and 2 (p adj = 0.001) and pegboard test (p adj = 0.00002). The median GNS was -0.12 (Interquartile Range [IQR]: -0.51 to 0.19). The median GDS was 0.17 (IQR: 0-0.43), which translates into one in five PLWH having a GDS suggesting NCI. GNS and GDS were not associated with HIV-related factors or functional ability. Grip strength was consistently associated with the global scores (p Conclusion Grip strength warrants further investigation as a potential screening tool for NCI among these middle-aged PLWH.

items.title: Affect integration as a potential mechanism of change in social anxiety disorder: A study of within-client effects.
items.abstract: Objective Research suggests that individuals with social anxiety disorder (SAD) often struggle to accurately perceive and utilize their emotions in adaptive ways. The present study investigated whether affect integration-a construct reflecting the adaptive utilization of emotion-serves as a mechanism of change in Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and Metacognitive Therapy (MCT) for SAD. Methods The sample comprised 88 clients who reported on their level of affect integration, social anxiety symptoms, and interpersonal functioning at five occasions throughout treatment and follow-up. We disaggregated within- and between-client components of these measures to examine the effects of affect integration on subsequent social anxiety symptoms and interpersonal problems. Results At the within-client level, increases in affect integration at a given occasion were significantly associated with lower subsequent levels of interpersonal problems, specifically reducing social avoidance and submissiveness. In contrast, the within-client effect on social anxiety symptoms was not significant. Instead, a significant between-client effect emerged, demonstrating that clients who maintained higher average levels of affect integration across therapy reported lower overall social anxiety. Conclusion Overall, these findings provide nuanced support for affect integration as a meaningful factor in therapeutic change for SAD, showing a direct, time-varying capacity to precede improvements in core interpersonal problems. Clinical or methodological significance of this article What is the clinical significance of this article? This study suggests that learning to better recognize, tolerate, and express emotions may help people with social anxiety disorder improve their interpersonal functioning and reduce their anxiety. Findings highlight affect integration as a promising target for therapy, particularly for addressing difficulties with avoidance, low assertiveness, and overly submissive behavior that often keep individuals socially isolated. By clarifying how emotional skills contribute to recovery, this research may guide the development of more effective treatments for one of the most common and impairing anxiety disorders.

items.title: A Systematic Review of the Psychosocial Needs of Marginalized Adolescents and Young Adults with Cancer.
items.abstract: The psychosocial needs of adolescents and young adults with cancer (AYACs) have now been recognized as developmentally distinct from other age cohorts in the cancer patient population. Nevertheless, variation in these experiences among AYACs, due to different group identity characteristics and related disadvantages, has yet to be addressed. This article presents a systematic review of the psychosocial needs of AYACs, aged 15-39, belonging to marginalized groups, during their active cancer phase. Four databases were searched under Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analyses guidelines, resulting in the screening of 7025 articles and a final selection of 19 articles. Following quality review, thematic analysis of the 19 studies produced six themes that give a broad overview of the psychosocial needs of these groups. These were Psychosocial Wellbeing, Future Outlooks, Financial Hardship, Inequity of Care, Relationships and Cumulative Burden . Several of these themes were found to relate to multiple marginalized AYAC groups, including racial/ethnic minority, LGBTQ+ and socioeconomically disadvantaged AYACs. Direct comparisons between marginalized and nonmarginalized AYAC groups could not be made. No psychosocial interventions designed to meet the needs of AYACs at risk of marginalization were found. The review highlights gaps in the knowledge that make meeting the psychosocial needs of these groups problematic, including a lack of disaggregated descriptive data.

items.title: Abusive Youth-to-Parent Aggression: Diagnostic Accuracy and Clinical Cut-Off.
items.abstract: The demand for intervention programs for families suffering from situations of youth-to-parent aggression (YPA) has increased. The objective of the study was to validate tools for early identification of abusive YPA. To this end, we examined the diagnostic accuracy of three indicators (adolescent and parental psychological functioning and adolescents' verbal aggression) when discriminating abusive YPA from non-abusive cases. Our sample comprised 413 participants from a northen Spain, assessed between 2015 and 2018, including 133 adolescents (32.2%) and 280 parents (67.8%). Participants were drawn from a clinical sample receiving intervention for abusive YPA ( n = 195) and a community sample without abusive YPA ( n = 218). The clinical sample consisted of 52 adolescents aged 10 to 21 years (54% females; M age = 15.63, SD = 2.19), and 143 parents (63% mothers; M age = 47.29, SD = 6.77). The community sample consisted of 81 adolescents (53% female; M age = 15.22, SD = 1.53) and 137 parents (55% mothers; M age = 46.87, SD = 4.81) and was comparable to the clinical sample in terms of gender, age, ethnicity, and place of residence. Psychological functioning was measured with the Outcome Questionnaire (OQ-45), and adolescents' verbal aggression was measured using the Conflict Tactics Scales Child-Parents (CTS-CP). Logistic regression and Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis evaluated predictive capacity and identified optimal cut-off scores, respectively. Adolescents' verbal aggression showed the highest diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve = 0.878), with an optimal cut-off score of 2.50 yielding 77% sensitivity and 86% specificity. Verbal aggression measured by CTS-CP represents a promising component for rapid screening tools in clinical, educational, and forensic contexts.

items.title: Understanding COVID-19 immunization information systems in primary healthcare across 28 European countries: Eurodata study.
items.abstract: Aim To describe Immunization Information Systems (IIS) and vaccine safety surveillance mechanisms in primary health care (PHC) across Europe. Background IIS played a crucial role in monitoring the COVID-19 vaccination in Europe. Adequate vaccine safety surveillance systems after COVID-19 vaccination are essential to detect potential adverse events following immunization (AEFI). Methods A descriptive study was conducted, capturing retrospective data from the initial year of the COVID-19 vaccination campaign in 28 European countries. An ad hoc semi-structured questionnaire was employed to gather information on IIS and AEFI registration for key informants. Results PHC participated in administering COVID-19 vaccination in 26 European countries, being volunteered in 2. National-level IIS were established in 27 countries. Online registration for COVID-19 vaccines and AEFI from PHC was conducted in 27 countries. Heterogeneous information was recorded in the IIS, including the vaccination setting in 17 countries. Integration between IIS and Electronic Health Records (EHR) in PHC settings was observed in 18 countries. Online open data for IIS were provided in 18 countries, while 17 did so for AEFI. Conclusion PHC participated in COVID-19 vaccination in most European countries. IIS and AEFI notifications were well established in Europe; however, the integration of IIS and the EHR in PHC is limited.

items.title: Emotion Regulation Under Constraint: Residential Care and the Limits of the Process Model.
items.abstract: Objectives Older adults report high emotional wellbeing, yet age differences in emotion regulation strategies are inconsistent. Aging theory attributes this to preferential use of situation-focused strategies, particularly situation selection and situation modification. This review asks what follows when institutional living constrains those strategies. Methods Narrative review. Literature was identified from the reference lists of four recent syntheses, supplemented by targeted database searches and citation tracking, screened at title, abstract and full text, and appraised against Gross's process model. Results Residential care reduces control over place, company and daily structure, constraining the strategies aging theory identifies as best suited to later life. We propose that constraint compresses rather than removes situation-focused regulation, shifting it from selection among life situations to selection among moments within a fixed situation. This operates below the resolution of strategy-level instruments, all validated in community-dwelling samples. Conclusions The emotion regulation literature in aging is substantially a literature about community-dwelling older adults, and its findings should not be assumed to transfer to residential care. Clinical implications Interventions targeting cognitive change may be appropriate by default rather than by design; interventions restoring environmental discretion have an evidence base the regulation literature has not connected to this account.

items.title: Examining the associations between MOXO d-CPT performance and teacher ratings in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.
items.abstract: The objective of the study was to examine the convergence of teacher-rated behavioral ratings and performance in Distracted Continuous Performance Test (d-CPT) among children with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). Group differences in MOXO d-CPT performance between ADHD presentations were also examined. This retrospective study included a selected clinical sample of 40 children aged 6-18 who were administered MOXO d-CPT and diagnosed with ADHD at the Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Clinic of University Hospital. Turgay DSM-IV-Based Disruptive Behavior Disorders Scale and Conners Teacher-Rating Scale-Short Form were used to investigate teacher ratings. Statistical analyses were done through Spearman's correlation coefficient and Mann-Whitney-U tests. For all the analyses, Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons. Children's mean age was 10.57 years, and 65% were boys. In the unadjusted analyses, age was positively correlated with MOXO timing scores ( r = 0.332, p = 0.036), and MOXO hyperactivity scores were negatively correlated with the Oppositional subscale of the Conners Teacher Rating Scale-Short Form ( r = -0.326, p = 0.040). Despite some significance in the unadjusted analyses, the correlations between MOXO d-CPT performance and teacher ratings and the differences between ADHD presentations did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Overall, the findings indicate limited convergence between MOXO d-CPT performance and teacher-reported behavioral measures. Given the small, selected clinical sample, these findings should be considered exploratory and interpreted cautiously. Additionally, given the small sample and limited statistical power, smaller but potentially meaningful associations cannot be excluded.

items.title: Impact of single-ventricle heart disease on ethnically diverse families.
items.abstract: Background Care for patients with single-ventricle heart disease requires lifelong, multidisciplinary management; however, its impact on caregivers' socio-economic and psychological well-being remains inadequately explored. Methods We conducted a survey of caregivers of patients with single-ventricle heart disease who presented to our tertiary centre from November 2024 to November 2025, collecting anonymous responses on the self-reported social, economic, and psychological impact of the disease on families. Results A total of 104 caregivers completed the survey (response rate > 96%). Most respondents were of non-White ethnicity (64%), with 47% identifying as Hispanic. Approximately one-third of families lived remotely, including 60% in rural communities and nearly 20% at high elevation. One-quarter of parents reported high out-of-pocket medical expenses. Hispanic parents more frequently reported income loss due to reduced work hours compared with White parents (58% vs 35%, p = 0.03). Self-reported mental health disease burden was high amongst caregivers (40%), siblings (30%), and spouses (15%), regardless of ethnicity or educational level. Survey identified several actionable items such as topics that were not adequately discussed during peri-natal counselling, including high medical cost of disease (65%), caregiver burnout (75%), and anticipated mental health disorders in children (56%). Conclusion Single-ventricle heart disease imposes substantial social, financial, and self-reported psychological burdens on families. These findings highlight opportunities to improve anticipatory guidance and counselling at diagnosis. Expanding cost-effective, multidisciplinary care models, including comprehensive Fontan programs, may help mitigate these challenges. As advances in care improve survival, greater attention to caregivers and family well-being remains essential.

items.title: Outcomes and Adherence of Groups With Different Levels of Low-back-pain Chronification in a Multimodal Rehabilitation Program.
items.abstract: Objective Although psychotherapy is recommended for chronic low-back-pain patients, especially those at high level of chronification, patients' participation in this is unclear. This study was established to examine risk group-specific adherence to and benefits from multimodal rehabilitation including optional psychotherapy. Methods In this prospective cohort study, a total of 279 patients with chronic low back pain (68% female; mean age 53.2 ± 6.6 years) participated in a 6-month multimodal outpatient program with optional psychotherapy. Psychosocial questionnaires and physical assessments were applied before and after the intervention. Differences in adherence outcomes, and predictors of transitions between risk groups were analysed statistically. Results The high-risk group showed poorer adjusted post-treatment outcomes in terms of pain-related disability and current health status compared to the low-risk group, and less than the medium-risk group in pain intensity. Additionally, the high-risk group demonstrated significantly lower device-defined adherence to the training than the low-risk group, but no significant difference in utilization of psychotherapy. Higher baseline disability scores predicted a lower likelihood of transitioning to a better pain-chronification-level. Discussion Patients classified as high risk showed less observed improvement after multimodal rehabilitation than lower-risk groups, underscoring the need to investigate the effect of psychotherapy within multimodal rehabilitation programs.

items.title: Publicly Available Genomic Evidence for Nipah and Avian Influenza Viruses in Bangladesh: A Scoping Assessment of Metadata Completeness and Surveillance Representativeness at the Human–Animal Interface
items.abstract: Bangladesh experiences recurrent Nipah virus (NiV) outbreaks and sustained avian influenza virus (AIV) activity. Whether public genomic records contain metadata needed to assess surveillance representativeness across hosts, locations, and time is unclear.We conducted a structured, source-based scoping assessment of publicly documented NiV and AIV genomic records from Bangladesh (2001–2025), drawing on NCBI GenBank/INSDC and cited peer-reviewed and public-health sources. A pilot registry contained 108 entries (55 NiV, 53 AIV). Metadata were retained only when explicitly reported; unverified fields were recorded as not extracted. The registry is not a complete census. Five analytical questions were prespecified; several could not be evaluated because accession-level metadata were unavailable. The 33-accession AIV set containing H5N1 and H3N8 was excluded from H5/H9-specific interpretation. In the pilot registry, 9/108 entries (8.3%) had explicitly reported host species; the separate host-implied category was not added. Twelve entries (11.1%) had a full collection date; 21 (19.4%) had any collection date. Eight entries (7.4%) had an explicit district. The registry lists 22 NiV accession identifiers from a 2026 study, whereas the publication reports 23 newly sequenced N-gene records; this remains unresolved. Eight AIV accessions ( PV961349.1 – PV961356.1) represent eight segments of one chicken H5N1 isolate, not eight genomes. Twelve MN994-series records are HA-gene sequences from environmental live-bird-market samples.The pilot registry demonstrates substantial metadata limitations. Explicit host information was available for 8.3% of entries and explicit district for 7.4%; these prevent reliable quantitative assessment of host, district-level, and temporal representativeness and do not establish absence of surveillance or viral circulation. Accession-level reconstruction with transparent verification tiers and harmonised identifiers is required before quantitative representativeness indices or district-level priorities can be calculated.

items.title: Plate to Poo – An outreach activity to introduce the role of diet in shaping the gut microbiota​
items.abstract: The gut microbiota plays a crucial role in host health. However, public understanding of microorganisms is often dominated by a germ-centric perspective, where microbes are primarily associated with disease rather than beneficial biological functions. Improving public awareness of the gut microbiota is therefore important for promoting microbiology literacy and encouraging a more balanced understanding of microbial life. Plate to Poo is an interactive drop-in activity aimed at highlighting the relationship between diet and the gut microbiota. The activity demonstrates how dietary patterns in different countries can shape distinct microbial communities within the gut. Using colourful visuals and hands-on challenges, participants explored how nutritional components of foods influence microbial growth and diversity. Participants were asked to choose a country and select two foods commonly associated with that region. Using Food Cards and Microbe Cards, they identified microbial preferences for different nutrients and constructed a representative poo microbiota by matching microbes to the selected food. These microbes were then added to country-specific poo sheets, resulting in colourful visual representations of diet-associated gut microbial communities. By combining interactive learning with creative problem-solving, the activity aimed to improve understanding of the beneficial roles of gut microbes.

items.title: “A Living Dead”: A Qualitative Journey into Kidney Failure Experiences and Public Health Advocacy in Ghana
items.abstract: Abstract Individuals diagnosed with kidney failure often face the profound existential shock of feeling like the “living dead” due to a wide spectrum of serious, life-threatening complications. This study explored the lived experiences of individuals diagnosed with kidney failure who are undergoing haemodialysis in Ghana. Employing a purposive sampling and qualitative phenomenological research design, data were gathered through face-to-face semi-structured interviews with 15 participants (10 males, 5 females). The thematic analysis revealed a distinct narrative arc: the shock of initial diagnosis, intense emotional and psychological responses, complex healthcare experiences, adaptation to life after diagnosis, and active coping strategies coupled with a strong desire for public kidney health advocacy. The study concludes that while patients endure intense physical, emotional, and psychosocial distress throughout their treatment journey, they concurrently emerge as crucial voices for preventative health. To improve patient outcomes and honor this advocacy, there is an urgent need for intensified public awareness, lifestyle education, and subsidized early screening campaigns to promote early detection across Ghana.

items.title: From Involvement to Authorship: Co-Producing Publication Guidance with Public Contributors in Electronic Health Record Research
items.abstract: Abstract Background: There is a growing recognition of the importance of including patients and the public in research publications. However, there is limited guidance on how to effectively involve contributors as co-authors, particularly in quantitative studies using large datasets. Methods: This work drew on two projects exploring inequalities in primary care and respiratory virus burden using electronic health records (EHR). We aim to describe the co-production of guidance with a public advisory group to support meaningful co-authorship in research involving large health datasets. We worked with six contributors who varied in age, gender, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, and experiences of chronic illness, disability, and respiratory infections. We wanted to include public contributors as co-authors in our publications, however this required thoughtful planning to ensure their involvement was meaningful and not tokenistic. We held an online workshop to develop the guidance and discussed review timelines, how to give comments, payment, and strategies for reviewing technical drafts. This was informed by ongoing involvement activities and reflexive discussions, alongside researcher feedback. This paper was co-authored with advisory group members in line with the co-produced guidance developed through this work. Results: We identified four key areas for consideration: 1) establish roles and expectations across publication stages, 2) balance technical concepts and language with patient perspectives, 3) support contributors to give feedback that feedback that strengthened the interpretation, relevance and communication of the research, and informing how their feedback was used, and 4) negotiate authorship criteria, including comments while respecting anonymity, and the technical aspects involved in producing and publishing a manuscript. This highlighted a need to bring together technical expertise required to produce knowledge from large health datasets with the experiential expertise needed to interpret what that means for the public. Conclusion: Patient co-authorship in EHR research requires structure and support to ensure contributors are meaningfully involved across the publication process. Our co-produced guidance offers strategies to improve transparency, effectively engage with feedback, and recognise lived experience as a distinct and valuable form of expertise. This work shows how publication is not solely about disseminating research findings, but can be a collaborative process of knowledge production.

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of salivary immunoglobulin A for early leprosy diagnosis: a systematic review protocol
items.abstract: Abstract Background Leprosy remains a significant public health challenge worldwide. Effective disease control depends on early diagnosis and timely treatment to prevent transmission. Because laboratory confirmation lacks an established reference standard, clinicians primarily rely on clinical examination. Serological assays often yield reactive results that require careful interpretation, particularly in asymptomatic individuals and household contacts. Saliva sampling offers a simple, noninvasive, and low-cost approach with minimal contamination risk. This protocol focuses on salivary immunoglobulin A (sIgA) as a supplementary diagnostic marker and aims to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of sIgA detection in leprosy. Methods We will conduct a systematic review guided by the question: “What is the diagnostic accuracy of sIgA detection for the early diagnosis of leprosy?” We will identify studies through electronic databases and reference list screening. We will include diagnostic accuracy studies evaluating IgA in saliva for leprosy screening or diagnosis, regardless of immunoassay format. Studies assessing IgA exclusively in serum, plasma, or other non-salivary specimens will be excluded. Eligible studies will involve leprosy patients, household contacts, or individuals at risk of Mycobacterium leprae infection and will report sufficient data to estimate diagnostic performance. Two reviewers will independently conduct study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. We will synthesize results narratively and perform meta-analysis using random-effects models when data permit. Discussion This systematic review will assess the diagnostic performance of sIgA-based tests and their potential role in early leprosy detection. The findings may support improved diagnostic strategies, contribute to early case identification, and guide future research on salivary biomarkers for M. leprae infection. items.title: Burnout among internationally educated nurses in the United Kingdom National Health Service (NHS): A scoping review
items.abstract: Abstract Aim. To identify and synthesize the existing literature on burnout among Internationally educated nurses (IENs) working in the United Kingdom National Health Service. Design. Scoping review Methods This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology. Data sources MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase (Elsevier), CINAHL Complete (EBSCOhost), and Web of Science (Clarivate) were searched on 6th June 2026 with no date restrictions. Results The search yielded 1,668 records, of which 671 duplicates were removed. Following title and abstract screening of 997 records, 21 articles underwent full-text review. No studies met the predefined eligibility criteria for inclusion. Although 19 excluded studies examined burnout among nursing populations in the UK, none focused specifically on internationally educated nurses. Two studies examined internationally educated nurses, but neither assessed burnout as an outcome. Consequently, no evidence was identified regarding burnout among internationally educated nurses working in the UK NHS. Conclusion This review identified a substantial gap in the literature regarding burnout among IENs in the UK NHS. Despite decades of research examining burnout among nurses, internationally educated nurses have remained largely absent from this body of evidence. Given the increasing reliance of the NHS on IENs, research is urgently needed to understand burnout, wellbeing, and retention within this workforce and to inform targeted interventions, policy development, and workforce support strategies. items.title: Security Has Left the Barracks: Towards a New Theory of African Security
items.abstract: Abstract For decades, African security has been predominantly conceptualised through a state-centric and military paradigm that prioritises territorial defence, sovereignty and armed conflict. Although this perspective remains relevant, it is increasingly inadequate for explaining the multidimensional and interconnected security challenges confronting contemporary Africa. This article strongly argues that security has progressively migrated beyond military institutions into broader societal domains. These domains are attributed with political instability, economic vulnerability, identity conflicts, cyber insecurity, community violence, public health crises and environmental changes that increasingly shape security outcomes. In order to underscore this transformation, the article introduces the Barracks Migration Theory (BMT), a theoretical framework which posits that the principal arenas of security have shifted from the barracks to seven interconnected domains: the Ballot (Political Security), Belief (Identity and Social Security), Bank (Economic and Financial Security), Borough (Community Security), Browser (Cyber and Digital Security), Body (Human and Health Security), and Biosphere (Environmental and Ecological Security). The paper draws on illustrative but concrete cases and experiences from the present-day African security challenges to prove that contemporary African insecurity is multi-domain and dynamic and spreads itself through all these domains which are perceptually distinct but interconnected. It argues that while military organizations continue to be essential for securing peace, they have ceased to own the monopoly of security affairs governance. Through the diffusion of security across societal domains, Barracks Migration Theory proposes an African perspective to understand Security Studies.

items.title: Building a Truly Sustainable Pediatric Antimicrobial Stewardship Program: A Quasi-Experimental Study and Time Series Analysis Conducted in a Tertiary Children's Hospital in China
items.abstract: Abstract Background Antimicrobial overuse in paediatrics remains a critical global public health crisis accelerating antimicrobial resistance (AMR) 1 . Standard single-component antimicrobial stewardship programmes (ASPs) often produce only temporary improvements and fail to drive long-term behavioural shifts in complex paediatric clinical environments 2 . Methods We conducted a retrospective quasi-experimental interrupted time series (ITS) analysis at a 1000-bed tertiary children’s hospital in Dongguan, China, spanning 48 months (January 2022–December 2025). The hospital was Dongguan Eighth People's Hospital (Dongguan Children's Hospital). The study was split into three phases: 12-month pre-intervention baseline (2022), 12-month ASP implementation (2023), and 24-month post-implementation follow-up (2024–2025). A five-pillar paediatric-targeted ASP was fully rolled out in January 2023, consisting of leadership governance, embedded electronic clinical guidelines, real-time collaborative prescription audit and feedback, institutional education and caregiver awareness and attitude change, and transparent departmental performance reporting. The primary endpoint was antibiotic use density (AUD), quantified as defined daily doses (DDD) per 100 patient-days. Segmented linear regression with Prais-Winsten transformation was used to account for residual autocorrelation; a two-sided p-value Results A total of 48 months of data were analysed. The mean monthly AUD decreased significantly from 43.15 ± 7.39 DDD/100 patient-days in 2022 to 28.83 ± 2.05 DDD/100 patient-days in 2025, representing a relative reduction of 33.2%. ITS analysis confirmed a significant immediate level change of -10.53 DDD/100 patient-days (95% CI: -15.2 to -5.86, P P = 0.018). Patient safety indicators remained stable, with length of stay (mean 6.7 days, P > 0.05) and 30-day mortality (0.9%, P > 0.05) showing no significant differences. Conclusions A coordinated, multi-modal paediatric ASP built on five integrated pillars was associated with large and sustained reductions in inpatient antibiotic consumption without compromising paediatric patient safety, while multidrug-resistant pathogen prevalence remained stable. This framework provides a potentially replicable operational approach to addressing systemic barriers to antimicrobial stewardship in paediatric hospitals.

items.title: Client Perspectives and Experiences with Service Availability and Readiness for Hypertension and Diabetes Care in Urban and Rural Public Health Facilities in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background The World Health Organization's global action plan for noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) emphasises that readiness of health facilities to manage hypertension and diabetes (H and D) must ultimately translate into a positive experience for the clients who use these services. Facility-level audits alone do not capture whether clients perceive care as accessible, timely, and effective. Objective This study assessed and compared the perspectives and experiences of clients receiving hypertension and diabetes care in selected urban and rural public health facilities in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria, as a client-centred complement to a parallel facility-readiness assessment. Materials and Methods A comparative cross-sectional design using a mixed-methods approach was employed. A semi-structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire was used to interview 220 consenting adult clients (110 urban, 110 rural) with hypertension and/or diabetes. Four focus group discussions (two urban, two rural) explored client expectations. Quantitative data were analysed in SPSS version 20 using chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression; qualitative data were analysed thematically. Results The mean age of clients was comparable between urban (41.7 ± 13.2 years) and rural (40.4 ± 14.5 years) areas (p = 0.502). Urban clients were significantly less likely to wait more than 30 minutes during their last two visits (odds ratio [OR] = 0.10; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.01–69; p = 0.022) and were more likely to receive all prescribed medications (OR = 2.95; 95% CI = 0.77–11.2; p = 0.111). Significantly more urban clients reported improvement in their condition with prescribed medication than rural clients. The reverse pattern was reported for some equipment- and provider-related items, with rural clients more often reporting that functional blood pressure equipment, available care providers, and a clean clinic environment were present. Qualitatively, urban clients more often reported satisfaction with drug availability and diagnostic testing, while rural clients' suggestions centred on improving drug supply, equipment, and staffing. Conclusion Client experiences broadly corroborated the facility-level finding of greater readiness in urban than rural primary health facilities, particularly regarding waiting time and medicine availability. The rural clients rated providers, cleanliness, and willingness to recommend the facility more favourably. Integrating client perspectives with facility audits provides a more complete and actionable picture of service readiness for hypertension and diabetes care.

items.title: Premarital Screening of Thalassemia in Punjab: A Policy Perspective
items.abstract: Abstract Thalassemia is one of the most prevalent inherited haemoglobin disorders worldwide, with a particularly high burden in low- and middle-income countries such as Pakistan. With a carrier rate of approximately 5–8% and thousands of affected births annually, β-thalassemia poses significant challenges. Premarital screening has been proposed as a preventive strategy; however, policy development and implementation remain limited in Punjab, Pakistan. This study aimed to explore the political, institutional, legal, and socio-cultural challenges associated with the formulation and implementation of a premarital thalassemia screening policy in Punjab, and to examine stakeholders’ perspectives regarding the proposed Thalassemia Prevention Act. A qualitative research design was employed using an interpretive approach. Purposive sampling was used to recruit key stakeholders involved in health legislation and policy formulation, including policymakers, legislators, bureaucrats, and health program officials. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews. Thematic analysis was applied to identify major themes and subthemes related to barriers in policy formulation and implementation. Findings revealed multiple interrelated barriers to premarital screening policy development. Key challenges included limited evidence-based policymaking, inadequate research organization and interpretation, insufficient bureaucratic engagement during early formulation stages, and lack of detailed legal enforcement mechanisms. Political will emerged as a critical enabling factor, although inconsistencies in leadership commitment delayed legislative progress. Socio-cultural factors, including high rates of consanguineous marriages and religious sensitivities surrounding antenatal diagnosis, further influenced policy feasibility. Economic analysis indicated that preventive screening could significantly reduce long-term treatment costs associated with thalassemia major. Participants emphasized the importance of public awareness campaigns, stakeholder collaboration, and integration of scientific research into legislative processes. The successful implementation of premarital thalassemia screening in Punjab requires sustained political commitment, institutional coordination, robust legal frameworks, and evidence-informed policymaking. A comprehensive and culturally sensitive policy approach could shift Pakistan’s response from reactive disease management to proactive genetic prevention, offering a sustainable model for other low- and middle-income settings.

items.title: Prevalence and antimicrobial resistance of Salmonella spp. in human, animal, and environmental reservoirs in Africa: A systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Salmonella is a leading cause of foodborne and enteric infections worldwide, with increasing antimicrobial resistance (AMR) threatening human and animal health. In Africa, fragmented surveillance systems limit understanding of Salmonella epidemiology. This review synthesized evidence on the prevalence, serovar distribution, AMR, and One Health transmission dynamics of Salmonella spp. across Africa. Methods: PubMed was searched following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Of 109 records identified, 64 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis and 21 studies reporting prevalence in human stool samples were included in a random-effects meta-analysis. Study quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger’s regression test. Results: Most studies were of high quality (57/64). Salmonella spp. were reported in human, animal, food, and environmental reservoirs, supporting circulation at the human–animal–environment interface. The most frequently reported serovars were S. Typhimurium, S. Enteritidis, and S. Kentucky. Antimicrobial susceptibility data revealed widespread resistance to β-lactams, tetracyclines, sulfonamides, aminoglycosides, and fluoroquinolones. Common resistance determinants included blaTEM, blaCTX-M, blaSHV, tet(A), tet(B), sul1, sul2, dfrA, aadA, and qnr . Multidrug-resistant phenotypes were frequently associated with plasmids and class 1 integrons. The pooled prevalence of human Salmonella infection was 6% (95% CI, 5–9%), with substantial heterogeneity (I²=89.7%). No significant publication bias was detected. Conclusions: Salmonellosis remains a major public health challenge in Africa. Shared serovars and resistance determinants across reservoirs highlight the need for integrated One Health surveillance, antimicrobial stewardship, and strengthened food safety systems.

items.title: Impact of Incarceration on Black Maternal Health: Descriptive Analysis of Care for Birthing People in the NYC Jail System
items.abstract: Abstract Background In the U.S., Black women are incarcerated at 1.6 times the rate of white women and experience pregnancy-related morbidity at twice the rate. Black birthing people experiencing incarceration are placed at the intersection of racial inequities, medical complexity, and structural barriers to care. However, information regarding the effect of incarceration on Black maternal health and data describing the health needs of incarcerated birthing people remain limited. This study characterized medical comorbidities and pregnancy outcomes among birthing people incarcerated in New York City and evaluated outcomes before and after a collaborative reproductive health intervention. Methods This retrospective observational study included pregnant people incarcerated at Rikers Island who received obstetric care at Elmhurst Hospital and delivered within the NYC public safety net system between July 2019 and July 2023. The intervention linked jail-based prenatal care with hospital obstetric telehealth consultations, specialty visits, and multidisciplinary coordination. Demographic and clinical characteristics and maternal and neonatal outcomes were compared before and after implementation. Results Among 44 patients, 45.5% identified as Black and 13.6% as white. Chronic medical conditions affected 77.3%, 86.4% had a documented psychiatric diagnosis, and 86.4% had a history of substance use. During pregnancy, 27.3% experienced hypertensive disorders and 9.1% had a sexually transmitted infection. Cesarean delivery decreased from 36.8% before to 12.0% after intervention implementation (p = 0.07). Among patients delivering at Elmhurst Hospital, Cesarean delivery decreased from 75.0% to 14.3% (p = 0.04). Maternal complications and neonatal outcomes did not significantly differ. Preterm birth affected 20.5% of the cohort. Conclusions This predominantly Black cohort of pregnant people experiencing incarceration had substantial medical and psychiatric comorbidity, as well as elevated rates of preterm birth. The collaborative reproductive health intervention was associated with reduced Cesarean delivery, suggesting that continuity between correctional and community obstetric care may improve maternal outcomes by mitigating care fragmentation. Larger studies in this patient population are needed to further evaluate the impact of incarceration on Black maternal and neonatal health, and to inform integrated models addressing behavioral health, substance use, and racial inequities in pregnancy.

items.title: Evaluating AI-Driven Chatbots for Acute Myocardial Infarction Public Health Advice
items.abstract: Abstract Objective To compare the safety, accuracy, empathy, information quality, and readability of four generative artificial intelligence chatbots answering public questions about acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Methods This paired cross-sectional benchmark evaluated 70 English-language questions, selected from 120 candidates across seven domains, using ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Doubao web interfaces on June 8–10, 2026. Three clinicians independently rated 280 responses. Binary safety classifications used majority voting; six other clinician-rated outcomes used arithmetic means. Safety was compared using Cochran's Q and exact McNemar tests; non-binary outcomes used Friedman and paired Wilcoxon tests with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Wilson and question-level bootstrap intervals summarized rates and effects. Results Thirty-four responses across 15 questions were classified as potentially unsafe. Unsafe-response rates were 12/70 (17.1%) for DeepSeek, 9/70 (12.9%) for Doubao, 7/70 (10.0%) for Gemini, and 6/70 (8.6%) for ChatGPT ( Q = 7.000; P = 0.072). No pairwise safety comparison was significant after adjustment; the ChatGPT–DeepSeek safe-rate difference was 8.6 percentage points (unadjusted bootstrap 95% CI , 1.4–17.1), with an adjusted exact P = 0.375. Accuracy and empathy differed across models (Kendall's W = 0.444 and 0.601, respectively). ChatGPT had the highest observed medians for accuracy (5.00) and empathy (4.33). Nevertheless, 27/34 unsafe responses had mean accuracy scores of at least 4. JAMA transparency scores were low across models. Mean Flesch-Kincaid grade levels ranged from 11.23 to 20.07. Illustrative safety concerns involved contradictory emergency-call timing, medication instructions, diagnostic overconfidence, and context-dependent omissions. Conclusions Favorable overall content ratings coexisted with clinically relevant safety concerns and substantial reading demands. These single-generation findings do not establish equivalent safety, reproducibility, patient comprehension, or clinical benefit; chatbot AMI advice requires clinical review and explicit emergency escalation.

items.title: Clinical Segregation of Joint Replacement Surgery Between Israel’s Public and Private Hospitals, 2020–2025: A National Analysis of Case- Mix and Its Policy Implications
items.abstract: Abstract Background Israel has a mixed public–private hospital system, and elective joint replacement is increasingly performed in private hospitals. This study describes national trends in procedure volume and Ministry-classified complexity by hospital sector from 2020 to 2025. Methods We analyzed aggregate national data published by the Israeli Ministry of Health for 2020–2025 for total knee replacement (TKR), total hip replacement (THR), and partial hip replacement (PHR). Counts and proportions were summarized descriptively by procedure, sector, year, and the Ministry’s simple/complex classification. No patient-level adjustment or inferential testing was performed. Results National procedure volume increased from 10,764 in 2020 to 15,848 in 2025 (47.2%). Private-hospital volume increased by 93.3%, compared with 24.5% in public hospitals; the private share rose from 33.1% to 43.4%. In 2025, 24.8% of procedures in public hospitals and 1.90% in private hospitals were classified as complex. The difference varied by procedure type and was particularly influenced by partial hip replacements: all complex partial hip replacements reported during the study period were performed in public hospitals. The public-sector complex caseload increased from 1,614 to 2,227 procedures. Conclusions The aggregate data show a substantial and persistent difference in the distribution of Ministry-classified complexity between hospital sectors. They do not establish whether the difference reflects provider selection, patient choice, referral practices, differences in institutional services, or a combination of these factors. The possible implications for reimbursement and surgical training require direct study using linked patient-level, cost, tariff, and training data.

items.title: Human Vaccines Cold Supply Chain Practices In Public Health Facilities At Kilimanjaro Region Tanzania
items.abstract: Abstract Background Vaccines are important products in the prevention of illnesses, but failure to ensure the requirements in the vaccine cold supply chain during storage, transportation, and distribution might result in an increased risk of vaccine-preventable diseases. Therefore, this study was conducted to assess the vaccine cold supply chain practices in public health facilities in Kilimanjaro region. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional design using a quantitative approach was conducted in 32 health facilities in the Kilimanjaro region, Tanzania. A structured questionnaire was used to collect data. The collected data was cleaned, coded and analyzed by using STATA 18. Results There were 32 public health facilities and majority located in rural areas (78.1%). Nurses predominantly operated the cold vaccine chain (93.8%). Compliance to storage protocols was high, notably in maintaining cleanliness (96.9%) and ensuring dry floors (100%). However, significant gaps were observed. Compliance to the vaccine cold chain during distribution was high across all facilities in using special containers and loading ice packs. Disparities were observed in the use of functional car/motorbike in case of refrigerator failure and utilization of transportation resources. At least (90.6%) health facilities complied with vaccine cold supply chain requirements. Conclusion The study highlights high compliance with vaccine cold supply chain practices in Kilimanjaro's public health facilities, particularly in cleanliness and temperature maintenance. However, while healthcare workers demonstrated good knowledge, gaps remain that indicate opportunities for improvement in various vaccine handling aspects.

items.title: AI-Driven Deep Learning Framework for Robust Multiclass Dementia Classification Using EEG Data
items.abstract: Abstract Dementia is a growing public health concern worldwide. Accurately differentiating among its various forms can facilitate earlier clinical assessment and support more effective management strategies. Electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a promising tool for dementia assessment because it is noninvasive, inexpensive, portable, easy to administer, and capable of capturing brain activity with high temporal resolution. However, existing EEG-based approaches often rely on manually engineered features, evaluate only a limited number of classification tasks, or employ models with limited generalisability across multiple diagnostic classes. This study proposes a deep learning framework to classify dementia-related conditions from resting-state EEG. The framework integrates systematic signal preprocessing, 5-second multichannel EEG segmentation, and a two-dimensional convolutional neural network to learn hierarchical spatiotemporal representations and distinguish different forms of dementia patients from healthy controls. The proposed framework was evaluated via a publicly available dataset comprising 88 participants: 36 with Alzheimer’s disease (AD), 23 with frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and 29 healthy controls (HC). Performance was assessed using 10-fold cross-validation across one multiclass task (AD vs FTD vs HC) and three binary tasks (AD vs HC, FTD vs HC, and AD+FTD vs HC). The framework achieved an average multiclass accuracy of 98.78% and binary accuracies of 99.21%, 99.40%, and 99.15%, together with consistently high sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1 scores. These findings demonstrate the potential of combining automated EEG preprocessing with convolutional neural network (CNN) based representation learning to support accurate dementia classification and the development of accessible, cost-effective clinical decision-support tools.

items.title: The Role of Nurses in Addressing Climate-Driven Mental Health Challenges: A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Climate change is one of the most critical public health challenge. Exposure to extreme weather events can lead to anxiety, depression, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), eco-anxiety, ecological grief, and suicidal ideation. Nurses as frontline community-based professionals, play a vital role in addressing climate-driven mental health impacts. Aim/Objectives: Aims to explore the roles and challenges of nurses in addressing mental health impacts associated with climate change. The specific objectives are: (1)to identify the climate driven mental health challenges (2) to examine nursing interventions for supporting affected individuals, and (3) to identify barriers influencing nurses’ ability to respond effectively. Methods: The literature search was conducted using PubMed, Google Scholar, CINAHL, PsycINFO and Scopus. A purposive sampling technique was applied. Inclusion criteria were: (i) empirical studies, reviews, commentaries that reported mental health related to climate events (ii) explicit description of nurses’ roles, interventions. The quality of the included studies was assessed by considering study design, clarity of objectives, and relevance to the review question. After title and abstract screening, 10 were excluded due to irrelevance. A final total of 08 articles was included based on full-text review. Findings: Nurses play a central role in screening, providing psychoeducation, engaging with the community, building resilience, and advocating for patients. Barriers to effective nursing responses included limited climate- and mental‑health‑specific content in nursing curricula, scarce resources and staffing during climate emergencies, lack of standardized protocols and emotional burden and burnout among nurses. Conclusions and Recommendations: Nurses are pivotal in mitigating climate‑driven mental health challenges through early identification, holistic care, community engagement, and advocacy. Future research should focus on evaluating specific nurse-led interventions for eco-anxiety, ecological grief, and disaster‑related distress.

items.title: Policy as a Route to Food System Transformation: A Scoping Review of Evidence from Europe and the United Kingdom
items.abstract: Background: Policy interventions can contribute to food systems transformations which improve population health, environmental sustainability, and social equity. However, there is a lack of knowledge around how such policies are designed, implemented, and governed. This scoping review forms part of a wider project examining research, practice and funding landscapes for sustainable food systems in Europe, Switzerland and the United Kingdom (UK). Objectives To map and synthesise recent peer-reviewed evidence on policy as a route to food system transformation, focusing on policy instruments, governance approaches, implementation challenges and evidence gaps. Eligibility criteria Eligible sources were English-language, peer-reviewed empirical studies (quantitative, qualitative or mixed-methods) published from January 2022 to June 2025 and addressing food system transformation in relation to climate change mitigation and human health in Europe, EEA, Switzerland and the UK. Sources of evidence We searched Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed and EBSCOhost databases, supplemented by citation snowballing using Inciteful.xyz. Charting methods Data were extracted through a structured, iterative charting process combining artificial intelligence-assisted thematic coding in Atlas.TI with human verification. Themes were mapped to predefined domains covering policy instruments, governance, implementation, and outcomes. Results We identified 129 papers that examined diverse policy instruments, including regulatory frameworks, fiscal measures, public procurement policies and agricultural subsidies. Studies frequently position policy as essential for large-scale change, but also highlight persistent challenges: fragmented governance, political constraints and limited policy coherence. Evidence is stronger on what policy changes are needed than on how to implement and sustain them. Key gaps include limited evaluation of policy effectiveness, insufficient attention to equity and governance processes, and few integrated analyses of combined policy instruments. Conclusions Policy remains a critical but complex route to food system transformation. Future research should prioritise applied policy analysis, including evaluation, political economy and implementation studies, while strengthening understanding of policy coherence, multi-level governance and evidence translation into practice.

items.title: Examining the relationship between objective and patient-reported physical function in adults with cancer.
items.abstract: Background Cancer and its therapies negatively impact physical function (PF), which is commonly captured using patient-reported PF measures. Though important, patient-report PF tools may fail to capture important aspects of objectively measured PF, limiting their ability to provide a comprehensive assessment of PF. Objective This study aimed to compare patient-reported (PROMIS-Physical Function Computer Adaptive Test, PROMIS PF) and objective (Bellarmine Norton Assessment Tool, BNAT) measures of PF in adults with a history of cancer. Methods This cross-sectional study included a referred and volunteer sample of 94 adults with a history of cancer (91.5% women, 60.1 ± 10.8 years) who completed the BNAT and the PROMIS PF. The BNAT includes the 2-minute step test (MST), 30-second sit-to-stand (STS), 30-second arm curl, and timed-up-and-go (TUG), with total scores calculated from the sum of subscale scores. Pearson's correlations, variance (r2), and descriptive statistics were used to evaluate the relationships between BNAT and PROMIS scores. Results Weak correlations were observed between PROMIS PF total scores and BNAT total scores (r = 0.313, p = 0.002) and between the PROMIS PF and BNAT raw scores, including STS (r = 0.362, p = 0.001), arm curl (r = 0.320, p = 0.002), and TUG (r = -0.319, p = 0.002). Variance explained ranged from 3.3%-13.1%, suggesting limited overlap between subjective and objective measures. Conclusion Our findings suggest that patient-reported and performance-based assessments of PF are generally weakly associated in adults with a history of cancer. These findings highlight the potential value of incorporating both approaches to provide a more comprehensive understanding of PF in clinical and research settings. items.title: Rethinking functional mobility within contemporary physical activity guidelines: a commentary.
items.abstract: Regular physical activity promotes health, prevents chronic disease, and supports healthy aging, yet current physical activity recommendations primarily emphasize movement behavior rather than the capacities that enable safe and effective participation. In this Commentary, we propose functional mobility as a proposed movement-capacity construct that complements the behavioral focus of physical activity by integrating joint mobility, muscular strength and power, balance and postural control, coordination, motor control, cardiorespiratory endurance, and movement adaptability. We distinguish functional mobility from physical activity, physical fitness, physical function, functional performance, and intrinsic capacity while recognizing their reciprocal relationships. Building on the World Health Organization's International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health and Healthy Ageing frameworks, we present a noncausal, heuristic model in which functional mobility connects movement behavior with functional performance and healthy aging. We discuss implications for clinical practice, rehabilitation, and public health without proposing that this framework replace current physical activity recommendations. Research priorities include reaching consensus on the construct's definition, developing multidimensional assessment approaches, validating the construct across diverse populations, and evaluating interventions. Considering both how much individuals move and their capacity to meet everyday movement demands may broaden the study of movement health and inform efforts to preserve participation, independence, and quality of life across the lifespan.

items.title: Hand and finger symptoms in older adults: a clinical audit of detection and management gaps in Danish general practice.
items.abstract: Background Hand osteoarthritis (OA) is common among older adults. Recommendations support a combination of non-pharmacological and pharmacological treatments. However, real-world data on prevalence and treatment patterns in primary care are lacking. Aim To investigate the prevalence and characteristics of hand and finger pain/swelling among elderly patients presenting to general practice, and to audit the quality and comprehensiveness of their clinical management against evidence-based recommendations. Design and setting We conducted a four-week clinical audit of all consecutive patients ≥70 years of age attending general practices in Denmark with recording of current symptoms and signs characteristic of hand OA as well as prior related diagnostic investigations and treatments. Results The study included 348 patients from 16 general practices, with 42% ( n = 147) experiencing hand/or finger pain/swelling. Pain during usage (64%, n = 95) and stiffness (39%, n = 57) were the most common symptoms. Clinical findings suggestive of hand OA were present in 61% ( n = 90) of symptomatic patients, with 41% ( n = 60) reporting reduced activities of daily living. Only 50% ( n = 73) of symptomatic patients had previously consulted their GP about these symptoms, and referral rates to specialists and allied health professionals were low. Management strategies were limited, with 33% ( n = 49) using analgesics and 7.5% ( n = 11) using assistive devices. Conclusion Hand and finger symptoms are prevalent among older adults in general practice, with significant functional impact. Management patterns displayed low referral rates to allied healthcare professionals and limited use of non-pharmacological interventions. Further research is needed to understand patient preferences and barriers to accessing recommended care.

items.title: Impacts of COVID-19 on Modifiable Lifestyle Behaviors and Associations With Mental Well-Being Among Medical Students and Health Care Workers in Vietnam: Cross-Sectional Online Survey.
items.abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted daily life and mental health globally; yet, little is known about how multiple modifiable lifestyle behaviors shape psychological outcomes among young health-affiliated populations in low- and middle-income settings such as Vietnam. Objective This study aimed to examine changes in modifiable lifestyle behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic and their associations with depression, anxiety, and perceived stress among medical students and health care workers in Vietnam, most of whom were young people aged 16 to 20 years. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted from September to November 2021 among 817 medical students and health care workers recruited through medical universities and health care facilities across Vietnam using snowball sampling. The sample was predominantly young, with 72.5% (591/815) aged 16 to 20 years, and 68.8% (558/811) were female individuals. This period captured the late Delta-driven fourth wave and Vietnam's transition from heterogeneous local restrictions to "safe and flexible adaptation," when daily routines, mobility, online learning/work, and mental well-being remained disrupted. The questionnaire assessed demographics, 14 lifestyle behaviors grouped into positive, diet/media-related, substance use, and violence-related domains, alongside validated Vietnamese-language measures of depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 [PHQ-9]), anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 [GAD-7]), and stress (Perceived Stress Scale-4 [PSS-4]). Separate multivariable Tobit regression models were applied to account for bounded-scale outcomes with potential floor effects. Results are reported as unstandardized coefficients with 95% CIs. Results High stress was common (n=522, 63.9%; mean PSS-4 6.9, SD 2.2). Mean PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores were 5.2 (SD 4.7) and 3.1 (SD 3.6), respectively, and participants with higher stress had higher PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores than those with lower stress (both P Conclusions Lifestyle behaviors were associated with mental well-being under pandemic conditions among a predominantly young, health-affiliated sample in Vietnam. Because participants were recruited through an online snowball-sampling approach and were largely affiliated with medical universities or health care facilities, the findings should be interpreted as context-specific evidence rather than as estimates for the general Vietnamese adult population. Public health responses, particularly in educational and health-related settings, should incorporate behavior-focused strategies, promoting healthy routines, balanced diets, constructive digital use, and nonviolent coping to strengthen resilience in future crises.

items.title: A Structured Exercise Intervention for Individuals With Psychotic Disorders Treated With Long-Acting Injectable Antipsychotics: Protocol for a Nonrandomized Controlled Study.
items.abstract: Background Individuals with psychotic disorders have high rates of physical comorbidity and considerably reduced quality of life, often aggravated by the adverse metabolic effects associated with injectable antipsychotic treatment. Physical exercise has been identified as a promising strategy for improving physical and mental health in this population. This article describes the protocol for a structured multimodal physical exercise program designed to be implemented within outpatient psychiatric services for individuals treated with long-acting injectable (LAI) antipsychotics. Objective This study aims to evaluate the impact of a structured exercise program on psychotic symptomatology in individuals with psychotic disorders receiving LAI antipsychotics. Secondary objectives include assessing the effects of the intervention on metabolic outcomes, particularly body composition and cardiometabolic risk factors. Exploratory analyses will be performed to investigate potential associations between exercise participation and longitudinal changes in antipsychotic treatment patterns, as well as variations in circulating biomarkers such as brain-derived neurotrophic factor, dopamine, and serotonin. Methods This is a prospective, controlled, longitudinal study developed in accordance with SPIRIT (Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials) recommendations. The study will recruit a clinical population of 151 eligible participants diagnosed with psychotic disorders (mean age 46.40, SD 13.60 years) receiving LAI antipsychotics. This protocol describes the implementation and evaluation of a 24-week supervised multimodal exercise program integrated into routine psychiatric outpatient care. Participants receiving LAI antipsychotics will be allocated to either the exercise program or a treatment-as-usual control group. The intervention will include supervised circuit-based sessions combining aerobic, resistance, mobility, and balance exercises, performed twice weekly, with a progressive training load and an additional autonomous walking component introduced in the second phase of the program. Clinical, functional, psychological, and cardiometabolic outcomes will be assessed at baseline (preintervention), after 12 weeks, after 24 weeks, and at an 8-week follow-up. The study has obtained ethical approval from the Ethics Committee of the Local Health Unit of Trás-os-Montes e Alto Douro, and written informed consent will be obtained from all participants. Results The study was funded in January 2026. Recruitment and data collection began on January 1, 2026, and are expected to be completed by November 30, 2026. As of manuscript submission (May 2026), 25 participants had been recruited. Data analysis is projected for December 2026, with findings expected to be published in spring 2027. Conclusions Structured exercise interventions integrated into routine psychiatric care may represent an important strategy to improve the physical health, functional capacity, and overall well-being of individuals with psychotic disorders treated with LAI antipsychotics.

items.title: Comparative cardiovascular safety of febuxostat, allopurinol, and benzbromarone in Taiwanese patients with gout: a retrospective time-varying exposure analysis.
items.abstract: Background The comparative cardiovascular safety of urate-lowering therapies in patients with gout remains controversial. Our previous network meta-analysis suggested a directionally lower cardiovascular risk with benzbromarone than with febuxostat or allopurinol, but direct head-to-head evidence between benzbromarone and febuxostat was limited. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the National Taiwan University Hospital integrated Medical Database. Adults with gout treated with febuxostat, allopurinol, or benzbromarone between July 31, 2016 and August 31, 2023 were included. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of myocardial infarction and stroke. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular death. Cox proportional hazards models with time-varying exposure were used to evaluate the time to first occurrence of events. Results The cohort comprised 3,240 patients, with a median follow-up duration of 4.41 years; 151 patients experienced MACE. All-cause mortality rates per 1,000 person-years were 17.99 overall and 11.31, 25.85, and 9.72 in the benzbromarone, febuxostat, and allopurinol fixed-exposure groups, respectively. In fully adjusted time-varying model using benzbromarone as the reference, no statistically significant difference in MACE was detected for allopurinol (HR 1.63, 95% CI 0.85-3.13) or febuxostat (HR 1.17, 95% CI 0.81-1.69). Febuxostat was associated with higher all-cause mortality than benzbromarone (HR 1.52, 95% CI 1.13-2.04), and allopurinol was associated with higher stroke risk than benzbromarone (HR 2.02, 95% CI 1.04-3.92). Conclusion No statistically significant difference was observed in MACE. However, relative to benzbromarone, febuxostat and allopurinol were associated with higher all-cause mortality and higher stroke risk, respectively.

items.title: Seasonal water scarcity and household storage practices as determinants of microbial contamination in stored drinking water in remote karst highlands of northern Vietnam.
items.abstract: Safe drinking water is essential for public health; however, seasonal water scarcity can undermine safe household water access and management. This study examined associations between seasonal water scarcity, household storage practices, and total coliform contamination in stored drinking water in the Dong Van Karst Plateau, northern Vietnam. Data from 821 households, including 772 surveyed in both seasons, were analysed using mixed-effects logistic regression and interaction tests. Water-use patterns differed between seasons: rainwater was most common in the rainy season (37.8%), whereas multisource use predominated in the dry season (62.5%). Total coliform contamination was high in both seasons and higher in the dry season (84.1% vs. 78.3%). Uncovered storage tanks (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 5.80; 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.84-11.88), dipping water from storage containers (AOR 4.91; 95% CI 2.51-9.63), storage for more than 45 days (AOR 6.49; 95% CI 2.12-19.88), and multisource use (AOR 3.94; 95% CI 1.67-9.29) were associated with higher odds of contamination. The association with dipping was stronger in the rainy season. Climate-driven water scarcity and unsafe storage behaviors jointly shape microbial contamination risk. Improving storage practices and ensuring reliable water supply systems are essential to reduce contamination in climate-vulnerable mountainous regions.
