items.title: Attempted Suicide Short Intervention Program: Qualitative Implementation Results from a Type 1 Hybrid Effectiveness-Implementation Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Objective Suicide is a public health crisis. One intervention with evidence is the Attempted Suicide Short Intervention Program (ASSIP). ASSIP is a three-session intervention with caring letters delivered alongside usual care with a goal of reducing the risk of suicidal behavior. Within a hybrid type 1 effectiveness-implementation randomized controlled trial (RCT), we conducted a qualitative implementation-focused process evaluation. Method We conducted semi-structured qualitative interviews with 19 participants including clinicians and administrators ( n = 8) at ASSIP trial sites, ASSIP naïve clinicians and administrators ( n = 8) at non-trial sites, and staff who assisted with recruitment ( n = 3). We sampled all clinicians, administrators, and staff who were involved with trial delivery. We sampled a similar number of naïve clinicians and administrators to those who delivered the intervention. Results ASSIP naïve participants expressed skepticism about the effectiveness of a three session intervention, concerns about the time allotted for psychotherapy in community settings, and concerns about video security and storage. Clinician and administrator participants from trial sites reported leadership support, technological infrastructure, and protected time were important in ensuring their ability to deliver the intervention. ASSIP naïve participants expressed positive opinions and thought ASSIP could be beneficial to their patients. Conclusions Results point to several implementation strategies to implementation ASSIP in mental health clinics. Lessons learned from the hybrid type 1 effectiveness-implementation RCT may inform mental health clinics in implementing ASSIP as part of routine care.

items.title: Visual function and circadian rest-activity rhythms in US older adults: The National Health and Aging Trends Study.
items.abstract: Study objectives To evaluate associations of visual function with accelerometer-derived rest-activity rhythm (RAR) metrics and 24-hour continuous activity patterns among older adults. Methods We analyzed data from 728 U.S. Medicare beneficiaries (weighted mean age 79.1±6.0 years, 78% White, 56% female) who completed objective vision assessments and provided ≥ 3 days of accelerometer data in NHATS Round 11 (2021). Visual functions included distance acuity, near acuity, and contrast sensitivity. Wrist-worn accelerometer data were used to derive parametric RAR metrics (amplitude, mesor, acrophase, alpha, beta, and percent rhythm) and nonparametric RAR metrics (relative amplitude, intradaily variability [IV], interdaily stability [IS]). Associations were examined using weighted linear regression and function-on-scalar regression (FOSR). Results Poorer visual function, regardless of type, was associated with lower amplitude (rhythm strength, both parametric and non-parametric metrics) and lower percent rhythm (rhythmicity), but not with mesor (average activity level), acrophase (peak activity timing), or alpha (peak-trough width). Distance acuity showed a statistically significant nonlinear association with IS. We did not observe any statistically significant associations for beta and IV after type 1 error correction. FOSR showed lower daytime activity and higher nighttime activity during typical sleep hours among those with vision impairment, with simultaneous significance limited to a small portion of the day. Findings were robust across sensitivity analyses. Conclusions Worse visual function was associated with weaker and less robust circadian RARs in a representative sample of older adults. Longitudinal and mechanistic studies are warranted to understand the intertwined relationships between visual function and circadian health.

items.title: Screen Time: Adherence to Recommendations, Daily Patterns and Health in Swedish Preschoolers.
items.abstract: Aim To describe screen time outside preschool and adherence to the 60-minute daily recommendation across the week among Swedish preschool children, and to examine secondary associations with socioeconomic and health indicators. Methods This citywide observational study included 2624 children aged 3-5 years from 124 public preschools in Stockholm. Parents completed repeated 24-hour screen-time diaries in 2020-2021, contributing 27 401 daily reports. Mixed-effects models compared weekdays with weekends and assessed socioeconomic and health associations. Results Mean reported screen time outside preschool was 61.5 minutes per day, and 53.7% met the recommendation. Reported screen time was 19.9 minutes per day higher on weekends than weekdays, while adherence was 42.8% and 60.7%, respectively. Adherence declined markedly on Friday. Socioeconomic differences were inconclusive. Exceeding 60 minutes per day was associated with shorter sleep, greater behavioural difficulties and lower adherence to the physical activity recommendation. Associations with poor sleep quality or grip strength were inconclusive. Conclusion Only around half of preschool children met the screen-time recommendation. The pronounced Friday and weekend decline suggests that family-focused strategies should complement preschool policy; health associations were modest and observational.

items.title: Can the pediatric clinical eye be taught? The role of digital tools in medical education.
items.abstract: Recognizing that a child is seriously unwell before a full examination is completed remains one of the most valued yet least explicitly taught competencies in pediatrics. In practice, experienced clinicians often form an early judgment from a child's appearance, breathing, movement, interaction, muscle tone, and the overall tempo of illness. Yet traditional teaching tends to compress these dynamic observations into brief written labels, while student exposure to informative cases remains uneven and largely dependent on chance. This editorial argues that the pediatric clinical eye is teachable and that digital educational tools may help make this tacit expertise more explicit, structured, and accessible to learners earlier in training. Recent literature supports the educational value of video-based learning, simulation-based training, and digital practice environments in health professions education. Against this background, this paper presents a digital educational application developed as part of a doctoral implementation project as an illustrative educational initiative rather than a completed diagnostic tool. The project centers on a structured audiovisual repository of real pediatric cases linked to clinical context and follow-up, which can be used to support repeated observation, feedback, and clinical reasoning. Digital tools are not proposed as a replacement for pediatric judgment. Their purpose is narrower: to help learners recognize clinically important cues and refine their judgments through repeated feedback. With appropriate governance and close integration with bedside teaching, such tools may help make expert observation more explicit and support the development of better-calibrated clinical reasoning.

items.title: Visual communication in medicine: a drawing workshop for medical students.
items.abstract: Problem Visuals enhance patient comprehension and attention, making them a valuable component of patient-centered care. Drawing has been explored as a useful strategy for explaining medical concepts, although formal instruction remains uncommon in medical education. Prior interventions have been limited to small elective courses with potential selection bias. Approach To address the training gap, the authors designed and incorporated a visual communication workshop into the Medical College of Georgia pre-clerkship curriculum in March of 2025 and explored its feasibility in an already dense medical curriculum. The workshop targeted students of all artistic backgrounds and appropriately addressed students' lack of confidence by emphasizing that drawing for a patient is about communicating information to improve patient care, not about talent. Various drawing techniques were taught, such as simplifying with basic shapes and using arrows, symbols, and color, featuring instructor demonstrations, hands-on practice, and role-playing exercises. Furthermore, students applied these skills during a standardized patient encounter (SPE) five weeks later in May of 2025 for additional practice. Outcomes The workshop engaged 207 students and was successfully integrated into the pre-clerkship curriculum, demonstrating feasibility at scale and for students of varied artistic background. Students applied techniques into role-playing exercises in a variety of ways. Drawing was successfully implemented in an SPE, with students in groups of 3-5 per standardized patient. Students readily incorporated drawing into the encounter to communicate the case pathology and procedure, using drawing techniques to differing degrees. According to informal discussion, standardized patients perceived the drawings as helpful for understanding, suggesting potential value for real world application. Next steps The workshop's brief and concise format, along with its applicability for non-artists, supports replication at other institutions. Future evaluation should include objective and longitudinal assessment of student outcomes. Additional research is needed to explore the impact on patient understanding and health outcomes.

items.title: Carryover of Aflatoxin From Dairy Feed to Milk: A Systematic Review (1 January 2004-31 December 2024).
items.abstract: Aflatoxins (AFs), toxic metabolites produced by Aspergillus species, are frequent contaminants of dairy cattle feed regularly transferred into milk and dairy products. Their presence poses major public health risks, including liver cancer and growth impairment, among others. Understanding the extent of carryover from feed to milk is critical for food safety and regulatory control. A systematic review was conducted to synthesise evidence on aflatoxin carryover in dairy systems over the past two decades. Literature searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase. Studies investigating aflatoxin levels in dairy feed and milk, as well as carryover rates, were included. Data extraction focused on contamination levels, feed treatment efficiency, aflatoxins carryover rates, and mitigation measures. Twenty-seven eligible studies were identified. AFB 1 concentrations in dairy feed ranged from undetectable to 598 µg/kg. In milk, AFM 1 levels reached up to 22.2 µg/kg, with reported carryover rates up to 15%. The findings highlight variability in contamination across regions and production systems. This review underscores the continuing risk of aflatoxin in dairy products, identifies knowledge gaps and emerging threats, and emphasises the need for improved interventions to safeguard food safety and public health.

items.title: Middle Ear Rhabdomyosarcoma: An Updated Survival Analysis From the Children's Oncology Group.
items.abstract: Background Middle ear rhabdomyosarcoma (ME-RMS) is often locally advanced at diagnosis with extension occurring through the tympanic membrane, intracranially, or laterally in front of or under the ear but rarely metastasizes distantly. We describe the presentation and outcomes of patients with ME-RMS treated on recent Children's Oncology Group (COG) clinical trials. Procedure Patients with ME-RMS enrolled on COG studies for newly diagnosed RMS from 1997 to 2022 were included. Demographic information, tumor characteristics, and survival information were analyzed using descriptive and survival statistics. Results Fifty-one patients with ME-RMS were identified. The majority (68.6%) were male and under 10 years old (98%). Tumor histology was most commonly embryonal (47.1%) or botryoid (37.3%). The majority (76.5%) had tumors ≤5 cm. Lymph node involvement was identified in 27.5%. Most tumors were classified as COG Stage 2 (54.9%) or 3 (39.2%), with the vast majority Intergroup Rhabdomyosarcoma Study (IRS) Group III (92.2%). Most (96.1%) received radiation therapy for local control. The 4-year event-free survival (EFS) was 72.6% (95% CI 59.8-85.3) and overall survival (OS) 76.2% (95% CI 63.8-88.7) for the entire cohort. There was no difference in EFS or OS related to tumor size, COG stage, or clinical group. Patients treated on study D9803 had a numerically higher, but not statistically significant 4-year EFS (81.5%, 95% CI 66.8-96.1) and OS (85.2%, 95% CI 71.5-98.9) compared with ARST0531 and ARST1431, which had a combined 4-year EFS (60.9%, 95% CI 37.3-84.5) and OS (64.5%, 95% CI 40.6-88.3). Conclusions ME-RMS is a rare, locally aggressive tumor that predominantly affects young children. Outcomes remain suboptimal without demonstrated improvement over the 25-year period of this study. Although survival did not significantly differ across treatment protocols, the observed numerically lower survival with reduced cyclophosphamide exposure on more recent trials supports further evaluation of treatment intensity in this population.

items.title: Systemic therapies and cardiovascular events in older adults with psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis.
items.abstract: Background Psoriatic disease is associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Shared inflammatory pathways may allow systemic therapies to influence cardiovascular outcomes; however, evidence in older adults remains limited. Objectives To estimate the association between systemic therapy classes and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in older adults with psoriatic disease. Methods We conducted a population-based cohort study using linked administrative health data from Ontario, Canada. We identified adults aged ≥66 years with psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis who newly initiated systemic therapy between April 2007-March 2022. Time-varying exposure classes were methotrexate, other older medications, anti-TNF, anti-IL17, anti-IL12 or 23 biologics and tofacitinib. MACE, the primary outcome, included coronary heart disease, cerebrovascular events, heart failure and peripheral arterial disease. Using Andersen-Gill recurrent-event models, we estimated adjusted rate ratios, comparing current use of each medication class with non-use of that class. Results Among 8967 older adults, 51.3% were female and the median age at treatment initiation was 71 years (interquartile range [IQR], 68-76). Over a median follow-up of 5.3 years (IQR, 2.8-8.5), participants contributed 53,378 person-years, during which 2942 recurrent MACE occurred. In fully adjusted analyses, compared with the respective medication class non-use, methotrexate use was significantly associated with lower MACE rates (rate ratio [RR], 0.81; 95% CI, 0.71-0.92), as was anti-TNF biologic use (RR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.62-0.98). Estimates for anti-IL12 or 23 (RR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.68-1.08) and anti-IL17 biologics (RR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.57-1.06) were directionally consistent with anti-TNF biologics but imprecise, reflecting limited power. Other older systemic medications (RR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.87-1.19) and tofacitinib (RR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.28-1.68) showed no clear evidence of association. Conclusions In older adults with psoriatic disease, methotrexate and anti-TNF biologics were associated with lower MACE rates. Estimates for newer biologics were directionally consistent but imprecise, supporting further longitudinal cardiovascular safety evaluation in this high-risk population.

items.title: Syphilis: Epidemiology, Presentation, Treatment, and Key Considerations for Nurses.
items.abstract: Abstract Syphilis has resurged dramatically in the United States, posing a growing public health threat. Reported cases reached 209,253 in 2023, the highest annual total in more than 70 years. Of particular concern is the sharp rise in congenital syphilis with 3,882 infants affected in 2023, a 10-fold increase from a decade earlier. These trends are driven by barriers to timely testing and treatment, gaps in adequate prenatal care, and structural inequities that disproportionately place the syphilis burden on marginalized communities. Nurses play a central role in screening, patient education, treatment support, and addressing systemic barriers, making their involvement essential in reversing the current trajectory. This article reviews syphilis epidemiology, symptoms, diagnostic interpretation, treatment administration, and monitoring considerations for nursing care.

items.title: Development and validation of an instrument for auditing the food environment in online grocery retail in Brazil: AUDITNOVA-e.
items.abstract: Objective To develop, validate and assess the reliability of an instrument for auditing advertising, availability, price, variety and nutritional labelling in Brazilian online supermarkets. Design Methodological study. Setting This methodological study involved the development, content validation and reliability analysis of AUDITNOVA-e, an audit tool based on AUDITNOVA aimed at assessing the food environment in Brazilian online supermarkets, focusing exclusively on web platforms (websites). Content validation was conducted by ten experts to calculate the content validity index (CVI). Inter-rater and test-retest reliability were evaluated using the percentage of agreement and Gwet's AC1 coefficients. Pearson's correlation coefficient was used to assess the degree of linear correlation between quantitative variables of price and variety. Participants Ten experts with experience in food environment research participated in the content validation stage. Results The overall CVI was 0·83. Inter-rater and test-retest reliability showed, for most variables, a percentage of agreement equal to or greater than 80 %, with Gwet's AC1 coefficients indicating substantial to almost perfect agreement. Variables related to availability, nutritional labelling and price type demonstrated high reliability. Price and brand variety indicators exhibited strong and significant positive linear correlations between measurements obtained by researchers and across visits. Conclusion AUDITNOVA-e proved to be a reliable tool for monitoring the online grocery retail environment in Brazil, helping fill a gap in the availability of valid measures for assessment.

items.title: General practitioners' perspectives on collaboration with community health workers and proactive outreach to vulnerable people - a focus group study.
items.abstract: Background Health inequities are persistent and structural, particularly affecting people in vulnerable contexts who face barriers to healthcare. General practice, as the first point of contact, can help address these inequities through proactive outreach to those most in need. Objective This study explored Flemish general practitioners' (GPs) perspectives on employing community health workers (CHWs) for proactive outreach to people in vulnerable contexts who underuse healthcare services. It aimed to inform how outreach practices and collaboration with CHWs might be structurally embedded within general practice. Methods Twenty-two Flemish GPs participated in four qualitative focus groups. Audio recordings were transcribed and analysed inductively using thematic analysis with MAXQDA software. Results GPs found vulnerability hard to define, recognising it mainly through patterns of healthcare underuse, care disengagement, and unmet needs rather than social categories, making it difficult to identify who should be the focus of CHW outreach. This ambiguity generated uncertainty about professional responsibilities. Combined with high workload and limited structural support, this culminated in feelings of powerlessness. CHWs were perceived as valuable intermediaries for equity-oriented outreach, bridging gaps between general practice and people who underuse healthcare services. However, their role and positioning remained unclear, highlighting the need for careful integration into general practice structures. Conclusion GPs acknowledged the importance of outreach and support roles that CHWs could take on. However, their employment was not seen as a neutral fix. Clear frameworks aligning professional responsibility, organisational support, policy, and ethical reflection are needed to address health inequities within universal general practice systems.

items.title: Differential ratiometric fluorescence sensing enabled by molecularly imprinted dual-emission carbon dots for ultrasensitive bisphenol A determination.
items.abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA), a well-known endocrine disruptor, has attracted significant public concern due to its potential health risks. In this work, a molecularly imprinted ratiometric fluorescence sensor (bCDs&oCDs@SiO 2 @MIPs) based on blue emission carbon dots (bCDs) and orange-emissive carbon dots encapsulated in silica (oCDs@SiO 2 ) was constructed for the detection of BPA. The composite was fabricated by synthesizing CDs through a one-pot hydrothermal method, followed by the formation of a molecularly imprinted shell on the particle surface via a sol-gel process. The imprinted layer exhibits specific recognition of BPA, enhancing the selectivity of the sensor. The sensor mechanism relies on the decrease in fluorescence intensity at 430 nm of bCDs with increasing BPA concentration, while the fluorescence intensity at 570 nm of oCDs@SiO 2 remains constant, serving as a reference signal. The ratio ( I 430 / I 570 ) displayed an excellent linear correlation with BPA concentration over the range of 0-4000 nM ( R 2 = 0.9963), with a detection limit of 0.5 nM. Spiked recoveries in real samples ranged from 83.31% to 105.92%, with relative standard deviations between 0.81% and 4.52%. These results demonstrate the significant potential of this sensing system for precise and rapid determination of BPA in practical samples.

items.title: Understanding the Correctional Nursing Workforce: A Comparative Analysis of Wisconsin Registered Nurses.
items.abstract: Correctional nurses present an understudied part of the nursing workforce despite their complex patient population. A robust understanding of the correctional nursing workforce is needed to support staffing, retention, and workforce planning in prisons and jails. We describe the correctional nursing workforce in Wisconsin and compare correctional nurses with nurses practicing in other settings. Data from the 2024 Wisconsin Registered Nurse Survey were used to compare sociodemographic and career characteristics of correctional nurses with nurses practicing in hospitals, extended care, and community/public health settings. Comparisons were made using chi-squared tests, Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, and t -tests. Multiple differences were identified between correctional nurses and nurses in other settings in terms of educational attainment, likelihood of providing direct patient care, as well as demographic differences including race. When asked the most important factor in career decisions, correctional nurses more frequently selected benefits and less frequently selected career satisfaction compared to other nurses. Importantly, no difference in intent to continue in the present place of work was observed. Correctional nurses present unique sociodemographic and career characteristics compared to nurses in other settings, calling for the need of tailored policies and research that are responsive to correctional nurses' needs.

items.title: Towards Clarifying the Duty to Minimise Healthcare's Environmental Impacts.
items.abstract: We are seeing increasing work in bioethics to defend and define an ethical duty to minimise healthcare's environmental impacts. So far, the duty is often defined in terms of reducing healthcare's greenhouse gas emissions and two positions have emerged on whether and what limits to the duty apply: soft exceptionalism and non-exceptionalism. Yet, the philosophical grounds for the duty to minimise healthcare's environmental impacts are often not well explained or clearly articulated. That matters because, as this paper argues, different philosophical grounds generate different understandings of the duty's content and limits. In particular, this paper focuses on the implications of using different justice-based grounds for the duty. Section I first establishes that different axes of justice-social, environmental, ecological-can each be used to ground a general duty to minimise healthcare's environmental impacts. Section II shows that a range of ontologies underlie the conceptions of justice encompassed within those axes. Section III then demonstrates that the selected axis of justice and underlying ontology affects the nature-limits and content-of the resultant duty to minimise healthcare's environmental impacts. Ultimately, numerous different ways to understand the duty's limits and content are shown to exist. Many of those understandings require more than reducing healthcare's greenhouse gas emissions, and not all are consistent with soft exceptionalism or non-exceptionalism. To conclude, the paper considers whether reasons exist for favouring certain interpretations of the duty over others.

items.title: "We Felt This Tether to the Hospital": Lessons From the 2025 Los Angeles Wildfires for Climate-Era Disaster Preparedness in Pediatric Cancer Care.
items.abstract: Introduction The January 2025 Los Angeles wildfires were among the most destructive disasters in California's history, displacing thousands of densely populated communities. Pediatric cancer patients represent a vulnerable population, as their interrupted treatment, immunocompromised status, and dependence on specialized care create compounding risks during disasters. This qualitative investigation examines the impact of the wildfires on pediatric cancer patients or survivors, their caregivers, and clinicians. Methods We conducted in-depth interviews (n = 13) with caregivers of children in active treatment or survivorship for cancer affected by the wildfires and focus group discussions with pediatric cancer care clinicians (n = 9) serving fire-impacted and at-risk communities. Thematic analysis was performed. Results Five themes captured how the wildfires disrupted pediatric cancer care and created intersecting burdens for caregivers and clinicians alike: (1) treatment disruptions, delays, and stressors; (2) concerns about healthcare access and hospital proximity in evacuation decisions; (3) gaps in timely and responsive communication; (4) compounding challenges for clinicians navigating personal wildfire impacts while delivering care; and (5) health system coordination, preparedness, and lessons learned. Conclusions The wildfires exposed major gaps in how health systems support pediatric cancer patients during climate disasters. To improve resilience, health systems must invest in cross-institutional coordination, condition-specific clinical guidance, and communicate proactively with families before and during disasters. Future research should examine environmental hazard effects in medically vulnerable children and track longitudinal outcomes following care disruptions. Resilience in pediatric cancer care cannot be built in the aftermath of a disaster; it must be cultivated deliberately in the periods between them.

items.title: Post-traumatic stress, distress, coping and sleep quality in early-career paramedics.
items.abstract: Background Paramedics are exposed to trauma, placing them at elevated risk of mental health symptoms. However, limited research has examined symptom trajectories and associated factors in early-career paramedics. Aims This study explored changes in psychological distress and post-traumatic stress symptoms during the first year of paramedic practice and whether coping styles or sleep quality are associated with these changes. Methods Intern paramedics (N = 21; 71% female; Mage = 24.2, SD = 4.1) completed measures at five timepoints, including the General Health Questionnaire (psychological distress), Post-traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) Checklist for Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5), Coping Strategies Inventory and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Longitudinal analyses explored symptom trajectories and associated factors over 12 months. Results PTSD symptoms significantly increased (B = 0.9 [95% CI 0.2-1.6] P = 0.013). Psychological distress showed a significant quadratic effect (B = -13.5 [95% CI -23.7 to -3.4] P = 0.011). There was a significant association for between-person sleep quality and both PTSD symptoms (P Conclusions Psychological distress and PTSD symptoms increased during the first year of paramedic practice, with overall sleep quality a correlate of mental health. Early identification of sleep difficulties may support targeted interventions. Further research is needed to explore whether coping strategies become more influential as paramedics transition into autonomous roles.

items.title: Incidences of suicide and unintentional poisoning mortality after discharge from involuntary psychiatric hospitalization.
items.abstract: Aims Approximately 1 million involuntary psychiatric hospitalizations (IPHs) occur annually in the United States, but post-discharge outcomes are understudied. This study sought to characterize incidences of suicide and unintentional poisoning death following IPH and investigate factors associated with these outcomes. Methods Using data from the New Opportunities for Health and Resilience Measures for Suicide Prevention project, this population-based retrospective cohort study included all people with ≥1 IPH initiated in King County, Washington, from 2016 to 2022 ( N = 22,104). IPH records were linked to state death records. Crude cumulative incidences and incidence rates of suicide and unintentional poisoning mortality after discharge were estimated. Cox regressions were used to investigate associations with sociodemographic and clinical variables. Results The median age was 37 years (interquartile range: 27-53) at most recent IPH; 55.5% of participants were men, and the mean follow-up time was 2.49 years. The 1-month rates of suicide and unintentional poisoning were 1,180.6 and 2,192.5 per 100,000 person-years, respectively, compared with rates of 173.0 and 402.0 per 100,000 person-years from 1 to 7 years post-discharge (incidence rate ratio suicide [IRR] = 6.82; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 4.20-11.08; IRR poisoning = 5.45; 95% CI: 3.85-7.72). The 30-day and 1-year cumulative incidences were 0.10% (95% CI: 0.06-0.15%) and 0.57% (95% CI: 0.47-0.68%) for suicide and 0.18% (95% CI: 0.13-0.24%) and 0.91% (95% CI: 0.79-1.05%) for unintentional poisoning. Suicide by suffocation or hanging was more common than other suicide methods, including firearms. A Danger-to-Self detention order was significantly associated with the rates of suicide (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 2.20, 95% CI: 1.42-3.43) and unintentional poisoning mortality (aHR = 1.44, 95% CI: 1.06-1.96) compared to a Danger-to-Others order. Conclusions The suicide and unintentional poisoning mortality rates in this study underscore the importance of improving post-discharge care for people who undergo IPH, as a critical period of heightened risk was seen in the first month and year after discharge. Improved transition to post-discharge care, preventive measures such as means restriction, and substance use interventions represent opportunities for future study. Further research is needed to understand the effects of policies and healthcare practices on risks of mortality and other adverse events after IPH, and the possibility that IPHs entail iatrogenic harm, so that reliable recommendations to reduce mortality from suicide and unintentional poisoning can be developed for clinicians and policymakers.

items.title: Ginsenoside Rb1 attenuates adriamycin-induced cardiotoxic dysfunction in rats with changes in myocardial AMPK activity and CaV1.2 phosphorylation.
items.abstract: This study examined whether ginsenoside Rb1 (Gs-Rb1) attenuated systolic dysfunction in adriamycin (Adr)-treated rats and whether this response was accompanied by changes in serum NT-proBNP, myocardial AMPK activity, and Ser1928-phosphorylated LTCC/CaV1.2. Fifty male Wistar rats were assigned to five groups: control, HF, Gs-Rb1, AraA, and AraA + Gs-Rb1. Echocardiography assessed cardiac function. Serum NT-proBNP was measured by ELISA, AMPK activity was determined enzymatically, and total LTCC and phosphorylated LTCC/CaV1.2 were assessed by western blotting. Correlation and multivariable regression analyses examined associations between myocardial readouts and systolic function. Compared with HF rats, Gs-Rb1-treated rats showed higher LVEF, stroke volume, and cardiac output, together with lower serum NT-proBNP. Gs-Rb1 also increased myocardial AMPK activity, Ser1928-phosphorylated LTCC/CaV1.2 abundance, and the pLTCC/tLTCC ratio, whereas total LTCC abundance did not differ among groups. AraA attenuated these changes. The pLTCC/tLTCC ratio was positively correlated with LVEF and myocardial AMPK activity and negatively correlated with serum NT-proBNP. In multivariable regression, AMPK activity and NT-proBNP remained independently associated with LVEF, whereas pLTCC/tLTCC did not. Overall, Gs-Rb1 attenuated Adr-induced cardiac dysfunction in rats. Functional improvement was accompanied by lower serum NT-proBNP, higher myocardial AMPK activity and increased LTCC/CaV1.2 phosphorylation, supporting pharmacological involvement of AMPK-associated signaling in this model.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of potassium-containing low-sodium salt substitutes for cardiovascular disease prevention in mixed adult populations: an overview of reviews.
items.abstract: Potassium-containing low-sodium salt substitutes (LSSS) replace part of sodium chloride with potassium chloride to lower sodium intake and increase potassium intake. Yet, the review literature is overlapping and methodologically heterogeneous. This overview of reviews assessed the efficacy, safety, and evidence quality of potassium-containing LSSS for blood pressure, cardiovascular outcomes, and adverse events. Following a registered PROSPERO protocol (CRD420261294404), we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Global Health (EBSCO) and the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews from inception to 6 March 2026. Eleven reviews met eligibility. Methodological confidence (AMSTAR 2) was high in one, moderate in three, low in five, and critically low in two, and primary-study overlap was very high. With LSSS, 24-h urinary sodium was lower by 9.41-35.82 mmol/d and 24-h urinary potassium was higher by 7.19-17.22 mmol/d. Review-level pooled estimates favoured potassium-containing LSSS for systolic (mean difference -4.00 to -8.87 mmHg) and diastolic blood pressure (-1.42 to -4.04 mmHg). Later reviews also reported lower all-cause mortality (RR 0.88-0.89), cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.72-0.87), composite cardiovascular events, and selected stroke outcomes. However, these clinical-outcome estimates drew heavily on overlapping primary studies, particularly the Salt Substitute and Stroke Study, and are less independently replicated than the blood-pressure evidence. Serum potassium changed minimally (-0.02 to 0.18 mmol/L), with no clear excess of hyperkalaemia or serious adverse events reported. LSSS consistently lowered blood pressure; cardiovascular-event and mortality benefits remain promising but less certain. Trials outside East Asia with clearer formulation reporting and stronger safety data in higher-risk populations are needed.

items.title: The Effectiveness of Educational Interventions for Mental Health Professionals in Reducing Stigmatization Toward People Attracted to Children: A Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Mental Health Professionals (MHPs) often hold strong negative attitudes toward people attracted to children, hindering the provision of essential treatment. This stigmatization contributes to mental health challenges among people attracted to children and increases risk factors for child sexual abuse. Despite the significance of addressing these attitudes, limited research and small sample sizes highlight the need for a meta-analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of educational interventions in reducing stigmatization among MHPs. A literature search identified three studies that met the inclusion criteria: (a) involving MHPs who may encounter people attracted to children, (b) using educational interventions focused on people attracted to children, (c) assessing attitudes toward people attracted to children, (d) including pre- and post-data, (e) being peer-reviewed and empirical, (f) using quantitative data, and (g) written in English. In addition, three further studies were identified that met the same inclusion criteria, except for criterion (a), as these studies involved a sample of the general public rather than MHPs. These studies were included to enhance generalizability; however, caution is advised when interpreting the findings. Variables assessed included dangerousness, social distance, intentionality, deviance, punitiveness, anger, sympathy, and motivation to treat. Educational interventions significantly improved perceptions of dangerousness ( d = 0.73), social distance ( d = 0.33), intentionality ( d = 0.38), and punitiveness ( d = 0.77). Non-significant effects were observed for deviance ( d = 0.21), anger ( d = -0.22), sympathy ( d = -0.12), and motivation to treat ( d = -0.04). These findings suggest that educational interventions can effectively reduce stigmatization among MHPs.

items.title: Overweight Mothers and Stunted Children: Household Double Burden of Malnutrition in Samoa.
items.abstract: Objective Understanding the prevalence of double burden of malnutrition (DBM) and the factors associated with it at the household level is critical for creating effective policies and interventions that simultaneously address these nutrition challenges. In Samoa, while evidence of the occurrence of undernutrition and overnutrition within the same household is increasing, our understanding of the contributing factors is currently lacking. This study investigated the prevalence and correlates of DBM (mothers with overweight/obesity and stunted children) at the household level in Samoa. Design We used cross-sectional data from the Samoa Demographic and Health - Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey from 2019-2020 for the analyses. We conducted analyses using generalised estimating equations (GEE) logistic regression to identify factors associated with the overall occurrence of intrahousehold DBM. Setting Nationally representative cross-sectional survey in Samoa. Participants Children Results The prevalence of households with women with overnutrition and stunted children was 6.3%. Household economic status as measured by wealth index was associated with the risk of household-level DBM. No significant associations were found for the other household-level and individual-level factors. Conclusions A comprehensive and multi-pronged strategy focused on addressing socioeconomic disparities is needed to address the double burden of malnutrition in Samoa. By addressing these issues, public health initiatives can ensure better health outcomes for all community members, paving the way for a healthier and more prosperous future for Samoans.

items.title: Neutrophil Extracellular Traps at the Intersection of Cancer and Sepsis: A Narrative Review.
items.abstract: Cancer and sepsis are two leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Advances in oncologic treatments have increased survival rates for a variety of cancers, but they have also increased the number of patients with severe immune dysfunction. Consequently, infections that might otherwise stay localized can quickly progress to sepsis. There is an additional connection between sepsis and cancer. Dysregulated inflammatory signaling, metabolic reprogramming, endothelial damage, and disruptions in coagulation pathways represent a complex, interconnected array of immunological processes involved in both conditions. The host must simultaneously manage infection and respond to tumor-driven immune modulation, contributing to a precarious immunological balance. Consequently, compared with non-oncologic populations, cancer patients who develop sepsis often exhibit severe immune dysfunction and greater vulnerability to secondary infections. The innate immune system is essential to this complex biological environment. Neutrophils are crucial early host defense effector cells that contribute to pathogen clearance through several mechanisms. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), which are extracellular networks of chromatin fibers decorated with antimicrobial proteins capable of capturing and neutralizing pathogens, have been identified as a crucial mediator connecting infection, inflammation, and thrombosis. Excessive or unchecked NET formation can have adverse effects. Growing evidence indicates that NETs play a role in immunothrombotic phenomena, organ dysfunction, and microvascular injury during sepsis. Additionally, NETs have been increasingly linked to tumor biology, where they may aid immune escape, stimulate tumor growth, and promote metastatic spread. Understanding the dual role of NETs at the nexus of infection and cancer is essential. This narrative review analyzes available data on neutrophils and NETs in cancer patients with sepsis, highlighting emerging mechanisms and potential therapeutic implications.

items.title: The inspired-expired temperature gradient: a candidate bedside readout of airway gas-conditioning stress during invasive ventilation.
items.abstract: Ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI) is framed almost entirely in mechanical terms - tidal stress, strain and mechanical power - while the thermal conditioning of inspired gas is treated as a humidification housekeeping problem rather than a determinant of injury. Yet tracheal intubation abolishes most of the upper airway's heat- and water-exchanging capacity, and both inadequate and excessive gas conditioning provoke epithelial damage and airway inflammation in controlled animal ventilation. We propose that the breath-by-breath difference between expired and inspired gas temperature at the airway opening (ΔT = Tₑ - Tᵢ) is a physically simple, continuously available signal reflecting the heat the airway exchanges with each breath, and that the magnitude and trajectory of ΔT carry information about gas-conditioning adequacy and, plausibly, airway and lung injury during invasive ventilation. The same temperature difference has already been measured at the bedside in mechanically ventilated patients, but generally interpreted as a property of the humidification device or of ventilation-perfusion mismatch, rather than as a signal from the injured lung itself. Because expired gas temperature is also influenced by pulmonary blood flow and core temperature, these effects must be separated before any injury-related interpretation can be made. We outline the physiological rationale, existing measurement precedents, falsifiable predictions, and a staged approach to testing this hypothesis.

items.title: Myocardial Scar-Detected Cardiac Magnetic Resonance on Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing Outcomes: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Background The implantation of conduction system pacing (CSP), in particular left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), involves deep septal lead deployment 1.5 cm distal to the His bundle to achieve subendocardial capture of the left bundle branch; hence, myocardial scar is theoretically a critical determinant of both procedural success and subsequent CRT response. This review aimed to evaluate the impact of myocardial scar assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance late gadolinium enhancement (CMR-LGE) on LBBAP outcomes. Methods Three electronic databases (Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect) were searched for eligible studies from database inception until June, 12 2026. When at least two studies reported comparable quantitative outcomes, random-effects meta-analysis was performed using RStudio. Results Eight studies (n = 581 patients) met the eligibility criteria. Qualitatively, the presence of myocardial scar attenuates lead placement and electrical resynchronization, with smaller reductions in left ventricular activation and dyssynchrony, wider paced QRS duration, and more loss of conduction-system capture. Higher scar burden was associated with attenuated reverse remodeling (LVEF improvement, LVESV reduction, and LVEDD reduction). Higher scar burden was also associated with a higher risk of heart failure hospitalization, ventricular arrhythmia, and all-cause mortality. Quantitatively, CRT responders had lower baseline global LGE burden (MD -6.27%; 95% CI -10.84 to -1.70; p = 0.0072) and septal LGE burden (MD -7.94%; 95% CI -11.87 to -4.00; p Conclusion Myocardial scar may determine LBBAP outcomes, with the septal scar emerging as the most consistent predictor of worse outcomes. This qualitative early analysis supports pre-procedural LGE-CMR in selected LBBAP patients.

items.title: Estimating the Risk Associated with Cross-Contamination in a Foodborne Illness Outbreak.
items.abstract: Restaurant inspections are a routine public health intervention to reduce foodborne illness transmission. An analysis of routine inspections that preceded a 2015 Salmonella serotype Newport outbreak associated with contaminated tomatoes suggested that food code violations that could contribute to cross-contamination were associated with increased transmission at outbreak restaurants. Here, we expand our retrospective analysis to estimate the risk of illness due to the contaminated tomatoes directly and the elevated risk due to cross-contamination at the restaurant by determining the rate of illness based on the volume of tomatoes distributed to restaurants with and without specific food code violations. Relative risks for illnesses associated with these violations ranged from 3.05 to 4.01. The attributable fraction of outbreak cases in restaurants with these violations ranged from 67.2% to 75.1%. Mean rates of illness per restaurant ranged from 0.35 cases per 100 boxes of tomatoes for restaurants with none of the violations to 2.13 cases per 100 boxes of tomatoes for restaurants with 2 or 3 of the violations. These findings link the elevated risk of transmission to food handling behaviors in restaurants and represent a methodological approach for quantifying the risk of food safety violations identified through routine restaurant inspections.

items.title: School lunch consumption and caregiver perspectives on lunch provision in low-income Canadian elementary schools: a mixed-methods observational study using the NOVA classification.
items.abstract: Objective To characterise participant-level NOVA category presence and weight contribution in school-lunch intake, compare weight contribution by provenance, examine category presence by provenance, age group and reported gender and explore caregiver perspectives shaping lunch provision. items.title: Long-term PM<sub>10</sub> exposure and the risk of cerebrovascular and cancer mortality: a prospective cohort study in Taiwan.
items.abstract: Background Particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter of 10 ) can induce oxidative stress, thereby accelerating the development of atherosclerosis and promoting cellular mutations. However, evidence regarding the long-term effects of PM 10 exposure on cerebrovascular- and cancer-related mortality remains inconsistent. Objective This prospective cohort study evaluated the associations between annual variations in PM 10 exposure and the risks of cerebrovascular- and cancer-related mortality among Taiwanese adults. Methods We prospectively followed 82,579 adults who maintained the same residential address from 2005 to 2017. Cause-specific mortality outcomes were ascertained through Taiwan's national death certificate database over a mean follow-up of 10.6 years. Annual average residential PM 10 concentrations were estimated using an ordinary kriging model, and associations with mortality were examined using Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models accounting for competing risks. Results Across 872,745 person-years of follow-up, 2,553 deaths occurred, including 163 (6.4%) from cerebrovascular disease and 1,203 (47.1%) from cancer. After adjustment for sociodemographic factors, lifestyle behaviors, and comorbidities, each 10 μg/m 3 increase in PM 10 exposure was associated with higher all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.12; 95% CI, 1.09-1.16). Higher PM 10 exposure was also associated with increased cerebrovascular mortality (aHR, 1.18; 95% CI, 1.05-1.32) and cancer mortality (aHR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.05-1.15). Conclusions Long-term exposure to PM 10 was significantly associated with increased risks of cerebrovascular and cancer-related mortality. These findings underscore the need for proactive air pollution control strategies to reduce preventable deaths.

items.title: Limb Asymmetries on WASP-39b: A Multi-GCM Comparison of Chemistry, Clouds, and Hazes
items.abstract: With JWST, observing separate spectra of the morning and evening limbs of hot Jupiters has finally become a reality. The first such observation was reported for WASP-39b, where the evening terminator was observed to have a larger transit radius by about 400 ppm and a stronger 4.3 μ m CO 2 feature than the morning terminator. Multiple factors, including temperature differences, photo/thermochemistry, clouds, and hazes, could cause such limb asymmetries. To interpret these new limb asymmetry observations, a detailed understanding of how the relevant processes affect morning and evening spectra grounded in forward models is needed. Focusing on WASP-39b, we compare simulations from five different general circulation models (GCMs), including one simulating disequilibrium thermochemistry and one with cloud radiative feedback, to the recent WASP-39b limb asymmetry observations. We also post-process the temperature structures of all simulations with a 2D photochemical model and one simulation with a cloud microphysics model. Although the temperatures predicted by the different models vary considerably, the models are remarkably consistent in their predicted morning–evening temperature differences. Several equilibrium-chemistry simulations predict strong methane features in the morning spectrum, not seen in the observations. When including disequilibrium processes, horizontal transport homogenizes methane, and these methane features disappear. However, even after including photochemistry and clouds, our models still cannot reproduce the observed ∼2000 ppm asymmetry in the CO 2 feature. A combination of factors, such as varying metallicity and unexplored parameters in cloud models, may explain the discrepancy, emphasizing the need for future models integrating cloud microphysics and feedback across a broader parameter space.

items.title: Confining nonlinear electrodynamics black holes: from thermodynamic phases to high-frequency phenomena with accretion process
items.abstract: We investigate a static, spherically symmetric black hole arising from Einstein gravity coupled to a confining nonlinear electrodynamics model in which Maxwell theory is recovered in the strong-field regime while nonlinear corrections govern the weak-field domain. The metric function is asymptotically Schwarzschild but carries a Q3/(9ξ2r4) correction, with the standard Reissner-Nordstr¨om Q2/r2 term absent.The Maxwell limit thus appears in the ultraviolet rather than in the infrared, opposite to Born-Infeld, Bardeen-type, and exponential-logarithmic models [ 1 –5 ], and the parameter combination Q3/ξ2 defines an observable axis without counterpart in those constructions. We map this axis onto the horizon structure, weak-field deflection in vacuum and in plasma and axion-plasmon media, gravitational redshift, photon sphere (governed by a quartic equation), Lyapunov exponent, and shadow size, with all leading corrections proportional to Q3/ξ2 rather than Q2. The Joule-Thomson expansion coefficient and heat capacity locate a second-order phase transition with mean-field exponents β = 1/2 and γ = 1, the constant-pressure heat capacity diverging there as a simple pole, while the inversion-to-critical temperature ratio Ti/Tc ≈ 0.46 at (M, Q, ξ) = (1, 0.5, 0.5) deviates from the value 1/2 characteristic of charged AdS black holes, providing a model-distinguishing thermodynamic quantity. Fully relativistic Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton simulations show that the confining geometry enhances the mass accretion rate by a factor of about 1.4 relative to Schwarzschild and generates stable 3 : 2 and 2 : 1 HFQPO commensurabilities matching observations from black hole X-ray binaries. Discriminants from shadow imaging, X-ray spectroscopy, and timing data are collected in Table II. The model reproduces HFQPO pairs without invoking black hole spin.

items.title: Electromagnetically-Induced transparency bridges disconnected light-harvesting networks
items.abstract: The energy-transfer efficiency of the natural photosynthesis system seems to be perfectly optimized during the evolution for millions of years. However, how to enhance the efficiency in the artificial light-harvesting systems is still unclear. In this paper, we investigate the energy-transfer process in the photosystem I (PSI). When there is no effective coupling between the outer antenna (OA) and the reaction center (RC), the two light-harvesting networks are disconnected and thus the energy transfer is inefficient. In order to repair these disconnected networks, we introduce a bridge with three sites between them. We find that by modulating the level structure of the 3-site bridge to be resonant, the energy transfer via the dark state will be enhanced and even outperform the original PSI. Our discoveries may shed light on the designing mechanism of artificial light-harvesting systems.

items.title: A Quantum Computing Framework for VLBI Data Correlation
items.abstract: This work presents a quantum computing framework for very-long-baseline interferometry (VLBI) data correlation. It is shown that a classical baseband time series data of a length N can be embedded into a quantum superposition state using amplitude encoding with only log2N qubits. The basic VLBI correlation and fringe fitting operations, including fringe rotation, a Fourier transform, delay compensation, and cross correlation, can be implemented via quantum algorithms with significantly reduced computational complexity. A single-baseline quantum pipeline for geodetic VLBI data processing is constructed, and its feasibility and accuracy are validated through direct comparison with a classical pipeline. Amplitude encoding of large data volumes remains the primary bottleneck in quantum computing. However, the quantized nature of VLBI raw data helps reduce the state preparation complexity. This investigation demonstrates that quantum computation offers a promising paradigm for VLBI data correlation and is likely to play a role in future VLBI systems.

items.title: Bounce, turnaround, and the anisotropy problem in cyclic cosmology on a brane with a timelike extra dimension
items.abstract: We study cosmological bounces, turnarounds, and cyclic evolution on an anisotropic Bianchi-I brane embedded in a five-dimensional bulk with a timelike extra dimension, within the Shtanov–Sahni braneworld framework. Restricting to the flat, dark-radiation-free, effective- $$\Lambda $$ Λ -free branch of the general anisotropic brane Friedmann equation, we drive the dynamics with a single canonical scalar field obeying the uniform-rate condition $$\dot{\phi }=-\lambda =\textrm{const}$$ ϕ ˙ = - λ = const, with shear anisotropy encoded through a geometric term $$\Omega _\sigma (a)\propto a^{-6}$$ Ω σ (a) ∝ a - 6. We derive a general turning-point classification valid for any fluid obeying the null energy condition: turnarounds at negative energy density occur unconditionally, while bounces at $$\rho >\rho _c$$ ρ > ρ c occur only when the negative high-energy brane correction dominates the decelerating shear term. Specializing to the uniform-rate scalar, we obtain closed-form bounce and turnaround conditions, the leading-order excess of the bounce density above critical, and a matching condition for a finite cyclic branch connecting a bounce at $$N_B$$ N B to a turnaround at $$N_T$$ N T. We identify post-bounce superinflationary and post-shear-dilution ordinary-inflationary regimes, obtain a closed-form expression for the duration of the superinflationary stage, $$\Delta N_\textrm{sinf}\simeq \rho _c/6\lambda ^2=|\sigma |/3\lambda ^2$$ Δ N sinf ≃ ρ c / 6 λ 2 = | σ | / 3 λ 2, which scales linearly with the brane tension, and show that the numbers of e -folds separating the bounce, the pivot and the end of inflation are fixed analytically by the tilt and the pivot density fraction alone, compute the single-field curvature power spectrum, and derive parameter relations fixing $$H_*$$ H ∗, $$\lambda $$ λ, $$\rho _c$$ ρ c, and the shear amplitude $$\Sigma _g^2$$ Σ g

items.title: Photometry Is All You Need: Supernova Classification as a Mixing Problem
items.abstract: In the era of large-scale photometric surveys, scalable and robust methods for classifying supernova (SN) populations are increasingly necessary. Often, spectroscopy is essential in addition to photometry to reliably classify SNe; however, complete spectroscopic follow-up is infeasible for all of the millions of transient light curves being collected by facilities such as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. Using light curves of SNe Ia and Ibc observed with the Zwicky Transient Facility, we frame the classification of large SN populations as a mixing problem. We fit all objects using a semianalytical SN model powered by radioactive decay, and we model the resulting distributions of fit parameters with a Gaussian mixture model to optimize the shared population mixing fraction. This approach allows us to reliably constrain the ratio of the populations and classify SNe Ia and Ibc with ≥90% accuracy without any need for labeled training data, i.e., a spectroscopic dataset. We validate this method for varying population mixing fractions and explore the impact of including spectroscopic, photometric, or no redshift information, and a small amount of known labels. Overall, this method allows for fast and accurate SN classification and population characterization using only photometry.

items.title: The Radio–FIR Correlation in the Context of Deep Radio Source Counts
items.abstract: Increasingly deep, confusion-limited radio surveys have pushed direct radio source-count measurements down to tens of μ Jy at 1.4 GHz. Confusion-noise P (D) analyses extend the statistical counts to below 1 μ Jy. Radio source counts have allowed for constraints on the radio-derived star formation rate density (SFRD) history through models of the backwards evolution of the local radio luminosity function, using the radio–far-infrared (FIR) correlation, q ∝ log (L FIR / L 1.4), to convert radio luminosities to FIR luminosities and, hence, star formation rates. Recent deep radio source counts from MeerKAT suggest a potential tension in the SFRD history between radio and UV/IR measurements at 1 ≲ z ≲ 2. This corresponds to a ≳3 σ discrepancy between the predicted and measured source counts near the star-forming galaxy (SFG) source count S 2 n (S) peak of ∼30 μ Jy under both a pure luminosity (PLE) and combined luminosity and density evolution (LADE). We consider what the requirement of agreement between radio source counts and the observed UV/IR SFRD indicates about the redshift evolution of the radio–FIR correlation and its intrinsic scatter out to z = 3. We introduce a radio-luminosity based parameterization to q FIR (z) based on changing thermal radio fractions alone that agrees with the observed stellar-mass dependent q FIR (z) better than a nonevolving or decreasing q FIR (z). Despite this, we find that a decreasing q FIR (z) at fixed radio luminosity provides better agreement between source counts and the observed SFRD, while a q FIR (z) that breaks down due to cosmic ray losses requires an intrinsic scatter up to σ q ≈ 0.3 dex.

items.title: Predicting Primordial Non-Gaussianity Measurements in the CSST Spectroscopic Survey
items.abstract: Primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG) is a fundamental probe of the physics of the early Universe and inflation. Here we present a comprehensive study of the constraints on the local-type PNG parameter, f NL, for the spectroscopic galaxy survey of the upcoming Chinese Space Station Survey Telescope (CSST). Utilizing the high-resolution Jiutian N -body simulation suite, we construct realistic mock catalogs for emission line galaxies (ELGs) at three representative redshifts z = 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9. The expected CSST observational characteristics are also considered, including redshift uncertainties and selection functions based on signal-to-noise ratios of emission lines. We develop a robust analysis framework for the redshift-space galaxy power spectrum and bispectrum that accounts for redshift-space distortions, scale-dependent bias, and nonlinear effects. For the parameter p in the PNG bias b ϕ with p = 0.55, we find f NL = −4 ± 43 if only using the power-spectrum data, and f NL = 3 ± 41 after combining the bispectrum data, reducing the uncertainty by ∼5%. For the p = 1 case, the constraint results are f NL = −3 ± 86 and 5 4 − 80 + 70 for comparison. This work demonstrates the potential of the Stage IV surveys like CSST to probe inflationary physics, and highlights the importance of higher-order statistics in extracting information from large-scale structure surveys.

items.title: Astronomical Cardiology II: A Search For Heartbeat Stars Using APOGEE and TESS
items.abstract: Stellar binaries in short-period, highly eccentric systems with significant tidal deformations near pericenter, also known as heartbeat stars, are a laboratory for studying dynamical tides and oscillations in stars. We identify 50 heartbeat stars using TESS light curves of stars identified as binaries using SDSS APOGEE. We fit their phase-folded TESS light curves with an analytic model to measure their orbital periods, eccentricities, inclinations, and arguments of periastron. We measure the mass function of targets with enough APOGEE radial velocity observations to obtain a constraint on the secondary mass. We confirm our previous results that the non-giant heartbeat stars have started to evolve off the main sequence and that the fraction of (near) main sequence binaries that are heartbeat stars rises rapidly with effective temperature.

items.title: Dynamically Tunable Electromagnetically Induced Transparency in a Vanadium-Dioxide-Based Terahertz Metasurface
items.abstract: A dynamically tunable terahertz (THz) electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) metasurface integrated with vanadium dioxide (VO 2) is proposed and numerically investigated. The unit cell comprises gold resonators and VO 2 strips patterned on a silicon dioxide substrate. When VO 2 is in the insulating state (σ = 2×10 2 S/m), the bright resonator is directly excited by the incident THz wave, while the dark resonator is indirectly activated through near-field coupling. Destructive interference between these coupled modes generates a pronounced EIT transparency window at approximately 0.72 THz with a peak transmission of 0.82. The underlying mode-coupling mechanism is corroborated by electric-field distributions and a coupled Lorentz-oscillator model, which exhibits excellent agreement with full-wave simulations. As VO 2 undergoes an insulator-to-metal transition (σ = 2×10 5 S/m), the dramatically increased conductivity reconstructs the surface current distribution and enhances ohmic losses in the dark mode, thereby disrupting the phase-matching condition required for EIT. Consequently, the original transparency window is suppressed, and the spectral response is reconfigured into a broad transmission band near 0.50 THz. Furthermore, the metasurface exhibits tunable slow-light characteristics, achieving a maximum group delay of approximately 5–6 ps in the insulating state. Parametric analysis reveals that the VO 2 gap length critically governs the coupling strength and resonance position. Owing to its simple geometry, wideband tunability, and dynamic control of both amplitude and dispersion, the proposed VO 2 -integrated metasurface offers a promising platform for reconfigurable THz modulators, optical switches, filters, and slow-light devices.

items.title: ALMA Observations of Molecular Complexity in the Large Magellanic Cloud: The N 83 Star-forming Region
items.abstract: We report the results of the 1.2 mm continuum and molecular line ∼0.1 parsec-scale observations with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) of two fields in the star-forming region N 83 in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC). This study is third in a series of investigations exploring molecular complexity in a low-metallicity and high UV flux environment of the LMC. We determine the physical and chemical properties of five sources detected with ALMA based on spectral modeling with XCLASS and the analysis of the continuum emission. The temperatures exceeding 100 K, small sizes, and high H 2 volume densities of sources N 83A–mm A and B indicate that they are hot cores. N 83A–mm A/B are associated with complex organic molecules: methanol (CH 3 OH), methyl cyanide (CH 3 CN), and dimethyl ether (CH 3 OCH 3). We also found CH 3 OH in three cold cores, and extended cold CH 3 OH emission in both fields. We detected SO, 33 SO, SO 2, OCS, H 2 CS, CS, C 33 S, HC 15 N, H 13 CN, HNCO, HDCO, H 13 CO +, SiO, and CH 2 CO in at least one core. Molecular abundances with respect to H 2 fit into the trends previously reported for the Magellanic hot cores: the CH 3 OH abundance varies significantly, while the abundances of S-bearing species show small variations. We found evidence for strong UV radiation and complex kinematics in both ALMA fields in N 83. The feedback-produced shocks are important drivers of the chemistry of S-bearing species, SiO, and CH 3 OH inside and outside of hot cores. Local effects have a large impact on the chemical composition and abundances of star-forming cores in the LMC.

items.title: Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Emission from Star-forming and Quiescent Galaxies at z = 0.5–0.8 Probed by JWST/MIRI
items.abstract: We investigate emission from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) dust molecules in 224 MIRI-selected star-forming and quiescent galaxies (QGs) at z = 0.5–0.8 in the GOODS-South field using multiwavelength data from the AstroSat/UVIT, JWST, Hubble Space Telescope, Herschel, and MUSE. We define an observed diagnostic parameter, f PAH, as the ratio of JWST/MIRI F1280W to the average of F770W and F2550W band fluxes, and demonstrate that it effectively traces the PAH mass fraction (q PAH) by capturing 7.7 μ m PAH emission at our targeted redshift. We observe a bimodal distribution of similar nature in both f PAH and q PAH, suggesting that PAH enrichment in galaxies goes through a rapid transition phase from a PAH poor to a PAH-rich system, at about 70% solar metallicity. For the star-forming galaxies (SFGs; i.e., ∼78% of the total sample), we find that f PAH increases with stellar mass and rest-frame far-UV luminosity, identifying massive, UV-bright galaxies to have higher PAH mass fraction. However, the majority of the massive QGs show lower PAH mass fraction relative to that of SFGs of similar mass, suggesting PAH and smaller dust grains are more susceptible to destruction during quenching processes. Among SFGs, we observe an anticorrelation between f PAH and the O32 emission-line ratio, suggesting PAH photodissociation in strongly ionized interstellar medium. This anticorrelation, along with a correlation between f PAH and gas-phase metallicity 12+log(O/H), indicates that low-mass, metal-poor SFGs, which are increasingly common at even higher redshifts, host more extreme conditions less favorable for PAH production and survival.

items.title: The Influence of Hubble Expansion on the Future Merger of the Milky Way and Andromeda
items.abstract: Most existing idealized simulations of galaxy mergers neglect Hubble expansion, as the local Hubble flow is curved by overdensities and the expansion effect is weak at these scales. However, even in the gravity-dominated Local Group (LG), the expansion itself still persists, and it has been shown to be important in some LG-related studies. Here we take the future merger of the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda (M31) as a case study to investigate the differences between simulations with and without Hubble expansion. We perform a suite of idealized N -body simulations of the MW–M31 system under pure Newtonian, ΛCDM, and w 0 w a CDM scenarios, testing different masses and proper motions of galaxies informed by current observational constraints. At low M31 tangential velocities, especially in cases where the two galaxies merge within a Hubble time, the expansion effect is negligible; but at high velocities (> 66.5 km s −1), the ΛCDM simulations introduce a noticeable delay in the merger time compared to the Newtonian ones and may even alter the final fate of the system, but the caveat here is that the isolated-pair idealization and the assumed expansion history break down. The delay is also present but less pronounced in the w 0 w a CDM runs. When M33 and the Large Magellanic Cloud are included, the differences in merger times are reduced. In summary, Hubble expansion can play a noticeable role for galaxy mergers with high tangential velocities, but its actual influence on the MW–M31 merger depends on the precise masses and proper motions to be determined in the future.

items.title: Revisiting the Missing Baryon Problem: Baryon Redistribution across Halo Evolution
items.abstract: The baryon fraction provides a fundamental diagnostic of baryonic matter distribution within dark matter halos and the baryon cycle. While its cosmic value is well constrained, the baryon content within halos on nearly all scales is significantly lower than the cosmic mean; this is called the “missing baryon problem.” Using the high spatial, mass, and temporal resolutions of the NewCluster simulation, we investigate the baryon fraction evolution by tracing halo assembly histories from merger trees and gas tracer particles. We identify three distinct evolutionary phases: an early growth phase driven by cold accretion in low-mass halos, a suppression phase likely dominated by supernova feedback, and a recovery phase in massive halos enabled by deeper potential wells and hot-mode accretion. We further find that the redshift dependence of baryon fraction, particularly in low-mass halos, is influenced by the thermal state of the intergalactic medium, with suppression emerging after the surrounding gas becomes persistently hotter than the halo virial temperature. In addition, the scatter in baryon fraction at fixed halo mass correlates with the large-scale environment, with baryon-rich halos preferentially residing closer to filamentary structures. Overall, our results highlight that baryon fraction evolution is governed by the interplay between feedback and environment, requiring a time-resolved perspective on the baryon cycle.

items.title: Detection of Impulse Control Behaviors in Parkinson's Disease: Incremental Yield of Unstructured Psychiatric Interviews over QUIP Screening and Routine Clinical Assessment.
items.abstract: Impulse control behaviors (ICBs) are common but under-recognized non-motor complications of Parkinson's disease (PD), arising from dopaminergic overstimulation of fronto-striatal reward circuits. Self-report tools such as the Questionnaire for Impulsive-Compulsive Disorders in PD (QUIP) are limited by reduced insight, recall bias and reluctance to disclose sensitive behaviors. To compare approaches to ICB detection in PD-outpatient referral documentation, QUIP screening, and a clinician-led unstructured psychiatric interview (UPI) integrating informant testimony-and to characterize the spectrum and co-occurrence of ICB subtypes. In this prospective observational single-center study, 144 inpatients with idiopathic PD were evaluated at admission to a neuropsychiatric unit by these approaches. Detection rates were compared using McNemar's test. ICBs were identified in 13.2% via referral data, 20.8% via QUIP and 36.1% via UPI (McNemar p < 0.001). UPI yielded a 15.3-percentage-point increment over QUIP, including detection of reckless generosity (not represented in QUIP) and clinically relevant presentations of dopamine dysregulation syndrome and punding that were under-detected by screening items. Co-occurring ICBs were common: 27.8% of patients exhibited two or more subtypes, 14.6% four or more, and 2.1% up to seven. In a subgroup analysis, patients with ≥6 ICBs (n = 7) were uniformly male, dopamine agonist-treated, younger and had longer disease duration. Routine clinical assessment and self-report screening substantially underestimate the prevalence and complexity of ICBs in PD. A comprehensive informant-supported psychiatric interview improves detection and reveals clinically relevant phenotypic clustering, with implications for dopaminergic therapy adjustment and pre-DBS evaluation.

items.title: Association of Feeding Therapy Timing and Frequency With Time to Independent Oral Feeding in Infants With Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy.
items.abstract: Objective To characterize feeding therapy utilization and delivery patterns and examine associations of therapy dose (timing and frequency) with time to independent oral feeding in infants with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE). Study design We conducted a retrospective cohort study of infants with HIE treated with therapeutic hypothermia and discharged feeding independently by mouth from two Level IV neonatal intensive care unit (NICUs) between 2017 and 2024. Multivariable linear regression assessed associations of therapy timing and frequency with time to independent oral feeding, adjusting for encephalopathy severity, abnormality on brain magnetic resonance imaging, and intubation days. Results Among 358 infants, 326 (91%) received feeding therapy. Therapy was initiated a median of 1.5 d after therapeutic hypothermia and was delivered at a median of 3.5 sessions per week. Each day of delayed initiation was associated with a 0.5 d longer time to independent oral feeding (95% CI 0.3-0.7), and each additional weekly session with a 1 d shorter time to independent oral feeding (95% CI: -1.5 to -0.5). Conclusion Earlier initiation and greater frequency of feeding therapy were associated with faster attainment of independent oral feeding. Therapy timing and frequency may represent potentially modifiable aspects of NICU care that warrant prospective investigation.

items.title: A minimal physical model of adhesion-dependent protrusion explains confined haptotaxis and oscillatory cell migration.
items.abstract: Haptotaxis is the directed migration of cells along gradients of substrate adhesion, and is an important guidance mechanism in biology. Recent experiments on fibronectin-patterned tracks show that cells typically migrate toward higher adhesion, then oscillate around the adhesion maximum, with substantial variability in speed and cell length. To explain these cellular shape and migration dynamics we present a minimal model for confined haptotaxis, built around one key physical ingredient: local adhesion strength directly enhances the recruitment of protrusive actin polymerization activity at the cell edge. This coupling creates a front-rear difference in protrusive activity, biasing the cell towards polarization in the direction of the higher adhesion. Quantitative comparison with experiment shows strong agreement at multiple levels: cell population-level directionality statistics and position-dependent changes in cell length and velocity. At the single-cell level, the model reproduces the full diversity of experimentally observed trajectories, including haptotactic bias and its dependence on adhesion-gradient strength, initial position, length and speed variations, myosin II inhibition, and migration on inverted adhesion gradients. Variability in experimental trajectories and migration speed is explained by differences in intrinsic actin polymerization activity and stochastic fluctuations, accounting for the full spectrum of observed migration patterns. Together, our results identify adhesion-dependent amplification of protrusive activity as a minimal and sufficient physical mechanism for understanding haptotaxis.

items.title: Mitochondrial dynamics regulation in neurogenesis during cerebral ischemia-reperfusion.
items.abstract: Background Ischemic stroke ranks among the leading causes of death and disability worldwide. Vascular recanalization after stroke can trigger cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury(CIRI), which disturbs mitochondrial homeostasis and blunts endogenous neurogenesis, limiting brain functional recovery. Although mitochondrial dynamics govern neural stem cell fate under physiological conditions, how this machinery reshapes neurogenesis specifically in the pathological context of CIRI remains incompletely synthesized. Objective This review focuses on the mechanistic links between mitochondrial dynamics disturbance, impaired energy metabolism, and defective endogenous neurogenesis under CIRI, as well as therapeutic strategies targeting mitochondrial dynamics to restore neurogenesis after reperfusion insult. Methods Relevant literature on neurogenesis, energy metabolism, and mitochondrial dynamics was reviewed to elucidate their roles in CIRI. Additionally, experimental data on mitochondrial dynamics-related proteins regulating neurogenesis were examined, with special attention to findings obtained from cerebral ischemia-reperfusion experimental models. Results Therapeutic approaches promoting endogenous neurogenesis represent a novel strategy for treating ischemic-induced neural injury. Neurogenesis is closely linked to mitochondrial energy metabolism. In CIRI, reperfusion stress disrupts the balance of mitochondrial fission-fusion, which further impairs metabolic reprogramming required for neural stem cell activation, proliferation and neuronal survival. Direct in-vivo evidence connecting mitochondrial dynamics remodeling to neurogenesis in CIRI is still limited. Targeting mitochondrial dynamics to rescue energy homeostasis may serve as a means to revive endogenous neurogenesis post-CIRI. Conclusion Energy metabolism and pathological changes following cerebral ischemia-reperfusion are closely associated with mitochondrial dynamics. Modulating mitochondrial dynamics holds potential to rescue metabolic disturbance and restore neurogenesis after CIRI.
