items.title: Multivariate and temporal relationships between continuously derived individualized intracranial pressure (iICP) thresholds and multi-modal cerebral physiology in moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury.
items.abstract: Current moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) management relies on guideline-based intracranial pressure (ICP) and cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) thresholds to mitigate secondary brain injury. However, these fixed, population-derived targets fail to account for substantial inter- and intra-patient variability in cerebral physiology. Individualized intracranial pressure (iICP) has emerged as a promising personalized physiologic target. Recently, the feasibility of continuous derivation of iICP has been demonstrated. However, the relationship between continuously derived iICP and multimodal cerebral physiology remains unknown. A retrospective exploratory analysis was conducted using high-frequency physiologic data from adult patients with moderate-to-severe TBI enrolled in the Winnipeg Acute TBI database. Continuous iICP estimates were retrospectively derived at 1-minute intervals using a previously described algorithm. Associations between iICP-derived burden and established cerebral physiologic insult burden metrics were evaluated using linear regression analysis. Multivariate physiologic structure was characterized using hierarchical clustering, k-means clustering, and principal component analysis. Temporal relationships were evaluated using cross-correlation, Granger causality, and VARIMA-based impulse response function analyses. A total of 150 patients were included. Compared with conventional guideline-based ICP thresholds, burden above iICP demonstrated stronger associations with cerebrovascular reactivity-based physiologic insult burden. Across clustering and principal component analyses, iICP consistently demonstrated greatest similarity to measures of intracranial dynamics while remaining distinct from both hemodynamic and cerebrovascular reactivity metrics. Temporal analyses revealed limited evidence of reproducible short-term coupling between iICP and individual physiologic parameters. However, impulse response function analyses demonstrated the largest modeled iICP responses following perturbations in MAP and CPP. Continuously derived iICP demonstrated distinct relationships with intracranial dynamics, cerebrovascular reactivity, and cerebral perfusion-related physiology. These findings provide hypothesis-generating physiologic characterization of iICP and support prospective, outcome-linked evaluation of its real-time clinical implementation.

items.title: Intracranial hemorrhage in glioblastoma: incidence, risk factors, and outcome.
items.abstract: The incidence, risk factors and clinical implications of intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) in patients with glioblastoma have not been well studied. We identified patients with WHO 2021 glioblastoma in the Zurich database and explored the incidence, putative risk factors, management and outcome of ICH. ICH was verified by central MRI and imaging report review. Among 387 patients diagnosed between 2010 and 2019, 40 had an ICH at diagnosis. Of these, 4 patients were on anti-platelet agents, and 2 patients were on anticoagulation. All ICH occurred in the tumor region. Patients with ICH at diagnosis were younger (p = 0.001), had less cardiac disease (p = 0.027), and had larger tumors (p = 0.020). Median survival was similar between patients with (15 months) or without (13 months) ICH at diagnosis. Among 22 patients with ICH later in the disease course, 7 patients (37%) experienced ICH prior to first progression. ICH were not intratumoral in 8 patients. Ten patients (45%) had no change in management, 7 patients (32%) were referred to palliative care. Nine patients (50%) had been pre-exposed to bevacizumab, yet, 193 patients (53%) without ICH had received bevacizumab, too. Five patients (23%) had platelet counts below 100,000/µl within 14 days prior to ICH. Median survival in the 22 patients who experienced ICH after diagnosis (17 months) was not inferior than in patients without ICH (13 months). ICH is rare in glioblastoma. It may be related to intrinsic features of the tumor and its blood vessels, however, platelet count and blood pressure should be monitored regularly. ICH does not signify a poor outcome overall.

items.title: X-linked Frmpd3 in Neurodevelopment and Neuronal Morphology: Insights into Cerebral Palsy.
items.abstract: Cerebral palsy (CP) is a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental disorders characterized by abnormalities in movement and posture. A higher proportion of X-linked genetic causes found in the CP cohort implies that X-linked variants may play a role in the etiology of CP in males. In this study, rare variants in X-linked FRMPD3 were identified in a cohort of 1073 sporadic males with CP via whole-exome sequencing. Three rare variants in X-linked FRMPD3, namely, c.157C > T (p.Arg53Ter), c.2505C > A (p.His835Gln), and c.4018G > T (p.Gly1340Trp), were prioritized for functional characterization. Functional analyses showed that the c.2505C > A variant led to a significant reduction in protein levels, whereas c.4018G > T did not. Knockdown of Frmpd3 via in utero electroporation altered the cortical distribution of GFP+ cells at E17.5, with reduced localization in the cortical plate, a finding that was also observed in Frmpd3 knockout mice generated using CRISPR/Cas9. Moreover, Frmpd3 knockout mice displayed motor deficits and morphological abnormalities of the corpus callosum. Meanwhile, cultured primary neurons from Frmpd3 knockout mice exhibited reduced dendritic length and altered dendritic complexity. Notably, Frmpd3 interacts with key synaptic proteins (including HOMER1, β-pix, PSD-95, GluN1, and GluN2B), and patient-derived variants H835Q and G1340W showed reduced interaction with PSD-95. Collectively, these findings support a role for Frmpd3 in cortical neurodevelopment and neuronal morphology. Although further human-based studies are warranted, our results provide experimental evidence for the role of Frmpd3 in brain development and suggest that altered FRMPD3 function may be relevant to CP.

items.title: Clinical significance of parenchymal venous reflux in borden type III dural arteriovenous fistulas.
items.abstract: To assess the association of parenchymal venous reflux (PVR) with clinical presentation in patients with Borden type III dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs), including intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), nonhemorrhagic neurological deficit (NHND) and functional status at presentation. This retrospective database study included 516 patients with Borden type III DAVFs. Clinical and angiographic characteristics at diagnosis were compared between patients with and without PVR. Separate logistic regression models assessed associations of PVR with aggressive presentation, ICH, and NHND, adjusting for age, sex, venous congestion, venous ectasia, and fistula location. Treatment and available follow-up information were summarized descriptively. Among 516 patients, 339 (65.7%) had PVR. Aggressive presentation occurred in 267/339 patients with PVR (78.8%) and 53/177 without PVR (29.9%), with an adjusted odds ratio (OR) of 8.95 (95% CI 5.53-14.49; P < 0.001). NHND occurred in 164/339 (48.4%) versus 9/177 (5.1%), with an adjusted OR of 18.89 (95% CI 8.90-40.13; P < 0.001). ICH occurred in 103/339 (30.4%) versus 44/177 (24.9%), with an adjusted OR of 1.33 (95% CI 0.84-2.11; P = 0.226). Patients with PVR also had higher mRS scores at presentation. PVR was associated with NHND and greater functional disability at presentation. The association with the composite aggressive presentation outcome was predominantly attributable to NHND.

items.title: Protective effects of PACAP38 eye drops treatment on the vertical information processing pathway in type 2 diabetic retinopathy.
items.abstract: Type 2 diabetic retinopathy (T2DR) is increasingly recognized as a neurodegenerative disease characterized by early neuronal and glial alterations in addition to microvascular damage. Pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP) has emerged as a promising neuroprotective agent. The present study investigated the protective effects of PACAP38 eye drops treatment in a rat model of T2DR, with a particular focus on retinal neuronal populations and synaptic integrity. Type 2 diabetes was induced by a combination of a high-fat diet and two low-dose intraperitoneal streptozotocin injections (30 mg kg-1, one week apart). Retinal morphology and cellular integrity were assessed using immunohistochemistry. Diabetes induced marked disruption of the outer limiting membrane, increased Müller cell gliosis, and pronounced degeneration of photoreceptors, synaptic structures, interneurons, and ganglion cells. Significant reductions were observed in the number of cone photoreceptor cell bodies, ribbon synapse-associated CTBP2 fluorescence, bipolar and rod bipolar cell populations, and in the number of Brn3a-positive ganglion cells. In contrast, horizontal cells showed relative resistance to diabetic injury. PACAP38 treatment markedly attenuated diabetes-induced retinal damage. PACAP38 preserved tight junction organization, reduced glial activation, significantly protected cone photoreceptors and their synaptic terminals, and maintained populations of bipolar, rod bipolar, and ganglion cells. Although rod photoreceptor loss and ribbon synapse alterations were only partially improved, overall retinal organization and neuronal survival were substantially preserved in PACAP38-treated diabetic animals. These findings demonstrate that topical PACAP38 administration exerts broad neuroprotective effects across multiple retinal layers and may support the preservation of vertical signal transmission in T2DR, highlighting its therapeutic potential in diabetic retinal neurodegeneration. Retinal function was not assessed in the present study; the conclusions presented here are therefore based on structural and marker-based evidence.

items.title: Characterisation of a nursery site for reef manta rays Mobula alfredi at Maamunagau Lagoon, Maldives.
items.abstract: Nursery areas are critical habitats for early life stages of many marine species, yet few have been identified for reef manta rays Mobula alfredi, despite their vulnerable conservation status. The Maldives Archipelago supports the world's largest known population of M. alfredi, but no nursery area has previously been characterised. We evaluated whether the Maamunagau Lagoon (MMGL), Raa Atoll meets three elasmobranch nursery criteria: (1) young-of-the-year (YoY; disc width ≤2000 mm) and juveniles are encountered more frequently than elsewhere, (2) they remain for extended periods and (3) the area is used repeatedly across years. From 2019 to 2022, photo-identification and stereo-video photogrammetry (SVP) quantified YoY and juvenile relative abundance, residency and site fidelity at MMGL and 10 other aggregation sites in Raa Atoll. Overall, 2786 sightings of 354 individual M. alfredi were documented, and 292 SVP size measurements were obtained from 105 individuals. Sightings per unit effort (SPUE, sightings per survey day) were significantly higher at Inner MMGL for juveniles (4.11 ± 0.11) and YoY (0.78 ± 0.05) than at all other sites (p < 0.001). Across the study period, YoY showed higher seasonal residency indices ( SRImin ) at Inner MMGL (11.9% ± 1.2%) than at Fringing MMGL (4.1 ± 0.6%) and all regional sites (7.9% ± 1.4%). Multi-year site fidelity was evident, with 88.1% of YoY resighted beyond their initial identification season, and some individuals recorded for four consecutive seasons. These findings make Inner MMGL the first documented nursery area for M. alfredi in the Maldives and therefore a priority site for conservation evaluation.

items.title: Precision Nutrition: Integrating Gut Microbiome, Multi-Omics, Artificial Intelligence and Digital Approaches for Personalized Dietary Interventions.
items.abstract: Precision nutrition is transforming nutritional science by replacing population-based dietary recommendations with individualized dietary strategies tailored to genetic, microbial, metabolic, and lifestyle variability. Advances in gut microbiome research, multi-omics technologies, including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and epigenomics, and artificial intelligence (AI) have created unprecedented opportunities to predict individual responses to diet and optimize metabolic health. This review provides an integrated overview of precision nutrition, emphasizing nutrient-gene interactions, gut microbiome dynamics, immune modulation, multi-omics approaches, and AI-driven predictive models that collectively support personalized dietary interventions. Furthermore, AI-based algorithms integrate multidimensional biological, clinical, lifestyle, and wearable sensor data to enable dynamic, real-time nutritional recommendations. The review also critically discusses the major translational challenges limiting clinical implementation, including biomarker validation, data harmonization, interoperability, explainable AI, reproducibility, ethical and regulatory issues, and equitable access to precision nutrition technologies. Finally, emerging concepts such as digital twins, adaptive nutrition algorithms, systems biology, and real-time metabolic monitoring are highlighted as promising strategies for advancing predictive, preventive, and personalized nutrition. By integrating molecular biology, microbiome science, multi-omics technologies, and digital health approaches, this review provides a comprehensive framework for accelerating the translation of precision nutrition from research to clinical practice.

items.title: Development of Rubus hirsutus as a woody-plant model system.
items.abstract: Model systems for long-lived woody plants are urgently needed to accelerate research in plant, evolutionary, and synthetic biology. Ideal model systems should combine well-annotated genomes with robust, user-friendly transformation and genome-editing platforms, as well as efficient strategies for multigene pyramiding. Here, we established a model system based on the woody shrub hirsute raspberry (Rubus hirsutus). First, we de novo assembled two telomere-to-telomere (T2T) Rosoideae genomes. Transcriptomic and pan-genomic analyses revealed extensive gene-level and genome-level diversification within these Rosoideae genomes, underpinning remarkable phenotypic variation across hundreds of wild species and thousands of cultivars. We then developed a leaf-based, tissue-culture-free, antibiotic-free transformation method and an Agrobacterium rhizogenes-mediated gene editing approach for R. hirsutus. We used these methods to establish an efficient sequential transformation strategy for multigene pyramiding and also generated early-flowering transgenic lines of R. hirsutus. Using our newly designed system, we rapidly and stably transformed R. hirsutus with approximately 500 genes and functionally characterized a series of genes and regulatory networks. This de novo-designed, long-lived woody-plant model system, which was derived from phylogenetically close but taxonomically diverse lineages, should greatly accelerate the advancement of our fundamental knowledge and advance translational research in plants.

items.title: Between Dependence and Participation: Medication Decision-Making Experiences Among Older Adults With Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity in the Chinese Healthcare Context.
items.abstract: Objective To explore factors influencing patient participation in medication decision-making among older adults with cardiovascular and metabolic multimorbidity, framed by the Health Ecology Model. Design Qualitative descriptive study. Methods Purposive sampling was used to recruit older adults with cardiometabolic multimorbidity from the cardiology department of a tertiary hospital in Guangzhou, between January and July 2026. Semi-structured interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. Data were analysed using thematic analysis. Results The findings were categorised into five dimensions of the Health Ecology Model: (1) Personal characteristics: medication knowledge limitations and reliance on medical authority; balancing medication burden against perceived necessity. (2) Behavioural characteristics: problem-triggered communication as a pattern of limited participation; experience-based independent medication decision-making. (3) Interpersonal network: doctor-patient trust and familiarity facilitating medication communication; the dual role of family members in medication decision-making participation; peer experience as an aid to decision-making. (4) Living and working conditions: financial concerns and disease risk perception in medication decision-making; medication access convenience and direct communication opportunities. (5) Policy environment level: health insurance reimbursement and perceived limitations of primary healthcare services. Conclusion Older adults with cardiometabolic multimorbidity demonstrate passive participation and heavy reliance on medical instructions, shaped by interacting factors across individual, interpersonal and system levels-including disease and medication literacy, health information access, risk perception, provider relationships, family support, financial burden and trust in primary care. Impact These findings provide clinicians and nurses in hospital and primary care settings with evidence to develop tailored health education and communication strategies that support shared decision-making and promote proactive health behaviours in this population. Patient or public contribution This study did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct or reporting. Reporting method COREQ (Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research).

items.title: Body fat optimizes rodent survival in a stochastic dryland ecosystem.
items.abstract: Climate change is rapidly altering the timing, quantity and variability of precipitation in dryland ecosystems with direct effects on the composition and abundance of primary producer and consumer communities. However, the causal mechanisms linking primary productivity to animal survival are rarely studied. Dryland ecosystems are highly sensitive to climate change, with pronounced declines in primary production and increasing variability in plant community composition. Specifically, variation in rainfall creates resource landscapes that differ in primary producer abundance, composition and nutritional quality, and consumers respond to these altered resource landscapes with changes in diet, body condition and ultimately survival. Dryland ecosystems therefore provide a natural context for testing the causal pathways linking climate-driven variation in primary productivity to changes in consumer diets, body condition and survival. We combined 10 years of longitudinal data on precipitation and plant biomass with paired measurements of individual diet and percent body fat from a community of granivorous desert rodents (Heteromyidae) using structural equation modelling to untangle the pathway(s) linking seasonal climate variation to consumer body fat. We then used Cormack-Jolly-Seber models to quantify the effects of percent body fat on apparent survival as a measure of individual fitness. We observed contrasting resource pathways between C 3 and C 4 primary producers: C 3 plant growth was influenced by season and precipitation, while C 4 plant growth was mediated primarily by precipitation. Consistent with predictions, rodents that consumed higher quality C 3 plants stored more body fat, but the link between body fat and survival varied among taxa as kangaroo rat survival decreased beyond a threshold of ~6%-7% body fat, while pocket mice exhibited no relationship. These findings illustrate that climate-mediated resource composition and abundance modulate diet by consumers, and our models reveal a direct pathway linking body condition to diet and the consumption of high-quality C 3 resources. Further, we show that body condition does not linearly increase survival, likely due to differences in life-history traits such as caching behaviour and mode of locomotion. Collectively, these results emphasize that individual survival likely emerges from interactions between resource landscapes, diet and consumer physiology.

items.title: Predators and wildlife management shape local-scale nutrient heterogeneity by altering carcass deposition rates.
items.abstract: Large-mammal carcasses create spatially concentrated nutrient pulses that increase environmental heterogeneity and promote biodiversity. Both predators and humans can alter the rate of large-animal carcass availability through mortality events or offsite removal. However, it is not well understood how these processes interact with wildlife population dynamics to influence nutrient heterogeneity across scales. Here, we compiled data on the difference in concentration of nitrogen (N) and 15 N-isotopes in plants growing on and off 201 large-mammal carcass sites as a proxy for how long nutrient signals persist after carcass deposition for different-sized animals. Our dataset was derived from four continents, spanned body masses 10-4000 kg and extended from 0 to 12 years after the carcass was deposited. We used Generalised Additive Mixed Models and integrated the resulting predictions of carcass-derived nutrient elevation and persistence into an agent-based model (ABM) that simulates the population turnover of large-herbivore species. Our empirical results reveal that both %N and δ 15 N signals in plants peaked after 2 years before declining to background levels within 4-8 years. While the absence of long-term measurements for the largest-bodied carcasses precluded us from assessing the expectation that elevated nutrient signals persisted for longer at these sites, our results confirm that the magnitude of the nutrient peak increases with body mass. ABM simulations revealed that predation and wildlife management interacted dynamically with ungulate density-dependent processes to determine carcass deposition rates. Maximum carcass deposition rates peaked at mid-levels of predation or culling and were lower at high mortality (due to lower ungulate density) and low mortality (due to slower population turnover). Carcass deposition rate and size were positively related to increased plant nutrient heterogeneity at the local scale but did not significantly alter plant heterogeneity at the landscape scale. Synthesis: Carcass-mediated nutrient heterogeneity emerges from the interaction between individual carcass characteristics and population-level mortality processes. Predators and wildlife management can therefore indirectly shape nutrient redistribution by altering both herbivore population dynamics and the rate at which carcasses enter ecosystems. Wildlife managers should engage with carcass deposition processes holistically to promote fine-scale nutrient heterogeneity and associated biodiversity.

items.title: Imported Melioidosis in Japan: Clinical Spectrum, Diagnostic Delays, Misidentification, and Laboratory Biosafety Risks.
items.abstract: Introduction Melioidosis, caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, is potentially fatal but rare in Japan. In non-endemic areas, detection and management are complicated by under-recognition, heterogeneous clinical presentation, delayed diagnosis, and misidentification. Methods We reviewed patients diagnosed with melioidosis at Saitama Medical Center, Saitama Medical University, from 2017 to 2025 and searched PubMed and Ichushi-Web for cases reported in Japan from 1990 to 2025. We extracted epidemiological, clinical, microbiological, treatment, and outcome data from all included cases. Results A total of 23 cases were included in the overall analysis, comprising 21 cases identified through the literature review and two institutional cases. All patients were male, with reported ages ranging from the 30s to 75 years, and diabetes mellitus was the predominant comorbidity. Clinical presentations ranged from acute disease to prolonged or relapsing courses and included pneumonia, abscesses, osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, infectious aneurysm, and lymphadenitis. Specific environmental exposures were often undocumented. The interval from symptom onset to microbiological diagnosis ranged from two days to approximately 22 months, and effective antimicrobial therapy was substantially delayed in some cases. Four patients experienced relapse, generally after insufficient treatment or inadequate eradication therapy. Misidentification or incomplete species-level identification occurred in five cases, particularly with matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry. Conclusions These findings suggest under-recognition of melioidosis in Japan, substantial diagnostic errors, and a risk of unrecognized laboratory exposure. Detailed travel and exposure histories, prompt effective therapy, adequate eradication therapy, careful interpretation of microbiological results, and clinician-laboratory communication are essential.

items.title: Contamination, Fish Bioaccumulation and Hazard Prioritization of Organophosphate Esters in the Yangtze River.
items.abstract: Despite mounting evidence of organophosphate esters (OPEs) contamination, ecotoxicological risk assessment remains severely hampered by the scarcity of biota exposure data in the Yangtze River. This study examined 23 target OPEs in surface water, sediment, and 27 wild fish species from the Yangtze River mainstream. OPEs were ubiquitously detected with total concentrations ranging from 9.07 to 189.99 ng/L in surface water, 0.001 to 45.63 μg/g dry weight (dw) in sediment, and 7.18 to 105.58 μg/g dw in wild fish. This study first reported the occurrence of three novel OPEs (N-OPEs), including RBDPP, TIPPP, and TBPP in surface water, and the ubiquitous occurrence of N-OPEs in the wild fish species. The liver exhibited the highest OPE accumulation, followed by intestine, brain, gonad, and muscle. Log K OW showed linear correlations with log bioaccumulation factors (BAFs), whereas non-linear relationships were observed with log biota-sediment accumulation factors (BSAFs) and trophic magnification factors (TMFs). The Toxicological Priority Index (ToxPi) scheme further identified 14 OPEs as posing high-priority ecological risks to wild fish. Among these, an N-OPE, Cresyl diphenyl phosphate (CDP) ranked the highest, underscoring it as the current primary compound of concern. Our study systematically characterized the environmental occurrence, bioaccumulation, and biomagnification potential of OPEs in wild fish from the Yangtze River. These findings establish a scientific rationale for prioritizing specific OPE congeners in future ecotoxicological investigations.

items.title: Redox conditions and free iron oxides jointly govern soil cadmium mobility during long-term organic fertilizer decomposition.
items.abstract: Organic fertilizer is widely used to mitigate cadmium (Cd) contamination in agricultural soils; however, its long-term effectiveness remains inconsistent among different soil types. To elucidate these contrasting responses, a 252-day incubation experiment was conducted using two typically Cd-contaminated soils (brown and paddy soils) amended with pig organic fertilizer under aerobic and flooded conditions. Temporal variations in acid-extractable Cd, aqueous Cd (aqCd), acid-extractable Fe, aqueous Fe (aqFe), and Fe oxide fractions were monitored, and the key regulators of aqCd were identified using XGBoost and SHAP analyses. Organic fertilizer decreased acid-extractable Cd under flooded conditions by 3.6%-18.8% in brown soil and 6.3%-25.2% in paddy soil, whereas under aerobic conditions it increased aqCd by 1.5%-154.6% and 1.3%-171.8%, respectively. Under flooding, its effects on aqCd differed markedly between soils, decreasing it by 12.4%-64.4% in brown soil but increasing it by 11.4%-153.8% in paddy soil. Notably, acid-extractable Fe was predominantly negatively correlated with acid-extractable Cd in the brown soil but positively correlated in the paddy soil, highlighting that Fe-mediated Cd mobility is governed by soil physicochemical properties. XGBoost-SHAP analysis identified amorphous Fe oxide content and soil acid-extractable Cd as the dominant predictors of aqCd. Importantly, a critical amorphous Fe oxide threshold of approximately 11.1 g/kg was identified. These findings demonstrate that the long-term effects of organic fertilizer on Cd mobility are jointly governed by dissolved organic carbon dynamics, Fe transformation, and soil Cd activity, and provide a reference quantitative threshold for predicting Cd mobility in contaminated agricultural soils.

items.title: Wild Crested Ibis Nipponia nippon became less fearful of humans during and after COVID-19 restrictions in the Hanzhong Basin, China.
items.abstract: The global outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2019 led many countries to implement lockdown policies, providing a unique opportunity to study the behavioral response mechanisms of animals to human activity disturbances. The Crested Ibis Nipponia nippon is an Endangered wetland bird in the Hanzhong Basin, China, which depends on coexistence with people. We measured alert distance (AD) and flight initiation distance (FID) of wild ibises before the pandemic (2013, n = 100; 2018, n = 21), during the 2021 lockdown (n = 42) and after restrictions were eased (2023, n = 50; 2025, n = 82), giving 295 records. FID did not differ between the two pre-pandemic years (P = 0.47), was 19% shorter during the pandemic (ratio 0.81, P = 0.007) and a further 17% shorter after reopening (ratio 0.83, P = 0.007), so post-pandemic FID was 33% shorter than before it (ratio 0.67, P < 0.001). AD declined in the same direction but not reliably during the pandemic (-7%, P = 0.103), falling clearly only after reopening (ratio 0.75, P < 0.001). Both distances increased with starting distance and distance to the nearest road and decreased with flock size, as economic escape theory predicts. Because local human activity did not explain the change, the shorter FID is best interpreted as increased tolerance rather than a response to the immediate density of people. This finding can provide an important case study for understanding the behavioral adaptation strategies of wildlife under sudden public events.

items.title: Discovery of antifeedant diterpenoids from Euphorbia helioscopia via an integrated mass strategy.
items.abstract: The widespread application of synthetic agrochemicals has raised growing concerns over resistance and environmental residues, driving renewed interest in plant-derived defensive metabolites. Diterpenoids, characterized by their extensive structural diversity and versatile ecological functions, are particularly attractive as natural modulators of insect behavior. Euphorbia helioscopia, a medicinal plant rich in terpenoid constituents, has long been recognized for its bioactive secondary metabolites; nevertheless, the full extent of its diterpenoid repertoire and associated chemical ecology remains insufficiently explored. In this study, an integrated mass spectrometry strategy, combining GNPS-based molecular networking with SIRIUS-assisted structural annotation, was established to systematically profile and guide the targeted isolation of diterpenoids from this species. Using two known diterpenoids as chemical probes, twenty compounds were obtained, including two previously undescribed compounds (1 and 2), whose structures were unequivocally elucidated by comprehensive NMR, HRESIMS, and ECD analyses. Owing to the limited availability of compound 2, its precursor 10 was subjected to TFA-mediated rearrangement, successfully converting it to compounds 2 and 3 in isolated yields of 18.6% and 34.6%, respectively, thereby securing sufficient quantities for subsequent evaluation. In the antifeedant assay against Helicoverpa armigera larvae, compound 4 exhibited moderate deterrent activity at 200 μg/mL, with a non-selective deterrence rate of 67.35% ± 4.62% at 24 h. Additionally, the AFC 50 value of compound 4 was 16.89 μg/mL, whereas the positive control azadirachtin had an AFC 50 of 5.472 μg/mL (95% CI: 0.3786-11.34 μg/mL). Overall, this study demonstrates that the integrated MS-based strategy is effective for uncovering the diterpenoid diversity in the n-BuOH of E. helioscopia, and the resulting compound set provides a solid chemical basis for subsequent ecological or pharmacological investigations.

items.title: Fernando de Noronha oceanic archipelago as sentinel site for transboundary marine litter in the tropical Atlantic.
items.abstract: Transboundary marine litter (TML) is an increasing global threat to marine and coastal environments. Oceanic archipelagos are particularly valuable for TML monitoring because of their capacity to accumulate floating debris. This study aimed to analyze the provenance of TML and improve potential source attribution on windward beaches of the Fernando de Noronha Archipelago (FNA), a UNESCO World Heritage Site and tourist destination. We combined brand auditing to assess product provenance and potential source regions with backtracking drift simulations to identify possible pathways. A total of 1595 plastic items were collected from three windward sites during a beach clean-up event in September 2025. The classification identified that beverage bottle caps and non-beverage caps accounted for 99.7% of all items. Brand auditing identified the provenance of 59.1% of items, of which 99.8% corresponded to brands neither manufactured nor marketed in Brazil. A total of 49 brands associated with 18 countries across Africa, Asia, Europe, and North America were identified. Among attributable foreign-branded items, brands associated with the Democratic Republic of the Congo (81.5%) and Angola (12.5%) predominated. Backtracking simulations identified a plausible existence of a transatlantic plastic corridor, with westward advection of the South Equatorial Current potentially connecting the eastern tropical Atlantic and FNA. Moreover, our results suggest that FNA functions as both a sentinel and a sink for TML potentially transported between Africa and Brazil. These findings highlight the need for coordinated global mitigation strategies and international cooperation, as the potential sources of this pollution extend beyond national borders.

items.title: Integrating established and emerging tools to assess wildlife condition from the ground, up.
items.abstract: Metabolic energy links individual physiology to population-level dynamics, making wildlife body condition a cornerstone of conservation science. Emerging technologies, including unoccupied aircraft systems, make remote assessment of animal condition possible at unprecedented scales, and physiologically grounded validation is essential for strong inference. Here we examine the strengths and challenges of traditional and remote methods, using a comparative perspective that emphasizes both lipid and lean mass dynamics in evaluating wildlife health. We provide a framework that integrates complementary approaches to assess wildlife condition across diverse systems, matching emerging methods with the required physiological resolution, species characteristics, and temporal and spatial scales, while enhancing research ethics. Expanding capacity to track wildlife energetics from individuals to populations requires novel approaches and is vital for conservation in a changing world.

items.title: Cooperative Excited-State Regulation and Framework Reconstruction in Polymeric Carbon Nitride for Efficient Photocatalytic Performance.
items.abstract: Polymeric carbon nitride (C 3 N 4 ) is a promising photocatalyst for solar hydrogen production, yet its performance is fundamentally limited by strong excitonic effects and inefficient carrier utilization. Here, we combine carbon dots (CD)-mediated excited-state regulation with LiCl/KCl-induced transformation of melon-like C 3 N 4 into a K-containing poly(heptazine imide) (PHI)-like framework. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy reveals CD-derived species contribute to lower-energy excited-state configurations with charge-transfer-like character, while subsequent framework transformation markedly accelerates excited-state relaxation dynamics. The combined strategy reduces the exciton binding energy from 79.4 to 41.6 meV, while photovoltage and photoelectrochemical measurements indicate enhanced charge separation and interfacial extraction, with the surface photovoltage increasing from 38 to 170 mV. Consequently, the optimized PHI-like photocatalyst derived from the CD-containing precursor (CD/K-PHI) achieves a hydrogen evolution rate of 5357.1 µmol g -1 h -1 , approximately 40.6 times that of pristine melon-like C 3 N 4 and 4.4 times that of its CD-free counterpart (K-PHI). This work demonstrates that coupling excited-state regulation with framework reconstruction provides an effective route to overcome excitonic losses and improve carrier utilization in polymeric photocatalysts.

items.title: Akkermansia muciniphila-driven metabolic homeostasis in cross-organ communications and diseases.
items.abstract: Akkermansia muciniphila ( A. muciniphila ) has emerged as a next-generation probiotic with broad effects on host metabolic homeostasis and immune modulation via cross-organ communications. However, the effects of A. muciniphila are not uniformly beneficial and vary with strain, diet, microbial community, host state, and disease context. Therefore, A. muciniphila is better viewed as a context-dependent modulator of host physiology. This review provides an overview of how A. muciniphila adapts to the mucus niche and links the gut to peripheral metabolic organs by coordinating intestinal barrier function, hormone secretion and immune responses across the gut-brain, gut-pancreas, gut-liver, gut-adipose, and gut-muscle axes. We further explore the multifaceted mechanistic interactions between A. muciniphila and metabolic diseases and immune disorders, with a particular focus on its bioactive effectors ( i.e., outer membrane proteins, metabolites, secreted peptides and extracellular vesicles) in gut-centered inter-organ communication. We also assess how these actions contribute to therapeutic potential, controversies and limitations of precision interventions involving A. muciniphila in different disease contexts.

items.title: Bioactive metabolite fractions from Spodoptera litura-damaged wild mungbean leaves differentially affect insect growth and bacterial metabolic activity.
items.abstract: Background Wild mungbean produces a diverse array of specialized metabolites that may contribute to plant defense. The wild accession CQ3114 has been reported to exhibit resistance to feeding by Spodoptera litura and changed in its metabolite profile following herbivore damage. In this study, we further fractionated metabolites extracted from S. litura-damaged aerial tissues of CQ3114 and evaluated the biological functions of the resulting fractions in relation to insect resistance and plant-microbe interactions. Results Metabolite profiling of ethanol extracts revealed differences between S. litura-damaged and undamaged CQ3114 aerial tissues. Ethanol extracts from the damaged tissues were subsequently fractionated into three solvent fractions based on polarity: butanol (BuOH), methanol (MeOH), and hexane (Hex). The BuOH fraction exhibited the highest 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical-scavenging rate (%), followed by the MeOH and Hex fractions. When incorporated into an artificial diet, the BuOH fraction reduced S. litura larval weight gain by approximately 25%, whereas the MeOH fraction did not significantly affect larval growth despite exhibiting relatively high antioxidant capacity. Further separation of the BuOH fraction yielded nine subfractions. Among them, F7 reduced S. litura larval weight gain by approximately 25%. Metabolic activity of the crucifer pathogen Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris (Xcc) in the subfraction F7 treatment (1,280 ppm) was 1.7​, which was 22.7% lower than that in the mock treatment. In addition, the metabolic activity of the beneficial bacterium Rhodopseudomonas palustris RPPS3 in the subfraction (1280 and 640 ppm) was approximately 2.5- to 3.0-fold higher than the mock treatment. Notably, F7 did not show the highest total phenolic content or DPPH scavenging activity among the subfractions, suggesting that these antioxidant-related measurements were not directly associated with its biological activities. Furthermore, at an equivalent mass concentration, F7 reduced larval weight gain to a similar extent as the parent BuOH fraction, leaving its relative contribution to the overall insect-inhibitory activity of the BuOH fraction remains unclear. Conclusions This study identified bioactive metabolite fractions from S. litura-damaged wild mungbean leaves that exhibit multifunctional activities, including suppression of S. litura larval growth and differential effects on the metabolic activities of phytopathogenic and potentially beneficial bacteria.

items.title: Mycosporine-like amino acids as potential UV filters for the human cornea: a perspective.
items.abstract: Mycosporine-like amino acids (MAAs) are small, water-soluble metabolites found widely in marine organisms and recognized as efficient natural ultraviolet (UV)-absorbing compounds. Most MAAs exhibit absorption maxima between approximately 310 and 360 nm, providing strong absorption in the UVB and short-wavelength UVA range, and efficiently dissipate absorbed UV energy as heat. Related mycosporines were first identified in fungi, while MAAs are widespread in cyanobacteria and algae and have also been detected in marine animals, including numerous invertebrates and the ocular tissues of fish. Their favorable photophysical properties, together with reported antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, make MAAs promising candidates for biomimetic photoprotection. Although translation into dermatological applications remains limited by challenges in production, extraction, and formulation, their physicochemical properties may also support alternative biomedical applications, including corneal protection. The cornea is directly exposed to solar UV radiation and absorbs most incident UVB and part of the UVA spectrum, thereby protecting deeper ocular tissues while itself being susceptible to UV-induced damage. Excessive UV exposure can cause photokeratitis and induce oxidative stress and DNA damage, while chronic exposure is associated with ocular surface disorders. Current ocular UV protection relies mainly on exposure reduction and optical barriers such as sunglasses and UV-blocking contact lenses. In this perspective, we discuss the photophysical and photochemical properties of MAAs and their translational potential for ocular photoprotection and propose MAAs as biomimetic lead compounds for future transparent, biocompatible UV-protective strategies targeting the ocular surface.

items.title: Phenotypic characterization of dairy camels in Kenya: insights from farmer engagement, morphometric, and reproduction data under extensive management.
items.abstract: In the arid and semi-arid regions camels constitute a vital component of pastoral livelihoods, serving as a primary source of income and nutrition. Approximately 70% of camel milk is produced within extensive production systems for domestic and commercial purposes. A cross-sectional study was conducted in Northern Kenya where camel farming is commonly practiced. The study was executed in two phases. Phase I involved structured questionnaires administered to camel owners. Camel basic morphometrics and blood samples were also collected for later genotypic characterization. The sampled camels were breeding bulls and lactating cows. Phase II included a focus group discussion (FGD) whence study participants were recruited through stakeholder mapping. Qualitative and quantitative data was analyzed through Taguette and R studio software. The study revealed unexploited camel dairy industry potential in a country that is the global leader in camel milk production. The sampled farms kept the Somali breed, which has two sub-types, namely Hoor and Gelab. Height measurements revealed that the bull was significantly taller at shoulder height (7.08 feet) than the cow (6.64 feet) (p 15 years (p < 0.05). Deliberate efforts need to be inculcated in milk value addition and camel breeding to secure food security within sub-Saharan Africa. The current extensive management systems will in the future, prove unsustainable given the population growth projections.

items.title: Fluorine substitution induces unconventional decarboxylation in perfluorohexanoic acid: homolytic bond cleavage and radical products.
items.abstract: Context Perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA), a representative short-chain perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acid (PFCA), has been increasingly detected in various environmental matrices, posing potential ecological and health risks. Decarboxylation is a critical initial step in its degradation, yet the molecular-level mechanism by which fluorine substitution governs this process-particularly whether it alters the C-C bond cleavage pathway-remains unresolved. In this study, using density functional theory (DFT) calculations combined with constrained geometry scanning, Fukui function analysis, Mayer bond order calculations, atomic charge distribution analysis, topological analysis, and spin population analysis, we systematically investigated the decarboxylation mechanism of PFHxA with normal hexanoic acid (HxA) as a comparative system. Our results reveal that fluorine substitution creates a balanced electron-withdrawing environment at both termini of the C5-C6 bond, attenuating its polarity to approach that of a non-polar covalent bond. During dissociation, the C5-C6 bond in PFHxA exhibits an abrupt drop in bond order and a surge in spin population on the C6 atom at a critical bond length, indicating homolytic cleavage that yields radical products. In contrast, the polar C5-C6 bond in HxA undergoes heterolytic cleavage to form an ion pair. This study clarifies the mechanism by which fluorine substitution induces a switch in the decarboxylation pathway from heterolytic to homolytic cleavage via modulation of C-C bond polarity, providing a theoretical basis for understanding the environmental transformation pathways of short-chain PFCAs and designing rational degradation strategies. Methods All quantum chemical calculations were performed using DFT with the ωB97X-D functional and the Def2-TZVP basis set. Initial molecular structures were constructed using GaussView, and geometry optimizations were carried out with Gaussian 16 to obtain optimized configurations. Wavefunction analyses were conducted using Multiwfn. The constrained geometry scanning method, implemented via Gaussian 16, was employed to systematically elongate the target C-C bond length to track the bond dissociation pathway. Unrestricted (open-shell) DFT was applied once the C5-C6 bond was substantially elongated.

items.title: Preliminary psychometric properties of CancellationTools quantified process variables on the Bells Test and their relationship with experienced clinician ratings of search strategy.
items.abstract: Whilst the Bells test is a robust measure of unilateral spatial neglect, the order and spatial sequence of target cancellations also provide information about the organisation of visual search. CancellationTools provides automated measures of these aspects of search behaviour. The primary aim of the current study was to examine preliminary psychometric properties of several CancellationTools variables for the Bells test to assess their relationship to experienced clinician ratings of search strategy. Mean distance, standardised mean distance, standardised angle, best r and intersections rate were calculated for the Bells Test in a diverse neurological sample (n = 101) and a healthy Australian sample (n = 57). Ratings of cancellation path organisation were completed by two experienced clinicians. Construct validity, criterion validity and preliminary test-retest reliability and exploratory test operating characteristics were examined. Standardised angle and best r showed good construct (convergent) validity with clinician ratings. Standardised angle, best r and intersections rate showed good divergent validity when compared with outcome variables. Best r and intersections rate showed the strongest differentiation across clinician-rated search-strategy categories. Good preliminary test-retest reliability was demonstrated for best r (ICC = .79). Best r showed good apparent same-sample discrimination (AUC = .884) when classifying disorganised versus other clinician-rated search strategies. Best r showed the strongest correspondence with clinician-rated search organisation and the highest preliminary pooled temporal stability estimate. However, the sample-derived operating point of < .7 requires independent validation and should not be interpreted as a clinically applicable cut-off.

items.title: Development, expert consensus, and pilot feasibility of a school-integrated telehealth model for childhood epilepsy care in India.
items.abstract: Objective To develop, validate through expert consensus, and pilot-test the feasibility of Tele-ESSI (Tele-School Health-led Epilepsy Smart Schools in India), a school-integrated telehealth intervention for childhood epilepsy in resource-limited settings. Methods A multi-phase, mixed-methods intervention development study was conducted across three geographically diverse districts in India. Phase 1 comprised a stakeholder needs assessment through structured workshops, focus group discussions (FGDs), and semi-structured interviews. Phase 2 involved participatory co-design and intervention development, followed by Phase 3, which involved expert validation using a two-round modified Delphi process (consensus threshold: ≥80% agreement; interquartile range ≤1.0). Phase 4 comprised pilot feasibility testing in five purposively selected schools (n = 30 teachers). Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, and qualitative data underwent thematic analysis. Results Three stakeholder workshops (n = 364 participants), FGDs, and in-depth interviews identified system-level gaps in epilepsy literacy, seizure first-aid capacity, and school-healthcare coordination. The resulting Tele-ESSI model integrated three core components: (1) telephonic clinical decision support, (2) structured capacity building, and (3) a multilingual digital integration platform. Fourteen experts completed the modified Delphi process, achieving ≥80% consensus across all domains (mean ratings 8.3-8.8/9). Pilot testing demonstrated high feasibility (4.62 ± 0.30), acceptability (4.44 ± 0.33), usability (4.52 ± 0.38), perceived effectiveness (4.38 ± 0.43), and satisfaction (4.13 ± 0.57). FRAME-guided refinements improved training clarity and digital accessibility. Significance Schools remain underutilized platforms for epilepsy care in low- and middle-income countries, where fragmented health-education coordination contributes to delayed management, stigma, and educational disruption. Tele-ESSI is a stakeholder-informed, consensus-validated, and pilot-tested model that addresses these system-level gaps through integrated clinical support and capacity building within the school setting. Findings support progression to a large-scale effectiveness trial. If effective, the model offers a replicable, scalable, intersectoral framework adaptable to comparable resource-constrained settings.

items.title: In their own voices: exploring language barriers in mental health care among Mandarin Chinese-speaking service users and their supporters in Germany.
items.abstract: Background Individuals who prefer a language other than a country's official or commonly spoken one(s) often encounter various barriers when accessing mental healthcare services. This study aimed to explore the experiences of first-generation Mandarin Chinese-speaking migrant service users in Germany, focusing on language-related challenges and their attitudes toward various strategies for overcoming them, including using qualified interpreters, informal interpreters (i.e., multilingual (mental) healthcare personnel or relatives/friends), and technological tools. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 Mandarin Chinese-speaking service users (SUs) and three supporters (SuPs) (i.e., individuals who help service users access mental healthcare services). The interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analyzed using a structuring qualitative content analysis approach, combining inductive and deductive coding. Results Participants were predominantly female (n = 8 female SUs, n = 3 female SuPs) and young (M SU = 30 years and M SuP = 29). Among the SUs, all were highly educated (i.e., Bachelor's degree or higher) and had an average length of residence in Germany of 5 years. Service users reported that language disparities and communicating in a different language than their first language led to cognitive challenges, such as the pressure of processing emotions while translating and a tendency to overthink. Feelings of being ignored and difficulties clarifying uncertainties hindered the development of a trusting therapeutic relationship. Additionally, cultural (e.g., stress of explaining cultural contexts) and structural barriers (e.g., difficulties in navigating the local healthcare system and limited therapist availability) further compounded the challenges. However, multilingual interactions with their mental healthcare providers also brought several benefits, including improved communication competence. General concerns were raised regarding the presence of a third party in a therapy setting, e.g., extended session durations and potential information loss. Specific concerns and advantages were expressed regarding the use of qualified interpreters (e.g., balancing empathy and neutrality), informal interpreters such as relatives or friends (e.g., emotional support and confidentiality issues) and technological tools (e.g., emotional nuance challenges and feeling less judged due to their objectivity and neutrality). Conclusion This study provides insights into the variety and complexity of language-related and cultural challenges Mandarin Chinese-speaking migrants face when accessing mental healthcare in Germany and highlights the importance of flexible and person-centered approaches to deal with language barriers, including increased accessibility and utilization of qualified interpreters. However, most participants in this study were female, young and highly educated. Future studies should include more diverse Mandarin Chinese-speaking migrants, e.g., in terms of age, gender, educational background and years of residency.

items.title: Maternal gestational diabetes mellitus and depression at 5 years postpartum.
items.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with a higher risk of maternal depression across the first postpartum year. However, whether this association persists remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the links between GDM and depressive symptoms at 5 years postpartum. We used data from 384 participants from the prospective pre-birth Gen3G cohort (Canada). We defined GDM according to international diagnostic criteria, based on a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test in the second trimester of pregnancy. We assessed glucose/insulin values as additional predictors. Among 384 participants, 38 had GDM in the second trimester of pregnancy. At 5 years, participants self-reported depressive symptoms using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale. Regression analyses examined associations between GDM and metabolic markers and depressive symptoms adjusting for demographic/lifestyle factors. We did not find evidence of associations between GDM and depressive symptoms at 5 years postpartum, albeit limited by our number of GDM cases.

items.title: Health-related beliefs scale for restrained eating among Chinese female college students: Development, reliability and validity.
items.abstract: This study developed and initially evaluated the Health-Related Beliefs Scale for Restrained Eating (HRBS-RE) among Chinese female college students, grounded in Health Belief Model. Cross-sectional data from 400 participants were used for psychometric evaluation. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a 25-item, five-factor structure encompassing perceived susceptibility, severity, benefits, barriers, and self-efficacy, with good model fit. The five subscales demonstrated satisfactory convergent validity, with average variance extracted values exceeding 0.50, and satisfactory discriminant validity. Cronbach's α coefficients ranged from 0.871 to 0.888, and subscale scores correlated significantly with Dutch Eating Behavior Questionnaire restrained eating scores ( r = 0.365-0.461), providing concurrent validity evidence. Overall, the findings provide preliminary psychometric evidence supporting the use of the HRBS-RE as a research instrument for assessing multidimensional health-related beliefs about restrained eating. The five subscales should be interpreted separately, and further validation in independent and more diverse samples is required.

items.title: EXPRESS: Judgments of Learning can Reactively Improve Lineup Identification in a Mock Theft Scenario.
items.abstract: Judgments of Learning (JOLs) can reactively improve recognition of single words and cue-target pairs. However, it remains unclear whether this effect is limited to lexical stimuli or extends to other types of study materials. We explored this possibility by testing whether JOLs would enhance lineup identification accuracy in an eyewitness memory paradigm. Participants viewed a brief mock theft video, and following the video presentation, some participants were asked to provide two JOLs predicting their ability to both identify the culprit in a target-present lineup and reject a target-absent lineup. All participants then completed a simultaneous lineup test, which was either target-present or target-absent. Compared to the no-JOL control group, participants who made JOLs were more likely to select the culprit in target-present lineups, though this increased accuracy did not extend to target-absent lineups. ROC analyses suggested that this pattern may have reflected improved discrimination for participants who made JOLs relative to the control group. Taken together, our findings suggest that JOLs can reactively improve recognition of non-lexical stimuli and suggest that a brief metacognitive prompt administered following an event may enhance eyewitness identification.

items.title: Exploring the potential interplay between pitch and loudness in the SMARC effect: A registered report.
items.abstract: The Spatial-Musical Association of Response Codes (SMARC) effect provides evidence of spatial associations for both pitch and loudness, with faster left/bottom responses to low pitch and low loudness, and faster right/top responses to high pitch and high loudness. Since previous studies suggest that pitch and loudness interact at a perceptual level but appear to be represented independently in tasks investigating their spatial associations, this study aimed to further explore their potential interaction within a vertical response setting in a SMARC task. Across two conditions, we presented the following combinations of stimuli: low pitch/low loudness, low pitch/high loudness, high pitch/low loudness, and high pitch/high loudness. In the first condition, we conducted a pitch-judgment task in which participants were required to judge pitch while ignoring loudness. In the second condition, we conducted a loudness-judgment task in which participants were required to judge loudness while ignoring pitch. We hypothesized that if pitch and loudness were independent, distinct SMARC effects would emerge for both. Conversely, if they interacted, we expected faster responses for compatible stimuli (low pitch/low loudness, high pitch/high loudness). The results, collected from two independent samples (University of Trieste and University of Padova), revealed a significant interaction between pitch and loudness, demonstrating that they interact during processing leading to spatial responses. Responses were fastest when the spatial response was congruent with both acoustic dimensions simultaneously, whereas conflicting acoustic features slowed down overall processing speed. Overall, these findings demonstrate that spatial-auditory associations are modulated by task demands.

items.title: Emotional challenges and coping strategies in the transition to fatherhood: perspectives of new fathers and health professionals: a qualitative study.
items.abstract: Fathers' needs are often overlooked in perinatal care. This study explored the emotional, practical, and relational challenges of transitioning to fatherhood and identified opportunities for digital support.We interviewed expectant and new fathers and health professionals working in perinatal care. Fathers discussed their emotional experiences, daily challenges, coping strategies, and interactions with healthcare services. Health professionals described existing support and gaps in care. We used thematic analysis to identify patterns across both groups. Fathers described worry, anxiety, frustration, and helplessness associated with sleep deprivation, changing relationships, work pressures, and uncertainty about caregiving. Many felt excluded from antenatal education and unsure how to support a partner experiencing emotional distress. Mother-centred care, limited involvement in appointments, and stigma around expressing emotions made it harder for fathers to seek help. Health professionals identified gaps in support and opportunities to involve fathers more actively in perinatal care.Fathers wanted to be involved and confident in caregiving, yet uncertainty about their role, exclusion from care, and social expectations that discourage vulnerability shaped their experiences of distress. The findings highlight the need for father-inclusive perinatal care and accessible digital tools that offer practical guidance, emotional support, and opportunities for connection. Further research with more diverse groups of fathers could inform the development of equitable and responsive interventions.

items.title: Stress-Induced Astrocytic ABCA1 Deficiency Caused Cholesterol Accumulation to Promote Synaptic Dysregulation and Behavioral Abnormalities.
items.abstract: Astrocytes supply cholesterol to neurons to support synaptic function, but how chronic stress disrupts this metabolic interaction remains unclear. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed reduced ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1) expression in hippocampal astrocytes of mice exposed to chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). Chronic stress was also associated with reduced astrocytic liver X receptor (LXR) protein, cholesterol accumulation, inflammatory astrocyte reactivity, impaired dorsal Cornu Ammonis 1 (CA1) synaptic transmission and neuronal excitability, and depression-like behaviors. Astrocyte-targeted ABCA1 overexpression ameliorated these metabolic, inflammatory, electrophysiological, and behavioral disorders. Conversely, astrocytic LXRα/β knockdown or pharmacological LXR inhibition reduced ABCA1 expression and reproduced key stress-associated phenotypes. Restoring ABCA1 expression substantially reversed the abnormalities induced by astrocytic LXRα/β knockdown, supporting ABCA1 as an important functional mediator of LXR-associated dysfunction. Pharmacological LXR activation and cyclodextrin-mediated cholesterol reduction produced complementary improvements. Together, these findings identify impaired cholesterol handling in in dorsal CA1 astrocytes as a mechanistic link connecting chronic stress, neuroinflammation, and neuronal dysfunction, suggest that restoring astrocytic cholesterol homeostasis may mitigate depression-related pathology.

items.title: The psychometric applicability of the Chinese version of the childhood autism rating scale, second edition (CARS2) in Taiwanese autistic children.
items.abstract: Accurate assessment of autism characteristics is crucial for both clinical practice and research. Although several autism-related measures have been validated in Taiwan, the psychometric properties of the Chinese version of the Childhood Autism Rating Scale, Second Edition (CARS2) have not yet been fully evaluated. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the reliability and validity of the CARS2 in Taiwanese autistic children. A total of 137 autistic children aged 3 to 12 years (mean = 6.32 ± 1.83 years) were assessed using either the CARS2 Standard Version (CARS2-ST) or High-Functioning Version (CARS2-HF), along with the Social Responsiveness Scale™, Second Edition (SRS™-2) and the Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales (VABS) First or Third Editions. The internal consistency for the CARS2-ST and CARS2-HF was good (α = 0.87 and 0.81, respectively). Convergent validity was supported by moderate to strong correlations between CARS2 scores and the SRS™-2 5-factor scores (r = 0.51-0.69, p < 0.001) and the SRS™-2 4-factor scores (r = 0.41-0.72, p < 0.001), as well as negative correlations with the VABS communication, socialization and motor domains (r = -0.72 to -0.44, p < 0.001). Responsiveness analyses among a subsample (n = 21) indicated borderline to significant reductions in CARS2-ST scores after intervention (Z = -3.50, p < 0.001), with medium effect sizes (Cliff's δ = -0.41). The findings support the use of the CARS2 as a culturally appropriate instrument with good internal consistency, construct validity, and responsiveness for assessing autism characteristics in Taiwanese children.

items.title: Statewide Stimulant Dispensing Trends 2014-2022: Rising Initiation Among Adults and Females.
items.abstract: Background Prescription stimulant dispensing in the United States has increased substantially in recent years, raising questions about changing treatment patterns and potential public health implications, including nonmedical use, diversion, and stimulant use disorder. Identifying when dispensing trends shift and which populations experience the greatest changes can help characterize evolving prescribing patterns and inform further research. Methods We conducted a repeated cross-sectional surveillance of Oregon Prescription Drug Monitoring Program data from 2014-2022. Annual rates of stimulant dispensing and treatment initiation (defined as no prescription stimulant dispensed in the preceding 12 months) were calculated per 1000 residents and stratified by age, sex, and medication type. Joinpoint regression was used to identify changes in dispensing trends over time. Results Between 2014 and 2022, 8.5 million stimulant prescriptions were dispensed to 423,235 million unique individuals. The rate of stimulant dispensing increased 75%, from 183 to 320 prescriptions per 1000 residents. The largest increases occurred among young adults aged 18-44 years and females. Joinpoint analysis identified an inflection point in 2020, with accelerated increases in stimulant dispensing and initiation, particularly among stimulant-naïve adults. Amphetamine formulations accounted for most of the observed growth, with additional increases in dexmethylphenidate and dextroamphetamin dispensing. Conclusions Prescription stimulant dispensing and initiation increased substantially in Oregon from 2014-2022, especially among young adults, female patients, and new users. Identifying these shifts provides a reference point for further investigation of changing treatment patterns and their potential clinical and public health implications.

items.title: Multiparty audience design is disrupted following moderate-severe traumatic brain injury: evidence of reduced spoken language adjustment.
items.abstract: Background Social communication impairments after traumatic brain injury (TBI) affect a range of skills required for effective conversation. We examined how adults with TBI adjust their communication when speaking to multiple communication partners with variable shared knowledge (multiparty audience design). Method 30 adults with moderate-severe TBI and 30 non-injured comparison (NC) participants played a referential communication game to assess multiparty audience design. In the Sorting phase, participants (the "Director"), described abstract images to two trained research assistant "Matchers" who sorted the same images in a matching order. They sorted the images four times, establishing shared labels for the images. In a later Test phase, we manipulated Matcher knowledge across three conditions: participants described the images again to groups of two Matchers who were either a) both knowledgeable about the image labels, b) both naïve, or c) mixed. We examined participants' adjustments in expression length, definite reference, and disfluency across Sorting phase rounds and Test phase conditions. Results In the Sorting phase, the TBI group showed reduced gains in referential efficiency over the four rounds of the game compared to non-injured peers. At Test phase, the TBI group significantly adjusted their spoken language for groups with one or more naïve listeners (i.e., longer expressions, more disfluencies, and fewer definite references), but the magnitude of these effects was significantly smaller than the NC group. Conclusions Participants with TBI showed reduced spoken language adjustment for multiparty audience design, potentially increasing risk for disruptions in navigating group communication in work, school, and interpersonal relationships.

items.title: Multimodal signals of multiparty audience design in moderate-severe traumatic brain injury: Divergent patterns in spoken language, gesture, and eye gaze.
items.abstract: Background Multiparty communication challenges speakers to adjust their messages for multiple addressees with varying knowledge levels. Such studies of multiparty audience design in both typical and clinical populations have narrowly focused on spoken language only. In the current study, we extend this analysis to examine how speakers with and without TBI adjust their gesture and eye gaze behaviors for multiparty audience design. Method 30 adults with moderate-severe TBI and 30 non-injured participants played a referential communication game with two Matchers. In the Sorting phase, they described abstract images repeatedly across four rounds. In a subsequent Test phase, participants described the images again to groups of two Matchers who were either both knowledgeable, both naïve, or mixed. We used video-based motion tracking to quantify adjustments in gesture form kinematics for groups of listeners with different levels of knowledge and manually annotated gaze events toward Matchers. Results Non-injured participants demonstrated a coordinated effort for multiparty audience design across modalities, maximizing the informativeness of their spoken and gestural descriptions and using gaze to monitor understanding in naïve and mixed group conditions. In contrast, despite showing reduced spoken language adjustment, participants with TBI showed preserved adjustment of kinematic features of gesture form and appropriately allocated gaze to naïve Matchers, signaling awareness of partner-specific knowledge representations. Participants with TBI produced gestures at significantly higher rates than non-injured peers. Conclusions The results highlight the importance of a multimodal approach to studying cognitive-communication disorders and new insights into cognitive mechanisms underlying disruptions to multiparty audience design.

items.title: The development of a "Cognitive Health Clinic" in a Canadian mental health hospital: Perceptions, needs, and recommendations of the clinical workforce prior to implementation.
items.abstract: Cognitive impairment is common in mental health disorders, yet access to cognitive assessment and intervention services remains scarce. This study evaluated the perceptions, needs, and recommendations of the clinical workforce towards a proposed specialized Cognitive Health Clinic (CHC) within a large mental health hospital. Using a cross-sectional design, an anonymous online survey examined views on the importance of cognitive health; interest in cognitive remediation (CR); helpfulness and utility of the CHC; and facilitators and barriers to implementation. A total of 149 responses were analyzed. Respondents reported that an average of 70.62% of their patients experience clinically significant cognitive difficulties. Although familiarity with CR was limited, interest in learning more was high (M =4.39/5). Respondents also rated the proposed CHC and its services as highly useful and identified several implementation facilitators and barriers related to education, logistics, referral processes, and clinic scope. We identified a clear perceived need for cognitive health services across diverse clinical populations. The findings also highlight a disconnect between recognition of cognitive health needs and familiarity with CR, reflecting an opportunity for education and implementation supports. Lessons learned about the CHC are discussed and may help the implementation of similar services.

items.title: Candidate Distress Phenotypes of Patients With Inherited Retinal Diseases.
items.abstract: Patients with inherited retinal diseases (IRDs) experience significant emotional distress, but their mental health remains both understudied and insufficiently addressed within the context of vision care. We aim to further understand the breadth and depth of the psychological state and needs of patients with IRDs. Fifty-two adults diagnosed with an IRD were recruited from the Retinal Dystrophy Clinic at the University of Michigan Kellogg Eye Center. Inclusion criteria required a genetic or phenotypic diagnosis in one of three IRD subtypes (macular dystrophy, rod-cone dystrophy, cone/cone-rod dystrophy). Consecutive sampling methodology was used. Michigan Vision Anxiety Questionnaire (MVAQ), Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9), Generalised Anxiety Disorder Assessment (GAD-7) and in-depth interview data were collected and analysed using cross-sectional psychometric and qualitative analysis. Study duration < 1 year. Participants reported elevated symptoms of depression, generalised anxiety and vision-specific anxiety, with small-to-moderate effect sizes compared to scale reference values. Vision-specific anxiety was moderately correlated with general emotional distress. Thematic analysis of interviews (n = 47) identified four candidate 'phenotypes of distress': future-oriented anxiety, loss and grief, overwhelmed/dysregulated and adaptive/high coping. The findings support the idea that vision distress is a partially independent dimension of psychological distress not fully captured by traditional depression and anxiety measures and the candidate phenotypes illustrate the varied ways individuals experience and manage distress related to vision loss. This study should inform future research building psychological interventions for patients with IRDs.

items.title: Assessment of Ankle Instability in Acute ATFL Tears using a Validated and Easy Ultrasound Technique.
items.abstract: To determine the value of clinical versus ultrasound stress testing in ankle sprains. All acute ankle sprain patients from 2015 to 2023 received threefold early and final clinical and ultrasound examinations, including stress testing, in a prospective cohort study. In 342 patients, ligament injuries were diagnosed by sonography: 192 (56.1%) ligamentous anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) tears, 111 (32.5%) osseous ATFL avulsions, 24 (7.0%) calcaneocuboid ligament tears, and 15 (4.4%) anterior tibiofibular ligament tears. Then, 117 patients with a complete ATFL tear were carefully further assessed with dynamic ultrasound. Hemarthros was found in 88.2%, and clinical tenderness at the ATFL in 89.1%. Clinical stress tests were only positive in 60.2%, but the talar shift of the injured side during stress ultrasound was Ø 3.9 mm (SD 0.19 mm), compared to 0.6 mm (SD 0.10 mm) on the uninjured side. Clinical accuracy compared to ultrasound stress testing was 66-70%, sensitivity 64-70%, and specificity 72-100%. Follow-up in 110 patients after 6 weeks of conservative treatment showed the talar shift of the injured side at 0.8 mm SD 0.95, indicating regained stability in 103 of 110 cases. Effusion/possibly hemarthros in sonography reliably indicates a ligament injury. Almost all ATFL tears exhibit instability, which clinical tests alone often fail to detect. The sonographic examination technique described here forms a practicable, immediate, nonpainful, measurable, validated, and reliable basis and yields sufficient accuracy to inform optimal therapeutic steps and ensure healing through regained stability. Ultrasound stability testing, therefore, should be implemented as the gold standard in the diagnostic process.

items.title: Exposure to a prenatal metal mixture and internalizing problems in preschool-aged children in the Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) cohort.
items.abstract: Internalizing problems, particularly anxiety and depressive disorders, are leading contributors to health burden worldwide. Emerging evidence suggests environmental chemicals, such as metals and metalloids, may play a role. We prospectively examined associations between prenatal exposure to a metal mixture [arsenic, cadmium, manganese, lead] and Child Behavior Checklist for Ages 1½-5 (CBCL/1½-5) outcomes [Total Problems, Internalizing Problems, Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5)-oriented scales for Depressive and Anxiety Problems] in N=1731 mother-child dyads from the United States Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes Cohort. Spot urine metal concentrations were measured by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry. We used Bayesian Kernel Machine Regression to examine associations between the metal mixture and each CBCL/1½-5 outcome. To explore sex differences, models were stratified by child sex. In the sample overall, higher exposure to the metal mixture predicted increased total problems, internalizing problems, and DSM-5 anxiety T-scores. We also observed greater likelihood of clinical-level DSM-5 depressive problems with greater exposure to the mixture. In stratified models, increased exposure to the metal mixture was associated with higher total, internalizing, and DSM-5 anxiety problem T-scores in females and with increased total and internalizing problem T-scores in males. The increased likelihood of clinical-level total problems, internalizing problems, DSM-5 depressive problems, and DSM-5 anxiety problems associated with greater exposure to the metal mixture was most strongly evident among females. These findings suggest that in utero metal exposures contribute to observed sexually dimorphic manifestations of internalizing problems.
