items.title: EMPODERA Intervention for Spanish-speaking Latino Caregivers of Critically Ill Oncology Patients: Cultural Adaptation Process.
items.abstract: Surrogate decision-makers of critically ill patients admitted to intensive care units (ICUs) often experience extreme psychological distress. For Spanish-speaking Latino caregivers, additional socioeconomic and healthcare challenges frequently compound their emotional suffering. The present study aimed to adapt the EMPOWER intervention to address the unique needs of Spanish-speaking Latino caregivers. Mixed-methods, approach to adapt the EMPOWER intervention to EMPODERA, guided by ecological validity and cultural adaptation process models. Spanish-speaking Latino caregivers of ICU patients (n=11), Latino critical care providers (n=7), and mental health providers who treat Latino caregivers (n=5) from one ICU at a comprehensive cancer center in New York City and professional networks across the U.S. and Latin America were recruited. The EMPOWER intervention (Enhancing & Mobilizing the POtential for Wellness & Emotional Resilience) is an ultra-brief intervention originally designed to improve coping and reduce distress in English-speaking surrogates. Analysis of the quantitative and qualitative findings suggest several adaptations including: (1) reduce stigma of assistance for mental health and provide educational materials promoting psychosocial care, (2) offer a resource booklet to address caregivers' social needs, (3) mitigate literacy issues using simple language and visual aids, and (4) include culturally-syntonic metaphors that resonate more effectively with the target audience. Our findings highlighted the significance of making key adaptations of EMPOWER. Feedback suggested the importance of clarifying definitions of concepts, using clear language, and incorporating values to align with Latino cultural values. Key informants also recommended supplementing the intervention with psychoeducational resources to address mental health stigma. Future research is needed to evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of EMPOWER for Latino caregivers.

items.title: Higher Shifting Ability Is Associated with Reduced Threat-Safety Differentiation During Fear Generalization.
items.abstract: Adaptive fear generalization is beneficial to help individuals efficiently cope with novel situations with potential threats based on previous knowledge in complex environments, while overgeneralization may lead to unnecessary fear responses to safe stimuli, increasing the susceptibility of some anxiety disorders. Previous studies have shown that the three core components of executive function - shifting, updating, and inhibition play an important role in fear processing. However, it remains unclear whether subcomponents of executive function modulate fear generalization or not. To fill this gap, a total of 80 participants were recruited to complete executive function and fear generalization tasks in this study. Specifically, the participants underwent three tasks assessing the three components of executive function, including shifting, updating, and inhibition. Subsequently, all participants completed fear learning and generalization tasks, and recorded their shock expectancy ratings, skin conductance response (SCR), and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) signals in the prefrontal region. We found that participants with high shifting ability showed reduced threat-safety differentiation and increased shock expectancy ratings to generalization stimuli(GS). During fear generalization, higher shifting ability was associated with lower oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO) responses in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. In contrast, updating and inhibition showed no comparable significant associations with behavioral fear generalization. Together, these findings highlight the distinct association of shifting ability with fear generalization behavior, accompanied by a localized prefrontal hemodynamic response.

items.title: Cognitive control in chronic mild and moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury: effects of injury severity and recent cannabis use.
items.abstract: Understanding effects of trauma severity on cognitive control and executive function following traumatic brain injury (TBI) is important for reliable evaluation of individual recovery trajectories. We report a study, in which we used a novel Working Memory Multimodal Attention Task (WM-MMAT) during fMRI to investigate cognitive control mechanisms in symptomatic adults with moderate-to-severe TBI (msTBI, n=38) and mild TBI (mTBI, n=37) in the chronic phase (>6 months post-injury), as well as in healthy controls (HC, n=41). 56% of the TBI participants reported using cannabis within the past 30 days. Our MRI data processing pipeline included an automatic identification of cortical lesions. Results showed significantly reduced task fMRI activity in both mTBI and msTBI patients, compared to HCs, in brain regions involved in motor control, visual attention, selective audio-visual attention, and verbal working memory. fMRI activities of those regions positively correlated with TBI patients' daily function according to the Glasgow Outcome Scale - Extended. When processing incongruent multisensory stimuli, mTBI and especially msTBI patients showed stronger engagement of cognitive control mechanisms than HCs, which reflected underlying cognitive deficits in TBI. When performing a 1-back task, msTBI patients, compared to HCs, demonstrated stronger recruitment of cognitive control processes related to working memory, while exhibiting cognitive and motor deficiencies overall. Both mTBI and msTBI patients showed significantly lower WM-MMAT task performance than HCs. These results reveal persistent cognitive impairments in chronic TBI that become more apparent as task difficulty increases and cannot be compensated through greater cognitive effort. Our fMRI findings also suggest that more frequent recent cannabis use among TBI patients may be associated with increased cognitive and motor deficits. Further investigation of the interplay between cognitive effects of TBI and those of cannabis exposure would be beneficial.

items.title: Directional dynamics of mental time travel: A Dynamic Causal Modeling study of past retrieval and future construction in early adulthood.
items.abstract: Mental time travel relies on a distributed network of brain regions, including the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC), hippocampus (HPC), and posteromedial cortex (PMC). Although the involvement of these regions is well documented, the directional interactions among selected network nodes as a function of temporal distance (near vs. far), temporal direction (past vs. future), and event domain (autobiographical memory vs. public events) remain poorly understood. We applied Dynamic Causal Modeling (DCM) to fMRI data from 23 healthy young adults performing a temporal-order judgment task on autobiographical and public events from four temporal periods (near/far and past/future), with response mappings compatible or non-compatible with a front-back mental timeline. For past autobiographical memories, Bayesian model comparison supported a predominantly vmPFC-to-HPC modulatory architecture. In the compatible condition, Bayesian model averaging revealed a distance-dependent change in the sign of this modulation, positive for recent and negative for remote memories, indicating increased and reduced coupling relative to the intrinsic connection, respectively. For future public events, model comparison strongly supported a direct vmPFC-to-HPC modulatory architecture, with positive modulation stronger for distant than near events and peaking for far-future non-compatible scenarios. No specific architecture received support for future autobiographical events. These findings indicate that effective connectivity among selected nodes of the broader mental time travel network varies with temporal distance and event domain. Autobiographical past and public future events show distinct patterns of prefrontal-hippocampal modulation, underscoring the importance of considering temporal context and representational demands when investigating the network dynamics of remembering and imagining.

items.title: Fear of amputation and death and quality of life in patients with intermittent claudication.
items.abstract: Intermittent claudication caused by peripheral artery disease (PAD) is associated with risk of major amputation and death, but it is unclear to what extent patients fear these complications and whether these fears influence quality of life (QoL) and risk of events. This study assessed the prevalence of fear of amputation and death amongst patients with intermittent claudication, and examined the association of these fears with QoL and risk of major amputation and death. In this prospective cohort study enrolling 354 patients, fear of amputation and death from PAD were assessed with two questionnaire items. Primary outcome was the combined incidence of major amputation and death. Secondary outcomes were disease-specific QoL assessed by PADQOL, mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Of the 354 patients, 202 (57.1%) either strongly agreed (76, 21.5%), agreed (67, 18.9%) or somewhat agreed (59, 16.7%) that they feared amputation. A total of 151 of the 354 patients (42.7%) indicated that they strongly agreed (50, 14.1%), agreed (35, 9.9%) or somewhat agreed (66, 18.6%) that they were afraid of dying because of PAD. Patients with higher scores for fear of amputation and death had significantly lower QoL scores. Median follow-up was 2.3 (interquartile range: 1.3, 7.0) years, during which time 60 (16.9%) deaths, 6 (1.7%) major amputations and 50 (14.1%) MACEs occurred. A one unit increase in the fear score was associated with an increased risk of both major amputation or death (unadjusted HR 1.11, 95% CI 1.02, 1.19, p=0.010; risk factor adjusted HR 1.10, 1.01, 1.19, p=0.027) and death alone (unadjusted HR 1.09, 95% CI 1.01, 1.18, p=0.029; risk factor adjusted HR 1.09, 1.00, 1.19, p=0.044), but not MACE. Among patients with intermittent claudication fear of amputation and death are common and associated with poorer QoL and increased risk of these events.

items.title: Disrupted Event Segmentation in Amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment: Everyday Memory and Entorhinal Correlates.
items.abstract: Event segmentation-the parsing of continuous experience into meaningful temporal units-supports everyday memory. Although prior research has examined event segmentation and memory in healthy aging and very mild dementia, it remains unclear whether explicit segmentation performance in neuropsychologically characterized amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) is differentially related to distinct components of episodic memory, including immediate and delayed memory for event gist and specific details, and how it relates to broader cognitive abilities and medial temporal lobe integrity. Healthy older adults (HOA) and individuals with aMCI viewed a naturalistic video, completed immediate memory tests, and performed explicit event segmentation during a second viewing. Structural MRI was available for a subset of participants. Compared with HOA, individuals with aMCI identified fewer event boundaries and showed lower agreement with a young-adult normative pattern. Segmentation agreement was associated with memory and working memory/executive composites in pooled analyses; within-group models were nonsignificant, and pooled associations may reflect group differences. After correction for multiple comparisons, lower segmentation agreement was associated with poorer one-day delayed detail recall in the aMCI group. Both groups showed better recognition of non-boundary than boundary objects, and better temporal order memory for across-event than within-event pairs. In the MRI subset, greater left entorhinal cortical thickness was associated with higher segmentation agreement, whereas hippocampal volume and parahippocampal cortical thickness were not. These findings identify altered explicit segmentation performance in aMCI and associations with broader cognitive functioning, delayed memory for event details, and entorhinal cortical integrity, although their causal organization remains unresolved.

items.title: Encoding-related fMRI BOLD activity predicts subsequent memory for studied scenes, but not subsequent identification of perceptually similar lures.
items.abstract: Pattern separation is widely regarded as a hippocampally mediated process that reduces interference between memories of similar experiences. Performance on the Mnemonic Similarity Task (MST), where the requirement is to discriminate between studied items (targets) and perceptually similar lures, is commonly held to depend on pattern separation. Specifically, it has been proposed that similar lure identification is supported by a recall-to-reject strategy, whereby lures are identified as such as a result of the retrieval of the corresponding studied item. According to this proposal, therefore, the encoding operations that support successful target recollection and successful lure identification should be closely similar, since both mnemonic judgments depend upon subsequent recollection of the study item. Here, using fMRI, we examined this prediction. In samples of cognitively healthy young and older adults, we employed a three-choice MST (target/lure/new) with scene and object images as test items. Using ROI-based univariate analyses, we assessed whether encoding-related activity was predictive of the identification of target and similar lure items on the subsequent memory test. The activity elicited by scene images predicted memory performance for subsequently presented targets but not for corresponding similar lures, arguably contrary to the recall-to-reject hypothesis. No effects could be identified for either class of object test items. The magnitude of the encoding effects for the scene targets was age-invariant, and, moreover, the scene SMEs demonstrated an age-invariant association with the target-lure discriminability metric.

items.title: Reconsidering Attentional Focus Taxonomies: The Case for Greater Nuance and Commentary on Peng et al. (2026).
items.abstract: Peng et al. (2026) audited and reclassified the attentional focus instructions of 87 studies, disaggregating external focus (EF) into proximal and distal nodes and showing that the resulting classification changes the meta-analytic ranking. We support the ambition, but argue that the nuance applied to EF is equally required for internal focus (IF). Critiques already published in this literature concern whether an instruction is relevant to the task, familiar to the performer, and individualised rather than universal; an audit of instruction wording addresses none of these. We illustrate the consequence with the core action component, a focus defined by its capacity to discriminate a given performer's optimal from suboptimal executions, which the taxonomy has no node for. A synthesis of this corpus is not interpretable until the conditions entering it are defined comparably rather than lexically.

items.title: Consistent Where It Counts: Movement Variability and Performance Under Social-Evaluative Pressure in Skilled and Less-Skilled Basketball Shooters.
items.abstract: Skilled actions look almost identical from one repetition to the next, and this similarity has led to the assumption that expertise eliminates variability. Accounts treating variability as an organised property suggest instead that skill lies in how variability is distributed across a movement, and that this distribution shapes how performance withstands pressure. Basketball shooters (30 skilled, 30 less-skilled) performed under three classes of constraint: increasing task difficulty, competing attentional demand, and escalating social-evaluative pressure, with competitive state anxiety measured throughout. Skilled performers were substantially more consistent at the shot outcome and at the two release parameters that set ball trajectory, with effects surviving correction across 12 variables; radial-error and release-speed effects also held within male participants alone. Group differences at the body were small and nonsignificant, but the corresponding measures had low split-half reliability, so that comparison is reported as inconclusive, not null. A single trial identified the individual with 84% accuracy, whereas skill level was recoverable only from the structure of variability and only weakly. Under rising pressure, within-person success fell in less-skilled performers but not in skilled performers, whose success was decoupled from anxiety across the anxiety range the groups shared, and increases in arm coordination variability tracked performance loss across the sample. A working-memory load impaired both groups equally. Consistency in skilled shooting is concentrated near the task outcome, movement reveals identity far more readily than skill, and protection under pressure is specific to social evaluation and does not extend to attentional load in general.

items.title: A shared path: How the encounter between Marie Elisabethe Luc and Jean-Martin Charcot shaped the diagnosis of multiple sclerosis.
items.abstract: The medical world has long celebrated pioneering doctors, whereas patients' stories remain largely hidden. One overlooked figure is Marie Elisabethe Luc (1821-1866), Jean-Martin Charcot's (1825-1893) key patient in defining multiple sclerosis (MS) nosology. This article reexamines parts of her life, drawing from unpublished records, and highlights her central role in shaping MS as a recognized condition. The year 2026 marks the 160th anniversary of the death of this patient.

items.title: The Prevalence and Associated Factors of Mastectomy in Women With Breast Cancer: A Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Mastectomy, as a common therapeutic intervention for breast carcinoma, is associated with considerable physical and psychological sequelae despite the efficacy in reduction of disease recurrence risk. The objective of this systematic review and meta-analysis study is to evaluate the prevalence, risk factors, protective factors, and psychological outcomes of mastectomy in women diagnosed with breast cancer. Associated data were retrieved from eligible studies using the keywords of "protective factors," "risk factors," "psychological outcomes," "related factors," "mastectomy," "breast emptying," "breast removal," "breast cancer," and "women." The search was applied in the databases of ScienceDirect, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Google Scholar search engine by October 2025. The records were managed using Citation Management Software of EndNote (v.8). The random-effects model was also employed to analyze eligible studies, and heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 index. According to the meta-analysis findings, the prevalence of mastectomy among women with breast cancer is 44.8% (95% confidence interval: 33.2-57.1). Meta-regression analysis demonstrated a decrease in prevalence following the acceleration in sample size and year of study conduction. Mastectomy is associated with a considerable prevalence rate and multidimensional outcomes. The findings underscore the necessity for the designation of personalized screening programs and the integration of psychological interventions into therapeutic protocols to enhance patients' quality of life and facilitate more informed treatment decision-making.

items.title: Feedback-related ERP differentiation is associated with emotional symptom burden in adolescents: Evidence from a multi-task ERP study.
items.abstract: Adolescence is marked by increasing vulnerability to anxiety and depressive symptoms. Event-related potentials (ERPs) provide temporally sensitive measures of cognitive-affective processing, but it remains unclear how dimensional emotional symptoms relate to response-control, conflict-related and feedback-related ERP indices in adolescence. We examined emotional symptom-ERP associations in school-recruited adolescents aged 15-17 years across Go/NoGo, Stroop-Simon and Cambridge Gambling Task (CGT) paradigms. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed with the GAD-7 and CES-D. Primary analyses focused on Go/NoGo and Stroop-Simon N2 difference amplitudes and CGT feedback-related ERP differentiation; P2 and behavioral-symptom analyses were exploratory. Because GAD-7 and CES-D scores were strongly correlated, combined and mutually adjusted symptom analyses were used to assess shared versus symptom-specific variance. The early feedback-related ERP difference (Loss - Win) was associated with both symptom scores, with higher scores corresponding to more positive, or less negative, difference amplitudes. Combined and mutually adjusted analyses were consistent with shared emotional symptom burden and did not provide clear evidence of symptom-specific associations. N2, P2, behavioral-symptom, and CGT ERP-behavior associations did not survive their respective FDR procedures. Early feedback-related ERP differentiation was associated with dimensional anxiety and depressive symptom scores in adolescents. Given data-informed ERP scoring, these findings are exploratory and do not establish between-task differences in association strength.

items.title: Generative AI Chatbot Responses to Suicide and Self-Harm: Systematic Review.
items.abstract: A growing number of US adults and youth confide in generative AI chatbots for mental health support, including disclosure of suicide and self-harm risk. While chatbot response quality, safety, and effectiveness could impact population-level suicide and self-harm rates, there are no systematic reviews of this burgeoning literature. We conducted a systematic review of studies evaluating generative AI chatbot responses to disclosure of suicide and self-harm risk. We followed PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 and PRISMA-S (PRISMA literature search extension) guidelines and preregistered the protocol on the Open Science Framework. We included English-language, peer-reviewed publications and preprints from 2020 to 2025 that empirically evaluated generative AI conversational responses to suicidal ideation, suicidal or nonsuicidal self-harm, or suicide-planning content. Eligible designs included audits, chatbot development, and adversarial "jailbreaking" studies. We excluded nongenerative systems, clinician-training tools, and prediction-only models. The final database searches were run from December 18 to 23, 2025 (PubMed, Embase, APA PsycINFO, IEEE Xplore, arXiv, and OSF Preprints). On July 26, 2026, publication status was rechecked to update preprint vs published classification. After deduplication, titles/abstracts and full texts were independently screened by 2 reviewers, with discrepancies resolved by consensus. Methodological quality was appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool 2018. We conducted a narrative synthesis across 7 safety domains and 5 AI classifications (proprietary, open-weight, companions, clinical, and study-specific). Of 1042 deduplicated records, 126 full texts were reviewed, and 29 were included (16 published; 13 preprints). Most studies evaluated suicidal content only (21/29). Twenty were solely audit studies, 2 chatbot development, and 1 jailbreaking. The rest combined approaches. Most used synthetic, single-turn prompts; only 6 used multiturn conversations. Most studies evaluated ≥2 of our 5 AI classifications (17/29). Proprietary models were included most frequently (23/29). When compared, proprietary models (eg, ChatGPT and Claude) tended to provide higher-quality responses than open-weight models (eg, Llama and DeepSeek) and many companions (eg, Replika and Character.AI); however, this trend weakened with sensitivity analysis. Chatbots generally performed well on emotional support, but responses were often generic and lacked context. Chatbots rarely assessed suicide or self-harm risk and performed most poorly when disclosure was ambiguous or moderate. Responses were inconsistent, often requiring multiple turns before referral to crisis resources or human support. Overtly harmful responses were rare under standard conditions but common under jailbreaking. Evidence is limited by the proportion of preprints, variable quality, synthetic single-turn prompts, small samples, heterogeneous outcomes, and rapid model versioning. Nonetheless, current chatbots tend to provide validation but struggle to escalate care, assess risk, and resist jailbreaking. Research is needed on stakeholder perspectives and on the short- and long-term clinical impact of chatbot responses using follow-up assessments in real-world or clinical settings. items.title: Basic psychological need satisfaction and work satisfaction among operators: A cross-sectional questionnaire study.
items.abstract: BackgroundWhile much attention has focused on technological development in manufacturing, less emphasis has been placed on psychological and social factors. This issue is particularly crucial in Sweden, where industries struggle to recruit and retain operators, while the number of older workers is rising.ObjectiveThis cross-sectional study aims to investigate whether the satisfaction of basic psychological needs is similarly associated with work satisfaction across age.MethodsA questionnaire survey was conducted among operators at two large companies in the automotive industry and two small and medium-sized enterprises in the turning and milling industry in Sweden. Confirmatory factor and regression analyses (N = 529) were used to investigate the relationship between basic psychological need satisfaction and work satisfaction and to test if this relationship is moderated by age.ResultsIn a multiple regression model predicting work satisfaction, autonomy need satisfaction exhibited the highest standardised regression coefficient, competence need satisfaction showed a weak but statistically significant association, whereas the regression coefficient for relatedness need satisfaction was not statistically significant. No statistically significant evidence of linear age moderation was found.ConclusionsThe findings highlight the importance of psychological need satisfaction for work satisfaction. Although autonomy need satisfaction exhibited the highest standardised regression coefficient, all needs had bivariate correlations with work satisfaction. Therefore, job redesign may benefit from supporting autonomy, competence through training, and fostering relatedness through peer collaboration. However, the cross-sectional design and potential measurement overlap warrant caution when interpreting these associations and their practical implications.

items.title: Association of Participation in a Community-Based Activity Program With Quality of Life in Independently Living Older Adults: A Cohort Study.
items.abstract: This study describes a community-based intervention program called the Healthy Living Program (HLP) that promotes healthy aging. A survey was conducted to understand how the HLP was associated with participants' health-related quality of life (HRQOL-4) (n = 177) over an 18-month period. Two groups were compared: those who were and were not exposed to the HLP. The groups did not differ on sociodemographic variables. In bivariate analyses, the exposed group had significantly higher self-perceived health and number of healthy days. Regression analyses at all follow-ups indicated that HLP exposure was significantly associated with number of healthy days. At six- and 12-month follow-up, HLP exposure was significantly associated with higher health ratings. Exposed individuals described feeling part of a community who shared interests and life experiences. Results suggest engaging in a customized, group-based program that promotes community-building is an effective approach to improving HRQOL for independently living older adults.

items.title: Interpersonal Vulnerability, Suicidal Ideation, and Multidimensional Physician-Assisted Suicide Attitudes in Korean Older Adults: A Network Analysis.
items.abstract: Attitudes toward physician-assisted suicide (PAS) combine ethical, medical, legal, and relational judgments that may intersect with, but are not equivalent to, suicidality. We estimated an EBICglasso Gaussian graphical model of perceived burdensomeness, thwarted belongingness, meaning in life, suicidal ideation, and seven PAS dimensions in 483 Korean adults aged 65 years or older. Perceived burdensomeness-suicidal ideation and thwarted belongingness-meaning in life were the strongest psychosocial edges. PAS dimensions formed a densely interconnected normative subsystem. The largest retained cross-community edge linked suicidal ideation with family/caregiving-burden PAS; this association was also positive in a nonregularized partial-correlation sensitivity analysis with a bootstrap interval excluding zero. Suicidal ideation and family/caregiving-burden PAS had the highest estimated bridge strengths in their respective communities, although bridge-rank stability was limited. Findings distinguish multidimensional end-of-life attitudes from clinical suicidality while identifying family-burden framing as a specific conditional interface.

items.title: Antipsychotic Co-Initiation Versus Monotherapy Initiation for People with Acute/Exacerbated Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
items.abstract: Antipsychotic co-initiation is sometimes used in schizophrenia spectrum disorders to expedite treatment response, although its use remains controversial due to mixed evidence. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to evaluate the benefits and harms of antipsychotic co-initiation. We searched the databases MEDLINE, PsycINFO, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from inception to 25 March, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing antipsychotic co-initiation with antipsychotic monotherapy initiation in people with acute/exacerbated schizophrenia spectrum disorders. All antipsychotic combinations were eligible. Trials were excluded if antipsychotics were initiated more than 1 week apart. Review phases were conducted in duplicate. Random-effects meta-analyses calculated standardized mean differences and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Absolute effects were estimated using mean differences and the monotherapy group event rate as the baseline risk. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias Tool 2 and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. Fifteen randomized controlled trials (1937 inpatients, mean age = 32.3 ± 5.6 years, male = 61%) testing 14 antipsychotic combinations over a mean of 10 weeks (range = 1-35) were included. Compared with monotherapy initiation, antipsychotic co-initiation likely improves treatment response (RR = 1.28, 95% CI 1.11, 1.48; moderate certainty), with effects observed as early as 1 week and greater benefits among people with lower symptom severity and those receiving first-generation combinations. Antipsychotic co-initiation may slightly reduce total symptoms (standardized mean difference = - 0.35, 95% CI - 0.71, 0.00) and negative symptoms (standardized mean difference = - 0.55, 95% CI - 1.08, - 0.02; both low certainty). There was little to no evidence of benefit for other efficacy outcomes, including positive symptoms, depressive symptoms, quality of life, and global illness severity (very low to moderate certainty). Antipsychotic co-initiation may not increase adverse effects (RR = 0.97, 95% CI 0.87, 1.09), serious adverse effects (RR = 1.51, 95% CI 0.50, 4.53), or any of the specific side effects examined, including extrapyramidal symptoms, anxiety, constipation, sialorrhea, fatigue, or weight gain (all low certainty). Antipsychotic co-initiation may not affect benzodiazepine (RR = 1.05, 95% CI 0.95, 1.15) or anticholinergic co-use (RR = 0.97, 95% CI 0.76, 1.23; both low certainty). All-cause discontinuation was similar between groups (RR = 0.96, 95% CI 0.81, 1.13; moderate certainty), as were specific-cause discontinuation rates (low-to-moderate certainty). Overall, 28% of participants did not complete the trials. Compared with monotherapy initiation, there is moderate certainty evidence that antipsychotic co-initiation improves treatment response in acute/exacerbated schizophrenia spectrum disorders without increasing short-term discontinuation. However, its impact on other outcomes remains less certain and with effect sizes that may not be clinically relevant. Evidence certainty was frequently downgraded due to the risk of bias from missing data and imprecision, therefore, adequately powered trials with improved retention strategies are needed.

items.title: Vision Impairment: Prevalence, Sex Differences, and Predictors from the Saudi National Disability Survey.
items.abstract: Vision impairment (VI) remains a priority public health concern in Saudi Arabia, yet national evidence on its distribution and determinants has been limited. Using the 2017 Saudi National Disability Survey (N = 20,408,362 Saudis), in which difficulty seeing (even when wearing glasses) was self- or proxy-reported using Washington Group questions and graded as mild, severe or extreme, we quantified the burden of VI, described sociodemographic and geographic patterns, tested sex differences across 12 indicators (region, severity, education, marital status, parental consanguinity, cause and duration of difficulty, in single- and multiple-disability subsets), and modelled predictors of co-occurring multiple disabilities versus VI only. Weighted prevalence estimates (approximate 95% confidence intervals [CIs]) were: no reported functional difficulty 92.9% (92.6-93.3); at least one difficulty in any functional domain 7.1% (6.7-7.4); and any VI 4.0% (3.7-4.3; n = 811,610), comprising 4.3% (3.9-4.7) of males and 3.6% (3.3-4.0) of females. VI co-occurred with at least one other difficulty in 2.1% (2.0-2.3) of the population and was the only difficulty in 1.8% (1.7-2.0). After correction for the survey design, sex differences remained significant only for marital status (Cramér's V = .289) and educational attainment (V = .217); effect sizes for the remaining indicators were small (V = .034-.163). In logistic models, higher odds of multiple disabilities (versus VI only) were associated with disease-related (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 3.25, 95% CI 2.23-4.72), traffic-accident (AOR = 3.88, 1.34-11.21) and other causes (AOR = 2.57, 1.62-4.09) relative to congenital causes, with female sex (AOR = 1.77, 1.34-2.35) and with residence in Makkah relative to Al-Riyadh (AOR = 1.63, 1.09-2.45); severe difficulty was associated with lower odds than mild difficulty (AOR = 0.70, 0.50-0.97), whereas consanguinity, duration and glasses use were not significantly associated. The findings indicate a substantial VI burden, with sex differences concentrated in education and marital status; because VI was self-reported rather than clinically assessed, these associations should be interpreted with caution. Policy should pair region-targeted screening with gender- and education-sensitive outreach, strengthen chronic-disease eye care, and expand low-vision rehabilitation; clinically verified, individual-level data are needed to confirm these patterns.

items.title: Multiple Levels of Analysis of the Positive Affect System: Relation to Depressive Symptoms in Parents and Children.
items.abstract: The positive affect system includes multiple features (e.g., hedonic, behavioral, motivational, and physiological) that are associated with depressive symptoms in youth and may serve as important mechanisms underlying depression. Examining associations between each feature with each other and with depressive symptoms can provide important information about the positive affect system and its link to mood disorders. Moreover, studying these relations in children who vary in risk of depression may provide information about vulnerabilities underlying depression. This study examined these questions in a sample of 8- to 10-year-old (M = 9.34; SD = 0.85) children of mothers with and without a depression history. Correlational and regression analyses revealed significant associations among some PA features; these associations were not significantly moderated by mothers' depression history. One positive affect feature, lower motivation, was associated with higher depressive symptoms in children, and this association was specific to offspring of mothers with a depression history in exploratory analyses (interaction p = .021). Regardless of mothers' depression history, children's higher depressive symptoms were associated with less adaptive emotion regulation after accounting for anxiety symptoms; the corresponding association with anxiety symptoms was nonsignificant after accounting for depressive symptoms. Overall, the mixed levels of association across the measures of positive affect provide limited evidence of convergence of these features of the positive affect system, with a limited role of children's current depression level and mothers' depression history.

items.title: Unveiling the silent player: miR-135a-5p as a candidate marker in 5-FU resistance in colorectal cancer.
items.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, and resistance to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) is a major obstacle to effective treatment. A better understanding of the microRNA (miRNA)-associated expression mechanisms underlying this chemoresistance is crucial for improving patient outcomes. This study combined bioinformatics with experimental validation. RNA sequencing datasets (GSE119481 for miRNA, and GSE196900 for mRNA) were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database and analyzed to identify differentially expressed miRNAs and genes. In vitro, an HCT116 cell line with acquired resistance to 5-FU was generated and characterized using an MTT assay. Apoptosis and cell-cycle distribution were assessed by flow cytometry. Expression levels of the candidate miRNA and target genes were assessed by qRT-PCR in 5-FU-sensitive and 5-FU-resistant HCT116 cells using three independent biological replicates (n = 3), with each biological replicate analyzed in technical duplicate. Group comparisons were performed using Student's t-test, and P ≤ 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Bioinformatic analysis revealed a network of differentially expressed miRNAs and genes associated with 5-FU resistance. The 5-FU-resistant HCT116 cell line exhibited a significantly higher IC50, reduced apoptosis, and an altered cell-cycle profile upon 5-FU treatment. An integrated analysis highlighted miR-135a-5p as a candidate regulatory miRNA and KLF8 as a putative target gene. qRT-PCR showed differential expression patterns of miR-135a-5p and KLF8 in 5-FU-resistant compared with 5-FU-sensitive cells. This study identified a putative miR-135a-5p/KLF8 expression relationship associated with 5-FU resistance in HCT116 cells. These findings provide a basis for further investigation of the potential involvement of miR-135a-5p and KLF8 in 5-FU resistance in CRC. However, direct miRNA-KLF8 binding, causal regulation, biomarker value, and therapeutic potential require validation through luciferase reporter and miRNA gain- and loss-of-function experiments.

items.title: Speech-in-noise perception with hearing aids using a remote microphone or smartphone accessibility feature: a double-blind randomized crossover trial.
items.abstract: To compare speech-in-noise performance with hearing aids alone, a proprietary remote microphone, and the iPhone Live Listen accessibility feature in adults with sensorineural hearing loss. Randomised, double-blind crossover study. The present analysis included three listening conditions: hearing aids alone, hearing aids coupled to EduMic, and hearing aids connected to Live Listen. HINT-Brazil sentence lists were presented at a fixed -10 dB signal-to-noise ratio. Performance was analysed using a linear mixed-effects model. Twenty-two adult bilateral hearing-aid users. Listening condition significantly affected performance (Wald χ2(2)=32.20, p<.001). Compared with hearing aids alone, sentence recognition increased by 23.18 percentage points with EduMic (95% CI, 11.09-35.28; p<.001) and 34.32 percentage points with Live Listen (95% CI, 22.22-46.41; p<.001). Live Listen exceeded EduMic by 11.14 percentage points, but the difference was not statistically significant (95% CI, -0.96 to 23.23; p=.071). Both remote-microphone approaches improved speech-in-noise performance relative to hearing aids alone. No statistically significant difference was detected between Live Listen and EduMic; this should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence.

items.title: Detection of Wolbachia (Rickettsiales: Anaplasmataceae) strain in Aedes albopictus (Diptera: Culicidae) from diverse breeding habitats in Sarawak, Malaysian Borneo: First report on baseline data for dengue vector control strategies.
items.abstract: Dengue fever remains a major public health issue in Malaysia, and Sarawak reports an increasing number of cases each year. Wolbachia (Rickettsiales: Anaplasmataceae), an endosymbiotic bacterium naturally found in some insect populations, offers a new method for controlling dengue vectors by releasing Wolbachia-infected Aedes mosquitoes. However, there is currently a scarcity of baseline data on natural Wolbachia infection status in mosquito populations from Sarawak. A cross-sectional study was conducted from March to May 2025 across 21 locations within a higher education institution campus in Sarawak. Mosquito larvae and pupae were collected from active breeding sites, reared to adulthood and identified morphologically using taxonomic keys. Wolbachia detection was performed by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) targeting the Wolbachia surface protein (wsp) gene for strains A and B. Additionally, the dengue virus was detected by reverse-transcriptase PCR (RT-PCR). A total of 277 mosquito larvae and pupae were collected from 32 active breeding sites. Fifteen different breeding habitat types were identified, with tires (28.9%) and discarded containers (23.5%) being the most common. Morphological identification of 119 successfully emerged adults revealed that 93.3% (n = 111) were Aedes albopictus and 6.7% (n = 8) were Culex quinquefasciatus. No Aedes aegypti was recorded. Clear water (59.4%) was the predominant water quality at breeding sites, followed by turbid (34.4%) and polluted (6.3%). Wolbachia screening of 14 pooled A. albopictus samples showed an overall pool positivity rate of 42.9% (6/14 pools). As exact pool sizes were not recorded, this value could not be converted to individual-level prevalence and should be interpreted as an upper bound. A single infection with the Wolbachia strain B was detected in two pools, while superinfection with both strains A and B was observed in four pools. No single Wolbachia A infection was detected. Likewise, all samples tested negative for the dengue virus.This study provides the first baseline data on natural Wolbachia infection in A. albopictus populations from Sarawak. The presence of both single and superinfections suggests the potential for utilizing Wolbachia-based vector control strategies in the region. These findings will inform future planning for the release of Wolbachia-infected Aedes mosquitoes as part of integrated dengue control programs in Sarawak.

items.title: Cervical cancer risk perception and associated factors among women living with HIV in Nigeria.
items.abstract: This study assessed cervical cancer risk perception and associated factors among women living with HIV (WLHIV) in Nigeria. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis using baseline data from the Accelerating Cervical Cancer Elimination through the Integration of Screen-and-Treat Services (ACCESS) Study. The analytic sample included 1,873 participants aware of cervical cancer. Mixed-effects multinomial logistic regression was used to examine factors associated with perceived cervical cancer risk, using "no risk" as the reference category. Overall, perceived themselves at risk 37.6%: 6.6% reported high risk, 12.7% moderate, and 18.4% low risk. In contrast, 28% perceived no risk and 34% were uncertain. WLHIV with high cervical cancer knowledge had higher adjusted relative risk ratios for perceiving high (aRRR = 2.70, 95% CI: 1.74-4.20), moderate (aRRR = 2.03, 95% CI: 1.37-3.00), and low (aRRR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.00-1.91) risk, but were less likely to report uncertainty (aRRR = 0.66, 95% CI: 0.45-0.98). Age, educational attainment, ethnicity, marital status, and duration of HIV diagnosis were also independently associated with specific levels of perceived risk. Cervical cancer risk perception was suboptimal, with nearly two-thirds perceiving no risk or uncertainty. Culturally appropriate cervical cancer education and targeted risk communication should be integrated into HIV care programs.

items.title: Tetrahydrocannabinol beverages sold by online alcohol retailers.
items.abstract: Sales of intoxicating tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) beverages have expanded rapidly in the United States (US), despite Food and Drug Administration guidance indicating they are being sold unlawfully. Prominent alcohol brands, manufacturers and retailers have entered this market. To inform regulatory and enforcement efforts to reduce use and associated harms, we aimed to characterize the online THC beverage market related to top brands, potency and price. From October to December 2025, data were collected regarding THC beverages from 8 US-based online alcohol retailers. Searches were conducted using an incognito browser and the terms 'delta', 'thc', 'tetrahydrocannabinol', 'cbd' and 'hemp'. Alcohol retailers were selected to represent state retailers differing by alcohol control status and cannabis/derived cannabis laws and a national retail chain. A PhD-level researcher coded product characteristics including brand, THC content, package size, container size, price and presence of other cannabinoids or functional ingredients. Neither of the state-owned and operated liquor store chains sold THC beverages. The remaining six retailers sold THC beverages in cans (n = 6 retailers), as 'spirits' (n = 2 retailers) and 'shots' (n = 3 retailers). Across retailers, there were 323 unique canned THC beverage products across 142 brands. Cans contained an average of 7.4 mg of THC (range: 1.5 mg-20 mg), had an average price of US$21.36 per package (range: US$4.99-US$54.99) and an average price per mg of THC of US$0.74 (range: US$0.25-US$2.90). There were 24 unique THC spirit products across 12 brands; most did not specify the THC content. The average price of THC spirits was US$34.49 (range: US$21.99-US$64.99). There were 25 products sold as 'shots' across 15 brands, each containing an average of 7.36 mg of THC (range: 2 mg-10 mg). The 'shots' cost an average of US$4.59 (range: US$1.50-US$7.49) and an average of US$0.71 per mg of THC (range: US$0.30-US$2.00). Across all products, >30% contained non-intoxicating cannabinoids (cannabidiol, cannabigerol, cannabinol, cannabichromene) and a few contained non-THC substances that are often marketed for functional effects (caffeine, L-theanine, lion's mane, electrolytes, Reishi, blue lotus, cordyceps, maca, rhodiola, chamomile, tryptophan, melatonin and magnesium). Among 8 United States-based online alcohol retailers surveyed in late 2025, tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) beverages were not sold by the state-owned/operated chains; the other locations sold numerous THC beverage products across many brands. THC beverages often contained ∼7-8mg of THC per can/shot and were available for as low as US$1.50. Some products contained non-intoxicating cannabinoids or other non-THC substances. The accessibility of THC beverages in the United States through established alcohol retailers may facilitate normalization and market expansion.

items.title: Bridge that Gap: Health System Perspectives on Community Health Workers Addressing Racial Disparities in Palliative Care.
items.abstract: Persistent disparities exist in access to palliative care services, with African Americans receiving less and lower-quality care. Community health workers (CHWs) have been shown to improve health disparities in multiple settings.12 We characterized the perspectives of administrators, clinicians, and CHWs on barriers to palliative care use, and how CHWs could address these barriers, by conducting an analysis of qualitative interviews with interviewees from three medical systems in the US. We identified three barriers and mechanisms by which CHWs may mitigate barriers: limited health literacy and CHWs serving as educators; competing priorities linked to structural disadvantage and CHWs providing logistical support; and mistrust of the health care system and CHWs serving as trusted intermediaries. Integrating CHWs may improve engagement and equitable access to palliative care among African American patients, with broader implications for other marginalized populations.

items.title: Lived experiences of conscientious objection to euthanasia: A constructivist grounded theory study among palliative care physicians.
items.abstract: Assisted dying is being legalized in a growing number of jurisdictions, intensifying debates about conscientious objection in end-of-life care. Although widely discussed in theoretical studies, conscientious objection is often portrayed as a fixed, binary stance. Empirical research has questioned this framing but remains scarce in how physicians experience and enact this practice. To explore the lived experiences of conscientious objection to euthanasia among palliative care physicians, and to examine how societal, institutional, and personal factors shape ethical reasoning and practice. Qualitative interview study using a constructivist grounded theory. Semi-structured interviews explored experiences of conscientious objection, team dynamics, and institutional contexts. 24 physicians from 18 palliative care units across Belgium participated. Units varied in type, size, and worldview orientation. Participants had diverse professional backgrounds and substantial experience with euthanasia requests. Physicians described conscientious objection as a situated, relational, and evolving practice shaped by societal narratives, organizational cultures, and personal moral integration. Refusals were not always grounded in explicit moral opposition; relational, emotional, and interpretive considerations also informed decision-making. Our analysis identified six lived positions reflecting fluid, context-sensitive ways of navigating participation and refusal: principled objectors, silent strugglers, boundary setters, relational discerners, legal compliers, and self-protective objectors. Conscientious objection to euthanasia cannot be reduced to a fixed, categorical stance; it is a dynamic, context-sensitive practice. Ethical guidance and policy should recognize its relational and interpretive dimensions. Dialogue between theoretical and empirical accounts is needed to develop a comprehensive understanding of conscientious objection as a lived moral practice.

items.title: Frequency of Reintervention after Uterine-Preserving Procedures Among Women with Fibroids, 2014-2023.
items.abstract: Uterine-preserving procedures, including myomectomy, uterine artery embolization (UAE), and radiofrequency ablation, are increasingly used for uterine fibroid management. However, comparative evidence on reintervention following these procedures remains limited. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients aged 18-50 years who were diagnosed with uterine fibroids and underwent a uterine-preserving fibroid-directed procedure between January 2015 and December 2022. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients undergoing reintervention according to initial procedure type. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations between clinical and demographic factors and reintervention. Among patients undergoing uterine-preserving procedures, the overall frequency of reintervention was 13%, with variation across initial procedure types (hysteroscopic myomectomy: 23%; myomectomy: 7%; UAE: 16%; radiofrequency ablation: 9%; and multiple procedures: 10%; p = 0.002). In multivariable analysis, receiving care in a rural setting compared with an urban setting (odds ratio [OR] 1.95, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.27-2.97, p < 0.01), lack of insurance compared with private insurance (OR 1.67, 95% CI 1.06-2.63, p = 0.01), and a diagnosis of intramural fibroids (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.02-2.01, p = 0.037) were associated with higher odds of reintervention. Patients aged 18-29 years had lower odds of reintervention compared with those 35-39 years (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.23-0.90, p = 0.02). Intramural fibroids, rural care setting, and lack of insurance were associated with higher odds of reintervention, whereas younger age and initial myomectomy were associated with lower odds. Optimization of initial treatment decisions and increased access to care are needed to reduce reintervention and improve patient outcomes.

items.title: Cannabis use among psychiatric in-patients: Prevalence, clinical characteristics and hospital outcomes.
items.abstract: Cannabis use is common among people receiving psychiatric care and may be associated with more complex clinical presentations and inpatient trajectories, but its prevalence and association with hospitalization outcomes remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of documented cannabis use during psychiatric hospitalizations and to explore associated socio-demographic, clinical and hospitalization characteristics. Retrospective observational study analyzing routinely collected data from the electronic health records of patients admitted between 2019 and 2024. Descriptive statistics and multivariable analyses were conducted to examine associations of cannabis use with length of stay, seclusion and restraint. Psychiatric inpatient units of the Groupe Hospitalier Universitaire (GHU) Paris Psychiatrie et Neurosciences hospital group, a network of public psychiatric hospitals in Paris, France. 32 429 hospital stays corresponding to 17 040 individual adult patients. The median age was 40 years (interquartile range 28-54) and 45.4% were female. Documented cannabis use was the main exposure, identified through multiple complementary sources: a positive urine toxicology result, presence of a cannabis-related diagnosis in structured clinical data and a natural language processing keyword search algorithm applied to free clinical notes. Outcomes were length of stay, seclusion and restraint. Covariates included socio-demographic, clinical and hospitalization characteristics such as age, sex, diagnostic category, comorbidities, housing status and legal admission status. Cannabis use was documented in 25.0% of patients, and an overall increase was observed over the study period despite year-to-year fluctuations. Compared with individuals without documented use, those with identified use were more often male, younger and had higher rates of psychotic disorders and comorbidity. In multivariable models, the association between documented cannabis use and length of stay varied according to legal admission status, whereas no interaction with legal admission status was observed for seclusion or restraint. Cannabis use was associated with longer length of stay, with adjusted ratios of mean length of stay of 1.22 [95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.16-1.27] for voluntary admissions, 1.23 (95% CI = 1.17-1.29) for involuntary admissions under a civil procedure, 1.39 (95% CI = 1.28-1.50) for state-ordered admissions and 1.64 (95% CI = 1.24-2.16) for incarcerated and forensic patients. Documented cannabis use was also associated with higher odds of seclusion [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.73, 95% CI = 1.56-1.91] and restraint (aOR = 1.88, 95% CI = 1.48-2.37). Cannabis use appears to occur in about a quarter of psychiatric inpatients in Paris, France, and prevalence is rising; it appears to be associated with longer (vs. shorter) hospitalizations and higher odds of coercive interventions (vs. no coercive interventions) during the stay.

items.title: The digital divide among hospital outpatients: sociodemographic and socioeconomic factors associated with self-rated digital competence.
items.abstract: Digital patient portals are increasingly being implemented in hospitals and have the potential to improve healthcare delivery and patient participation. However, limited digital competence may prevent certain patient groups from benefiting equally from these services and may contribute to the digital divide. This study aimed to identify the sociodemographic and socioeconomic factors associated with self-rated digital competence among hospital outpatients. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among outpatients of three clinics at a German university hospital between October 2024 and July 2025. Self-rated digital competence was assessed using five items of the ICT Self-Concept Scale (ICT-SC25). Associations with sociodemographic, socioeconomic and health-related characteristics were examined using multiple linear regression with heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors. Of N = 653 patients, n = 596 were included in the regression analysis. The mean digital competence score was 4.54 (SD 1.23) on a six-point scale. Higher self-rated digital competence was associated with younger age (B=-0.25 per 10 years, 95% CI -0.32 to -0.17, p < 0.001), male gender (B = 0.30, 95% CI 0.12 to 0.47, p < 0.001), upper secondary (B = 0.64, 95% CI 0.28 to 1.01, p < 0.001) and tertiary education (B = 0.77, 95% CI 0.42 to 1.12, p < 0.001) compared with lower secondary education, and having a partner (B = 0.27, 95% CI 0.06 to 0.47, p = 0.011). Compared with employed patients, retired (B=-0.36, 95% CI -0.64 to -0.08, p = 0.013) and non-employed patients (B=-0.31, 95% CI -0.62 to -0.003, p = 0.048) reported lower digital competence. Native language, migration background, number of chronic diseases and clinic were not significantly associated with digital competence. The model explained 33.1% of the variance (adjusted R²=0.312). In a sensitivity analysis adjusting for income (n = 510), the associations with non-employment and partner status were no longer statistically significant. Self-rated digital competence among hospital outpatients is unequally distributed across sociodemographic and socioeconomic groups. Digital health services may unintentionally reinforce existing social inequalities if these patient groups are not adequately supported. Implementation strategies for patient portals should therefore include targeted support alongside technological solutions.

items.title: Early detection and proportion of child risk for mental health problems and parental stress in routine school entry exams: a pilot study.
items.abstract: Early childhood is a crucial period for subsequent psychological development and young children are highly sensitive to adversities such as parental stress. Screening for risk factors and mental health problems (MHP) in preschool-aged children could enhance early prevention and intervention and lower the detrimental impact of persistent emotional and behavioral difficulties. The school entry examination (SEE) as the only mandatory public health screening in Germany during childhood has extensive reach but currently neglects the area of mental health assessment. To test the potential added value, the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ-P) and the Parental Stress Scale (PSS) were used to assess child risk for MHP and parental stress across two German study centers in addition to the routine SEE procedure. The study determined the proportion of preschool children (n = 561) with elevated risk for MHP according to the SDQ-P vs. the routine SEE procedure. Potentially associated factors with preschool risk for MHP, such as parental stress, were analyzed through a multiple linear regression model. The proportion of children at risk for MHP was 15.8%, the SDQ-P identified children that were not identified through the routine SEE process and the patterns of agreement varied significantly between the study centers. The overall mean PSS total score was 35.86. Parental stress had the strongest association with the SDQ-P total difficulties score, followed by lower parental educational status and male sex (child). The detection of child risk for MHP with the SDQ-P at two different sites in Germany revealed discrepancies when compared with the routine SEE procedures and significant variations between the study centers in terms of agreement patterns and detection rates were observed. In order to enhance the comparability of results and improve identification rates of children at risk for MHP, standardizing the routine SEE assessment in the field of mental health should be considered as a future step. The results underscore the interdependence of child, family and social risk factors, which is why a combination of those should be considered when assessing the need for preventive measures or intervention.

items.title: Development of a Regional Mobile Health Alliance: A Practice-Based Coordination Model.
items.abstract: Mobile health units have revolutionized the way that health care is delivered throughout the world. They can provide a range of accessible services and quality care to our most vulnerable populations. Barriers to health care such as transportation, cost, and long wait times can be mitigated through the utilization of mobile health units. Coordinating efforts through community collaboration and collective effort can further expand access to care, reduce service duplication, promote the sharing of resources, and strengthen total impact. This article describes the creation of a regional Mobile Health Alliance which provides a forum for organizations with mobile health units in Western New York (WNY) to align and maximize their efforts. This innovation, led by the University at Buffalo School of Public Health and Health Professions (UB SPHHP), aimed to fulfill needs in local communities ranging from general health services and education such as cardiometabolic screenings and vaccinations to more focused services such as dentistry, cancer screenings, and behavioral health management. Alliance members have reported that they have gained contact information and networking opportunities from other organizations thus highlighting the importance of coordination among group members. They also reported preventing or minimizing service duplication and sharing resources because of their collaborative involvement with the alliance. Early implementation insights include leveraging data from the alliance to support mobile health policy, promoting interprofessional education through academic partnerships, and creating a local recurring event that brings together both primary and specialty care units in a target service area.

items.title: Oncologic Outcomes of Blue Dye-Only Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy After Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Initially Node-Positive Breast Cancer: A Multicenter Cohort Study from the Brazilian Public Health System.
items.abstract: Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is increasingly used to de-escalate axillary surgery in patients with breast cancer with axillary downstaging. Evidence supporting blue dye-only mapping with Patent Blue V remains limited, particularly in resource-limited settings. This multicenter retrospective cohort study included women with invasive breast cancer treated at three public hospitals within the Brazilian Unified Health System between 2017 and 2021. Eligible patients received NAC, converted to clinically node-negative status (ycN0), and underwent definitive breast and axillary surgery. The primary analysis compared patients with initially node-positive disease (cN1-cN2) converted to ycN0 who underwent Patent Blue V-only SLNB or axillary lymph node dissection (ALND). The primary endpoint was axillary recurrence. Secondary endpoints included locoregional recurrence, distant recurrence-free survival and overall survival. Overall, 369 patients were included: 163 underwent SLNB and 206 underwent ALND. The primary analysis included 78 SLNB and 174 ALND patients with cN1-cN2 disease converted to ycN0. Median follow-up was 55.0 and 55.7 months, respectively. Axillary recurrence occurred in 2.6% after SLNB and 2.3% after ALND (P = 1.000). Local recurrence was 3.8% versus 4.6% (P = 1.000), and locoregional recurrence was 16.7% versus 17.2% (P = 0.911). The 5-year distant recurrence-free survival was 85.7% versus 87.3% (P = 0.851), and 5-year overall survival was 88.7% versus 88.2% (P = 0.506). Patent Blue V-only SLNB after NAC was associated with low axillary recurrence and oncologic outcomes comparable to those with ALND in selected initially node-positive patients downstaged to ycN0, supporting its pragmatic use in public health settings.

items.title: Integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance for high-resolution tracking of measles virus evolution and transmission.
items.abstract: Measles outbreaks have surged globally, challenging surveillance and control efforts. In South Africa, the 2024-2025 measles outbreak led to nearly 4,000 reported cases, triggering a nationwide vaccination campaign. However, tracking measles virus (MeV; species Morbillivirus hominis) transmission and evolution remains difficult at scale, particularly in settings with limited access to care, diagnostic testing and sequencing capacity. Wastewater can enable population-scale virus surveillance, but low MeV concentrations limit detection sensitivity and sequencing quality. Here we show that overcoming these technical challenges enables integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance that expands the coverage and resolution of MeV monitoring. We developed a virus concentration and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) workflow and applied it to 4,502 wastewater samples collected across all nine provinces of South Africa during the 2024-2025 outbreak. Wastewater MeV genotype prevalence tracked clinical estimates, and phylogenetic analyses combining wastewater and clinical sequences revealed geographically structured transmission and previously undetected inter-provincial spread. WGS recovered transmission links not captured by the field standard approach, which targets a 450-nucleotide region of the nucleoprotein gene (N450), highlighting the importance of WGS to accurately characterize transmission dynamics. Our study provides a cost-effective and scalable genomic surveillance approach to support measles control and elimination.

items.title: Paediatric metabolic syndrome criteria as predictors of early adult metabolic syndrome: findings from the EPITeen cohort.
items.abstract: Several definitions of metabolic syndrome (MetS) are used in paediatric populations. This study investigates the predictive capacity of five MetS definitions at age 13 for identifying MetS at age 27 and explores whether adding non-classic variables improves prediction. Participants from the EPITeen cohort (n = 815) with valid data on MetS components at ages 13 and 27 were included. At age 13, MetS was defined using Cook, Ferranti, Ford, Agudelo, and International Diabetes Federation (IDF) criteria, and at age 27 using the Alberti consensus. Predictive capacity was estimated using the area under the ROC curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Performance metrics such as sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, accuracy, and likelihood ratios were calculated. Non-classic variables were added to the criterion with a higher AUC. At age 13, MetS prevalence ranged from 0.9% (IDF) to 12.5% (Ferranti), and at age 27 it was 3.4%. Ferranti definition had the highest AUC (0.696; 95% CI 0.609-0.784), although not significantly higher than the other criteria. Ferranti was also the least conservative criterion, classifying substantially more adolescents as having MetS (77.4%) but with lower specificity, accuracy, and likelihood ratios than the other criteria. LDL-C was the only non-classic variable that showed a significant improvement in Ferranti's AUC (0.765; 95% CI 0.683-0.846). Paediatric MetS definitions showed limited ability to predict MetS in early adulthood. Ferranti definition with LDL-C demonstrated the best predictive capacity and, due to its performance metrics, can support targeted preventive public health strategies throughout the life course.

items.title: Bridging genomic translation gap: a systematic review of genomic literacy as the foundation for effective healthcare and public health practices.
items.abstract: Genomic literacy gaps among healthcare professionals (HCPs) directly impact patient outcomes through diagnostic errors, misinterpretation of results, and inequitable access to precision medicine. Understanding these competency deficits is critical for reducing disparities in genomic medicine implementation. Using Rogers' knowledge typology and Miller's clinical competency hierarchy, we systematically analyzed 69 studies (2014-2024). Study quality was appraised using the Modified Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) to evaluate methodological rigor across diverse study designs. PRISMA guidelines were followed throughout. Substantive genomic competency gaps persist globally among HCPs, characterized by foundational knowledge deficits in genomic medicine; limited integration of genomics into clinical workflows; pronounced disparities across specialties, clinical domains and countries/regions. Effective interventions include role-specific pathways to boost confidence and microlearning to sustain knowledge long-term, with blended modalities preferred. Precision education integrating competency-based role-specific training, reinforced microlearning, and equity-focused implementation tools offers a promising pathway to equitable genomic healthcare. Validation through inclusive implementation remains essential.

items.title: External Validation of Diabetes Risk Prediction Models in Women With a History of Gestational Diabetes.
items.abstract: The aim of the study was to externally validate diabetes risk prediction models in women with a history of gestational diabetes. Discrimination was evaluated with the Harrell's C-index. Calibration was evaluated by comparing predicted risks against observed risks. Among the 1180 participants, 104 cases of incident diabetes were identified during a median follow-up of 8.1 years. Harrell's C-index was 0.819 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.774-0.864) for the model proposed by Belsti et al., 0.788 (95% CI 0.740-0.836) for the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Diabetes Risk Model, 0.773 (95% CI 0.723-0.824) for the Framingham Diabetes Risk Model (FDRM), 0.770 (95% CI 0.722-0.818) for the Man model, 0.736 (95% CI 0.685-0.788) for the Ignell model, 0.707 (95% CI 0.653-0.761) for the Li model, 0.706 (95% CI 0.654-0.758) for the Köhler model, 0.702 (95% CI 0.650-0.754) for the Finnish Diabetes Risk Score, 0.689 (95% CI 0.636-0.742) for the American Diabetes Association Diabetes Risk Test and 0.665 (95% CI 0.607-0.723) for the Parkhi model. The Belsti model, ARIC model and FDRM showed good calibration after in-cohort recalibration for 5- and 10-year incident diabetes. The sensitivity of the median score of the Belsti model was 93% (95% CI 83%-100%) for incident diabetes at Year 5. Among women with prior gestational diabetes, the Belsti et al. model demonstrated good discrimination for predicting incident diabetes and may help guide screening frequency. The ARIC model and the FDRM are simple, valid tools for diabetes risk prediction in this population.

items.title: Association of fibrosis-4 index with cardio-cerebro-renal morbidity and mortality in type 2 diabetes beyond liver diseases.
items.abstract: This study hypothesized that the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index could serve as a simple marker for risk stratification of multiple organ outcomes, including cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and renal diseases, beyond liver disease in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Patients with T2DM who had sufficient data to calculate FIB-4 within one year before or after diagnosis were identified from a multi-hospital system in Taiwan between January 2008 and December 2023. Outcomes included the incidence of and mortality from cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and renal diseases. Adjusted incidence rate ratios (aIRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Poisson regression. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for mortality were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression. Among 54,651 patients (379,481 person-years), risks generally increased across FIB-4 categories. Compared with the low FIB-4 group ( 2.67) FIB-4 groups had higher risks of incident cardiovascular disease (aIRR: 1.34, 95%CI: 1.22-1.46 and aIRR: 1.94, 95%CI: 1.74-2.17, respectively) and cardiovascular mortality (aHR: 1.27, 95%CI: 1.08-1.49 and aHR: 1.77, 95% CI: 1.46-2.14, respectively). Higher FIB-4 levels were also associated with incident renal disease (aIRR: 1.18; 95%CI: 1.07-1.30 and aIRR: 1.25, 95%CI: 1.10-1.41, respectively), but not significantly with renal disease-related mortality (aHR: 1.01, 95%CI: 0.76-1.33 and aHR: 1.35, 95%CI: 0.96-1.89, respectively). Associations with incident cerebrovascular disease (aIRR: 1.05, 95%CI: 0.93-1.19 and aIRR: 1.13, 95%CI: 0.96-1.33, respectively) and cerebrovascular mortality (aHR: 0.98, 95%CI: 0.75-1.29 and aHR: 1.20, 95%CI: 0.86-1.68, respectively) were not statistically significant. Beyond liver disease, the FIB-4 index may serve as a simple clinical marker for stratifying the risks of cardiovascular disease incidence and mortality, and incident renal disease, in patients with T2DM.

items.title: Phosphate Additives in Ultra-Processed Foods: Greater Intake, Distribution, and Bioavailability, With Hidden Risks to Kidney Health.
items.abstract: Scientific interest in phosphate-containing food additives (Pi-additives) stems from their relevance to dietary management of chronic kidney disease, whereas public concerns are centered on excess phosphate intake associated with their largely unrestricted use in the industrial processing of widely consumed foods and beverages and a potential link to premature mortality. This perspective examines how Western diets have transitioned toward ultra-processed foods and beverages, which now account for 60%-70% of calorie intake, and how this shift has been linked to the rise in noncommunicable diseases-notably chronic kidney disease-and mortality and to substantial increases in Pi-additive intake, contributing to excessive phosphorus consumption. We describe the broad range of inorganic and organic Pi-additives and their regulation by the European Union and US Food and Drug Administration, their technical functions that promote extensive use in food processing, and differences in phosphate absorption. Survey intake limitations and inadequate nutrient databases hinder determination of needed individual intake exposure estimates of Pi-additives critical to determining safe use and causal associations of high Pi-additive ultra-processed food intake with kidney disease risk. Together, these intake needs and Pi-additive features provide the basis for exploring mechanisms underlying the toxic effects of Pi-additives on kidney health and related chronic diseases.

items.title: Large language model (LLM) & counseling for fetal malformations.
items.abstract: Congenital anomalies affect approximately 3 to 5% of all pregnancies and represent a leading cause of infant morbidity and mortality worldwide. When a fetal malformation is detected on mid-trimester anatomic ultrasound, the clinical encounter that follows is not merely a medical consultation. It is an ethically charged event requiring the clinician to simultaneously respect maternal autonomy, apply beneficence-based clinical judgment, and, after viability, fulfill obligations to the fetal patient as well. This article applies the professional responsibility model, grounded in the ethics of medicine as a profession developed by John Gregory and Thomas Percival, to the counseling process following prenatal detection of a fetal anomaly. The model requires physicians to maintain scientific and clinical competence, to place the health-related interests of both patients as their primary concern, and to preserve medicine as a public trust. Within this framework, autonomy, beneficence, and justice each impose specific obligations, and a preventive ethics approach demands that clinicians anticipate and address ethical conflict before it escalates. Large language models (LLMs) offer genuine capabilities to support these ethical obligations: personalizing diagnostic information, bridging language and health literacy barriers, and extending clinical support beyond the encounter itself. However, LLM-generated content should be clinician-reviewed before reaching patients, informed consent processes should disclose AI involvement, and implementation should actively address equity across care settings. The physician's role as guide, interpreter, and compassionate presence cannot be delegated to any algorithmic system. With appropriate governance, LLMs amplify the art of counseling rather than replace it.
