items.title: Association Between FLAIR Vascular Hyperintensities and Angiographic Collateral Status in Acute MCA Occlusion.
items.abstract: The clinical significance of Fluid Attenuated Inversion Recovery (FLAIR) vascular hyperintensities (FVHs) in acute ischemic stroke remains debated, particularly regarding their relationship with leptomeningeal collateral circulation. We aimed to assess the association between FVHs on baseline MRI and angiographic collateral status evaluated by digital subtraction angiography (DSA) in patients with middle cerebral artery (MCA) occlusion. We conducted a retrospective observational study including patients treated between 2010 to 2018 for an acute ischemic stroke due to isolated M1 MCA occlusion from two cohorts. All patients underwent baseline MRI with FLAIR sequences and pre-treatment DSA. FVHs were assessed using two approaches: a topographic score (FVH-ASPECTS) and a semi-quantitative score based on the number of axial FLAIR slices showing at least one FVH (FVH-slices). Collateral status was graded using the ASITN/SIR scale and dichotomized as poor (grades 0-2) or good (grades 3-4). Associations were evaluated using Spearman correlation, nonparametric tests, and logistic regression. Technical sensitivity analyses accounted for slice thickness and interslice spacing. Interreader agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients. Fifty-two patients were included. FVH-slices showed moderate-to-good interreader agreement (ICC = 0.77), whereas FVH-ASPECTS had lower reproducibility (ICC = 0.34). FVH-slices was weakly correlated with the full ASITN/SIR scale (ρ = 0.27, P = .053) and was higher in patients with good collaterals (P = .021). In univariable logistic regression, each 1-point increase was associated with higher odds of good collateral status (OR = 1.30; 95% CI, 1.00-1.70), but this association was attenuated after accounting for acquisition parameters. FVH-ASPECTS correlated with the full ASITN/SIR scale (ρ = 0.30, P = .029) but was not significantly associated with dichotomized collateral status. Neither FVH score nor ASITN/SIR grade was associated with 3-month functional outcome. FVH-slices was more reproducible than FVH-ASPECTS and showed a weak positive association with angiographic collateral status. However, attenuation after technical adjustment and the limited sample size indicate that these exploratory findings require prospective validation.

items.title: Changes in Biological Age Acceleration and Risk of Incident Diabetes: Results From Three Large Cohort Studies.
items.abstract: To investigate the associations of baseline and longitudinal changes in biological age acceleration with incident diabetes in three large prospective cohorts. This multi-cohort study included 474 109 participants from the Kailuan and Dongfeng-Tongji cohorts in China and the UK Biobank. Biological age was estimated using PhenoAge and Klemera-Doubal Method (KDM) age, both derived from nine routinely measured clinical indicators. Biological age acceleration was defined as the residual from regressing biological age on chronological age within each cohort, separately at baseline and the first follow-up. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were applied to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the associations of baseline biological age acceleration and its longitudinal changes (persistent accelerated ageing, delayed accelerated ageing, recovery from accelerated ageing and stable non-accelerated ageing) with the risk of diabetes. Results from the three cohorts were pooled using meta-analysis. Compared with non-accelerated ageing, baseline accelerated ageing was associated with a higher risk of diabetes (PhenoAge: pooled HR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.21-1.48; KDM age: pooled HR = 1.60, 95% CI: 1.34-1.92). In analyses of longitudinal changes, compared with participants with persistent accelerated ageing, those with delayed or recovered accelerated ageing had 21%-34% lower risks of diabetes (pooled HR ranges: PhenoAge, 0.72-0.79; KDM age, 0.66-0.67). Participants who consistently maintained non-accelerated ageing had the lowest risk of diabetes (PhenoAge: pooled HR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.54-0.61; KDM age: pooled HR = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.38-0.61). These findings suggest that biological age acceleration and its changes are associated with diabetes risks.

items.title: Regenerative Endodontic Treatment in Traumatized Immature Permanent Teeth: How Predictable Is the Outcome?
items.abstract: Pulp necrosis following traumatic dental injury in an immature permanent tooth interrupts root development, leaving thin dentinal walls and an open apex that compromise long-term tooth survival. Conventional apexification can predictably achieve apical barrier formation and periapical healing but does not promote continued root maturation. Regenerative endodontic treatment (RET) was developed to address this biological limitation. Two decades of experimental and clinical research have established the biological rationale and clinical potential of RET. Current evidence indicates that RET generally achieves its primary goal of periapical healing. However, its secondary goal-continued root development, including increased root length and dentinal wall thickness-is considerably less predictable. Radiographic root maturation varies substantially and does not necessarily translate into improved long-term tooth survival. The tertiary goal, recovery of pulp sensibility, is also inconsistently achieved, and predictable regeneration of a functional pulp-dentin complex has yet to be demonstrated. The aim of this mini-review was to synthesize the current evidence on the biological basis, clinical protocols, outcomes, adverse events, and long-term prognosis of RET in traumatized immature permanent teeth, with particular emphasis on treatment predictability. Three clinically and biologically distinct outcomes are distinguished: resolution of apical disease, continued root development, and true tissue regeneration. By integrating clinical and translational evidence, we identify what can reasonably be expected from RET, where uncertainty remains, and which factors may influence long-term outcomes. RET outcomes appear to be influenced by trauma severity, pre-operative apical periodontitis, and antimicrobial effectiveness. Periapical healing is the most consistently achieved outcome, whereas continued root maturation is less predictable, and regeneration of a functional pulp-dentin complex has not been demonstrated clinically. Whether RET provides a long-term survival advantage over apexification remains uncertain. Much of the available evidence derives from mixed populations of traumatic and developmental etiologies, and trauma-related pulp necrosis is associated with poorer continued root maturation.

items.title: Variable Demands Between Medical and Surgical Specialties in Initial Board Certification.
items.abstract: To characterize differences in initial specialty certification requirements, costs, and examination outcomes between American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS) member surgical and medical specialties. This descriptive study evaluated publicly available initial certification data for 24 primary ABMS member boards and five additional specialty-specific residency pathways (29 specialties total). Data from the 2024 testing cycle included certification costs, examination scheduling, first-time pass rates, case-list submission and oral examination requirements, and time in practice before certification eligibility. Specialties were classified using American College of Surgeons definitions and compared using Welch's t-tests and Fisher's exact tests. Written examination pass rates were similar between surgical and medical specialties (91.3% vs 86.5%, p = 0.11). Surgical specialties had fewer annual written examination dates (1.4 vs 11.4, p = 0.02) and more frequently required oral examinations (100% vs 22.2%, p < 0.001), case-list submissions (90.9% vs 16.7%, p < 0.001), and time in practice before certification eligibility (72.7% vs 16.1%, p < 0.01). Mean total certification costs were higher for surgical than medical specialties ($3,558 vs $2,305, p < 0.001), exceeding the maximum certification cost of any medical specialty. Initial ABMS certification requirements vary substantially across specialties. Surgical specialties generally impose greater financial and procedural burdens despite similar written examination pass rates. Greater transparency and evidence-based standardization may reduce these burdens and promote equitable access while preserving public trust.

items.title: Gestational PET-NP exposure induces placental injury and fetal growth restriction with a PPARα-associated transcriptional response.
items.abstract: The placental toxicity of polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastics (PET-NPs) during pregnancy remains poorly understood. Pregnant mice were orally exposed to 20-nm PET-NPs at 10 mg/kg/day from gestational day 3.5 to 17.5. PET-NP-associated fluorescence was detected in placental tissues, accompanied by placental injury, reduced fetal weight and crown-rump length, increased embryo mortality, and decreased fetal number. Placental RNA sequencing identified 1,532 differentially expressed genes. Enrichment analyses revealed suppression of proliferation-related transcriptional programs and positive enrichment of the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) signaling gene set. Network toxicology analysis also identified PPAR signaling and prioritized Ppara as a candidate for further investigation. PET-NP exposure increased placental expression of Ppara, Rxra, Acox1, Cd36, Acadm, and Pdk4. GW6471 treatment attenuated these transcriptional changes, alleviated placental injury, and improved fetal growth and embryo survival. Immunofluorescence staining further showed enhanced PPARα signals in CK7-positive trophoblast regions. In vitro, HTR8/SVneo trophoblasts internalized PET-NPs and subsequently exhibited impaired proliferation and migration, which were partially restored by GW6471. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the placental and developmental toxicity of gestational PET-NP exposure and support the potential involvement of a PPARα-associated response in the observed toxicity.

items.title: Detection of Early Enamel Optical Changes Following Erosive-Abrasive Challenges and Treatment Effects Using the Optipen Reflectometer: a Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the ability of a portable optical reflectometer to clinically detect early enamel optical changes caused by combined erosive-abrasive challenges, as well as to evaluate the effects of a standard treatment applied to previously eroded enamel. In this short-term randomized clinical trial, 72 participants were allocated to six groups according to treatment (water or Elmex® Erosion Protection) and challenge condition (control, erosion, or erosion+abrasion). After baseline measurements, all participants underwent a standardized erosive challenge, which consisted of rinsing with 30 ml of cola-based soft drink to create a comparable erosive condition. Enamel surface reflection intensity (%SRI) was measured on maxillary central incisors using a portable optical reflectometer (Optipen) before and after treatment application, after two hours of salivary exposure, and after final challenge. The final challenge consisted of water rinsing, cola rinsing, or cola rinsing followed by toothbrushing, according to group allocation. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA and Tukey's test (p<0.05). Significant effects were observed for treatment (p=0.001), condition (p=0.038), and moment (p=0.001), as well as for the interactions treatment × moment (p=0.035) and condition × moment (p=0.001). The erosive-abrasive condition resulted in the lowest %SRI values after the final challenge, regardless of treatment (p<0.05). Elmex® resulted in higher %SRI values than water immediately after treatment and after final challenge (p<0.05). The Optipen Reflectometer was able to detect early changes in enamel surface optical properties associated with erosive-abrasive challenges, as well as treatment-related differences in surface reflectance under clinical conditions. Portable optical reflectometry may provide a useful noninvasive approach for assessing early enamel optical changes associated with erosive-abrasive challenges, as well as treatment responses in vivo, supporting preventive research.

items.title: The Congenital Heart Technical Skill Study: Can Peer Surgeon Assessment of Technical Skill Predict Outcomes?
items.abstract: Motivated to improve patient outcomes, we launched The Congenital Heart Technical Skill Study in 2015. In this proof-of-concept study, we sought to test the validity of leveraging single, representative, self-selected, video recordings of volunteer, operating congenital heart surgeons and a peer-review mechanism to assess surgeon technical skill. In this national collaboration, volunteer surgeons submitted self-selected, "representative" videos of themselves performing: 1) Norwood procedures, 2) complete atrioventricular canal (CAVC) repairs, and/or 3) arterial switch operations (ASOs). Twenty-nine peer-surgeons from 21 centers rated pre-designated video segments, using a modified Objective Structured Assessment of Technical Skills Score (OSATS; scale 1-5). Operations were graded on five specific domains (gentleness, tissue exposure, instrument handling, time/motion, and flow of operation) and given summary scores. Scores were linked via NPI to all cases performed by participating surgeons over five contemporaneous years in The Society of Thoracic Surgeons-Congenital Heart Surgery Database. Logistic regression quantified risk-adjusted associations between skill scores and a composite outcome (major morbidity or mortality) among three, concentric, cohorts: 1) All Norwood, 2) all neonatal, and 3) all pediatric index cases. Models adjusted for clinical characteristics and clustered standard errors by surgeon. Seventeen surgeons from 14 centers submitted videos of themselves performing Norwood procedures (n=12), CAVC repairs (n=11), and ASOs (n=14). Over 5 years, these surgeons performed 234 Norwood, 1,755 index neonatal, and 8,559 index pediatric cases. Mean overall skill scores were 3.2 (SD ∼1.0) on Norwood, CAVC, and ASO videos. Scores correlated highly across sub-procedures (ρ's 0.8-0.9). Norwood and CAVC video scores were significantly associated with Norwood outcomes. One standard deviation increase in skill scores was associated with reduction in the risk-adjusted predicted probability of major morbidity or mortality among 5-years of surgeons' Norwood cases from 43% to 25%. Associations between skill scores and outcomes were weaker among all index neonatal and all index pediatric cases. Congenital heart surgeons' technical skills can be measured directly via peer assessment of single, representative, self-selected, video recordings. These Congenital Heart Technical Skill Scores (CHTSS) are strongly associated with risk-adjusted morbidity-free survival across five years of surgeons' Norwood cases. This could serve as a valuable tool in surgeons' quest for technical mastery and-more importantly-in the quest to improve patient outcomes.

items.title: Methodological and Reporting Quality of Systematic Reviews on Myopia Control: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal.
items.abstract: To evaluate the methodological confidence, reporting completeness, and citation impact of systematic reviews on interventions for myopia control. This study identifies priorities for improving methodological rigor and reporting completeness to support more reliable and clinically informative evidence synthesis in myopia. PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and Embase were searched from inception to November 13, 2025. Eligible articles were systematic reviews of interventions for myopia control or prevention that evaluated efficacy, effectiveness, and/or safety and were published in English-language academic journals. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed methodological rigor using AMSTAR 2 and reporting completeness using PRISMA 2020. Citation impact was quantified using the Web of Science-reported Average per Year metric retrieved on September 5, 2026, and analysed as log(average citations per year + 1). The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251169971). Ninety-one systematic reviews were included. Forty-five reviews (49%) were published in 2024 or 2025, and 56 (62%) had corresponding authors from China. AMSTAR 2 rated 51 reviews (56%) as critically low confidence, 26 (29%) as low, 6 (7%) as moderate, and 8 (9%) as high. Common limitations included inadequate protocol prespecification, incomplete literature searches, insufficient justification for excluded studies, and suboptimal risk-of-bias assessment. Mean PRISMA 2020 adherence was 75%, but certainty-of-evidence reporting was uncommon. Among 80 reviews with available citation data, citation impact did not differ across AMSTAR 2 confidence groups (P=0.38), but differed across intervention categories (P=0.01) and was weakly associated with journal impact factor (r=0.23; P=0.037). Systematic reviews on myopia control have increased rapidly but frequently show important methodological limitations. Clinicians should interpret the conclusions of these reviews cautiously, with more attention to the underlying quality of the evidence synthesis. Future evidence syntheses should prioritize rigor over volume through adherence to AMSTAR 2 and PRISMA 2020 standards and the development of living systematic reviews with outcome-level certainty assessments updated as new evidence emerges.

items.title: Free-living daily myofibrillar protein synthesis rates do not differ between vegan and omnivorous diets providing the RDA for protein in older adults.
items.abstract: Limited data exist on whether vegan diets providing modest protein intakes support daily myofibrillar protein synthesis (MyoPS) rates in older adults OBJECTIVES: To compare daily MyoPS rates, muscle thickness and gene expression in rested and exercised muscle between vegan and isonitrogenous omnivorous diets meeting the protein RDA METHODS: Twenty-two healthy older adults (12 males/10 females; age: 67±4 y; BMI: 25±3 kg/m2) participated in a randomised, parallel-group trial. After 3 days consuming habitual diets, participants consumed a 7-day vegan (VEGAN; n=11) or omnivorous (OMNI; n=11; 69% animal-derived protein) diet providing 0.8 g protein/kg body mass/day. Participants performed three unilateral resistance exercise bouts during the intervention. Deuterated water determined daily MyoPS rates during habitual and intervention periods. Muscle mRNA expression of 48 genes and ultrasound-derived quadriceps muscle thickness were assessed before and after intervention RESULTS: Protein intake decreased by 26% relative to habitual intake (P 0.05). Neither muscle thickness nor mRNA expression differed between groups (all P>0.05), although ten genes changed expression following the combined dietary and exercise intervention (P<0.05). A feasible vegan diet meeting the protein RDA, despite providing less protein than habitual intakes, supports daily MyoPS rates that do not differ from those supported by an isonitrogenous omnivorous diet in healthy older adults. This trial was registered at clinicaltrials.gov as NCT05985369.

items.title: Blood product use and direct costs after a bundled change in cardiac surgery and hemostatic management: a Brazilian before-and-after cohort study.
items.abstract: Viscoelastic testing reduces transfusion in cardiac surgery in high-income settings. Data from Brazilian publicly financed cardiac surgery programs are scarce. In February 2025 the organization replaced Del Nido cardioplegia with intermittent aortic cross-clamping and concomitantly introduced Rotational Thromboelastometry (ROTEM)-guided hemostatic management. Retrospective single-center before-and-after cohort of 137 consecutive adults undergoing elective coronary or heart valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass covered by public health system contracts, 68 before, 69 after the change. The primary outcome was total direct cost per patient (blood components, prothrombin complex concentrate, ROTEM consumables); secondary outcomes were this cost without consumables, transfusion exposure, mortality and re-exploration for bleeding. Analyses used bootstrap intervals, overlap weighting and bypass-duration stratification. Mean total direct cost per patient fell from BRL 1,230.16 to 526.78 (-703.38, 95% CI -1,148.24 to -240.71; -USD 130.13; -Int$ 275.40), a 57.2% reduction; without consumables, -BRL 839.03 (-1,254.85 to -418.57), 68.2%. Transfusion exposure fell from 61.8% to 39.1% (p = 0.010) and labile component units from 411 to 87, mostly through plasma and cryoprecipitate. Only 10 of 69 post-implementation patients underwent ROTEM. Median bypass duration fell from 77.5 to 51 minutes; accounting for it always attenuated the association. Mortality (7.4% vs. 7.2%) and re-exploration (1.5% vs. 2.9%) did not differ. The bundled change was accompanied by lower blood product use and direct costs. With ten deaths and three re-explorations, safety cannot be established. The differences should be interpreted at the level of the bundled organizational change and cannot be attributed to viscoelastic testing alone.

items.title: Quantifying transport contributions to elemental PM in Barcelona: a high-time-resolution multisite approach.
items.abstract: Recent changes in elemental particulate matter (PMel., or sum of individual elements analysed) concentrations and composition from road traffic and shipping call for an updated assessment. High-time-resolution PMel. measurements at three strategically selected Barcelona sites urban background (UBG), traffic (TRF), and harbour (HARB), enabled source- and element-specific assessment of urban air quality. Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF) was applied independently to PM10-el. and/or PM2.5-el. at each site. The high-resolution measurements captured short-term pollution episodes and distinguished local from regional/secondary sources. Compared with UBG, the hotspots (TRF, HARB) were enriched in anthropogenic (Fe, Cu, Zn, Ba, Cr, Mn, Pb, Ni, V) and crustal elements (Si, Ca, Ti, Fe). Sources of regional origin contributed 40-70% of PM10-el. and PM2.5-el. across all sites. Transport-related increments were substantial: Brake and Tyre-road wear contributions at TRF were >3-times higher than at UBG, and 1-h shipping plumes at HARB increased PM2.5-el. concentrations by ∼1.2 μg m-3 (∼26-40-times) relative to UBG. The multisite approach improved source apportionment by reducing the misattribution of ship-related S to Regional at the inland sites. The findings highlight the need for targeted mitigation strategies addressing both traffic and coastal shipping emissions.

items.title: A Novel Scoring System for Systematic Assessment of Functional Studies of KCNQ1 Variants.
items.abstract: Until recently, functional characterization has remained underutilized in the classification of variants in the KCNQ1 gene due to application at only the supporting level of evidence (PS3_Supporting or BS3_Supporting). The Potassium Channel Arrhythmia Variant Curation Expert Panel (VCEP) has addressed this by introducing a framework based on the most advanced methodologies currently available to guide the evaluation of functional evidence for PS3 or BS3 at enhanced strength. The development of a point-scoring system that rewards independent evidence from diverse assays reduces uncertainty in the evaluation of functional studies for KCNQ1 and other ion channel genes, providing a more reliable framework for variant interpretation.

items.title: From Selection to Seedlings: Tracking the Fate of Chestnuts and Acorns Cached by Blue Jays (Cyanocitta cristata).
items.abstract: Scatter-hoarding by rodents and birds is a key seed dispersal mutualism shaping forest ecosystems dominated by oaks (genus Quercus ) in eastern North America. Two processes of forest change, the ongoing decline of oak and the anticipated reintroduction of American chestnut ( Castanea dentata ; hereafter chestnut), are likely to be strongly influenced by the caching behavior of scatter-hoarding species. One of the most important long-distance dispersers of acorns and chestnuts in eastern North America is the Blue Jay ( Cyanocitta cristata ; hereafter jays). In this study, we assess the seed dispersal effectiveness of jays for chestnut and two species of oak common to the central Appalachians, white oak ( Quercus alba ) and black oak ( Quercus velutina ). We use radio telemetry of tagged seeds to track the initial fate of seeds taken by jays, and to locate cache sites. By planting seeds at cache sites and paired random locations we determine cache site habitat preferences of jays, and track the pilferage rates, germination, stem emergence, and seedling growth of planted seeds. Jays preferred to cache in shrubby early-successional habitat, and cached the three seed species at similar rates (~35%). Dispersal effectiveness was strongly limited by pilferage rates (> 80%), and first-year seedling survival of cached seeds was 2.6% for white oaks, 3.8% for black oaks, and 6.2% for chestnuts. Seed shadows of jay-dispersed seeds did not differ between the tree species, and most cache sites were located within 150 m of the origin sites (max dispersal distance = 460 m). We found some marginal support for the directed dispersal hypothesis, as stem emergence for both oak species was greater at cache sites than random sites. Overall, our results support the idea that jay scatter-hoarding behavior will shape chestnut reintroduction efforts and future oak regeneration.

items.title: As Canada Fast-Tracks Approvals on Landmark "Nation-Building Projects," Consider How Current Regulations Have Failed Canadian Wildlife and Indigenous Communities.
items.abstract: Shifting global economic forces have led Canada-the world's 2nd-largest country and 11th-biggest economy-to expedite development of natural resources and lessen dependence on the USA. This seismic shift in policy comes with new legislation that eases current regulations to allow faster development. We briefly highlight a body of research showing that current policies do not adequately protect biodiversity, thus fail to meet legal mandates for biodiversity conservation and legal treaty with Indigenous peoples. Diluting safeguards against environmental damage that are already demonstrably insufficient is likely to produce poor outcomes for wildlife. Instead of sidestepping regulations, investment in development can be accompanied by investment in nature and people. Planning informed by science and by Indigenous knowledge can strengthen Canada not only economically but also conserve its biotic communities while improving aspects of cultural life for Indigenous communities.

items.title: Field-Based Estimation of Bone Collagen Trophic Discrimination Factors in Brown Bears.
items.abstract: Trophic discrimination factors (TDFs) are essential for interpreting isotope data, but tissue- and species-specific estimates are often unavailable for long-turnover tissues in large mammals because long-term controlled feeding experiments are logistically difficult. This limitation is especially acute for bone collagen, which is the tissue most frequently analyzed in archaeological studies and is also promising for ecological studies of extant animals, because bone collagen permits retrospective reconstruction of isotopic histories. However, interpretation of bone collagen isotope ratios is often difficult because bone collagen-specific TDFs remain poorly resolved. Here, we estimated bone collagen TDFs for δ 13 C and δ 15 N in free-ranging brown bears ( Ursus arctos ) from the Shiretoko Peninsula, Hokkaido, Japan, using field-derived consumer and food-resource isotope data. Isotope ratios of femoral bone collagen were combined with isotope data for eight major dietary categories identified from regional food-resource and stomach-content information. Source isotope uncertainty was propagated by repeatedly drawing category-level source means from Bayesian posterior distributions, constructing source isotope convex hulls, and estimating the two-dimensional translation that best aligned source and consumer isotope spaces. Simulations evaluated recovery of known TDFs under varying diet compositions and isotope-space geometries. Estimated TDFs were 5.2‰ for δ 13 C and 3.6‰ for δ 15 N, with empirical 95% quantile intervals of 4.3‰-5.7‰ and 2.3‰-4.3‰, respectively. Recovery accuracy depended strongly on the geometry of consumer isotope ratios relative to the source mixing space, but simulated datasets most similar to the observed geometry showed lower median Euclidean error than the full simulation set. To our knowledge, this study provides the first estimates of TDFs for brown bear bone collagen. Although these estimates are derived from field data rather than conventional controlled feeding experiments, our approach provides a new framework for estimating TDFs in tissues such as bone collagen, for which experimental determination is difficult.

items.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Proteomic Analysis Reveals Altitude-Associated Molecular Responses in the Honey Bee (Apis mellifera).
items.abstract: Honey bees inhabit a broad range of elevations, yet how they adjust physiologically and molecularly to high-altitude environments remains incompletely understood. Here, we compared the thoracic transcriptomes and proteomes of Apis mellifera populations collected from high- and low-altitude sites in Tibet. In high-altitude bees, transcriptional changes were mainly associated with oxidative phosphorylation, the citrate cycle, pyruvate metabolism, thermogenesis, cardiac muscle contraction, and motor proteins, indicating prominent changes in pathways related to energy metabolism and muscle-related functions. In contrast, genes associated with longevity regulation were predominantly downregulated. Proteomic differences were mainly concentrated in metabolic pathways. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further revealed increased expression of immune-related molecules in high-altitude bees. Because immune activity is energetically costly, this response may represent an additional component of the energetic investment required for high-altitude adaptation. The coordinated molecular changes in energy metabolism, muscle function, and immune activity may help honey bees maintain physiological performance under high-altitude conditions, while the downregulation of longevity-associated pathways may reflect trade-offs in resource allocation and somatic maintenance. These results highlight the coordinated molecular adjustments underlying honey bee responses to high-altitude environments.

items.title: Sensitivity of Landscape Genomic Outlier Detection to Outbreak Dynamics.
items.abstract: Landscape genomics aims to link patterns of genetic variation to environmental heterogeneity and is widely used to infer local adaptation in natural populations. These approaches typically assume that genetic patterns are relatively stable through time, an assumption that is unlikely to hold in outbreaking species characterized by rapid changes in population size, connectivity, and spatial extent. During outbreaks, demographic processes can generate spatial structure through expansion and drift, and subsequently erode that structure through increased dispersal and admixture, complicating the detection of adaptive variation. Here, we use a large SNP dataset from the eastern spruce budworm ( Choristoneura fumiferana ) to test how outbreak dynamics affect the identification of putative adaptive loci. We compared outlier loci across multiple time points (2013-2017) using three commonly applied methods (OutFLANK, LFMM, and redundancy analysis-[RDA]). Across methods, the number of detected outliers declined sharply through time, with little overlap in locus identity among years and limited agreement among methods. These results suggest that signals interpreted as local adaptation may be sensitive to demographic context and are often transient, emerging during early stages of expansion and breaking down as connectivity increases and allele frequencies become more homogeneous. Under these conditions, genome-scan approaches can produce unstable or misleading results, often reflecting demographic processes rather than selection. This has direct implications for the use of genomic data in management and monitoring, particularly for native outbreaking and invasive species, where inference of connectivity, dispersal, and adaptive potential is often based on single snapshots of genetic variation.

items.title: Statistical optimization of morphological analysis for various developed zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (ZIFs) using design of experiments.
items.abstract: Zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (ZIFs) have attracted considerable attention owing to their high porosity, stability, and controllable physicochemical characteristics that can be used in drug delivery, gas separation, catalysis, and sensing, where particle size plays a critical role in determining performance. In this study, the design of experiment (DOE) approach based on response surface methodology (RSM) was used to optimize synthesis parameters of three types of zeolitic imidazolate frameworks, including ZIF-4, ZIF-11, and ZIF-67. Central composite design (CCD) was employed to examine the individual and combined influence of the concentration of metal precursors, ligands, and volume of solvent on the average particle size. Quadratic regression equations for each system were derived and validated via ANOVA. All three models were statistically significant ( p ≤ 0.0001), with R 2 values ranging from 0.9309 to 0.9793 and non-significant lack-of-fit tests ( p > 0.05). Numerical optimization using the desirability function identified predicted optimal particle sizes of 114.754, 63.822, and 102.531 µm for ZIF-4, ZIF-11, and ZIF-67, respectively. Experimental validation yielded particle sizes of 123.54, 66.50, and 103.60 µm, corresponding to relative prediction errors of 7.11%, 4.03%, and 1.03%, respectively. The close agreement between the predicted and experimentally measured particle sizes supports the predictive capability of the developed models within the investigated experimental domains. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis provided morphological and particle size characterization of the optimized samples, while X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis confirmed the characteristic crystalline structures of the synthesized ZIFs. Overall, the developed DOE-RSM framework provides a systematic approach for optimizing ZIF synthesis conditions and controlling particle size within the investigated experimental ranges.

items.title: The New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax) currently affecting the Americas and risk factors for the EU.
items.abstract: The New World screwworm (NWS), Cochliomyia hominivorax , is an obligate parasite of living warm-blooded animals that causes traumatic myiasis in domestic and wild animals and humans. Following its re-emergence in Panama in June 2023, NWS spread northwards through Central America and Mexico and was detected in the United States in June 2026. This scientific report summarises available information on the biology, ecology, identification, host susceptibility and health effects of NWS; describes the current incursions and measures recommended or applied in affected and at-risk countries; and considers potential pathways for entry into the European Union (EU). Evidence was collected through a systematic literature review and reviews of official and other relevant sources. NWS has a broad host range, with cattle the principal livestock species affected in the current incursions, while infestations also occur in other domestic animals, wildlife and humans. Its development, survival and activity are strongly influenced by temperature and environmental conditions, and the movement of infested animals is an important driver of geographic spread. Surveillance, animal inspection and treatment, movement controls and the sterile insect technique (SIT) are key components of current control programmes; SIT was associated with successful area-wide eradication in historical programmes in the past. Potential pathways for entry into the EU include movement of infested live animals and infested human travellers. Importation through non-live animal commodities and commodities of non-animal origin is not considered a potential pathway, while introduction through migratory birds is not considered biologically plausible. Important uncertainties arise from differences in surveillance and reporting, underdetection of infestations and unquantified illegal animal movements.

items.title: Structural connectivity measures predict urban bird richness better than functional connectivity measures, even after controlling for habitat amount.
items.abstract: Context Urban planning increasingly emphasizes landscape connectivity to mitigate biodiversity loss. However, across the many connectivity measures available, they are rarely validated against biological outcomes or disentangled from the independent effects of habitat amount, especially across spatial scales. Thus, the independent role of connectivity structuring biodiversity is unclear. Objectives Our objective was to evaluate how different types of connectivity metrics independently predict urban species richness after controlling for habitat availability. We aimed to quantify the strength and direction of the relationship between a set of connectivity metrics on urban avian richness. Methods We evaluated the relationship between bird species richness, based on 148,899 eBird checklists across 18 Canadian cities, and a set of connectivity metrics calculated with high-resolution land cover data using generalized additive models. We modelled checklist-level bird richness as a function of ten connectivity metrics spanning four categories, structural, graph‑network, potential, and functional connectivity. To disentangle the independent effect of the connectivity metrics, the models included habitat amount and sampling effort, across three spatial scales. Results Generalized additive models accounting for habitat amount, sampling effort, spatial autocorrelation, and city effects explained 30-33% of deviance in species richness, but connectivity metrics contributed relatively little independent explanatory power. Contrary to expectations, simple structural metrics describing greenspace aggregation and cohesion were positively associated with species richness, and consistently outperformed graph‑based, potential, and functional measures. However, connectivity effects weakened with increasing spatial scale. Conclusions Our results suggest that, for urban birds, landscape configuration influences richness primarily through habitat aggregation, supporting the use of simple structural metrics in urban conservation planning.

items.title: Amino acids in insects: An integrated regulatory network linking metabolism, nutrient sensing, physiology, behavior and adaptation.
items.abstract: Amino acids are fundamental to insect biology, but their functions extend far beyond their established roles as substrates for protein synthesis and nitrogen metabolism. They also act as metabolic intermediates, signaling molecules and determinants of resource allocation. This review follows a causal sequence: dietary and symbiont-derived supply, nutrient choice, digestion and transport, tissue allocation and metabolic fate, intracellular sensing and endocrine integration, and physiological, behavioral and ecological outcomes. Amino acid requirements differ among species, life stages and symbiotic states, and we separate individual free amino acids, hydrolysates, intact proteins, protein-to-carbohydrate balance and general nutritional status, which are often treated as interchangeable exposures. Nutritional geometry has established whole-animal regulation of macronutrient intake in several orders, whereas amino acid-specific appetite has been resolved at the cellular level mainly in Drosophila. Isotope-tracer studies in Lepidoptera, Hymenoptera and mosquitoes show how dietary amino acids are oxidized, incorporated and transferred to eggs, and TORC1 and GCN2 emerge as interacting, context-dependent components of a larger signaling network. We assess amino acid effects on development, immunity, stress tolerance, neural function, parasitoid-host and microbial interactions, and we mark where inference outruns experiment. Applications in pest and vector management are graded by whether they rest on laboratory mechanism, behavioral assay or field trial. We close with research priorities framed as specific questions, including functional tests beyond Diptera, tissue-resolved flux analysis and integration of amino acid signals with carbohydrate and lipid signals.

items.title: Multiple elements, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and stable isotope ratios (δ<sup>13</sup>C and δ<sup>15</sup>N) in the blood and feathers of White Stork nestlings.
items.abstract: White Storks (Ciconia ciconia) forage across agricultural, wetland, urban and waste-associated habitats, making their nestlings potential sentinels of local pollutant exposure. We sampled 30 nestlings from 26 nests in Podunavlje (20 nestlings, 17 nests) and at the Jakuševec landfill (10 nestlings, 9 nests), Croatia. In Podunavlje, feathers were analysed for δ 13 C, δ 15 N, total mercury (Hg) and 39 other elements, and whole blood for 38 elements; 16 priority polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) were measured in blood from both areas. Isotope-element associations were evaluated at the nest level in Podunavlje only. Feather δ 15 N was positively associated with feather Hg and explained most of its variation (R 2 = 0.64), whereas feather δ 13 C showed an exploratory association with blood barium (Ba). Blood PAH profiles were dominated by low-molecular-weight compounds, particularly naphthalene, and pyrene, medium-molecular-weight PAHs and acenaphthene were higher at Jakuševec. These findings illustrate the potential value of White Stork nestlings for preliminary biomonitoring and warrant larger, replicated studies.

items.title: An integrated overview from RadoNorm work package 4: advances and remaining challenges in radon and NORM risk assessment.
items.abstract: This paper synthesizes the achievements of Work Package 4 (WP4) of the European RadoNorm project (2020-2025) in radon and naturally occurring radioactive material (NORM) risk assessment. WP4 addressed four interconnected questions: the joint action of radon and tobacco smoke in lung carcinogenesis, health effects beyond adult lung cancer such as extrapulmonary diseases and childhood cancers, methodological uncertainties in radon risk estimates, also including thoron interference, and combined radiological and chemical stressors in wildlife.Combining epidemiological, mechanistic, dosimetric, and ecological approaches, the project advanced understanding on several fronts. On the epidemiological side, re-analysis of three European case-control studies indicated that the radon-smoking interaction was better described as sub-multiplicative than strictly multiplicative, with the functional form varying between populations. Lifetime Excess Absolute Risk estimates were in turn found to depend on model choice, with miner-based models yielding higher values per exposure unit than residential-based ones. A multinational childhood cancer analysis used organ-specific radon doses for the first time, whereas investigations of extrapulmonary endpoints found no clear evidence of radon-related risks at low exposures, however uncertainties remain. Mechanistic work complemented these findings by identifying conserved alterations in DNA repair pathways across species and distinct molecular profiles from combined radon and cigarette smoke exposure, with Adverse Outcome Pathway and Aggregate Exposure Pathway frameworks providing a mechanistic basis for the combined effects. Methodological and ecological contributions complemented the results: historical radon surveys in low-radon regions were shown to overestimate radon concentrations by up to a factor of two when thoron contributions were ignored, and a new population-level model incorporating mortality, reproduction, repair, and acclimation processes extended risk assessment to combined radiological and chemical stressors in non-human biota.Building on these results, six research directions are proposed to guide the next generation of work in this field. On the mechanistic and biological side, these include the translation of qualitative mechanistic evidence into quantitative Adverse Outcome Pathways that link defined exposure levels to adverse outcomes, a broader characterization of low-dose non-cancer and developmental effects at environmentally relevant exposure levels, and the derivation of age-specific exposure-response functions to inform radiation protection guidance for children. On the measurement and infrastructure side, systematic quantification of thoron-related bias at the European scale through coordinated detector re-evaluation and paired radon-thoron measurement campaigns, together with the deployment of federated analysis platforms to enable multinational pooled analyses, would support the empirical basis of future risk estimates. In the ecological domain, empirical parameterization of population models for chronic low-dose mixed exposures is required to render such models predictive rather than exploratory. Addressing these research directions would contribute to keeping regulatory frameworks aligned with the EU Beating Cancer Plan and One Health strategies informed by current scientific evidence.

items.title: "It's their house": unintended consequences of healthcare privatization in US Correctional facilities.
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to intend to examine correctional healthcare workers' different experiences and challenges in private versus public settings across the US. While quantitative research consistently demonstrates that privatized correctional healthcare produces worse health outcomes, this study sought to identify mechanisms responsible. Design/methodology/approach The author conducted semi-structured interviews with correctional healthcare workers in jails and prisons across the US in facilities with private (n = 19) and public (n = 27) healthcare. Findings Healthcare workers in correctional facilities with private healthcare reported less autonomy and authority when negotiating with custody staff and readily acquiesced to appeals of "safety and security." Additionally, the turnover of private healthcare companies resulted in administrative and policy turnover, leading to compromised ethical standards and procedures. Originality/value The study supplements quantitative research that documents higher mortality in privatized settings. By interviewing frontline healthcare workers, the study provides insight into how contracting care alters workplace dynamics above and beyond simple "cost-cutting" explanations.

items.abstract: Strong gravitational lensing is a powerful tool for investigating the universe's large-scale structure and understanding the properties of dark matter and dark energy. The magnification and distortion of distant background sources by cluster lenses have enabled detailed studies of both lens and source populations, making these systems promising probes for precision cosmology. While classical strong-lenses are well understood, much remains to be explored for hyperbolic-umbilic (HU) exotic lenses, which produce unique telescopic effects and uncommon images with potentially very high magnifications. Identifying and quantifying these objects, along with characterising their geometric configurations, could have broad implications for studies of galaxy clusters and lensed galaxy populations. z<10 ). items.title: Cosmic CORALS: Timing the Universe with high-z star clusters
items.abstract: In this work, we explore the potential of anchoring the age--redshift relation across cosmic time by probing the oldest star clusters at high redshifts, now observed thanks to the Space Telescope in strongly lensed fields. As a case study, we consider one of the highest-redshift systems observed, the Cosmic Gems arc at z=9.625. We performed image deconvolution of multi-band JWST imaging, identifying a total of 20 point sources along the arc. We derived the stellar ages through a cosmology-independent spectral energy distribution fitting framework, ensuring that these measurements can be used as unbiased cosmological anchors. By combining these high-z systems with state-of-the-art local globular cluster ages, we performed a joint Bayesian fit to the age--redshift relation in a flat Λ cold dark matter model, measuring H_0=70^ James Webb +27 _ -16 km -1 Mpc^ -1 and Ω_m=0.33^ +0.37 _ -0.21 . While these constraints are still loose, we show that the slope of the degeneracy, a power law in the Ω_m - H_0 plane, is highly dependent on the redshift of the sources, becoming shallower as redshift increases. Leveraging this geometric rotation, we present forecasts showing that a future sample of ∼ 300 lensed proto-globular clusters well distributed up to z ≈ 10 could tighten the statistical precision to 4% on H_0 and 11% on Ω_m; this is competitive with and independent of methods currently in use. The present work, therefore, represents a new avenue in cosmology and comes at a timely moment, when JWST is observing high-redshift lensed star clusters routinely and and the Space Telescope are uncovering new strong lensing fields, and close to the start of operation of the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. items.title: The X-ray catalogue of FGK stars within 10 pc: The coronal temperature-brightness relation explained with the RTV scaling law
items.abstract: A comprehensive measurement of stellar X-ray emission has important implications for our understanding of stellar dynamos, exoplanet atmosphere loss, and evaporation of protoplanetary disks. However, the samples discussed in the literature are often biased and the X-ray properties reported in published catalogues are often not homogeneously derived. We present a volume-limited catalogue of X-ray detections of the FGK-type main-sequence stars within 10,pc, which properly accounts for stellar multiplicity and considers the instrumental effect of optical loading of the X-ray detectors. The FGK,10pc sample derives from a recent Gaia -based catalogue of all stars in a sky volume of 10,pc around the Sun from which we extract all stars of spectral type F, G, and K. To build the X-ray catalogue, we retrieved and analysed all observations from SRG (Spectrum Roentgen Gamma)/eROSITA and XMM-Newton for stars in the FGK,10pc sample, and we cross-matched the sample with ROSAT catalogues. After accounting for optical loading, flares, and multiplicity, we fitted thermal plasma models to the X-ray spectra to derive X-ray fluxes and coronal temperatures. The FGK,10pc sample comprises 60 stars and has an X-ray completeness of 95%. We present a detailed investigation of the relation between coronal temperature and X-ray surface flux and we find the result to be consistent with the ranges covered by different types of coronal magnetic structures observed on the Sun. The lower end of the temperature-brightness relation is defined by the Maunder minimum star HD,166620 and three other stars whose positions identify them as possible Maunder minimum candidates. We identify systematic differences between the temperature-brightness law derived from XMM-Newton and eROSITA data that we attribute to their different instrumental response functions. For the first time, we study the impact of variability, both short-term flaring and long-term activity cycles, on the evolution of coronal temperature along with X-ray brightness. With the exception of three stars, a remarkably small scatter is observed in the temperature-brightness relation across the whole FGK,10pc sample. A natural explanation of the empirical kT-F_!̊m X relation is provided by the Rosner-Tucker-Vaiana (RTV) scaling laws defined for solar hydrostatic magnetic loops. The small spread of the observed relation indicates a universal scaling between the length and filling factor of coronal loops. Three observed outliers to the relation are stars that deviate from this invariance of the ratio of loop length to filling factor for an unknown reason.

items.title: The Pristine Survey. XXX. Mapping substructures in the inner and outer halo with blue horizontal branch stars
items.abstract: Blue horizontal branch (BHB) stars serve as good standard candles and kinematic tracers of the Milky Way halo. The halo displays various overdensities and kinematical substructures of different shapes and sizes. Our objective is to investigate the substructure in three dimensions and the bulk motion of the halo up to distances well exceeding the limit of the parallaxes. Gaia We selected BHB stars in the łeft(u-CaHK̊ight) _ 0-$(g-r) _ 0$ colour-colour diagram with a hierarchical Bayesian mixture model of three populations: BHB stars, blue straggler stars, and outliers. Using CaHK photometry derived from XP spectra and the Pristine survey, we provide both a shallow and a deep catalogue of BHB stars of 7,057 and 8,824 stars, respectively, where the deep catalogue is restricted to the deeper Pristine footprint compared to the shallower with XP. Using the shallow catalogue, we trace to larger distances 6D substructures identified earlier within a 2.5 kpc from the Sun, including accepted populations; namely, Gaia-Enceladus, Thamnos, Helmi streams, Sequoia, and other smaller halo substructures such as ED-3, ED-4, and ED-6. The deep catalogue provides reliable distance measurements for a more detailed 3D mapping of the Sagittarius stream and of the Pisces Overdensity. We add new candidate BHB stars with line-of-sight velocities to existing catalogues and confirm previously reported differences between the northern and southern Galactic hemispheres, likely due to the infall of the Large Magellanic Cloud. Gaia Gaia This research demonstrates that probabilistic photometric classification can effectively identify distant candidate BHB stars, and can provide catalogues of these stars that enhance our understanding of the 3D and 6D structures in the halo of the Milky Way.

items.title: The spatial structure of solar magnetoconvection at scales up to 60 Mm.
items.abstract: While convective motions at the scale of granules on the solar surface are well understood, those of mesogranular and supergranulation are not. At still larger scales, the lack of giant cells is a major mystery. We aim to slightly improve understanding of the radial and horizontal flows associated with mesogranular scales and supergranulation. We performed a deep MURaM small-scale dynamo simulation, extending from 50 Mm below the solar surface and with a horizontal size of 60 Mm and sufficient resolution to begin to properly resolve the magnetic bright points in intergranular lanes. We determined the structure of the convective modes from the simulations at different scales, and compared the power spectra to those which have been previously observed. At all scales that are resolved by the simulation, the simulated flows agree with the amplitude implied by Doppler measurements and local correlation tracking measurements. The power in the vertical Doppler velocities at supergranular and larger scales is shown to be affected by density perturbations near the surface. The structure of the modes at depth is simple, as expected from previous studies, except the horizontal forcing scale scales as H_̊ho^2/3 instead of H̊ho. The simulations reproduce the observations up to scales of 60 Mm. Within the simulated range, l>=70, no excess power associated with the convective conundrum is detected.

items.title: ALMA detection of continuum emission from GQ Lup B
items.abstract: GQ Lup B is a massive (10-40 M_ Jup ) companion orbiting the young T-Tauri star GQ Lup A at a projected distance of ∼110 au (0.7''). It lies outside the circumprimary disk in the submillimeter continuum , but its ∼,63^̧irc inclined orbit intersects the primary's gas disk twice per period. We report a 5.8σ detection of continuum emission at the location of GQ Lup B, obtained with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at 0.89 mm (band 7). We associate this emission with a dusty disk around the companion, already detected by VLT/NACO and JWST/MIRI in the mid-infrared. To date, this is the third disk observed at millimeter wavelengths around a companion spanning the brown dwarf and planetary mass regimes , following PDS 70 c, a gas giant embedded in the parent circumstellar disk, and SR 12 c, a planetary mass companion at 1200 au from the primary. We retrieve a point source with a peak intensity of 54.5 , co-spatial with GRAVITY astrometry. The emission is spatially unresolved, Jy, beam^ -1 placing an upper limit of 2.3 au on the source radius (from a synthesized beam of ∼,29 disks. mas). For comparison, this is smaller than 1/3 of the Hill radius (3-5 au for GQ Lup B, depending on the assumed mass), the theoretical upper limit for circumplanetary Assuming optically thin thermal emission from millimeter-sized grains in a disk-like structure , we infer a mass of 0.0032 M_⊕, while the optically thick limit yields an emission radius of 0.2 au. Assuming a gas-to-dust ratio of 100, our results indicate a very low disk-mass-to-accretion-rate ratio, on the order of sim10^4 yr, analogously to the highest accretors in the stellar mass regime. In the case of GQ Lup B, this can be explained by its periodic crossing of the circumprimary disk, which could deliver a substantial amount of gas to the companion's disk over a long timescale.

items.title: Precise deep-learning reconstruction of galaxy cluster mass maps and substructures from optical observations
items.abstract: Accurately mapping the total mass distribution within galaxy clusters, including dark matter, is fundamental to understanding structure formation and constraining cosmological parameters. Standard mass mapping relies almost exclusively on gravitational lensing, which often yields smooth distributions based on analytical profiles, thereby missing critical internal substructures. We introduce a complementary, simulation-based inference approach to reconstruct detailed galaxy cluster mass maps and resolve internal substructures directly from optical imaging. We trained deep learning models on realistic hydro-simulated galaxy clusters to interpret observed cluster images. This framework was then applied to observations of real galaxy clusters obtained by the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) as part of the Cluster Lensing And Supernova survey with Hubble (CLASH) program. The reconstructed mass maps successfully reproduce the overall shapes and radial mass profiles of the CLASH clusters, showing strong agreement with independent gravitational lensing measurements. Using the subhalos derived from these reconstructed maps, we find that their mass functions exhibit a power-law behavior broadly consistent with predictions from numerical simulations. Our results demonstrate that combining optical imaging with deep learning provides a scalable, physically meaningful approach to mapping cluster masses. This framework opens a new avenue for utilizing upcoming wide-field imaging surveys to systematically study dark matter substructures, complementing traditional lensing techniques across much larger samples. Furthermore, the model is inherently flexible and can integrate multiwavelength data, such as X-ray and Sunyaev-Zeldovich observations, to further improve total mass predictions.

items.title: Properties of chromium and manganese in Tycho's supernova remnant with XRISM/Resolve
items.abstract: The X-ray emission of young supernova remnants (SNRs) gives access to the composition and spatial distribution of elements ejected in supernovae. The emission from the ejecta provides crucial insights into the explosion mechanism, especially for Fe-group elements formed in the innermost layers of the star. The objective of this paper is to provide constraints on the supernova progenitor and explosion mechanism of Tycho's type Ia supernova remnant by studying the properties of Cr and Mn. We analyzed /Resolve high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy observations of five regions of Tychos's supernova remnant, which were performed during the performance-verification phase and the AO1 phase. Gaussian line modeling was first used to determine the spatial distribution and intensity of Cr and Mn Kα lines. We then modeled the emission of the Cr, Mn and Fe plasma in each pointing with two nonequilibrium ionization shock models to reproduce both the front- and rear-emitting sides of the shocked ejecta shell. Mass ratios of Cr/Fe, Mn/Fe, and Mn/Cr are compared with expectations from different Type Ia supernova models from 1D and 3D numerical simulations. XRISM The unprecedented spectral resolution of /Resolve allows us to detect significant emission lines of Cr and Mn in different regions of Tycho's supernova remnant, even on small scales, providing a much more precise spatial distribution of Cr and Mn with respect to previous measurements. Significant Cr and Mn emission lines are observed in the Fe-bright northeastern-to-southeastern emitting rim; some are observed in the center region, but none in the southern region. The observed mass ratios of Mn/Fe, Cr/Fe, and Mn/Cr, are consistent with 1D delayed detonation models of near-Chandrasekhar-mass Type Ia supernovae and 1D pure-detonation models of 1 M_⊙ sub-Chandrasekhar-mass progenitors. In both cases, the observations imply supersolar zero-age main-sequence progenitor metallicities. XRISM Overall, the best agreement is found for models with metallicities too high to be realistic for Tycho's location. This points to additional sources of neutronization such as carbon simmering for a Chandrasekhar-mass progenitor. For sub-Chandrasekhar-mass, double-detonation models with a white-dwarf mass lower than 1M_⊙ are suggested.

items.title: Associations between multiple early risk factors and cognitive functioning at time of diagnosis in adolescents and adults with first-episode psychosis.
items.abstract: First-episode psychosis (FEP) is associated with widespread cognitive impairments. Several early risk factors for psychosis have been identified, and some studies suggest associations between early risk factors and cognition, yet the literature is sparse in psychosis populations. Clinical cohorts of adolescent and adult patients with FEP and healthy controls (HC) were linked with register-based information (N = 276). Gestational age, Apgar scores, birth weight and length, parental age, and season of birth were extracted from the Danish medical birth registry. Cognition was assessed at time of diagnosis using BACS, CANTAB, and WAIS-III/WISC-IV. Missing data was imputed using MICE. Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) was used to examine patterns of associations. Post hoc analyses explored group differences according to diagnosis, age, and sex. CCA resulted in two significant patterns of associations. CCA1 was stable across imputations (r = 0.44, p = .036, pmin = .017, pmax = .055) and constituted by a risk profile of lower maternal age, lower birth length, being small for gestational age, and lower birth weight and a cognitive profile of lower estimated IQ and poorer working memory, mental flexibility, processing speed, verbal fluency, and motor latency. The pattern was more expressed in FEP compared to HC and in adults compared to adolescents. CCA2 was more unstable across imputations (r = 0.38, p = .033, pmin = .003, pmax = .168) and constituted by a broad pattern of minor loadings. Cognitive functioning later in life is associated with multiple early risk factors, underscoring the complexity of developmental processes and the importance of the early developmental context in shaping cognitive trajectories.

items.title: The invisible insult: replication-independent neurotoxicity of viral and bacterial factors in post-infectious neurological syndromes.
items.abstract: Post-viral neurological syndromes, including Neuro-PASC (long COVID), HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders, and flavivirus-associated encephalopathies, present a paradox: neurological dysfunction persists despite minimal or absent viral replication in the central nervous system (CNS), challenging the replication-dependent models of neuropathogenesis. This review synthesizes evidence for a "protein-as-pathogen" framework in which viral proteins, independent of intact virus or active replication, act as neurotoxic effectors: they breach the blood-brain barrier, activate neuroinflammatory cascades, induce neuronal death, and seed chronic proteinopathies. The same principle extends to bacterial factors such as lipopolysaccharide and curli, which converge on these pathways and point to a CNS vulnerability independent of pathogen class. We treat this as a complement to replication- and reservoir-based pathogenesis, not a replacement. We performed a comprehensive analysis of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein (S1) as a paradigmatic case study, then extended this framework through comparative analysis of human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1) gp120, flavivirus proteins (NS1, capsid, NS2A), and influenza A proteins (M1, NS1, nucleoprotein). Despite distinct viral origins and structural properties, these proteins exploit conserved host vulnerabilities. Toll-like receptor (TLR) 4 emerges as a convergent hub for microglial activation, with downstream NOD-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome assembly amplifying neuroinflammation through interleukin (IL)-1β release. Mitochondrial dysfunction, characterized by membrane depolarization, reactive oxygen species production, and impaired mitophagy, links acute protein exposure to chronic oxidative stress and proteinopathic seeding. Neuronal death pathways show virus-specific divergence: S1 induces necroptosis via NRP1/RIPK1, gp120 triggers apoptosis through CXCR4/CCR5 acting in concert with microglia-derived neurotoxins, and ZIKV envelope protein activates PARP-1-dependent parthanatos. All proteins converge on IL-1β-mediated inflammatory neuronal killing and complement-dependent synaptic elimination that persists beyond detectable viral clearance. The protein-as-pathogen framework reveals mechanistic unity across superficially disparate post-viral and post-bacterial syndromes and identifies druggable convergent pathways, including TLR4, NLRP3, complement, and mitochondrial targets, amenable to therapeutic intervention with existing compounds. This framework has direct implications for diagnosis (protein biomarkers), prognosis (determinants of protein persistence), and treatment (protein-targeted versus downstream anti-inflammatory strategies) of post-viral neurological disease.

items.title: Inequalities in quitting smoking and use of support among women by age and socioeconomic position: a population study in England.
items.abstract: Mid-life may be a particularly challenging period to quit smoking among women, especially those from less advantaged socioeconomic groups. Differences in quit attempt characteristics, use of evidence-based support, and nicotine dependence may contribute to lower quit success, but their relative importance remains unclear. We analysed data from 7,791 women in the Smoking Toolkit Study (England, 2013-2026) who attempted to stop smoking in the past year. Age was categorised as younger (16-44 years), mid-life (45-60 years), and older (> 60 years), and social grade as more (ABC1) or less advantaged (C2DE). Logistic regression models examined differences in quit attempt characteristics (planned vs. unplanned, abrupt vs. gradual), use of evidence-based support (e-cigarettes, prescription nicotine replacement therapy, non-nicotine pharmacotherapy, face-to-face behavioural support), and quit success, adjusted for survey year and relevant covariates. Mid-life women had the lowest quit success (18.1%) compared with younger (22.3%) and older women (20.6%), with the lowest quit success observed among less advantaged mid-life women (15.8% vs. 25.2% among more advantaged younger women; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.56, 95%CI 0.45-0.69). Yet, mid-life women were among the most likely to use evidence-based support (more advantaged: 45.8%; less advantaged: 47.4%), comparable to younger less advantaged women (46.4%) and higher than other groups (36.9-40.0%). Adjustment for quit attempt characteristics and use of evidence-based support had minimal impact on age-related differences in quit success. However, adjustment for nicotine dependence attenuated the lower odds of success in mid-life women. In fully adjusted models with younger more advantaged women as the reference category, less advantaged mid-life women had the lowest odds of quitting (aOR = 0.75, 95%CI 0.58-0.98), older more advantaged women had higher odds (aOR = 1.36, 95%CI 1.02-1.82), and differences for other groups were not evident (aORs 0.93-1.16). Less advantaged mid-life women are the least likely to be successful in their attempts to stop smoking, despite relatively high uptake of evidence-based support. Higher nicotine dependence partly explains this disparity, but other factors also likely contribute and warrant further investigation.

items.title: Consciousness, complexity, and clinical implications.
items.abstract: Consciousness remains one of science's most challenging problems because it cannot be exhaustively characterized as a single function, computation, or behavior; it also refers to the presence and organization of subjective experience. This position paper integrates clinical neurology, neurophysiology, psychiatry, psychoanalysis, embodied cognition, moral neuroscience, theoretical physics, philosophy of mind, and neurotechnology. We argue that, despite major advances in identifying neural correlates, computational models, and behavioral markers, contemporary consciousness research has not resolved the explanatory gap between objective description and subjective experience. We propose that claims about consciousness at neurophysiological, embodied, cognitive, social, and ontological levels should be coordinated through explicit cross-level constraints rather than merged into a single unitary theory. These domains have different evidential roles and are not all constituents of consciousness. Perturbational measures of cortical complexity, including the Perturbational Complexity Index (PCI) and its state-transition variant (PCIst), support assessment of preserved conscious capacity in studied human populations. They do not independently determine a clinical diagnosis or phenomenal content. Evidence from aphasia, sleep, anesthesia, and disorders of consciousness also demonstrates dissociations among language, wakefulness, behavioral responsiveness, and conscious experience. Perspectives from embodied simulation, mind-object identity, quantum information, and the philosophy of physics are treated here as heuristic stress tests rather than as mechanistic accounts; they keep open foundational questions concerning subjectivity, representation, and the role of the observer. We advocate constrained pluralism, a methodological framework in which consciousness is conceptualized as an integrated, embodied, relational, and temporally extended process. Such an approach provides a coherent foundation for future research while strengthening the dialogue between neuroscience, clinical practice, philosophy, and neuroethics.

items.title: MoCA deficits and white matter in Huntington's disease.
items.abstract: This study explored the relationship between the Montreal Cognitive Assessment's (MoCA) subdomains and white matter changes in Huntington's disease (HD). items.title: ACC hyperactivity and synaptic remodeling underlie sensory hypersensitivity in Adnp-haploinsufficient mice.
items.abstract: Pathogenic variants in the transcriptional regulator ADNP cause a frequent autism syndrome marked by pronounced tactile and pain hypersensitivity, yet the responsible cortical circuits are poorly defined. Here we show that Adnp-haploinsufficient (Adnp-HT) mice exhibit mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity together with enhanced shock-related defensive responding. Caudal conditional Adnp deletion did not reproduce these phenotypes, arguing against a dominant peripheral or spinal contribution. c-Fos mapping and ultrahigh-field fMRI revealed stimulus-evoked hyperresponsiveness across a distributed sensory-affective network that included the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), and recordings from naive mice identified increased intrinsic excitability and altered synaptic transmission in ACC pyramidal neurons. Global chemogenetic inhibition of ACC excitatory neurons only partially normalized mechanical and paw-heat hypersensitivity but increased shock-related freezing, whereas inhibition of electric-foot-shock-activated (FosTRAP2) ACC ensembles normalized mechanical and paw-heat responses and attenuated baseline and early shock-related freezing. Multiomic profiling, MERFISH, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing converged on synaptic and ion-channel programs in layer 2/3 and layer 5 excitatory neurons. These results identify the ACC as a major, but not exclusive, cortical contributor within a broader network and support cell-type- and ensemble-resolved approaches to ADNP-linked sensory abnormalities.

items.title: Untangling the motives for avoiding contraception among women who underwent elective termination of pregnancy in Belgrade (Serbia).
items.abstract: Unwanted pregnancies and induced abortions are the key health issues in Serbia. Empirical evidence suggests that the use of widely accessible contraception methods among Serbian women is low. The purpose of this study was to investigate the reasons for not using contraception as well as factors that might impact those reasons among women who have had an induced abortion. Women who sought abortion at the Clinic for Obstetrics and Gynaecology, University Clinical Center of Serbia from 2022 to 2024 were enrolled in this cross-sectional study. They responded to an anonymous questionnaire examining their demographic data, lifestyle and habits, medical history, and reasons for not using contraceptives prior to this pregnancy. Responses of 433 women aged 16 to 49 years (mean age 32.0 ± 6.7 years) were analysed. The most common reasons for avoiding contraception were being afraid to take hormones (22.6%) and not knowing how to count the cycle days (22.4%). Majority of women (28.4%) had multiple reasons not to use contraception while 28.2% could not specify the reason. Being afraid of hormonal contraception was associated with having recurrent abortions. Belonging to national minorities and having chronic illnesses was associated with not knowing how to count the cycle days. The fact that women did not use contraception because it is expensive was associated with having lower salary and vigorous physical activity intensity at work. Being bothered to take the contraception regularly was associated with being an atheist and having gynaecological illnesses. Women who thought that they could not get pregnant easily were more likely from national minorities, not married or partnered and had previous Caesarean Sections. It is of paramount importance to improve counselling on contraception throughout the reproductive period to optimise family planning for Serbian women.

items.title: Endophytic fungi shape tree epigenomes and enhance thermotolerance under climate warming.
items.abstract: Background Rising global temperatures threaten the survival and regeneration of temperate and boreal forests. Yet how microbial symbioses contribute to tree heat-resilience remains unclear. Results Here, we integrated field ecological surveys with controlled multi-omics analyses and found that soil fungal diversity declined, accompanied by enrichment of potentially beneficial taxa along regional variation in max temperature of the warmest month (BIO5). Inoculation with representative endophytes significantly promoted birch (Betula platyphylla) growth and photosynthetic performance under non-stress conditions. Furthermore, endophytic fungi enhance thermal tolerance in birch by establishing a transcriptional chromatin state at heat-responsive genes that facilitates their activation under heat stress. Integrative network analyses identified regulatory networks linking fungal symbiosis to thermotolerance pathways. Conclusion These findings connect macroecological patterns to molecular mechanisms, uncovering an epigenetic basis for microbe-mediated heat adaptation in trees and highlighting symbiotic fungi as both key partners and practical means to strengthen forest resilience under climate warming. items.title: Assessment of phenotypic variability of F 1 hybrids of winter rapeseed and their parental forms using multivariate statistical methods.
items.abstract: The effect of genotype, environment (year) and their interaction is one of the main target in breeding programs and play important role in the final expression of quality traits and seed yield of winter oilseed rape. In this study, phenotypic traits, yield and yield components and also biochemical traits of 72 hybrids and their parental forms were investigated. Plant material were tested in the field experiments in a randomized complete block design with three replications during two growing seasons. Field observations were recorded on beginning and length of flowering, seed yield and its structure: the number of branches and siliques per plant, the silique length, the number of seeds per silique, the thousand seed weight and biochemical traits: oil content, saturated (palmitic, stearic) and unsaturated fatty acids (oleic, linoleic, linolenic) and eicosenic acid in the seed oil and glucosinolates (GLS) content (alkenyl, indolyl, total glucosinolates and total alkenyl GLS content), protein and fibre (ADF, NDF) content (26 traits). The use of multivariate statistical methods allowed for the simultaneous characterization and grouping of tested genotypes in terms of 26 traits. Two-way multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) revealed significant effects of both genotype (G) and environment (E-year) as well as the G×E interaction regarding all analyzed traits, except oleic acid and indolyl glucosinolate content. Graphic images of the distribution of hybrids and their parental forms in the space of the two canonical variates showed a great variation between the plant materials, both in terms of yield, structure of yield as well as oil content and all biochemical traits.
