items.title: The Hawkes Hypergraph Copy Model: A Semi-mechanistic Generative Model for Temporal Hypergraphs
items.abstract: Many complex networks involve time-varying relations between more than two nodes. Such networks are naturally modeled by temporal hypergraphs. We propose the Hawkes Hypergraph Copy Model (HHCM), a semi-mechanistic model for temporal hypergraphs that combines a Hawkes process to model the timestamps of hyperedges with a noisy copy mechanism to model the nodes present in hyperedges. Each hyperedge is either generated as an exogenous event with a baseline rate or an endogenous event as a noisy copy of a previous hyperedge. Our proposed model can be used for credit attribution, where the objective is to quantify the influence or contribution of a prior hyperedge to a current one. We apply the HHCM to perform attribution on several real network datasets with higher-order relations, including email networks and militarized interstate dispute networks.

items.title: Discovery of Trailing Spiral Dust Alignment in the Dust Polarization of HL Tau at $λ= 2.1$ mm
items.abstract: Polarimetric observations of protoplanetary disks at (sub)millimeter wavelengths constrain dust grain properties, dynamics, and alignment mechanisms. We present new high-resolution ALMA Band 4 (2.1 mm) polarization observations of HL Tau with spatial resolutions of $\sim$0.08$''$ (11.78 au) and $\sim$0.19$''$ (27.99 au). Linearly decomposing the polarization into contributions from dust scattering and thermal emission by aligned grains, we analyze the new Band 4 data and published high-resolution Band 7 (870 $μ$m) observations. Thermal emission from aligned grains dominates the polarization across the disk at Band 4, in contrast to the scattering-dominated Band 7, and both mechanisms vary radially with the disk substructures, consistent with expected optical depth variations. At Band 4, we detect a coherent angular deviation from purely azimuthal grain alignment, in which the streamlines of the alignment field yield trailing spirals with respect to disk rotation. A single global offset angle quantifies this deviation as $2.83^\circ\pm0.33^\circ$ and $4.10^\circ\pm0.09^\circ$ (statistical uncertainties) from two robust weightings, and the detection reaches a significance of $\approx7σ$ under conservative uncertainty estimates. This trailing orientation is consistent with aerodynamic ("badminton birdie-like") alignment driven by gas-dust drift near pressure bumps. However, under an axisymmetric disk velocity structure, this interpretation requires Stokes numbers two to three orders of magnitude larger than expected for the grains dominating the millimeter emission. At Band 7, the polarization angle is weakly sensitive to the alignment direction and exhibits a near/far-side antisymmetric structure that the model cannot reproduce. The Band 7 data therefore neither support nor contradict the Band 4 result.

items.title: Graph Parameterization for Invariant Manifolds Attached to Quasi-Periodic Tori
items.abstract: We develop a high-order Fourier-Taylor graph-parameterization method for computing local invariant manifolds attached to reducible quasi-periodic invariant tori of discrete dynamical systems, with particular emphasis on Poincaré maps. Assuming that the invariant torus and its Floquet reduction are known, we represent the manifold as a graph over a selected spectral subspace and compute its coefficients recursively through jet transport and cohomological equations on the torus. The formulation accommodates stable, unstable, and center spectral selections. For center manifolds, it simultaneously determines the nonlinear reduced dynamics, providing a low-dimensional representation from which nearby invariant objects can be lifted to the original phase space. For real systems with complex-conjugate Floquet multipliers, we derive an equivalent real formulation based on Hermitian symmetry and Krawtchouk transformations. This allows real-valued jet transport while retaining the advantages of complex spectral coordinates in the cohomological solver. The implementation also incorporates inverse dynamics for stable directions, multiple shooting, coordinate scaling, and a posteriori validation tests. Numerical experiments with a quasi-periodically forced pendulum, an oscillating solar sail in the Earth-Moon system, and a simplified solar system model illustrate the construction and its computational properties. In the solar-sail benchmark, the real formulation reduces computation time by approximately a factor of 2.2 compared with the complex implementation.

items.title: Funding Landscape of Early-Career Scientists: A Perspective from the AGU SPA Early Career Leadership Advisory Committee
items.abstract: Like researchers across many scientific fields, early-career researchers in heliophysics face a critical transition from supervised research to independent scientific inquiry. However, the funding landscape that should support this transition is fragmented and unpredictable. Here we examine the current funding opportunities available to early-career researchers in heliophysics alongside the historical experiences of established scientists who navigated similar transitions. We catalog the major U.S. federal programs targeting early-career space physicists, documenting their eligibility constraints, selection rates, and accessibility. Access varies with career stage, appointment type, citizenship requirements, and solicitation schedules, and selection rates can swing sharply: the NASA Heliophysics Early Career Investigator Program (ECIP) selected 28% of proposals in 2022 but only 6% in 2024. To provide historical context, we collected survey responses from 30 researchers whose PhDs span 1972-2016 and conducted eight interviews with mid- and senior-career researchers. Most respondents viewed the present funding environment as more difficult than their own early careers, identifying predictability of opportunity, not ease, as what enabled earlier generations to build independence. Salary support alone does not guarantee opportunities to develop scientific leadership; accessible PI awards and real responsibility within collaborative projects can both contribute to that development. We recommend predictable, adequately sized grant programs for early-career principal investigators, transparent reporting of selection statistics across all early-career programs, continued use of dual-anonymous peer review, and named leadership roles for early-career researchers within large projects.

items.title: Formation of Electron Velocity Distribution Functions at low-\{beta} Quasi-Perpendicular Shocks From Physical-Mass-Ratio PIC Simulations
items.abstract: At low-\{beta} quasi-perpendicular shocks, the origins of upstream field-aligned electron beams and downstream flat-top distributions remain unresolved. Using 2D fully kinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations at the physical ion-to-electron mass ratio (mi/me = 1836), we found that the shock transition region is dominated by electromagnetic whistler-mode turbulence driven by the modified two-stream instability (MTSI) of reflected ions, not by the electrostatic instabilities as suggested by some previous studies using a reduced mass ratio. Beams in the upstream are produced mainly by shock-drift acceleration (SDA) at the ramp, whereas we attribute the downstream flat-top distributions to nonuniform acceleration by the parallel electric field. Electrons experience different field strengths, polarities, and interaction durations along their trajectories, leading to a spread of parallel velocity changes that broadens and flattens the distribution. These results highlight the importance of using the physical mass ratio in exploring the electron dynamics of low-\{beta} shocks.

items.title: Mass Spectral Evidence for Iron Sulfate in Venus' Cloud Aerosol
items.abstract: Venus' cloud aerosols play pivotal roles in the thermal, chemical, and optical properties of the atmosphere. Here, we present mass spectral evidence that the cloud aerosols contain abundant iron sulfates. Data from the Pioneer Venus Large Probe Neutral Mass Spectrometer (LNMS) suggest that cloud aerosols inadvertently collected into the inlets at ~48-51 km and thermally decomposed below the clouds, releasing several compounds into the LNMS. At 23 km and below, multiple iron species (54Fe+, 56FeO+, 54FeO+, 56Fe2O+, and 56Fe2O2+) and other decomposition gases were detected. Quantitative treatment of these mass signals suggested the release of Fe2O3, SO2, O2, SO3, H2SO4, and H2O, consistent with the thermal decomposition of hydronium-bearing ferric sulfates. The resulting mole ratio for iron to sulfate (2.0 +/- 1.1) aligns with hydronium jarosite ((H3O)Fe3(SO4)2(OH)6), which likely formed within the inlets after aerosol capture, dehydration, and loss of sulfuric acid. Our thermochemical calculations support these assessments. Speciation of the ferric sulfates in the native aerosols remains unconstrained (e.g., solution and/or particle phases). Peak fits to the thermal release profiles yielded the abundances of the bulk iron (0.8 +/- 0.4 mg m-3) and aerosol-derived compounds, including hydronium jarosite (2.2 +/- 1.2 mg m-3, 30 +/- 17 wt%), water (3.7 +/- 0.4 mg m-3, 50 +/- 10 wt%), and sulfuric acid (1.5 +/- 0.2 mg m-3, 20 +/- 5 wt%). Surface sourcing of the cloud iron is likely minor. Instead, cosmic dust influx could deliver iron to the clouds in a geologically short time (2.4 +/- 1.5 Myr).

items.title: Planetary Habitable Zones around Magnetized White Dwarfs
items.abstract: White dwarfs are known to host remnant planetary material, indicating that rocky objects can survive post-main-sequence evolution and migrate into very close orbits. However, the decline of white dwarf luminosity makes it difficult for a planet to remain habitable for long when relying only on the white dwarf's irradiative heating. While several non-radiative energy sources have been proposed, the role of white dwarf magnetism in planetary energy budgets remains largely unexplored. We examine whether magnetic unipolar induction could provide sustained heating for close-in rocky planets. By coupling white dwarf cooling tracks with an orbit-dependent induction model, we evaluate the contribution of ohmic dissipation to planetary surface energy budgets and estimate the upper limit with efficient heat deposition. It is possible for the induction heating to supply a nearly steady surface energy flux for certain orbital distances and stellar spins, partially offsetting the decline in the white dwarf irradiation at late times. This leads to a persistent outer temperate region and, in some cases, a narrow inner zone that emerges after substantial cooling, identifying magnetic induction as a viable long-lived supplement to radiative heating.

items.title: The Phases of Hierarchy
items.abstract: We develop a dynamical phase theory of hierarchy, in which depth decides whether a population of size $N$ that revises its own environment can correct it without overcorrecting. The statistics that let a large majority detect a small bias - the basis of the Condorcet jury theorem - also make its response grow as $\sqrt{N}$. Fed back into the environment it is judging, this sharpening destabilises the matched state through a flip bifurcation at a critical loop gain, which we obtain analytically for a class of models we term adaptive normal forms. We show that this instability can be attenuated by hierarchical layering, requiring a depth scaling logarithmically with $N$. This recovers known logarithmic bounds in organisational economics directly from dynamic stability conditions. Hierarchical depth carries its own costs however, and by analysing the signal chain transmission up the hierarchy we show that beyond a finite depth no correction reaches the top before its deadline, and that below it the cost of arrival grows exponentially with depth. A hierarchy that is too flat therefore oscillates and one that is too deep cannot be steered in time, leaving a bounded window of depth between an unstable flat phase and a frozen inertial phase. We further show that these results can be generalised by treating each layer as a real-space renormalisation step, classifying aggregation rules by how they transmit bias. This establishes a connection between these dynamic results to attention in Transformers, where a residual update is diffusion on the token graph and depth plays the role of scale. Finally we show these phase boundaries are observable in finite sampling, and propose measurements which may characterise the proposed phases in real adaptive systems.

items.title: OutLines: Modeling Spectral Lines from Winds, Bubbles, and Outflows
items.abstract: Studies of kinematics and geometry of outflowing gas rely on modeling features in integrated spectra using empirical quantiles or fitting multiple Gaussian or Voigt profiles. Such methods can miss key underlying physics and even lead to spurious interpretations of observations. To address this problem, we present the public python code OutLines, which predicts spectral emission and absorption line profiles produced by winds, bubbles, and outflows. By design, OutLines is phenomenologically and scale agnostic to bridge the gap between observations and simulations across a broad swath of astrophysics. The OutLines code accounts for differences in velocity field, density profile, and outflow geometries, making OutLines versatile for a wide variety of astrophysical phenomena. We demonstrate the wide applicability of OutLines by using the code to model line profiles in an H ii region knot, super star clusters, a starburst galaxy, and an AGN. In each of these contexts, we illustrate how OutLines can illuminate key underlying physics in ways that improve scientific understanding and address important open questions in astronomy, including the key mechanisms in the baryon cycle, the evolution of H ii regions and galaxies, and even Lyman continuum escape. OutLines will be a critical resource as massively multiplexed spectroscopic surveys with facilities like WEAVE and 4MOST come online, providing the means to probe feedback with deeper, higher resolution spectroscopy for unprecedented large samples of objects.

items.title: Binary neutron star mergers with $\sc{sphincs}$ $\sc{bssn}$: Temperature-dependent equations of state and damping of constraint violations
items.abstract: Neutron star mergers hold the key to several grand challenges of contemporary (astro-)physics. In view of the upcoming next generation of ground-based detectors, it is crucial to keep improving theoretical predictions to harvest the full scientific returns from these investments. We introduce here a substantial update of our Lagrangian numerical relativity code SPHINCS BSSN. Apart from changing our unit system, we add constraint damping terms to the BSSN spacetime evolution equations. We demonstrate that this measure reduces, without noteworthy computational cost, the Hamiltonian constraint violations by more than an order of magnitude. We further implement contributions to thermal energy and pressure that are based on Fermi liquid theory and contain a parametrization of the Dirac effective mass. These terms can be combined with any cold equation of state, and they enhance the physical realism of our simulations and introduce a physics-based concept of a temperature. In a set of merger simulations, we demonstrate good agreement with other temperature-dependent numerical relativity simulations. For a fixed cold equation of state and binary configuration, we find that the explored range of Dirac effective masses translates into shifts of ∼ 50 ~Hz in the dominant post-merger gravitational-wave peak frequency.

items.title: Quantum Pontus-Mpemba effect in dissipative quasiperiodic chains
items.abstract: A finite interval of auxiliary thermal preparation can shorten the total relaxation time to an infinite-temperature state, even after its duration is included. We study this Pontus–Mpemba effect in single-particle quasiperiodic chains with local Markovian dephasing, using mosaic and power-law hopping models. Hamiltonian eigenstate preparations and fixed initial-state families are compared to resolve the joint role of spatial modulation and initial-state structure. Under the tested protocol, the clean-chain eigenstate family shows no net acceleration in the clean limit, whereas a subset of the same initial density matrices benefits from introducing the mosaic potential. The tested site-localized states, by contrast, accelerate at both potentials. A reflection-restoration diagnostic identifies the symmetry selection rule governing access to a slow density mode. Finite-time population redistribution and coherence damping then quantitatively account for the net time saving of a representative state. These results link the state-selective response to quasiperiodic modulation with the dynamical action of auxiliary preparation: the potential and initial-state structure determine the excited slow components, while intermediate-state engineering changes their amplitudes and the complete relaxation time.

items.title: Tracking the Brownian Motion of DNA‐Functionalized Magnetic Submicron‐Sized Particle Agglomerates for Conformation Analysis Beyond the Optical Resolution Limit
items.abstract: Brownian motion provides access to hydrodynamic properties of submicron objects independent of their optical resolvability. A diffusion-based approach for inferring effective size distributions of agglomerates of DNA-functionalized magnetic submicron-sized particles (MPs), with a magnetic core and a polystyrene shell, is presented. Using multi-particle tracking microscopy, the Brownian dynamics of MPs grafted with double-stranded (ds) DNA of varying contour length under low-salt conditions are analyzed. A physically motivated model relates dsDNA contour length to effective hydrodynamic diameter via an attenuated corona description. The measured diffusion coefficient distributions exhibit a systematic, monotonic dependence on dsDNA length in quantitative agreement with the model. Although tracked objects are predominantly agglomerates rather than isolated MPs, the length-dependent signal persists: the dsDNA corona sets the hydrodynamic scaling and distribution broadening of diffusivity, while agglomeration mainly adds a size offset. Because size information is encoded in Brownian dynamics rather than the optical image, the method resolves differences in hydrodynamic size far below the optical diffraction limit, following the same principle underlying nanoparticle tracking analysis. This distribution-based readout is inherently tolerant to polydispersity and aggregation and is anchored on core-size distributions measured independently by transmission electron microscopy. It is a simple, promising strategy for future biotechnological monitoring assays.

items.title: Quantum timekeeping and the dynamics of scrambling in critical systems
items.abstract: Interacting quantum many-body systems can rapidly scramble quantum information, raising the question of how precisely local subsystems can track the passage of time during this evolution. In this work, we develop a quantum metrological framework for quantum chaos by showing that local subsystems of information scrambling systems naturally function as quantum stopwatches. The reduced quantum state of a subsystem encodes the passage of time through its local temporal distinguishability along its dynamical trajectory. Treating time as the estimation parameter, we then derive a generalized quantum Cramer-Rao bound that directly relates the precision of time estimation to the decay of out-of-time ordered correlators (OTOCs) and subsystem quantum Fisher information (QFI). For a single qubit subsystem, we obtain an exact relation between the incoherent component of subsystem QFI and the decay rate of OTOCs in quantumly chaotic dynamics, while the total subsystem QFI provides an upper bound to the corresponding decay rate. Furthermore, using a scaling analysis based on imaginary-time correlators, we investigate under what conditions the incoherent subsystem QFI exhibits critical amplification near quantum phase transitions. Our results are demonstrated and verified by a numerical analysis of the dynamics of a chaotic Ising chain.

items.title: Paragenetic Formation of Aqueous Alteration Minerals Under Volcanically Active, Oxidative Weathering Conditions on Mars
items.abstract: The chemical weathering of the Martian basaltic crust produces a complex assemblage of aqueous alteration minerals. These alteration minerals can provide critical constraints on the composition of the aqueous and atmospheric systems that produce them. Alteration minerals discovered on Mars include massive global deposits of phyllosilicates, sulfates, and iron (oxyhydr)oxides and localized detections of carbonates and halides. These deposits are rarely monomineralic and are the result of complex geological and geochemical processing of the surface material. Several physicochemical parameters influence and determine the type of alteration mineral produced, including temperature, composition of the atmosphere, amount and composition of the alteration fluid, availability of oxidants, and the protolith. Here, we take a thermodynamic modeling approach to study the alteration of the average crust using the “Mazatzal” basalt at 25°C under volcanically active oxidative conditions. We simulated alteration under variable compositions of CO 2 and S‐bearing species at water‐to‐rock ratios between 0.1 and 10 6. Our results indicate that the alteration is strongly influenced by system acidity and the presence of S‐bearing gases. The alteration assemblage mostly comprised of phyllosilicates and sulfates; minor alteration phases included simpler silicates, oxides, and carbonates; chloride minerals did not form under modeled conditions. Our model assemblages are compared with alteration assemblages observed on Mars and are used to suggest potential pathways of their formation.

items.title: Supermassive Black Holes: modelling strongly and weakly magnetised misaligned accretion disks
items.abstract: In this paper, we carry out a numerical study of spinning supermassive black holes where the angular momentum of the accretion disk is misaligned with respect to the spin vector. We conduct a parameter survey covering a range of initial disk misalignment angles ($\mathcal {T}_\mathrm{init}=15\circ , 45\circ , 75\circ$) with either the Magnetically Arrested Disk (MAD) or Standard And Normal Evolution (SANE) magnetic field configurations, using the general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) code KHARMA. Our misaligned accretion disks are initialised around a Kerr black hole with spin a* = 0.9375. We find that models in the MAD state can align with the black hole up to ∼10 rg, even in extremely misaligned models ($\mathcal {T}_\mathrm{init}=75^\circ$), which has not been seen before. SANE remain misaligned up to the black hole, reaching maximum disk tilt at ∼10rg, with this radius growing as disk misalignment increases. However, the maximum disk tilt does not have a linear relationship with the initial disk misalignment, and appears to have a maximum value of ∼50○ for the black hole spin considered here. We also show misaligned disk simulations produced by KHARMA are consistent with other GRMHD codes for a variety of problems.

items.title: Impact of the equation of state on core collapse supernovae: I. The low- T / | W | instability
items.abstract: Rapidly rotating core-collapse supernovae are promising sources of multimessenger emission, as non-axisymmetric dynamics in the newly formed proto-neutron star can leave characteristic imprints on both gravitational waves and neutrinos. We present three-dimensional neutrino-magnetohydrodynamics simulations of the collapse of a rapidly rotating 35 M ⊙ progenitor, performed with five different finite-temperature nuclear equations of state, to investigate how dense-matter physics affects the development of the low- T / | W | instability and its associated multimessenger signatures. We find that the low- T / | W | instability develops in all equation of state (EOS) models considered, indicating that its occurrence is robust for this rapidly rotating progenitor. However, its onset time, dominant azimuthal structure, lifetime, and characteristic multimessenger frequencies vary among models, reflecting differences in the evolving proto-neutron star structure and rotation profile. The instability produces large-scale spiral modes that generate quasi-periodic gravitational wave emission and modulate the neutrino luminosities, especially along directions close to the equatorial plane. The dominant gravitational wave frequency associated with the instability correlates with the effective stiffness and compactness of the proto-neutron star: models with more compact/stiffer configurations emit at higher frequencies. This suggests that, in rapidly rotating core-collapse supernovae, the frequency of the low- T / | W | instability-driven gravitational wave signal may provide a diagnostic of the dense-matter EOS, complementary to the information carried by the neutrino signal.

items.title: Constraining AGN Accretion Physics with Black Hole Mass–Luminosity Scaling Relations
items.abstract: We test how supermassive black holes are fed by combining new black hole mass–luminosity relations with physically motivated feeding models. We build a uniform sample of 1729 unobscured blue quasars (z ≲ 2) by cross-matching Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) DR16 with eROSITA and augment it with hyperluminous quasars (WISSH, HYPERION) plus 49 JWST broad-line active galactic nuclei (AGN) at z > 3.5. We find for the SDSS-eRosita sample of blue quasars a near-linear scaling of bolometric luminosity with mass (slope 0.91 ± 0.01) and a shallower hard-X-ray trend (slope 0.73 ± 0.01). Classical hot-mode (Bondi) accretion underpredicts the observed luminosities by ≳2 dex at the high-mass end and is inconsistent with the measured slopes. In contrast, chaotic cold accretion (CCA)—in which multiphase gas condenses, collides, and rains onto the nucleus—consistently reproduces both the normalization and the near-linear slope expected from halo thermodynamics. The shallower X-ray relation points to a decreasing coronal power fraction with black hole mass. JWST broad-line AGN frequently appear X-ray weak or H α enhanced. The latter case can be due to contributions from collisional ionization and photoionization from star formation to the broad H α emission, leading to an overestimate of AGN luminosities and black hole masses. In the former case, the X-ray weakness is consistent with coronal shielding or anisotropy at high accretion rates. Overall, the data favor CCA-driven, self-regulated feeding over local spherical capture across M BH ∼ 10 7 –10 10 M ⊙ and motivate extending these tests to lower masses and higher redshifts.

items.title: Narrow spectral artifact investigation and mitigation in LIGO data from the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run
items.abstract: We present efforts to identify, characterize, and mitigate narrow spectral artifacts in LIGO detector data during the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run. Narrow spectral artifacts in gravitational-wave detectors are non-astrophysical noise sources that can degrade searches for narrowband persistent gravitational waves. Identifying and, where possible, mitigating these noise sources is one of the core efforts of the LIGO Detector Characterization group. Key software tools have been updated and new tools deployed for the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run to facilitate investigations and data monitoring. We discuss these tool upgrades, and present several identified narrowband artifacts that have been successfully investigated and mitigated in LIGO data and others that remain unresolved. Regardless of whether artifacts are mitigated or not, narrowband persistent gravitational-wave searches require information on which frequency bands contain non-astrophysical artifacts. Minimizing the number of bands containing non-astrophysical artifacts is essential to maximize the potential for discovery of a new class of gravitational-wave signals.

items.title: Out-of-Equilibrium Effects in Non-Radial Relativistic Stellar Perturbations: A Model-Agnostic Formulation and Mode Analysis
items.abstract: We present a systematic, model-agnostic analysis of out-of-equilibrium effects, including viscosity and thermal conductivity, in non-radial oscillations of relativistic stars. Extending the Lindblom-Detweiler formalism, we construct, to our knowledge, the first general framework for linear, non-radial relativistic stellar perturbations that incorporates generic nonequilibrium corrections to the perfect-fluid sector in both the even- and odd-parity channels. Our framework is formulated in terms of the tensorial structure and thermodynamic decomposition of generic corrections without relying on any specific constitutive relations, thereby allowing us to elucidate, at a structural level, how these effects enter the perturbation equations and contribute to geometric deformations and fluid fluctuations. As an application, we consider the Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun fluid and perturbatively investigate shifts in the frequencies and damping times of modes connected to their perfect-fluid counterparts in the limit of vanishing transport coefficients. We also identify structural features of the closed eigenvalue problem that suggest the possibility of additional mode families. Our formalism provides a unified framework for analyzing how different relativistic fluid theories modify the structure of non-radial stellar perturbations.

items.title: Evaluating the Fourier approximation in pulsar timing array analysis
items.abstract: Pulsar timing arrays search for stochastic processes such as gravitational waves by comparing pulse time of arrival data for millisecond pulsars to expectations from a background with a given power spectral density (PSD). To make the analysis computationally tractable, the Bayesian likelihood is usually computed using an approximation in which the signal is taken to be a sum of Fourier modes appropriate to the total time of observation, even though the true signal is not periodic. We study the difference between likelihoods computed with this Fourier approximation method for power law spectra and those computed exactly (or using more-closely spaced frequencies as a proxy for the exact result) in the NANOGrav 15-year dataset. We find that the true marginal likelihoods for power-law PSDs are on average about half as large as the likelihoods computed using the Fourier approximation. This could lead to an error of a factor of two in model comparison. However, in the important comparison of uncorrelated vs. Hellings-Downs correlated models, a very similar correction appears in both, so the model comparison is essentially unaffected. We also compare parameter estimation results for power law PSDs, finding little difference between the methods. We briefly discuss spectra with sharper features, for which the approximation could be much worse.

items.title: Quantum Teleportation Toward the Quantum Internet: A Concise Review
items.abstract: Quantum networks play a pivotal role in quantum information science, as they not only provide a secure communication platform for remote access to quantum computers but also serve as the strategic core for achieving large‐scale quantum information processing, forming the foundational infrastructure for the future global‐scale quantum internet. Quantum teleportation, which enables the transmission of unknown quantum states over long distances by employing quantum entanglement together with classical communication, is essential for the distribution of quantum resources in the construction of the global‐scale quantum internet. To realize a global‐scale quantum internet, quantum repeater protocols represent one of the most promising approaches for enabling quantum communication between any nodes. This concise review presents representative experimental demonstrations of quantum teleportation for constructing quantum networks across different physical platforms. Along this trajectory, the review discusses current challenges, open issues, and future perspectives toward a scalable and practical quantum internet.

items.title: The influence of feedback on the baryonic content of haloes in the COLIBRE simulations
items.abstract: We present predictions for the relationship between halo gas mass fraction and halo mass, $f_{\rm gas}^{200}-M_{200}$, from the COLIBRE cosmological simulations of galaxy formation, and explore how the gas content of haloes is influenced by feedback from supernovae and active galactic nuclei (AGN) over time. The $f_{\rm gas}^{200}-M_{200}$ relation in COLIBRE is non-monotonic, with a peak at M200 ∼ 1011.5 − 12 M⊙. Below this mass, supernova feedback efficiently expels gas from the haloes of dwarf galaxies; above it, AGN feedback efficiently depletes the haloes of galaxy groups. The relation rises for M200 ≳ 1013 M⊙, as AGN-driven expulsion becomes less efficient. The fiducial COLIBRE model yields group and cluster gas fractions that agree with Chandra and XMM-Newton X-ray constraints. While these gas fractions are lower than those in simulations such as EAGLE and IllustrisTNG, they are high relative to constraints from some recent eROSITA stacking analyses, and to gas fractions in hydrodynamical and baryonification models that reproduce both the eROSITA stacks and kinetic Sunyaev-Zel’dovich (kSZ) effect measurements. COLIBRE’s hybrid AGN feedback model, which combines thermal and jet-driven feedback, produces lower gas fractions in better agreement with eROSITA stacks and kSZ constraints (but worse agreement with Chandra and XMM-Newton). We investigate why COLIBRE exhibits better agreement with these observational constraints in comparison to EAGLE and other contemporary simulations, and explore how simulation resolution affects the impact of feedback. Our results demonstrate that halo gas fractions are a sensitive probe of feedback physics, and can differ significantly between simulations that otherwise produce very similar galaxy populations.

items.title: Electrical control of valley hybridization in moiré quantum dots
items.abstract: Smooth electrostatic gates generally have little ability to mix atomic valleys, whose large momentum separation requires short-range perturbations. In moiré superlattices, the relevant valley extrema can instead be separated by much smaller momenta, opening a route to gate-controlled valley hybridization. Here we investigate this mechanism in gate-defined quantum dots in twisted WSe 2 bilayers. Using a continuum model, we show that smooth lateral confinement produces a lowest-orbital doublet associated with the two moiré valleys. The confinement radius and depth tune the hybridization between these states, while a displacement field controls their detuning. These dependencies are captured by an effective two-level Hamiltonian with two noncommuting electrostatic control terms. For small dots, the valley splitting reaches several hundred microelectronvolts, while the doublet remains separated from excited orbitals by energies on the millielectronvolt scale. These results demonstrate electrical control of moiré-valley hybridization and identify the confined valley doublet as a promising candidate for a valley-based qubit.

items.title: Hardware‐Assisted Sample‐Based Quantum Diagonalization for Molecular Potential‐Energy Curves
items.abstract: Sample‐based quantum diagonalization (SQD) combines quantum‐hardware sampling with classical diagonalization in a selected determinant space. We apply SQD to the potential‐energy curves of HeH +, ArH +, and H 2 O using 6–31G and correlation‐consistent polarized valence double‐zeta (cc‐pVDZ) active‐space Hamiltonians. Bitstrings are generated with shallow local unitary cluster Jastrow (LUCJ) circuits constructed from coupled‐cluster singles and doubles (CCSD) amplitudes based on restricted Hartree–Fock (RHF) references. The largest calculation uses 46 qubits. In the original production calculations, equilibrium SQD deviations from same‐active‐space full configuration interaction (FCI) are 0.00, 2.51, and 6.34 millihartree (mHa) for HeH +, ArH +, and H 2 O, respectively. Independent H 2 O validation runs yield a mean deviation of 1.85 mHa and a 0.333‐mHa run‐to‐run standard deviation, with selected spaces retaining 2.21%–2.27% of the 78.4‐million‐determinant sector. An RHF‐only state‐preparation control shows sensitivity to the CCSD‐informed state‐preparation prior, while SCI states remain predominantly singlet. These results quantify accuracy, reproducibility, selected‐space reduction, and classical cost of hardware‐assisted SQD.

items.title: Testing the spin-induced multipole moments of compact binary coalescences using the flexible theory-independent framework
items.abstract: According to the no-hair theorem, the multipole moments of an electrically neutral black hole in general relativity are entirely determined by its mass and spin. However, this is not in general true for compact objects: The multipole moments of neutron stars or exotic compact objects can depend on their formation history and internal processes, which are encoded in an equation of state. Furthermore, their spin-induced multipole moments differ from those of black holes of the same mass and spin, leaving an imprint on the dynamics and emitted gravitational waves of the binary. Gravitational waves can thus be used to test the nature of compact binary coalescences. Here, we present a test of the spin-induced quadrupole and octupole moments of compact objects based on the flexible theory-independent (FTI) framework. FTI is a parameterized inspiral test of general relativity which enables the addition of post-Newtonian coefficient deviations to the gravitational-wave phase of a generic aligned-spin frequency-domain waveform model. We use this test on synthetic signals to study the measurability of spin-induced quadrupole and octupole moments. Next, we apply the test to a subset of signals observed by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration. Lastly, we present forecasts for next-generation ground-based detectors, such as Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer. Our estimates suggest that these detectors will be capable of placing stringent constraints on the spin-induced quadrupole and octupole moments of 𝒪 ( 10 − 2 ) and 𝒪 ( 10 − 1 ) respectively, which is two orders of magnitude tighter than current constraints, and thus on the nature of black holes in a compact binary coalescence.

items.title: Year-round aerosol variability across monsoon regimes at a near-equatorial Indian Ocean receptor
items.abstract: Year-round observations of aerosol characteristics remain scarce over the equatorial Indian Ocean, particularly at receptor locations far from South Asian continental sources. Here, we present measurements of fine particulate matter (PM 2.5) chemical composition, aerosol optical properties, meteorology, air-mass transport, and five supporting dual-carbon isotope measurements from the Maldives Climate Observatory at Gan (MCOG; 0.69° S, 73.15° E) during the 2022 seasonal cycle. During the northeast monsoon (NEM), continental influence from South and Southeast Asia coincided with higher PM 2.5 concentrations (5.6±2.7µgm-3), aerosol optical depth at 500 nm (AOD 500; 0.17±0.09), black carbon (BC), organic carbon (OC), and non-sea-salt sulfate. In the southwest monsoon (SWM), PM 2.5 and AOD 500 were approximately 41 % and 35 % lower, respectively, while the relative contribution of marine aerosol increased. These differences likely reflect the combined influence of changes in air-mass origin and monsoon meteorology, including increased precipitation and wet scavenging during the SWM. Despite pronounced changes in aerosol abundance and composition, the BC mass absorption cross-section at 658 nm (BC-MAC 658) differed only modestly between the NEM (8.8±2.9m2g-1) and SWM (10.2±3.2m2g-1), with no statistically significant seasonal difference. The isotope measurements showed substantial sample-to-sample variability, with fossil-dominated and mixed fossil–contemporary signatures occurring within both monsoon regimes. These observations provide a year-round benchmark for aerosol transport, wet removal, composition, and BC absorption at a near-equatorial Indian Ocean receptor, complementary to previous measurements from the northern Maldives and useful for evaluating regional chemical-transport and Earth system models.

items.title: The what, how and where of statistical learning: a neurocognitive synthesis.
items.abstract: The ability to learn environmental regularities - statistical learning - is crucial for language, cognition and behaviour. Despite decades of research, fundamental questions remain about what statistical learning is, how the mind supports it and where in the brain it is implemented. We address these questions with a framework based on Marr's levels of analysis. At the 'what' level, we suggest that statistical learning is best defined in terms of its goal: to learn latent structure in the input across repeated exposures. We focus on three widely studied sequential statistical learning tasks that embody this definition: embedded pattern, artificial grammar and serial reaction time tasks. At the 'how' and 'where' levels, our comprehensive reviews reveal that sequential statistical learning depends on at least two cognitive learning processes (prediction-based learning and chunking) and two well-established neural learning circuits (rooted in the basal ganglia and the medial temporal lobe). We describe empirically motivated 'many-to-many' mappings between the tasks, learning processes and neural circuits that integrate the three levels. Further, we suggest that task, input and learner characteristics can shift the relative reliance on these processes and circuits. Overall, our synthesis elucidates the cognitive and neural substrates of sequential statistical learning and provides predictions to guide future research.

items.title: Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes.
items.abstract: Heterochromatin typically represses genes 1,2 , yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation 3-7 . How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent 8 . In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self-non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly 8 . By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer-promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

items.title: Context-dependent response of endothelial cells to PIK3CA mutation.
items.abstract: Cancer-associated mutations in PIK3CA underlie congenital overgrowth disorders that frequently involve the vasculature 1,2 . Among the affected tissues, the endothelium commonly exhibits aberrant expansion, leading to vascular malformations 3 . Notably, these lesions arise predominantly in veins and capillaries, whereas arteries are largely spared, for reasons that remain unclear. Here, using genetic lineage tracing, we show that endothelial expression of PIK3CA H1047R drives profound clonal expansion of capillary and venous endothelial cells, whereas mature arterial endothelial cells are refractory to pathological PI3K activation. Expression of PIK3CA H1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features, providing a mechanistic explanation for the paucity of arterial lesions after PIK3CA genetic perturbation. Mechanistically, these effects are mediated by two complementary downstream branches of PI3K signalling: increased proliferation, which drives vascular overgrowth, and upregulation of the venous-specifying transcription factor NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), which suppresses arterial differentiation. Together, our findings reveal that pathogenic responses to PIK3CA H1047R are dictated by endothelial differentiation state and fate trajectory, and demonstrate that arterial endothelium is intrinsically resistant to oncogenic PI3K signalling. Arteries are therefore shielded from PIK3CA mutations, explaining the rarity of arterial malformations in PIK3CA-driven disease.

items.title: Multidimensional motor unit control after paralysing spinal cord injury using non-invasive recordings.
items.abstract: Spinal cord injury results in profound motor impairment, which affects approximately 20 million people worldwide. Regaining hand use is one of their highest priorities. Interestingly, even severely affected individuals can still use spared connections to generate detectable activity (measured with electromyography) in their paralysed muscles when attempting to perform a movement. Here we asked whether participants with no hand function due to a cervical spinal cord injury could still control the activity of motor units from paralysed muscles, which we detected using high-density surface electromyographic recordings. Participants could readily control their motor units to accurately perform three different one-dimensional tracking tasks that imposed different control requirements, with performance plateauing after a few days of practice. Moreover, this accurate control readily transferred to a two-dimensional cursor navigation task, allowing participants to play a series of one-dimensional ('Pong') and two-dimensional ('Snake') games and to navigate a virtual wheelchair using three independent control signals. This robust performance was achieved despite the presence of spasticity, and even in one participant who had a motor complete injury. These findings demonstrate the promise of non-invasive motor unit recordings for restoring hand function and suggest potential avenues for rehabilitation after paralysis.

items.title: Examining the impact of genome-wide findings for tobacco use through GWAS-impact analysis: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Background Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) transformed our understanding of complex trait genetics by identifying thousands of disease-associated variants. A tobacco use GWAS by Liu and colleagues, published in 2019, represents a landmark achievement in addiction genetics, identifying 406 loci associated with tobacco use behaviors. Despite widespread citation, the research impact and translational applications of these findings remain uncharacterized. Methods We conducted a 'GWAS-impact analysis', systematically searching PubMed and Web of Science for studies citing Liu et al. 10 through June 2023. Studies were included if they utilized tobacco use summary statistics in follow-up analyses. Two reviewers independently screened articles and extracted data on phenotypes, analytical methods, and clinical applications. We used ADHD as a case study to illustrate how different analytical approaches can be applied to investigate a single phenotype relationship. Results We identified 345 studies investigating tobacco use in relation to 1857 phenotypes across diverse health domains. General substance use (n = 203), Interventions on whole body (n = 124; an ICHI chapter that includes BMI and other anthropometric measurements), and Mental, behavioral or neurodevelopmental disorders (n = 100) dominated the research landscape. Mendelian randomization was the predominant analytical approach ( ~ 72% of studies), followed by polygenic score analyses and genetic correlation methods. Only three studies examined clinical applications. Version reporting was often inconsistent. Of the 345 included studies, 134 (38.8%) could not be classified by which version of the summary statistics they used, and only 22 (6.4%) reported using the version computed without UK Biobank participants. Conclusions These findings map research uptake while exposing a persistent translational gap, indicating the need for standardized phenotyping, triangulated causal inference, and evaluations establishing whether tobacco genetics adds clinical value beyond existing risk assessment.

items.title: Developmental changes in the carotid body transcriptome accompanying the maturation of chemosensitivity.
items.abstract: The carotid body (CB) chemoreceptors mature perinatally to regulate fetal cardiovascular and postnatal ventilatory responses to hypoxia. This maturation is associated with an increase in the sensitivity of the CB electrophysiological response to hypoxia (chemosensitivity): a process that is incompletely understood but critical to systemic oxygen homeostasis. Hypothesizing that perinatal CB gene expression changes would reveal candidate mechanisms for oxygen chemosensitivity, we studied the CB transcriptome in sheep, where perinatal CB physiology is well-characterised. Ovine CB-mediated cardiovascular reflexes are detectable in the fetus and mature between fetal days 120-145 (term), while sustained hypoxic ventilatory responses are established by postnatal day 15. We performed RNA-sequencing on sheep CBs at each of these stages, and adults, along with the superior cervical ganglion as an oxygen-insensitive control. This allowed us to define tissue-specific changes in the CB transcriptome correlating with chemosensitivity maturation. Progressive CB enrichment was observed in genes implicated in murine CB chemosensitivity, including potassium channels (KCNK9), mitochondrial complex IV regulators (NDUFA4L2, HIGD1C) and hypoxia-inducible factor-2α (EPAS1). Genes with this expression pattern were also enriched for regulators of diacylglycerol, particularly DGKH. Together, this builds a detailed picture of the CB transcriptional signature, with core features established in fetal life and conserved across species. We also observed down-regulated CB expression of genes encoding multiple metabolic pathways, including the tricarboxylic acid cycle, oxidative phosphorylation and ATP/GTP consuming processes. Tissue respirometry confirmed depressed oxidative metabolism in the CB vs. control non-chemosensory tissues, suggesting that this bioenergetic phenotype may be important for chemosensitivity. KEY POINTS: The carotid body (CB) chemoreceptors mediate rapid cardiorespiratory responses to hypoxia that maintain systemic oxygen homeostasis, but mechanisms of oxygen chemosensitivity remain incompletely understood. CB-mediated chemoreflexes mature during the perinatal period, with increasing sensitivity of the oxygen chemosensory response. We performed RNA-sequencing of sheep CB across three perinatal stages and adults, enabling us to identify gene expression changes that correlate with functional state. We describe a CB transcriptomic signature that is conserved across species, established in fetal life, and correlates with maturation. This includes TASK1/3, variant isoforms of complex IV, and EPAS1/hypoxia-inducible factor-2α. We also found progressive CB-enrichment of diacylglycerol signalling genes, potentially signifying a role in chemosensitivity. The sheep CB transcriptome also revealed striking down-regulation of metabolic pathways, and respirometry on fresh tissue confirms low CB oxygen consumption relative to control tissues. Alongside known variants of mitochondrial complex IV, this suppressed metabolic state may contribute to CB oxygen chemosensitivity.

items.title: Locus Ceruleus-Noradrenaline Signaling in the Prefrontal Cortex: From Adaptive Behavior to Circuit Mechanisms.
items.abstract: Noradrenaline (NA) released by the locus ceruleus (LC) is a key modulator of prefrontal cortex (PFC) function and adaptive behavior. Advances in genetic and optical tools have enabled precise manipulation and monitoring of LC-PFC interactions in rodents, revealing projection- and context-specific roles of noradrenergic signaling. In this review, we synthesize evidence that LC-NA inputs to distinct PFC subregions differentially support cognitive flexibility, inhibitory control, and fear and safety learning. We further examine how phasic and baseline components of LC activity, spatiotemporal NA release dynamics, and effects specific to receptor subtypes and cell types contribute to this functional diversity. Integrating these findings with emerging computational frameworks, we propose that LC activity provides temporally precise signals linked to actions, outcomes, surprise, and uncertainty. These signals shape PFC representations to promote contingency updating, strategy switching, and stable control, depending on task demands.

items.title: Whole-brain mapping of TMS-induced discomfort with large-scale concurrent TMS-fMRI.
items.abstract: Background Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is widely used for causal brain mapping and neuromodulation therapies, yet TMS-induced discomfort remains a prevalent and under-characterized confound that may influence measured neural responses. This study aimed to characterize the whole-brain neural signatures of TMS-induced discomfort and quantify its contribution to TMS-evoked neural activity. Methods A total of 165 participants, including healthy individuals (N = 80) and individuals with elevated depression and/or anxiety symptoms (N = 85), underwent concurrent TMS-fMRI across 11 cortical stimulation sites, yielding 1,535 runs. Following each run, participants rated TMS-induced discomfort using the Subjective Units of Distress Scale (SUDS). Multivariate brain-discomfort associations were modeled using a principal component analysis and sparse canonical correlation analysis (PCA-sCCA) framework with cross-validation. Results TMS-induced discomfort varied systematically across stimulation sites, with greater discomfort reported for frontal and inferior regions. PCA-sCCA identified distributed neural signatures of TMS-induced discomfort spanning sensorimotor, attentional, limbic, and default mode networks, as well as subcortical regions. Neural signatures differed between healthy and symptomatic groups, demonstrating both shared and group-specific patterns. The discomfort-related activity comprised approximately 12% and 25% of TMS-evoked neural responses in healthy and symptomatic groups, respectively, with greater contributions observed at frontal stimulation sites. Accounting for the discomfort-related component altered estimates of TMS-evoked response magnitude and effect size. Conclusions TMS-induced discomfort engages distributed brain-wide networks and constitutes a substantial component of TMS-evoked neural responses. These findings identify discomfort-related activity as an important confounding factor in TMS studies and highlight the need to routinely assess TMS-induced discomfort and consider its potential influence when estimating TMS-evoked neural effects, thereby improving the interpretability and rigor of TMS research and therapeutic applications.

items.title: Prenatal exposure to melamine, its derivatives, and aromatic amines in relation to infant anthropometry in the ECHO Cohort: an exploratory analysis.
items.abstract: Background Prenatal exposure to melamine, its derivates, and aromatic amines (AAs) has been linked to altered birthweight and gestational duration, but the impact on postnatal growth remains underexplored. We explored associations between prenatal exposure to these chemicals and anthropometric outcomes during infancy (0-12 months). Methods We quantified maternal urinary concentrations of melamine, three melamine derivatives, and 41 AAs in mother-infant pairs from three sites of the Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) Cohort to investigate associations with repeated measures of infant weight-for-age, length-for-age, and weight-for-length z-scores (n=1,391). We used linear mixed models, analyzing chemicals as continuous (log-transformed) or dichotomous variables based on detection frequency (≥75%, and 5-75%, respectively). Results Melamine, two melamine derivatives, and four AAs were detected in at least 75% of participants. In individual analyte analyses, associations of melamine, its derivatives, and AAs with infant anthropometric outcomes were generally null. Mixture analyses of AAs, melamine and its derivatives, and all analytes combined were also not associated with infant anthropometric outcomes. Conclusion In this exploratory study based on a single prenatal urine sample, we found no statistically significant associations after correction for multiple comparisons.

items.title: Regional Dissociation Between Axonal Injury and Astrocytic Reactivity Following Diffuse Traumatic Brain Injury.
items.abstract: Background Diffuse traumatic brain injury (TBI) induces heterogeneous pathological responses across brain regions, including traumatic axonal pathology and reactive astrogliosis. Although regional differences in astrocytic responses are well documented, it remains unclear whether astrocytic reactivity parallels axonal pathology following the same diffuse traumatic event. This study investigated their spatial relationship after diffuse TBI. New method Adult male Wistar rats were subjected to diffuse impact-acceleration TBI using a modified Marmarou model. At 24h, the pyramidal decussation (PDx) and pontomedullary junction (PmJ) were examined. Axonal pathology was quantified by amyloid precursor protein (APP)-positive axonal retraction bulbs, while astrocytic reactivity was quantified by glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP)-positive tissue area. Results APP-positive axonal pathology was greater in the PDx than in the PmJ (5.96 ± 2.50 vs. 0.27 ± 0.15 bulbs/mm²). GFAP immunoreactivity increased in both regions following injury. However, astrocytic reactivity did not parallel axonal pathology: relative to controls, GFAP-positive area increased 1.66-fold in the PDx and 2.79-fold in the PmJ. Comparison with existing methods Unlike approaches that assess regional astrogliosis or axonal pathology independently, the present approach evaluates their regional distributions within the same diffuse TBI model, revealing spatial dissociation between these pathological responses. GFAP-based astrocytic reactivity should therefore not necessarily be interpreted as a direct surrogate for local axonal pathology. Conclusion These findings demonstrate divergent regional patterns of axonal pathology and astrocytic reactivity after diffuse TBI. The PDx showed greater axonal pathology, whereas the PmJ showed a greater relative GFAP response, suggesting distinct regional regulation of these pathological responses.

items.title: Associations between systematic sports training and visual processing in adolescents: Behavioral and ERP evidence.
items.abstract: Adolescent visual systems continue to develop, but their association with systematic sports training is not well understood. We compared 33 adolescents with more than 1.5 years of sports training and 33 peers without specialized training. Participants completed behavioral tests and an electroencephalography (EEG) task with occluded faces, complete faces, and buildings. Principal event-related potential (ERP) analyses included 29 exercise participants and 23 controls per face condition. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied within analysis families. Four behavioral differences survived correction: the exercise group responded faster on negative dot-probe and Go/No-Go trials and was more accurate in high-load multiple-object tracking and shape perception (all q <.05). The exercise group showed lower occipital P1 component amplitudes for both face positions (component-family q =.002; global q =.009). The complete-face occipital N1 difference attenuated after P1 adjustment (q =.604), whereas the frontal late slow-wave difference remained after adjustment for preceding components (difference = 2.88 µV, 95% CI [1.09, 4.67]; component-family q =.004; global q =.009). Some exploratory posterior comparisons were nominally significant, but none survived FDR correction. Systematic sports training history was associated with better performance on selected cognitive tasks and differences in early occipital P1 and late frontal activity in adolescents.

items.title: Precision in detecting ocular hypotensive effects of topical medications, laser trabeculoplasty, and trabecular meshwork bypass stent implantation surgery.
items.abstract: To determine the precision in calculating intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction following laser trabeculoplasty (SLT), trabecular meshwork bypass stenting (Hydrus), or prostaglandin analog (PGA) initiation using individual pre- and post-intervention measurements. Longitudinal multi-site observational study. Patients with primary open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension treated with SLT, Hydrus, or PGA who underwent home IOP monitoring for 1 week before and after treatment as part of their routine care. Subjects used a rebound home tonometer to obtain multiple daily measurements. The average of all IOP measurements before and after treatment was used to calculate the "best available estimate" (BAE) of change in IOP. Individual or matched pairs and triplets of IOP values in each period were sampled in a bootstrap fashion to determine the precision of IOP comparisons, defined as being within 2mmHg of the BAE. Linear mixed-effects modeling (LMM) and multivariable linear regression (MLR) were used to account for the inclusion of both eyes. Fraction of IOP change measurements within 2mmHg of the BAE. 66 subjects (125 eyes) successfully recorded multiple daily IOP measurements before and after SLT, Hydrus, and PGA, with a mean change in IOP of in 1.7 mmHg (SE 0.32), 2.1 mmHg (0.38), and 2.2 mmHg (0.40), respectively. About 54% of IOP comparisons before and after treatment were within 2 mmHg of the BAE, with no significant differences across interventions (Dirichlet mixed-effects model). Accounting for diurnal variation improved precision: comparing only paired PM IOP values, clinic hour IOP values, or IOP values within two hours of each other increased this percentage to 56.7%, 57.0%, and 60.0%, respectively (p<0.005). Comparing the average of 2 or 3 IOP measurements before and after the interventions increased the precision to 69.6% and 83.7%, respectively (p<0.001). Single IOP comparisons identify the change in IOP only slightly more than half the time. Results were similar regardless of IOP lowering intervention. Measuring IOP at similar times of day or taking multiple measurements before and after treatment improves precision. Home tonometry may be beneficial in assessing effectiveness of glaucoma therapy.

items.title: Cocaine self-administration induces region-specific lipidomic remodeling across the rat nucleus accumbens, dorsal striatum, and orbitofrontal cortex.
items.abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that cocaine exposure dysregulates brain lipid homeostasis; however, prior studies have relied on noncontingent exposure, which does not capture the volitional nature of drug intake and may produce neuroadaptations distinct from cocaine self-administration (SA). We therefore determined whether cocaine SA altered the lipidome in corticostriatal regions implicated in cocaine use disorder. Adult male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent at least 14 daily 6-hour sessions of long-access intravenous SA, receiving cocaine (0.75 mg/kg/infusion) or saline (n = 8/group). Eighteen hours after the final session, untargeted liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry was used to profile lipids in the nucleus accumbens (NAc), dorsal striatum (DS), and orbitofrontal cortex (OFC). We detected 647 lipid species across 22 classes. Cocaine SA altered 216 species in the NAc, 157 in the DS, and 28 in the OFC, indicating greater lipidomic remodeling in the striatum than the cortex. These changes included increases in sphingolipids, lysophospholipids, and glycerophospholipids and decreases in glycerolipids, consistent with a shift from lipid storage toward membrane-associated and signaling pools. Seventeen lipid species were altered across all three regions. Ceramide was the most prominent shared feature, with increased relative abundance in each region and altered sphingoid base composition in the NAc and OFC, including enrichment of d18:2-containing ceramides. Given the role of ceramide in membrane organization and signaling, its accumulation may contribute to altered corticostriatal neurotransmission following cocaine SA. Overall, these findings identify lipid metabolism as an underexplored component of cocaine-induced neuroadaptations and ceramide metabolism as a key pathway for future mechanistic investigation.

items.title: Timing of DOAC initiation after ischaemic stroke with atrial fibrillation: a UK survey of changes in opinion and practice.
items.abstract: Several recent clinical trials have reported that early direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) initiation following acute ischaemic stroke and atrial fibrillation is safe and non-inferior to delayed DOAC initiation. This study aims to explore whether these findings are associated with changes in clinical practice. An online survey was sent to UK based clinicians via national organisations in 2025. Responders were asked to select what day following acute ischaemic stroke they would initiate anticoagulation in three case vignettes of differing stroke severity. Responses were compared to a survey conducted in 2018, prior to the publication of the trials TIMING, ELAN, START and OPTIMAS. Median values and interquartile ranges for the day in which responders would initiate anticoagulation were generated for each vignette and compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. Questions surrounding confidence in early DOAC initiation and whether clinical practice has changed following the OPTIMAS trial were asked. Sixty-seven people responded to the 2025 survey. In mild stroke the median day of DOAC initiation was day 1 (IQR 1-3); in moderate stroke day 3 (IQR 2-5) and in severe stroke day 7 (IQR 4-14). This was significantly lower in all three vignettes compared to the 2018 survey, with the differences in median between surveys being 2 days in mild stroke (p <0.001), 4 days in moderate stroke (p <0.001) and 7 days in severe stroke (p <0.001). 98.5% (n=65) of responders felt very or somewhat confident in early DOAC initiation and 86.3% (n=57) reported a change in their clinical practice. In this online survey, following the publication of several trials including OPTIMAS, UK-based clinicians demonstrate and report greater confidence in the early initiation of DOACs following acute ischaemic stroke. Over 85% of respondents reported a change in clinical practice, suggesting that trial data can rapidly influence patient care.

items.title: Pathogenic mechanism of exacerbated brain atrophy in Alzheimer's disease exhibiting co-pathology of TDP-43.
items.abstract: While most Alzheimer's disease (AD) which is associated with Limbic Predominant Age-related TDP-43 Encephalopathy (LATE) exhibits accelerated brain atrophy, the pathogenic mechanism remains undefined. In this Perspective, we offer a feed-forward model of TDP-43 dysfunction linked to tauopathy that underpins such exacerbated neuron loss in AD with the co-pathology of TDP-43. Since TDP-43 dysfunction may be initiated in some central neurons of the aging human brain, we modeled this aspect of the human pathophysiology by ablating the gene encoding TDP-43 in excitatory neurons of the mouse forebrain and crossbred them to a tau-seeding mouse model. We found that such selective loss of TDP-43 function facilitated the pathological conversion of endogenous tau to accelerate tauopathy, resulting in exacerbated neuron loss. Since endogenous tau is a substrate of caspases, our finding that TDP-43 dysfunction activated caspase 3 could account at least in part for such an impact on tauopathy. Surprisingly, in our tau-seeding mouse model with deposition of Ab plaques, TDP-43 proteinopathy occurred during late-stage of disease, the emergence of which is dependent on tauopathy. We propose a novel mouse model of AD with the co-pathology of TDP-43 and discuss the potential use of such model to clarify disease mechanisms, disclose novel targets, and to test therapeutic strategies designed to attenuate proteinopathies of tau and TDP-43.

items.title: The gut-lung-brain axis in ischemic stroke.
items.abstract: Ischemic stroke disrupts intestinal homeostasis and pulmonary host defense, but a continuous microbiota-mediated pathway to secondary brain injury remains unproven. This narrative review evaluates gut-brain, gut-lung, and lung-brain interactions, distinguishing experimental evidence, clinical associations, and findings from other disease models. Experimental studies support intestinal microbial and immune contributions to stroke outcomes, barrier dysfunction, and dissemination of selected gut-associated bacteria. However, intestinal expansion is not necessarily required for pulmonary colonization, and microbial origin does not establish transmission routes. Aspiration, hematogenous or lymphatic dissemination, and impaired pulmonary clearance require separate investigation. Pneumonia is associated with poorer neurological outcomes, but microbiome-specific causation remains unestablished. Pulmonary microbiota-dependent immune and neural mechanisms identified in autoimmune and migraine models provide mechanistic precedents, yet their relevance to ischemic stroke remains uncertain. The gut-lung-brain axis therefore represents an evidence-informed framework rather than a proven self-sustaining causal cycle. Establishing microbial sources, transmission routes, and pulmonary mediation of brain injury is essential to identify actionable peripheral mechanisms influencing stroke injury and recovery.

items.title: A noxious stimulus increases the release of dopamine from the nucleus accumbens of mice during pentobarbital sedation, but not during loss of the righting reflex: a behavioral and in vivo brain microdialysis study.
items.abstract: The mesolimbic dopamine (DA) pathway plays a crucial role in arousal and motivation by transmitting DA from the ventral tegmental area to the nucleus accumbens (NAc). We investigated whether the selective DA uptake inhibitor GBR-12909 could reverse the impairment or loss of the righting reflex (LORR)-reflecting sedation and unconsciousness, respectively-induced by the hypnotic pentobarbital, and whether reserpine, a monoamine-depleting agent, could enhance pentobarbital's effects. Additionally, we examined whether a noxious stimulus would increase DA release from the NAc during pentobarbital sedation or LORR. Male ddY mice were administered pentobarbital (15‒80 mg/kg), GBR-12909 (10 mg/kg), or reserpine (5 mg/kg) intraperitoneally. Sedation or LORR was evaluated using the righting reflex test. In vivo brain microdialysis was conducted to measure DA concentrations in the NAc. Ten minutes after the pentobarbital injection, a tail clamp was applied as a noxious stimulus. Based on the righting reflex results, the sedative dose of pentobarbital was identified as 20 mg/kg, with LORR induced at 40 mg/kg. GBR-12909 reversed the sedative effects of low-dose pentobarbital, but did not alter high-dose effects. Reserpine abolished the righting reflex in all pentobarbital-sedated mice. The tail clamp increased NAc DA levels during sedation, but not during LORR. These results suggest that salient environmental events, such as painful stimuli, activate the mesolimbic DA pathway during pentobarbital sedation, but not during LORR. Similarly, the pharmacological activation of DA neurons reversed sedation, but not LORR, suggesting that DA nerve stimulation during sedation could lead to arousal similar to that caused by painful stimuli.

items.title: Feature extraction and recognition of EEG signals induced by natural plant odors for emotion-aware olfactory interfaces.
items.abstract: Olfactory-induced emotions have received increasing attention. However, the neural responses of the brain to natural plant odors remain underexplored in the context of brain-computer interface (BCI) applications. This study proposes an olfactory experimental paradigm using plant odors, comprising three types of stimuli: positive (sweet osmanthus), neutral (air), and negative (Antidesma bunius). The features of electroencephalography (EEG) signals are firstly analyzed in the time, frequency and spatial domains. The energy of the EEG induced by the three types of odors varies differently as the sniffing continues. Gamma-band activity showed significant differences between positive and negative emotions. Spatially, positive emotions primarily activated the frontal and temporal lobes, while negative emotions mainly activated the occipital and parietal lobes. To achieve recognition accuracy, a novel deep learning method that integrates Riemannian geometry filtering has been proposed. The average result of the three-category classification for the 12 subjects reaches 75.22 %, and this result outperforms several traditional baseline methods and deep learning baseline methods. By demonstrating an effective EEG-based emotion recognition framework using natural plant odors, this study provides a new engineering perspective for affective BCIs, with potential applications in emotional therapy and personalized emotion regulation.

items.title: Neurocomputational Mechanisms Underlying Differential Framing Effects on Generosity and Honesty.
items.abstract: The framing effect, a robust cognitive bias, demonstrates that human decision-making is influenced by whether outcomes are presented as gains or losses. Nevertheless, substantial debate remains regarding the extent to which loss frames facilitate or inhibit prosocial behaviors, and the neurocognitive processes through which frames drive these divergent effects remain poorly understood. We combined behavioral analyses, computational modeling, and brain imaging to dissect the neurocognitive substrates underpinning framing effects on two distinct forms of prosociality: generosity and honesty. Fifty-three healthy adult participants completed both the Dictator Game (DG), which primarily captures generosity-related considerations, and the Message Game (MG), which involves honesty-related considerations, allowing us to examine how gain versus loss frames affect choices across these two prosocial decision contexts. Behavioral analyses revealed a significant game type × frame interaction, while computational modeling further identified opposite frame-related changes in the generosity-related parameter β and the honesty-related parameter δ, together revealing differential framing effects across prosocial domains. At the neural level, activations in the amygdala and ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) were modulated by frame and game type: both regions showed greater activation for DG in the gain frame and MG in the loss frame than for DG in the loss frame and MG in the gain frame. Moreover, functional coupling between the vmPFC and temporoparietal junction (TPJ) exhibited an interaction effect consistent with the regional activation pattern, while amygdala and TPJ coupling showed a similar interaction trend. Collectively, these findings suggest the involvement of an amygdala-TPJ-vmPFC circuit in framing-related decision-making, with the TPJ potentially participating in interactions between affective and value-related processes that may contribute to differential framing effects on generosity and honesty.

items.title: Unraveling the interplay between sensory information and semantic architecture in brain concept representation: the role of abstraction.
items.abstract: Introduction Understanding how abstract and concrete words are represented in the brain requires disentangling the contribution of sensorimotor information from the organization of semantic knowledge. These dimensions, here referred to as abstractness and abstraction, respectively, are typically confounded, limiting our ability to identify their distinct neural correlates. Objectives The present study aimed to dissociate the roles of abstractness and abstraction in word processing by introducing superordinate words as a critical comparison category. Methods Behavioral norming and feature production tasks were used to quantify sensory-related properties and semantic architecture, operationalized in terms of generalizability, feature relevance, and representational specificity. These measures informed computational models capturing abstractness, abstraction, sensorimotor content, and distributional similarity. Neural data were acquired using electroencephalography and analyzed with representational similarity analysis to assess model-brain correspondence over time. Results Behaviorally, superordinate words patterned with concrete words on sensory properties but with abstract words on measures of semantic architecture. In the electrophysiological data, concrete words elicited stronger negativities than both abstract and superordinate words in the N400 and N700 time windows, whereas the contrast between abstract and superordinate words did not reach significance. Representational similarity analysis revealed that, among the models tested, the abstraction model was significantly associated with the neural response patterns in the N400 and N700 latencies, whereas models based on abstractness, sensorimotor or distributional information did not reach the significance threshold. Conclusion Within the participants and stimuli tested, these results indicate that semantic architecture provides a useful framework for understanding the neural dynamics of word processing, alongside sensorimotor grounding. They suggest that abstraction may play a central role in structuring conceptual representations, providing a unifying account that bridges embodied and formal theories of semantic representation.
