items.title: Neural correlates of body-focused attention following emotion induction in women with somatic symptom disorder and panic disorder.
items.abstract: Background Somatic symptom disorder (SSD) and panic disorder (PD) involve distressing bodily symptoms but may differ in body-focused attention and emotional processing. The primary objective was to compare neural responses to masked emotional stimuli following somatic attention (SOM) versus cognitive distraction (DIS) across women with SSD, PD, and healthy controls. Secondary objectives explored regional GABA/tCr ratios and brain-clinical correlations. Methods Forty-seven women (16 SSD, 10 PD, 21 controls) were enrolled. Following negative autobiographical emotion induction, participants completed SOM and DIS, each followed by backward masking. Bilateral amygdala and primary somatosensory cortex GABA/tCr ratios were measured using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy. Results A right thalamic group × task interaction was significant (pFWE = 0.021). Descriptively, responses were higher following SOM than DIS in PD, with the reverse pattern in SSD; exploratory post hoc comparisons were nonsignificant after correction. Omnibus group effects involved the left superior temporal gyrus (pFWE = 0.014) and right angular gyrus (pFWE = 0.002). Extracted values suggested lower superior temporal gyrus activation in SSD and higher angular activation in PD. Left insula pattern in a similar direction did not survive whole-brain FWE correction. Exploratory, uncorrected correlations linked angular responses to somatosensory amplification in PD. No significant GABA/tCr group differences were detected. Conclusions SSD and PD showed differing neural response patterns following body-focused attention in an emotionally activated context. Descriptively, PD showed greater thalamic recruitment, whereas SSD showed reduced sensory-affective engagement. These findings suggest possible differences in neural processes underlying bodily distress, although specific group and condition differences require confirmation.

items.title: Association between admission plasma HCO3 concentration and time to post-hospital mortality in 4950 bipolar patients hospitalized for suicidal attempts, ideations, or other reasons.
items.abstract: Background Bipolar disorder (BD) is associated with premature mortality following psychiatric hospitalization and suicidal behavior. Risk prediction remains limited, highlighting the need for readily available biomarkers. Admission plasma bicarbonate (HCO₃ - ) was examined in relation to suicidality and post-hospital mortality. Methods We analyzed electronic health records of 4950 BD patients hospitalized January 2002-December 2025 with ≥2 hospitalizations. Patients were classified as suicide attempt (SA+), suicidal ideation without attempt (SA-/SI+), or neither (SA-/SI-). Clinical and laboratory measures within 2 days of admission were compared by group and sex, with Tukey testing for HCO₃ - . Among decedents, sex-stratified analyses compared discharge-to-death intervals across groups and examined HCO₃ - -time-to-death associations. Results 331 patients (6.7%) were SA+, 2388 (48.2%) SA-/SI+, and 2231 (45.1%) SA-/SI-. Admission HCO₃ - varied by suicidality group and sex (both q = 0.0006), with lowest concentrations in SA+ females and males. Tukey comparisons confirmed lower HCO₃ - than in the other groups. Among SA+ decedents, males died younger than females (41.0 ± 10.1 vs. 50.4 ± 11.2 years) and had a shorter discharge-to-death interval (4.28 ± 3.58 vs. 7.54 ± 4.94 years). Among male decedents, post-hospital survival differed across groups (p = 0.0318), with SA+ shortest, and lower admission HCO₃ - was associated with shorter time to death (p = 0.007). Conclusions Admission HCO₃ - may reflect physiological vulnerability in hospitalized BD patients, particularly in relation to suicidal behavior and post-hospital outcomes. These decedent-only findings reflect the timing of death rather than mortality risk in the full cohort. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether HCO₃ - can provide clinically useful information alongside psychiatric/medical assessment or post-hospital risk stratification.

items.title: Reproductive genetic literacy and health equity: barriers to access and informed decision-making across the reproductive care trajectory.
items.abstract: Background Reproductive genetic testing has transformed reproductive medicine by offering couples the means to identify and manage (heritable) genetic risks before and during pregnancy. Despite the rapid expansion in genetic testing availability, its clinical promise and real-world uptake remain uneven, particularly among ethnic minorities and individuals with lower education. Although declining or postponing testing can represent an informed and value-consistent choice, limited awareness, difficulties interpreting probabilistic or uncertain findings, and emotional barriers may restrict meaningful engagement. Despite efforts to improve counseling and informed choice, there is a lack of integrative frameworks explaining how these individual and systemic factors interact and contribute to inequalities in reproductive genetic care. Objective and rationale We examined barriers to acquiring, interpreting, and applying reproductive genetic information in both screening (general-risk) and diagnostic (high-risk) contexts. We used established behavioral science frameworks to understand why people struggle with reproductive genetic information and sought to develop a conceptual model explaining barriers to informed decision-making. Search methods We searched PubMed from database inception to July 2026 for relevant English-language publications. Reference lists of relevant reviews and key studies were also screened to identify additional sources. Evidence was integrated using a hybrid deductive-inductive thematic approach. Health literacy theory and the Intervention Mapping framework informed the initial coding structure, while additional themes were identified through iterative analysis of the included studies. Outcomes We identified 2643 records, screened 412 abstracts, and assessed 354 full-text articles, of which 162 were included in the final analysis. Studies were excluded primarily due to a technical or diagnostic focus (n = 128) or limited attention to patient experience (n = 64). Three interrelated domains of barriers were identified: (i) cognitive barriers, including limited awareness, misinterpretation of probabilistic results (e.g. variants of uncertain significance), and complex terminology that impede comprehension; (ii) emotional barriers, including anxiety, guilt, and moral conflict, which may distort decision-making; and (iii) systemic barriers, including time-constrained consultations, language barriers, and inconsistent counseling practices that constrain access to and engagement with reproductive genetic services. Wider implications Reproductive genetic literacy should be understood as a shared responsibility between individuals and the systems that generate, communicate, and contextualize genomic information, rather than as an individual knowledge deficit. Improving it requires reducing unnecessary cognitive demands, communicating uncertainty transparently, providing emotionally and culturally responsive counseling, strengthening professional genomic communication competencies, and ensuring equitable access to understandable decision support. The framework proposed here provides a foundation for designing and evaluating literacy-centered interventions intended to strengthen informed, equitable, and value-consistent reproductive decision-making. Registration number N/A.

items.title: Reduced thalamic inhibition underlies prosocial helping deficits in a genetic mouse model of autism.
items.abstract: Prosocial helping is vital for reciprocal relationships. Deficits in prosocial helping behaviors are observed in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), but the causal relationship and molecular mechanisms driving these deficits remain poorly understood. Using a novel mouse model of the rescuable ASD-associated Nlgn3 R451C mutation, we revealed severe deficits in helping behaviors that are not attributable to changes in sensory processing, cognition, emotional contagion, anxiety, social motivation, or motor ability. The helping deficits are linked to thalamic hypoactivation, dysregulation of inhibitory synaptic gene networks, and impaired inhibitory transmission in the mediodorsal thalamus (MD). Restoring endogenous NLGN3 expression in MD neurons and 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) microdosing each partially rescued helping and concomitant inhibitory transmission deficits. Our work establishes a cause-and-effect relationship between a single ASD-associated gene and deficits in helping behaviors, reveals reduced thalamic inhibition as a potential underlying mechanism, and provides evidence that MDMA microdosing rescues these deficits, paving the way for treating helping deficits in individuals with ASD.

items.title: Neurotropic viruses derange FOXG1 and pTBK1 localization in human neural progenitors.
items.abstract: Microcephaly is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder primarily caused by depletion of neural progenitor cells (NPCs), premature differentiation, and/or cell death. Here, we investigated the effects of four neurotropic viruses (HSV2, HCMV, COXB5, and CHIKV-R) on human neocortical neuroepithelial stem cells and induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived NPCs. Viral infection induced nuclear displacement of FOXG1, a transcription factor instrumental in telencephalic development, and severely impaired NPC proliferation, survival, and differentiation. Additionally, exposure to viruses triggered relocation of phosphorylated TBK1 from centrosomes to mitochondria in NPCs and its activation in mature neurons. These findings reveal convergent roles for FOXG1 and TBK1 in virus-associated microcephaly, highlight the selective vulnerability of telencephalic NPCs to viral insults, and shed light on the molecular logic governing cell-cycle progression, differentiation, innate immune responses, and cell death during human cortical development.

items.title: Preliminary safety observations following measles-mumps-rubella vaccination in natalizumab-treated patients with multiple sclerosis: a case series in the context of rising measles incidence in Italy.
items.abstract: Background In Natalizumab (NTZ)-treated patients, only inactivated vaccines are proven safe; live vaccines require caution. Italy shows a measles resurgence, mainly in unvaccinated people with notable complications. Vaccine coverage is insufficient. Objectives Given rising risk, our multiple sclerosis Disease Management Team endorsed measles vaccination during NTZ therapy for susceptible patients, consistent with prior selective VZV vaccination. Results To date, 11 patients have been vaccinated with the Measles-Mumps-Rubella (MMR) vaccine during NTZ treatment at our centre. In three cases, co-administration with the VZV vaccine was necessary. None of the patients who received the vaccine developed vaccine-associated adverse reactions or VZV infection. Conclusions Management of MS requires an integrated approach that balances immunosuppressive treatment risks with preventive strategies, such as vaccination, to reduce infection risk while ensuring patient safety. Larger patient cohorts are needed to confirm our preliminary findings.

items.title: The Physical Prediction Quotient (PPQ-Short): An online measure of mechanical reasoning and a test of sex differences.
items.abstract: Mechanical reasoning is relevant to problem-solving in STEM. The present studies evaluated the Physical Prediction Quotient (PPQ-Short), a 12-item score derived from the Physical Prediction Questionnaire (PPQ), as a short online measure of one aspect of mechanical reasoning, and tested its associations with sex, systemising-related measures, and STEM occupation. Across two online studies (N = 1732; 1072 females), participants completed a 20-item PPQ subset alongside short-form measures of systemising (SQ-10), empathising (EQ-10), autistic traits (AQ-10), and, in Study 2, obsessive-compulsive traits (OCI-R, DOCS). The PPQ-Short was derived from these 20 items by factor analysis and showed good-to-excellent psychometric properties, including a unidimensional structure, high internal consistency (α = 0.86-0.89; GLB = 0.95-0.97), and acceptable-to-good validation fit in Study 2. Males scored higher than females on the PPQ-Short (Cohen's d = 1.03), and sex assigned at birth was the strongest and most stable predictor in multivariable models. PPQ-Short scores showed a small positive association with SQ-10 and a small negative association with EQ-10. Participants with a more systemising cognitive style scored higher than those with a more empathising cognitive style (d = 0.47), and STEM professionals scored higher than non-STEM professionals (d = 0.46). Secondary autism and OCD analyses indicated that diagnostic and symmetry/ordering-related symptom profiles were not consistently associated with higher PPQ-Short performance. These findings support the PPQ-Short as an online measure of one aspect of mechanical reasoning, while also showing that mechanical reasoning performance and self-reported systemising drive are related but not interchangeable.

items.title: Optimizing Eculizumab and Ravulizumab Initiation in Myasthenia Gravis: Infection Risk, Vaccination Timing, and Antibiotic Prophylaxis.
items.abstract: Purpose of review Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune neuromuscular disorder characterized by fatigable muscle weakness and fluctuating symptoms. Complement component 5 inhibitor therapies (C5ITs) such as ravulizumab and eculizumab are rapidly acting treatments for generalized MG (gMG) but associated with an increased risk of meningococcal infection. As such, an ideal strategy for initiating C5IT requires effective mitigation of meningococcal infection risk that permits timely amelioration of disease burden. While C5ITs are approved for several indications, this review focuses on gMG. The available data on infection risk associated with eculizumab and ravulizumab are discussed, and practical approaches for starting these medications are presented. Recent findings Previously, C5IT could be started 2 weeks after the initial doses of meningococcal vaccines. The 2024 updates to meningococcal vaccination policies in the United States extended the completion schedule from 2 months to 6 months and allowed for clinical judgment in initiating C5ITs earlier. In treating patients whose severity of gMG necessitates starting C5ITs before the 6-month vaccination schedule can be completed, clinicians need to consider several factors, including the risk of meningococcal infection, whether the expected reduction in disease burden and improvement in quality of life justify the infection risk, and the potential complications of prolonged antibiotic prophylaxis as an infection risk mitigation strategy. Summary In our opinion, data used to support the change in vaccine schedule did not show a substantial difference in seroresponses. Since C5ITs are likely to remain an important treatment option for gMG, consideration of early vaccination after the diagnosis is recommended to minimize delays in the initiation of C5ITs. Clinical trial data suggest that risk of meningococcal infection in patients with gMG is low, particularly during the first 6 months after C5IT initiation. The evidence supporting the use of extended antibiotic prophylaxis in this patient population is currently scarce. However, clinicians must ensure that the patient is fully aware of the risk, the symptoms of meningococcal disease, and the need for prompt medical attention if those symptoms occur. By taking a comprehensive, individualized approach, clinicians can facilitate the safe and effective use of C5ITs in patients with gMG.

items.title: Say No to Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infections: A Sustained Quality Improvement Initiative in the Neuro Intensive Care Unit.
items.abstract: Background In 2022 and 2023, the Neuroscience Intensive Care Unit (ICU) reported 12 catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs), a marked increase from previous years, prompting a comprehensive review of catheter use, current urine culture collection practices, and evidence-based practices. Objectives The aim of this quality improvement (QI) project was to address gaps in urine culture collection technique, reduce excessive catheter days, foster a unit culture that prioritized evidence-based urinary catheter management, and reduce CAUTI rates over a 3-year period. Methods A multidisciplinary initiative was launched, involving staff education, protocol development, and process changes. Key interventions included direct education sessions on proper urine culture collection, implementation of the Neuroscience ICU Urinary Protocol, the Urinary Catheter Nurse-Driven Removal Protocol, and the Urinalysis (UA) and Urine Culture Collection Protocol. Data management involves monthly audits and real-time education to ensure adherence to protocols. Results Indwelling catheter utilization rates and urine culture collections remained high. However, the unit achieved a 100% reduction in reportable CAUTIs in 2024 and 2025. The unit has 1 CAUTI thus far in 2026. This reflects improved adherence to collection protocols and standard urinary catheter care. Discussion Ongoing collaboration, education, and use of evidence-based practices may be important for sustaining these results and encouraging further improvements in other units. The initiative fostered a culture of critical thinking and autonomy among nurses, with ongoing audits and celebrations of milestones supporting sustained engagement.

items.title: Stress unmasks disconnected endocrine coordination of glucose metabolism in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
items.abstract: Skeletal muscle orchestrates systemic metabolism, dynamically coordinating glucose uptake and fuel use to match energy demand. In Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), loss of dystrophin is associated with altered metabolic regulation. Using physiological stress to unmask metabolic deficits in the mdx mouse model of DMD, we show that stress hormone signaling rises without an appropriate poststress rise in insulin secretion, maintaining hyperglycemia despite elevated basal glucose uptake in skeletal muscle. Rather than reflecting increased gluconeogenesis, this hyperglycemia appears to stem from impaired glucose oxidative disposal; skeletal muscle stores glucose as glycogen instead of oxidizing it, while the heart and brain show persistent, tissue-specific uptake differences. Restoring insulin availability transiently corrects glucose control and reverses stress-induced deficits. Instead of correcting glucose handling, removing excess glucose directly using empagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor) prevents stress-induced increases in blood glucose. These findings identify a breakdown in endocrine-metabolic coordination underlying metabolic vulnerability in DMD and demonstrate two mechanistically distinct routes, restoring insulin secretion or bypassing it entirely, to restore metabolic resilience under stress.

items.title: Biological augmentation of electronic health records through estimation of patient proteomes.
items.abstract: High-dimensional proteomic profiling can improve clinical risk prediction and provide insight into disease biology, but routine acquisition of omic data at population scale remains impractical. We developed Real-world AI-based Biomarker Inference Technology (RABIT), a machine learning framework that biologically augments electronic health records (EHRs) by projecting longitudinal clinical histories into a high-dimensional proteomic representation space learned from paired EHR and plasma proteomics. RABIT was trained using patients with paired EHRs and measured plasma proteomics and externally validated in an independent cohort with paired data. RABIT profiles showed broad concordance with measured protein expression and more closely resembled measured proteomics than their input EHR. Incorporating these biologically augmented representations improved 5-year disease onset prediction across 14 conditions ( n = 449,223; mean adjusted AUPRC increase of 33.7%) and generalized to an external cohort ( n = 1,038,419; mean adjusted AUPRC increase of 70.3%). RABIT profiles reproduced clinically meaningful organ-specific biological changes in response to aging and further outperformed models built from comprehensive established clinical predictors in prediction of chronic kidney disease progression, major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and response to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. Last, RABIT enabled biological signatures derived from small discovery cohorts to be extended to population-scale clinical datasets, generating clinically relevant hypotheses linking cytomegalovirus-associated immune states to variation in brain tumor outcomes. Together, these results demonstrate that biological augmentation of EHRs can enable molecularly informed clinical prediction and hypothesis generation at population scale.

items.title: Impact of training data size and multi-step output strategies on AI-based dekadal and monthly rainfall forecasting.
items.abstract: In climatology and hydrology, rainfall time series are characterized by strong seasonality and cyclic behavior, making reliable forecasting a major challenge for agricultural planning. Accurate forecasts of dekadal and monthly rainfall are essential to optimize crop calendars and improve agricultural productivity. A robust forecasting framework should therefore maintain high predictive performance across different historical record lengths and temporal resolutions. This study evaluated the stability of six artificial intelligence algorithms (SVR, RF, CatBoost, ANN, LSTM, and TNN) combined with four multi-step forecasting strategies (Recursive, Direct, DIRMO, and MIMO). Two historical rainfall datasets spanning 37 and 54 years (providing 30 and 44 years of historical-data configuration, respectively) were used to forecast cumulative rainfall for the next three dekads or months based on a year of historical observations. The two historical-data configurations exhibited substantial differences in forecast accuracy between the machine learning models evaluated. For forecasting dekadal rainfall, the best-performing models achieved RMSE values of approximately 24 mm with the 30-year training-period configuration and approximately 14-15 mm with the 44-year training-period configuration, while the lowest MAE decreased from approximately 17 mm to approximately 10 mm. Similar differences were observed for monthly rainfall forecasting. Non-parametric statistical analyses, including the Friedman, Nemenyi post-hoc, and paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, identified statistically significant differences in forecasting errors between the two historical-data configurations. The pairwise comparisons further showed that the Recursive strategy consistently underperformed the Direct, DIRMO, and MIMO strategies, whereas no significant differences were detected among the latter three. CatBoost and RF maintained consistently high predictive performance across both monthly and dekadal resolutions, while the TNN achieved performance comparable to these tree-based models for dekadal forecasting. In contrast, SVR showed competitive performance at the monthly scale but significantly lower performance at the dekadal scale. Overall, the results demonstrate that rainfall forecasting performance depends not only on the choice of machine learning algorithm but also on the interaction between historical-data configuration, temporal resolution, and forecasting strategy. The comparison of the two historical-data configurations, together with the differences observed across forecasting strategies and model types, provides useful evidence for assessing the robustness of multi-step rainfall forecasting and for informing the development of AI-based decision-support systems for climate-resilient agricultural planning in data-scarce regions.

items.title: Role of sodium-calcium exchanger for impulse conduction in the sinoatrial node of adult mice Impulse conduction in the sinoatrial node.
items.abstract: The sodium-calcium exchanger is the primary mechanism for removing calcium from the cell. Its role in impulse generation (ignition/pacing) of the sinoatrial node has been actively discussed, but the significance for impulse conduction is unknown. A deeper understanding of these mechanisms is essential for understanding the pathophysiology underlying the resulting sinus node dysfunction. In the long term, this could lay the groundwork for pharmacological treatment of these conditions, which to date mostly require the implantation of a pacemaker. To investigate impulse conduction we perform immunofluorescence and fibrotic histological stainings and correlate our findings with electrophysiological data of sharp electrode measurements in the intact sinoatrial node from atrial-specific sodium-calcium exchanger knockout mice. Successful impulse conduction requires overcoming the source/sink mismatch between sinoatrial node and atrial myocardium. Sinoatrial node from knockout shows a significantly higher degree of fibrosis as well as an altered connexin distribution (trend towards a decrease of Connexin 40 in the right atrium, trend towards an increase of Connexin 45 and significant increase of Connexin 40 in the HCN4 positive sinoatrial node), which might have an impact on impaired impulse conduction. Sharp electrode measurements reveal that there are no pacemaker potentials in the sinus node of adult sodium-calcium exchanger knockout mice (sinus arrest) but spontaneous action potentials at the borders to the atria with a typical burst-pause pattern. An atrial-specific knockout of sodium-calcium exchanger appears to influence the source-sink relationship, which can lead to impaired sinoatrial conduction and thus to sinus node dysfunction. Various factors seem to play a role here: altered connexin expression, fibrosis and impaired coupling of membrane and calcium clock possibly due to altered calcium homeostasis. Therefore we conclude that the sodium-calcium exchanger is important not only for the impulse generation, but also for its conduction.

items.title: The role of perceived employability and basic psychological needs in predicting academic outcomes: A semiparametric SEM Approach.
items.abstract: This study examines how university students' perceived employability (PE) and basic psychological need (BPN) satisfaction influence academic motivation and academic outcomes, with gender and university type as moderators. Drawing on self-determination theory and employability frameworks, a moderated mediation model tested via partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) on a sample of 699 undergraduates is proposed. Results indicate that BPN satisfaction was unexpectedly negatively associated with academic motivation, a relationship moderated by gender. Perceived employability showed no significant direct or indirect benefits for academic outcomes, and a slight negative mediated effect suggested that higher confidence in employment prospects can reduce academic motivation. Academic motivation, in turn, did not directly predict academic performance measures in this sample. Crucially, a strong moderating effect of university type was found: The positive impact of motivation on academic success was far greater in private university settings than public ones, leading to a high explained variance in outcomes. These findings highlight the nuanced interplay of career perceptions, psychological needs, and context in shaping student success. Theoretical implications for self-determination theory and employability research and practical recommendations for supporting student motivation are offered in different institutional environments. Limitations (e.g., cross-sectional design and single-country context) and future research directions are also presented.

items.title: Health beliefs and sources of influence in hypothetical robotic surgery decision-making: A nationwide survey in South Korea.
items.abstract: Robotic surgery (RS) is a high-cost surgical option, and decisions about its use may involve input beyond the treating physician. Less is known about the sources of influence individuals rely on when considering RS than about institutional and surgeon perspectives. Drawing on selected concepts from the Health Belief Model (HBM), this study examined associations between HBM-informed measures and reported sources of influence in hypothetical RS decision-making among South Korean adults. A nationwide online survey of 1,012 adults aged 19-69 years was conducted from 26 November to 4 December 2025. The reported primary source of influence, assessed without a defined alternative procedure, was collapsed into doctors' recommendation, family/friends, and other sources. Multinomial logistic regression, with doctors' recommendation as the reference, included sociodemographic, health-related, HBM-informed, and context-related factors. Doctors' recommendation was most frequently reported (54.3%), followed by family/friends (24.8%). Agreement that colorectal cancer represented a serious health threat was associated with lower odds of reporting family/friends (adjusted OR [aOR] = 0.40, 95% CI 0.25-0.65) or other sources (aOR = 0.35, 95% CI 0.21-0.59) rather than doctors. Greater concern about postoperative complications or pain relative to cost showed a similar pattern (family/friends: aOR = 0.57, 95% CI 0.39-0.84; other sources: aOR = 0.48, 95% CI 0.32-0.73). RS experience in respondents or their immediate family was associated with higher odds of reporting family/friends rather than doctors (aOR = 2.03, 95% CI 1.06-3.91). Perceived disease threat and clinical risk concern were associated with greater relative reliance on doctors, whereas prior RS experience was associated with greater reliance on family/friends. Professional risk communication may be particularly relevant when individuals perceive substantial clinical risk.

items.title: Segmentation of sparse coronary artery calcifications in computed tomography via 2.5D multi-slice feature fusion.
items.abstract: Objective Accurate segmentation of coronary artery calcification (CAC) on computed tomography (CT) is critical for reliable cardiovascular risk assessment but remains challenging due to the small and sparse nature of calcified lesions. Although 3D models improve inter-slice consistency, their computational and memory demands motivate alternatives for high-resolution CT segmentation. This study investigates whether the essential inter-slice continuity required for CAC segmentation can be recovered using a reusable 2.5D design compatible with standard 2D networks. Methods We propose a 2.5D segmentation framework that augments conventional 2D encoder-decoder architectures with a localized multi-slice feature fusion module. The framework selectively restores inter-slice continuity by refining a reference slice through self-attention and incorporating anatomically aligned context from its immediate neighboring slices via cross-attention, without volumetric processing. The module is encoder-agnostic and plug-and-play, enabling seamless integration into both convolutional and Transformer-based backbones. The approach was evaluated using patient-level five-fold cross-validation on a public CAC dataset comprising 433 cardiac-gated CT scans with vessel-wise annotations. Results Across all evaluated backbones, the proposed framework consistently improved mean Dice Similarity Coefficient and mean Intersection over Union relative to paired 2D baselines, with additional parameters and computation. The largest class-wise gains were observed in underrepresented artery categories. Attention map analysis provided qualitative support for anatomically coherent inter-slice aggregation. Comparisons with the evaluated 3D models showed competitive segmentation performance with shorter inference times and generally lower peak GPU memory. Conclusion This study demonstrates that localized inter-slice continuity can be effectively incorporated into 2D CAC segmentation frameworks without full volumetric processing. The findings support technical feasibility in the evaluated cohort, while external validation and assessment of downstream calcium scoring are needed before clinical application.

items.title: A phenomenological study of financial toxicity in patients with chronic heart failure: Experiences, coping strategies, and support needs.
items.abstract: Aims To explore the lived experience of financial toxicity among patients with chronic heart failure (CHF) and to inform the development of intervention strategies. Design A qualitative study was undertaken from December 2023 to January 2024. Methods Using a descriptive phenomenological approach, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 CHF patients from a tertiary hospital in Chengdu between December 2023 and January 2024. Participants had been diagnosed with CHF and had been taking medication for at least three months. Maximum variation sampling was employed to ensure diverse perspectives. Data were analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step phenomenological analysis method. Results Three major themes emerged: (1) The burden of survival and emotional toll (including ongoing treatment cost pressures, treatment sustainability concerns, and altered family dynamics); (2) Adaptive responses to financial constraints (including proactive financial planning and treatment decision-making under economic pressure); and (3) Support requirements and expectations (including demands for financial transparency, comprehensive disease management guidance, and psychological support systems). Conclusion This study illuminates the multifaceted nature of financial toxicity in CHF patients, revealing its profound impact on both economic and psycho-social well-being. The findings highlight the complex interplay between financial burden, emotional distress, and family role transitions, while demonstrating patients' resilience through various coping strategies. These insights provide a foundation for developing targeted interventions and comprehensive support systems that address both the practical and emotional dimensions of financial toxicity. Implications for the profession By exploring the nature of patients' financial toxicity, this study provides guidelines for clinical nurses to alleviate the symptoms of patients' financial toxicity,that provides new guidance for clinical evaluation and identification of financial toxicity, and makes nursing more humane. Impact This study is the first to reveal the nature of financial toxicity in patients with CHF. It is found that the financial toxicity of patients with CHF is multifaceted and affects their treatment decisions and prognosis, which needs to be paid attention to. This study will have far-reaching implications for patients, healthcare providers, and social support policies. Reporting method To ensure rigorous reporting standards, the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) was used as a guideline. Patient or public contribution The recruited patients cooperated fully with the staff when they were informed of the purpose and significance of the study during medical visits or hospitalizations. Their willingness to open up and share their experiences with us about financial toxicity provided an important contribution to the conduct of the study.

items.title: Systematic comparison of machine learning approaches for metabolomic biomarker discovery under severe batch effects: From neural networks to support vector machines.
items.abstract: Machine learning is widely applied to metabolomic biomarker discovery, yet systematic comparisons of diverse modeling strategies remain rare, particularly in datasets dominated by severe batch effects. We present a comprehensive and reproducible modeling framework comparing six machine learning approaches for metabolomic classification under extreme technical variation. Using a publicly available metabolomic dataset of five grass species (two barley, two wheat, and one Brachypodium) infected with Fusarium culmorum (116 samples, 24 911 features), we address a scenario in which batch effects exceed biological signal by 4.9-fold (R²_batch/R²_treatment = 4.9:1). Our framework integrates: (i) ComBat batch correction to reduce technical variation while preserving biological signal, (ii) robust Median Absolute Deviation (MAD)-based feature prescreening resistant to batch-driven variance, (iii) shrinkage-regularized differential correlation networks (Ledoit-Wolf) to derive stable edge features capturing infection-related metabolite rewiring, (iv) systematic epoch optimization for a shallow neural network baseline, and (v) comprehensive evaluation of six model classes: shallow neural network, elastic net, random forest, XGBoost, SVM with linear kernel, and SVM with RBF kernel. XGBoost achieved the highest observed performance (AUROC = 0.869, 95% BCa CI: 0.700-0.956), but the difference versus the elastic net baseline (AUROC = 0.754, DeLong p = 0.065) did not reach statistical significance. Bootstrap confidence intervals (BCa, 2,000 iterations) and pairwise statistical tests (DeLong, McNemar) provided rigorous model comparisons. While all models showed modest discriminative ability (AUROC range: 0.754-0.869), reflecting the inherent difficulty of classification under severe batch effects with small sample sizes, tree-based ensemble approaches (XGBoost, Random Forest) showed the strongest point estimates for extracting non-linear biological signal from correlation-network-derived edge features. These results demonstrate that principled feature engineering, batch correction, and systematic model comparison can identify meaningful differences in challenging metabolomic datasets, but larger independent cohorts are needed to confirm model ranking. The proposed open-source workflow provides transparent guidance for datasets in which batch effects dominate biological signal in high-dimensional metabolomics and related omics settings.

items.title: Artificial intelligence literacy, lifelong learning tendency, and teacher-perceived student development among teachers engaged in mathematics gifted education: A survey-based study.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) literacy has become important for teachers' professional development. This survey examined its relationships with lifelong learning tendency and teacher-perceived student development among 353 teachers engaged in mathematics gifted education in China. Four AI-literacy dimensions, two lifelong-learning dimensions, and a four-item teacher-perceived student-development score were analyzed. The outcome was adapted from an existing teacher-report framework. Analyses included reliability, separate and joint confirmatory factor models, discriminant-validity checks, correlations, hierarchical linear regression with HC3 robust inference, and repeated 10-fold cross-validation. Teacher-perceived student development showed internal consistency (alpha = .852; omega = .853) and a well-fitting one-factor model. Correlations with the six teacher characteristics were positive (r = .315-.359). The full regression explained 19.0% of the variance, with mean out-of-fold R2 of .131. Lifelong learning added little beyond AI literacy (delta R2 = .00075; robust block p = .845). AI perception had B = .180 (HC3 p = .0497; Holm-adjusted p = .298); none of the six focal coefficients was significant after Holm adjustment. This study documents positive associations of AI literacy and lifelong learning tendency with teacher-perceived student development, with overlapping explanatory contributions in the combined model. These findings identify AI literacy and lifelong learning as interrelated professional attributes relevant to teacher-perceived student development in mathematics gifted education.

items.title: Nutrient combination enhances neural stem cells proliferation and neuronal differentiation.
items.abstract: Early neurodevelopment is critical for lifelong cognition, and nutrition plays a key role in regulating neural stem cells (NSCs). The mechanisms by which nutrients synergistically influence early brain development still require further investigation, particularly in the context of how specific nutritional components interact at a cellular level. The study revealed significant synergistic interactions among DHA, ARA, PL, and SL in upregulating cellular markers associated with NSC proliferation, early neuronal differentiation, and synaptic maturation. Specifically, a formulation containing DHA and ARA combined with PL (5 ng/mL) and SL (2.6 ng/mL) markedly elevated the expression of key functional markers (BDNF, MAG, NGF, MAP-2, Tuj-1, and Synaptophysin) compared to single or dual components. These in vitro findings demonstrate that an optimized lipid-glycan combination enhances neurodevelopmental marker expression within a safe dosage window, providing a rational empirical baseline for future in vivo preclinical research.

items.title: Clinical balance deficits and gait alterations associated with Iliopsoas tightness in community-dwelling older adults: A cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: This study investigated whether iliopsoas tightness (ILT) in community-dwelling older adults is associated with impaired clinical balance and altered gait mechanics. In this cross-sectional exploratory study, written informed consent was obtained from all participants, and reporting followed STROBE guidelines. Sixty adults aged 65-75 years were classified using the Modified Thomas Test into an IL-tightness group (n = 30) and a no-tightness group (n = 30); IL tightness was defined as a positive Modified Thomas Test, indicated by failure of the posterior thigh to reach the examination table (>10° hip flexion). The primary outcome was functional balance assessed by the Berg Balance Scale (BBS). Overground walking was recorded using a Bertec force plate (1,000 Hz). Secondary outcomes included ground reaction force (GRF) variables. Between-group comparisons were performed using Welch's t-tests, with complementary one-way ANOVA and Hedges' g effect sizes. False-discovery-rate (FDR) correction was applied to secondary biomechanical outcomes. Participants with iliopsoas tightness demonstrated significantly lower balance scores compared with the normal group (BBS: 44.57 ± 2.05 vs. 52.47 ± 2.49; 95% CI: -9.98 to -5.82; p .05). ILT in older adults is significantly associated with reduced functional balance and subtle alterations in early-stance gait mechanics. Interventions enhancing terminal-stance hip extension and propulsion may improve postural control and walking efficiency. IRCT20240917063072N1.

items.title: Influence of menopausal status on the association between serum α-Klotho levels and depression in middle-aged and elderly women: A cross-sectional study from NHANES 2007-2016.
items.abstract: Depression tends to affect women more frequently, and hormonal and biochemical changes during menopause may increase the risk. While serum α-Klotho may influence depression through oxidative stress and inflammation, whether this association differs by menopausal status remains unknown. Therefore, we investigated the association between serum α-Klotho and depression in middle-aged and older women according to menopausal status. We included 5,373 women aged ≥ 40 years from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2007-2016: 4,047 postmenopausal, 1,326 premenopausal. The Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) measured depressive symptoms, with PHQ-9 ≥ 10 marking a positive screen. Serum α-Klotho was log-transformed and grouped into quartiles (Q1-Q4). We fit multivariable regression models adjusting for age, body mass index (BMI), and comorbid conditions, then ran stratified and interaction analyses for effect modification by age, marital status, BMI, hypertension, and serum uric acid. In postmenopausal women, we found lower odds of clinically relevant depressive symptoms at higher serum α-Klotho, reaching adjusted OR 0.70 (95% CI 0.52-0.95) in Q3. The premenopausal group (n = 1,326) showed no association. Sensitivity analyses sharpened the inverse pattern among women aged ≥ 55 years, those living alone, women with a normal BMI, and those with hypertension (OR range 0.30-0.45). Formally, though, the menopausal status × α-Klotho interaction was non-significant (P for interaction > 0.05). The timing and mechanisms remain unresolved. Longitudinal cohorts should establish both and show whether the Klotho pathway offers a realistic intervention target for groups at elevated depression risk.

items.title: Qualitative instability in dynamic eye-movement patterns during handwriting in students with handwriting difficulties: A wearable eye-tracking study.
items.abstract: Handwriting requires the dynamic integration of visual and motor processes, but standardized tests typically assess static abilities and do not capture real-time coordination. This study examined the dynamic eye-movement patterns underlying handwriting difficulties (HD), focusing on why students with preserved motor coordination may still lack handwriting fluency. Thirty-six participants - 17 students with HD (7 boys, and 10 girls; mean age = 12.42 ± 3.58 years) and 19 typically developing (TD) students (7 boys, and 12 girls; mean age = 17.08 ± 0.73 years) - completed a sentence-copying task using a wearable eye-tracking device. To isolate dynamic visuomotor integration from basic motor deficits, the HD group was functionally categorized using Beery-VMI Motor Coordination (MC) scores into low-MC (HDL; n = 9) and high-MC (HDH; n = 8) subgroups. Mixed-factorial ANCOVAs controlling for chronological age compared gaze behavior across the HDL, HDH, and TD groups and two areas of interest: the display and paper. Significant Group × Area interactions were found for mean fixation duration (p = .003) and paper observation ratio (p = .005). TD students exhibited differentiated gaze strategies with longer fixation durations (p < .001) and higher observation ratios (p < .001) on the paper. In contrast, both HD subgroups showed fragmented, undifferentiated gaze patterns across the task areas. Despite having MC scores comparable to those of TD students, the HDH group failed to achieve stable paper fixations, coinciding with significantly lower handwriting fluency across groups (p = .003 for the between-group difference in letters per minute). These findings indicate that HD may be associated with qualitative instability in visual monitoring rather than isolated motor deficits. "Observable looking back and forth" behavior may therefore facilitate classroom screening, while interventions should target integrated dynamic gaze-stabilization rather than isolated motor skills.

items.title: Healthcare worker burnout and heart rate variability.
items.abstract: Occupational burnout is a psychological state that occurs after chronic, persistent workplace stress and impacts individual employees and organizations. It is characterized by three subdomains: emotional exhaustion (EE), depersonalization (DP), and personal accomplishment (PA). It is usually assessed through self-report measures, which have limitations. Identifying physiological correlates of occupational burnout could facilitate passive screening and provide outcome measures for workplace interventions. Prior studies suggest that low heart rate variability (HRV) may be a physiological correlate of burnout, but were limited by small sample sizes and cross-sectional study designs. We used a larger sample size and longitudinal design to conduct an exploratory analysis of associations between sleep-based HRV (using a commercially available wearable device) and self-reported burnout symptoms (abbreviated Maslach Burnout Inventory) among healthcare workers (N = 823) during the COVID-19 pandemic between April and December 2020, and to assess changes in burnout severity. Population-aggregated EE increased in July (+3.3%) and September (+6.1%), but the absolute change in the first and last burnout subdomain scores was negligible. Using linear mixed-effects models adjusted for sex, age, weekday/weekend type, and sleep length, greater EE was associated with lower (1) rMSSD during deep sleep (-0.417, 95% CI: -0.674, -0.160, P = 0.001), and (2) rMSSD (-0.663, 95% CI: -0.977, -0.348, P < 0.001) and HF-HRV (-1.594 × 10 ⁻ ⁴, 95% CI: -2.859 × 10 ⁻ ⁴, -3.294 × 10 ⁻ 5, P = 0.013) during REM sleep. Lower PA was associated with lower rMSSD during deep sleep (-0.235, 95% CI: -0.440, -0.030, P = 0.024) and greater DP was associated with higher rMSSD during deep (0.538, 95% CI: 0.285, 0.792, P < 0.001) and REM sleep (0.369, 95% CI: 0.059, 0.679, P = 0.020). The proportion of variance in HRV explained by burnout symptoms was very small, with small effect sizes despite consistent directional patterns. These exploratory findings identify patterns for future investigation but require confirmation in an independent, preregistered study with prespecified primary outcomes.

items.title: The limits of tolerance: A field experiment on anti-Israel bias at a German University.
items.abstract: After October 7, 2023, reports of anti-Israel expressions at German universities have raised questions about the prevalence and nature of such sentiments in academic environments. Traditional survey-based research on politically sensitive attitudes toward Israel is often limited by response and social-desirability bias. This study introduces a novel field-experimental approach to observing how symbols associated with Israel are treated in a real-world university setting. Using event history analysis, it examines the removal probability of stickers of the Israeli flag compared to German, US, Palestinian, and rainbow flags at a German university. Over a 24-week period, 600 stickers were placed on 50 university notice boards and were monitored over 14-day cycles. The results show a pronounced and consistent pattern of differential removal: the Israeli flag had the highest removal rate, with only 47.5% of these stickers remaining at the end of the observation period-substantially lower than the survival rates of the other flags (which range from 68-80%). Regression analysis confirms that Israeli flags faced the highest removal hazard, with an estimated removal hazard 3.7 to 4.4 times that of the rainbow flag and more than twice that of the German flag. Politically motivated removals were much less frequent and showed a similar descriptive pattern, with Israeli flag stickers accounting for the largest number of events, although the small number of cases limits statistical inference. Among the control variables, removal hazards were highest in hallways of the humanities, shared humanities/social sciences, and central facilities, while higher hallway traffic was associated with lower removal hazards. The comparison set-which includes other national flags and a non-national symbol-argues against simple explanations based on indiscriminate vandalism, broad anti-nationalism, or anti-imperialism within the set of symbols studied, pointing instead to a specific anti-Israel bias relative to the included comparators. Whether this bias reflects antisemitic sentiment remains an open question, as individual motivations cannot be observed.

items.title: Context-dependent recruitment of mouse prefrontal ensembles exhibits distinct vulnerabilities to MeCP2 deficiency.
items.abstract: Adaptive behavior depends on flexible recruitment of prefrontal neuronal populations across contexts, yet how this recruitment is altered in neurodevelopmental disorders remains unclear. Using in vivo calcium imaging in freely moving mice, we find two largely non-overlapping medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) neuronal populations preferentially activated around entry into the center or corners of an open field (center-ON and corner-ON). Subsets of these populations are differentially re-recruited across elevated plus maze and social interaction tasks, indicating flexible, context-dependent population recruitment. Behavioral output is associated with the relative recruitment balance of these populations. In female heterozygous Mecp2+/- mice modeling Rett syndrome (RTT), a severe neurodevelopmental disorder caused by MECP2 mutations, center-ON representation and activity are preferentially reduced, whereas corner-ON properties are comparatively preserved. These findings show that mPFC neuronal populations are flexibly recruited across behavioral contexts and indicate that MeCP2 deficiency selectively disrupts prefrontal population coding rather than producing uniform prefrontal hypoactivity.

items.title: Synaptic Vesicle Glycoprotein 2A and Excitatory-Inhibitory Balance in Psychiatric Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A) is widely used as a positron emission tomography (PET) proxy of synaptic density. PET studies have consistently reported SV2A deficits across schizophrenia-related disorders. Beyond its structural role, SV2A is involved in calcium-dependent neurotransmission and may contribute to the regulation of network excitatory-inhibitory balance. To systematically synthesize preclinical evidence on the role of SV2A in kindling (ie, hyperexcitation) development, an experimental intervention that induces long-lasting increases in brain excitability, and to examine the associations of SV2A modulation with kindling development as a model of hyperexcitation, with implications for interpretation of SV2A PET findings in neuropsychiatric disorders. EMBASE, MEDLINE, and PsycINFO were searched from inception to December 30, 2025. Experimental animal studies assessing SV2A expression or pharmacological or genetic modulation in kindling models. Two independent reviewers performed study selection, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment (Systematic Review Centre for Laboratory Animal Experimentation tool). This systematic review was registered in PROSPERO and conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood estimation were conducted for seizure severity and odds of reaching kindling criteria. Heterogeneity was assessed using Q, τ2, and I2 statistics, and meta-regression analyses examined potential moderators. Changes in SV2A expression, seizure severity, and odds of reaching kindling criteria. Thirty studies were included across 3 categories: SV2A measurement (7 studies), genetic (2 studies) and pharmacological modulation (22 studies), with 1 study contributing to 2 of these categories. Kindling experiments in wild-type animals consistently reported higher hippocampal SV2A expression, primarily in GABAergic neurons. Genetic models of reduced SV2A function showed higher susceptibility to kindling. SV2A-targeting interventions were associated with significantly lower seizure severity (Hedge g = -2.16; 95% CI, -2.95 to -1.37; P < .001; I2 = 82.3%) and lower odds of reaching kindling (odds ratio, 0.04; 95% CI, 0.02 to 0.08; P < .001; I2 = 0.4%). This meta-analysis found that SV2A expression is dynamically regulated by neuronal activity and may represent a compensatory mechanism aimed at restoring synaptic homeostasis in response to repeated excitatory stimulation. These findings suggest that SV2A may index not only synaptic density but also circuit resilience, with potential relevance for neuropsychiatric disorders characterized by excitatory-inhibitory dysregulation.

items.title: National Trends and Projections in Utilization of Emergency Department CT and MRI Across Radiology Subspecialties.
items.abstract: Background: Prior studies have documented increasing utilization of emergency department (ED) CT and MRI but have generally focused on restricted populations or on individual modalities, anatomic regions, or clinical indications. Purpose: To characterize temporal trends in utilization of CT and MRI across radiology subspecialties in U.S. EDs and to project future such utilization shifts. Methods: This retrospective study used deidentified aggregate EHR data from U.S. healthcare organizations participating in the Epic Cosmos platform. The platform was queried from 2016 to 2025 to identify annual counts for ED encounters and associated CT and MRI events, stratified by subspecialty, age group, and U.S. census region. Utilization was expressed per 100 ED encounters. Quasi-Poisson regression models were used to determine annual percentage change and to project utilization through 2030. Results: The analysis included 431,876,897 ED encounters during the study period. Utilization per 100 encounters for CT increased from 27.3 to 53.9 (annual percentage change, 7.4%), for MRI from 3.6 to 5.4 (4.3%) and for CT and MRI combined from 30.9 to 59.3 (7.1%). The proportion of ED encounters without CT or MRI decreased from 80.0% in 2016 to 66.8% in 2025. Utilization per 100 encounters increased for all subspecialties (6.2-9.1%), age groups (5.0-6.2%), and census regions (5.6-7.6%). Among subspecialties, the contribution to the absolute increase in utilization was greatest for neuroradiology (36.3%) and body imaging (29.0%). Assuming that the trend from 2016 through 2025 remained unchanged through 2030, utilization per 100 encounters was projected to increase further for CT to 78.4, for MRI to 6.7, and for CT and MRI combined to 84.8. In sensitivity analyses, projected utilization per 100 encounters for CT and MRI combined in 2030 was 85.5 when excluding calender years 2020 and 2021 (relating to the COVID-19 pandemic) and 80.6 when modeling based on only years 2022 through 2025. Conclusion: Per-encounter ED utilization of CT and MRI increased substantially from 2016 to 2025; the growth occurred broadly across subspecialties, age groups, and census regions. Clinical Impact: These findings may inform targeted workforce allocation, scanner capacity planning, workflow redesign, and imaging stewardship strategies, to help address evolving ED imaging demands.

items.title: Blood-Based Pathway Transcriptomics for Multicohort Classification of Parkinson's Disease: An Exploratory Computational Study.
items.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is increasingly recognized as a disorder with systemic immune manifestations. However, reproducible blood-based transcriptomic signatures remain elusive because single-gene effects are small and sensitive to cohort and platform differences. We developed an immune-pathway blood transcriptomic classifier by transforming public GEO expression profiles into single-sample gene-set enrichment scores (ssGSEA). A frozen panel of 118 immune-related pathways was used to train an elastic-net regularized logistic-regression model. The discovery analysis included 501 samples (246 PD cases, comprising idiopathic and genetic PD, and 255 controls, comprising healthy controls and unaffected mutation carriers). Strict nested 10-fold cross-validation yielded ROC-AUC = 0.629 and PR-AUC = 0.629. In external whole-blood cohorts, directional ROC-AUC was 0.660 in GSE6613 and 0.567 in GSE72267; after standardizing scores relative to controls within each cohort, the pooled ROC-AUC was 0.623 (n = 131) and the pooled PR-AUC was 0.780 against a PD prevalence of 0.687. Model coefficients assigned both positive and negative weights across correlated immune-pathway features. These findings indicate that immune-pathway representations of whole-blood transcriptomes contain a modest, externally detectable PD-associated signal. The model is exploratory rather than diagnostic: the analysis does not establish disease specificity, causal mechanisms, or equivalence between peripheral blood and brain biology, and it requires prospective RNA-seq validation with harmonized demographic and clinical metadata.

items.title: Ammonia Neurotoxicity and the Potential Relevance of Ammonia-Induced Cell Death to Selected Neurodegenerative Diseases.
items.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and Huntington's disease, are characterized by the progressive loss of neuronal structure and function. Increasing evidence indicates that disturbances in ammonia metabolism and elevated ammonia exposure can impair neuronal and glial function through mitochondrial dysfunction, altered energy metabolism, oxidative stress, neurotransmitter imbalance, and neuroinflammation. However, these established neurotoxic effects should be distinguished from ammonia-induced cell death, a lysosomal-mitochondrial injury mechanism reported in activated effector CD8⁺ T cells. In this process, intracellular ammonia accumulation induces lysosomal alkalinization, impairs autophagic clearance of damaged mitochondria, disrupts mitochondrial homeostasis, and ultimately causes cell death. At present, direct evidence demonstrating ammonia-induced cell death in neurons or in experimental models of neurodegenerative diseases is lacking. Nevertheless, several pathological features associated with ammonia-associated neurotoxicity, including mitochondrial damage, lysosomal dysfunction, defective autophagy, oxidative stress, and energy failure, overlap with processes implicated in neurodegeneration. This mechanistic convergence raises the possibility that similar ammonia-associated lysosomal-mitochondrial injury may contribute to neuronal vulnerability under specific pathological conditions, although this hypothesis requires direct experimental validation. This review summarizes ammonia production, transport, detoxification, and neurotoxicity; describes the molecular features of ammonia-induced cell death; and critically evaluates the evidence linking ammonia metabolism abnormalities to neurodegenerative diseases. We further discuss therapeutic strategies aimed at reducing ammonia burden, preserving mitochondrial and lysosomal function, modulating the gut-liver-brain axis, and limiting oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. Finally, we highlight major evidence gaps and propose experimental approaches needed to determine whether the reported lysosomal-mitochondrial injury mechanism contributes causally to neuronal death in neurodegenerative diseases.

items.title: Semi-automated segmentation of 2D T1-defined black holes on 3D T1-weighted gradient-echo images in multiple sclerosis.
items.abstract: To develop and validate a semi-automated method for segmenting 2DT1-weighted (T1w) spin-echo (SE)-defined black holes (BHs) on 3DT1w gradient-echo (GRE) images in people with multiple sclerosis (pwMS), accounting for the increased sensitivity of the GRE protocol. Eighty-eight pwMS with 2DT1w SE, 3DT1w GRE, and 3D-FLAIR scans were selected from the Amsterdam MS cohort. A semi-automated 3DT1w BH method (3DBHSeg) was developed in an optimization set (n = 20) using cortical gray matter (cGM)-based intensity thresholding, optimized against manually segmented 2DT1w-defined BHs. Performance was evaluated in a validation set (n = 68) using a hybrid score, incorporating voxel-wise, lesion-wise, and volumetric agreement metrics. Associations between BH volume and EDSS score were assessed using adjusted linear regression models. The optimal threshold for BH segmentation was 0.95 × median(cGM) intensity. In the validation set, median BH volume was 1.54 mL (IQR: 0.80-2.57 mL) for 3DBHSeg and 1.24 mL (IQR: 0.65-2.47 mL) for the 2DT1w reference, with a hybrid score of 0.76, an ICC (absolute agreement) of 0.92 (95% CI [0.87-0.95]), and a mean DSC of 0.59 ± 0.10. The median BH/FLAIR lesion volume ratio was 24.3%. Log-transformed 3DBHSeg volume was associated with EDSS score (B = 0.33, p = 0.04), whereas FLAIR lesion volume was not (B = 0.19, p = 0.30). 3DBHSeg enables segmentation of BHs on heavily T1-weighted 3D GRE images in accordance with their definition on mildly T1-weighted 2D SE images, allowing quantification of severe tissue damage in MS. Question Black holes reflect areas of severe tissue damage in multiple sclerosis, yet no validated segmentation method exists for contemporary 3D T1-weighted gradient-echo acquisitions. Findings Our method, 3DBHSeg, segmented black holes on 3D T1-weighted images, achieving an ICC of 0.92 and DSC of 0.59 relative to a 2D T1-weighted reference. Clinical relevance 3DBHSeg enables identification of black holes, as originally defined on 2D T1-weighted images, directly on 3D gradient-echo acquisitions, allowing quantification of severe tissue damage associated with clinical disability in multiple sclerosis in the absence of 2D T1 images.

items.title: Consensus on procedural steps and end-product definition for robotic distal and total gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy: the MASTER-D2 Delphi study.
items.abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate consensus among experts in robotic gastric cancer surgery on the procedural steps of robotic distal and total gastrectomy (DG, TG) and the anatomical end-points of D2 lymphadenectomy. Variability in intraoperative performance during gastric cancer surgery impacts immediate postoperative and long-term oncological outcomes. There is no consensus on the procedural steps and anatomical end-points for robotic gastrectomy. A modified Delphi was conducted with 15 expert surgeons from Europe, Asia and North America. Items were generated via hierarchical task analysis, rated through two anonymous online rounds, and finalised at an in-person meeting. Consensus was defined as ≥ 80% agreement. Internal consistency, inter-rater agreement, and stability were assessed. Of 19 invited experts, 15 (79%) completed Rounds 1 and 2, and 13 (86.7%) attended Round 3. Consensus was achieved on 85 statements: 62 of 67 items for DG, 57 of 65 for TG, and 14 items defining the anatomical boundaries and post-dissection end-product of a D2 lymphadenectomy. Ten items did not reach consensus. Inter-rater agreement improved between the online rounds. Consensus was reached on the procedural steps of robotic DG and TG and the anatomical end-points of D2 lymphadenectomy, defining the content to be scored in each phase by a future surgical quality assurance tool. These 85 statements provide the content evidence for MASTER-D2. Evidence of reliability, and of relations to surgeon experience and patient outcomes, will be gathered through video-based testing in future studies.

items.title: Trauma & Stroke: Cerebrovascular Complications in Traumatic Brain Injury.
items.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for cerebrovascular complications that contribute to mortality and long-term disability. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the mechanisms, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and management of cerebrovascular complications after TBI, including post-traumatic cerebral infarction, blunt cerebrovascular injury, post-traumatic vasospasm, delayed cerebral ischemia, and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis. Recent studies have improved understanding of the roles of endothelial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, coagulopathy, and impaired cerebral autoregulation in the pathogenesis of cerebrovascular injury after TBI. Contemporary trauma and stroke guidelines increasingly support systematic vascular imaging, multidisciplinary decision-making, and individualized antithrombotic strategies. Early identification of cerebrovascular complications requires serial neurological assessments, targeted vascular imaging, and physiologic monitoring. Management should be guided by the specific vascular phenotype while balancing ischemic and hemorrhagic risks. Future prospective studies are needed to standardize diagnostic criteria, refine surveillance strategies, and optimize mechanism-specific therapies.

items.title: Association of baseline dopamine transporter binding with early clinical stage transitions and functional milestones in individuals at risk for Parkinson's disease.
items.abstract: Early progression in individuals at risk for Parkinson's disease (PD) can involve both emerging symptoms and changes in daily function. Identifying baseline markers associated with these changes could inform longitudinal assessment and risk stratification. Although lower dopamine transporter (DAT) binding has been linked to clinical conversion, its relationship with early clinical stage transitions and functional milestones across different PD risk populations remains unclear. Using prospectively collected data from the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative, we studied 1,696 GBA1 or LRRK2 variant carriers and individuals with isolated rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder or hyposmia. Adjusted cause-specific Cox models assessed baseline putaminal DAT binding in relation to first clinical stage progression and functional milestones over three years. Additional analyses evaluated α-synuclein seed amplification assay (SAA) status and baseline clinical stage. Lower DAT-binding was linked to higher stage-progression hazard, with a steeper gradient at lower values (Holm-adjusted P < 0.001; unadjusted nonlinearity P = 0.020). Each 0.5-unit lower specific binding ratio corresponded to a higher hazard of first attainment of functional impairment (hazard ratio [HR] 1.55, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.26-1.90). Milestone hazard was higher at baseline stage ≥ 3 than stage 2 (HR 3.14, 95% CI 2.30-4.29). DAT binding was not significantly associated with milestones. SAA positivity showed no significant relationship with stage progression or milestones. These findings link baseline DAT binding to early clinical stage transitions and baseline functional impairment to subsequent milestones, supporting further evaluation of both measures for risk stratification in longitudinal studies.

items.title: Jump: Making Large-Scale Connectomics Accessible
items.abstract: Large-scale connectomic resources generated from volumetric electron microscopy (EM) have transformed neuroscience by enabling detailed 3D reconstructions of cellular and subcellular morphology and connectivity across hundreds of thousands of cells in diverse tissues and organisms. Recent advances in machine learning-based cell classification and automated segmentation have enabled large-scale annotation of these datasets, yet barriers remain in validating automated classifications and extracting biological insights. To address these challenges, we developed Jump, a suite of user-friendly web-based platforms generated using Claude. These platforms support interactive exploration, expert-guided community review, and quantitative analysis of multiple publicly available EM datasets, while building a growing repository of community-generated annotations. Using uJump, which hosts data from the MICrONS mouse visual cortex dataset, as an example, we demonstrate rapid retrieval of specific cell populations, region-of-interest filtering, biological inspection of cells, and extraction of quantitative morphological and spatial metrics. We showcase analytical features including cell abundance and spatial organisation, connectivity, local cellular neighbourhoods, and volumetric measurements. Using pericytes and endothelial cells as a case study on the cortical vasculature, we further demonstrate how manual review and reclassification can generate accurately identified cell populations for downstream analyses. Consistent with the open-science principles underpinning many large-scale EM resources, Jump is designed to enable broad community participation. By lowering technical barriers to the use of EM datasets, Jump increases analytical efficiency and promotes collaborative efforts to accurately classify cells and structures. Expert-reviewed annotations can be shared across the community, allowing users to build on existing work rather than repeatedly validating the same automated classifications. Collectively, Jump will help researchers to accelerate biological discovery from connectomic datasets.

items.title: Detail: species-agnostic, generalizable animal behavior analysis using foundation model embeddings
items.abstract: Automated tools for quantifying and classifying animal behavior from video data are crucial for neuroscience, medicine, and biology. Automated analysis of animal behavior from video usually starts with pose estimation, which needs manually annotated training frames for each new species or setup and reduces an animal to a small number of biased keypoints. Here we present Detail, a behavior analysis package built on foundation vision models, for species- and context-agnostic analysis of animal behavior. Animals are segmented from video frames using SAM 3, egocentrically aligned using keypoints placed by DINOv3 patch matching, and encoded by a frozen DINOv3 model as high-dimensional pose embeddings. Beyond a few annotated example frames, no labeled training data are required. Segmentation and keypoint models can be distilled into YOLO models that run quickly on a single consumer graphics card. Analysis modules operate directly on the pose embeddings for unsupervised behavior discovery, example-based behavior retrieval, precision auditing, and statistical comparison across experimental conditions. At the core of Detail is a pose embedding space, generated from an experiment's videos, that represents animal behavior. The complete workflow, from installation to analysis, is available through graphical and command-line interfaces for scripted and high-throughput use. Detail is available at https://github.com/detail-embedding/detail.

items.title: A decision support toolkit for AI-ready neuroscience data governance
items.abstract: Contemporary human neuroscience relies on exchanging and analyzing neurodata across global institutions andjurisdictions. However, regulatory architecture fails to maintain continuity of protection across distributed researchenvironments. Our comparison of 93 countries and 10 operative governance units across Africa, Europe, LatinAmerica and the Caribbean, and North America shows that neurodata are rarely recognized as distinct regulatoryobjects, usually falling under broader legal classifications. While international sharing is permitted in principle,transformation into derivatives, embeddings, and AI models raises questions about the scope and implementation ofcontinuing safeguards. We show that international exchange is defined by conditional interoperability, where effectivesafeguards require aligning legal, institutional, and technical controls. To operationalize these findings, we introduce amodular governance toolkit for the data-to-model lifecycle, including a Neurodata Risk Classification Framework,decision support tools for neurodata transfer and transformation, and a Neurodata Transfer and Access Agreement tosustain protection without global legal harmonization.

items.title: A decision support toolkit for AI-ready neuroscience data governance
items.abstract: Contemporary human neuroscience relies on exchanging and analyzing neurodata across global institutions andjurisdictions. However, regulatory architecture fails to maintain continuity of protection across distributed researchenvironments. Our comparison of 93 countries and 10 operative governance units across Africa, Europe, LatinAmerica and the Caribbean, and North America shows that neurodata are rarely recognized as distinct regulatoryobjects, usually falling under broader legal classifications. While international sharing is permitted in principle,transformation into derivatives, embeddings, and AI models raises questions about the scope and implementation ofcontinuing safeguards. We show that international exchange is defined by conditional interoperability, where effectivesafeguards require aligning legal, institutional, and technical controls. To operationalize these findings, we introduce amodular governance toolkit for the data-to-model lifecycle, including a Neurodata Risk Classification Framework,decision support tools for neurodata transfer and transformation, and a Neurodata Transfer and Access Agreement tosustain protection without global legal harmonization.

items.title: A flexible model for photosynthetic growth of phycobilisome-containing cyanobacteria under different colors of light.
items.abstract: Phycobilisome (PBS)-containing cyanobacteria and red algae often achieve much higher growth rates in colors absorbed by their PBS than in blue light absorbed by the chlorophyll Soret band. Although this phenomenon is well known, the underlying mechanisms and quantitative role of PBS remain incompletely understood. Here, we address the question why growth is higher for colors absorbed by the PBS, and assess the role of the flexible, modular structure of the photosynthetic machinery. To this end, we developed a mechanistic growth model linking light absorption by chlorophyll and phycobilin pigments to the electron transport rate through the Z-scheme of photosynthesis, maximized by flexible adjustment of the PSI/PSII ratio and redistribution of PBS antennae. Applying this model to Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 under different light colors, we reproduce experimental growth rates as well as changes in PSI/PSII stoichiometry measured by 77K fluorescence. The model shows that high growth rates in orange and red light arise primarily from the large absorption cross-sections of the PBS and photosystems, respectively. In line with experimental data, the model predicts a decrease of the PSI/PSII ratio in blue light. Contrary to previous hypotheses, the model does not support a stronger imbalance between PSI and PSII in blue light than in other colors; instead, it attributes low growth rates in blue light to a low photochemical efficiency of both photosystems. These results demonstrate that wavelength-dependent growth in PBS-containing phototrophs emerges naturally from the spectral absorption properties of their photosynthetic machinery and the efficiency of their photosystems.
