items.title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage.
items.abstract: Over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH 4 ), exerting a slow net cooling effect 1 . Artificial drainage of these ecosystems-a centuries-old practice 2,3 -causes decomposition and the re-release of CO 2 but suppresses CH 4 emissions 4 , with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale 5 . Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800-2020 by combining a new flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO 2 and CH 4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48-99) mW m -2 -equivalent to 2.7 (1.8-3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing-originating from 0.4-0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO 2 emissions (+83 (52-110) mW m -2 ) over that of avoided CH 4 emissions (-9 (-15--2) mW m -2 ). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining currently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO 2 and CH 4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate.

items.title: Sources and drivers of antibiotic resistance genes across rivers and lakes.
items.abstract: River and lake ecosystems are important reservoirs and transmission pathways for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), yet the global distribution, sources and risks of their resistomes remain poorly understood. Here we analysed 4,128 river and lake metagenomes (water and sediment) from 42 countries and regions and constructed a comprehensive genome-resolved catalogue of ARG-carrying bacteria, revealing key pathogenic vectors of resistance. Clinically important ARGs, including bla OXA and mcr, were widespread and showed distinct biogeographical patterns, highlighting rivers and lakes as potential sentinels for global antimicrobial resistance surveillance. Here, using an integrative source-tracking framework, we identified aquaculture, hospital sewage and municipal sewage as major contributors to riverine resistomes, with the estimated contribution of aquaculture increasing from 11% in 2012 to 40% in 2020. Human population and aquaculture intensity emerged as key drivers of the distribution and associated risks of river and lake resistomes. We further generated a predictive global map of freshwater resistome risk. By transforming metagenomic data into a tool for tracing antimicrobial resistance, our study establishes rivers as potential early-warning systems and supports their integration into One Health surveillance frameworks.

items.title: Toward scalable population genomics from environmental DNA.
items.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has transformed biodiversity monitoring and is increasingly used to recover within-species genetic variation. Over the past decade, PCR-based approaches have demonstrated the potential of eDNA for population genetic inference, but important limitations remain in accessing genome-wide nuclear variation. Here, we argue that hybridization capture could represent a key methodological step toward scalable population genomics from eDNA across aquatic, terrestrial, and aerial ecosystems. Drawing on lessons from paleogenomics, where capture-based enrichment has revolutionized the recovery of ancient nuclear DNA from complex environmental samples, we outline its promise, current limitations, and provide recommendations for future applications. We discuss how this approach could support the integration of genetic diversity indicators into global biodiversity monitoring and conservation policies.

items.title: Feeding habits of the notothenioid fishes Patagonotothen sima (Richardson, 1845) and Patagonotothen cornucola (Richardson, 1844) along shallow waters of argentine patagonia.
items.abstract: Information on the feeding ecology of intertidal notothenioid fishes remains limited in Argentine Patagonia, particularly for Patagonotothen sima. This study examined the diets of P. sima and P. cornucola and their spatial and seasonal variation using stomach-content analysis. Sampling was conducted at four coastal localities between March 2021 and March 2022. Patagonotothen sima was collected at two localities and P. cornucola at three; the interspecific comparison was restricted to Cerro Avanzado during winter. Patagonotothen sima fed mainly on polychaetes and small crustaceans, including tanaidaceans, amphipods and decapods, and exhibited an intermediate niche breadth (0.44). In P. cornucola, amphipods and polychaetes were important at Cerro Avanzado, whereas Exosphaeroma sp. and amphipods were prominent at Yamana. At El Pique, the diet was dominated by Exosphaeroma sp., with a narrow niche breadth (0.25), compared with intermediate values at Cerro Avanzado (0.56) and Yamana (0.59). Significant Site × Season interactions were detected in both species, as well as an interspecific difference at Cerro Avanzado during winter. These findings provide a detailed characterisation of the diet of P. sima in Argentine Patagonia and highlight spatial and seasonal variation in the trophic ecology of both species.

items.title: High-altitude microbial communities maintain carbon pool stability through functional redundancy under physical disturbance.
items.abstract: High-altitude alpine ecosystems are recognized as significant carbon reservoirs, yet their vulnerability to physical disturbance from accelerating infrastructure development remains uncertain. The conventional view holds that these ecosystems, with their harsh environmental conditions, are particularly susceptible to carbon loss following disturbance. Here we challenge this assumption by demonstrating that high-altitude microbial communities possess greater functional redundancy, which is strongly associated with reduced soil organic carbon (SOC) loss upon physical disturbance. Along a 621-km elevational transect (700-4,300 m a.s.l.) on the south-eastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, we collected paired soil samples from undisturbed and physically disturbed sites, and integrated soil carbon fractionation, metagenomic sequencing, and targeted metabolomics. We found that high-altitude soils had higher SOC and microbial necromass carbon (MNC) content, coupled with greater Pielou's evenness of carbon-cycle functional genes-a proxy for functional redundancy-than low-altitude soils. Following physical disturbance, MNC loss rates were significantly lower at high elevations than at low elevations, and this buffering effect was strongly explained by functional redundancy (R 2 = 0.64, P < 0.001), whereas taxonomic composition contributed a comparatively minor proportion (6%). Metabolomic analysis revealed that disturbance-induced depletion of nucleotide metabolites was less pronounced at high elevations, and the depletion patterns were significantly correlated with both functional redundancy and MNC loss, suggesting nucleotide metabolism as a potential mechanistic pathway linking functional redundancy to carbon stability. During post-disturbance recovery (3-5 years), however, the functional redundancy advantage was masked by temperature limitation: absolute recovery rates were slower at high elevations, although recovery efficiency per unit temperature was higher. These findings demonstrate that high-altitude microbial communities maintain carbon pool stability through functional redundancy, a mechanism that is decoupled from taxonomic identity, but the recovery phase is constrained by low temperatures. Our study provides a mechanistic framework for understanding elevation-dependent soil carbon resistance, informing the management of alpine ecosystems under accelerating anthropogenic disturbance.

items.title: River recreational swimming: A non-negligible source of aquatic antibiotic resistance genes and pathogenic bacteria.
items.abstract: Water-based recreational activities represent an important pathway for introducing microbial contaminants into aquatic systems. However, the impact of river swimming on riverine antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and human bacterial pathogens (HBPs, including potential HBPs) remains poorly characterized. In this study, we investigated the longitudinal variations of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), mobile genetic elements (MGEs), and HBPs in three river swimming zones with different human traffic densities. The results showed a significant increase in the cumulative absolute abundance of ARGs (0.20 to 1.01 log 10 units) after swimming activities, which was positively associated with swimmer traffic. Taxonomic profiling based on full-length 16S rRNA sequencing also revealed that swimming activities could drive a 2.24-to-2.78-fold enrichment of potential HBPs in proximal downstream water. Longitudinal tracking of the river with the highest swimmer traffic showed a natural attenuation of ARGs and shared HBPs in distal downstream water, indicating the self-purification capacity of river systems, but their abundance remained higher than upstream baseline levels. Network analysis further exhibited significant co-occurrence patterns among potential HBPs, ARGs, and MGEs, suggesting possible ARG carriage by HBPs and a theoretical risk of MGE-facilitated dissemination in river water. Finally, SourceTracker analysis revealed that skin and saliva were important contributors to the proximal downstream microbial load. This study provides comprehensive insights into swimming-induced microbial pollution and highlights the urgent need for implementing source controls to safeguard public health in recreational rivers.

items.title: Size distribution, dry deposition and health risk of atmospheric per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances in a metro-mountainous city, southwest China.
items.abstract: A total of fourteen sets of size-segregated (>9.0, 4.7-9.0, 2.1-4.7, 0.7-2.1, and <0.7 μm) atmospheric particle samples, covering four seasons from October 2023 to August 2024, were collected from Chongqing, a metro-mountainous city in southwest China. These samples were analyzed for 20 target per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) by HPLC-MS/MS to understand their size distribution, atmospheric deposition and health risk. The seasonal average concentration of PFAS was 367.65 ± 144.58 pg·m-3, with higher levels observed in autumn and winter than in spring and summer. The PFAS were mainly enriched in fine particles, with particles smaller than 2.1 μm contributing 53.6%-75.7% of the total. Seasonally, fine-particle enrichment was more pronounced in autumn and summer, whereas the size distribution was relatively more dispersed in spring and winter. The dry deposition flux of PFAS was estimated as an annual average of 106.95 ± 48.93 ng·m-2·d-1 and 149.50 ± 100.14 ng·m-2·d-1 using two different deposition models. The health risk assessment showed that the HQ values for inhalation exposure to the assessed PFAS were below 1 for all age groups, indicating low non-carcinogenic risk. However, the enrichment of PFAS in fine particles and their deposition in deeper regions of the respiratory tract still deserve further attention. This study provides size-resolved evidence for understanding the occurrence, deposition output, and inhalation exposure risk of particle-bound PFAS in Chongqing. It also offers a useful reference for future studies of atmospheric PFAS in mountainous urban environments.

items.title: Phylogenomic reconstruction and chromosome-scale genome evolution during lineage diversification in Morchella.
items.abstract: Lineage diversification in fungi involves evolutionary changes across multiple genomic scales. Although gene gain, loss, and sequence divergence have been widely studied, the broader relevance of chromosome compartmentalization beyond the pathogen-focused systems in which it has been studied remains unclear. Here, we generated 18 high-quality Morchella genome assemblies and integrated them with 39 published genomes to establish a 57-genome comparative framework. A time-calibrated phylogenomic analysis of 91 ascomycete genomes resolved Elata and non-Elata as the two major lineages of Morchella. Gene-tree discordance was consistent with incomplete lineage sorting, and tests of allele sharing suggested a possible contribution from historical gene exchange. Chromosome-scale comparisons across 19 high-contiguity genomes identified a conserved core karyotype comprising approximately 24 chromosome groups, together with lineage-associated accessory chromosome (AS) remodeling. Unlike the preservation of core chromosome architecture, AS chromosomes showed reduced conservation, increased repeat content, and heterogeneous gene repertoires. Ancestry analyses revealed that AS chromosomes possess mosaic gene repertoires that include both deeply conserved genes traceable to related lineages and lineage-associated gene components. Across the 57-genome pangenome, 1,575 lineage-biased orthogroups were identified, and chromosome-aware reconciliation demonstrated that lineage-biased repertoires were significantly enriched among AS-associated families after controlling for copy number, prevalence, and multiple-testing effects. Gene-family turnover and sequence evolutionary-rate differences provided complementary but partially independent signals of genome diversification. Together, our results reveal that Morchella diversification is associated with the coexistence of a conserved chromosome framework and spatially structured gene-repertoire remodeling. These findings highlight chromosome-scale organization as an important evolutionary dimension linking genome architecture and lineage diversification in macroascomycete lineage.

items.title: Community Diversity and Predictive Distribution of Japanese Encephalitis Virus Vectors Across North Borneo Sabah Malaysia.
items.abstract: Japanese encephalitis (JE) is an important but neglected tropical disease that remains endemic in Borneo, Malaysia. Effective management and monitoring of the disease require information about the mosquito vector; however, data on the ecology and spatial distribution of Culex mosquitoes associated with Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) are limited. This study characterized Culex community composition across multiple districts in Sabah and predicted the spatial distribution of major vector species using species distribution modeling (SDM). Mosquitoes were collected from Tawau, Semporna, Sandakan, and Kudat using CDC light traps, BG-Sentinel traps, and human-baited double nets during peak activity periods. Community diversity and species composition were analyzed using analysis of variance (ANOVA) and Detrended Correspondence Analysis (DCA), while multiple machine learning algorithms were evaluated for SDM performance. A total of 3,169 mosquitoes were identified, with Cx. quinquefasciatus and Cx. vishnui as the dominant taxa. DCA revealed distinct habitat associations among vector species, with Cx. vishnui strongly associated with coastal environments, while Cx. tritaeniorhynchus, the principal JEV vector, was more frequently associated with forested habitats. SDM projections identified highly suitable habitats for Cx. tritaeniorhynchus along the western coast and northern Kudat, while the predicted distribution of Cx. quinquefasciatus closely overlapped with densely populated urban and peri-urban areas in western Sabah. These findings demonstrate substantial spatial heterogeneity in Culex vector distribution across Sabah and highlight ecological hotspots where intensified vector surveillance, targeted control measures, and JE prevention strategies should be prioritized.

items.title: Co-metabolic removal of perfluorooctanoic acid and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid by marine diatom Chaetoceros calcitrans MZB-1 using positively-charged organic compounds and common carbon sources.
items.abstract: While microalgae can degrade emerging pollutants, the removal of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) remains limited, which can be effectively improved via co-metabolism. The impacts of six common carbon sources and three positively-charged organic compounds on the removal of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) by marine diatom Chaetoceros calcitrans MZB-1 were studied, focusing on the potential biological mechanism underlying the co-metabolism. Among the common carbon sources, sodium succinate (200 mg/L) was suitable for enhancing removal of PFOA, while glycine (500 mg/L) was beneficial for the better removal of PFOS, with removal efficiencies increasing to 38.16% and 37.56%, respectively. This stimulation was accompanied by an induction of key degrading enzymes, i.e. cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP450) for PFOA and taurine dioxygenase (TauD) for PFOS in microalgae. Among the three positively-charged organic compounds, lysine (Lys, 100 mg/L) and arginine (Arg, 200 mg/L) were beneficial for the elimination of PFOA and PFOS, respectively, with corresponding removal efficiencies of 39.24% and 42.78%. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and zeta potential measurement indicated that the binding of NH 3 + group in Arg and Lys to the COO - group on the algal surface led to a decrease in surface negative charge, thereby enhancing the biosorption of PFOA and PFOS. Meanwhile, amino acids accelerated the growth of the alga and the secretion of extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) including polysaccharides and proteins, which were beneficial for biosorption and biodegradation. To our knowledge, this is the first study using positively-charged organic compounds as cometabolic substrates to enhance PFASs removal.

items.title: Bridging medical and ecological microbiology: The case of the pathogen.
items.abstract: Microbes and microbiomes (e.g., microbial communities) are studied both in medicine and microbial ecology. Each field studies microbes for a different purpose, also using different methods and research questions. This paper examines the way pathogen as a concept is studied and re-conceptualized when the research question centers on microbial interactions. Based on Helen Longino's Critical Contextual Empiricism and Elizabeth Lloyd's Logic of Research Question, I elaborate on the role and possibilities of re-conceptualizing the pathogen in microbiome and microbiology studies. I analyze the conceptualization of pathogen as the object of study looking at two studies from lab in microbial ecology and microbiome in medicine: the Segev lab studies microbial interactions in the oceanic phycosphere, and the Geva-Zatorsky labthat studies microbial-host interactions and their effect on the host's physiological condition., Both labs studying microbial interactions, but within different systems. I discuss the logic of research question, linked with the cognitive goals and set of epistemic and non-epistemic values involved in these fields. Medicine looks at microbial causality within the host organism, and ecology looks at the microbial role in the biogeochemical cycle. Examining these differences, I discuss the importance of the conceptual and methodological bridges between these disciplinary fields and suggest possible directions. Particularly, it provides a useful framework for ecological studies of microbial pathogenicity in medicine.

items.title: Respiration-Humidity-Gated β-Ionone Release From an Edible Cyclodextrin Metal-Organic Framework Primes Host Defense.
items.abstract: Biologically generated microenvironmental changes offer an opportunity to couple material activation directly to host physiology. Here, we construct a host-responsive volatile-delivery interface by loading β-ionone into an edible γ-cyclodextrin metal-organic framework (γ-CD-MOF). Directional K + ···O═C ion-dipole interactions stabilize β-ionone within the framework, increasing its thermal-release onset to 163°C (ΔT ≈ 99°C relative to free β-ionone) and suppressing premature loss under dry conditions. Hydration competitively disrupts these interactions, producing a gated release response above approximately 60% relative humidity. In non-vented packaging, respiration of the high-respiration model fruit Rubus idaeus increases relative humidity from ∼55% to 93%-96%, thereby driving material activation within the β-ionone release window. Molecular dynamics simulations support this mechanism, showing loss of the anhydrous K + ···O = C coordination feature upon hydration as water competitively displaces β-ionone. The released β-ionone acts predominantly as an airborne elicitor rather than a direct fungicide under the tested conditions, activating phenylpropanoid-associated defense, accelerating cell-wall lignification, and sustaining redox homeostasis, which collectively reduces decay by >70% over seven days. Together, these results establish a host-responsive material interface that translates respiration-derived humidity into gated β-ionone release, thereby coupling material activation to downstream host-defense responses.

items.title: Arctic forcing of European spring productivity and agricultural yields linked to Barents Sea ice loss.
items.abstract: Arctic sea ice loss reshapes midlatitude climate, yet its cascading impacts on terrestrial carbon cycling and food security remain unclear. Barents Sea ice area (BSIA) has experienced the Arctic's fastest decline. Using four decades of satellite observations, agricultural statistics, and Earth system model (ESM) simulations, we identify late-winter BSIA as a key driver of European spring productivity. Interannual BSIA reductions substantially enhance gross primary productivity (GPP) and raise national wheat yields by up to 16.5% in Eastern Europe, a global breadbasket. Reanalysis and model experiments reveal that reduced BSIA alters large-scale circulation through stratosphere-troposphere coupling, wave-mean flow interactions, and Rossby wave propagation. Anomalous subsidence drives adiabatic and radiative warming; cyclonic flow strengthens warm-air advection, together alleviating thermal constraints on photosynthesis. Although most ESMs capture atmospheric teleconnections, they systematically underestimate productivity responses due to underrepresented GPP-temperature sensitivity. BSIA decline accounts for approximately half of the four-decade increase in Eastern European productivity, highlighting an overlooked Arctic forcing of midlatitude carbon dynamics.

items.title: Systematic clustering alignment and feature characterization for single-cell omics using ACE-OF-Clust.
items.abstract: Clustering is widely used to identify cell types in cellular-resolution transcriptomic data, including single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST). Mixed-membership clustering assigns fractional memberships across clusters and captures continuous variation beyond hard clustering, but integrating and interpreting results from either approach is complicated by the "clustering alignment problem," which arises from label switching, multi-modality, and differences in model settings (including differing numbers of clusters). We introduce ACE-OF-Clust, enabling a four-step workflow for single-cell clustering: multiple clustering, clustering alignment, model comparison, and identification of informative features. ACE-OF-Clust introduces direct comparison of clustering solutions, assesses consistency against annotations, and leverages feature-level clustering profiles to prioritize genes discriminating among cell types, as well as to evaluate how gene sets contribute to clustering patterns. We demonstrate its utility using PBMC scRNA-seq data, breast cancer and mouse embryo ST data, and single-cell multi-omic data. ACE-OF-Clust quantifies cross-omic clustering variability and suggests putative cross-omic regulatory links. Overall, ACE-OF-Clust increases the interpretability, flexibility, and robustness of single-cell clustering, providing a scalable tool for studying cellular heterogeneity and gene expression dynamics.

items.title: Seven novel short read genomes of placozoans.
items.abstract: To explore ancestry and genomic flux in the phylum Placozoa we have generated the most comprehensive and diverse set of placozoan genomes to date. Existing placozoan genomes from the databases and seven new short read genomes, including that of Polyplacotoma mediterranea (Class Polyplacotomia), which is sister to all other extant placozoans (Class Uniplacotomia), are included in this study. All but one of the novel genomes have BUSCO values above 90%. The genome of Polyplacotoma mediterranea is the smallest of all placozoan genomes known to date (75 Mb). Intron size, together with a lower number of genes, is suspected to be one cause of this genome size disparity as Polyplacotoma introns are significantly smaller than introns in other members of the phylum. An analysis of synteny indicates several chromosomal inversion events among the members of the phylum.

items.title: Spatially constrained clustering of urban morphology for solar and wind performance assessment: The case of Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
items.abstract: Addis Ababa, a rapidly growing city in sub-Saharan Africa, is characterized by spontaneous and unplanned urban development, making it challenging to derive simplified spatial models for sustainable urban analysis. This study examines urban morphological clusters based on building height and footprint characteristics and investigates their relationships with solar and wind performance indicators. The methodology comprised four analytical stages. First, spatially constrained hierarchical clustering was performed in GeoDa to classify urban morphology using relevant building variables, resulting in 31 morphological clusters across 861 boundary units. Second, a statistically and spatially robust sampling procedure identified 92 representative samples. Third, solar and wind performance indicators were computed. Fourth, the performance indicators were validated using Grasshopper-Rhino with Ladybug for solar performance and ANSYS Fluent for wind performance. Regression analysis was subsequently conducted to evaluate statistically significant relationships among morphological and performance indicators. For solar performance, ground space index and façade-to-site ratio exhibited negative relationships with façade solar irradiation, whereas sky view factor showed a positive relationship. For wind performance, displacement height was negatively associated with block-scale wind performance. A positive relationship was also identified between façade solar irradiation and wind velocity magnitude. The proposed approach provides a systematic means of extracting meaningful relationships between urban morphology and environmental performance in cities lacking well-defined spatial models, thereby supporting evidence-based sustainable urban development.

items.title: A protocol study for a systematic review and Bayesian hierarchical meta-analysis of global epidemiology and spatial distribution of toxoplasmosis in sheep.
items.abstract: Background Toxoplasma gondii is a globally distributed zoonotic parasite that poses significant public health risks through infected sheep and their products. This protocol aims to estimate the global apparent and diagnostic-accuracy-adjusted true seroprevalence of T. gondii in sheep and investigate its spatial distribution using Bayesian hierarchical meta-analysis, meta-regression, and geographic information systems (GIS). Methods Following PRISMA-P guidelines, PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar will be searched from inception to 31 December 2026 without language restrictions. Eligible cross-sectional studies will be independently screened, and data will be extracted and assessed for risk of bias using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Apparent prevalence will be estimated through conventional meta-analysis, while Bayesian hierarchical models will estimate true prevalence and evaluate epidemiological covariates, accounting for diagnostic sensitivity and specificity. True prevalence estimation will be restricted to studies with suitable diagnostic validation evidence, and prior sensitivity analyses will assess the robustness of estimates. GIS and Bayesian binomial geostatistical modeling will be used to investigate spatial variation in seroprevalence and associated environmental factors while accounting for spatial autocorrelation and uncertainty. Discussion This review will provide global estimates of apparent seroprevalence and, where adequate validation evidence exists, diagnostic-accuracy-adjusted true seroprevalence of T. gondii in sheep. Integrating Bayesian hierarchical and geostatistical approaches may improve understanding of epidemiological and geographic patterns and support evidence-informed veterinary and public health interventions. Systematic review registration PROSPERO registration number: CRD42020205941.

items.title: Risk-weighted import dependence reveals uneven supply exposure across U.S. seafood species.
items.abstract: The U.S. seafood system is often described as highly import-dependent, but aggregate import statistics obscure which seafood groups have the greatest structural supply exposure and why. We developed a species-specific U.S. Seafood Dependency Risk Index (U.S.-SDRI) to characterize structural exposure to potential supply disruptions across 22 core seafood groups from 2009 to 2023 by integrating foreign trade, domestic production, and country-level vulnerability and readiness data. The index combined export-adjusted import dependence, supplier concentration, and exporter risk. Dependency risk varied substantially across species groups. Tilapia had the highest mean risk score (0.68), followed by lobster, tuna, trout, clams, shrimp, squid/octopus, and snapper/grouper. Component profiles showed that exposure contributors differed across seafood groups: U.S. tilapia supply combined complete import dependence with moderate supplier concentration and exporter risk; lobster combined import dependence with high supplier concentration; and tuna and shrimp combined high import dependence with higher exporter risk. Self-reliance and U.S.-SDRI rankings differed for 16 of 22 groups, indicating that adding supplier concentration and exporter risk changed the relative ordering of most species groups. A source-country profile and an illustrative sourcing-reallocation scenario showed how differences and assumed changes in supplier structure can affect measured exposure under the framework. The framework therefore provides a screening tool for species-specific monitoring, preparedness, and risk-informed seafood planning in the U.S.

items.title: Strategic coexistence theory for evolutionary games.
items.abstract: Evolutionary game theory and ecological coexistence theory both seek to predict the outcome of competition between biological entities, be they strategies or species, but the two fields have relied on largely separate approaches. Replicator equations provide a foundation for predicting the outcome of strategic competition, but comparing how different mechanisms alter competition across games remains challenging. Inspired by modern coexistence theory from community ecology, we develop Strategic Coexistence Theory (SCT), which translates payoff-based invasion conditions at monomorphic boundary conditions into strategic niche differences and fitness differences between any two competing strategies described by classic replicator dynamics. We show that SCT recovers the classic classification of two-strategy games and also allows us to compare mechanisms for the evolution of cooperation within a shared niche-fitness difference space. In stochastic games, environmental stochasticity increases both boundary invasion growth rates, whereas in multiplayer public-goods games, nonlinear benefits can either stabilize or destabilize competition. These applications also show that the number or stability of internal equilibria generally cannot be predicted from invasion growth rates at monomorphic boundaries, illustrating a key limitation of characterizing competitive systems using boundary invasion rates alone. Together, these results show that SCT provides a coexistence-theoretic perspective for characterizing how different mechanisms alter strategy competition across games.

items.title: The mapping of Indonesian skin type based on the Baumann Skin Type Indicator - Indonesia (BSTI - Ina) 2022: A multicenter study.
items.abstract: Choosing appropriate skincare agents according to skin type remains a challenge in dermatology. The Baumann Skin Type Indicator (BSTI) classifies skin into 16 types based on four parameters, and its 2022 simplified version has been translated, adapted, and validated for Indonesian adults as the BSTI-Ina 2022. This study is the first to use BSTI-Ina 2022 to describe the distribution of skin types and associated sociodemographic characteristics in the Indonesian population. To date, no gold standard for skin-type determination exists in Indonesia. Our study is the first multicenter study in Indonesia to map the distribution of skin types among the Indonesian population using the previously validated Baumann Skin Type Indicator-Indonesia (BSTI-Ina) 2022, which can assist in determining skin types among Indonesians. This multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted in 13 dermatology and venereology residency institutes throughout Indonesia. Inclusion criteria are individuals aged 18-59 years with type III-V Fitzpatrick skin type who are willing to complete the BSTI-Ina 2022 questionnaire. Data were analyzed to calculate skin type distribution using BSTI-Ina 2022, which was categorized by sex, age, and geographical area. Among 1950 participants, the most common BSTI skin type was Oily, Sensitive, Pigmented, Wrinkled (OSPW) (22.2%). Based on sex, the distribution of BSTI skin types differed significantly between males and females (p value = 0.001), with OSNW being the most common type among males (24.4%) and DSPW being the most common type among females (24.0%). Based on geographical area represented by an island, OSPW is most common in Sumatra (22.2%), Java (22.2%), Sulawesi (19.0%), and Bali (28.7%) (p value < 0.01). Based on age represented by Glogau scale, OSPW was the most prevalent in the Glogau I (22.4%) and Glogau II (23.10%) groups, while Dry, Resistant, Pigmented, Wrinkled (DRPW) was the most prevalent (18.5%) in the Glogau III group. Overall, the most dominant skin categories were oily (57.8%), sensitive (67.5%), pigmented (61.4%), and wrinkle-prone (87.3%). The most common skin type in Indonesia is OSPW. This finding supports the development of more personalized skin care that is suitable for Indonesian skin.

items.title: ESG reporting perceptions from lecturer perspectives: The case of Vietnamese Universities.
items.abstract: Higher education institutions play a key role in developing Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) expertise and knowledge. Lecturers are central to translating ESG strategies into educational and organizational outcomes, yet their perceptions of ESG reporting remain under-explored in Vietnam. This study examines individual and institutional factors associated with lecturers' perceptions of ESG reporting, drawing on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), Institutional Theory, Stakeholder Theory, and Diffusion of Innovations (DOI) theory. Survey data from 437 eligible university lecturers in Vietnam were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Results show significant positive associations for innovation policies, sustainability action programs, social pressure, attitude, perceived usefulness, and knowledge, while subjective norm and leadership show no significant direct associations. Academic specialization, included as a control variable, is also positively associated with Lecturers' perceptions of ESG reporting. Institutional ESG publication significantly negatively associated, suggesting that formal disclosure does not necessarily correspond to favorable individual perceptions, although the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Innovation policies significantly moderate the relationship between subjective norm and lecturers' perceptions of ESG reporting, while other tested moderating effects are not statistically significant. Overall, the findings highlight the interplay between individual evaluations and institutional conditions in understanding lecturers' perceptions of ESG reporting in Vietnamese higher education.

items.title: Plasma metabolic signature in the association between air pollution and cataract risk: A longitudinal cohort study.
items.abstract: Air pollution exposure has been reported to be associated with cataract risk; however, the underlying mechanism in this relationship remains unclear. We included 199,528 cataract-free participants from the UK Biobank prospective cohort study. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate associations of air pollution with cataract risk. Elastic net regression was utilized to identify each air pollutant-related metabolic signatures, and mediation analysis were performed to evaluate mediation effect. Results showed that higher exposure to PM2.5 (adjusted hazard ratios [HR] for each quantile increase: 1.05; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.03-1.06; FDR-adjusted P < 0.001), NO2 (adjusted HR: 1.02; 95%CI: 1.01-1.04; FDR-adjusted P = 0.008), and NOx (adjusted HR: 1.03; 95%CI: 1.01-1.04; FDR-adjusted P < 0.001) was significantly associated with an elevated cataract risk, whereas PM10 and PMcoarse showing no significant difference. We identified metabolic signatures comprising 35 metabolites for PM2.5, 28 for NO2, and 13 for NOx. Metabolic signatures were associated with incident cataract, with HRs of 1.06 (95% CI: 1.04-1.08) per standard deviation (SD) increment in the PM2.5-related metabolic signature, 1.05 (95% CI: 1.03-1.07) for the NO2-related metabolic signature, and 1.04 (95% CI: 1.03-1.06) for the NOx-related metabolic signature, respectively. Mediation analysis showed that metabolic signatures significantly mediated 4.03%, 6.58%, and 2.22% of the effects of PM2.5, NO2, and NOx on cataract risk, respectively, and certain metabolites, such as lactate and albumin, showing partial mediation of this association. Our findings underscore that air pollution exposure is associated with a higher risk of cataract, with metabolic signatures partially mediating this association.

items.title: Protocol to identify and date ancient whole-genome duplications using K<sub>S</sub> age distributions and molecular clock estimates.
items.abstract: Ancient polyploidy, the result of whole-genome duplication (WGD), has occurred repeatedly throughout the tree of life, yet the inference of ancient WGDs remains a challenging task. Here, we present a computational protocol for the inference of ancient WGDs using K S age distributions and molecular clock estimates. We describe steps to search for the remnants of ancient WGDs and the ensuing identification and dating in an evolutionary time frame. This protocol is suitable for WGD investigation of newly generated genome data. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Chen et al. 1 .

items.title: Three novel Pseudanabaena species (Pseudanabaenales, Cyanobacteriophyta) from frozen glacial and post-glacial lakes in polar regions: Cryotolerance as a potential mechanism for long-term survival of freeze-thaw adapted types.
items.abstract: Frozen Pseudanabaena-dominated phytobenthic mats were collected from four ecologically similar, shallow, low-conductivity glacial and post-glacial early Holocene lakes in the Arctic and Antarctica. Four isolated strains were subsequently analyzed using a polyphasic approach (morphology, ultrastructure, 16S rRNA gene phylogeny, ITS rRNA region analyses), resulting in the description of three novel Pseudanabaena species (P. gelidogaleata, P. lacugelata, and P. prelichiana). Field observations, complemented with controlled in vitro experiments, confirmed the ability of the new species to withstand freeze-thaw treatments, irrespective of the cryogenic intensity (-20, -80, -196°C). Despite their similar cryoresistance, all species displayed unique phenotypic features-such as cell-shape plasticity with polymorphic "behavior" (within-trichome transitions in morphology), variable constrictions across a range of intensities (including some rare constriction patterns), and different types of swollen/involution cells. These findings, along with ultrastructural observations, blur traditional taxonomic boundaries between Pseudanabaena and related genera. Molecular clock analyses confirmed four diversification lineages within Pseudanabaena and revealed that the three new species represent ancient lineages predating their current habitats, with evolutionary origins dating back to the Mesozoic and Eocene epochs. Overall, the results propose a potential mechanism of long-term survival of Pseudanabaena, probably facilitated by cryopreservation within frozen lakes. Comprehensive molecular analyses strongly suggested a common ancestor between the Arctic P. gelidogaleata and several psychrotolerant strains isolated from Antarctica. This finding may further support the hypothesis of a more global distribution of cold-adapted ecotypes. The study provides new insights into the complex ecology, biogeography, and adaptability of Pseudanabaena cryotypes under extreme conditions.

items.title: Association between anthropogenic food consumption, physiological stress, and anxiety-related behaviors in wild Barbary macaques (Macaca sylvanus) within a tourist context in Algeria.
items.abstract: Wildlife tourism involving primates has increasingly been promoted as a sustainable strategy for conservation and local development. However, its impact on animal welfare, particularly stress and anxiety, is still poorly documented in wild settings. This study investigated whether anthropogenic food consumption was associated with physiological stress and anxiety-related behaviors in wild Barbary macaques (Macaca sylvanus) exposed to tourism activities in Gouraya National Park, Algeria. Eighteen adult individuals from two habituated groups were observed from June 2021 to January 2022. A total of 107 fecal samples were collected to quantify fecal cortisol metabolites (FCMs) as a measure of physiological stress. In parallel, behavioral observations were conducted to assess anxiety-related behaviors, including self-directed behaviors. Higher anthropogenic food consumption was associated with higher FCM concentrations, increased self-directed behaviors, and higher scratching rates. Seasonal patterns were also observed: FCM tended to be higher during the rainy season, whereas scratching rates increased significantly during warmer and drier periods. These temporal discrepancies between physiological and behavioral markers underscore the importance of interpreting stress responses within both ecological and social contexts. Overall, these findings highlight the potential welfare costs of unregulated wildlife tourism and support the implementation of integrated management strategies that consider both, conservation objectives and animal welfare.

items.title: Effect of compost co‑applied with kaolinite and iron oxide on the physico-chemical and biochemical properties of abandoned mine tailings.
items.abstract: Mine tailings (MTs) are usually accumulated in large surfaces disturbing natural ecosystems. Application of organic amendments (OAs) has been considered for managing these wastes; however, some OAs can mobilize metal(loid)s due to their labile carbon fractions. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of compost with kaolinite (Ka) and iron oxide (Fe) on physico-chemical and biochemical properties of an abandoned MT. A composite sample of MT was taken. A commercial compost, Ka and Fe were used to establish the experiment. A full randomized design was performed as follows: 1) MT; 2) MT + Compost; 3) MT + Compost + Ka; 4) MT + Compost + Fe; 5) MT + Compost + Ka + Fe. Inorganic additives were added to compost at 2% w/w and treatments comprised the addition of 20% v/v of the amendment to MT in pots (0.5 L). The addition of compost alone and with inorganic additives increased the pH (up to up to 2.7 units), total organic carbon (up to 4.5 times), water holding capacity (WHC; up to 98%), and nutrient contents of MTs. Also, the available Cu contents decreased up to 57%, while available As increased from 0.12 to 1.66-3.85 mg As kg -1 by the addition of OAs, as well as the enzyme activities and the catabolic capacity of microbial communities. Thus, the incorporation of OAs improved conditions for the rehabilitation of MTs, primarily through increased pH, WHC, carbon and nutrient content, and reduced Cu availability, which increased microbial activity associated to biogeochemical cycling. Future research should focus on long-term monitoring of metal(loid) dynamics and plant uptake to ensure the sustainability of these remediation approaches in mine site restoration programs.

items.title: Shigella's c-di-GMP-specific phosphodiesterases modulate biofilm and virulence phenotypes.
items.abstract: To establish infection and cause disease, the intracellular pathogen Shigella must successfully navigate a series of host defenses and distinct microenvironments within the human body. One way Shigella navigates these environments is by using the secondary messenger c-di-GMP, which regulates many different bacterial behaviors. C-di-GMP is synthesized by diguanylate cyclases and broken down by c-di-GMP-specific phosphodiesterases (PDEs). In this study, we investigated how Shigella flexneri 's c-di-GMP-specific PDEs impact c-di-GMP turnover and subsequently biofilm and virulence phenotypes. We knocked out each of S. flexneri 's six c-di-GMP-specific PDEs to determine how these PDEs impact biofilm, virulence, and c-di-GMP levels within the bacterial cell. We found that these PDEs negatively regulate c-di-GMP levels while modulating S. flexneri 's virulence and biofilm behavior. We also noted that altering the expression of these S. flexneri PDEs changes bacterial cell size. Transcriptome analysis revealed that a S. flexneri Δ pdeB strain differentially expresses many genes, including increased expression of virulence genes ipgD and ipgE, and reduced expression of genes associated with lipid metabolism. We confirmed that a S. flexneri Δ pdeB strain has reduced levels of C19 fatty acid methyl ester. This study highlights the complexities of c-di-GMP signaling in regulating numerous Shigella pathways.IMPORTANCE Shigella , an intracellular human pathogen and the causative agent of dysentery, infects hundreds of millions of people worldwide each year. The rapid rise of antibiotic-resistant Shigella strains underscores the urgent need to better understand its physiology and identify new therapeutic targets. In this study, we investigated how Shigella c-di-GMP-specific phosphodiesterases regulate c-di-GMP levels and associated bacterial phenotypes. We found that altering the expression of enzymes involved in c-di-GMP degradation significantly impacts Shigella biofilm formation, host cell invasion, and the composition of the bacterial cell membrane.

items.title: Ecological Feedback Dimensionality and Trade-Off Shape Govern Cancer Phenotypic Diversification
items.abstract: Cancer cells face a variety of trade-offs in their microenvironment, from competition vs. colonization to immune evasion vs. rapid proliferation. Whether such trade-offs drive cancer cell populations to a single optimal phenotype or to a stable coexistence of phenotypes depends on the trade-off's shape and the number of independent ecological feedbacks that cells impose on each other and on their environment. We introduce trade-off and invasion plots (TIPs), a geometric tool from adaptive dynamics that determines the evolutionary outcome from the curvature of a trade-off relative to a pair of invasion boundaries, to cancer and ground our analysis in simple consumer-resource metabolic models. We show that the dimension of the ecological feedback determines whether diversification can occur: a one-dimensional feedback leads to monomorphism, whereas a two-dimensional feedback can promote evolutionary branching to a stable dimorphism. Furthermore, we show that the curvature of the allocation trade-off governs whether a single metabolic generalist (attractor), a stable dimorphism of specialists (evolutionary branching), or a single specialist (repellor) occurs. Both results are cancer-specific instances of long-established principles in theoretical ecology, namely the bound that the dimension of the feedback environment places on coexistence, and the fitness-set geometry relating trade-off curvature to specialization. Our contribution therefore primarily lies in bringing this mature eco-evolutionary machinery to bear on intratumoral heterogeneity.

items.title: A microbiota-dependent fitness locus promotes intraspecies competition and cell envelope resilience in gut bacterium Phocaeicola vulgatus
items.abstract: A central question in gut microbial ecology is how dominant bacterial species establish and occupy their niches amid inter- and intraspecies competition. Phocaeicola vulgatus (Pvu) is a Gram-negative anaerobe and prevalent member of the human gut microbiome that can integrate into established gut communities without antibiotic pretreatment, yet mechanisms underlying this competitive success remain poorly understood. Using in vivo transposon insertion sequencing, we identified a three-gene locus that promotes Pvu intraspecies fitness in the presence of a complex microbiota but is dispensable in germ-free hosts. The locus encodes a predicted HU/IHF superfamily histone-like DNA-binding protein (DifH), a hypothetical lipid-binding protein (DifS), and a FadL-like outer-membrane transporter (DifT). In vitro genetic and transcriptomic analyses implicated these genes in cell envelope resilience. Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing revealed that DifH binds a specific repetitive DNA motif at its own locus and a limited set of additional loci involved in metabolism, envelope biogenesis, and cellular defense. Together, these findings identify a previously unrecognized fitness locus that promotes cell envelope resilience, enables intraspecies competition, and supports Pvu persistence within complex gut microbial communities. More broadly, these results uncover mechanisms by which this dominant gut commensal secures its niche and suggests avenues to therapeutically modulate gut microbiota composition.

items.title: Diverse ecological pressures govern microbial heterogeneity across dark ocean ecosystems
items.abstract: The deep ocean regulates Earth's biogeochemical cycles, yet accelerating warming, deoxygenation, and biodiversity loss threaten to fundamentally disrupt these processes. Despite microorganisms' central role in global elemental cycling, deep-sea microbial communities remain poorly characterized, limiting our capacity to predict ecosystem responses to ongoing environmental perturbation. Although ocean circulation connects marine ecosystems across vast distances in the absence of physical barriers, secondary factors including depth, redox chemistry, and substrate availability create distinct microbial habitats. A key unresolved question is how these ecological pressures differentially shape microbial community structure beyond dispersal alone. Here, we examine the microbial ecology of two biogeochemically distinct yet spatially connected marine habitats at the East Pacific Rise (EPR) spreading center in the Pacific Ocean: deep-sea hydrothermal plumes and oxygen minimum zones. Using serial filtration coupled with community metagenomics, we reconstruct >700 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) and perform comprehensive taxonomic, metabolic, and abundance profiling across both systems. We reveal pronounced community differentiation driven by redox chemistry, as well as under appreciated ecological pressures that exert strong and previously overlooked structuring influence on these communities. Our findings establish that deep-ocean microbial ecology is governed by a complex hierarchy of environmental forces extending well beyond physical dispersal, with direct implications for forecasting microbial responses to accelerating ocean deoxygenation and climate change.

items.title: Modeling skin cancer in vitro: From 2-dimensional monolayers to sophisticated 3-dimensional organotypic models.
items.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) in vitro skin cancer models have become an essential basis for studying the complex pathophysiology of skin cancers and therefore provide a useful platform for the development of alternative, tailored therapeutic approaches. Compared with 2-dimensional cell culture systems, 3D models have emerged as more physiologically relevant systems because they precisely recapitulate the tissue architecture, tumor-microenvironmental interactions, and processes such as immune cell infiltration. This review discusses the advances and limitations of currently available in vitro models representing cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, malignant melanoma, and Merkel cell carcinoma, pointing out future directions to improve translational relevance.

items.title: Male chickadees with better spatial cognition sire more extra-pair young.
items.abstract: Across animal taxa, females commonly mate with more than one male, even in monogamous mating systems. These extra-pair copulations and resulting young may increase the fitness of the female via a variety of mechanisms. The 'good genes' hypothesis suggests that socially monogamous females mate outside their pair bond to increase the fitness of their offspring via indirect genetic benefits, because extra-pair males do not provide parental care. We tested this hypothesis by quantifying extra-pair paternity in nonmigratory, food-caching mountain chickadees ( Poecile gambeli ). Chickadees rely on spatial cognition to recover scattered food caches, and variation in spatial cognition is associated with increased survival, longer lifespan, and is heritable. However, less is known about the role of sexual selection on spatial cognitive abilities. In the current study, we found that (1) males with better spatial cognitive abilities sired more extra-pair young and produced heavier offspring in their own nests compared to their poorer-performing counterparts, and (2) extra-pair males had significantly better spatial cognition than the social males they cuckolded. These results suggest that sexual selection shapes the evolution of spatial cognition in food-caching chickadees and are consistent with the good genes hypothesis, which posits that females gain indirect genetic benefits via extra-pair young.

items.title: Social work informatics: an equity framework for health informatics.
items.abstract: Objectives Social work informatics (SWI) was proposed as a professional specialty in 2006, yet social work remains under-represented in health informatics governance, research, and system design even as artificial intelligence (AI) shapes high-stakes clinical decisions. This paper introduces the SWI Equity Framework, positioning social work as a leader in designing equitable health informatics systems. Materials and methods The framework was developed through a synthesis of social work, health informatics, and health equity literature. Results The framework identifies 6 domains: reflexive system co-design, social determinants of health data integration, training-data quality and representation, contextual interpretation of AI outputs, community leadership, and equitable accountability. Discussion The framework highlights opportunities to integrate social work expertise throughout the health informatics lifecycle, moving beyond consultation toward active participation in system design, implementation, and governance. It also outlines pathways for advancing social work informatics through education, interdisciplinary research, health systems, and professional infrastructure. Conclusion Social work is particularly well positioned to advance the equity agenda of health informatics and offers profession-specific expertise that can strengthen equity, accountability, and implementation across the informatics lifecycle.

items.title: Spatial Synchronization and Determinants of Multidimensional Biodiversity and Endemism Across Multiple Taxa in China.
items.abstract: Understanding the spatial alignment of multidimensional biodiversity across taxonomic groups is a central challenge for conservation. It remains unclear whether the spatial synchronization of taxonomic, genetic, and phylogenetic diversity, alongside their respective endemism patterns, exhibits a unified spatial structure across terrestrial taxa in China. Here, we presented a national-scale assessment using occurrence data for 2105 terrestrial vertebrates, 15 963 vascular plants, and 28 894 insects, with phylogenetic and genetic analyses based on data-matched subsets. We revealed strong spatial coupling between vascular plants and insects, contrasting with weaker congruence in terrestrial vertebrates. Across taxa, taxonomic diversity (TD), phylogenetic diversity (PD), weighted endemism (WE), and phylogenetic endemism (PE) were generally more spatially congruent than genetic diversity (GD) and genetic endemism (GE). In widespread-species analyses, energy, water availability, and climatic seasonality were the primary determinants of TD and PD, whereas human activity showed relatively small independent contributions. Notably, several previously unrecognized complementary hotspots were identified, including the Tianmu Mountains, the Middle-Lower Yangtze Plain Mountains, the Taihangshan-Lvliangshan and Nuluerhushan-Heishan Mountain Systems, which warrant further assessment of conservation coverage. These findings indicate that vertebrate- or taxonomic-diversity-based conservation alone may not adequately protect plant and insect biodiversity, supporting multidimensional and taxon-specific conservation planning in China.

items.title: Longitudinal Associations Between Problematic Internet Use Components and Adolescents' Quality of Life.
items.abstract: Although problematic Internet use (PIU) has been increasingly associated with poorer health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in adolescents, longitudinal evidence examining the longitudinal associations between specific PIU components and HRQoL remains limited. Guided by the cognitive-behavioral model of PIU, this study investigated the longitudinal relationships between four PIU components (preference for online social interaction, mood regulation, deficient self-regulation, and negative consequences) and HRQoL across three time points. The sample comprised 2,616 Spanish adolescents. A random intercept cross-lagged panel model was employed to disentangle between-person from within-person associations between variables. At the between-person level, all PIU components were positively interrelated and negatively associated with HRQoL. At the within-person level, only deficits in self-regulation preceded subsequent increases in mood regulation. Additionally, deficits in self-regulation were the only PIU component to precede decreases in HRQoL over time. Bidirectional associations were also observed, as declines in HRQoL preceded worsening self-regulation deficits and negative consequences. These findings highlight the role of self-regulation deficits in PIU and their association with adolescent well-being, underscoring the importance of targeting self-regulation processes in prevention and intervention efforts.

items.title: Evaluation of α-pyrrolidinovalerophenone and its enantiomers in male and female Sprague-Dawley rats trained to discriminate 3,4-methylenedioxypyrovalerone.
items.abstract: Synthetic cathinones have been on the illicit drug market for almost two decades and remain a significant public health concern. Preclinical behavioral pharmacology investigations are essential to characterizing the psychoactive effects of novel substances. This study characterized the discriminative stimulus effects of α-pyrrolidinovalerophenone (α-PVP) and its enantiomers in comparison to those of 3,4-methylenedioxypyrovalerone (MDPV). Male (N = 8) and female (N = 8) Sprague-Dawley rats were trained to discriminate 0.5 mg/kg MDPV from saline under a fixed ratio 20 schedule of food reinforcement, and substitution tests were conducted with MDPV (0.05-0.5 mg/kg), racemic α-PVP (RS-α-PVP) (0.05-0.5 mg/kg), (S)-α-PVP (0.05-1 mg/kg) and (R)-α-PVP (0.05-10 mg/kg). All three substances produced a dose-dependent increase in MDPV-lever responses. Full substitution was observed in females at the highest dose of all three test compounds, and all except (R)-α-PVP substituted fully in males. These results illustrate that α-PVP, and its enantiomers produce similar discriminative stimulus effects to those of MDPV with few differences between males and females. Although the current findings add to the existing behavioral pharmacology of α-PVP, further investigations into its precise mechanisms of action are critical to advancing medical treatments for substance abuse disorders involving this and related synthetic cathinones.

items.title: Examining gambling problems through the lens of outcome expectancies and maladaptive personality traits: direct associations and interactions.
items.abstract: Background Gambling outcome expectancies are the beliefs a person holds about the effects of gambling. These can influence gambling behaviour directly and in combination with individual and situational factors. A particularly important set of individual factors are maladaptive personality traits. However, few studies have examined how gambling outcome expectancies interact with maladaptive personality traits in relation to gambling problems and recent gambling symptoms. Methods The present study used a cross-sectional survey design to examine the gambling outcome expectancies of excitement, escape, ego, social, and money, alongside the five maladaptive personality traits of negative affect, disinhibition, antagonism, detachment, and psychoticism, in a large sample of active gamblers, defined as adults who had gambled for money in the past 30 days (N = 1501, 50.1% men, M age = 44.6 years). Associations with gambling problems (past 12 months) and recent gambling symptoms (past week) were assessed both individually and through interactions, using structural equation modelling. Results The results showed that escape expectancies, followed by ego enhancement expectancies, were most strongly associated with gambling problems and recent gambling symptoms. Among maladaptive personality traits, disinhibition and antagonism presented the strongest associations with gambling problems and recent gambling symptoms. Exploratory moderation analyses revealed that money expectancies were less strongly linked to gambling problems among individuals higher in psychoticism. Conclusions Our findings suggest that escape- and ego-related gambling expectancies, together with disinhibition and antagonism, are central correlates of gambling problems and recent gambling symptoms, and that their potential interplay may inform future research on assessment, prevention, and intervention for individuals with gambling-related problems or at risk of gambling-related harms.

items.title: AI-Faces by Illinois: A database of AI-generated faces depicting children.
items.abstract: Faces serve as gateways of impression formation during human interactions and are widely used as stimuli throughout psychological research. To source these stimuli, researchers often rely on established databases of photographs of adults' and children's faces or public image repositories like Google Images. Although these resources have proven valuable, there are important limitations, especially for research using images of children. This manuscript introduces a novel alternative to those databases: AI-Faces by Illinois, a database of 1152 photorealistic, AI-generated images depicting child faces that is freely available for non-commercial use (OSF link to images and norming data: https://osf.io/vurm5/ ; additional GitHub repository: https://github.com/AI-Face-By-Illinois/ai-face-by-illinois.github.io ; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/ ). These images vary systematically by perceived age (3, 6, 10, 15 years), gender (boy, girl), race/ethnicity (Black, East Asian, Latine, Middle Eastern/North African, Native American, Pacific Islander, South Asian, White), and emotional expression (ten smiling, four angry, and four frowning images per group). Two norming studies (Study 1: N = 1261, Study 2: N = 131) revealed that adults rated the AI-generated images as equally real as the photographs of children from existing databases and perceived them in line with their prompted age, gender, race/ethnicity, and emotion. The images also elicited perceptual biases similar to those documented in research using real faces, supporting their ecological validity. This manuscript highlights the methodological advantages and new ethical considerations of using AI-generated child faces in psychological research.

items.title: Dyslexia Eye Tracking COrpus (DECO): First- and second-language book reading in adults with dyslexia.
items.abstract: Openly available eye-tracking corpora have been indispensable for the progress in psycholinguistic theories of reading. Past corpus work extensively covered typical reading in a range of languages, but left reading difficulties relatively under-documented. In this article, we present a novel corpus, the Dyslexia Eye Tracking COrpus (DECO). It includes eye-tracking data collected from 20 Dutch-English bilingual adults in higher education with a diagnosis of developmental dyslexia. They read an entire novel (almost 60,000 words), with one half presented in their first language (Dutch) and the other half in their second language (English). After each chapter the participants answered multiple reading comprehension questions. Additionally, all participants completed several measures of linguistic abilities, including vocabulary, spelling, a 1-min reading test, and a language questionnaire. This corpus is the largest of its kind and is a direct extension of the existing Ghent Eye-Tracking Corpus (GECO) of typical reading. In combination with GECO, it provides researchers with a unique resource for studying naturalistic reading in dyslexia and its intersection with bilingualism. All data and materials are available on GitHub: https://github.com/SamBoeve/Dyslexia-Eyetracking-COrpus-DECO .

items.title: Adaptive digital mathematics training in infantile hydrocephalus: behavioural outcomes following a three-month cognitive intervention.
items.abstract: Background Infantile hydrocephalus (IH) is associated with neurocognitive challenges, including mathematics difficulties. This study evaluated mathematics performance following a three-month home-based intervention using Calcularis 2.0, an adaptive computerized mathematics training program, in children with IH. Methods Eleven children with IH (mean age = 10.1 years) and 19 typically developing (TD) controls (mean age = 10.3 years) participated in a 12-week home-based intervention targeting approximately 20 minutes of training per day, 3-5 days per week. Arithmetic fluency, written calculation, and mental arithmetic were assessed before and after training. Between-group differences were evaluated using unadjusted gain-score comparisons and baseline-adjusted analyses of covariance. Results Children with IH demonstrated lower baseline performance across all mathematics measures than TD controls. Both groups showed significant pre-post improvements across mathematics outcomes (all p .001). Unadjusted analyses indicated significantly greater gains in the IH group for addition fluency (p = .005) and written calculation (p .001), which remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons. However, these differences were no longer significant after adjustment for baseline performance. Group differences were not significant for subtraction fluency, multiplication fluency, or mental arithmetic. Vocabulary and general knowledge measures did not show significant pre-post changes. Conclusions Children with IH demonstrated measurable improvements in mathematics performance over the training period. However, the absence of significant baseline-adjusted group effects and an analyzed no-intervention comparison prevents these improvements from being attributed specifically to Calcularis. Larger controlled studies are needed to establish intervention efficacy.

items.title: Fifty-five crowdsourced designs assessing carbon pricing support in the USA.
items.abstract: A carbon price is an effective and cost-efficient policy to mitigate emissions, yet low public acceptance and limited political support remain major barriers to its widespread implementation. This crowdsourced 'many-designs' project presents results from 55 behavioural interventions on real-world support for carbon pricing, independently developed by international research teams. By implementing all designs simultaneously with almost 20,000 US residents, this preregistered study shows very small positive but statistically significant effects of behavioural interventions on a set of design-specific proxies of real-world support (Cohen's d = 0.06; 99.5% confidence interval (CI) 0.001 to 0.124) and on 4 out of 5 common measures of stated support (Cohen's d values 0.06-0.08; 99.5% CIs from 0.006 to 0.112 and from 0.020 to 0.133; between 1.7 and 2.4 percentage points in increased support across outcomes), including the willingness to endorse a carbon price that internalizes the social costs of US$120 per ton of CO 2 emissions (d = 0.06; 99.5% CI 0.012 to 0.118). Furthermore, the results reveal low-to-medium between-study heterogeneity (τ = 0.07-0.12). Lastly, we identify strong overconfidence among research teams regarding the expected effects of their interventions and those of their peers, indicating a miscalibration of community expectations.

items.title: Neurotransmitter pathway-specific polygenic risk for psychiatric disorders and brain morphology in adolescents.
items.abstract: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Schizophrenia (SCZ), and Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) are highly heritable and have been linked to brain morphology. We investigated how genetic variation in neurotransmitter systems is associated with brain morphology using pathway-specific polygenic risk scores (PGS) in adolescence. We studied 8591 participants of European ancestry (ages 9-14 years; 13,551 brain images) from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development and the Generation R Study. Genome-wide PGS for ADHD, SCZ, and MDD were computed alongside pathway-specific PGSs for the glutamate, GABA, dopamine, and serotonin pathways. Vertex-wise mega-analyses of cortical surface area and thickness using linear mixed-effects random-intercept models were conducted. Genome-wide and pathway-specific PGSs for ADHD were associated with smaller cortical surface area, with spatially extensive genome-wide clusters (82,508 mm²) and more localized pathway-specific clusters (up to 10,237 mm²). For SCZ, pathway-specific PGSs were associated with significant surface-area clusters totaling 4302 mm², compared with 1129 mm² for the genome-wide PGS. The serotonin PGS for SCZ was linked to a smaller lingual gyrus (1041 mm²), while the GABA PGS was associated with a larger surface area in temporal and cingulate regions (2004 mm²). A higher genome-wide PGS for MDD was related to a smaller surface area (4936 mm²) in frontotemporal regions. Pathway-specific PGSs for MDD were associated with a smaller orbitofrontal (glutamate) and precuneus (GABA) surface area, with cluster sizes between 197-297 mm². Associations with cortical thickness were limited. These results demonstrate that partitioning genetic risk for ADHD, SCZ, and MDD into neurotransmitter-specific pathways reveals distinct cortical surface area signatures in adolescence.

items.title: Exploring enhanced self-esteem reactivity in response to social prediction errors in adolescence.
items.abstract: Self-esteem is a cornerstone of mental health across the lifespan. Throughout life, but particularly during adolescence, self-esteem is shaped by social appraisals. Previous work in adults has shown that momentary fluctuations in self-esteem are explained not only by whether we are liked by others but also by whether we are liked more or less than expected (social prediction errors). Here, we examine age-related differences in how social experiences shape self-esteem in 141 participants aged 10-40 years using an experimental social evaluation task and ecological momentary assessment. In the experiment, self-esteem reactivity to unexpected social feedback follows a non-linear age-related pattern, peaking in late adolescence. In daily life, self-esteem reactivity to perceived pleasantness of social interaction and naturalistic social prediction errors is stronger in younger participants. Individual differences in experimental and daily-life self-esteem reactivity are associated, highlighting heightened self-esteem malleability during adolescence.

items.title: Environmental factors associated with sleep health in middle-aged and older adults: Findings from the Canadian longitudinal study on aging.
items.abstract: Objectives This study aimed to investigate the association between environmental factors and dimensions of sleep health among middle-aged and older adults in Canada, including sleep satisfaction, sleep latency, and sleep duration. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study using data from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging Comprehensive Cohort (n=30,097), linked with environmental exposure data from the Canadian Urban Environmental Health Research Consortium. Binary sleep outcomes were analyzed using modified Poisson regression, whereas continuous sleep outcomes were analyzed using linear regression. Models assessed associations with environmental factors (green space, air pollution, noise, physical and social environments), adjusting for demographic, behavioral, and health-related covariates. Results Greater Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) was consistently associated with better sleep health, including lower risk of prolonged sleep latency and longer sleep duration. Higher intersection density was associated with sleep dissatisfaction and shorter sleep duration. Air pollution showed mixed results; higher NO₂ was associated with lower risk of prolonged sleep latency in both models, whereas ozone showed protective associations in domain-specific models. Higher relative humidity was associated with shorter sleep duration, as was nighttime light in domain-specific models. Conclusions Environmental exposures may play a meaningful role in shaping sleep health among middle-aged and older adults in Canada. Urban greening and reductions in light and noise pollution may be promising strategies to improve sleep. However, associations with air pollution were inconsistent and warrant further investigation. These findings underscore the multifaceted environmental determinants of sleep health and the potential for targeted public health and urban planning interventions.

items.title: Social Influence in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Preference for Humans Does Not Deter Artificial Intelligence Influence.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming a source of social influence. But people often prefer human over AI sources (algorithm aversion/preference for humans), which might prevent AI from influencing humans. However, we outline a theoretical framework that suggests that preferences do not play a causal role in influence. To test this framework, we investigated under which conditions preferences predict AI influence. Participants ( N = 1,254) indicated their adviser preference and then made incentivised decisions while receiving advice from AI or human advisers. Participants preferred human over AI advisers but were influenced by AI and humans similarly. A strong aversion to AI advisers had no (Study 1) or a trivial relation (Study 2 and 3) with AI influence, which was explained by confounding variables. When manipulated, preferences did not predict advice-taking, but adviser trustworthiness and competence did (Study 3). Our results suggest that for predicting AI influence, understanding domain-specific social cognitions, not preferences, is critical.

items.title: Neural-transcriptomic responses to social stress in adolescent females: testing the social signal transduction theory of depression.
items.abstract: Although social stressors strongly predict major depressive disorder (MDD), the biological mechanisms that transduce experiences of social stress into depression pathogenesis remain unclear, especially among adolescents. The Social Signal Transduction Theory of Depression hypothesizes that neural sensitivity to social stressors alters immune responses and, thus, risk for depression, but few studies have tested this hypothesis. To investigate, we comprehensively characterized neural and transcriptomic responses to an fMRI-based social evaluation stressor in 44 psychiatrically healthy adolescent females (M Age = 14.79, SD = 1.23). Longitudinal analyses examined how neural activity during the stressor predicted changes in gene expression from baseline to 35 min (Follow-up 1) and 65 min (Follow-up 2) later. Exploratory analyses tested whether neural-gene expression changes differed by maternal MDD history. Results revealed that transcriptional responses to the stressor varied most consistently with anterior insula-anterior cingulate cortex (insula-ACC) and insula-ventromedial prefrontal cortex (insula-VMPFC) connectivity. After false discovery rate correction, insula-ACC and insula-VMPFC connectivity were associated with at least a 2-fold difference in expression of 907 and 1,193 genes, respectively. Whereas greater insula-ACC connectivity was related to upregulation of several immune pathways, greater insula-VMPFC connectivity was generally associated with downregulation of these pathways. Brain-wide analyses identified additional neural networks related to immunity, many involving cerebellar regions, and superior frontal, middle frontal, and inferior temporal gyri. Maternal MDD history further moderated these patterns. These data are thus consistent with the Social Signal Transduction Theory of Depression and help elucidate individual differences in neural-genomic responses to social evaluation that shape risk for depression in adolescent females.
