items.title: Harmonising cardiovascular risk classification across prediction functions using population percentiles: The ORESTES study.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention strategies use risk prediction functions to classify individuals into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk categories. Currently recommended thresholds allocate markedly different proportions of the population to these categories across functions. We aimed to develop a percentile-based approach for deriving population-calibrated cut-off points across models and to replicate the approach in an independent cohort. We analysed 437,733 participants aged 45-74 years from a population-based cohort in Catalonia, Spain (PADRIS), and replicated findings in 644,989 participants from other Spanish regions (BIFAP). CVD risk was estimated using Framingham, REGICOR, FRESCO, SCORE2, CUORE, and the AHA Pooled Cohort Equation. For each function, percentile-based cut-off points corresponding approximately to the lower 65%, middle 20%, and upper 15% of the population risk distribution were derived, as an example. We compared population classification, event incidence, and illustrative numbers needed to treat (NNT). During a median follow-up of 9.6 years in PADRIS (4.2 million person-years), 10-year incidence was 4.7% for CVD. Guideline-recommended thresholds produced substantial heterogeneity in population classification, with 12-29% of individuals classified as high risk by functions. Despite these differences, discrimination was broadly similar across models. Percentile-based thresholds harmonised category distributions across risk functions, with similar illustrative NNT estimates. Findings were replicated in BIFAP. Commonly used CAD and CVD risk functions classify substantially different proportions of the population into intermediate- and high-risk categories. A percentile-based population approach may harmonise relative risk categorisation across models without modifying the underlying continuous risk estimates.

items.title: Modified LRINEC score incorporating bullae and band-form neutrophils for differentiating necrotizing fasciitis from severe cellulitis.
items.abstract: Necrotizing fasciitis (NF) is a rapidly progressive, life-threatening condition that is often difficult to distinguish from severe cellulitis because of overlapping early clinical features. Although the Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis (LRINEC) score was developed for early diagnosis, its performance has been inconsistent across validation studies. We aimed to identify additional predictors from common clinical and laboratory indicators, develop a modified LRINEC (m-LRINEC) score, and validate its diagnostic performance. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with NF or severe cellulitis at a tertiary center. NF cases from 2007 to 2017 were identified using ICD-9/10 codes and confirmed by operative or pathological findings. Severe cellulitis controls were selected using standardized SSTI severity criteria and systemic inflammatory response syndrome criteria. An independent cohort from 2018 to 2022 was used for validation. Variables significant in univariate analysis were entered into stepwise logistic regression to construct the m-LRINEC score. The derivation cohort comprised 103 patients with NF and 152 with severe cellulitis. Stepwise logistic regression identified three predictors of NF: LRINEC score, bullae formation, and band-form neutrophils. The m-LRINEC (LRINEC score + 4 points for bullae + 7 points for band forms) score outperformed the original score, with AUROCs of 0.805 vs. 0.635 in the derivation cohort and 0.954 vs. 0.867 in the validation cohort. Klebsiella pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus were the predominant pathogens in monomicrobial NF. The m-LRINEC score improves diagnostic performance and may facilitate recognition and management of NF.

items.title: Prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder and risk of neurodevelopmental disorders: Scandinavian multinational cohort study.
items.abstract: To assess whether prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) increases the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in children. Population based cohort study. Nationwide register data on births, dispensed drugs, and specialist healthcare diagnoses from Denmark, Norway, and Sweden. 3 643 376 children born in 2000-21 followed up for a median 9 years after birth in Sweden and 10 years in Norway and Denmark. Prenatal exposure, defined as ≥1 filled prescription for ADHD drug treatment anytime during pregnancy or in the second/third trimester (≥98 days after the last menstrual period). Analyses were also done for monotherapy with methylphenidate, amphetamines, and atomoxetine. Unexposed pregnancies had no filled prescriptions for ADHD drugs during pregnancy. Neurodevelopmental disorders (any, subgroups, and individual disorders), identified on the basis of inpatient and outpatient diagnoses in specialist healthcare. Propensity score overlap weighted Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate adjusted (weighted) hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Data from Denmark were analysed separately, and results were pooled using random effects meta-analysis. 7595 (0.2%) children were prenatally exposed to any ADHD drug (5230 methylphenidate, 1510 amphetamines, 553 atomoxetine only). About one third (n=2389) were exposed in the second/third trimester. After control for confounders, neither any nor second/third trimester exposure to ADHD drugs overall or by drug type was associated with increased risk of any neurodevelopmental disorder (weighted hazard ratio 1.05, 95% confidence interval 0.98 to 1.12), behavioural and emotional disorders (1.04, 0.97 to 1.12), or disorders of psychological and intellectual development (1.06, 0.96 to 1.18). Some elevated hazard ratios for infrequent outcomes were observed but not consistently identified across analyses. This multinational cohort study found no increased risk of childhood neurodevelopmental disorders associated with prenatal exposure to ADHD drugs. These findings strengthen existing evidence and can assist pregnant people and clinicians in weighing the benefits and risks of such treatment during pregnancy.

items.title: Preconception antidepressant use in fathers and risk of metabolic disorders in offspring: Danish population based cohort study.
items.abstract: To investigate the associations between paternal antidepressant use during spermatogenesis and risk of metabolic disorders in offspring. Nationwide population based cohort study. Danish national registers. 1 365 887 liveborn singleton infants in Denmark from 2000 to 2023, followed from birth until 31 December 2023, death, emigration, or first occurrence of outcome, whichever came first. Metabolic disorders in offspring, including type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, and overweight or obesity, were identified from hospital and prescription records. Offspring of fathers who took antidepressants during spermatogenesis (three months before pregnancy) were compared with those of fathers who did not take antidepressants during this period and fathers who used antidepressants only during pregnancy to further account for underlying paternal mental health conditions. Associations between paternal antidepressant use and metabolic disorders, collectively and individually, were estimated as propensity score weighted hazard ratios using Cox regression. 23 572 (1.7%) offspring were born to fathers who used antidepressants during spermatogenesis. During a mean follow-up of 12.1 years (standard deviation 7.0 years), 18 353 (1.3%) offspring were diagnosed with a metabolic disorder, including 364 whose fathers used antidepressants during spermatogenesis and 17 989 whose fathers did not use antidepressants during this period (1.39 v 1.11 events per 1000 person years, respectively). Offspring whose fathers used antidepressants during spermatogenesis had a slightly higher risk of developing metabolic disorders (weighted hazard ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.04 to 1.38) compared with offspring who were unexposed. The associations varied by specific metabolic outcomes, with weighted hazard ratios ranging from 0.81 (95% CI 0.45 to 1.47) for hypercholesterolaemia to 1.64 (95% CI 1.21 to 2.22) for hypertension. However, when compared with offspring of fathers who took antidepressants during the pregnancy period only, no increased risk was found of any metabolic disorders (0.75, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.98) or of specific metabolic disorders. The slightly increased risk of metabolic disorders in offspring of fathers using antidepressants during spermatogenesis was probably attributable to underlying paternal mental health disorders. These findings offer reassurance for men treated with antidepressants before pregnancy.

items.title: [Obesity disease management program for adults: an empirical-ethical analysis].
items.abstract: Obesity poses major challenges to the German healthcare system due to its high prevalence. To date, no standardised model of routine care has been established. In 2023, the structural framework for a Disease Management Program (DMP) for obesity was adopted; however, nationwide contractual implementation has yet to be achieved. Ethical reflection on DMPs remains an underexplored area of research. A retrospective analysis was conducted on 20 semi-structured interviews with participants in a weight reduction programme to identify and critically reflect on requirements for a DMP. The interviews were transcribed, pseudonymised, and coded using qualitative data analysis software. Data were analysed by means of qualitative content analysis. Ethical mid-level principles (relational autonomy, care, and justice) were applied within the framework of empirical ethics to interpret the data and derive normative conclusions for healthcare practice. The findings indicate that, due to the lack of structured care pathways, participants are largely left to manage their obesity on their own and often try numerous diets, mostly without achieving sustainable success. In addition, some individuals are unable to participate in an appropriate structured programme because of limited financial or time resources, as reimbursement policies among statutory health insurance providers are inconsistent. Participants also frequently reported experiences of weight-related stigma and emphasised the importance of social support provided by peer groups. From an ethical perspective, a DMP for obesity should not primarily be understood as an instrument for behavioural control or cost containment, but rather as a normative framework for shaping equitable and patient-centred care. An ethically robust obesity DMP should actively promote patient autonomy, provide holistic and compassionate care, and reduce rather than reinforce structural inequalities. Achieving these aims requires clearer allocation of responsibilities and stronger interprofessional collaboration. Moreover, the findings suggest that an obesity DMP should be embedded within broader societal efforts to promote health and prevent obesity.

items.title: The association between prenatal exposure to metals and food allergy in children.
items.abstract: Food allergy is a global health concern. Prenatal exposure to heavy metals has been associated with immune dysregulation and may influence child food allergy (CFA) risk. We investigated associations between prenatal metals (non-essential and essential) and CFA. This study included 555 mother-child pairs in New York City from the PRogramming of Intergenerational Stress Mechanisms (PRISM) cohort, a prospective pregnancy cohort. Prenatal levels of antimony, arsenic, aluminum, copper, cadmium, lead, manganese, and zinc were measured in urine samples collected mid-pregnancy. Child food allergy was reported by mothers from ages two to thirty-four months. Individual and mixture associations were examined using multivariable logistic and weighted quantile sum (WQS) regressions, respectively, adjusting for maternal race/ethnicity, age, educational attainment, prenatal urinary creatinine level, gestational age at sample collection, and child sex. Women were predominantly Black (55%) and Non-Black Hispanic (39%). Child food allergy prevalence was 19%. In individual multivariable adjusted models, CFA was associated with manganese (OR=1.29 per doubling of exposure, 95%CI: 1.12-1.51) and aluminum (OR=1.27, 95%CI:1.07-1.53) concentrations, and marginally associated with antimony (OR=1.25, 95%CI: 0.98-1.60) and lead (OR=1.15, 95%CI: 0.97-1.37) concentrations. In WQS models for an overall mixture effect, a decile increase in the mixture was associated with increased odds of CFA in the overall sample (OR=1.19 , 95%CI: 1.06-1.35), driven primarily by manganese, antimony and aluminum. In sex-stratified WQS analyses, a decile increase in the mixture was associated with increased CFA (OR=1.31, 95%CI: 1.07-1.62) in male children compared to non-significant increase (OR = 1.10, 95%CI: 0.94-1.29) in females. Prenatal metal exposures were positively associated with parent-reported CFA, particularly among males.

items.title: Oral microbiome signatures were associated with per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and circulating cardiometabolic biomarkers.
items.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widespread environmental contaminants linked to cardiometabolic health, yet the role of the oral microbiome remains unexplored. We examined associations between PFAS exposure, oral microbiome, and circulating cardiometabolic biomarkers. In 381 adults from the Chicago Multiethnic Prevention and Surveillance Study (COMPASS), we measured five serum PFAS (PFOA, br-PFOS, n-PFOS, n-PFHxS, ∑PFOS). The oral microbiome was profiled in saliva. We used ANCOM-BC2 to identify PFAS-associated taxa (FDR<0.05) and constructed PFAS-oral microbiome indices. Associations of these indices with oral microbiome composition and six cardiometabolic biomarkers (ghrelin, resistin, leptin, C-peptide, CK-MB, MCP-1) were evaluated. PFAS exposure was significantly associated with 42 taxa. Positive associations were predominantly observed with obligate anaerobes linked to periodontitis (e.g., Sphaerochaeta, Fretibacterium), while inverse associations were observed for facultative anaerobes and beneficial genera (e.g., Bifidobacterium, Butyrivibrio). Single PFAS compounds and individual taxa showed few associations with oral microbiome diversity or cardiometabolic biomarkers. In contrast, PFAS-oral microbiome indices were significantly associated with alpha diversity and explained significant variation in beta diversity (R2=4.7%-7.0%, all p-value < 0.001). The PFOA-oral microbiome index was positively associated with MCP-1, and the n-PFHxS-oral microbiome index was inversely associated with C-peptide. PFAS exposure is associated with oral microbiome signatures characterized by obligate anaerobes and periodontitis-related taxa, alongside lower abundance of beneficial bacteria. PFAS-microbiome indices were associated with inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers, suggesting that the oral microbiome may be involved in the pathways linking PFAS exposure to cardiometabolic health. Longitudinal studies are needed to confirm causality.

items.title: Self-administered hormonal contraception use and screening bimanual pelvic examinations: associations in an employer-sponsored insurance claims database.
items.abstract: We sought to test our hypothesis that the prevalence of screening pelvic examinations at preventive care visits was higher for users of self-administered hormonal contraception (SAHC) compared to non-users of SAHC. We identified females ages 15 to 54 enrolled in a large, employer-sponsored insurance claims database and used prescription fills around an index preventive care visit to classify them as non-users, recent users, ongoing users, or new users of SAHC. We compared each user group to SAHC non-users, balanced covariates using inverse probability of treatment weights, and calculated the relative prevalence of screening pelvic examinations, i.e., those that occurred in the absence of a coded medical indication, on index visit for each SAHC user group compared to non-users. At the index preventive care visits, the crude prevalence of screening pelvic exams was 43.9% for SAHC non-users, 54.5% for recent, 60.3% for ongoing, and 63.7% for new SAHC users. The weighted relative prevalence of screening pelvic exams was 1.21 among ongoing SAHC users vs. non-users (95% confidence interval, CI, 1.20-1.21), 1.19 among new vs. non-users (95% CI 1.19-1.20), and 1.14 among recent vs. non-users (95% CI 1.14-1.14). Individuals classified as recent, ongoing, or new SAHC users at the time of a preventive care visit experienced a higher prevalence of screening pelvic exams at that visit compared to non-users of SAHC. Future work is needed to examine the potential barrier that screening pelvic exams pose to SAHC use and strategies to de-implement the practice of performing them when prescribing or caring for SAHC users.

items.title: Displaced Knowledge: Abortion-related False Information, Legal Ambiguity, and Grassroots Resistance in Post-Dobbs Texas.
items.abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine how false information about abortion is experienced, navigated, and resisted by those supporting abortion access in Texas following the U.S. Supreme Court's decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization. We conducted a secondary thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with 15 grassroots abortion activists recruited through purposive and snowball sampling between November 2023 and April 2024. Guided by a reproductive justice perspective, we examined activists' experiences with abortion-related false information, including its perceived sources, impacts, and organizational responses. Activists described barriers to accessing accurate abortion information, including fragmented digital platforms, limited Spanish-language resources, and misleading information from crisis pregnancy centers. Participants reported that legal uncertainty contributed to fear and self-censorship, with healthcare providers, educational institutions, and community partners increasingly reluctant to share abortion-related information. In response, activists relied on trusted community networks, developed educational materials, directed individuals to vetted abortion resources, and organized campaigns to expose misleading practices at crisis pregnancy centers. In restrictive policy environments, abortion information is not eliminated but displaced from formal clinical systems into informal networks, disproportionately burdening marginalized communities. In response, activists described information-sharing through trusted community networks, vetted resources, and community education. Restrictive abortion policy environments may affect not only access to abortion care but also pathways to accurate reproductive health information. Activists' reliance on trusted community networks highlights opportunities for healthcare systems to strengthen connections with community-based information pathways.

items.title: Exclusion of patients experiencing homelessness from Canadian linked health administrative data research: A critical investigation.
items.abstract: In Canada, health administrative research typically includes encounters linked through a valid health card number (HCN), which serves as proof of public insurance coverage. Patients experiencing homelessness (PEH) often lack valid HCNs, which can lead to exclusion and bias. We compared invalid HCN in emergency department (ED) visits between PEH and people not experiencing homelessness (PNEH). This population-level study included ED visits in jurisdictions with complete reporting (Ontario, Alberta, and Yukon) from April 1, 2022, to March 31, 2023. PEH were identified using ICD-10-CA codes Z59.0 and Z59.1. The primary outcome was invalid HCN. Differences between PEH and PNEH were estimated using adjusted incidence rate ratios (aIRR) from Poisson generalized linear models with robust variance. Subgroup aIRRs were compared with the overall aIRR using ratios of IRRs (RIRR) with 95% confidence intervals from seemingly unrelated estimation. Among 100,082 PEH and 6,838,899 PNEH visits, PEH were over three times more likely to have invalid HCN (9.0% vs. 2.2%; aIRR 3.38 [95% CI 3.31-3.45]). PEH-PNEH differences were significantly above average for visits covered through provincial or territorial healthcare plans (RIRR 2.66 [2.55-2.71]), ages 40-59 (RIRR 1.31 [1.26-1.35]) ages 60+ (RIRR 2.54 [2.39-2.71]), and circulatory (RIRR 1.51 [1.26-1.81]), respiratory (RIRR 1.26 [1.12-1.42]) and digestive system visits (RIRR 1.18 [1.02-1.36]). They were significantly below average for mental and behavioural disorders (RIRR 0.83 [0.80-0.86]) and injuries affecting specific body regions (RIRR 0.85 [0.80-0.91]). Restricting to visits with valid HCNs overestimated disparities for substance use and cold-related injuries, but the net effect on estimates using all visits was modest. PEH health encounters are disproportionately and non-randomly excluded from administrative data research linked using HCN. Non-random exclusion could result in biased disparity estimates. Health administrative data infrastructure reliant on health card identifiers should consider implementing more inclusive linkage approaches.

items.title: Adipocyte lipolysis associates with long-term development of hyperlipidaemia.
items.abstract: Adipocyte functions (cellularity, lipid breakdown and synthesis) associate with simultaneous presence of elevated circulating lipid levels. This study examined if such features also relate to future development of hyperlipidaemia. Between 1988-2016 we investigated 1004 Swedish individuals with biochemical/anthropometric examinations, a health questionnaire, and abdominal subcutaneous adipocyte size, basal and stimulated lipolysis (triglyceride breakdown), and adipose insulin resistance (Adipo-IR, fasting serum levels of insulin times fatty acids). All individuals were contacted again 2018-22 for a repeated health survey (17 years in mean observation time). A response was obtained from 280 participants, whereof 210 individuals did not haveout hyperlipidaemia at baseline and follow-up and 44 developed a hyperlipidaemia diagnosis at follow-up. These groups were compared by unpaired t-test and logistic regression, while considering the influence of relevant co-factors. Of all functional features, only the basal (spontaneous) adipocyte lipolysis rate (log10 µmoles of glycerol release per number of adipocytes) independently associated with development of hyperlipidaemia over time. The basal lipolysis rate was about 45 % increased (p = 0.0002) in those developing hyperlipidaemia. This relationship with hyperlipidaemia development was independent of sex, age, body mass index, initial lipid levels, waist-to-hip ratio, bariatric surgery, observation time, insulin resistance, body weight changes over time , smoking, physical activity or simultaneous presence of type 2 diabetes. The basal rate of fat cell lipolysis associates with future development of hyperlipidaemia even following adjustment for pertinent co-factors.

items.title: HELZ2 knockdown alleviates hepatic steatosis and reduces inflammatory responses in mice.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) involves hepatic steatosis, metabolic dysfunction and inflammation. HELZ2 has been linked to hepatic lipid metabolism and immune transcription, but its role in MAFLD remains unclear. Peripheral-blood whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed in eight patients with MAFLD and eight healthy controls. Candidate genes were examined by RT-qPCR in an independent cohort. We studied HELZ2 in HFD-fed mice via AAV8-mediated knockdown and in a public human liver RNA-sequencing cohort. HELZ2 was nominally upregulated in the discovery cohort but lost significance after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (log2FC = 0.677; nominal P = 0.00475; adjusted P = 0.999). It had the highest discovery-cohort AUC (0.922) and was the only prioritized gene significantly increased in validation. Peripheral-blood HELZ2 strongly correlated with clinical parameters of MAFLD, including BMI, liver enzymes, and lipid profiles. In an independent liver cohort (GSE135251), HELZ2 expression was higher in the fatty liver disease group (median ratio, 1.42; two-sided Wilcoxon P = 0.000709). HFD feeding increased hepatic HELZ2 expression, TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB-associated signaling, circulating cytokines, and CD86/iNOS, while reducing Arg1/CD206. HELZ2 knockdown reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, steatosis, and serum ALT/AST, with minimal body-weight effects, and reversed the pathway-associated readouts, circulating cytokines, and tissue-marker changes. HELZ2 is associated with MAFLD, and its knockdown alleviated hepatic steatosis and liver injury in HFD-fed mice. These improvements were accompanied by reduced inflammatory responses and TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB-associated signaling, together with altered M1/M2-associated tissue-marker expression. The findings do not establish a direct HELZ2-TLR interaction or macrophage-specific polarization effects; the underlying molecular mechanism remains unresolved.

items.title: Differential Cardio-Cerebrovascular Health Implications of PM 2.5 Oxidative Potential Metrics: DTTm versus DTTv in a large Chinese Adult Population.
items.abstract: Existing studies have shown that fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is associated with an increased risk of cardio-cerebrovascular diseases (CCVD), while the oxidative potential of PM2.5 (OPP) has emerged as a toxicity-relevant metric. However, epidemiological evidence linking OPP exposure to CCVD remains limited. This study examined the association between OPP exposure and CCVD among 788,472 adults in the Pearl River Delta region of Guangdong Province, China, and compared the associations of the two OPP metrics (DTTm and DTTv). CCVD outcomes were self-reported physician-diagnosed conditions including coronary heart disease and cerebrovascular diseases. Participants were assigned OPP exposures based on geocoded residential addresses using spatial-temporal exposure models. Associations were estimated using spatial generalized linear mixed models that adjusted for potential confounders. Each interquartile range (IQR) increase in OPP exposure was associated with higher odds of overall CCVD (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.10-1.13 for DTTm; OR = 1.03, 95% CI: 1.02-1.05 for DTTv). Similar patterns were observed for coronary heart disease (OR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.17-1.20 for DTTm; OR = 1.07, 95% CI: 1.05-1.09 for DTTv). Overall, associations were numerically larger for DTTm than for DTTv across CCVD outcomes. Furthermore, associations of DTTm with CCVD were larger in magnitude among participants aged <65 years, those with higher education and income, non-smokers, regular exercisers, and individuals with normal weight, whereas no clear or significant subgroup differences were observed for DTTv except for age, education and income. These findings support further investigation of OPP as a complementary metric to PM2.5 mass concentration in epidemiological studies of CCVD. However, given the cross-sectional study design, causal inferences cannot be made, and prospective studies are needed to confirm these associations and clarify the potential health effects of OPP.

items.title: Enhanced Protection by Fluoride Varnish with Nano-Sized Sodium Trimetaphosphate Against Enamel Erosive Wear: An In Situ Study.
items.abstract: To assess the effects of fluoride varnishes containing micrometric or nano-sized sodium trimetaphosphate (TMPmicro or TMPnano, respectively) on erosive tooth wear (ETW) in situ. In this randomized, double-blind, crossover study, 14 participants wore palatal devices containing bovine enamel blocks (n=4/device), which received each of the four varnish treatments in separate experimental periods: Placebo (Pla - without F/TMP); 5% NaF (5NaF); 5NaF + 5% TMPmicro (5-TMPmicro); and 5NaF + 5% TMPnano (5-TMPnano). After 6 h of intraoral exposure and varnish removal, the blocks underwent four daily erosive challenges ex vivo for five days (ERO, 0.05 M citric acid, pH 3.2, 90 s), while two blocks were additionally subjected to abrasion by brushing (ERO+ABR). Profilometry, surface hardness (SH), cross-sectional hardness (ΔKHN) and computed X-ray micro tomography (gHAp × cm⁻³ × µm) were performed. Data were analyzed using two-way repeated-measures ANOVA and Holm-Sidak's test (p<0.05). ETW, integrated mineral loss and depth of mineral loss of the remaining eroded enamel showed a consistent treatment ranking under both conditions, with the greatest protection observed for 5-TMPnano, followed by 5-TMPmicro, 5NaF, and Pla. Compared with 5NaF, ETW was reduced by 20-22% with 5-TMPmicro and 40-50% with 5-TMPnano under ERO and ERO+ABR. A similar pattern was observed for hardness in depth (ΔKHN at 5-30 µm from the enamel surface), except between 5-TMPmicro and 5-TMPnano. Compared with 5NaF, SH loss was significantly lower for both TMP-containing varnishes under ERO, but only for 5-TMPnano under ERO+ABR. F varnish supplemented with TMP significantly reduced ETW in situ, and nano-sized TMP provided additional protection. The addition of TMP to 5% NaF varnishes, especially as nanoparticles, may enhance their protective effect against enamel erosive wear.

items.title: Survival of root canal-treated teeth during a 15-year observation period in public dental service: A register-based study.
items.abstract: Regardless of the increasing numbers of studies investigating outcomes of non-surgical root canal treatment (nsRCT), it is important to explore long-term survival of root canal-treated teeth (RCTT) in clinical practice. This study aimed to assess survival of RCTT in public dental service (PDS) in a 15-year observation period, and to evaluate the impact of patient-, tooth-, and operator-related factors on tooth survival. This retrospective register-based study was conducted by using data obtained from electronic patient records of the PDS of the City of Helsinki. Altogether 84 320 non-surgically RCTT between 2002 and 2016 were included in the study. Survival of the RCTT was assessed with Kaplan-Meier estimator and Cox regression model. Cumulative survival rates after primary nsRCT in a five-, 10- and 15-year observation period were 91.1%, 82.8% and 77.2%, respectively. Hazard of tooth extraction was highest in older age groups, and for molar teeth. Teeth restored with indirect restorations had over 50% lower hazard of tooth extraction compared to those restored with direct restorations. Placement of coronal restoration after 12 months of root canal filling was found to decrease the likelihood of tooth survival. The cumulative survival rates of RCTT in the PDS were similar to those reported in previous studies elsewhere. Higher age and molars were risk factors for tooth extraction. Placement of indirect restoration was associated with higher likelihood of tooth survival, supporting its consideration as part of the coronal restorative management of RCTT. Confounding factors such as treatment history and restorability of the tooth and caries risk of the patient should be taken into account in future studies. Long-term tooth survival rates after endodontic treatments can be acceptable in routine clinical practice where most of the treatments are performed by general dentists. Tooth survival was associated with factors related to restorative treatment highlighting its importance in retention of root canal-treated teeth.

items.title: Requirements under external constraint: infection prevention and control in field hospitals.
items.abstract: Field hospitals must maintain baseline infection prevention and control (IPC) when access to external services and resources is restricted. This analysis examines how external constraint changes the fulfilment of established IPC requirements, not the requirements themselves. WHO Standard Precautions provided the international baseline, supported by NATO doctrine on routine IPC in medical treatment facilities. Eleven precautions were expressed as functional target states and mapped to dependencies on Infrastructure, Material, Human, Organization and Assurance. Typical external fulfilment pathways were identified, and consequences of constraining supply, removal, processing, space and specialist capacity were examined. Constraint shifts fulfilment onto the organic system. Across the precautions examined, consequences of this shift could be described using three recurring, non-exclusive dynamics: depletion of finite inputs, accumulation of outputs that cannot leave the system, and saturation of finite organic capacity. IPC capability cannot be inferred from nominal configuration alone; fulfilment pathways must be made explicit before constraint produces failure.

items.title: Immunogenicity and safety of a live-attenuated varicella vaccine in healthy individuals aged ≥13 years in China: a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, non-inferiority trial.
items.abstract: This phase 3, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, non-inferiority trial compared test and control varicella vaccines (VarVs) in healthy participants aged ≥13 years without prior varicella vaccination or disease. Conducted at a single center in China (July 2023-March 2024), 1,600 eligible participants were stratified by age (13-17 vs. ≥18 years) and randomized 1:1:1:1 to receive test or control VarV on 0- and 4-week or 0- and 8-week schedule. Primary endpoints were seroconversion rate (SR) difference and geometric mean titer (GMT) ratio at 42 days post-full immunization. Non-inferiority required the lower bound of two-sided 95% CI for SR difference >-5.00% and for GMT ratio >0.67. Primary safety endpoint was incidence of adverse reaction (AR) within 28 days after either dose. In per-protocol population (n =1,444), test VarV was non-inferior to control VarV for SR (difference 3.97%, 95% CI 0.75%, 7.18%) and GMT (ratio 1.20, 95% CI 1.09, 1.33). Local ARs were higher with test VarV, including injection-site pain (7.01% vs. 3.63%), erythema (3.00% vs. 1.13%), swelling (2.88% vs. 0.75%), and induration (2.88% vs. 0.25%), all mild to moderate. Serious adverse events were balanced (0.88% each), with no deaths or sequelae. Test VarV demonstrated non-inferior immunogenicity and acceptable safety. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) Identifier: ChiCTR2500098374 (Retrospectively registered-March 6, 2025). Available from https://www.chictr.org.cn. This trial was sponsored by Shanghai Rongsheng Biotech Co., Ltd.

items.title: Impact of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist Treatment on Post-Operative Atrial Fibrillation.
items.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists have demonstrated cardiovascular benefits with anti-inflammatory and anti-arrhythmic properties. This study aimed to evaluate the association of GLP-1 use with postoperative atrial fibrillation and mortality in patients undergoing cardiac surgery. This was a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery from 2010 to 2025. Patients were stratified into GLP-1 users and non-users. Patients with a history of atrial fibrillation (AF), concurrent MAZE procedure, and prior cardioversions or ablations were excluded. The primary outcome was incidence of new onset postoperative AF within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included AF-related readmissions and all-cause mortality. Multivariable adjusted regression models were used to compare POAF incidence and time-to-event secondary outcomes. A total of 8,672 patients were included. The 411 GLP-1 users were younger with higher BMI and HbA1c and were more likely to have diabetes compared to non-users (all p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment, GLP-1 users demonstrated a significantly lower incidence of postoperative AF compared to non-users (29.0% vs. 34.6%, RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.71-0.99, p=0.038). AF-related readmission in GLP-1 users were 1.2% at 1 year and 3.5% at 5 years, compared to 2.9% and 6.5% in non-users, respectively (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.30-1.13, p=0.111). One- and five-year mortality was similar between groups (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.67-1.25, p=0.561). In this large real-world cohort, GLP-1 agonist use was associated with significant reduction of new onset postoperative AF and trended towards lower AF related readmissions. These findings support further investigation of GLP-1s in perioperative cardiac surgery.

items.title: Evolution of cardiovascular risk scores in type 2 diabetes: Insights from the USA, the UK, and China.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D), and cardiovascular risk scores increasingly inform preventive strategies and treatment decisions. However, these scores have been developed across diverse populations, regions, and time periods using heterogeneous methodological approaches, raising questions about their comparability, transportability, and applicability in diabetes care. We provide an up-to-date synthesis of cardiovascular risk scores relevant to T2D in the USA, the UK, and China, drawing on reviews, guideline documents, and targeted literature searches across these settings and relevant regional or global contexts. Models were compared across 20 methodological and implementation domains. A total of 56 cardiovascular risk score entries were identified, including 31 classified as general-population models and 25 as T2D-specific models. These models differed substantially in derivation populations, predictor composition, outcome definitions, prediction horizons, validation patterns, and implementation characteristics, while T2D-specific models more frequently included diabetes-related predictors such as glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), diabetes duration, albuminuria, and renal function. Descriptive evidence based largely on indirect cross-study comparisons did not establish a consistent performance advantage for either category. Marked regional variation may reflect differences in epidemiology, healthcare systems, data infrastructure, and guideline traditions, which could influence model development, recalibration, and clinical use. Cardiovascular risk prediction has gradually moved towards larger datasets, richer predictor information, broader cardiovascular outcomes, greater emphasis on validation, and more accessible implementation formats. Overall, cardiovascular risk scores in T2D show substantial heterogeneity, and no single model is optimal across all settings. Selection of cardiovascular risk scores in T2D patients should place emphasis on population-specific validation, calibration, alignment of the predicted outcome and prediction horizon with the clinical decision, predictor availability, and implementation feasibility, rather than model category alone. Local recalibration and periodic performance reassessment may be particularly relevant when absolute risk estimates inform threshold-based preventive treatment decisions. (300 /300 words).

items.title: Prevalence and Correlates of Appearance- and Performance-Enhancing Drugs and Substances Use among a Population-Based Sample of Canadians: A Cross-Sectional Survey, 2026.
items.abstract: To estimate the prevalence and sociodemographic correlates of appearance- and performance-enhancing drugs and substances (APEDS), including legal supplements and illicit drugs, among Canadians. Data were from 4,017 Canadians who participated in a cross-sectional, population-based survey administered by Mental Health Research Canada. Lifetime and current use of six APEDS (protein drinks/powders, creatine, pre-workout drinks/powders, anabolic-androgenic steroids [AAS], injectable/oral peptides, and other hormone-like or muscle-building drugs) without a medical prescription were assessed. Prevalence of APEDS use was determined among the overall sample, and by age, gender, and race/ethnicity. Six separate logistic regression models were estimated to determine the sociodemographic associations with lifetime use of each APEDS. Use of protein drinks/powders was most prevalent amongst Canadians (35.2% lifetime; 13.2% current). Lifetime AAS, peptide, and other hormone-like drug use each approximated 5%. Lifetime use of all APEDS was highest among 16-29-year-olds. Cisgender men had higher odds than cisgender women of using creatine, pre-workout drinks/powders, AAS, peptides, and other hormone-like drugs. In this population-based Canadian sample, legal APEDS were commonly used, and illicit APEDS were used by a smaller but non-trivial minority, particularly younger adults, cisgender men, participants identifying with a racial or ethnic minority group, and those engaged in muscle-building exercise.

items.title: Validation and Establishment of the Contrast Volume Prediction Model: For Optimizing Renal Efficiency in EVAR (the FORE-EVAR calculator).
items.abstract: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) is a preventable complication associated with iodinated contrast volume during endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR). We previously published a prediction model "For Optimizing Renal Efficiency in EVAR" (FORE-EVAR) which utilizes 13 patient-specific variables to generate a recommended contrast-volume threshold to prevent CA-AKI after EVAR. This study evaluates FORE-EVAR against machine-learning models and establishes FORE-EVAR's user-interface for general use. Eight machine-learning algorithms were applied to a 49,417-patient Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) EVAR cohort (2003-July 2024). Following comparison of FORE-EVAR with machine-learning models, an updated VQI EVAR dataset (August 2024-October 2025) of 7,112 new patients was used for temporal validation. Using split-sample approach (80% training; 20% validation) of the 49,417-patient dataset, FORE-EVAR demonstrated a strong AUC=0.753 (comparable to machine-learning models [range=0.712-0.759]) with similar performance across other predictive metrics. Importantly, FORE-EVAR requires input of 13 patient variables which is significantly less than the 50+ variables required by machine-learning models. The comparable prediction metrics and simplicity of variables support FORE-EVAR as a practical candidate for clinical implementation. Temporal validation with the 7,112-patient dataset showed AUC=0.706, emphasizing FORE-EVAR's predictability across cohorts. FORE-EVAR's user-interface provides three personalized outputs: CA-AKI risk category (Low, Moderate, High, or Very High); a recommended contrast volume threshold; and predicted CA-AKI risk at fixed volumes of 50mL and 100mL for procedural guidance. FORE-EVAR is a validated prediction tool which provides valuable patient-specific contrast-volume recommendations. Prospective studies are needed to evaluate FORE-EVAR's impact on intraoperative contrast volume and incidence of CA-AKI.

items.title: Eating practices and associated occupational and health factors among teachers in a Brazilian state public-school system.
items.abstract: To assess eating practices according to the Dietary Guidelines for the Brazilian Population and associated factors among basic education teachers in the state public-school system of Montes Claros, Minas Gerais, Brazil. In this cross-sectional study, 1907 teachers completed an online questionnaire in October-December 2021. Eating practices were assessed using a validated 24-item scale; associations were examined using Poisson regression with robust variance. Eating practices were adequate in 50.9%, required modification in 38.7%, and were inadequate in 10.4%. Higher prevalence of practices requiring modification or classified as inadequate was associated with male sex (1.14; 1.03-1.27), working ≥40 h/week (1.15; 1.01-1.31), suspected common mental disorder (1.52; 1.35-1.72), poor or very poor sleep quality (1.23; 1.10-1.37), and being sedentary or irregularly active (1.30; 1.16-1.45); age ≥ 44 years was associated with lower prevalence (0.87; 0.80-0.96). Estimates are adjusted prevalence ratios with 95% confidence intervals. These findings highlight occupational, psychosocial, and behavioral factors that may be relevant to workplace health-promotion strategies aimed at supporting healthier eating practices among teachers.

items.title: Evidence translation and community engagement within US cancer centers.
items.abstract: The National Cancer Institute requires cancer centers to maintain Community Outreach and Engagement components (COEs) that bridge research and community priorities to support evidence translation. Limited information exists on how COEs implement evidence-based interventions (EBIs) with community partners. We describe how COEs translate evidence into practice and promising community engagement practices. We conducted semi-structured interviews in 2021 with COE leaders at 38 NCI-designated US cancer centers. EBIs were categorized along a community engagement continuum, and cross-cutting themes and highly-engaged practices were identified. Transcripts were double-coded and analyzed using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. COEs implemented a wide range of EBIs at varying levels of community engagement. Implementation was shaped by community- and data-driven priority setting, leadership support, staffing constraints, and sustainability challenges. Highly-engaged EBIs involved community partners in identification, adapting materials, training faculty/staff on community engagement, and participating in evaluation and data analysis. They were most common among COEs with strong leadership support and dedicated funding. Findings suggest well-supported COEs enabled more highly engaged EBI implementation. Institutional commitment and meaningful community partnership roles are important considerations for COEs seeking to embed community engagement throughout implementation and enhance reach and effectiveness of EBIs to reduce cancer disparities.

items.title: AI-Assisted PROTAC Design for Cancer Therapy: An Evidence-to-Decision Framework for Designer, Connector and Predictor Roles.
items.abstract: AI methods are used in proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) discovery for candidate generation, ternary-complex modelling and property prediction. These tasks are organised here into Designer, Connector and Predictor roles to examine how computational outputs can inform experimental decisions in cancer drug discovery. Published studies connect selected computationally generated compounds to biological testing and show how new measurements can inform chemical optimisation and property-model refinement. Case studies of linker modifications and PKMYT1 stereoisomers illustrate discrepancies between binding and cellular degradation. Further preclinical and clinical findings show why target depletion must be interpreted alongside pathway suppression, tissue exposure and tolerability. The analysis identifies measurements that could distinguish competing explanations and guide changes to candidate chemistry, structural hypotheses, prediction models or experimental conditions. Predictive performance depends on chemical and biological context, so validation needs to reflect the compounds, targets and endpoints encountered in the intended application. Exposure-response models can help interpret pharmacological findings when supported by relevant tissue and pathway measurements. Clinical outcomes are also distinguished from evidence of AI involvement in individual candidates. Current evidence supports specific connections between computation and experiment. Prospective comparisons are needed to determine whether coordinating these methods improves candidate selection and pharmacological outcomes.

items.title: Multivariate genome-wide association study of cardiometabolic diseases reveals shared genetic architecture and enhances risk prediction through integrated polygenic and proteomic risk scores.
items.abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases (CMD) are interconnected, but their shared and domain-specific genetic architecture and the value of integrating genetic and proteomic information for risk prediction remain unclear. We applied LD score regression, factor analyses, and genomic structural equation modeling to genome-wide association summary statistics for seven CMD components in European-ancestry cohorts. We performed multivariate genome-wide association analysis, functional annotation, tissue and cell-type enrichment, gene prioritization, and pathway analysis. Polygenic risk scores (PRS) were evaluated in 310,708 UK Biobank participants, and proteomic risk scores (ProRS) were developed and tested in a proteomics subset of 33,253 participants. A hierarchical model identified cardiac (coronary artery disease and heart failure), vascular (stroke and hypertension), and metabolic (body mass index, type 2 diabetes, and triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio) factors underlying a higher-order CMD factor. We identified 328 independent CMD-associated variants, including 15 novel variants, and prioritized 297 high-confidence CMD genes. Heritability was enriched in brain regions, adipose tissue, and gastrointestinal mucosa. Participants in the highest versus lowest CMD-PRS decile had 2.82-fold higher CMD risk. ProRS outperformed PRS for CMD prediction (AUC, 0.740 versus 0.681), while the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.741. Participants with high PRS and high ProRS had the greatest risk (HR, 2.51; 95% CI, 2.29-2.75). CMD reflects shared genetic liability with distinguishable cardiac, vascular, and metabolic components. Plasma proteomics adds predictive information to inherited risk and may improve risk stratification, although external validation and a parsimonious protein panel are required before clinical implementation.

items.title: Wider social determinants of the presentation and outcomes of patients enrolled in small abdominal aortic aneurysm surveillance.
items.abstract: Elective repair offers better outcomes than urgent repair for patients in small abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) surveillance who reach treatment thresholds, or treatment being declined due to surgical risk. Internationally, socioeconomically deprived, ethnic minority, and rural populations receive fewer guideline recommended surgical procedures. In Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ), Māori face barriers to timely surgical access. This multicentre, observational analysis of prospectively collected AAA surveillance data (2002 - 2019) examined disparities in AAA stage at diagnosis and elective repair by socioeconomic deprivation, ethnicity, and distance to vascular services. Patients with incidentally detected AAAs were grouped by socioeconomic deprivation, ethnicity (Māori/non-Māori), and travel time to vascular services. Outcomes included age and AAA diameter at diagnosis, and elective repair rates. Cumulative incidence functions estimated 36 month probability of elective repair, with cause specific Cox regression adjusted for comorbidities. 1 684 patients were eligible for analysis. Patients in highly deprived areas were diagnosed younger, but higher deprivation was associated with lower elective repair rates (hazard ratio [HR] 0.85, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.75 - 0.98; p = .02). Māori were diagnosed younger (68.7 vs. 73.4 years; p < .001) yet had lower elective repair rates for medium (≥ 45 mm) AAAs in univariable analysis (36 month probability 0.27 vs. 0.54; p = .04) and multivariable analysis controlling for covariates (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.29 - 0.86; p = .01) despite reaching treatment thresholds at least as often. Rural location was not associated with repair rates. Socioeconomic and ethnic inequities in outcomes of small AAA surveillance exist in NZ. Patients in more deprived areas had lower elective repair rates. Māori received fewer elective repairs despite equivalent or greater clinical need, likely reflecting higher comorbidity burden and operative risk. Earlier diagnosis, improved access to specialist care, including national AAA screening, enhanced risk factor management, and strengthened primary care access may reduce inequity. Socioeconomic, ethnic, and geographical factors should inform equitable screening and service delivery.

items.title: A Rare Presentation of Paediatric Hyperparathyroidism: Parafibromin Deficiency Leading to a Diagnosis of Hyperparathyroidism-Jaw Tumour Syndrome.
items.abstract: Atypical parafibromin-deficient parathyroid tumour is a recently described endocrine neoplasm. Parafibromin deficiency is often associated with parathyroid carcinoma. However, in the absence of invasive features, atypical parafibromin-deficient neoplasms display distinct morphological characteristics that are strongly associated with germline CDC73 variants and hyperparathyroidism (HPT)-jaw tumour (HPT-JT) syndrome. We present a 12-year-old female with hypercalcaemia secondary to primary HPT (PHPT). Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of the patient's tumour and germline DNA from peripheral blood identified an inherited deep intronic CDC73 variant (NM_024529.5:c.729+1118A>G) and a somatic nonsense variant (NM_024529.5:c.85G>T; p.[Glu29 ∗ ]). RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) of tumour tissue and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) demonstrated that c.729+1118A>G causes near-complete loss of canonical exon 7-8 splicing due to inclusion of a pseudoexon in intron 7, resulting in a frameshift, premature termination codon and nonsense-mediated decay (NMD). Together, these findings supported the two variants occurring in trans, consistent with biallelic CDC73 inactivation in the tumour and establishing a molecular diagnosis of HPT-JT syndrome. This case highlights the value of integrating histopathology, parafibromin immunohistochemistry (IHC) and RNA-seq studies to establish the likely pathogenicity of a deep intronic CDC73 variant. Given the ongoing risk of recurrent parathyroid disease, parathyroid carcinoma and jaw, renal and uterine tumours, early molecular diagnosis of HPT-JT syndrome is essential for appropriate lifelong surveillance and management.

items.title: Experimentally Defined T m-Guided Exon-Exon Junction Primer Design Enables Specific Discrimination of Transcript Variants with High Structural Overlap.
items.abstract: Accurate detection of individual RNA transcript variants remains challenging when closely related transcripts share extensive exonic sequences and differ primarily in exon connectivity. Analysis of curated human RefSeq transcripts identified 9,546 protein-coding genes containing at least one structurally contained transcript variant (defined as a transcript whose exons are each fully contained within those of a sibling transcript), highlighting the need for transcript-discriminating assays beyond conventional exon-targeted polymerase chain reaction (PCR). We developed a melting-temperature ( T m )-guided exon-exon junction reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR) strategy that independently evaluates the 5' and 3' exon-matching arms of junction-spanning primers. Systematic experiments demonstrated that amplification became undetectable when the T m of a partially matched primer segment was approximately 13 to 16 °C below the PCR annealing temperature, supporting an approximately 15 °C arm-specific threshold as a conservative empirical design guideline. T m -guided exon-exon junction primers, including those generated using the automated TransPrimer tool, enabled selective amplification of structurally contained transcript variants of HTRA1-AS1, apurinic/apyrimidinic endodeoxyribonuclease 1, and glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase; reduced heteroduplex formation; and yielded single predominant quantitative PCR (qPCR) melting peaks. Most evaluated primer pairs exhibited amplification efficiencies of 90% to 110% and coefficients of determination ( R 2 ) greater than 0.98. Together, these findings establish an experimentally supported framework for designing transcript-discriminating RT-PCR and qPCR assays, particularly when unique exonic sequences are limited or absent.

items.title: Exosome-like nanoparticles from blueberries modulate hypoxia-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative unbalance in RAW 264.7 cells through the activation of adaptative response.
items.abstract: Cellular adaptation to hypoxia involves a metabolic shift from mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis, primarily driven by hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α), often accompanied by increased reactive species (RS) production and oxidative stress. Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) counteracts these effects by regulating antioxidant defences and redox homeostasis. In macrophages, these mechanisms contribute to inflammatory activation and disease progression. Plant-derived exosome-like nanoparticles (ELNs) have emerged as potential therapeutic agents. This study investigates, for the first time, the protective effects of blueberry-derived ELNs (B-ELNs) against hypoxia-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress in RAW 264.7 macrophages. Hypoxia increased RS production by approximately 150% compared with normoxia. B-ELNs attenuated RS production (approximately 115%), reduced HIF-1α stabilisation (from 2.62- to 1.25-fold), and activated Nrf2 signalling (2.38-fold). These findings suggest that B-ELNs counteract hypoxia-induced metabolic and redox alterations, highlighting their potential as protective bioactive nanostructures against cellular stress.

items.title: Advanced Microstructural MRI and Clinical Characterization of Paramagnetic Rim Lesion Heterogeneity in Multiple Sclerosis.
items.abstract: Objective Paramagnetic rim lesions (PRLs) reflect chronic active lesions in multiple sclerosis (MS), but their microstructural heterogeneity remains unclear. We characterized quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (qMRI) abnormalities within PRLs, identified data-driven PRL profiles, and examined their associations with disability, brain volumetry, and serum biomarkers. Methods In this longitudinal study, 175 people with MS (pwMS) and 105 healthy controls underwent multiparametric qMRI. Clinical/serum follow-up was available for 113 pwMS (median, 4.4 years). Lesional/perilesional qMRI metrics were derived. Principal component analysis (PCA) characterized PRL heterogeneity, and clustering identified PRL profiles. Mixed-effects models assessed associations with disability, brain parenchymal fraction (BPF), serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (sGFAP). Longitudinal and retrospective MRI assessed 2-year cluster stability and the presence of corresponding lesions 3 years earlier, respectively. Results PRLs showed greater lesional and perilesional microstructural abnormalities than non-PRLs. PCA identified a dominant continuous damage dimension, along which clustering identified 2 reproducible low- and high-damage profiles. High-damage PRLs were associated with higher disability (β = 0.43; p = 0.035) and lower BPF (β = -0.25; p = 0.002), whereas low-damage PRLs were associated with higher sNfL (β = 0.35; p = 0.010). Longitudinally, low-damage PRLs were associated with steeper increases in disability (β interaction = 0.12; p = 0.023) and sGFAP (β interaction = 0.19; p = 0.030), and less favorable microstructural trajectories. Cluster assignments were largely stable longitudinally, and similar proportions of lesions from both clusters were already present 3 years earlier. Interpretation PRLs exhibit clinically meaningful heterogeneity along a continuous damage spectrum, with cluster assignments largely stable longitudinally. High-damage PRLs are associated with established neurodegeneration, whereas low-damage PRLs show features of ongoing biological activity and worse clinical evolution, supporting the relevance of PRL heterogeneity for prognostic stratification. items.title: Effects of emotional mouth expression on the expected participation in Cyberball.
items.abstract: Social exclusion threatens fundamental psychological needs and elicits neural responses indexed by the P3 event-related potential during the Cyberball paradigm. P3 response to a transition from inclusion to exclusion can be modulated by referential facial cues of the putative co-players, such as gaze direction. While gaze direction modulates the P3 exclusion effect, the influence of co-players' emotional mouth expressions remains unclear. Here we investigated whether happy, sad, or neutral mouth expressions of co-player avatars modulate the P3 response to exclusion in a between-subjects ERP study. Participants were assigned to one of three groups whose co-player avatars displayed happy, sad, or neutral mouth expressions throughout the exclusion block, while gaze remained neutral and forward facing. Exclusion enhanced P3 amplitude at fronto-central sites across all groups, confirming the expected expectancy violation response. However, mouth expression did not significantly modulate the P3, self-reported need threat, or negative mood. These findings suggest that affective valence conveyed by co-players' mouth expressions does not alter the expectancy violation mechanism indexed by the P3 during Cyberball exclusion.

items.title: Restoring neuronal CD47 alleviates microglia dependent synaptic loss and memory decline in diet-induced obesity mice.
items.abstract: Healthy synapses are protected from elimination by inhibitory "don't-eat-me" signals, but how these checkpoints fail during metabolic disease is unknown. Here, we demonstrate that diet-induced obesity triggers cognitive decline by dismantling this crucial neuroimmune safeguard. A high-fat diet rapidly induces neuronal insulin resistance in the hippocampus, suppressing neural activity and causing a selective loss of synaptic CD47, a key "don't-eat-me" molecule. This breach in the CD47-SIRPα checkpoint unleashes microglia to excessively prune synapses, causing synaptic attrition and memory impairment. While loss of CD47 accelerates this pathology, restoring its expression in hippocampal neurons provides a robust rescue, halting over-pruning and preserving cognitive function even under continuous metabolic stress. Our work elucidates a hierarchical mechanism where early metabolic dysfunction disarms a synaptic self-defense system, initiating microglia-driven neurodegeneration. We thus identify the neuronal CD47-SIRPα axis as a critical, druggable target to intercept cognitive decline in obesity and diabetes.

items.title: Oligodendrocyte ER-phagy restricts excessive myelination by degrading sphingolipid synthases.
items.abstract: Myelination is critical for nervous system function. Numerous signaling pathways have been identified that promote myelin sheath growth, disruption of which can lead to hypomyelination. However, the negative regulators of myelin sheath expansion remain poorly defined. Here, we identify endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-phagy as a cellular brake on central nervous system myelination that restricts myelin sheath thickness during brain development. ER-phagy is active in oligodendrocytes during myelin membrane expansion and limits the abundance of ER-resident sphingolipid synthases, including ceramide synthase 2 (Cers2). Impairment of ER-phagy accumulates ER, elevates sphingolipid production, drives excessive myelin thickening, and alters social behavior after prolonged juvenile social isolation. Genetic deletion of Cers2, which synthesizes long-chain ceramides essential for sphingolipid biogenesis, rescues the hypermyelination phenotype caused by ER-phagy disruption. Together, our findings establish that ER-phagy-sphingolipid axis represses myelin growth and reveal a mechanistic link between ER homeostasis and myelin production by oligodendrocytes, providing insight into the cellular mechanisms underlying pathological hypermyelination.

items.title: Parasitoid wasp response to infection with a reproductive manipulator symbiont reveals subtle changes in host proteome in life-long symbiosis
items.abstract: Encarsia is a genus of minute parasitoid wasp of the family Aphelinidae. Interestingly, many species of this genus carry bacterial symbionts, such as the reproductive manipulator Cardinium . Most of what is known about Encarsia physiology comes from studies on their ecology, morphology, and reproductive phenotypes associated with symbiont interactions, however, there is limited research exploring the molecular physiology of these species and the broader Aphelinidae family. Here, we present proteomes of male and female adult Encarsia suzannae with and without the cytoplasmic incompatibility inducing symbiont Cardinium hertigii c Eper1. We identified proteins that respond to symbiont infection and propose potential targets for symbiont-host cell manipulation and reproductive phenotypes. We also characterized the expressed innate immune capacity of the wasp and found that expression patterns were suggestive of a limited immune response toward Cardinium . Lastly, we identified expression differences in proteins putatively involved in sensory biology which may provide insights into cryptic Cardinium -induced phenotypes. Overall, our data suggest that subtle differences in E. suzannae physiology may support life-long Cardinium association. These data provide a molecular overview of E. suzannae and can be used as the basis for further characterization of Encarsia and, more broadly, a reference for the molecular physiology of Aphelinidae.

items.title: Body Size in Damselfly Survival: Insights from Mark-Recapture Studies
items.abstract: Body size is one of the main drivers of animal biology and ecology. The present study investigates the role of body size on damselfly survival probability, emphasizing its relationship with odonata behavioural traits. A meta-regression analysis was carried out on novel and previously published datasets of mark-recapture studies belonging to 22 damselfly populations of 17 species. Our results indicate that models incorporating body size as an individual covariate are similar or outperform those without it, suggesting that body size significantly influences survival rates. While large body size is advantageous in territorial and aggressive species (e.g., Polythore, Paraphlebia, Mnesarete, Calopteryx), it also positively affects survival in some non-territorial species, such as Hemiphlebia mirabilis and Coenagrion castellani. Other species, however, exhibit a small-size advantage, particularly in three-dimensional habitats requiring high manoeuvrability, as seen in some Ischnura and other species with low or absence of aggressiveness. This study highlights the heterogeneity of body size effects on survival and underscores the importance of including body size as a covariate in demographic studies of odonates to better understand survival patterns across species.

items.title: Visibility Bias in AI-Based Underwater Fish Monitoring: A Scoping Review of Ecological Validity and a Reporting Checklist
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly detects and counts fish in underwater imagery, but turbidity, light attenuation, low light, and distance affect which fish are visible. Ecology treats this as imperfect detection; the AI literature mostly treats it as an image-quality problem. This PRISMA-ScR scoping review coded 183 AI studies (2015–2026), identified through structured and database searches and evaluated on field-monitoring imagery from natural waters, on five dimensions of the observation process: visibility characterization, data independence, external-domain robustness, calibration and false-positive control, and ecological endpoint validation. A language model coded each study twice; the first author checked 90 studies (49%) against the full text, and the second author's blind coding of 40 randomly sampled studies agreed with 87% of its ratings. No study reported performance stratified by measured visibility, and only two measured water clarity with an instrument. Training and test data were separated by video, day, site, or region in 58 studies (32%); 18 (10%) compared the same model inside and outside its training domain; none reported a standard calibration metric; and 59 (32%) linked outputs to an ecological quantity, only 6 against a reference independent of the imagery. We propose a draft eleven-item reporting checklist (MRCUAI) and research agenda.

items.title: Colorless but Never Dull: Population Genomics, Hybridization, and Color Evolution in Southern Africa's "White" Darkling Beetles (Onymacris).
items.abstract: Best known for charismatic "fog-basking" species, the African tenebrionid genus Onymacris (Allard 1885) comprises remarkable phenotypic diversity that includes eight "white" taxa. "White" Onymacris differ from their uniformly black congeners in a graded loss of elytral pigmentation, including two pure white species ( Onymacris bicolor , O. candidipennis ). We examine phylogenetic relationships of the "white" Onymacris to explore color evolution, testing possible roles of convergence and introgression in pigment loss. Population genomic (3RAD) data resulted in a phylogenetic hypothesis derived from 1097 loci. 3RAD species relationships were compared with a mtDNA-based phylogeny, both of which resolved species relationships and indicated that pure white elytra evolved convergently. Variational autoencoder (VAE) clustering and admixture analyses showed that some species have undergone population genetic fragmentation whereas others have experienced recent gene flow and hybridization. Although white coloration is rare in tenebrionids, our collective results, including ancestral state reconstruction, demonstrate the repeated independent evolution of this trait in Onymacris , highlighting unresolved questions regarding its evolutionary origins.

items.title: Assessing how wind affects bird migration across the continental United States using a novel wind-favourability metric.
items.abstract: Across migratory bird species that breed in the northern hemisphere, post-breeding or fall migrations generally appear to be longer in duration than pre-breeding migrations in the spring. One explanation is that birds encounter less favourable winds during fall migration than they do during spring migration. We tested whether winds were more favourable in the spring for migrating birds by combining wind data for the continental United States from 1995 to 2024 with a radar-derived metric for the preferred direction of movement for migratory birds. From these two data sources, we generated a novel index for wind favourability that we could apply across the three major North American flyways. We found evidence for more favourable winds during the spring, especially for the central and eastern flyways, but the western flyway tended to have more favourable winds during the fall. These findings help explain differences in spring and fall migration and highlight the importance of the low-level jet (an air current that flows through the centre of North America) in the aerial habitats of migrating animals. To enable others to use the tools presented here, we provide R code for data compilation and analysis as well as a shiny app that enables users to quickly map and visualize wind favourability.

items.title: Upscaling Vessel Characteristics to Species Distribution Patterns of Angiosperms Based on an Anatomically Derived Safety-Efficiency Spectrum.
items.abstract: Xylem architecture governs plant water transport and underpins adaptation to water availability. While large vessels and high intervessel connectivity enhance hydraulic efficiency, they may reduce hydraulic safety via embolism resistance. Because this trade-off is non-linear, embolism resistance alone incompletely captures hydraulic strategy and species distributions. Here, we propose a framework introducing end wall pressure difference ( ∆P ) and conductivity ( KW ) as anatomically derived proxies capturing this safety-efficiency spectrum. We measured vessel diameter, vessel length, intervessel pit membrane thickness and intervessel connectivity for six temperate broadleaf species. Predictive mixed-effects models were then applied to 162 angiosperm species, estimating KW and ΔP based on vessel diameter and embolism resistance from the literature. These safety-efficiency estimates were analysed against mean annual precipitation and ecological strategies. Estimates of KW and ΔP followed a convex trade-off consistent across small (n = 6) and large (n = 162) datasets. Safe species with low KW and high ΔP clustered in low-precipitation regions and aligned with stress-tolerance, whereas high-efficiency species dominated wetter environments and corresponded to competitive strategies. Our framework reveals a mechanistic link between anatomy, hydraulic strategy and distribution patterns. It extends beyond empirical hydraulic metrics and provides a scalable, anatomical approach linking xylem traits, ecology and biogeography.

items.title: Litter size in an invasive species is decoupled from the pressures of elevation and water availability: the beaver in Tierra del Fuego.
items.abstract: Background A problematic invader in South America is the beaver (Castor canadensis). In its native range, stable-water levels and settlement location are among the drivers of litter size variation. Understanding how habitat differences (such as water availability and elevation) influence litter sizes can improve management decision-making for beaver population control in the invaded system. We used reproductive data from beavers that were completely eradicated from three invaded systems of Tierra del Fuego, Argentina (Mountain, Ecotone, and Steppe). We assessed the number of offspring per female produced in relation to watercourses gradients and elevation; the relationship between the density of females and the order of watercourse; and the effect of population management on settlement elevation. Results Watercourse gradient and elevation did not affect litter size, whereas female density increased with water availability. The highest densities of females were recorded in watercourses with intermediate to high water availability in the Mountain (2.1 and 1.5 females/linear km) and the Steppe (0.1 and 0.2 females/linear km), and in the Ecotone in watercourses with low to intermediate water availability (0.4 females/linear km). Conclusion In invaded systems, female beavers occupy several elevations and watercourses with higher water availability. However, these features did not limit litter size in the studied areas. This differs from the reported reproductive pattern in the native range of beavers. This empirical evidence calls for reflection on future control strategies: to maximize the return on the control investment we suggest concentrating trapping efforts on medium- and low-elevation watercourses. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

items.title: Directional seismic signals encode socially relevant information in a solitary rodent.
items.abstract: Communication signals must transmit information efficiently through the physical environment. 1 , 2 , 3 In subterranean habitats, where visual and airborne acoustic cues are severely constrained, 4 , 5 many animals rely on substrate-borne vibrations. 6 , 7 , 8 However, it remains unclear whether seismic signals are directed toward intended receivers and whether they encode socially relevant information about the signaler. Here, we investigated seismic communication in the blind mole rat (BMR; Nannospalax galili), a solitary subterranean rodent that produces vibrations by head drumming against tunnel walls. 9 , 10 , 11 Using a semi-natural outdoor setup equipped with more than 30 geophones, we examined the spatial and informational structure of seismic signaling during social interactions while manipulating the position and sex of conspecific intruders. We found that head-drumming signals were distributed non-uniformly and were biased toward the location of the conspecific intruder, producing a broad directional radiation pattern. Signal production rate was also modulated by social context, as BMRs produced more head drums during opposite-sex than same-sex encounters and exhibited sex-dependent temporal dynamics over the course of interactions. Finally, machine-learning analyses showed that head drumming contains individual-specific structure in both single-drum waveforms and the temporal organization of drum sequences, with individual classification remaining above chance across recording sessions and behavioral roles. Together, these findings establish seismic communication as a receiver-directed, information-rich signaling system that simultaneously encodes spatial, individual, and social information. More broadly, our results extend the principle of receiver-directed communication to the seismic modality and suggest that communication systems can converge on common strategies for transmitting biologically relevant information despite fundamentally different physical environments.

items.title: Nutrient-leaching trade-offs of food-waste compost valorization: linked roles of organic matter, salinity and microplastics in agricultural soils.
items.abstract: Food-waste compost recycles nutrients but also introduces soluble salts and residual microplastics (MPs), creating a coupled amendment matrix whose effects cannot be inferred from isolated-polymer studies alone. This study examined these effects through complementary batch adsorption, soil incubation and column-leaching experiments. PE and PP showed polymer-dependent adsorption of humic substances under different ionic strengths. During soil incubation, elevated PE and PP additions were associated with distinct temporal patterns of mineral-N accumulation. PP advanced the NH 4 + -N peak from day 25 to day 13 and showed apparent net nitrification rates of 7.0-7.8 mg/kg/d, whereas PE was associated with delayed mineral-N release and greater late-stage NO 3 - -N accumulation, with 2.5 % PE exceeding 200 mg/L by day 60. In soil columns, microplastic-containing compost reduced cumulative NO 3 - -N leaching by 43.3 % and 33.9 % and TN leaching by 28.74 % and 24.11 % under the two compost-substitution regimes, respectively, compared with chemical fertilization. However, the higher compost-input treatment showed greater nitrate accumulation and higher cumulative N loss than the moderate-substitution treatment. Compost substitution also induced treatment-dependent bacterial succession and differences in PICRUSt2-predicted functional potentials. Overall, food-waste compost reduced aqueous N losses under the tested conditions, but increasing compost input did not proportionally improve this benefit. Compost management should therefore consider available N input, salinity and residual MPs together rather than nutrient replacement alone.
