items.title: The algorithmic behavioral sink: Modeling the transition to irreversible demographic collapse
items.abstract: In 2025, the vast majority of major global economies reported a Total Fertility Rate below the replacement level of 2.1. This synchronized collapse has persisted despite extensive pro-natalist financial interventions, revealing a structural limitation in conventional linear demographic models. This paper proposes that the ubiquity of mobile internet and Artificial Intelligence acts as a synthetic mating disruptor, precipitating a non-linear phase transition in human pair-bonding dynamics. Treating the marriage market as a complex system governed by thermodynamic constraints, we present a Fermi-Dirac selection model, using national income distributions as the input spectrum and fitted with Japanese longitudinal data to illustrate how digital hyper-reality generates an increasingly prohibitive Marriage Energy Barrier. Our model quantifies a Tech Factor that decouples female mating expectations from local economic realities during initial courtship, a distortion we predict will be severely exacerbated as AI evolves into an emotional substitute. Projections indicate that this substitution effect is accelerating; without intervention, the world post 2040 risks entering an irreversible demographic contraction, as the sudden surge in TFR required for recovery is biologically impossible. Ultimately, this framework explains why traditional financial subsidies fail to reverse falling birth rates and suggests that digital convenience may represent a behavioral Great Filter that erodes the imperative for species persistence.

items.title: A dedicated survey of fast-rotating near-Earth asteroids with the Two-meter Twin Telescope. II. Tumblers
items.abstract: Fast rotation dominates the metre- to decametre-size near-Earth asteroid (NEA) population, but the incidence of non-principal-axis (NPA) rotation, or tumbling, in this regime is essentially unconstrained. We establish how common NPA rotation is among small, fast-rotating NEAs, how its prevalence varies with size, and what it implies for the internal structure and recent dynamical history of these bodies. We analysed the homogeneous high-cadence sample obtained with the Two-meter Twin Telescope at Teide Observatory and presented in the first paper of this series. Light curves showing coherent residual structure under a single-frequency Fourier model were refitted with a bivariate Fourier series in two independent frequencies, and dynamical modes were assigned from the normalised harmonic amplitude spectrum. We confirm 32 NPA rotators, 14 with both periods reliably resolved, with periods spanning 0.48-46.4 min and estimated diameters of 7-140 m. The most extreme object with both periods resolved, 2025 FB8 (shortest period $P_1 = 71$ s, estimated diameter $D \simeq 7$ m), is the fastest and smallest such tumbler characterised to date. Eight objects satisfy our harmonic quality criteria, and all eight are consistent with long-axis mode rotation. The tumbler fraction among fast rotators is 16.0 %, rising from 13.8 % at absolute magnitude $H < 26$ to 22.5 % at $H \geq 26$. Twenty-three of the 32 lie above the spin limit of a cohesionless rubble pile; none exceeds the lunar-regolith limit. Tumbling is common among small fast rotators, with no evidence that it becomes rarer towards the smallest sizes. Fast tumblers require modest cohesion but no monolithic interior, occupying the same structural domain as their principal-axis counterparts.

items.title: Cross-Stream Self-Supervised Learning Inspired by Feature-Biased Visual Processing in the Brain
items.abstract: Humans and other animals develop rich visual representations without explicit object-category labels. Self-supervised learning (SSL) offers a computational framework for studying how such representations emerge from visual experience. Many contrastive SSL models, such as SimCLR, learn by being robust to augmented views of the same image, which may fail to preserve visual attributes such as color and orientation. Inspired by feature-specific visual processing streams in the brain, we propose BioCLR, an SSL framework that uses color- and orientation-biased networks to guide representation learning. We combine BioCLR with SimCLR into a BioCLR hybrid model, pretrain it on ImageNet-100, and evaluate it on this dataset and four transfer datasets. In frozen linear evaluation, the BioCLR hybrid outperforms SimCLR across all datasets and mitigates negative transfer on a handwritten-character dataset. In limited-label fine-tuning, it outperforms SimCLR in most transfer conditions. Compared with the AugSelf and RotNet hybrids, which incorporate color and orientation information into SimCLR in other ways, the BioCLR hybrid shows the best overall performance, particularly in limited-label fine-tuning. Ablation analyses suggest that orientation guidance helps more than color guidance on these datasets, and that combining both generally improves frozen linear evaluation performance. Together, these findings suggest that incorporating feature-specific information into SSL can improve representation quality and model adaptability, and that the learning mechanism used to incorporate this information matters. For neuroscience, these results suggest that specialized visual streams in the brain may provide learning signals that guide visual representation learning without explicit supervision. For machine learning, they imply that principles of feature-biased processing in visual cortex may improve SSL.

items.title: Understanding robustness and enabling remediation of neuroimaging-based deep neural networks for digital security: Semantic segmentation of brain tumors as illustrative study
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Applications of deep learning models in neuroimaging have significantly advanced translational neuroscience, offering substantial benefits to human health. However, recent cybersecurity threats have undermined the reliability of digital neuroscience tools, posing challenges to the clinical neuroscience community. A critical issue is the automated semantic segmentation of malignant or premalignant brain tumors, essential for neurosurgery and radiotherapy planning. New methods: This study investigates the robustness of customary deep learning models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and more recent Vision Transformers (ViTs) in semantic segmentation against adversarial attacks. We assess the performance of CNNs and ViTs under ideal nonhostile conditions and then under cybersecurity threats. Results: Our findings reveal that while CNNs perform well in ideal conditions, their efficiency sharply declines under adversarial perturbations. In contrast, ViTs maintain their segmentation performance even when subjected to adversarial attacks. This study is the first to apply Visual Transformers for cybersecurity challenge, leveraging advanced capabilities of VITs to enhance robustness against digital perturbations. Comparison with existing methods: Compared to CNNs, which are widely used for neuroimages but vulnerable to adversarial attacks, ViTs demonstrate superior resilience. Our research highlights that ViTs are as effective as CNNs under ideal conditions but offer enhanced protection from cybersecurity angle, making them a more robust choice for neuroimaging applications. Conclusion: Our results indicate that for large-scale segmentation operation in neuroimaging, such as lesion segmentation tasks, ViT-based models should be preferred over CNN-based models. This shift could provide inherent protection against prevalent digital threats, ensuring more reliable and secure neuroimaging diagnostics.

items.title: Expression of human-specific SRGAP2C increases representational capacity in mice
items.abstract: The brain of modern humans has evolved remarkable computational abilities enabling higher cognitive functions. Recent progress in evolutionary genomics and experimental neuroscience has identified several human-specific genetic modifiers of brain development that underlie the emergence of human-specific traits of cortical circuit connectivity and function. The human-specific gene SRGAP2C emerged by partial duplication of the ancestral gene SRGAP2A which encodes a postsynaptic protein regulating synaptic development. SRGAP2C inhibits all known functions of SRGAP2A and its expression in mouse cortical pyramidal neurons leads to neotenic synaptic maturation, increased cortico-cortical connectivity, increased reliability of sensory coding by cortical layer 2/3 PNs, and improved learning of a sensory discrimination task. However, it remains unclear whether SRGAP2C expression in the mouse cortex is sufficient to produce changes in cognition. To test this idea, we trained adult wild-type (WT) and SRGAP2C mice on a Go-NoGo task that involves learning to associate a whisker stimulus with the presence of a water reward. SRGAP2C mice displayed a licking strategy that accelerated the learning of stimulus-reward associations at the cost of punishment timeouts compared to WT mice. The licking strategy was selective to the task, not driven by a general increase in consumptive behavior, and it accelerated the information that SRGAP2C mice gathered in early learning. SRGAP2C mice also displayed more structured behavior later in training and were, overall, better information channels than their WT counterparts. A computational model confirmed that SRGAP2C mice learning strategy increases representational capacity. Our results reveal that expression of human-specific gene SRGAP2C in cortical circuits is sufficient to increase the cognitive abilities of mice by optimizing the use sensory information to guide action. The human-specific gene SRGAP2C might have contributed to the emergence of distinct functional cortical circuit features underlying our unique learning abilities and flexible decision-making.

items.title: Covert control over the real-time dynamics of human interactions with Ducksoup
items.abstract: Uncovering how facial and vocal signals shape social interactions is difficult because researcherscannot control how humans behave during free conversations. Here we demonstrate that recentadvances in AI-based transformation filters enable researchers to have covert experimental controlover the real-time dynamics of social interactions. We introduce Ducksoup, a scientificvideoconference platform that allows researchers to collect social interaction experiments online,realistically transform participants' faces and voices in real time mid-conversation, record thesynchronized interactions and extract multimodal time series from recordings for analysis. In apreregistered experiment (N = 64 participants), we replicate recent laboratory findings in a fullyonline setup: artificially aligning participants’ smiles increased mutual enjoyment while remainingundetected. The paradigm also revealed feedback effects on participants’ spontaneous facial, vocaland verbal behavior. By combining the ecological validity of free interactions with experimentalcontrol and scalable data collection, Ducksoup turns natural conversations into a causalexperimental paradigm for psychology and neuroscience.

items.title: Ocular Metrics for Fatigue Assessment: A Survey from Physiology to Machine Learning
items.abstract: Abstract Fatigue is pervasive and safety-critical, yet objective biomarkers remain limited, resulting in a gap between subjective reports and clinical decision-making. The eye provides a non-invasive readout of central nervous system function: changes in eyelid behaviour, eye movements, and pupillary dynamics track arousal, executive control, and visual strain. This PRISMA-guided, PROSPERO-registered review integrates work in medicine, psychology, and neuroscience with computational methods to map ocular biomarkers to fatigue phenotypes and their detection pipelines. We synthesize evidence linking eyelid metrics, saccadic and pursuit dynamics, fixational stability, and pupillometry to drowsiness, cognitive/mental fatigue, visual fatigue, and clinical fatigue states, then trace how computer vision and machine learning operationalize these signals. A dominant literature focus on driver drowsiness emerges: eyelid-based indicators are mature and robust, with metrics like increased blink duration and a higher Percentage of Eye Closure (PERCLOS) strongly correlating with performance lapses and microsleeps, while cognitive, visual, and clinical fatigue remain comparatively under-explored in computer science despite richer treatment in clinical domains. Methodologically, the field is shifting from feature engineering to end-to-end and sequence-aware models, but progress is constrained by heterogeneous ground truth labels, scarce public benchmarks, and lab-to-wild generalization gaps. We conclude with a roadmap advocating multimodal, privacy-preserving systems; standardized, phenotype-aware benchmarks; and validation that combines behavioural performance, physiology, and self-report, to enable holistic, ethically grounded fatigue monitoring beyond driving scenarios.

items.title: Motor neuron disease due to a novel PIK3R1 mutation.
items.abstract: Mutations in PIK3R1, which encodes the regulatory subunit (p85α) of class I phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K), are associated with immunologic and developmental disorders, but their effects on the nervous system have not been studied. We identified a novel heterozygous frameshift mutation (PIK3R1 c.1710dup) in a patient with common variable immunodeficiency who developed adult-onset, slowly progressive ALS-like motor-neuron disease. Studies of patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) demonstrated PIK3R1 haploinsufficiency with selective AKT activation. Investigation of patient's iPSC-derived motor neurons (iMNs) showed reduced neuronal electrical activity, and markedly increased apoptosis. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed coordinated up-regulation of differentiation and apoptosis programs across neuronal and glial clusters. Engineering the PIK3R1 c.1710dup mutation into healthy-control iPSCs reproduced the impaired electrical activity, increased apoptosis, and transcriptional vulnerability, confirming the variant's cell-intrinsic pathogenicity. In contrast, introduction of canonical APDS2-associated PIK3R1 splice mutations into the same genetic background did not produce these abnormalities, establishing a variant-class-specific mechanism of PI3K dysfunction. Together, these findings define PIK3R1 c.1710dup as a distinct pathogenic variant that links PI3K-pathway dysregulation to human motor-neuron degeneration and expands the mechanistic spectrum of PIK3R1-associated disease.

items.title: Smoking Very Low Nicotine Content Cigarettes Produces Measurable Cardiovascular and Autonomic Effects: Evidence Informing FDA-Proposed Reduced Nicotine Standard.
items.abstract: Introduction The FDA proposed limiting nicotine in combustible cigarettes to ≤ 0.70 mg/g to reduce addictiveness. The tobacco industry has argued that such standards would render cigarettes functionally zero nicotine products, an interpretation industry contends exceeds the FDA's statutory authority. This study addresses this argument by extending existing evidence. It examined whether puffing a 0.4 mg/g very low nicotine content (VLNC) cigarette produced autonomic and cardiovascular responses distinct from a nicotine- and tobacco-free cigarette substitute (CS). Methods Twenty-four adults who smoke took 8 puffs from a CS followed by a 0.4 mg/g cigarette. ECG (heart rate, RMSSD), the time-varying electrodermal activity index (TVSymp), and arterial stiffness (pulse wave velocity [PWV]) were recorded across pre-puffing, puffing, and post-puffing periods. Results Change scores from their respective pre-puffing (Δ) indicated that heart rate increased during puffing (Δ = 3.64 ± 4.26 bpm) and post-puffing (Δ = 2.66 ± 2.80 bpm; Ps Conclusions Smoking 0.4 mg/g cigarette produced measurable autonomic and cardiovascular effects. These findings inform ongoing regulatory discussions and indicate that VLNC cigarettes are not functionally equivalent to "zero nicotine" products.

items.title: The Role of Affective Traits and Social Cognition in Envy and Schadenfreude.
items.abstract: Complex social emotions like envy and Schadenfreude challenge traditional models of social cognition by revealing how affective traits interact with cognitive processes to shape counter-empathic responses. Although theoretically linked to empathy and theory of mind (ToM), their associations with traits like alexithymia and anhedonia remain underexplored. This study tested a structural model connecting affective traits (alexithymia, anhedonia), social cognition (ToM, empathy), and social emotions (envy, Schadenfreude ) in 125 healthy adults using validated measures and structural equation modeling. Results showed that alexithymia indirectly influenced empathy and envy via reduced ToM, while empathy did not directly predict these emotions. Alexithymia correlated positively with anhedonia and negatively with ToM. Anhedonia predicted lower empathy. Envy strongly predicted Schadenfreude , underscoring the role of upward social comparison. Findings suggest that these emotions arise from distinct affective and cognitive mechanisms, offering a novel framework for understanding socio-emotional functioning in both healthy and clinical populations.

items.title: Sildenafil for Fetal Growth Restriction - An Individual Participant Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Background Phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors have been investigated as an in utero therapy for fetal growth restriction (FGR). Methods We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomized trials of phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors versus placebo/no treatment in singleton pregnancies with FGR. The primary outcome was infant survival without serious adverse outcome. Secondary outcomes included gestation at birth and birth weight z score among liveborn infants. Predefined subgroups were evaluated. Results Of 19 eligible trials, 4 contributed data. Of 492 participants, 240 had been assigned to placebo and 252 to the phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitor sildenafil. Infant survival without serious adverse outcome occurred in 110 of 240 participants (45.8%) assigned to placebo versus 113 of 252 participants (44.8%) assigned to sildenafil (relative risk [RR], 0.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78 to 1.17). No apparent interaction was observed between subgroups. There was no apparent difference in gestation at birth (mean difference -0.5 weeks; 95% CI, -1.3 to 0.2) or birth weight z score (mean difference, 0.0; 95% CI, -0.2 to 0.2). Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn occurred in 10 of 176 participants (5.7%) assigned to placebo versus 27 of 197 participants (13.7%) assigned to sildenafil (RR, 2.39; 95% CI, 1.23 to 4.61); nitric oxide was used in 15 of 176 participants (8.5%) assigned to placebo versus 20 of 197 participants (10.2%) assigned to sildenafil (RR, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.64 to 2.29). Conclusions Maternal sildenafil therapy for FGR was not associated with improved outcomes for infants. It was associated with persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn but not with an increase in nitric oxide therapy. items.title: A Phase 2 Study of Imlifidase in the Treatment of Guillain-Barré Syndrome.
items.abstract: Background Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS), a life-threatening neuropathy, results in prolonged disability despite standard-of-care treatment. Imlifidase specifically cleaves immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies and may benefit patients with GBS by rapidly depleting pathologic IgG autoantibodies, resulting in less severe disease and faster recovery. Methods This open-label, single-arm, multicenter, phase 2 study enrolled adults with severe GBS (i.e., GBS disability scale [GBS-DS] grades ranging from 3 to 5; GBS-DS grades range from 0 to 6, with higher numbers indicating more severe disability). It investigated safety, adverse event profile, efficacy, pharmacodynamics, and pharmacokinetics of one dose of imlifidase within 12 days of symptom onset followed by standard-dose intravenous immune globulin (IVIG). Twenty-seven participants with confirmed GBS were assessed by using standard GBS outcome measures, including GBS-DS and the Medical Research Council sum score (scores range from 0 to 60, with a lower score indicting more severe weakness). Results Median (95% confidence interval) time to improve at least one GBS-DS grade was 6 (3.0 to 16.0) days, and time to independent walking was 16 (4.0 to 92.0) days. Within 1 week, 37% of patients were able to walk independently, and the mean improvement in the Medical Research Council sum score was 10.7 points. Twenty-five participants (83%) experienced at least one treatment-emergent adverse event. Most were grade 1 (mild) or grade 2 (moderate). Five were assessed as being grade 3 (severe) and two events as being grade 4 (life-threatening or disabling intensity), including one death. Conclusions A single dose of imlifidase followed by IVIG in participants with severe GBS was associated with rapid functional improvements. These results support a randomized controlled trial to further investigate IgG-depleting strategies in GBS. (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03943589.).

items.title: Patient-reported outcomes after orthopaedic surgery: Addressing non-response, missing data and selection bias.
items.abstract: Patient-reported outcome measures inform evaluation after orthopaedic surgery, but favourable scores among responders may not reflect outcomes across the entire treated cohort. Non-response, meaning failure to provide requested outcome data, can affect estimates of improvement, procedure comparisons and registry benchmarking. Drawing on examples from anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction and knee arthroplasty, this editorial distinguishes missing item responses, missing assessments and incomplete baseline-follow-up pairs. Neither response rates, observed similarities nor statistical adjustments guarantee the absence of non-response bias. Priorities include reporting assessment-specific and paired-analysis denominators, comparing available characteristics of responders and non-responders, documenting reasons for missingness and explaining analytical assumptions. Sensitivity analyses should examine whether clinically plausible assumptions about missing outcomes alter or limit clinical conclusions; reassurance is limited to the scenarios examined. Accessible collection methods and proportionate questionnaire burden may support participation. Conclusions should reflect the population represented, analytical assumptions and remaining uncertainty about the wider treated cohort.

items.title: Differential impact of dynein pathogenic variants on mitotic spindle organization and cortical organoid growth.
items.abstract: Mutations in the dynein heavy chain gene (DYNC1H1) cause a spectrum of neurological disorders, including malformations of cortical development (MCD) and spinal muscular atrophy with lower extremity predominance (SMALED). How these mutations differentially affect dynein functions in the nervous system, leading to distinct pathologies, remains unknown. Using patient-derived cortical organoids, we address how MCD- and SMALED-causing dynein mutations alter human cortical development. We show that MCD-associated mutations alter the growth of organoids, but that SMALED organoids are unaffected, consistent with the microcephaly phenotypes of individuals with MCD. These defects are mirrored by a large increase in apoptotic cell death in MCD organoids. MCD mutations - but not SMALED mutations - strongly affect radial glial progenitor divisions, by inducing severe mitotic spindle defects and leading to prolonged mitotic duration. Mitotic checkpoint inhibition alleviates mitotic delay but fails to prevent apoptosis, indicating that mitotic arrest is not the cause of cell death in MCD. These findings reveal how specific dynein mutations can distinctly disrupt cortical development, establishing mitotic spindle dysfunction and apoptosis as central mechanisms underlying dynein-related microcephaly.

items.title: Compensatory Trunk Neuromuscular Control During Early Rehabilitation After Motor Incomplete Spinal Cord Injury.
items.abstract: Background Motor incomplete spinal cord injury (SCI) reduces trunk control and limits function of the limbs, yet mechanisms underlying trunk neuromuscular recovery remain unclear. This observational study investigated changes in trunk motor control in individuals with recent motor incomplete cervical or thoracic SCI. Methods Thirty-six participants with SCI and 20 controls were recruited from hospitals and the community, respectively. All participants with SCI received tailored inpatient rehabilitation and were assessed at baseline and 4 weeks later. Participants performed trunk goal-directed tasks: forward and lateral reaches, and postural tasks: bilateral shoulder flexion at comfortable and rapid speeds, while we recorded lumbar erector spinae (ES) muscle activity using high-density surface electromyography (HDsEMG) and trunk and upper-limb movement with 2D video. The American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale (AIS) total motor scores were also collected. Results Lumbar ES EMG activity was lower in participants with SCI than in controls. In SCI, ES activation was more caudal during shoulder flexion than forward reaching, while controls showed consistent patterns across tasks. After 4 weeks of rehabilitation, participants with SCI significantly improved motor scores, forward reaching distance, and trunk displacement. Participants with AIS C exhibited a progressive caudal shift in ES activation over time, while those with AIS D showed a stable activation pattern. Conclusions These findings indicate that improvements in trunk function after SCI may arise through different neuromuscular strategies depending on injury severity. Incorporating additional trunk-focused kinematics and HDsEMG measurements may help to detect these compensatory patterns early, guiding interventions that balance compensation with strategies that promote more optimal trunk control.

items.title: Applying functional MRI analysis techniques to whole-brain calcium-imaging data to investigate structural and functional relationships in Drosophila melanogaster.
items.abstract: Clarifying the relationship between structure and function is important for understanding the brain. In Drosophila melanogaster , FlyEM and FlyWire electron microscopy-based connectome data, and whole-brain calcium-imaging data are available. We applied pre-processing methods from functional magnetic resonance imaging to whole-brain calcium-imaging data and comprehensively investigated the optimal parameters. Then, we found that the FC-SC (functional and structural connectivity) correlation decreased linearly with region of interest count, and this trend was the same in flies and humans. We also developed a new, more robust method to quantify the degree of pre- and post-synaptic segregation, and investigated this in the fly whole-brain. This revealed that many neurons have unsegregated synapses. We extracted highly unsegregated synapses and compared them with random-extracted null SC matrices. Their FC-SC correlation was significantly higher, indicating that these synapses contribute to FC well. Conversely, highly segregated synapses showed significantly lower FC-SC correlation and contribute less to FC. Neurons with unsegregated synapses, like non-spiking neurons, are spread throughout the whole-brain, and they are thought to have a significant influence on FC.

items.title: AI-Driven Intelligent ECM-Mimetic Hydrogel Scaffolds for Brain Organoid Engineering.
items.abstract: Brain organoids are increasingly used for scalable modeling of human neurodevelopment and disease, but their reproducibility and translational value remain limited by reliance on ill-defined matrices such as Matrigel. Although Matrigel provides several brain-relevant features, including soft, viscoelastic, and non-fibrillar properties, its composition is poorly defined, batch-variable, and difficult to tune in a standardized manner. Considering the physicochemical characteristics of the native brain extracellular matrix (ECM), brain organoid culture requires ECM-like materials that reproduce brain-specific mechanical, transport, and signaling cues rather than merely providing 3D support. This review presents a rational framework for engineering intelligent ECM-mimetic hydrogel scaffolds for advanced brain organoid culture. It summarizes key features of the native brain ECM and introduces material rationality as the systematic selection and engineering of hydrogels according to brain-specific biological, physical, and translational design requirements. The review also highlights how artificial intelligence (AI) can navigate high-dimensional material design spaces through surrogate modeling, digital twins, and closed-loop optimization informed by multi-physics and multi-omics feedback. Ultimately, AI-driven scaffold design may enable more reproducible, mature, and scalable brain organoid models.

items.title: Accuracy and Difficulty of the Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test Across Racial Groups.
items.abstract: Prior research has identified racial group differences in performance on social cognitive tasks related to emotion recognition. Little work has examined racial group differences within the Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test (RMET), a task designed to assess theory of mind, particularly among American samples. Further, our understanding of participants' perceived ease of the task and its association with performance on social cognition tasks is lacking. This study sought to fill this gap using two university samples. In sample 1, undergraduates ( n = 1,494) provided data including the RMET and demographic information. In sample 2, undergraduates ( n = 189) completed the RMET with additional questions assessing perceived ease of RMET items, as well as demographic information. Participants identifying as White, Asian, or an other race performed significantly better on the RMET than Black participants. No significant differences were found between racial minority and White participants on perceived ease of the RMET. Race did not significantly moderate associations between perceived ease and performance. This study adds to the growing body of evidence suggesting that diverse samples may exhibit racial differences in performance on the RMET. Additional work should clarify whether discrepancies in perceived and objective social cognition performance vary by racial groups.

items.title: Estradiol and working memory: Further evidence for the role of dopamine and COMT gene polymorphism over the menstrual cycle.
items.abstract: Background The hormone 17β-estradiol is the dominant form of estrogen in women of reproductive age. Some past work suggests that estradiol may influence women's performance on working memory (WM) tasks that have high executive demands. However, evidence is limited, and the cellular mechanisms that underlie any such effects are largely unknown. Methods and aims Here we used a prospective repeated-measures crossover design to evaluate whether natural variation in estradiol availability over the female ovarian cycle is associated with discernible variations in performance on three neuropsychological tests of WM function. Performance was evaluated during the early follicular phase (low estradiol) and midluteal phase of the cycle (high estradiol). Based on the hypothesis that estradiol-driven variations in dopamine (DA) activity may underlie the effects, we used genotyping to characterize a common allelic variant in the catechol- O -methyltransferase gene ( COMT Val 158 Met) and the dopamine transporter ( DAT1 3'-VNTR). Results Our results showed that menstrual cycle-dependent variation in accuracy was present on all 3 WM tasks, with a medium to large effect size. A significant interaction between high estradiol and COMT genotype was found for Digit Randomization and Spatial Working Memory tests, but no interaction was found on a Self-Ordered Pointing test. In contrast, women's DAT1 genotype moderated the effect of high estradiol on self-ordered pointing. WM accuracy was correlated in a graded manner with the magnitude of the rise in estradiol during the high-estrogen phase. Conclusions We conclude that brain dopamine activity likely mediates, in part, the impact of 17β-estradiol on WM performance.

items.title: Predictors of Recovery From Aphasia After Stroke.
items.abstract: Predicting recovery from aphasia after stroke is challenging, yet essential. Accurate prognoses would enable stroke survivors and families to establish realistic expectations and make informed decisions, allow clinicians to plan rehabilitation, and inform the development and implementation of interventions. This review synthesizes current evidence on predictors of aphasia recovery, integrating diverse biological, behavioral, environmental, and temporal determinants into a unified conceptual framework organized around 3 fundamental determinants: the integrity of the language network, neuroplasticity throughout the remaining brain, and the passage of time. Lesion location and extent are powerful predictors, accounting for more than half of the variance in aphasia outcomes, but other interacting factors contribute to heterogeneous recovery trajectories, including variability in language network organization and effects of diaschisis. The capacity for neuroplasticity depends on the brain health and functionality of surviving tissue, but the realization of this potential depends critically on engagement in language use, which can be promoted by intensive speech-language therapy, social participation and supportive communication environments. Recovery follows a predictable decelerating time course, with rapid early gains driven primarily by reperfusion and resolution of dysfunction in brain regions that support language, and modest but meaningful longer-term improvements deriving from neuroplastic changes. This framework provides a practical heuristic for understanding aphasia recovery, developing clinical prediction tools, and identifying modifiable factors to optimize outcomes.

items.title: Consensus-Based Diagnostic Criteria for Parsonage-Turner Syndrome/Neuralgic Amyotrophy: A Modified Delphi Study.
items.abstract: Introduction/aims Parsonage-Turner syndrome (PTS), also known as neuralgic amyotrophy (NA), is an acute-onset peripheral neuropathy predominately affecting the upper extremity and causing substantial pain and disability. No formal international consensus-based diagnostic criteria exist, contributing to diagnostic delays, inconsistent terminology, and limited ability to collate and systematically analyze data. This study aimed to develop consensus-based diagnostic criteria and a diagnostic algorithm for PTS/NA. Methods A modified Delphi study was conducted with an international, multidisciplinary panel of experts selected based on clinical and research experience with PTS/NA. A steering committee drafted preliminary statements informed by a literature review and panelist-derived diagnostic challenges across 9 domains. Two electronic survey rounds used Likert-scale and binary response formats, with consensus defined as ≥ 75% agreement or disagreement. Results All 13 panelists completed both rounds (100% response rate). Of 86 items, 52 (60%) reached agreement. The panel endorsed "Parsonage-Turner syndrome" and "neuralgic amyotrophy" as interchangeable terms. Classic PTS/NA was defined by acute-onset severe pain (≥ 7/10) and severe weakness in a non-myotomal distribution. Non-classic presentations warranted confirmatory electrodiagnostic testing and/or nerve-focused imaging. Hourglass-like nerve constrictions were considered likely pathognomonic (100% agreement). If steroids were considered, early initiation was recommended in classic presentations, even before confirmatory testing. Discussion These criteria may shorten time to diagnosis, standardize terminology, guide resource utilization, and facilitate clinical trials. Future research should prioritize validation of the criteria in patient cohorts.

items.title: FOXM1-induced TRIM9 inhibits neutrophil extracellular traps formation to attenuate cerebral I/R injury via STING/AMPK axis.
items.abstract: Background Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major challenge in stroke management, with neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) playing a key role in exacerbating damage. This study aimed to elucidate the function and mechanism of FOXM1 in cerebral I/R injury. Methods A mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in bEnd.3 endothelial cells were established. NETs formation was assessed by detecting MPO-DNA complexes, H3Cit, and neutrophil elastase. Inflammatory cytokines were evaluated using RT-qPCR, and protein stability was assessed by cycloheximide chase assay. Molecular interactions were examined using chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP), co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and dual luciferase reporter assay. Results FOXM1 was downregulated following I/R. FOXM1 overexpression reduced infarct volume, edema, and NETs formation in MCAO mice. In vitro , FOXM1 upregulation attenuated endothelial injury in OGD/R-stimulated bEnd.3 cells and decreased the release of NETs markers. Mechanistically, FOXM1 directly bound to the promoter of TRIM9 and activated its transcription. TRIM9 subsequently promoted K48-linked ubiquitination and degradation of HMGB1, thereby influencing STING/AMPK signaling and reducing NETs formation. Knockdown of either TRIM9 or FOXM1 partially reversed the effects of HMGB1 depletion on NETs formation. Conclusion FOXM1 overexpression ameliorated cerebral I/R injury by enhancing TRIM9 expression, which suppressed NETs formation through HMGB1-modulated STING/AMPK signaling.

items.title: Hyperactivity of the posterior cingulate cortex during interpreting communicative intentions based on the speaker-listener relationship in autism spectrum disorder.
items.abstract: Speakers' intended meanings are often inferred from extra-linguistic social factors such as the speaker-listener relationship, yet how individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) incorporate such relational cues remains unclear. Using fMRI, we investigated whether and how individuals with autism utilize speaker-listener relationship cues to interpret communicative intentions. Twenty adults with ASD and 20 matched typically developed (TD) controls completed a discourse comprehension task where the interpretation of a target remark depended on the speaker-listener relationship or not. Behaviorally, both groups showed faster reactions in the social factor condition, indicating that the social context facilitated their responses. However, the ASD group was less accurate overall. Across the groups, core discourse regions, including the medial prefrontal cortex and inferior frontal gyrus, were engaged. Critically, ASD participants exhibited increased activation in the posterior cingulate cortex (PCC), whereas TD participants showed PCC deactivation. Functional connectivity analyses further indicated reduced PCC connectivity with the left angular gyrus and right fusiform gyrus in ASD compared with TD. These findings suggest that, despite broadly comparable task engagement, individuals with ASD rely on different PCC-centered neural mechanisms when integrating speaker-listener relationship information to infer communicative intentions.

items.title: The electrochemical physiology of organelles.
items.abstract: Membrane-bound organelles maintain distinct chemical environments that are essential for their specialized functions. Yet, while organelle morphology, protein composition and dynamics have been extensively characterized, very little was known about their lumenal microenvironment prior to work from our laboratory. Here, we chart the development of a chemical imaging approach that enabled the measurement of ions, reactive species and membrane potential within native organelles in living cells and organisms. These measurements reveal that organelles maintain characteristic ionic and electrical states, that populations of even a specific type of organelle can be chemically heterogeneous, and that lumenal ion levels change during organelle maturation or physiological events. Beyond simply defining the ionic milieu of organelle lumens, quantitative ion imaging revealed new ion transport mechanisms, demonstrated that cell surface ion channels are active in organelles, mapped reactive-species production at subcellular spatial resolution and linked organelle physiology to disease states and cellular behavior. Together, these findings reveal that organelles have electroal behaviour because they harbor transmembrane ion gradients, ion transporting proteins, and membrane potential. We discuss how this emerging view may illuminate inside-out signaling across organelle membranes and outline the technological advances required to move from static chemical maps toward real-time, single-organelle physiology in living systems.

items.title: Multivariate searchlight decoding of structural disconnection and network features for predicting post-stroke deficits.
items.abstract: Objective. Lesion-symptom mapping and structural disconnection analyses have advanced our understanding of post-stroke deficits but remain predominantly based on forward inference, limiting identification of regions specifically predictive of behavioral impairment. We developed a multivariate voxelwise searchlight decoding framework for inverse inference integrating probabilistic structural disconnection with network-topological features. Approach. The analysis included 326 stroke patients from the GRECogVASC cohort assessed six months after stroke. For each patient, an age-specific probabilistic structural disconnection map was reconstructed using normative diffusion MRI tractography from 403 healthy controls. Within each voxel-centered searchlight, four features were extracted: disconnection probability, degree, clustering coefficient, and closeness centrality. Support vector machine classifiers were trained within deficit-specific decoding spaces using balanced bootstrap aggregation and majority voting to predict motor, executive, and processing-action-speed impairments. Statistical significance was assessed using 1000 permutations, retaining voxels that consistently performed above chance across bootstrap iterations. Decoding-derived regions were subsequently assessed for within-cohort individual-level classification. Main results. Initial validation focused on left and right motor impairments, identifying predictive regions primarily within the contralateral precentral gyrus, internal capsule, and corticospinal tract, with mean accuracy ranges of 68.7%-77.9%, 66.4%-74.6%, and 64.8%-71.8%, respectively. At the individual level, decoding-derived masks preserved overall classification performance, with accuracy improvements of up to 2.6% for individual deficits while reducing voxel dimensionality by up to 95.4%. Executive dysfunction and processing-action-speed deficits showed statistically above-chance but lower accuracies (54.5%-66.9%). Executive dysfunction involved predominantly left-lateralized frontotemporal regions, whereas processing-action-speed deficits involved distributed fronto-insular, temporal, parietal, visual-association, and commissural pathways. Significance. The multivariate searchlight decoding framework integrating structural disconnection and network topology provides an inverse-inference approach complementary to lesion- and disconnection-symptom mapping for identifying spatially specific predictive patterns after stroke. The strong motor findings provide proof-of-concept support for the approach, whereas the cognitive results support its extension to distributed behavioral domains while underscoring the need for independent replication before neuroanatomical or clinical interpretation (Clinical trial registration: NCT01339195).

items.title: Role-Aware Line-Graph Neural Networks for Interpretable Prediction of Pairwise Microbial Interactions
items.abstract: Predicting how microbial species affect each other's growth is a key challenge in microbial ecology. Using one of the largest available pairwise interaction datasets, comprising 20 soil bacteria co-cultured under 39 carbon conditions (15{,}074 directional measurements), we predicted whether one species has a positive or negative effect on the growth of another from monoculture growth, metabolic profiles, and phylogeny. Existing machine learning approaches treat each measurement as an independent sample, although experiments that share a species under the same condition are biologically related. We therefore represented the data as a role-aware line graph: each node is one directional measurement, and two nodes are connected when, under the same carbon condition, they share the same effector or the same affected species. This allows graph neural networks (GNNs) to pass information between related interactions. Our role-aware GAT-SAGE model achieved an F1-score of 81.38% for one-way prediction, outperforming the 73.79% previously reported for Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). For two-way interaction types (mutualism, competition, and parasitism), GAT-SAGE reached a macro F1-score of 60.34%. This exceeded the 55.71% of a neural network without graph structure but was below the 64.24% of XGBoost. Mutualism remained difficult to predict for all models. Layer-wise relevance propagation showed that one-way effects depend mainly on monoculture growth, whereas two-way interaction types depend more on the carbon environment. Encoding the dependency structure of interaction experiments thus adds information beyond the features of each measurement and provides interpretable insight into microbial interactions.

items.title: The blue dragon nudibranch (Glaucus atlanticus) shifts to less venomous prey in the Mediterranean, with no evidence of defensive microbial symbionts
items.abstract: Glaucus atlanticus ("blue dragon"), is an aeolid nudibranch that acquires chemical defense through sequestration of nematocysts from its primary prey, the highly venomous Physalia physalis ("Portuguese man-of-war"). In August 2025 hundreds of G. atlanticus individuals appeared near Alicante (Spain), prompting temporary beach closures due to concerns about potential envenomation. This unusual occurrence, in a region where P. physalis is typically absent, raises questions about the trophic ecology and defensive strategies of this species under novel environmental conditions. Here, we used COI metabarcoding of gut to characterize the diet of G. atlanticus and combined it with 16S rRNA gene sequencing of cerata, gut, mucus, and central dorsal epidermis to assess potential microbial transfer from alternative prey that could contribute to the synthesis of defensive compounds, given that the role of microbes in chemical defense of aeolid nudibranchs was not assessed previously. We detected a trophic shift toward alternative cnidarian prey, including Pelagia noctiluca and Porpita porpita, which are not considered highly hazardous. Microbiome comparisons with P. porpita, as well as comparison of core microbiomes across different body parts of G. atlanticus, revealed no evidence of prey-derived transfer of mutualistic bacteria. Instead, G. atlanticus harbored distinct microbial communities dominated by environmentally widespread taxa, including potential opportunistic pathogens, with no indication of symbionts associated with defensive functions. Altogether, these findings indicate that, despite trophic flexibility, G. atlanticus may have limited capacity to maintain its defensive mechanisms in the absence of its primary prey.

items.title: How is human well-being shaped? A global cross-national empirical analysis from the sustainable-development-system perspective
items.abstract: Abstract Sustainable development is a complex coupled system of ecology, technology, institutions and human well-being. Clarifying the synergistic mechanisms of multiple factors is key to advancing the global sustainability transition. Existing sustainable development frameworks mostly focus on the enumeration of development goals, lacking a systematic deconstruction of the logical hierarchy, transmission pathways and conditional dependencies among factors, which makes it difficult to explain the marked divergence in sustainability outcomes across countries. To this end, this paper constructs a logical analytical framework for a human-well-being-oriented sustainable development system, selects proxy indicators, and quantitatively examines the empirical associations between core factors and human well-being, together with their country-specific differentiated characteristics. The core scientific contributions of this study are twofold: at the theoretical level, it reconstructs the hierarchical logical system of sustainable development factors, proposes a logical transmission chain linking natural capital, technological capacity and institutional equity to human well-being, and establishes a systematic analytical paradigm of “base constraints–instrumental conditions–institutional adjustment–ultimate goal”; at the empirical level, it identifies the comprehensive patterns of association between core factors and human well-being, as well as cross-country heterogeneity.The study provides a theoretical analytical framework and cross-national empirical support for countries at different development stages to advance well-being-oriented sustainable development and improve the global sustainable development governance system.

items.title: Tracing Invisible Tracks: Spatial Ecology and Activity Patterns of the Neotropical Rattlesnake Crotalus simus (Serpentes: Viperidae)
items.abstract: Abstract Background Spatial ecology provides valuable insights into animal natural history, behaviour, and conservation. Radiotelemetry is one of the few techniques available to monitor snakes over extended periods. However, most research has focused on a few species from temperate regions, leaving a significant gap in our understanding of tropical snake spatial ecology and translocation effectiveness. We studied the tropical rattlesnake Crotalus simus , taking advantage of the extensive spatial ecology research available for the genus. Specifically, we determined (1) spatial ecology patterns, (2) environmental influences on activity and shelter use, and (3) translocation effects. Methods We used radiotelemetry to track 14 Mesoamerican rattlesnakes ( C. simus ), five residents and nine translocated, for over two years in northwestern Costa Rica. We estimated home ranges using minimum convex polygons (MCP), kernel density estimators (KDE and aKDE), and dynamic Brownian bridge movement models (dBBMM), and assessed movement and activity patterns. We compared spatial-use parameters between resident and translocated individuals. Results The dBBMM provided the most suitable home-range estimates, averaging 10.31 ± 4.14 ha, with core areas of 1.82 ± 0.69 ha. Mean daily movement was 14.49 ± 2.15 m. Greater moon visibility and lower humidity were associated with longer displacements, whereas movement probability increased with temperature and humidity. Snakes exhibited predominantly nocturnal sit-and-wait behaviour, remaining inactive during the day and ambushing prey at night. Shelter use was also diel-dependent, with snakes more often sheltered during the day and unsheltered at night. Temperature and habitat features, including canopy cover, understory complexity, and proximity to fallen logs, were associated with activity and shelter use. Translocated individuals were less likely to move than residents, but no differences were detected in other spatial-use parameters. Conclusions Our findings provide new insights into the spatial ecology of C. simus in tropical forests. Although translocated snakes were less likely to move, translocation had no detectable effect on home-range size or other spatial-use parameters, and recorded mortalities were similar between groups. In Costa Rica, translocation may therefore represent a viable management alternative to sacrificing snakes in human–snake conflict situations.

items.title: Impact of Drought on the Population Dynamics of the Grey-Backed Camaroptera Camaroptera brachyura
items.abstract: Little is known about population densities and population dynamics in passerine Afrotropical birds, although these are vital data in ecology and conservation of any avian species. The population density of the Grey-backed Camaroptera was assessed by means of the territory mapping method in a plot (400 ha) composed of man-modified acacia savanna. The plot is situated in Ogongo, Omusati Region, north-central Namibia. The density was much the same in 2012 and 2017 (2.3 and 2.5 p./100 ha respectively). However, after a prolonged drought in 2018-2019, the birds were still absent in October/November 2019; in February/March 2020, only two territo-ries were located; but in April the population density has already reached a level from 2017; in the subsequent months (May/June) the population density has increased by 100%, i.e. 4.3 pairs/100 ha. Most territories were established in a close proximity to ar-tificial water bodies surrounded usually by luxuriant vegetation. Low site tenacity has been evidenced. Ogongo stands therefore prominently as the only known site in the north-central Namibia (Ovamboland) where the species developed a viable population. The highest population density of the species (13.0 pairs / 100 ha) in Namibia was rec-orded in urbanised habitat of Katima Mulilo.

items.title: Genomic analysis of Klebsiella pneumoniae bloodstream isolates reveals rare hypervirulence, no convergence with antimicrobial resistance, and a blaSHV promoter variant associated with elevated cefiderocol MICs at a German university hospital.
items.abstract: Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKp) and the convergence of hypervirulence with antimicrobial resistance have raised concern worldwide, but contemporary, prospective data from Central Europe remain limited. We characterized K. pneumoniae bloodstream isolates from a German university hospital, focusing on hypervirulence and antimicrobial resistance. Bloodstream isolates were collected at University Medical Center of Schleswig-Holstein, Lübeck, Germany, between May and December 2023. In total, 74 K. pneumoniae were genotyped using whole-genome sequencing. Genomic virulence and resistance determinants were characterized with Kleborate and Russo criterion. A core-genome phylogeny was reconstructed. Hypervirulence was assessed genotypically and phenotypically using string test, in vitro growth kinetics, and the Galleria mellonella killing assay. Findings were compared against 5,514 publicly available bloodstream-derived genomes. Genomically predicted hvKp were rare (2/74 by Kleborate; 1/74 by Russo) and belonged to the classical high-risk clones ST23 and ST380, neither of which carried acquired resistance genes. Eleven isolates were resistant to third-generation cephalosporins (nine bla CTX-M-15 , two bla CTX-M-14 ), and two were carbapenem-resistant through bla OXA-48 . Three isolates carried a C-112A bla SHV promoter mutation associated with elevated cefiderocol MICs (0.5-4 mg/L). Neither growth kinetics nor G. mellonella killing distinguished the two hypervirulent isolates from non-hypervirulent. In the public data set, the overall hvKp prevalence was low, with no significant increase between 2012 and 2025. In this cohort, hypervirulent K. pneumoniae was rare and showed no convergence with acquired resistance. These findings suggest that convergent MDR-hvKp lineages remain uncommon and support the continued use of genomic surveillance to detect their possible future emergence. Importance Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKp) has emerged as a major public health concern because it causes more invasive and often more severe infections than classical K. pneumoniae , and its convergence with antimicrobial resistance could further limit treatment options. However, prospective data on the prevalence of hvKp specifically from bloodstream infections remain scarce, particularly in Europe. By combining genomic analysis of a prospective bloodstream-infection cohort with more than 5,500 publicly available genomes, we show that hypervirulent strains remain uncommon and that convergence with acquired antimicrobial resistance is still rare in this setting. These findings provide an important baseline for ongoing genomic surveillance of hvKp. In addition, the same surveillance approach also flagged a previously reported bla SHV promoter variant associated with elevated cefiderocol MICs, indicating a potential emerging mechanism that warrants further investigation as cefiderocol use becomes more widespread.

items.title: Should I stay or should I go: Hypoxia thresholds of the three-spined stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus).
items.abstract: We established hypoxia avoidance thresholds of three-spined stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus) using a customized choice-flume system. Stickleback is an opportunistic species, increasing in abundance in several aquatic systems. We show that sticklebacks avoid oxygen levels commonly reported in many coastal areas. When prey was available in severe hypoxia (10% O 2 sat), fish still spent 50.9% of the 30-min feeding period in the hypoxic side, compared with 78.5% in the prey side under normoxia. These findings provide a prey-dependent estimate of hypoxia sensitivity in an abundant northern-temperate coastal fish and highlight the need to test whether laboratory thresholds predict field distributions.

items.title: Ecological Resilience and Microbial Dysbiosis in the Oral Microbiome: A Systems-Level Conceptual Framework.
items.abstract: The human oral microbiome is a highly organised, dynamic microbial ecosystem that contributes to oral homeostasis through complex interactions among microorganisms, the host immune system and the local environment. Growing evidence indicates that oral diseases are associated with ecological disruption rather than the proliferation of individual pathogens alone. Environmental perturbations, including dietary changes, poor oral hygiene, smoking, antimicrobial exposure, ageing, salivary dysfunction and systemic disorders, can alter microbial community structure, functional activity and host responses, promoting dysbiosis. Established concepts, including the ecological plaque hypothesis, keystone pathogen hypothesis and polymicrobial synergy and dysbiosis model, explain complementary aspects of oral disease development. However, an integrated framework linking cumulative environmental stress, microbial interaction networks, ecological resilience, functional changes and host-microbiome feedback remains underdeveloped. This critical narrative review synthesises evidence from microbial ecology, multi-omics, systems biology, network analysis, antimicrobial resistance and oral-systemic interactions to propose the ecological collapse model (ECM) as a hypothesis-generating conceptual framework. The ECM proposes that oral dysbiosis may develop through interacting processes of functional adaptation, ecological destabilisation and persistent community disruption. The review also examines the oral microbiome as a reservoir of antimicrobial resistance determinants and discusses potential ecological interventions, including host-response modulation, precision antimicrobials and microbiome-directed therapies. These approaches may complement established oral healthcare but require further evaluation of their efficacy, safety and durability. The ECM provides a testable framework for investigating relationships among environmental perturbation, microbial function, ecological resilience and persistent dysbiosis. Longitudinal, experimental and translational studies are needed to determine whether its proposed indicators can predict disease progression or guide microbiome-informed interventions.

items.title: Developmental bias explains the evolutionary trend towards simple leaf shapes.
items.abstract: The relative influence of developmental bias and natural selection on evolutionary outcomes remains a central, unresolved question in evolutionary biology. Here, we combine large-scale phylogenetic trees with herbarium data to confirm that, across the evolutionary history of angiosperms, transitions from complex to simple leaf shapes have occurred at a significantly higher rate than the reverse. To investigate whether this directional trend reflects an underlying developmental bias, we simulate evolutionary transitions by introducing random mutations into a well-established computational model of leaf development. Despite excluding selection, the transition rates produced by the model closely align with those observed in the phylogenetic data. This agreement indicates that a strong developmental bias, reflecting the relative ease with which gene regulatory networks generate simple over complex leaves, has played a major role in shaping the evolution of leaf morphology. Our findings echo recent work showing that similar biases towards simplicity influence the evolution of molecular structures, including RNA secondary structures and protein quaternary assemblies. Together, these results suggest that a developmental bias favouring simplicity may be a widespread and general feature of evolutionary systems.

items.title: Neutral thorium(IV)-di-palladium(II)-cacodylate-bridged-complex.
items.abstract: Herein, we report on the synthesis and structural characterization of a neutral palladium(II)-cacodylate-bridged complex containing a thorium(IV) ion and cacodylate capping groups, [Th IV PdII2{(CH 3 ) 2 AsO 2 } 8 ] (1). Complex 1 was synthesized using a simple one-pot technique in aqueous medium at pH 7. The thorium ion is sandwiched by two palladium(II) ions creating a unique Pd II ⋯Th IV ⋯Pd II core, which is bridged by eight cacodylate ligands.

items.title: The Unappreciated Helper: When an AI Facilitation Agent Improves Group Efficiency Despite Poorer User Perceptions
items.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence make it possible to embed AI facilitation agents in collaborative settings, where they can deliver real-time recommendations based on ongoing group discussions. This experimental study examined how group members perceive a collaborative platform with or without such an agent and evaluated the agent’s effects on group communication and performance. A total of 187 undergraduate psychology students collaborated in 50 groups of three or four members on a digital platform with a synchronous text chat. Groups were randomly assigned to one of two conditions (25 groups per condition): with an AI facilitation agent (n = 96 participants) that encouraged information sharing when exchanges were insufficient, or without the agent (n = 91 participants). Participants rated the platform’s acceptability, perceived support, sense of intrusion, and affective reactions. Participants in the AI condition rated the platform as less acceptable and less supportive, but not more intrusive or unpleasant. Nevertheless, groups assisted by the agent were more efficient, completing the task faster with less communicative effort. Descriptive analyses of group interactions in the three minutes before and after the agent’s interventions showed a shift from providing information toward requesting information, expressing opinions, and agreeing, without change in overall interaction volume. These findings reveal a gap between objective performance and subjective perceptions, highlighting the need to design AI agents that improve group efficiency while fostering members’ sense of support and acceptance.

items.title: Rooted in Resilience: Applying Ego Psychology to HIV-Affirmative Social Work Practice
items.abstract: Abstract Individuals living with HIV commonly experience intersecting psychological, relational, and societal stressors related to health, stigma, loss, and disclosure. This case study explores the application of ego psychology with a focus on support for grieving and resilience against stigma to HIV-affirmative clinical social work practice with a 26-year-old gay man who experienced acute grief, anticipatory anxiety, insomnia, and difficulty concentrating after receiving an HIV diagnosis and losing his long-term partner to AIDS. Ego functioning, adaptive defenses, affect regulation, relationship patterns, and environmental supports and stressors identified through an eco-map were all included in the formulation, which drew on person-in-environment and intersectional perspectives. Supportive and psychodynamic interventions informed by ego psychology included role-playing, structured problem-solving, psychoeducation, guided grief exploration, reflective listening, and investigation of intellectualization and avoidance. The proposed treatment plan incorporates the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), client self-report, clinician observations and behavioral indicators of relational and community participation to monitor clinical progress. The proposed six-month, ego psychology-informed treatment plan identifies measurable targets for improvement in relational assertiveness, anxiety regulation, sleep, community involvement, and integration of grief related to partner loss and HIV diagnosis, and reduced avoidance related to the diagnosis. Incorporating HIV-related stigma, sexual orientation, relationship vulnerability, and broader person-in-environment characteristics, the case illustrates how ego psychology may be operationalized through quantifiable, client-centered outcomes. Integrating psychodynamic theory with culturally responsive, resilience-informed, and outcome-informed therapy for clients managing chronic illness, bereavement, and identity-related stress is one of the implications for clinical social work.

items.title: Pakikipagkapwa in Greater Bilbao, Basque Country: Gendered Homemaking and Postcolonial Belonging among Filipino Domestic and Care Workers
items.abstract: Abstract Based on semi-structured interviews with ten Filipino domestic and care workers and one key informant, as well as participant observation at five Filipino community events in Greater Bilbao between March and July 2024, this article brings Boccagni and Hondagneu-Sotelo’s (2023) homemaking approach into dialogue with pakikipagkapwa , the Filipino ethical practice of relating to others through kapwa (shared personhood). Associations, shared food, sport, and religious fellowship sustained companionship, practical support, and cultural continuity. Analyzed through postcolonial theory, Catholic rituals introduced under Spanish rule served in migration as resources for belonging rather than explicit acts of resistance. At the same time, participants’ assertions of shared humanity directly contested devaluation based on class and national origin. The principal finding is relational ambivalence. Ties that made hardship bearable could also reinforce expectations of sacrifice and accommodate unequal employment and family relationships. Women carried much of the organizational and liturgical work sustaining community life, gaining visibility that did not necessarily translate into decision-making authority. The article distinguishes recognition, practical support, and material protection, and proposes a “structural floor” of income security, enforceable rights, and accessible assistance beneath relational belonging. By treating pakikipagkapwa and the Filipino psychology from which it derives as an interpretive framework rather than solely as cultural material, the article complements institution-focused integration research by foregrounding migrants’ own relational terms of recognition.

items.title: Expanding the Reach of Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Insomnia: National Dissemination of Sleep Education to Provisional Psychologists.
items.abstract: Cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is the gold-standard treatment for insomnia; however, it is rarely taught in graduate psychology pathways, which limits its reach. Guided by the RE-AIM framework, this study evaluated the reach and effectiveness of a sleep and CBT-I education workshop for provisional psychologists in Australia. In 2024, the Australasian Sleep Association offered a free, online sleep workshop to all provisional psychologists nationally studying a graduate psychology pathway (e.g., Master's, Doctorate or completing an internship pathway), with registrants compared to the total number of provisional psychologists registered with the Psychology Board of Australia. Pre-post assessments measured sleep and CBT-I knowledge, self-efficacy to manage sleep disturbances and participants' sleep health. Results indicated that the workshop reached 10.3% of all provisional psychologists in Australia in 2024 (n = 819). Significant improvements were observed in attendees' sleep and CBT-I knowledge, self-efficacy in managing sleep disturbances, and personal sleep health (all p's < 0.001). Satisfaction ratings for the workshop overall were very positive, with 88% rating the workshop as Very Good or Excellent. This study demonstrates that a free, online sleep education workshop can reach a substantial proportion of provisional psychologists in Australia and effectively improve their CBT-I knowledge, self-efficacy to manage sleep disturbances, and sleep health. However, continued and expanded sleep education efforts are needed to improve the dissemination of CBT-I into psychological practice and improve mental health outcomes.

items.title: An exploratory mixed methods program evaluation of adult Mental Health First Aid on a college campus.
items.abstract: Objective Mental health issues among college-aged individuals are rising. Gatekeeper programs like Mental Health First Aid (MHFA) may play a critical role in meeting needs. This study builds on prior work, exploring how MHFA was implemented on a university campus and how outcomes, such as MHFA knowledge and skill retention, changed over time. Participants Quantitative analyses included 126 MHFA-trained individuals, and 22 interviewees. Methods Utilizing mixed-methods, this study aimed to evaluate whether training gains were maintained across two time points, 3- and 6-months post-training. Individual interviews explored training experiences. Results MHFA knowledge and self-efficacy generally remained stable over time. Skill utilization increased between follow-up surveys. Evidence suggests that participants found it slightly easier over time to have a supportive conversation with someone experiencing a substance use crisis. Conclusion College settings should increase access to gatekeeper trainings like MHFA to increase mental health literacy, knowledge, confidence, and skills for community support.

items.title: Mental health and problematic internet, social media, and gaming use among Hispanic college emerging adults: A structural equation modeling approach.
items.abstract: Objective: Technology use has proliferated worldwide, including internet, social media, and gaming use. One's technology use may become problematic, which typically includes excessive use that interferes with daily and social functioning. This study investigated how depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and stress associate with problematic internet, social media, and gaming use via latent structural equation modeling among Hispanic emerging adult college students. Participants and Methods: Hispanic college students ( n = 424) completed an online cross-sectional survey assessing sociodemographics, depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, stress, and problematic internet, social media, and gaming use. Results: Depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and stress were positively associated with problematic internet ( β =.30, .29, and .37, respectively; p s β =.21, .26, and .30, respectively; p s β =.19, .15, and .25, respectively; p s = .001, .011, and Conclusions: Statistically significant positive associations were observed for all associations of interest. Prospective studies should examine temporality and mechanisms of these associations.

items.title: Disordered Eating Behaviors and Eating-Related Psychopathology in Young Adults 10 Years After Adolescent Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery.
items.abstract: Purpose We conducted a cross-sectional comparison of disordered eating behaviors (DEBs) and eating-related psychopathology 10 years following adolescent metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS), with nonsurgical excess weight (NS-EW) and nonsurgical healthy weight (NS-HW) comparators. Methods DEBs and eating-related psychopathology at year 10 were measured via the loss of control eating scale and the eating disorder examination (EDE)-bariatric surgery version. Results EDE Global, Shape Concerns, and Weight Concerns on the EDE in the post-MBS group were similar to NS-EW yet significantly higher than NS-HW. The post-MBS group reported significantly lower odds of EDE restraint than NS-EW but significantly higher odds than NS-HW. The post-MBS group reported significantly lower odds of EDE eating concerns and loss of control eating behavior than NS-EW. Discussion The post-MBS group appeared at lower risk for some DEBs and eating-related psychopathology than nonsurgical young adults with a similar range of excess weight, yet trajectories of body mass index, DEB, and eating-related psychopathology following bariatric surgery should be examined longitudinally.

items.title: Relational effects of sexual abuse disclosure: perspectives of victims, offenders, and confidants.
items.abstract: Background: Sexual abuse is a complex public health concern and is often perpetrated by someone known to the victim, frequently within an intrafamilial context, which complicates disclosure. Although previous research suggests that disclosure occurs in a social context, the perspectives of victims, offenders, and confidants on the relational effects of disclosure remain poorly understood. Objective: This study aimed to explore and compare the ways in which relationships among victims, offenders, and confidants changed after disclosure of sexual abuse from all three perspectives. Method: This study employed a cross-sectional, multi-perspective qualitative design. Victims, offenders and confidants answered closed- and open-ended questions in an online questionnaire developed for this study. The total sample ( N = 93) comprised three subgroups: victims ( n = 50), offenders ( n = 7), and confidants ( n = 36). 73% of all participants referred to the disclosure of intrafamilial abuse. Participants in each subgroup were recruited independently and were asked to describe post-disclosure changes in their relationships within their independent relational triad. Data from the open-ended questions were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results: Several overlapping themes were found across the three subgroups: (1) internalization of blame; (2) spectrum of alienation; and (3) longing for recognition and openness. These themes revealed the interconnected nature of emotions and experiences across relationship triads as well as perspectives unique to each of the three subgroups. Conclusions: The disclosure of sexual abuse mostly affected the relationships between victim, offender, and confidant negatively or ambivalently, often resulting in alienation, communicative tension and a disrupted family system. The findings point to the value of adopting a systemic framework when working with affected families that recognizes the interdependence of family members' responses, while prioritizing the victim's safety.

items.title: Growth disturbance following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with or without lateral extra-articular procedures in skeletally immature patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Purpose To evaluate the incidence of growth-related complications after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) combined with lateral extra-articular procedures (LEAP) in skeletally immature patients. It was hypothesized that adding a LEAP would not be associated with a relevant increase in growth-related complications. Methods A PRISMA-based systematic search of PubMed, MEDLINE, Scopus and Google Scholar was performed through November 2025. Studies (Levels I-IV) reporting radiographically assessed growth disturbances after ACLR combined with LEAP in skeletally immature patients and with a follow-up of ≥24 months were included. Growth disturbance was defined as limb length discrepancy (LLD) ≥ 10 mm and/or coronal plane angular difference ≥5° versus the contralateral limb. Methodological quality was assessed using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS). When comparative data were available, pooled risk ratios (RRs) were calculated. Results Thirteen studies were included, comprising 436 patients: 334/436 (77%) underwent ACLR + LEAP, and 102/436 (23%) underwent isolated ACLR. The overall methodological quality assessed by MINORS was moderate (mean score: 13, range: 10-17). Overall, growth disturbance occurred in 8 of 436 patients (1.8%). LLD occurred in 4/334 patients after ACLR + LEAP (1.2%; mean 12 ± 2 mm) and in 2/102 patients after isolated ACLR (1.9%; quantitative data not reported). Valgus deformity occurred in 2/334 patients after ACLR + LEAP (0.6%) and in 1/102 patients after isolated ACLR (0.9%). No varus deformity was reported. Meta-analysis was feasible only for valgus deformity (2 studies; 21 ACLR + LEAP vs. 37 isolated ACLR), showing no significant difference between groups (RR = 1.56 [95% CI = 0.35-6.90]; p = 0.56; I 2 = 66%). Conclusion Although the comparative analysis was underpowered by the low number of events, adding a LEAP to ACLR showed no statistically significant difference in growth-related complications compared to isolated ACLR in skeletally immature patients. Level of evidence Level IV.
