items.title: Predicting early treatment termination in opioid use disorder: a machine learning model for risk stratification.
items.abstract: Background: Half of patients with opioid use disorder (OUD) discontinue opioid agonist treatment within the first year. Identifying premature termination risk at intake could enable targeted clinical responses. Objectives: To develop and externally validate a machine learning model predicting premature treatment termination in OUD; to derive a clinical risk stratification system; and to identify variables most associated with predicted probability. Methods: Retrospective data from the Information System of the Andalusian (South Spain) Plan on Drugs and Addictions (SiPASDA) covered 11,475 patients (86.2% male) admitted to 121 public outpatient centers between 2015 and 2023 (90.8% termination rate). A CatBoost classifier was developed ( n = 10,328) and externally validated ( n = 1147). Predicted probabilities were discretized into low, moderate- and high‑risk strata. Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantified global and stratum-specific predictor contributions. Results: CRIBOOST achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.652 ± 0.018 in cross-validation and 0.646 externally. Termination rates rose monotonically across strata: 34.6% (low); 69.6% (moderate); 80.8% (high). Housing instability was the strongest positive predictor (SHAP= +0.569; +0.601 in high‑risk). Judicial referral was most protective (SHAP = -0.412), attenuating from low (-0.553) to high (-0.254); employment showed a similar gradient. Mood disorder (SHAP = +0.470) and benzodiazepine use disorder contributed positively, escalating with risk. Conclusions: CRIBOOST stratifies OUD patients into risk groups at admission using routine intake data, enabling clinicians to target retention-focused interventions where most needed and supporting efficient resource allocation. Stratum-specific SHAP contributions reveal which factors drive risk within each group, informing intervention design.

items.title: Rollout models of human planning with exact action probabilities.
items.abstract: One proposed mechanism for human planning is the mental simulation, or "rollout," of potential action sequences to evaluate future outcomes. While rollout-based models have seen great success in artificial intelligence, cognitive models that describe how people use rollouts remain scarce, in part because they are difficult to fit to behavioral data. Existing methods rely on computationally intensive simulations that result in approximate, noisy estimates of latent planning parameters. We introduce ROSETTE (Rollouts with Stochastic Early Termination and Tractable Estimation), a rollout-based model for finite goal-directed tasks with absorbing goals that provides analytically tractable, simulation-free model fitting. ROSETTE treats planning as a sequence of mental simulations formalized as an absorbing Markov chain. The model deterministically accumulates analytically computed expected rollout evidence and performs a variable number of policy-update cycles. We fit ROSETTE to data from human participants in two multi-step planning tasks and found that it well accounted for a rich set of summary statistics of behavior. By making this specific class of absorbing-goal rollout models tractable, our framework provides a testable account of how people may simulate and evaluate possible futures.

items.title: Cognitive control networks in human and macaque.
items.abstract: A much-replicated finding in human brain imaging is a distributed 'multiple-demand' or MD system, increasing in activity for many kinds of cognitive demand, and centrally involved in cognitive control. MD regions are proposed to encode a distributed mental model of critical task events, bound together in the roles and relationships needed to direct action selection. Though previous data hint at a corresponding network in the macaque, there has been no direct comparison to human data. Here we used functional magnetic resonance imaging to measure whole-brain activation in a multi-step saccadic maze task, compared to a control requiring similar moves but without goal-based decisions. Human data were a close match to the canonical MD network, extended to include adjacent regions, and in particular much of the canonical dorsal attention network. Data from two monkeys suggested correspondences in dorsomedial frontal, insula/orbitofrontal, and posterior temporal cortex. In lateral frontal cortex, there was just a single, largely dorsal activation patch, in contrast to multiple distinct human patches. In one animal, as in humans, there was accompanying activation of dorsal and medial parietal cortex. In macaques, as in humans, together with previous data, our findings suggest an extended and strongly interconnected brain network recruited by increased cognitive challenge.

items.title: Associations of meeting the guidelines for 24-hour movement behaviors with depressive symptoms and perceived stress across the first postpartum year.
items.abstract: Postpartum depression and stress have significant consequences for maternal health. While physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep independently influence mental health, their combined effects within the 24-hour movement framework during postpartum are not well understood. A secondary analysis in the Postpartum 24/7 cohort study (n = 50) examined adherence to the 2025 Canadian 24-hour movement behavior guidelines at 3, 6, and 12 months postpartum from device-based and self-reported measures (including a composite score [0-5] representing number of guidelines met). Guideline adherence was associated with self-reported depressive symptoms (Center for Epidemiological Studies-Depression Scale) and perceived stress (Perceived Stress Scale). Logistic and linear mixed-effects models evaluated changes in guideline adherence over time and associations with mental health outcomes. The proportion of participants meeting most guidelines remained stable across postpartum, though self-reported sleep duration (44-63%, p = 0.043) and device-measured sleep efficiency (62-80%, p = 0.017) improved over time. Across postpartum, meeting sleep quality guidelines was associated with lower depressive symptoms (β = -2.44, p = 0.002) and perceived stress (β = -3.87, p < 0.001) and avoiding screen time before bed was associated with lower perceived stress (β = -2.43, p = 0.041). Meeting physical activity and sedentary behavior guidelines was not associated with depressive symptoms or perceived stress after adjustment. Considered collectively, each additional guideline met was associated with lower depressive symptoms (β = -0.81, p = 0.02) and perceived stress (β = -1.90, p < 0.001) scores. Sleep quality guidelines were most consistently associated with better postpartum mental health; meeting more 24-hour movement behavior guidelines may confer additive benefits. These findings suggest a 24-hour behavior approach may help promote postpartum mental health.

items.title: Surprise Resets the Mind: An Adaptive Online Reset in Working Memory Selection.
items.abstract: Human cognition rapidly adapts to unexpected events in dynamic environments, but it remains unclear whether expectation violations rapidly influence the selection of attended information into working memory. Using the attribute-amnesia paradigm, we introduced expectation violations during the surprise trial to test whether unexpected changes improve reporting of a target feature that had been attended and used but was normally not reported. Across six experiments (total N = 250 college students, aged 17-27 years; 149 females), expectation violations reliably improved surprise-trial report of this feature, indicating greater availability in working memory. This effect occurred not only when the violation concerned the target, but also when it involved broader contextual or auditory changes, suggesting that the effect cannot be characterized simply as enhanced visual attention to the target. These findings suggest that expectation violations trigger a rapid, flexible adjustment of working-memory selection, highlighting its role in dynamically managing information under uncertainty.

items.title: Regulating for Others' Sake: An Integrative Framework of Prosocial Emotion Regulation.
items.abstract: People often regulate others' emotions for prosocial reasons, but when is emotion regulation considered prosocial? In the current article, we present an integrative framework of prosocial emotion regulation, the process of regulating other people's emotions with the intention of benefiting them. We define prosocial emotion regulation as requiring both a motive to help and a goal to alter or sustain another's emotional state. We outline potential predictors of prosocial emotion regulation, propose criteria evaluating its success (i.e., whether it benefits the recipient or not), and consider both its potential benefits and costs. Although prosocial emotion regulation can promote well-being and support social connection, it may also impose burdens on the regulator. We discuss the implications of prosocial emotion regulation across key domains, including emotion-regulation science, social relationships and group processes, early development, and health and well-being. Finally, we identify critical directions for future research to better understand the mechanisms, outcomes, and contexts in which prosocial emotion regulation operates.

items.title: Co-evaluation of co-production in mind and brain research: A dialogical approach.
items.abstract: Co-production is increasingly used in mental and neurological health research, but less is known about how co-production itself can be co-evaluated. We conducted a study that aimed to systematically co-evaluate a 9-month project that co-produced strategic priorities and internal research-funding procedures for a new mind and brain research centre. The co-evaluation used a mixed-method design, including qualitative, quantitative, dialogical and post-implementation approaches, informed by an adapted RQ + 4 Co-Pro framework. The project involved 14 adult contributors who were also participants in the co-evaluation, including seven community partners alongside academic, clinical and research staff. Contributors across these roles also brought lived or living experience of mental-health difficulties, neurodivergence and marginalisation. Reflexive thematic analysis examined contributors' written reflections; perceived power was measured midway through the project and again at completion; findings were returned to the team for dialogical co-interpretation; and funding-panel members later reflected on implementation of the co-produced procedures. Thematic analysis generated six themes concerning time and resources, roles and identities, leadership and power, communication, institutional barriers and emotional labour and gains. Mean Sense of Power scores increased from 5.34 to 5.61 (p = .023). Dialogical reflection revealed both convergent and differing interpretations of shared experiences. Our central learning was that equitable co-production requires time to build trust, enough structure for collective work to progress without closing down shared influence and institutional systems able to support participation. By retaining rather than resolving different viewpoints, we show how systematic, dialogical co-evaluation can turn contrasting experiences into practical learning for future co-production.

items.title: Armillaria mellea Polysaccharides Attenuate Depression-Like Behaviors in Mice Exposed to Chronic Restraint Stress.
items.abstract: Armillaria mellea polysaccharides (AMP) have been investigated for their antioxidant and neuroprotective properties. This study evaluated the behavioral effects of AMP during chronic restraint stress (CRS) exposure and explored accompanying hippocampal protein patterns. Fifty male C57BL/6 mice were assigned to control, CRS, low-dose AMP (50 mg/kg/day), high-dose AMP (100 mg/kg/day), or fluoxetine groups (10 mice per group). AMP was administered orally during 21 days of CRS. Behavioral assessments included sucrose preference, forced swimming, tail suspension, open-field exploration, and Morris water maze (MWM) testing. Histological staining and exploratory western blot measurements were also examined. AMP-treated mice showed lower immobility and improvements in selected sucrose-preference and spatial-learning outcomes relative to CRS mice. Locomotor differences complicate interpretation of the immobility-based outcomes. Hippocampal blots showed descriptive differences in inflammatory, apoptosis-related, synaptic protein, and phosphorylation markers for c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase. Western blot observations from three independent mice per group were interpreted as exploratory. The behavioral findings support further preclinical investigation of AMP during stress exposure.

items.title: Associations of Neighborhood Retail Availability and Psychosocial Resources with Smoking and Alcohol Co-use in Black Americans.
items.abstract: Smoking and alcohol use are established risk behaviors for cancer, but their co-use may increase cancer risk significantly. These behaviors are shaped not by social determinants of health alone but by the neighborhood retail environment, which often disadvantages Black Americans. Psychosocial resources, however, may serve as protective factors. We examined whether the availability of alcohol and tobacco stores in neighborhoods was associated with smoking and alcohol co-use in Black Americans and whether psychosocial resources moderated these associations. We analyzed data from a nationally representative probability sample of Black Americans linked to census-tract measures. Multinomial logistic regression models assessed the adjusted relative risk ratio (aRRR) of neighborhood alcohol and tobacco availability with two co-use outcomes: (1) current smoking and drinking, (2) current smoking and binge drinking. Greater neighborhood retail availability of alcohol stores was associated with a higher (aRRR = 1.07-1.08) likelihood of co-use. Religious involvement, among the psychosocial resources, was a protective factor; participants with medium (aRRR = 0.39-0.43) or high (aRRR = 0.33) involvement were less likely than those with low involvement to report either co-use; however, no significant moderating effect was detected. Our study underscores the need for multilevel and multisectoral strategies for reducing the risk of smoking and drinking and preventing cancer in Black Americans. Reducing co-use may require stronger regulation of alcohol than of tobacco retail density in underserved neighborhoods, alongside tax and pricing policies that limit access. Partnerships with trusted community institutions may also strengthen culturally relevant protective resources against co-use.

items.title: The benefit of external focus of attention is preserved in the VR punching task regardless of haptic information.
items.abstract: In punching a boxing bag, a salient source of information for the movement effect is the felt impact. Using virtual reality (VR), we manipulated the haptic information specifying the impact, to test if indeed the advantage of external focus relates to attention toward the movement effect. Twenty-four participants (18 males, 6 females) performed a punching task under both internal and external focus of attention instructions across two separate sessions. Participants wore a VR headset and punched a bag in two conditions: a virtual bag (without haptic information on the movement effect) and physical bag (with haptic information). Hand velocity at impact functioned as the performance measure. Linear mixed-effects model analysis revealed a significant main effect of attentional focus, with higher punching velocity under external compared to internal focus of attention. A significant main effect of bag was also observed, with higher velocity when striking the physical bag compared to the virtual bag. Critically, the interaction of attentional focus and bag condition was not significant, indicating that the advantage of external focus of attention was preserved regardless of the availability of haptic information related to movement effects. This finding challenges the explanation from common coding theory that the advantage of an external focus is due to its attention for anticipated movement effect. Rather, it is consistent with an ecological perspective that external focus is superior because it fosters attunement to task relevant information specifying the dynamic relation between the fist and the target.

items.title: Subgenome-Resolved Assembly of the Mahseer Tor tambra Reveals Allotetraploid Subgenomes Shared with Tor sinensis.
items.abstract: Mahseers ( Tor spp.) are cyprinids of high conservation and aquaculture value, and their genomes carry extensive gene duplication. Whether this duplication reflects 2 subgenomes has not been resolved at chromosome scale. We assembled a 1.76-Gb genome of a wild female Tor tambra from southern Thailand using Oxford Nanopore and Omni-C data. K-mer spectra were best fitted by a tetraploid model with a monoploid size of 0.85 Gb. Alignment to both subgenomes of Tor sinensis revealed 30 Hi-C joins between homoeologous chromosomes (22 confirmed with Hi-C); most were fold-back joins that leave a mirror-image contact signature yet pass standard contact-continuity checks. After correction, the scaffolds were ordered against the matching T. sinensis chromosomes, placing 1.56 Gb (88.4%) in 25 pseudo-chromosomes per subgenome (consensus quality value [QV] 31.7; 99.4% complete Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs [BUSCOs]). Subgenome-specific k-mers separated the 2 subgenomes without a reference (100% bootstrap support for every chromosome; 98.9% of 1-Mb windows consistent). In a joint analysis, each T. tambra chromosome grouped with its T. sinensis ortholog by subgenome rather than by species, and homoeolog divergence (median synonymous divergence 0.11 to 0.13) was about 5 times ortholog divergence (0.02). The 2 species therefore share the same pair of progenitor subgenomes. The public T. sinensis hap1 and hap2 sets each combine chromosomes from both subgenomes. Subgenome-matched gene trees grouped the copies of each subgenome from 4 species (88.1% of 1,602 loci), supporting a single allopolyploidization before the divergence of Tor and Neolissochilus , and placed T. tambra sister to T. tambroides . This assembly is a subgenome-aware reference for mahseer evolution and conservation.

items.title: Cerebral redistribution in late-onset fetal growth restriction: relation between abnormalities of individual Doppler components and adverse outcomes.
items.abstract: Objectives Cerebral redistribution consists of the preferential redirection of the arterial and well-oxygenated blood flow to the fetal brain and is commonly associated with fetal growth restriction (FGR) secondary to placental insufficiency. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the perinatal outcomes of fetuses with late-onset FGR and cerebral redistribution, examining whether outcomes differed according to the normality or abnormality of the individual Doppler components that determine a reduction in the cerebroplacental ratio (CPR). Methods This was a retrospective, multicenter cohort study conducted across four tertiary maternity units in Italy (University of Parma, Parma; Fondazione Policlinico Universitario 'A. Gemelli' IRCCS, Rome; IRCCS Materno Infantile Burlo Garofolo, Trieste; and University of Brescia, Brescia), including non-anomalous singleton pregnancies complicated by late-onset FGR associated with cerebral redistribution (defined as CPR th percentile according to the Fetal Medicine Foundation reference charts). The study included cases collected at the four participating units between January 2019 and December 2024. Cases were categorized according to umbilical artery (UA) and middle cerebral artery (MCA) Doppler data (Group 1: normal UA-pulsatility index (PI) (≤ 95 th percentile for gestational age) and MCA-PI (≥ 5 th percentile); Group 2: abnormal UA-PI (> 95 th percentile) and normal MCA-PI; Group 3: normal UA-PI and abnormal MCA-PI ( th percentile); and Group 4: abnormal UA-PI and MCA-PI), and perinatal outcomes were compared and evaluated using univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses. Results In total, 352 cases were included, of which 117 (33.2%) were assigned to Group 1, 84 (23.9%) to Group 2, 85 (24.1%) to Group 3 and 66 (18.8%) to Group 4. In the univariate logistic regression analysis, Group 4 showed greater odds of preterm delivery (odds ratio (OR), 2.07 (95% CI, 1.08-3.96); P = 0.03), birth weight rd percentile (OR, 2.44 (95% CI, 1.31-4.57); P = 0.01), neonatal hypoglycemia (OR, 3.34 (95% CI, 1.46-7.67); P rd percentile (OR, 1.92 (95% CI, 1.07-3.46); P = 0.03) and Group 3 showed greater odds of birth weight rd percentile (OR, 1.79 (95% CI, 1.01-3.26); P = 0.02) and CAPO (OR, 1.88 (95% CI, 1.05-3.38); P = 0.03) compared with Group 1. However, in the multivariable logistic regression analysis only Group 4 was associated with greater odds of birth weight rd percentile (adjusted OR, 2.11 (95% CI, 1.11-4.00); P = 0.02) and neonatal hypoglycemia (adjusted OR, 2.68 (95% CI, 1.10-6.50); P = 0.03) compared with Group 1. In the univariate logistic regression analysis, abnormal UA and MCA Doppler parameters were also associated with perinatal complications. However, none of the associations were confirmed after adjustment for gestational age at delivery and birth weight in the multivariable models. Conclusions In cases of late-onset FGR associated with cerebral redistribution, isolated abnormalities of the UA-PI or MCA-PI could not identify fetuses at increased risk of perinatal complications. However, the coexistence of both abnormal UA-PI and abnormal MCA-PI, indicating the highest extent of cerebral redistribution, was independently associated with perinatal complications including neonatal hypoglycemia and birth weight rd percentile. In such cases, birth weight was also independently associated with perinatal complications. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

items.title: Rehabilitating Sexual Offenders in Nigerian Correctional Institutions: A Multidisciplinary Evaluation of Current Practices and Pathways for Reform.
items.abstract: Despite global advances in evidence-based responses to sexual offending, little is known about how individuals convicted of sexual offences are assessed and treated in Nigerian correctional institutions. This study addresses this gap through a multidisciplinary qualitative inquiry conducted across six states in South-West Nigeria, drawing on interviews with incarcerated individuals, correctional staff, health professionals, NGO practitioners and legal officers. Drawing on the Risk-Need-Responsivity model, the Good Lives Model and Cognitive-Behavioural Therapy, the analysis reveals fragmented and non-standardised assessment practices, limited psychological screening at intake and reliance on informal judgement. Rehabilitation is largely generic, focused on vocational and educational programmes, while offence-specific psychological treatment remains marginal. Structural constraints, weak inter-agency coordination, limited NGO collaboration and the absence of integrated reintegration planning result in minimal continuity of post-release programmes. The findings highlight systemic governance and policy gaps, underscoring the need for legally grounded, context-sensitive, evidence-based reforms to strengthen rehabilitation and public safety.

items.title: Met4All: a dockerised Shiny application for DNA methylation array analysis, visualization and reporting.
items.abstract: Motivation DNA methylation profiling is widely used for tumour classification, biomarker discovery and the identification of molecular subgroups. However, routine analysis of Infinium methylation-array data typically requires combining multiple R packages and custom scripts for preprocessing, quality control and downstream interpretation. Results We developed Met4All (Methylation For All), a dockerised Shiny application for integrated analysis of Infinium HumanMethylation450K, EPIC and EPIC v2 array data. Met4All accepts both raw IDAT files and precomputed beta matrices, enabling either end-to-end preprocessing or direct downstream analysis within the same interface. It integrates automated quality control, normalisation, dimensionality reduction (MDS, PCA, UMAP), consensus heatmaps, global methylation profiling, two-group differential methylation analysis, gene-set enrichment testing and copy-number analysis. Structure discovery relies on unsupervised learning (UMAP with graph-based community detection, and consensus clustering); no supervised classification or model-based feature selection is implemented. Outputs are exportable as publication-ready plots and tables for use in downstream workflows. In a systematic comparison against nine representative tools, Met4All was the only one to make all 17 assessed criteria available within a single graphical interface, although individual criteria are supported by several of the frameworks compared. The framework has already supported published methylation studies and is illustrated here on independent public data. Met4All provides an accessible and reproducible environment for integrated methylation-array analysis without requiring extensive bioinformatics expertise. Availability Met4All is implemented in R as a dockerised Shiny application. Source code, Docker configuration files and documentation are available at https://github.com/gcampof/Met4All, and the version described here is archived at Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23265674). Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

items.title: "We take care of ours": Dementia Care Partner Perspectives on Consumer- vs Agency-Directed Care.
items.abstract: Background and objectives Medicaid-funded personal care provides essential support enabling persons with dementia to remain in the community. This care is managed either by an agency (agency-direction) or by the care recipient or their designee (consumer-direction). Persons with dementia are more likely to use consumer-direction, but little is known about what drives care model choice, or how the motivations for seeking care and resulting care experiences differ for users of each model. Research design and methods We conducted semi-structured interviews with care partners of community-living persons with dementia receiving personal care through New York Medicaid (n = 18), using directed content analysis to identify key themes. Results Three common goals guided the choice of consumer- vs agency-direction: maximize care quality, ensure provider continuity, and minimize care partner burden. The same goal could lead families to opposite decisions: some chose consumer-direction believing family provided higher-quality care, whereas others chose agency-direction trusting that aides were better trained. Ensuring continuity was most salient for consumer-direction users; minimizing burden most salient for agency-direction users. Regardless of care model, cultural norms and negative experiences with institutional care were primary motivators for using home-based personal care. Common challenges included service hours lagging escalating care needs, administrative obstacles to managing care, and insufficient support from the broader social network. Discussion and implications Personal care recipients and their families need flexible Medicaid policies enabling them to choose arrangements-including care setting and model-that best align with their needs and preferences, alongside resources to navigate a complex benefits system.

items.title: Implementing a Clinical Decision Support System for Pressure Injury Risk Management in Intensive Care Nursing: A Mixed-Methods Evaluation.
items.abstract: Aim To examine the impact of a Clinical Decision Support System for Pressure Injury Risk Management (CDSS-PIRM) on nurses' pressure injury risk management practices and pressure injury incidence in an intensive care unit, and to explore nurses' experiences of integrating the system into routine care. Design Explanatory sequential mixed-methods study involving pre-test and two post-test evaluation stages followed by qualitative interviews. Methods The study was conducted in an intensive care unit at a tertiary university hospital. The quantitative phase comprised 71 structured observations of nine ICU nurses' pressure injury risk management practices across three sequential stages: pre-test (baseline, n = 26), post-test 1 (CDSS-PIRM implementation without real-time alerts, n = 23) and post-test 2 (CDSS-PIRM implementation with real-time alerts, n = 22). Pressure injury incidence among 165 patients was tracked across the three implementation stages. Following the quantitative phase, the qualitative phase involved semi-structured interviews with seven nurses. Results Risk assessment practice scores were significantly higher at post-test 1 compared with the pre-test (median 3 [IQR 2-6] vs. 2 [IQR 1-2]; p = 0.016), while wound care practice scores improved significantly at post-test 2 (median 1.5 [IQR 0-2] vs. 0 [IQR 0-1]; p = 0.015). Overall pressure injury incidence remained unchanged (10.9%; pre-test: 9.68%; post-test 1: 11.63%; post-test 2: 11.67%; p = 0.920). Two main themes were identified: (i) experienced benefits (a comprehensive clinical guide with real-time prevention support and advanced documentation); and (ii) barriers to clinical integration (workload pressure, reliance on established routines, alert fatigue and infrastructure limitations). Conclusion Clinical decision support systems can strengthen specific nursing practices related to pressure injury prevention; however, contextual and organisational barriers may constrain their translation into measurable clinical outcomes. Reporting methods The Good Reporting of a Mixed Methods Study checklist was followed. Patient or public contribution No patient or public contribution. Implications for the profession and/or patient care These findings highlight the potential of clinical decision support systems to support nursing judgement, documentation and real-time prevention in the intensive care unit. Addressing contextual and organisational barriers is essential to optimise their integration into nursing workflows and improve patient safety outcomes. Impact This study demonstrates how a clinical decision support system can enhance pressure injury risk assessment and wound care practices in intensive care nursing. Findings reveal that improvements in nursing processes do not automatically translate into reduced pressure injury incidence, suggesting the influence of contextual and organisational factors. The study offers practical and conceptual insights for nurses, nurse managers and digital health researchers on implementing decision support technologies in complex care environments.

items.title: Meanings mothers attribute to caring for children with congenital toxoplasmosis: A virtual ethnography on Facebook®.
items.abstract: Introduction Congenital toxoplasmosis is a significant public health concern due to its severity and its profound impact on maternal and family care. Objective To explore how mothers of children with congenital toxoplasmosis use Facebook to share caregiving experiences and construct meanings related to their maternal trajectories within digital support networks. Method This is an exploratory, qualitative study based on virtual ethnography. The study followed six methodological steps: participant search, group characterization, data collection, interviews, transcription, and analysis. Seventeen Facebook® spaces, including personal accounts, pages, and groups, were analyzed, addressing topics such as birth narratives, diagnosis, sequelae, family impact, spirituality, and emotions. Subsequently, interviews were conducted with seven mothers. Results The results were organized into three thematic categories: (1) the impact of the diagnosis on family life and the search for information; (2) the resources mobilized by mothers to cope with atypical motherhood, such as social support, faith, and welcoming networks; and (3) the everyday uses of Facebook, with emphasis on visibility strategies, care with exposure, and the construction of belonging. Initially, mothers turned to virtual groups seeking support and information, later moving on to sharing their own experiences on personal profiles and other platforms. Conclusion The findings highlight the importance of understanding the emotional and informational needs of mothers of children with congenital toxoplasmosis, emphasizing the value of promoting welcoming and collaborative spaces in digital environments that foster mutual support and experience sharing.

items.title: Predicting personal PM<sub>2.5</sub> exposure among community-dwelling older adults using multi-source environmental, residential, and behavioral information.
items.abstract: Individual exposure to fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) varies according to environmental, residential, and behavioral contexts. This study aimed to predict personal PM 2.5 exposure among community-dwelling older adults and examine candidate variables using a Bayesian LASSO model incorporating information from multiple exposure-related domains. A total of 247 adults aged ≥60 years were recruited in Fuzhou, China. Each participant completed one 72-h personal PM 2.5 monitoring session during either the summer or winter campaign, with outdoor PM 2.5 measured concurrently and residential, environmental, behavioral, and time-activity information collected through a questionnaire survey. Posterior regression coefficients and their 95% credible intervals were estimated for candidate variables. The model yielded a Bayesian R 2 of 0.481 (95% credible interval [CrI]: 0.412-0.539) and an RMSE of 19.260 μg/m 3 (95% CrI: 18.797-19.876). Four variables had positive posterior regression coefficients, with 95% CrIs excluding zero: passive smoking only [16.157 μg/m 3 (95% CrI: 7.920-24.462)], current smoking [12.949 μg/m 3 (95% CrI: 7.047-18.843)], residence near a major road [7.398 μg/m 3 (95% CrI: 0.655-14.195)], and outdoor PM 2.5 concentration (per 1 SD) [6.531 μg/m 3 (95% CrI: 3.798-9.351)]. The coefficient directions of these four variables were highly consistent across repeated cross-validation. These findings may inform future studies aimed at further evaluating and refining individualized PM 2.5 exposure assessment in older populations.

items.title: Improving source identification of volatile organic compounds using Positive Matrix Factorization with adjusted photochemical-age parameterization and time-shifted organic molecular tracers in an industrial area.
items.abstract: Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF) is widely used for volatile organic compound (VOC) source apportionment, but conventional photochemical-age-based initial VOC (VOCini) estimation may be biased by fresh hyperlocal emissions in industrial areas. In addition, the temporal delay between VOC emissions and secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation is rarely considered in PMF. This study developed a hyperlocal source-adjusted VOCini framework (M-IVOCH) and further incorporated concurrent, 12-h shifted, and 24-h shifted SOA tracers using multiple time resolution PMF (M-IVOCH,SOA). Hourly VOCs and 12-h PM2.5 SOA tracers were measured over four field campaigns at a highly industrialized site in southern Taiwan. Excluding the hyperlocal source before VOCini estimation enabled gasoline evaporation and liquefied petroleum gas emissions to be resolved as distinct factors. Incorporating SOA tracers further resolved a secondary process-related factor and a secondary biomass burning factor that were not identified using routine VOC measurements alone, and the time-shifted tracers revealed day-night differences in secondary biomass burning factor. The industrial factor was also associated with 2-methylerythritol and phthalic acid, suggesting a possible connection between industrial emissions and SOA formation. Accounting for hyperlocal emissions and time-shifted SOA improved source identification and provided additional information for air pollution management in complex industrial environments.

items.title: Adding Locally Available Foods to SQ-LNS Increased Nutrient Intake but Not the Proportion of Infants Meeting Nutrient Requirements in Rural Zimbabwe: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements (SQ-LNS) improve linear growth but may not close all nutrient gaps. Whether locally available foods can help meet these gaps remains uncertain. Compare infant and young child feeding (IYCF) (ground maize+SQ-LNS) versus "IYCF-plus" (pro-vitamin A maize, SQ-LNS, moringa, egg and sugar beans) on the proportion of infants meeting nutrient requirements. Infants in rural Zimbabwe were randomized to IYCF or IYCF-plus from age 6mo. The primary outcome was the proportion meeting energy requirements at age 9mo using 24-hour dietary recalls. Secondary outcomes were proportion of children meeting protein, iron, zinc, and folate intakes, plus anthropometric indices and hemoglobin concentration. Tertiary outcomes were protein-quality indicators. Analyses used intention-to-treat mixed-effects logistic and linear regression. Among 192 infants (95 IYCF; 97 IYCF-plus), 9 exited and 2 died. At 9 months, 92.2% (95% CI 87.2, 97.2) in the IYCF arm and 92.5% (95% CI 87.9, 97.0) in the IYCF-plus arm met energy requirements (adjusted OR 1.0; 95% CI 0.3, 3.3). Protein adequacy was 100.0% versus 99.3%; iron adequacy was 84.4% versus 88.8%; zinc adequacy was 87.0% versus 93.0%; and folate adequacy was 97.7% versus 96.0%. Anthropometry and haemoglobin concentration showed no evidence of differences: LAZ mean difference -0.0 (95% CI -0.3, 0.2); WAZ -0.1 (-0.4, 0.2); WLZ -0.2 (-0.5, 0.2); haemoglobin concentration -0.0 (-0.3, 0.3). Protein-quality indicators were higher in the IYCF-plus arm than in the IYCF arm, including available protein (mean difference 2.3 g/kg; 95% CI 1.8, 2.8), Digestible Indispensable Amino Acid Score (DIAAS) (mean difference 79.7; 95% CI 68.9, 90.5), and all available amino acids. IYCF-plus using locally available foods plus SQ-LNS did not improve the proportion of infants meeting nutrient requirements more than SQ-LNS+maize alone, but improved protein quality. clinicaltrials.gov NCT04874688.

items.title: Trajectories of Antibiotic Consumption and Associations with Resistance Across Hospitals and Primary Care: A Population-Level Ecological Study in Shandong Province, China, 2012-2024.
items.abstract: To examine antibiotic consumption patterns and their associations with resistance in hospitals and primary healthcare facilities (PHFs) in Shandong Province to inform antimicrobial stewardship (AMS). Yearly antibiotic consumption (2012-2024) and resistance (2014-2024) data for six resistance phenotypes were obtained in Shandong (population >100 million). Antibiotics were classified using the WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical and AWaRe classification, with expressed as defined daily doses per 1,000 inhabitants per day (DID) and per 1,000 patient visits per day. Consumption structure was assessed using the Shannon index and Gini coefficient. Associations with resistance were examined using Spearman's rank correlation. Total antibiotic consumption decreased by 17.7%, from 11.98 DID in 2012 to 9.86 DID in 2024. Both hospitals and PHFs showed declining diversity and increasing concentration of consumption. Hospitals accounted for 27.7% of total antibiotic consumption, with increasing intensity and a shift towards fluoroquinolones and third-generation cephalosporins, whereas PHFs showed a marked decline and a shift towards extended-spectrum penicillins. Access antibiotics accounted for 27.0% in hospitals and 46.5% in PHFs in 2024. Ecological analyses showed broadly aligned consumption-resistance trends in PHFs, but divergent associations in hospitals. Antibiotic consumption declined in Shandong during a period of sustained AMS policies, but trends differed across healthcare settings. The alignment between primary care consumption and hospital-based resistance suggests that antibiotic use in PHFs may represent an important component of regional antimicrobial resistance dynamics. Future stewardship efforts should integrate consumption, resistance, and prescribing data to guide targeted interventions.

items.title: Examining the intersection of extreme heat exposures, social determinants of health, and adverse pregnancy outcomes: a scoping review.
items.abstract: Extreme heat exposure during pregnancy is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs), complications themselves linked to long-term maternal cardiovascular risk, and these effects appear to vary by social and environmental context (e.g., neighborhood deprivation, greenness, and rural-urban residence). We describe the U.S. evidence and characterize how social determinants of health (SDoH), particularly area-level measures, are defined in this literature. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched through July 14, 2025, plus secondary searches in September 2025. We included U.S.-focused empirical epidemiologic studies and evidence syntheses that (1) assessed extreme heat exposure in pregnancy; (2) incorporated at least one individual- or area-level SDoH as exposure, covariate, or effect modifier; and (3) reported at least one APO, from preterm birth, low birth weight, stillbirth, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and gestational diabetes to composite APOs, severe maternal morbidity, and acute cardiovascular events. Two reviewers independently screened records; a senior reviewer resolved conflicts. Data were extracted into standardized forms and synthesized narratively. Per scoping review guidance, formal risk-of-bias assessment was not performed. We included 37 studies (28 empirical and 9 reviews). Heat exposure was typically defined using percentile-based thresholds (most commonly the 90th or 95th local percentile), heat-wave definitions, apparent-temperature metrics, or absolute cutoffs, with the week before delivery the most frequent window. Preterm birth was the most evaluated outcome, followed by birthweight-related outcomes and stillbirth. Individual-level socioeconomic measures (e.g., education, insurance) appeared in nearly all empirical studies, whereas area-level measures-neighborhood income or poverty, deprivation indices, greenness or tree canopy, heat-trapping land cover, region, and rural-urban residence-appeared in fewer than half. Five of 12 studies incorporating area-level SDoH reported stronger heat-APO associations in disadvantaged or lower-greenness settings. Examples include heat-associated stillbirth risk only in the most deprived neighborhoods; heat-preterm birth associations strongest where both greenness and socioeconomic status were low; and stronger heat-gestational diabetes associations with lower greenness. U.S. studies reported associations between extreme heat in pregnancy and multiple APOs. Area-level SDoH and environmental context were inconsistently incorporated. Standardized use of place-based measures may better identify communities most vulnerable to heat and inform equity-focused, climate-resilient maternal health research and action. Heat exposure in pregnancy is linked to adverse outcomes, and risk may be higher in neighborhoods experiencing socioeconomic deprivation, highlighting the need to measure area-level social determinants in climate-maternal health research.

items.title: Genomic Characterization of a Typical Enteropathogenic Escherichia coli Isolate from an Egyptian Fruit Bat, Rousettus aegyptiacus from Coastal Kenya
items.abstract: Enteropathogenic Escherichia coli (EPEC) are responsible for significant morbidity and mortality cases among young children under the age of five, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Atypical EPEC has frequently been reported from animal hosts, however, information on the occurrence and genomic characteristics of typical EPEC in wildlife reservoirs remains limited. This study characterized an Escherichia coli isolated from an Egyptian fruit bat (Rousettus aegyptiacus) sampled in coastal Kenya using whole-genome sequencing. Oral and rectal swabs were collected from 24 bats captured in Kikambala, Kilifi County, Kenya. Bacterial isolates were cultured, sequenced on the Illumina NextSeq 1000 platform, and analyzed using a bioinformatics workflow that included in silico taxonomic classification, serotyping and multilocus sequence typing, virulence gene profiling, antimicrobial resistance gene detection, plasmid identification, and core genome phylogenetic analysis. One isolate, KIKB-471-SWR-A (O128:H6; ST15625), was classified as typical EPEC. Genomic analysis confirmed the characteristic virulence architecture of typical EPEC. Despite numerous antimicrobial resistance-associated genes being detected, the isolate remained phenotypically susceptible to all antimicrobials tested. The isolate clustered within an EPEC lineage, closely associated with a human-derived EPEC strain, and genetically distinct from both commensal and laboratory E. coli reference strains. Despite no evidence of zoonotic transmission, the findings demonstrated that wildlife can harbor E. coli lineages possessing virulence determinants associated with human pathogenic EPEC strains, underscoring the importance of genomic surveillance at wildlife?human interfaces within a One Health framework to improve the understanding of ecology, evolution, and public health significance of diarrheagenic E. coli.

items.title: GA-NIFS: A post-starburst main sequence disk galaxy undergoing ordered rotation at z = 4.26
items.abstract: Rotating galaxies with relaxed gaseous disks have been discovered across cosmic time, from the local Universe to high redshift. But few such sources have been confirmed at z > 4, making them a precious sample to examine the conditions required for such ordered kinematics in an early, more chaotic Universe. One of the best examples of this sample is the galaxy $\rm DLA0817g1$ (z = 4.2603), which shows remarkably clear rotation in ALMA [C ii] data. We present JWST/NIRSpec IFU data (R ∼ 2700) of $\rm DLA0817g1$, which we combine with archival ALMA [C ii] observations to place constraints on its ISM conditions and morpho-kinematics. From a combination of line ratios, we find a high gas-phase metallicity (Zgas ∼ 0.8 Z⊙), high fraction of obscured star formation, low ionisation (compared to other high-redshift galaxies observed with JWST), and no significant evidence for AGN. Dynamical modelling with $\rm ^{3D}$Barolo reveals nearly identical rotation in $\rm H\alpha$ and [C ii]. Using our metallicity estimate and previous CO and [C ii] detections, we derive a new estimate of the molecular gas mass, relieving a previous strain in the mass budget. Altogether, we suggest that this is a post-burst, main-sequence galaxy, where high levels of past star formation resulted in significant chemical enrichment (i.e., Zgas and Mdust), but the current activity is lower (i.e., lower ionisation parameter and lack of starburst activity). These new observations have opened a window into the interplay of gas, metallicity, star formation, and kinematics in a prototypical early disk galaxy.

items.title: The nature of the Norma arm as a bar-driven star-forming shock front
items.abstract: The Milky Way is commonly depicted as having four main spiral arms, including the Norma–outer arm, and a central stellar bar whose properties remain debated. Masers associated with young high-mass stars have been used to trace a segment of the ‘Norma arm’ extending from one end of the Galaxy’s central stellar bar. Recent work suggests that these masers may reside along a spiral arm or occupy the dominant x 1 stellar orbits that give the bar its shape. Here we use a new generation of N -body, hydrodynamic simulations to argue that these million-year-old masers instead trace the Galactic bar’s quadrant I shock front or, equivalently, its dust lane. This implies that the bar dust lane is star-forming, shedding new light on our understanding of star formation processes in the Milky Way. By associating the masers with the simulated shock front, we determine the parameters of the bar to be: a ≈ 4.3 ± 0.2 kpc, b ≈ 2.3 ± 0.2 kpc, ϕ = $${{20}_{-2}^{+5}}^{\circ }$$ 20 - 2 + 5 ∘ and Ω p ≲ 40 km s −1 kpc −1 , representing the semimajor and semiminor half-lengths of the bar, the inclination angle and the pattern speed, respectively. This raises questions about the Milky Way’s spiral structure and suggests that the Galactic bar is long, slow and star-forming.

items.title: Shared Understanding in Human-AI Teams: Coordination Continuity in Evolving Work
items.abstract: People are increasingly working with AI agents as part of extended, asynchronous workflows. In these settings, shared access to information does not guarantee a shared basis for action: goals, plans, and roles may persist while their current significance changes. We introduce coordination continuity, the extent to which collaborators sustain a workable basis for interdependent action as work progresses. Drawing on research on collaborative work, along with two qualitative team studies and a reflexive case from our own repository-based environment, we present a framework of three elements: durable representations of collaborative work; relative coordination properties that support interpretation of representations in the moment; and interaction mechanisms through which the status of representations can be understood and altered. We use a build-act-drift-rebuild heuristic and the notion of consequential moments to characterise when rebuilding may be needed. We draw eight design implications for collaborative AI infrastructure.

items.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
items.abstract: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters. The Actor interacts with the environment through a robot-control interface, while the Reflector converts execution evidence into reusable operational guidance. Hierarchical Memory Architecture maintains short-term execution context and long-term experiential knowledge to support execution and reflection. Evidence-based Experience Reflection grounds failure diagnosis in observed interactions, while Recursive Harness Self-Improvement refines operational guidance across successive attempts. Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboSPA, and RMBench demonstrate the effectiveness of Embodied-Harness in generalization under environmental variations, spatial reasoning, long-horizon planning, and memory-dependent manipulation. Our method achieves success rates of 82.4%, 76.7%, and 94.4% on the three benchmarks, respectively. Real-world evaluation further yields an average success rate of 96.7% across three manipulation tasks. These results highlight the potential of Embodied-Harness to improve robotic manipulation through experience-driven harness self-improvement.

items.title: Mammalian gonadal development: origins, specification and differentiation of ovary and testis cell lineages
items.abstract: Testicular and ovarian development requires the coordinated formation and assembly of multiple cell types that enable these organs to fulfill their roles in sexual differentiation, reproduction, and endocrine function. A defining feature of gonadal development is that both testes and ovaries arise from a common bipotential primordium, the genital ridge, composed of multipotent progenitors. In this Review, we synthesize current knowledge on the origin, specification, differentiation, and function of the major fetal gonadal somatic lineages, drawing primarily on mouse and human studies. We describe how the adrenogonadal primordium (AGP) gives rise to the gonadal primordium (GP), how coelomic epithelium-derived progenitors generate the supporting, steroidogenic/stromal, and supporting-like cell lineages, and how these progenitors become progressively fate-restricted. We highlight recent evidence for early lineage priming within spatially organized domains of the coelomic epithelium. We further examine the molecular pathways and cellular processes governing sex-specific differentiation of these lineages and discuss remaining gaps in our understanding of how bipotential gonads differentiate into testes or ovaries, and their implication for human health.

items.title: Spatial model of neurogliovascular unit: arachidonic acid can control the stability
items.abstract: Arachidonic acid metabolites can have both vasoconstrictor and vasodilator effects, thereby influencing neuronal activity. In this work, to analyze possible patterns of activity of nervous tissue in response to changes in the metabolic profile, a mathematical model of a spatially distributed system of connected neurogliovascular units was developed. We simulate the influence of arachidonic acid metabolites on the dynamics of the neurogliovascular unit during cortical spreading depression in order to determine the ways in which astrocytic activity influences the spatiotemporal characteristics of the propagating cortical depression wave. It is assumed that in the future the results of the theoretical study can be used to find ways to remove nervous tissue from pathological conditions that occur in epilepsy, migraines and a number of neurodegenerative diseases, including those associated with the occurrence of cortical depression waves.

items.title: Self-organized fractional silencing of pyramidal neurons under global depolarization in a spatial neuron-glial microcircuit model
items.abstract: Pathological transitions in nervous tissue, including epileptiform discharges and cortical spreading depolarization, depend on the interplay between cellular and interstitial mechanisms. We develop a biophysically detailed two-dimensional model of the neurogliovascular unit (NGVU) integrating neuronal populations in the Hodgkin-Huxley formalism, astrocyte-regulated extracellular potassium dynamics, extracellular neurotransmitter spillover, and noradrenergic neuromodulation. Numerical simulations show that inhibitory interneurons enter depolarization block (DB) at significantly lower extracellular potassium concentrations and stimulation intensities than pyramidal neurons. Early loss of inhibition shifts the local excitation-inhibition balance and triggers network hyperexcitability. In the spatially extended network, exceeding a critical stimulation threshold induces a transition from heterogeneous but spatially uniform firing to network fragmentation into stable active microclusters with self-sustained high-frequency firing. Pyramidal neurons with lower excitatory synaptic input receive less recurrent excitation, which protects them from DB. By continuously releasing potassium ions and glutamate into the extracellular space, pyramidal neurons drive strong depolarization in more densely connected neighbors and push them into deep DB. Simulations of localized astrocytic dysfunction predict a spatial limit for potassium clearance defects. Small damaged cores are fully compensated by diffusion and uptake by surrounding healthy astrocyte units. However, above a critical damage size, activity-dependent potassium buildup and firing positive feedback disrupt homeostasis in surrounding units, promoting persistent depolarized centers with self-sustained, spatially segregated pathological activity.

items.title: The Four-Step Action Loop with Feedback: A teachable perception-action framework for everyday self-regulation
items.abstract: Everyday stress is largely a learned pattern: a familiar cue, a fast reading of threat, an automatic reaction and a body that stays activated. Body-based practices such as mindfulness, interoceptive training, Somatic Experiencing and yoga target these patterns, but they are usually taught as techniques without a map of the mechanism they act on. Pain neuroscience education suggests that understanding such a mechanism can itself change experience. No comparable model exists for everyday self-regulation. This paper proposes the Four-Step Action Loop with Feedback, developed over six cohorts of a workshop for non-clinical adults. The loop describes any action as four steps: Sense (exteroception, proprioception and interoception), Process (perception as inference, weighted by context and safety), Choose (habitual reaction or goal-directed response after a pause) and Execute (autonomic and somatic output). Feedback from each outcome acts beneath all four steps, through synaptic plasticity, habit formation and allostatic load. The paper integrates the perception-action cycle, information-processing stages of choice, interoceptive inference, the autonomic space model and the defence cascade. It places a set of practices on the loop: full sensory awareness, grounding, orientation, resourcing, the pause, reduced stimulus and choice, slow movement and relaxation, each with a proposed mechanism and an assessment of the evidence. It also describes the model's translation into four practitioner skills. Seven testable propositions are derived for future evaluation. The model is offered as a teachable framework for wellbeing, not a treatment.

items.title: Classical visual illusions in vision-language models under an instruction ladder
items.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) often name the "illusory" answer when shown a classical visual illusion, but it is unclear whether that answer comes from the picture or from knowledge about famous figures. We drew 300 new stimuli of 25 classical illusions in three conditions--the illusion, the illusion with its inducing elements reversed, and a control with the inducing elements removed--and asked about each image at eight rungs of an instruction ladder that runs from a false fact, through a neutral question and an instruction to report the physical truth, to telling the model the name of the illusion and finally the true answer. Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5, with thinking off and on, gave 460,800 answers. When asked for the physical fact, all four settings almost never gave the illusion answer, and they resolved real 10% differences in the same displays. When asked how the picture looks, the illusion answers returned, and they did not vanish after the true answer was stated. Two measures that cancel position preferences and recognition of the figure suggest that much of this depends on the stimulus: among side answers, Sonnet with thinking chose the illusion side in 85% of cases after being told the truth (95% CI 74--96%), with 16 of the 25 illusions showing a stimulus-driven effect. Yet for five figures--the Fraser spiral, Kanizsa triangle, Pinna--Brelstaff rings, Ouchi pattern and, for Haiku, the rotating snakes--the models gave the illusion answer to the control images as well, which suggests that they answered from the figure rather than from the effect. A false fact was mostly followed on control images but not on illusion images. The stimuli, prompts, all responses and the code are released for testing further models; the Python code that draws the stimuli is parametric and can generate new illusion images for other studies with models or human observers.

items.title: Serial Dependence Emerges from Optimizing Vision for Noise Robustness
items.abstract: Human visual perception is dynamically shaped by the recent past, a phenomenon known as serial dependence. Mechanistic models show that a residual memory trace can generate this dependency, yet its functional purpose (why the visual system should carry information forward in time at all) remains debated. We tested the hypothesis that serial dependence emerges as a normative consequence of optimizing vision for robustness against sensory noise. We trained recurrent autoencoders (a CNN encoder, a ConvGRU memory module, and a CNN decoder) to reconstruct natural videos corrupted by Gaussian noise, with no objective referring to perceptual history. Models that used their temporal memory achieved lower reconstruction error than memory-free counterparts, and this advantage widened as training noise increased, indicating that integrating past context is an adaptive denoising strategy. Probing the trained models with Gabor and dot sequences, we found that memory gave rise to serial dependence spontaneously: an attractive bias toward previous orientations and a spatial "continuity field" toward recently seen locations, both strengthening with training noise. Across temporal delays, the model's serial dependence was strongest for the immediately preceding stimulus and decayed monotonically. This profile quantitatively matched human orientation judgments, including an independent public dataset, once a known response-autocorrelation confound was controlled: an apparent non-monotonicity in one dataset reflected this measurement artifact rather than a genuine model-human mismatch. These findings suggest that serial dependence need not be an idiosyncratic quirk but can arise as a byproduct of optimizing for noise robustness, offering a normative account of perceptual history-dependence that complements existing mechanistic explanations and links behavior to an underlying computational objective.

items.title: Topology-only Local Network Alignment, Part 2. DijSLA: Stochastic Greedy Extension for Cross-Species GO Annotation Prediction
items.abstract: Sequence similarity has long been a strong signal for protein function prediction, whereas the predictive value of network topology has been difficult to verify. Since a protein's function is largely defined by its interaction partners, and since similar interactions are expected across species, aligning protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks by topology alone should uncover functionally related proteins. Topology-only global network alignment has recently produced high-quality functional predictions, but it has yet to be shown that local regions of topological similarity can do the same. We introduce DijSLA (Dijkstra-inspired Stochastic Local Alignment), the first local network alignment algorithm designed from the ground up to use only topology. We adopt a seed-and-extend strategy: starting from seed pairs of proteins with similar network topology, we expand the alignment in a Dijkstra-inspired manner, following edges out of the aligned set to node pairs with near-maximal similarity. Rather than expanding deterministically, we inject randomness so that we can sample many high-quality alignments, in which node pairs with robust topological similarity "rise above" the noise and reveal functional similarity. Using networks and GO annotations from April 2010, we predict annotations validated against those from April 2020. With Network Alignment Frequency (NAF), a robustness measure that correlates with prediction precision, we make predictions with precision on par with or better than the best sequence-based methods and broadly similar to that of global topological alignment. Compared with existing local aligners, DijSLA produces larger, topologically high-quality alignments, which yield dramatically more predictions with higher validation rates, while using less CPU time and far less memory. Code is available at https://github.com/waynebhayes/BLANT/tree/master/CDijkstra.

items.title: Network versus market information in coupled opinion-return dynamics
items.abstract: When making investment decisions, investors can use common signals from the market and local signals from their social networks. We develop an agent-based opinion-return model in which agents follow fixed trading strategies and respond to either local network information or a common market signal. In our model, trend followers and contrarians select either a local network signal or a common market signal and then update their buy, hold, or sell opinions by following or opposing the signal, respectively. The aggregate opinion imbalance determines the return, which sets the market signal. We find that three collective regimes emerge depending on how much network information is used and the fraction of contrarians in the population. Persistent directional states occur when trend followers dominate, market-wide reversals appear when a contrarian-rich population relies on the common market signal, and opposing opinions coexist with small aggregate returns when the same population relies on network signals. With a common market signal, the majority strategy has the higher payoff scores, whereas increasing reliance on network signals reduces this difference. When only network information is used, higher network clustering is associated with greater polarisation and smaller return magnitudes when trend followers dominate. Degree heterogeneity has little effect on aggregate measures but changes the payoff scores of high- and low-degree agents. In contrarian-rich populations, local information thus reduces aggregate return fluctuations even as opposing opinions persist.

items.title: Carving the Neptunian desert as a function of stellar mass and lifetime XUV irradiation
items.abstract: The Neptunian desert is a prominent feature in the exoplanet population, thought to arise from both XUV-driven photoevaporation and tidal circularisation following high-eccentricity migration. However, the extent to which each mechanism contributes, and where, remains uncertain. We examine the desert as a function of stellar type as a test of these mechanisms. We determine the desert boundaries for subsamples of F, G, K, and M-hosted planets for radius against period, semi-major axis, bolometric instellation, and lifetime XUV irradiation. Going from F to M, we observe shifts in the boundary between 2.2-7.5 R$_\oplus$ towards shorter orbital periods, smaller orbital distances, and much smaller instellations. These shifts match changes in lifetime XUV irradiation as a function of stellar mass at fixed period, semi-major axis, and bolometric instellation, evidence towards a photoevaporative origin for the desert at these radii. This is especially the case for orbital period, where the boundary should be invariant across stellar types under the high-eccentricity mechanism. In lifetime XUV space, we see significant overlap in the boundary across stellar types up to 7.5 R$_\oplus$. While this could be further evidence towards the XUV-driven mechanism in this regime, our uncertainties cannot rule out a shift in the boundary of the magnitude expected under the high-eccentricity mechanism. Overall, our results suggest a photoevaporative origin of the Neptunian desert up to sub-Saturn radii, but increased sample sizes, especially for M-hosted, Neptune-sized planets, will help distinguish further between the mechanisms.

items.title: Citizen-informed scenarios to shape energy demand reduction strategies
items.abstract: Growing evidence has demonstrated the important role that energy demand reduction can play in achieving net zero. Despite this, the adoption of such measures in government strategies often remains limited, in part based on perceived public resistance to change. Using a novel combined deliberative-modelling approach, which fills a key gap in the literature, we find this is unfounded. Citizens both recognise the importance of and support demand-side interventions to achieve the UK's net-zero goals. This support, however, is conditional. If policy interventions can make demand-side choices practical and fair, we find citizens are prepared to reduce energy demand by at least 37% between 2025 and 2050, providing 20% of the abatement required to meet net-zero targets. Policymakers could thus unlock a wide range of demand reduction measures by acting on a more comprehensive understanding of public views and needs. Moreover, our approach offers a powerful framework, applicable in other contexts, to underpin policymaking with socially-informed quantitative modelling.

items.title: 2026 QQ8: Earth's temporary flyby of maximum lunation
items.abstract: Aims: On a rare occasion, asteroids are temporarily captured by the Earth to become the planet's interim companions. The discovery of asteroid 2026~QQ$_8$ provided an opportunity to study this class of objects, adding to the sparse discovery catalogue of Earth's temporary companions. Methods: We performed astrometric, photometric, and dynamical studies of 2026~QQ$_8$, and measured its solar radiation pressure signal to discern between a natural and an artificial origin. Results: We find 2026 QQ$_8$ to be of natural origin, with solar radiation pressure signal commensurable with natural objects and spectrophotometry of an S-type object. 2026 QQ$_8$ is Earth's third discovered otemporarily-captured companion on a flyby orbit, and the first long-duration one, owing this to being on the so-called "orbit of maximum lunation". Its unusual orbit lies close to the theoretical upper duration limit of an object captured in the Earth-Moon system, and has now been observed for the first time.

items.title: Hints of planet formation in progress around DR Tau from observations with LBT SHARK-NIR and SHARK-VIS
items.abstract: Protoplanetary disks are the primary sites of planet formation. However, the direct imaging of protoplanets still embedded within their parental disks remains a significant challenge, with only a small number of confirmed detections to date and several candidates awaiting verification. We search for embedded planets in the protoplanetary disk of the young star DRTau by targeting accretion signatures from forming sub-stellar objects. Using narrow-band imaging, we observe both visible Halpha and near-infrared Paschen-beta (Pabeta) emission to identify actively accreting companions. To this end, we performed high-contrast observations of DRTau using the SHARK-VIS (0.40-0.95 micron) and SHARK-NIR (0.96-1.70 micron) imagers at the LBT. The study uses a combination of narrow-band filters to isolate accretion signatures and broad-band filters for multi-wavelength characterization in both the visible and near-infrared. Our observations recover the primary disk structures previously identified in the literature, albeit at low signal-to-noise (S/N). We identify two compact features with S/N between 6 and 13 in both narrow- and broad-band filters. The first, an elongated structure, matches previous SPHERE detections, while the second, more compact feature, is now confirmed despite its low S/N in earlier datasets. A comparison over a seven-year baseline confirms the stability of both structures. Their observed orbital motion is consistent with Keplerian rotation, potentially suggesting the presence of an undetected planetary-mass companion (few MJup) at the location of the second feature. However, our analysis does not confirm Halpha or Pabeta emission originating from localized accretion. Instead, we conclude that the observed flux is likely stellar light reflected by dust at these locations and discuss alternative mechanisms that could account for such detections.

items.title: The GAPS programme at TNG. LXXXIII. Orbital refinement and atmospheric investigation of TOI-1518 b (BD+66 1610 b)
items.abstract: TOI-1518 b (BD+66 1610 b) is a highly irradiated ultra-hot Jupiter on a strongly misaligned orbit, a benchmark target for atmospheric and dynamical studies. We comprehensively characterise the TOI-1518 system by refining its orbital and physical parameters, and by investigating the chemical composition of the planetary atmosphere through transmission spectroscopy. We employed a joint Bayesian framework combining TESS photometry, HARPS-N high-resolution spectroscopy, and least-squares deconvolution profiles to break stellar geometrical degeneracies. We then applied single-line and cross-correlation function (CCF) transmission spectroscopy across theoretical templates. By anchoring the stellar projected rotational velocity ($v \sin i_\star \approx 79.7$ km s$^{-1}$), we confirmed the nearly polar orbit ($λ\approx 238^\circ$) and the theoretically predicted nodal precession ($\mathrm{d}i/\mathrm{d}t \approx 0.15^\circ$ yr$^{-1}$). We revealed an atmospheric Rossiter-McLaughlin (RM) effect and a bulk atmospheric blue-shift of $\approx -7.0$ km s$^{-1}$. Through transmission spectroscopy, we detected H I, C I, Na I, Ca I, Sc II, Ti II, V II, Cr I, Fe I, Fe II, Ni I, Sr II, Y II, Eu II, and W I. This marks the first detection of H I, C I, Sc II, V II, Sr II, Y II, Eu II, and W I in this planet, and the first ever detection of Eu II and W I in an exoplanetary atmosphere. Inconsistencies in the Na I doublet shifts suggest likely stellar contamination. Furthermore, time-resolved CCF analysis revealed morning-to-evening limb asymmetries for species like Mg I and Ba I, hinting at night-side cold traps. The atmosphere of TOI-1518 b exhibits a rich chemical inventory shaped by intense irradiation and bulk circulation. Our results emphasize the necessity of simultaneously modelling stellar line morphology and planetary tracks to accurately interpret atmospheric signals under strong RM effects.

items.title: How coalition size shapes bill cosponsorship in the U.S. Congress
items.abstract: Legislation is built by coalitions, yet studied through pairwise ties. Using five decades of U.S. House and Senate cosponsorship (1973-2025), we represent each bill as a group. Prior ties to current members predict who joins better than ties to the sponsor, and group history (earlier co-appearance with pairs of those members) produces a larger likelihood gain than sponsor ties alone. Coalition formation therefore retains a social memory of earlier groups: cooperation is organized around relational histories embedded in the coalition already assembled, which sponsor-cosponsor ties alone cannot recover. Completed coalitions also recur and share subgroups more often than degree- and size-preserving nulls predict. Party sorting peaks in coalitions of a few dozen members; as Congress polarized, small coalitions retained their cross-party share while mid-size coalitions became more partisan. Women are over-represented chiefly in coalitions led by Democratic women, although same-gender sponsor matching is close to zero after adjustment.

items.title: The First Adolescent Super-Earth-Sized Multi-Planet System Around an M Dwarf: TOI-2079
items.abstract: We identify two planets in close-in orbits around the M-type star TOI-2079 as the first super-Earth-sized planets orbiting a multi-planet M dwarf with a well-determined age of $1$-$2$\,Gyr. The interior planet, TOI-2079 b, has an orbital period of $1.49232359^{+0.00000099}_{-0.00000086}$ d, and the outer planet, TOI-2079 c, has an orbital period of $9.3174523\pm0.0000098$ d. The host star characterization is based on spectroscopic observations, which classify it from an M1.5 to an M3.5 dwarf with an effective temperature of $3695\pm77$ K. Further analysis determined TOI-2079's rotation period to be $17.33^{+0.29}_{-0.28}$ d. Multiple ground-based follow-up observations, combined with a state-of-the-art validation procedure, allow us to rule out possible astrophysical false-positive scenarios and validate the planetary nature of both objects. We find that the inner planet has a radius of $1.320\pm0.050 R_{\oplus}$ and $T_{\rm eq} = 867\pm27$ K, while the outer planet has $R_{\rm p} = 1.671\pm0.051 R_{\oplus}$ and $T_{\rm eq} = 473\pm15$ K.

items.title: Obliquity of Mercury with a fluid core and a deformable mantle
items.abstract: In anticipation of BepiColombo's orbital insertion in 2026, this study revisits the rotation of Mercury, modelling it with a fluid core and a deformable mantle. For this well-established physical model, we provide an analytical solution based on a novel Lagrangian formalism. Our approach enables a comprehensive 3D solution for the mantle's orientation, including the phase in longitude at the perihelion. The model incorporates dissipative torques from core-mantle boundary friction and tidal deformations, conservative pressure torques, and the effect of the planet's apsidal precession. We validate the equilibrium positions obtained numerically in previous studies, but identify discrepancies in earlier analytical works. These inconsistencies overestimated the out-of-Cassini-plane offset induced by tidal deformation by a factor of 100. Additionally, we explore the parameter space to determine where the spin axis deviates most from the Cassini plane and identify a region exhibiting bifurcation in the spin axis equilibrium position. This region cannot be adequately analysed using a model linearised with respect to the obliquity angle.

items.title: Adaptive Collective Decision-Making in Signed Networks
items.abstract: Collective decision-making often unfolds in networks where cooperation and antagonism coexist. Such signed interactions arise in social, biological, and robotic systems, and can lead to qualitatively different collective outcomes: consensus, polarization, or clustering. Existing signed network models typically explain these outcomes separately, leaving open how they can emerge within a single dynamical framework. Here, we introduce a generalized Laplacian flow for bi-partitioned signed networks, a class of networks that allows cooperative and antagonistic interactions both within and across two prescribed groups. The proposed model includes an adaptive social effort state, interpreted as a leaky memory of persistent signed network disagreement, which enables bounded and nontrivial steady-states beyond classical signed Laplacian flows. We derive conditions that determine whether the network reaches consensus, polarization, or clustering based on the spectral structure of the generalized Laplacian and effective resistance matrices. The framework applies beyond structurally balanced, weakly balanced, and quasi-structurally balanced networks, and reveals how changes in signed interaction strengths can shift a network between collective decision regimes. We validate the theory on stochastic block model networks, a judicial voting network, and a U.S. senate bill co-sponsorship network. Altogether, our results provide a structural and dynamical account of how mixed cooperative and antagonistic relationships shape emergent collective behaviors.
